Full time in the Stadium of Light. The curtain comes down at the end of the Premier League season for Sunderland and Swansea in a match which sees Garry Monk's men leave for the summer with an impressive 3-1 away victory. Wayne Routledge and Marvin Emnes netted for the visitors in the first half but Borini clawed a goal back shortly after the break for Sunderland. Any potential comeback was halted however thanks to a superb Wilfried Bony goal, who tops of a fantastic personal season. Swansea finish the season in a respectable 12th position, with Gus Poyet's men end up 14th after battling relegation! I'm Martin Macdonald, thanks for joining us! We'll see you for the 2014/15 season!
(90’) Three minutes of added time here and only a couple more minutes of the Premier League season. This comes the time of the year when we all take up another hobby! Can Swansea or Sunderland record another goal before they leave for the summer?!
(89’) How have Sunderland not got away a shot their?! The ball falls kindly to Altidore who is dispossessed after a brilliant tackle from Bartley. Then Colback latches on to the loose ball but can't get it out of his feet to get a strike away!
(87’) Not much happening in the latter stages here and it looks like the players in both sides are looking forward to their holidays. A well-earned break for some!
--- 85’ Yellow card L. Bridcutt is yellow-carded. ---
(85’) De Guzman and Dyer link up brilliantly down the right wing with a neat one-two which sees the latter break down to the byline and whip a cross to the front post. The Dutchman gets to the ball but just can't twist his body in the air and ends up glancing his header out of the box. Good clearance, Jonathan!
--- 84’ Substitution J. O'Shea is replaced with J. Altidore. ---
--- 83’ Yellow card F. Borini goes into the referee's book. ---
(83’) Gus Poyet is going for this now as he introduces an attacker, Jose Altidore, in place of a defender, John O'Shea. That's three strikers out there for Sunderland now, so we could be in for a grandstand finish!
(81’) The referee, Chris Foy, suffers the wrath of the Sunderland crowd as the penalises Vergini for a high foot just outside the box. It was never a free kick, really, and the home crowd have the right to feel aggrieved. Shelvey to take the set piece deep down the left flank.
(79’) The home side get a free kick about 30 yards from goal and, with Larsson substituted, it looks like Borini will be given the task. The Italian steps up and smashes the set-piece at goal but it goes high and wide and doesn't pose a threat to the Swansea goal.
(77’) Those substitutions have just hampered the tempo of the match as both sides are struggling to achieve a period of sustained possession at the moment. Swansea quite content to sit deep and soak up the pressure.
--- 75’ Substitution B. Davies enters play, replacing D. Tiendalli. ---
(75’) It is two changes in quick succession for Swansea and the second sees their Young Player of the Year, Ben Davies, come on to replace Dwight Tiendalli. Monk just utilising his squad in the final minutes of the Premier League season.
--- 73’ Substitution L. Britton enters the game and replaces J. Fulton. ---
(73’) Monk makes his second change of the match as he introduces Leon Britton in place of the debutant, Jay Fulton, who can be proud of his contribution in his first start for Swansea.
--- 71’ Substitution S. Larsson is done for the day. E. Ba is his replacement. ---
(71’) That'll be the last action of the Swede as he is substituted for El Hadji Ba. The former is yet another player who is out of contract in the summer, so there will certainly be a lot of suitors for his services!
(70’) LARSSON HITS THE POST AGAIN! He whips in yet another dangerous free kick to the back post which Tremmel manages to tip on to the woodwork! It actually looked like a magnificent save from the Swansea keeper!
--- 69’ Yellow card Jordi Amat is cautioned by the referee. ---
(68’) We've got some handbags just outside the box at the moment as Amat goes in strongly on Borini on the left-hand side of the penalty area. The Spaniard looked to have took the ball, but he took the man also! He goes into the book and Sunderland get the free kick.
(66’) Well, what on Earth is that from Vergini? The Argentine initially does well to stride forward through the middle and get into a decent position in front of the opposition box, but for some reason opts to dink the ball over the defence, which Tremmel easily claims out of the air. An odd one, that!
(64’) The last few minutes have just seen a bit of a drop in tempo as Swansea comfortably dictate the play in the middle of the park. No sign of the thunder from the home side as of yet, but you get the feeling there is another goal in this!
--- 63’ Substitution O. Celustka comes on for P. Bardsley. ---
(62’) Gus Poyet makes his first change of the match as Bardsley is replace by Celustka. That's an odd one, as the Scottish international has played well today. He's also out of contract in the summer, so have we seen him in a Sunderland shirt for the last time?
(60’) The Sunderland fans have aimed to get behind their team as much as they can, and the stadium was rocking as Borini clawed a goal back, but Bony halted the ascendancy of the hosts so quickly that it's just dampened the atmosphere slightly again. I'm sure the Black Cats faithful will find their voice again soon though!
(58’) Larsson gets the opportunity to whip another dangerous set-piece into the box but the Swede's free kick from the left-hand side is just a bit too deep, which means Wickham can't rise high enough to get a good connection. Swansea goal kick.
(56’) Garry Monk reacts quickly to that goal and makes his first substitution of the match. Jonathan De Guzman comes on to replace Emnes, who is awarded a yellow card for taking too long to leave he field. Bit harsh!
--- 55’ Substitution M. Emnes is done for the day. J. de Guzmán is his replacement. ---
--- 55’ Yellow card M. Emnes receives a yellow card. ---
--- 54’ Goal! GOOOOAAAALLL!!! GOOOAAALLL!! GOOOAAALLL!! SWANSEA REPLY QUICKLY!! The visitors counterattack at tremendous pace and the ball eventually comes to Bony, who skips past the challenge of Colback before lashing a strike in off the post! 3-1! ---
(52’) JOHNSON! How did that not go in! The 26-year-old goes on a signature run down the left wing and cuts inside before rifling a strike towards the bottom corner, that appears to come off the calf of Amat! Fortuitous clearance for Swansea!
--- 50’ Assist A. Johnson gave the assist. ---
--- 50’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOAAAAALLLLLL FOR SUNDERLAND!!! And it was simple enough! Johnson whips a superb cross to the front post and Borini gets behind his marker to bullet a header past Tremmel! 2-1! GAME ON! ---
(48’) Bright start to the second half from Sunderland as they look to grab an early goal to get a route back into contention here. Swansea haven't been completely rock solid at the back so far, so they can certainly be got at.
(46’) We are back under way in the Stadium of Light!
Half time in the Stadium of Light. Sunderland's massive effort over the past few weeks to avoid relegation looks to have caught up with them as they go into the break 2-0 down against Swansea at home in the last day of the season. Routledge and Emnes have been on target for the visitors, who looked pretty comfortable up until the last 10 minutes, as the Black Cats searched for a goal back. An interesting second half in store as both sides look to end the season on a high!
(44’) BARDSLEY!!! He almost scores a cracker! The left-back collects the ball 25 yards out and hits a rasper of a strike towards the top corner but Tremmel just retreats far enough to get up and tip the shot over the bar! Unlucky!
(42’) Wickham looks to latch on to a loose ball through to Tremmel and puts Amat under massive pressure, which forces the Swansea central defender to put the ball out for a throw in. Good work by the Sunderland forward.
(40’) Sunderland just can't seem to deal with the sheer brute strength of Bony and Emnes in attack. Opposition tackles are just bouncing off the duo as they hold up the ball in the final third, but Dyer and Routledge just need to anticipate more and get on the ball in the channels.
(38’) Bardsley, who's actually been one of Sunderland's biggest threats so far, finds himself in the final third once again and this time opts to cut inside on his right foot. He whips a shot at goal aiming for the far corner but his attempt goes a few yards wide of the post.
(36’) The Swansea fans have been in full voice for well over half-an-hour now as they cruise through this match with a two-goal lead. Definite musings of frustration among the Stadium of Light faithful though as they see their side put in an inept performance so far.
(34’) Vergini hits an aimless diagonal pass into the box and Tiendalli panics and heads behind with no opposition player with 30 yards. That was Tremmel's all the way, but there was no communication between the two Swansea men! Sunderland corner!
(32’) Bony loses the ball in the final third with an uncharacteristic poor touch which allows Sunderland to counterattack. Johnson drives down the right wing and typically cuts in on his left foot before looking to thread a pass through to Borini, but Shelvey reads it and intercepts.
(30’) Bardsley once again gets into an advanced position down that left wing and looks for Wickham at the back post, but the former Sheffield Wednesday loanee can't shake off the attentions of Taylor to get a header away, and the ball eventually goes out for a goal kick. The Sunderland fans scream for a foul, but there wasn't too much in it.
(28’) LARSSON HITS THE POST!!! The Swede cuts inside from the right wing and whips a fantastic, teasing cross into the box which eventually runs all the way through to bounce off the inside of the woodwork! Tremmel was beaten! So unlucky!
(26’) In the past couple of minutes though, Sunderland have just began to up their tempo. Two or three crosses are pumped into the box within about 30 seconds but a combination of Shelvey and Amat clear each time for the Swans.
(24’) Shelvey and Emnes have been terrific so far for the visitors. The former dictating play from the deeper areas and the latter holding up the play and providing support to Bony. Sunderland can't get anywhere near them at the moment!
(22’) Bardsley gets to the byline down the left flank and stands a cross to the back post which is eventually picked up by Routledge outside the area. The home fans are demanding a free kick as the ball appeared to come off the arm of the Swansea man, but the referee opts to play on. Would have been harsh!
--- 20’ Yellow card J. Fulton gets yellow. ---
(20’) The first booking of the match goes to debutant, Jat Fulton, who make a late challenge in the middle of the park. A pretty daft yellow to pick so early in the match!
(18’) The rain has been streaming down since before kick off today, and it is making for an extremely slick surface. Swansea have adapted to the conditions by far the better here, as they control the midfield with ease.
(16’) The hosts counterattack down the left-hand side through Johnson and he finds Wickham inside the box, who can't seem to sort out his feet in time to get a shot away, which allows Amat to make the interception!
(15’) Sunderland have barely got out of the blocks here! They need to get their act together, and quick!
--- 14’ Assist The assist came from W. Bony. ---
--- 14’ Goal! GOOOOOOOAAAALLLLLLL FOR SWANSEA!! They double their lead! The ball is played to the feet of Emnes inside the box and the on-loan Middlesborough man turns sharply before whipping a superb strike into the corner! 2-0! ---
(13’) Swansea continue to probe for their second goal here, and they look the more likely side at he moment!
(11’) It's been an impressive start from Routledge so far. The winger has took on Vergini two or three times down the left-hand side and each time has bettered the Argentine. Garry Monk will certainly be telling his man to keep up it up; definite source of danger for Sunderland.
(9’) Well, that certainly wasn't in the script for Gus Poyet and his side! The Stadium of Light crowd was full of song in the opening minutes, but the atmosphere has just been dampened by the Swans. Still plenty of time for more goals here, though.
--- 7’ Assist W. Routledge gave the assist. ---
--- 7’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOOOAAALLLLLL FOR SWANSEA!! The visitors counterattack through the middle and Routledge slides a lovely pass through to Dyer, who coolly finishes past Mannone! 1-0! ---
(5’) Johnson collects the ball on the right-hand side and looks to stretch his legs down the wing, but his path inside is just blocked by Taylor, who comes in with a well-timed tackle. Good defending.
(3’) As suspected, it is a fantastic atmosphere here today! Both sides who love vibrant, attacking football, and with no pressure on either side, we should be in for a cracker!
(1’) We are under way in the Stadium of Light!
For Swansea, Angel Rangel continues to remain absent due to a groin injury, which means Dwight Tiendally starting at right-back. There is also a debut for former Falkirk midfielder, Jay Fulton, in the middle of the park next to Jonjo Shelvey. The Scot makes his debut today in the last match of the season.
Lee Cattermole has picked up a knock and will be replaced in the middle of the park by Liam Bridcutt, who features in the middle with Jack Colback. Sebastian Larsson was a doubt for the match today, but has shook off a niggling muscle injury to be deployed on the left-hand side.

TEAM NEWS...
Swansea currently sit 13th in the Barclays Premier League, and Garry Monk was recently awarded for sustaining the Welsh side's status in the top division with the permanent manager position, after previously taking over as caretaker. Today is his first match as boss.

We should be in for a party atmosphere today in the last round of fixtures of the season as Sunderland and Swansea have both successfully avoided the drop. Two sides with no pressure, so should be an entertaining affair!

It was a stroll in the park for the North London side this afternoon as first half goals from Paulinho, an own goal from Nathan Baker and a penalty from Emmanuel Adebayor sealed Spurs' place in the top six and Euroopa League next season. Villa were woeful from beginning to end and contributed to their downfall with a lack of impotus and guile and were outclassed by their opponents.

Both sets of fans are cheering and having a great time but it is really a chance for both sides to give some invaluable match experience to youngsters in the ranks. Pritchard has looked alert for the hosts whislt Robertson was unlucky not to feed El Ahmadi in the box.

(22’) Bacuna wriggles free of Chiriches' intentions just outside the box. Rose plays a dodgy backpass to Lloris who slips as he kicks it! The Frenchman manages to put it out for a throw in but the Tottenham bakc four were dicing with danger there!

Both line-ups are out of the tunnel to a chorus of cheers at White Hart Lane...who will come out on top in this one?

Tactically, WBA will play with width through Brunt and Morrison, with Sessegnon and Amalfitano looking to find space behind Berahino, with Mulumbu sitting in front of the back three to provide screening cover.
West Brom have struggled to live up to some promising starts in the last few seasons and despite some genuinely quality players, alongside exciting prospects like Berihino, who starts today, they have flirted with the drop this season. They will be looking to end the season on a slight high with a win today and start again next season.
Stoke could finish ninth if they win today which would be a hugely satisfying highest league finish for the Potters. Mark Hughes has done an enormous amount to restore his reputation during his tenure at Stoke, with their transition towards a more fluid, attacking style of football paying dividends.
West Brom are safe from relegation in every respect other than pure mathematical certainty. It would require a WBA loss and a Norwich win by seventeen whole for West Brom to trouble the Championship next year. So that's not going to happen.
West Brom are not missing any obvious first-choice players, but Stoke would have likely picked Assaidi, who is out with some sort of knee injury, but sparkled last weekend against Fulham.

Good afternoon and welcome to this tasty looking midday London derby in the Premier League between West Ham and Tottenham. My name is Hayden Gribble and I will be bringing you all of the action of a game that some corners of the media have dubbed the ‘P45 derby’ as both managers will be looking for a win to ease the pressure on themselves and their teams. The teams news is coming right up...

My name is Ben Cullimore and it's been a pleasure describing the action to you this afternoon. Have a great rest of the weekend!
Hull remain on 37 points and are mathematically still in danger of being relegated, and they now face tough clashes against Manchester United and Everton in their final two games of the season. However, if 18th-place Norwich City fail to beat Chelsea tomorrow, their safety will be confirmed.
Aston Villa deservedly win all three points and, as a result of hitting the much sought-after 38-point mark, are guaranteed Premier League football for another season. Weimann was their hero, netting twice and playing a crucial role in the final third of the pitch, whilst Bowery had a great game after Agbonlahor's injury midway through the first half meant that he had to come on for only his seventh appearance of the season.
FT: ASTON VILLA 3-1 HULL CITY
(90’) Hull try to embark on one last attacking movement, but the Aston Villa defence sit deep and refuse to allow them a way through.
(90’) There will be three minutes of added time.
(90’) Westwood gives away a free kick to Hull 30 yards out on the right flank, which Huddlestone sends right over the heads of all of the players in the penalty area and out for a goalkick.
(88’) Hull players are dropping like flies in the final moments of the game. Now Livermore is lying on the floor, but it looks as if he's only suffering from cramp and nothing too serious.
(87’) Baker and Long clash off the ball on the edge of the Aston Villa penalty area, leaving the Irishman limping and clutching his leg.
(85’) Hull continue to press, and El Mohamady forces Lowton into clearing the ball out for a corner. It's whipped in towards Bruce, who heads the ball into Bowery and out for another corner. The next one is headed out to El Mohamady on the wing, who composes himself before setting up Bruce once again, but his final headed effort is poor and it fails to trouble Guzan.
(83’) Livermore slides in late on Westwood, taking out the Aston Villa player from behind and giving away a free kick. It's launched forward but Bacuna is unable to control it, instead heading the ball out for a Hull goalkick.
--- 81’ Substitution L. Bacuna enters the game and replaces A. Weimann. ---
(81’) Weimann receives a standing ovation as he makes his way off the pitch to be replaced by Bacuna. The Austrian has arguably been Aston Villa's best player today, and his impressive performance could well have guaranteed his side another season of Premier League football.
(80’) Bowery, who is the only Aston Villa player positioned in the Hull half of the pitch, receives the ball and has to push forward by himself. He tries a few step-overs before unleashing a long-range shot, but it's poor and flies well wide.
(78’) Aston Villa continue to sit deep and frustrate the Hull forwards, who remain unable to find a way through.
--- 76’ Substitution K. El Ahmadi enters play, replacing M. Albrighton. ---
(76’) Albrighton, who has got a slight groin strain, makes his way off the pitch to be replaced by El Ahmadi.
(76’) Huddlestone finds himself with the ball at his feet just outside the Aston Villa penalty area and he decides to shoot, but Guzan is able to dive low and save comfortably.
(75’) Much to the relief of Paul Lambert and the Aston Villa fans, Weimann is back on his feet and seems to have recovered.
(74’) Paul Lambert looks worried as Weimann lies hurt on the floor. He's been absolutely fantastic today, and it would be such a shame if he was to leave the pitch injured.
(72’) Things have calmed down somewhat, as Aston Villa seem content to push further back and defend their two-goal lead. Their defence hold their positions and frustrate Hull, forcing Figueroa into attempting a shot from 40 yards out that clears the goal by quite some distance.
--- 70’ Substitution Y. Sagbo enters play, replacing N. Jelavić. ---
(70’) Hull are in desperate need of a greater attacking threat up front if they are going to have any chance of making a comeback, so Steve Bruce has decided to replace the relatively ineffective Jelavic with Sagbo, who is desperately searching for only his third Premier League goal since joining from French club Evian last summer.
(68’) Delph rushes down the right wing before crossing in towards Bowery, who, despite being outnumbered three-to-one, makes a nuisance of himself and almost makes contact with the ball.
(66’) Both goalkeepers seem to be in the mood to rush out to the edge of their penalty areas, as, just moments after Guzan does so at one end, Harper does it at the other to dispossess Weimann. The veteran goalkeeper decides to go in with his feet, however, cutting out the danger at the last moment.
(64’) Huddlestone sends a fantastic long ball forward that flies over the top of the Aston Villa back line and into the path of Long, but Guzan rushes out and just about manages to collect the ball before the Irishman can make contact with it.
(62’) A Hull attack breaks down and Weimann and Bowery break away on a counter attack for Aston Villa. The Austrian lays the ball off for the substitute and he weaves in and out of the Hull defence on the edge of the penalty area before unleashing a shot that Harper has to tip over the crossbar with his finger tips.
(60’) After being on the back foot for the majority of the second half so far, Hull are finally gifted an opportunity to pull a goal back after a miskick by Clark, but both Jelavic and El Mohamady scuff their shots.
(58’) Aston Villa win a corner, which Albrighton sends into the heart of the Hull penalty area. Harper does just about enough to punch the ball away and out to the edge of the penalty area, where Albrighton picks it up once again and, with plenty of space around him, decides to unleash an ambitious shot on goal, but it flies well wide of the goal.
(56’) Aston Villa continue to push and pressurise the Hull defence, and the visitors continue to find it difficult to deal with a side that are so attack-minded, despite being two goals ahead with over half-an-hour left to play.
(54’) Another chance for Aston Villa! This time it's Bowery that beats Figueroa by twisting and turning around the Honduran before unleashing a low shot towards Harper, who dives down low to parry the ball away before pouncing on it.
(52’) Again, Weimann muscles his way past a Hull defender, this time Figueroa, but he decides to shoot from a tight angle and the effort fails to test Harper.
(50’) Weimann beats Bruce on the left flank and sends a long cross towards Albrighton near the back post. He tries to volley the ball into the centre of the penalty area but it fails to find an Aston Villa shirt, and Hull are able to clear the ball and regroup.
(49’) Weimann and Bertrand link up on the edge of the Hull penalty area as Aston Villa push forward looking for a fourth goal, but the on-loan Englishman is flagged for offside.
(47’) Early danger for Hull as Aston Villa are awarded a free kick on the left wing, but Albrighton's delivery is cut out and headed away up the pitch.
--- 46’ Substitution S. Quinn comes on for D. Meyler. ---
(45’) And we're off again!
Just one change has been made at half time and it's for Hull: Meyler has been replaced by Quinn.
The two teams are making their way back onto the pitch ahead of a vitally important second half. Aston Villa are just 45 minutes away from guaranteed Premier League safty, whilst Hull face the extremely difficult task of attempting to pull off a comeback against a strong and determined side that are full of confidence.
Aston Villa have easily been the better of the two sides at Villa Park this afternoon, and, as a result, they deservedly lead 3-1 at the half time break. Their dominance seems to have much to do with the timing of their opening goal, as falling behind after only 55 seconds had a damaging effect on Hull's confidence. From then onwards, bar a few periods of impressive attacking play, the visitors were always on the back foot, and they have continued to find it difficult to deal with the pace and power of Weimann, particularly down the right flank.
--- 45’ +3 Assist The assist came from J. Bowery. ---
--- 45’ +3 Goal! GOAL! Hull fail to put enough pressure on Bowery and the substitute whips in a wonderful cross towards Weimann, who rises high and nods in a fantastic headed effort past Harper. 3-1! ---
(45’) There's confusion between Davies and Harper, and the former ends up making a scruffy half-volleyed clearance that goes out for a Aston Villa corner.
(45’) Aston Villa are back on the front foot, as Hull look deflated, despite still having over half of the game left to play. Weimann and Figueroa fight for the ball near the corner flag, but the Honduran wins the battle and is able to shepherd the ball out for a goalkick.
(45’) There will be three minutes of added time.
--- 43’ Substitution A. Bruce enters the game and replaces J. Chester. ---
(43’) Things go from bad to worse for Hull, as Chester is forced off with a nasty injury. His replacement is Bruce, a former Birmingham City player, and, as expected, the home crowd greet his introduction with a chorus of boos.
--- 41’ Goal! GOAL! Aston Villa keep the pressure exerted on the Hull defence and are rewarded with a second goal. A corner finds Baker in the middle of the box and his towering header is cleared off the line by Jelavic, before his follow-up effort hits the crossbar. The Hull defence are all over the place and fail to clear the ball, allowing Weimann to head the ball over the line from point-blank range. 2-1! ---
(40’) Great play by Aston Villa! Weimann muscles his way past three Hull defenders before sprinting into the box and forcing Harper into pulling off a good save. The ball then finds its way out to Delph, who sends the ball back into the box, where Bowery sends a headed effort towards Harper, forcing the veteran goalkeeper to tip the ball over the crossbar.
(38’) Baker is forced into sending a bouncing pass back to Guzan, which the goalkeeper scuffs and puts out for a Hull corner. Huddlestone whips the ball into centre of the penalty area where it finds the head of Meyler, but his effort goes well wide of the goal.
(36’) A long ball forward almost finds Long, but, again, Guzan rushes out to cut out the danger. The Aston Villa back four are looking extremely nervous at the moment!
(34’) Brilliant save by Guzan! Huddlestone finds himself in plenty of space 30 yards out so he decides to unleash a rocket of a shot on goal, but the American goalkeeper dives to his left and pulls off a spectacular stop.
(32’) Hull win another free kick, this time further out on the left wing, and Huddlestone again takes it. This time he decides to send a more orthodox long ball into the box, but Guzan rushes out and collects it with ease.
(30’) The atmosphere inside Villa Park has gone sour and the emphasis is now entirely with Hull, who have finally woken up after a slow start to the game.
--- 28’ Goal! GOAL! Huddlestone decides to send the free kick out to the left hand side of the penalty area and Aston Villa are completely caught by surprise. Rosenior is unmarked and has plenty of time to set himself up before firing the ball towards goal, where it clips off Bowery before ending up in the bottom left-hand corner of the net. 1-1! ---
(27’) Vlaar dives into the back of Long and Hull are awarded a free kick in a dangerous position 25 yards away from goal.
(25’) Bowery makes an instant impact by flicking the ball onto Weimann down the right wing. He runs forward and beats Davies before trying to find Bowery, who has made a great run into the centre of the box, but the Austrian is crowded out and his pass is deflected out for a corner, which Hull are able to deal with.
--- 23’ Substitution J. Bowery enters play, replacing G. Agbonlahor. ---
(23’) Disappointment for Aston Villa as they're forced into making an early substitution. Agbonhalor is still struggling with the injury to his left knee, so he is replaced by Bowery.
(21’) Hull win a corner and throw a plethora of bodies forward to attack it. The ball is cleared but only as far as Rosenior, and the follow-up cross almost finds Jelavic, but Mike Dean blows his whistle and awards a free kick to Aston Vila after spotting some pushing and shoving in front of goal.
(19’) Albrighton dispossesses Meyler and Aston Villa break away on a counter attack. Weimann darts forward with the ball before being taken down from behind by Huddlestone, and referee Mike Dean awards the hosts a free kick. The resulting set-piece is launched forward but it's too heavy and it clears every player in the box.
(17’) Every Aston Villa player bar Guzan is in the Hull half of the pitch as they push forward in search of a second goal. However, the visitors have plenty of bodies behind the ball and break down yet another promising attacking movement.
(15’) Again, Hull attack down the left flank, and, again, Figueroa and Meyler link up well. The latter finds Long, who fires a low cross into the box, but it's poor and fails to trouble the Aston Villa defence.
(13’) The resulting set-piece is fails to find an Aston Villa shirt and is cleared away and up towards the halfway line by Davies, before being sent all the way back to Guzan.
(12’) Aston Villa are knocking on the door again and causing Hull problems in the final third. Agbonlahor, who seems to have recovered from his earlier knock, manages to get a shot away from the edge of the box despite being under pressure, but his effort is deflected out for a corner.
(11’) Patient build-up play by Hull in the middle of the pitch, but Aston Villa are pressing and putting them under serious pressure, which the visitors are finding hard to deal with.
(9’) Figueroa and Meyler link up on the left flank before the Irishman tries to set up Livermore, who made a darting run into the Aston Villa penalty area, but his lofted ball forward is too heavy and it bounces out for a goalkick.
(7’) Hull look determined after falling a goal behind so quickly. They break down the right flank and attempt to work their way into the box, but Delph stands tall and wins his side a throw-in deep in their own half of the pitch.
(5’) After receiving treatment, Agbonlahor is back on his feet, much to the relief of Paul Lambert who looked particularly worried.
(3’) It's gone from joy to agony for Aston Villa, as Agbonlahor is lying on the floor clutching his left knee.
--- 1’ Assist The assist came from M. Albrighton. ---
--- 1’ Goal! GOAL! A dream start for Aston Villa as Westwood puts them ahead after only 55 seconds! Agbonlahor bursts down the left wing before firing the ball across the box. Albrighton scuffs his shot but has time to lay the ball off to Westwood on the edge of the penalty area, and he fires his effort past Harper and into the back of the net. 1-0! ---
(1’) And we're off! Hull get us underway, kicking from right-to-left.
The sun is shining brightly and both sets of fans are in fine voice as the two teams make their way onto the pitch.
Aston Villa, meanwhile, are in desperate need of three points after failing to win any of their last six league games, with five of those clashes ending in defeat. The poor run has left them just three points clear of the relegation zone, and they, too, face two strong opponents - Manchester City and Tottenham Hotspur - in their final two games of the season. Realistically, today's game is their last chance to pick up a win, but it will by no means be an easy feat; Hull have conceded just 45 goals this season, fewer than both Liverpool and Tottenham Hotspur.
Hull are as good as safe from relegation after an impressive first season back in the Premier League, but a win today will guarantee their safety ahead of two tough games against Manchester United and Everton.
As for Hull, boss Steve Bruce has decided to make just one change to the side that valiantly fought back from 2-0 down to draw 2-2 away to Fulham last Saturday. Maynor Figueroa returns to the startling line up after missing out against the Cottagers last weekend, and he replaces Alex Bruce, who takes the Honduran's place on the substitutes' bench.
Paul Lambert has made two changes to the side that were comfortably beaten 4-1 by Swansea City last weekend. Leandro Bacuna and Karim El Ahmadi both drop to the bench, making way for Ciaran Clark and Matthew Lowton to replace them.

Good afternoon and welcome to the live text commentary of today's Premier League game between Aston Villa and Hull City. My name is Ben Cullimore and I will be keeping you up-to-date with all of the action from Villa Park.

Well, that's all from our LIVE coverage of events at Old Trafford. Thanks for joining, and we hope to see you again soon!
Well, what a result for Sunderland! Plenty to mull over for United, who were just not good enough in the final third. Giggs has his work cut out - will he be able to take the job permanently?
Having looked dead certs for relegation, the Black Cats are now three points clear of the drop zone. The result also means Fulham and Cardiff are both down after they lost their games.
That's FULL TIME at Old Trafford and Sunderland have won! What a result! Sunderland have had a remarkable run and they've produced a wonderful display to hold United at bay. Seb Larsson's fine volley has given Gus Poyet's men the spoils here today.
(90’) United win a goal kick and De Gea hammers it forward. Van Persie flicks it on but it goes to a yellow shirt, and the visitors come forward before Giaccherini draws a foul off Jones. Is that it?
(90’) Sunderland are so, so close to victory here. They have a free kick just inside their own half, and Mannone launches it forward before Altidore does well to hold it up and win a throw deep inside the United half.
(90’) Altidore is penalised this time as he fouls Evra, and the full-back squares to De Gea, who gets his clearance all wrong and the visitors have a throw inside the United half. Two minutes of stoppage time down; we've got two more to go.
--- 90’ +1 Yellow card N. Vidić is yellow-carded. ---
(90’) Oof, that's a silly one by Vidic. The United skipper charges in on Altidore and cleans the striker out right on the touchline. On another day, that could have been a red.
(90’) Januzaj tries to inspire something as he crosses from the left, Fletcher's header is cleared but it comes out to Carrick, but his shot is charged down by Cattermole, who throws absolutely everything at it.
(89’) Evra moves into an advanced position on the flank, but Vergini is again their to cover before winning a throw off the United man. Into the final minute of normal time...
(88’) Carrick looks for Van Persie with another measured pass, but Vergini reads the play well and charges in to cut the ball out. United's challenge in this game is going out with a bit of a whimper.
(87’) There's a break in play as Borini and Evra clash heads in the air. This will add minutes on to the end. Giggsy Time, anyone?
(86’) Hernandez slides a lovely ball through the defence for Van Persie inside the box, but again he strays offside and the flag goes up. Sunderland survive again.
(85’) Giggs is still on the touchline but is looking a little lost. His side just haven't been very good today. Sunderland are five minutes away from their first win at Old Trafford since 1968.
(84’) BORINI OFF THE BAR!! The Sunderland fans are cheering every  pass now, and Giaccherini slides a lovely pass through for Borini, who cuts on to his left and curls a beautiful effort past De Gea, but it doesn't beat the woodwork as it rattles back off the bar.
(83’) A priceless period of possession for the visitors, now, as they run the clock down and pass it along the back. United press but Poyet's men look assured on the ball.
(82’) De Gea is a lonely man right now as United continue to play inside the Sunderland half. Their sheer domination of possession has been bettered by the Black Cats' discipline and organisation, though.
(81’) HERNANDEZ!! Great chance to level it!! Evra finds space on the left after a lovely pass from Carrick. The full-back pulls the ball back to Hernandez, who spurns a glorious chance by scooping his effort well over the bar with his left foot.
(80’) Carrick looks for Welbeck with an early ball beyond the defence, but it's not accurate and goes out for a through amid groans from the stands. There's just not been enough quality from United this afternoon - or this season, in fact.
(78’) The hosts are STILL dominating possession, but they can't find a way through Sunderland. Hernandez flicks a lovely ball on for Van Persie, but the Netherlands striker is just a yard offside and the flag goes up.
(77’) WELBECK!! Fletcher plays the ball out wide to the substitute, who cuts inside before firing a venomous effort from 20 yards which fizzes just over Mannone's crossbar.
(75’) The visitors keep the ball away but Mannone then fluffs his lines, slicing a clearance straight out for a throw to United. Are the hosts going to get another chance?
--- 74’ Substitution L. Bridcutt enters the game and replaces S. Larsson. ---
(74’) How this is still 1-0, I'll never know. Two superb opportunities in short succession! Liam Bridcutt is on for the visitors as Poyet looks to tighten things up for the final 15 minutes or so.
(73’) VAN PERSIE!! Sunderland almost pay for their misses as Welbeck lays off to Jones, who fires in a low cross which Van Persie meets at the near post, getting in front of Mannone well but diverting it just wide.
(72’) GIACCHERINI AND COLBACK!! SO NEARLY 2-0!! Altidore and Borini link up brilliantly before the substitute fires the ball into the area. Giaccherini meets it with a first-time effort which flicks out off the post. Colback collects it before shooting from a tight angle, and his effort rifles into the side netting. What a chance!
(71’) The hosts' pressure continues, and everyone bar De Gea is inside the United half. Carrick wastes possession, though, as he fires the ball straight out for a goal kick with no-one wide to aim for.
(70’) Giaccherini plays the ball forward and Colback chases it well, but ends up fouling Jones and the hosts have possession once more. Time is quickly running out for Giggs' men.
(69’) Januzaj turns into a defender momentarily as he tracks back before producing a wonderful tackle to dispossess Giaccherini. He's worked very hard since coming on but United still look poor going forward.
(68’) Sunderland have a rare opportunity inside the United half as they win a throw near the corner flag. They're quickly forced backwards into their own half under good United pressure, but Poyet's men are keeping the ball well for now.
--- 67’ Substitution D. Welbeck comes on for A. Young. ---
(67’) Januzaj swings in the free kick and it flicks off the head of Borini before O'Shea hacks it clear. The hosts come back, though, and Vidic challenges for the ball before it drops to Jones, who fires a first-time effort way over the bar.
--- 66’ Substitution R. van Persie enters play, replacing Mata. ---
(66’) United win a free kick on the left-hand side and this is a good chance to whip the ball in. Meanwhile, Robin van Persie is back for the hosts as he and Danny Welbeck replace Mata and Young. It's an attacking change from Giggs, who wants his side to at least restore parity.
--- 65’ Substitution C. Wickham is replaced with J. Altidore. ---
(65’) A rare bit of respite for the visitors as they push into the United half, but Johnson loses out as the hosts win a throw. Just 25 minutes left for Poyet's men to hold on for a remarkable win.
(64’) Change for Sunderland as Wickham goes off to be replaced by Jozy Altidore. The striker hasn't netted today but it was his cross that set up Larsson's volley.
(62’) SHOULD BE 1-1!! A real scramble in the box!! The ball is fired in from a corner and Vidic is there in the six-yard box before laying down to Jones, who slices his effort before Carrick heads down at goal. Mannone can't gather and Vidic tries to win it but three Sunderland players manage to eventually get it away.
(61’) Fletcher does really well to evade two Sunderland players before sliding a pass through for Carrick. He spreads it wide to Januzaj, whose cross is far to heavy and it goes out the other side.
(60’) We've hit the hour, and Sunderland are still looking organised amid constant United possession. The hosts need to change their approach to break the visitors down - the crossing has to improve.
(59’) The corner is cleared but United come straight back. Young again, though, produces a very disappointing cross which evades everyone and goes behind for a corner.
(58’) Emanuele Giaccherini is on for Johnson as the United pressure goes on. Mata floats a lovely ball into the box for Hernandez, but Brown is there to cut it out and divert it behind for a corner to the hosts.
--- 57’ Substitution A. Johnson is replaced with E. Giaccherini. ---
(57’) Januzaj has definitely added something on that left-hand side for United. He's looked bright since coming on but needs his team-mates to up their game somewhat.
(56’) Jones and Young link up well on the right-hand side, but it's another poor cross as the former's delivery fails to beat the first man and Sunderland clear.
(55’) MANNONE!! Januzaj picks the ball up on the left and moves in towards the area. He has a chance to cross but goes it alone, and cuts on to his right before seeing his shot blocked behind for a corner. The Sunderland goalkeeper then completely fluffs a catch from the set piece, but fortunately for him Alonso is there to clear.
(54’) United have started to ramp up the pressure, with several passes inside the Sunderland half, but it's still all in front of the visitors. They look very well organised, and Johnson battles hard to win the ball before clearing away.
(53’) Fletcher looks for Young out on the right-hand side, but again it's all too easy for Sunderland to deal with and Alonso cuts it out comfortably.
--- 52’ Substitution A. Januzaj comes on for Nani. ---
(52’) It's an early change from Giggs as he hauls off Nani, who has been pretty ineffective in the United midfield. Adnan Januzaj is on in his place - can he inspire a comeback?
(51’) HERNANDEZ!! It's a glorious chance for United as Evra charges down the left and fires a low ball across the box. Hernandez meets it just yards from goal but Brown challenges superbly to divert it behind for a corner.
(50’) The hosts are again enjoying more possession, but a lot of it is inside their own half at the moment. The likes of Mata and Young aren't producing good deliveries and something needs to change if they are to score today.
(49’) Sunderland again do well to hold their shape and United are forced backwards, prompting impatient groans from the stands. They haven't had much to cheer about this afternoon.
(48’) Larsson poaches the ball away from Fletcher in midfield and Sunderland have possession. The hosts are pressing a bit harder, and higher up - something Giggs has clearly mentioned during the break.
(47’) Nani catches Vergini in possession but it's mopped up by Brown, who hammers the ball forward. The visitors are starting the half well but possession is changing hands pretty regularly as it's a little bit scrappy early on.
(46’) Poyet's men get the ball rolling and we're back underway. No changes at the break for either side.
Almost time to get back underway at Old Trafford. How will the next 45 minutes pan out? The visitors will give their survival hopes a massive boost if they can hold on to win here.
Can the hosts turn things around, or will Poyet's men maintain their discipline to hold on for another vital victory? Be sure to rejoin us when we get back underway for the second half.
The work in the final third from United has been poor. Their crossing has not been up to standard and Giggs has his work cut out in the half-time team talk.
HALF TIME at Old Trafford, and Sunderland go in ahead at the break after a well-made goal, while Ryan Giggs' men have looked rather clueless inside the Black Cats' half.
(45’) That was United's best chance of the half, and it wasn't even that good a chance. It's a damning indictment of their display so far this afternoon.
(45’) MATA!! Good work from Hernandez, who charges in from the right and looks for Nani with a decent ball, but Cattermole is there to clear. The hosts come back, though, and Nani flicks the ball out of the area for Mata, who drills a low effort at goal which Mannone saves well.
(43’) Jones gives the ball away in midfield this time and Alonso spreads it out to Vergini, who plays forward to Johnson and the winger forces a throw. The hosts look happy to see out the rest of the half as it is now.
(42’) De Gea shanks a clearance and Johnson has a glorious chance to run into the area, but he completely wastes it as he tries to wrong-foot Vidic, who stands firm and easily deals with the winger. It's not been a brilliant afternoon from him so far.
(41’) Ferdinand dinks the ball over the top looking for the run of Nani, but O'Shea is in control as he reads the pass and heads it away. United look pretty stale going forward.
(40’) Fletcher stops Vergini in his tracks and the hosts win possession once more. Mata then spreads it wide to Young with a lovely pass forward, but yet again the final ball is poor as his cross deflects off Vergini.
(39’) Approaching the final five minutes of the half, then, and Sunderland are looking more and more worth their lead. They are very disciplined at the back and United are already running out of ideas.
(38’) Johnson gets into a really good position as he escapes Evra on the flank, but his delivery is awful as he can't find either of two team-mates in the box, instead giving it straight to Ferdinand who hacks it clear.
(37’) Lovely work from Young, who tries his luck on the left and cuts inside Vergini before firing a low ball into the six-yard box, but Larsson watches it well and clears from in front of the near post.
(36’) Cattermole escapes a booking as he slides in on Mata, giving the hosts a free kick inside the Sunderland half. They take it short and continue to pass it in front of the visitors.
(35’) United have the ball again and they are constantly in control of the ball, but they still can't find their way through a resilient Sunderland side.

The teams are out at Old Trafford and we're just a few minutes away from kick-off. It's a beautiful day in Manchester, but will the sun be shining on Giggs' men this afternoon?
Poyet's men are without a win in 23 league matches against United, but have been in resurgent form of late. They held Manchester City at the Etihad Stadium before becoming the first team to beat Chelsea at home under Jose Mourinho, so they will be in confident mood this afternoon,
This is the fourth meeting between the two sides this season, after the Black Cats beat United on penalties in the League Cup semi-final. Each game has finished 2-1 this term, so will we see that for a fourth time?
Gus Poyet, meanwhile, names the same side that comfortably beat Cardiff last weekend, and it is the same XI for the fourth game in a row as in-form striker Connor Wickham leads the line once more. The striker has scored five in his last three appearances in the Premier League, having netted just once in his first 37.
Giggs makes five changes from his first game in charge against Norwich, but it's the same back four that kept a clean sheet in their rout over the Canaries. Nani, Darren Fletcher, Ashley Young and Javier Hernandez all come in, while Juan Mata's brace last week also earns him a start. Robin van Persie makes the bench for the Red Devils this afternoon.

Cardiff return to the Championship at the first time of asking, which is a shame, but they just have not been good enough at this level. For them, the rebuilding begins. For Newcastle, there are similar questions but, for now, the players are enjoying a little farewell wander round the pitch.
For Cardiff, tears and what-might-have-beens. Their strong second half efforts were not enough, and the substitution of Campbell was mystifying. Two excellent chances, firstly from Jones and then from Gunnarsson, could have been the turning point, but in their effort to push on, Cardiff left themselves too open.
Newcastle are slightly flattered by the final score, but, against a backdrop of fan unrest and walk-outs, the team should be commended for a decent victory in their final home game of the season.
Having said that, for the whole of the first half, Cardiff looked every inch the relegation certainties, bereft of ideas and reduced to chucking long passes forwards and hoping that the industry of Campbell or the pace of Zaha would be enough.
Well, well. In the end it looks like a comfortable score-line for Newcastle but, in truth, Alan Pardew's men were under the cosh for long periods of the second half.

(84’) Newcastle are basically giving up the ball now and Cardiff have pretty much all the possession. Gosling does release Sissoko on a rare foray but Marsahll gathers and Cardiff have it again.

Newcastle are by far the better team, but are not without issues. They look very narrow when the full-backs don't get forward, and while Sissoko has drifted in superbly, Gouffran has not contributed much at all. Ameobi has worked hard and been the best player so far, with Debuchy and Sissoko a tied, close second.
Cardiff are sitting deep and trying to break, largely by knocking it long to Campbell or Zaha on the left, but their inability to retain possession is killing their chances.
Krul's save from Zaha was superb, and Marshall has also saved well from Debuchy and claimed well from a few crosses too. He had no chance with the Newcastle goal, and Cardiff have generally left their 'keeper looking rather exposed.
Half-time between NEWCASTLE UNITED and CARDIFF CITY and it's the Toon Army who have the most the cheer. Not only has Ameobi's fine header put them one up, but one chance from Zaha aside, Cardiff have barely threatened.
(45’) Into extra time at the end of the first half, and Sissoko floats a cute ball into the Cardiff box after good running by Debuchy. It's cleared but won back by Tiote. Cardiff looked knackered and bereft of ideas and must be delighted when the whistle goes for half time.

(44’) There will be at least 2 mins of stoppage time. Which is kind of a shame.

(23’) Ameobi was pulled down but got a flicked header away anyway. Newcastle retain possession and are happy playing it around, waiting for Cardiff's pressing to pull them out of shape.

(16’) AMEOBI! Heads against the bar from that corner, and then the follow up header goes over. Cardiff's set-piece defending is woeful: you do not leave someone like Ameobi open.
(15’) MARSHALL! Diving low to his left, the outstanding Cardiff keeper parries a fiercely hit Debuchy drive. Newcastle have another corner...

(2’) Debuchy hits the corner directly on the volley and it was as high, wide, and handsome as you're likely to see. Having said that, the clearly rehearsed corner gave him very little chance to get a good strike.
(1’) And they are OFF! Sissoko immediately surges down the right and pulls it back for Remy, whose first touch is poor. Fabio blocks and it's a corner.

(62’) 21 players are inside the City half at the moment - Howard's looking a bit lonely up the other end. The hosts continue to play in front of Pellegrini's men as they look for some way through.
(60’) The hosts are enjoying all the possession as we hit the hour mark, but they're not doing too much with it. It's quiet in the stands and on the pitch at the moment - who can inject some life into this one?
(59’) Barkley is again running things in the middle for Everton, and he tries to find Lukaku with a measure ball beyond the defence, but it just goes behind the Belgian and runs through for Hart to collect.

(46’) City get the ball rolling once more as the second half gets underway.

That's HALF TIME at Goodison Park and Man City take a 2-1 lead into the break after Sergio Aguero and Edin Dzeko overturned Ross Barkley's stunning opener. It's an odd atmosphere on Merseyside, and it's not been a classic encounter so far.

(45’) Zabaleta fires the ball forward but it's nowhere near a City player and the hosts have possession again. They are still in no hurry, though, as they move it forward gradually.
(45’) Into the first of three added minutes and Everton move forward into the City half. Osman looks for Naismith with a pass towards the edge of the box, but Demichelis reads the play well and moves in to cut the ball out.
(45’) Everton look vulnerable, here, and Toure tries to take advantage as he exchanges passes with Milner before moving into the box, but Coleman does well to win the ball off the Ivorian. The hosts need half time to come quickly.
(44’) That is a massive goal. City have turned things around here - will the Premier League trophy be heading across Manchester?
--- 43’ Assist J. Milner gave the assist. ---
--- 43’ Goal! DZEKO PUTS CITY AHEAD!! The striker spurns one opportunity as he fires a poor effort from a tight angle, but it comes back out to Milner who floats in a wonderful cross, and the Bosnian produces a powerful header which flies into the bottom corner. ---
(42’) McCarthy works hard to slide in and win the ball off Dzeko before firing it wide to Coleman, who wins a throw for Everton. Osman then slides the ball forward for Naismith, who drives through the middle before firing a tame effort well wide from 30 yards.
(41’) We're approaching the break and it's now Everton who have possession. Both sides are keeping it well in periods, but since the goals we've had no real action in either box.
(40’) It looks like Garcia's booking was for a tug on Lukaku's shorts some time early. Back to the present, and City have the ball but aren't moving it around with much zip or urgency.
--- 39’ Yellow card Javi García goes into the referee's book. ---

(38’) This has been a very strange game, and the silence in the stands isn't particularly helping. There seem to be plenty of nerves among the City players and fans.
(37’) Barkley sprays a lovely pass out to the right for Stones, who produces a good driving run forward before looking for Lukaku with a pass through. The Belgian is offside, though, and the flag goes up for a free kick.
(36’) Javi Garcia slides a pass through for Nasri, who tries to emulate Barkley's strike with a curling effort from 30 yards, but the Frenchman's shot whistles well over the bar.
(35’) Jagielka has a bit of an awkward moment as he treads on the ball just outside his own area. Dzeko chases him down but the defender manages to keep the ball in play and square to Howard.
(34’) Naismith is getting a rough ride at the moment as he gets clattered by Zabaleta this time. The referee initially plays advantage but then blows as Lukaku stops running.
(33’) Javi Garcia is lucky to escape a booking as he flies in on Naismith and catches the Everton man pretty late with a raised leg. The cards stay in the referee's pocket, though, and Everton have a free kick on halfway.
(32’) Toure is involved in everything at the moment, and he tries to work space for a shot from the left-hand side, but he hammers the ball into a blue wall and the hosts come away with it.
(31’) Lukaku fires a wonderful ball out to the left for Baines, who looks to play a one-two with Naismith but Kompany clears. (30’) The Toffees try to break forward as Coleman charges down the right, but Fernandinho brings him down and the chance goes away. Everton keep possession with a short free kick and will look to slowly build another attack.
(29’) Baines cross is deflected behind for a corner, which City manage to hack away at the second attempt. Dzeko chases the clearance to close down Coleman, who produces a lovely piece of control to keep the ball away from the City striker.

(26’) OK, maybe Aguero is coming off after all. He's now down receiving treatment as Fernandinho gets ready to come on for the visitors. It's a blow for City, who could really do with his goals for their title push.
(25’) Clichy fires a dangerous-looking first-time diagonal ball into the middle, and Aguero manages to chase it but Howard gets there first. It doesn't look like the striker is going to come off just yet.
(24’) Aguero is definitely struggling - he's hardly moved from the centre circle. This looks like the end of the line for him today. The visitors have possession as play goes on, and the initiative is back with Pellegrini's men.
(23’) Aguero has put City back on level terms but appears to be struggling as he keeps feeling his groin. It could be an early exit for the diminutive striker today.
--- 22’ Assist Y. Touré gave the assist. ---
--- 22’ Goal! AGUERO EQUALISES!! The silence among the Everton fans seems to go even quieter as Toure slides the ball through for Aguero, who moves into the box before hammering the ball inside Howard's near post from a tight angle. ---
(21’) Penalty? Barkley picks the ball up in space and drives towards the box before going down under two City challenges. There are half-hearted appeals for a spot kick but Kompany got a touch on the ball and the referee waves play on.
(20’) The "olés" have started from the home fans, as Everton stroke the ball around beautifully. The ball then breaks into the path of Coleman, who wastes a good position by completely over-hitting his cross and putting it behind for a goal kick.
(19’) The pace and the atmosphere are making this feel a bit like a pre-season friendly. There's not much intensity at the moment, and City are allowing the hosts more time on the ball than they were at the start.
(18’) It's still very quiet in the stands despite that absolute stunner from Barkley. Everton have dealt with the City pressure and are now passing it around well just inside the visitors' half.
(17’) City have only won once here in their last 15 visits. They're behind again but are putting the hosts under plenty of pressure.
(16’) TOURE!! Dzeko charges forward and exchanges passes with Clichy before seeing his cross blocked by Coleman. The visitors come back quickly as Nasri sllides the ball into the box for Toure, who charges inside and fires over the bar.
(15’) McCarthy charges forward but loses out to Clichy on the flank. The visitors quickly surrender possession themselves, though, as Toure produces an uncharacteristically loose pass which Stones cuts out.
(14’) Chance for City as Milner cuts in from the right and plays a good ball into the box with the outside of his right foot. Toure is there to meet it but his header loops up into the air, giving Howard an easy bit of catching practice.
(13’) Pellegrini's men are looking to get right back in this, and Nasri drives towards the box but produces a loose touch, giving Barkley the chance to cut out the ball.
(12’) A goal that befits the magnitude of the occasion. Has that booked Barkley a flight to Brazil in June?
--- 11’ Assist S. Naismith gave the assist. ---
--- 11’ Goal! GOOOAAALLLLL!! WHAT A STRIKE!! That's an absolute beauty from Barkley, who receives the ball off Naismith before bending an absolute stunner into the top corner from all of 30 yards. Fantastic goal! ---
(10’) Oh dear, Pablo. That's one to forget for Zabaleta as Aguero slides a perfect pass through for the full-back, but his compatriot completely shanks his first-time effort and it flies into the stands.
(9’) GARCIA!! Toure and Nasri exchange passes on the left-hand corner of the box, and the latter's inswinging cross is headed behind by Jagielka. Javi Garcia meets Milner's corner at the near post, but his header is straight at Howard.
(8’) City press hard and the hosts are forced backwards, but they're passing it around nicely. It's a bit of a chess match at the moment, with neither side ready to commit too many forward just yet.
(7’) Osman looks for the run of Lukaku with a chipped ball over the top, but Kompany reads it perfectly as he steps in to head the ball clear. Both sides have started pretty well, here.
(6’) Good work from Baines on the left, as he cuts inside Zabaleta before playing the ball to the edge of the area for Naismith, who shoots first time on the turn, but can only fire his shot well wide.
(5’) It's freakishly quiet at Goodison Park. The fans aren't sure if they really want Everton to win as it'll give Liverpool the upper hand in the title race. Very odd.
(4’) Clichy swings in a dangerous ball from the left but Jagielka heads it away. It comes out to Javi Garcia, who drills a shot from distance but it's well blocked by McCarthy.
(3’) Good early chance for City as Aguero pulls the ball back from the by-line, but Milner can't quite get it out of his feet as Osman half clears. It comes back to Aguero, though, and he fires a dangerous ball into the box which Dzeko can't quite reach.
(2’) Everton keep the ball well early on before Alcaraz's ball forward evades Naismith and goes through to Demichelis. Both sides look like they'll be pressing hard throughout the game.

--- 90’ +1 Yellow card G. Dorrans gets yellow. ---
--- 90’ +1 Yellow card O. Giroud goes into the referee's book. ---

(90’) Berahino may fail to see the funny side of this but the Arsenal fans haven't. The young striker is released down the right but he falls flat on his face with no one around him in pursuit.
(88’) It was at this stage in Newcastle's game against Cardiff yesterday that Loic Remy netted. Why do I mention that, you ask? Because the striker is here today watching Arsenal. Make of that what you will.
(87’) Dawson sends another header over the bar and then Anichebe fails to pick out Dorrans with a pass as another WBA attack breaks down. This game isn't over yet.

(85’) Berahino sees his cross turned behind for a corner. The Baggies are definitely going for it now as Vydra comes on for Mulumbu for the final five minutes.
--- 83’ Yellow card C. Brunt gets yellow. ---
(83’) It's up and over the wall but Foster is across to make a comfortable save. The decent atmosphere that filled the Emirates in the opening minutes has subsided here and it's all gone a bit quiet.
(82’) Berahino takes out Ozil from behind to present the home side with a decent shooting opportunity. The German will take it himself.
--- 80’ Substitution M. Amalfitano is replaced with V. Anichebe. ---
--- 80’ Substitution Nacho Monreal is done for the day. T. Vermaelen is his replacement. ---
(80’) Mel does change things. He brings on 'super sub' Anichebe for the final few moments. Wenger also makes his final change as Vermaelen is on for Monreal.
(78’) Just over ten minutes to go and we've still seen just the one goal. Arsenal look quite happy with their lot. It's up to Mel to change things around if West Brom want to take something from this.
(76’) POST! Arsenal really should have this one wrapped up. A lovely move down the left sees Ozil cut the ball back into the area. It falls behind everyone but a poor touch from a WBA defender puts the ball in the path of Podolski, whose sliced half-volley comes off the post before hitting Foster on the shoulder.
(74’) A great opportunity for Ozil to wrap this game up! He dances his way into the area but he can't get his shot on target as it slithers wide of the far post.
(72’) Craig Dawson sends a looping header over the bar from yet another WBA corner. It wasn't a clear cut chance but that Arsenal defence does look to be creaking, just a little bit.
--- 70’ Substitution Cazorla is replaced with T. Rosický. ---
(70’) Arsenal make their second change of the game as Cazorla comes off and on comes Rosicky. Meanwhile Szczesny collects a weak free kick from WBA.
(68’) This a good little spell for WBA. They've forced a number of corners in quick succession and have Arsenal on the back foot. The only thing they haven't done is create a clear opening.
(66’) A great low cross from Brunt on the left tries to pick out Berahino. Mertesacker has to get his tackle perfect to put the ball behind for a corner, and he does.
--- 64’ Yellow card Nacho Monreal goes into the referee's book. ---
(64’) First substitution of the game as Kim Kallstrom comes on for Arteta. Moments later Monreal picks up the first booking of the match for blatantly pulling back Sessegnon right under Mike Jones' nose.
--- 63’ Substitution K. Källström enters the game and replaces Arteta. ---
(62’) Ozil is beginning to pull the strings now. He links up with Podolski whose cross is turned behind for yet another corner. Arsenal turning up the heat on WBA now.
(60’) Ozil has barely featured this afternoon for the home side but he gets involved here and delivers a great ball across the six-yard box that is missed by everyone.
(58’) The ball drops for Podolski in the WBA box but he just can't get the ball out from under his feet to test Foster. Giroud has the same problem when the ball breaks to him and he's crowded out by Baggies defenders.
(56’) A rash piece of defending from Monreal presents WBA with half a chance. The Spaniard dives in on the half-way line and Sessegnon skips away from him with ease. Sagna comes across and does well to quell the danger, preventing the former Sunderland man from picking out Berahino in the area.
(54’) Cazorla fires in a zipping low cross that is deflected behind for a corner. They've already scored from one set piece today but they can't add a second here as the visitors clear.
(52’) Arsenal are just stroking the ball around in the sun at the moment. West Brom aren't putting much pressure on the ball and that could spell trouble if they allow Wenger's side the freedom to look for that telling pass.
(50’) West Brom have a free kick inside the Arsenal half but it's easily cleared by the home side. They need to do better from those positions, especially when they are bringing up their big guns from the back.
(48’) Cazorla is almost in immediately but the ball trying to find him has just too much pace on it and the Spaniard can't quite get there. An early warning shot for West Brom.
(46’) Away we go then for the second period. Can Arsenal build on their first-half dominance?

HALF-TIME: ARSENAL 1-0 WEST BROM. The hosts lead at the break and they are good value for it. Giroud's header has set them on their way to celebrating fourth spot in style, but the Baggies are by no means out of this just yet.
(45’) We are into two minutes of added time now. Lugano's poor clearance finds Flamini on the edge of the box but Foster is able to hold his effort.
(44’) A few fouls have littered this first half and there are a couple of interesting match ups appearing. Flamini and Berahino have exchanged words on a couple of occasions now.
(42’) More desperate defending from WBA prevents Giroud from getting his shot away on the edge of the area. Their finding quite a bit of space Arsenal and the visitors are living dangerously.
(40’) Just five minutes until the break. It was a slow start to this one but the chances have picked up for both teams in the past few minutes.
(38’) A corner for West Brom delivers a real chance for Dawson. He rises unchallenged to meet the set piece but plants his header way over the bar. A poor effort.
(36’) Cazorla! The little Spaniard fires low and hard towards goal at the end of another flowing Arsenal move, but Foster is alert to get down and turn the ball behind.
(34’) An awful mistake from Monreal gives Berahino another shooting opportunity but his shot flies just over the bar. A few reminders for the hosts that WBA are still in this.

(28’) Flamini now has his shot blocked as Arsenal continue their search for a second. Dawson makes the brave challenge but it looks as though it may have winded him. We've stopped for a bit of treatment.

(24’) An audacious effort from Morrison attempts to catch Szczesny off his line from just inside the Arsenal half. He doesn't find the target, but the keeper may have been struggling if he did.
(22’) Dorrans has a cross blocked behind for a corner as Sagna gets across to stop it. The corner is met by Mulumbu but his knock-back can't find a team-mate.

(18’) Arsene Wenger is able to share a joke with his assistant on the bench. He's pretty happy with what he's seen so far.
(16’) Arsenal don't look content with just one and they're immediately back on the attack after going in front. This could get messy for Pepe Mel's side.
--- 14’ Assist The assist came from Cazorla. ---
--- 14’ Goal! GOOOAAALLL!!! GIROUD FOR ARSENAL!!! From the corner, Arsenal take the lead. Giroud has proven this season that he's lethal in the air and he shows his aerial prowess once more, meeting Cazorla's corner at the front post. ---
(13’) CHANCE! The ball breaks kindly to Cazorla on the edge of the area and his lethal strike looks goalbound - but a desperate block from Mulumbu sends the ball over the bar for a corner.
(11’) The home side are just beginning to turn the screw here. They've penned WBA back inside their own half and they can't get out!
(9’) A bright start this from both sides. Arsenal have another opportunity but Podolski's effort can't find the target.
(7’) Berahino has a real chance for WBA here as he's slipped in behind the Arsenal defence. He goes for goal instead of squaring it back across the box and Szczesny gets down well to save.

(3’) Arsenal enjoying some early possession as the Emirates gets uncharacteristically loud. Foster picks off Sagna's cross to bring to an end the first meaningful attack.
(1’) Away we go in the North London sunshine! It's a glorious day for football in the capital.
