(83’) Luiz fires a high ball towards the box and Ba goes up for it, but Turner beats the striker in the air to head clear. The Norwich centre-backs have been really impressive today - it's amazing to think they have the worst defensive record away from home in the league.
(82’) Ivanovic is riding his luck, to say the least, as he takes a massive handful of Redmond's shirt. The Norwich bench are all up saying the defender should be off for a second yellow, but the referee keeps his cards in his pockets.
(81’) It's a lovely delivery from the corner but Cahill and Terry are both unable to get something on it, and the visitors survive once more. We're inside the final 10 minutes, now, and a draw isn't particularly great for either side.
(80’) Willian floats a lovely ball across the box and Schurrle is there to meet it, firing a dangerous volley at goal which deflects behind off at least one Norwich defender, and the hosts have a corner.
(79’) HAZARD!! As soon as I say that, Hazard nearly makes me eat my words, as he picks the ball up on the edge of the box and evades three players before firing a low effort which Ruddy parries away. Torres it there to it first but his first-time reply is awful as it loops off his shin and well over.
(78’) To be honest, Chelsea don't look like scoring this afternoon. You could give them another 90 minutes and they'd probably struggle to find the net.
(77’) Whittaker finds Johnson with a lovely ball into midfield, before the visitors manage to spread it wide. They are forced backwards but still have the ball as they go forward in search of a priceless winner.
(76’) Hazard is spending a lot of time on the left and he does well to get past Snodgrass before firing in a low cross past Martin, but Bennett is again there to tidy up. He and Turner have been very solid so far today.
(75’) Willian and Johnson enjoy a little playground pushing in the middle of the pitch before Luiz decides to get involved. The Norwich man isn't too happy but he's the one penalised for the initial foul.
(74’) Norwich are growing in confidence here, and are starting to commit more men forward. They clearly feel this is there for the taking. Chelsea's pressure earlier in this half has just eased off for now.
--- 73’ Substitution N. Matić is done for the day. Fernando Torres is his replacement. ---
(73’) Fernando Torres is on for Matic as the Chelsea boss goes for it in these later stages. Meanwhile, Terry and Cahill have a little trouble coping with Redmond's quick pressing, but they manage to get it clear eventually.
(72’) That really would have been a shock - surely Mourinho won't have three home defeats in a row?
(71’) SNODGRASS!! WHAT A CHANCE!! Luiz loses the ball outside the Norwich box and the visitors break superbly. Redmond charges into the Chelsea half before setting Snodgrass away, but Cahill produces a magnificent challenge to deflect it behind just as the Norwich man lets fly. A vital block.
(70’) Nathan Redmond is on for Elmander for the final 20 minutes. Can he inspire an unlikely Norwich win? They're still on level terms, so you never know...
--- 69’ Substitution N. Redmond enters play, replacing J. Elmander. ---
(69’) WILLIAN!! A good chance wasted as Cole advances down the left before squaring inside to the Brazilian, who pushes it out of his feet and fires a shot way off target from a tight angle.
(68’) Hazard is popping up in some good positions this afternoon, and Cole squares it into the substitute, who manages to spread the ball out wide for Ivanovic, but it's another cross which is dealt with by the Norwich defence.
(67’) Matic has a rare effort at goal as Willian lays it off outside the box, but his first shot is blocked before the second deflects well wide for a corner. Schurrle fires it in low but Luiz hooks it high over the bar from the near post.
(66’) Schurrle charges down the left flank and looks to play a one-two with Hazard as he moves inside, but the Belgian's return pass it poor and Martin steps in to clear.
(65’) Matic is dispossessed by Whittaker but he and Willian work hard to win it back for the hosts. It's then played into Ba inside the box but the quality is again lacking as he can't hold it up for a team-mate, and Norwich are able to clear.
(64’) Elmander works hard to challenge Luiz, and the substitute produces a loose touch but is saved by the whistle as the referee spots a push by the Norwich striker.
(63’) Matic plays the ball forward to Schurrle, who steps inside before switching play out to Ivanovic. The defender fires in an early cross but Ba gets the wrong side of Turner before fouling the Norwich man, and it's a free kick.
(62’) Norwich relieve some more pressure but Howson is forced to give it away as he gets pinned on the touchline, and the hosts have possession once more. The tempo has definitely improved since the break, but we're still goalless.
(61’) Elmander does superbly to keep the ball in play on the far side, and Matic charges in to challenge the striker. It looks like he shoves the Swede on to the floor, and they all stop to look at the referee, but nothing is given and play goes on. Very strange!
--- 60’ Yellow card R. Bennett receives a yellow card. ---
(60’) Turns out it wasn't a booking for Hazard, after all, but actually for Ivanovic. The defender was a little exuberant in his protest to the referee. Meanwhile, Norwich get some respite as they win a throw near the corner flag inside Chelsea's half.
(59’) The relentless Chelsea pressure continues as Luiz slides the ball forward for Ba, who lays it back to Willian but the two of them are quickly closed down. Neither of those two have been particularly effective this afternoon.
--- 58’ Yellow card B. Ivanović is cautioned by the referee. ---
(58’) Well, replays show Hazard may have made quite a meal of that one and gone down before the contact. Looks like it might have been a very good call by the referee.
(57’) Ooh...big, BIG let-off for Norwich. Hazard goes down under Bennett's challenge in the box, but the referee books the Belgian for diving while the flag is also up for offside against Terry.
(56’) Norwich are struggling to get out of their own half at the moment, but the hosts are still producing some sloppy passes. They've had three quarters of the possession in this second half so far and it'll be hard for the Canaries to hold on at this rate.
(55’) Surprising moment from Luiz as he has some space outside the box but chooses not to shoot, instead spreading play wide. Hazard is on the left, now, and finds Cole on the overlap but the full-back's cross is headed away by Bennett.
(54’) Penalty? Appeals at the other end this time as Ivanovic plays the ball back to the edge of the box for Schurrle, who looks to get between Tettey and the ball. The Norwich man produces a clumsy looking challenge and the German goes down, but there's no whistle from the referee.
(53’) Martin floats the free kick towards the edge of the box and Turner gets up well to meet it, but his header loops up high and Schwarzer is able to come out and deal with the danger.
(52’) Snodgrass is down in pain after a challenge with Matic in midfield. It looks like the Chelsea man may have put a fair bit of his weight on the Scot's leg - he's not a small chap so that will have hurt.
(51’) Hazard is causing plenty of havoc here and he charges in from the right, giving Whittaker a lot to think about now. He plays the ball low into the six-yard box, but Schurrle fouls Bennett as he challenges for it.
(50’) Norwich are furious as they claim the use of the arm by Luiz to hold off Olsson, before the Brazilian is fouled by Howson on the touchline. He's getting involved quickly!
(49’) Ruddy was completely beaten, there. Encouraging signs for the Blues as the two changes almost have an immediate effect.
(48’) LUIZ HITS THE BAR!! Hazard is immediately involved as he moves the ball right before receiving it back. He lays it to Ivanovic inside the box and he rolls the ball into the path of Luiz, who smashes a first-time effort across goal and off the crossbar.
(47’) Schurrle loses out to Howson in midfield before he and Willian are penalised for a foul on the Norwich man. Chelsea win it back and Cole drives down the left-hand side before Johnson stops him in his tracks with a well-timed challenge.
--- 46’ Substitution F. Lampard is done for the day. David Luiz is his replacement. ---
--- 46’ Substitution Mohamed Salah is replaced with E. Hazard. ---
(46’) Norwich kick things off for the second half, and Hazard is indeed on for the hosts, as is David Luiz. Mourinho's not happy, clearly, and Salah and Lampard both give way.
It's almost time to get back underway at Stamford Bridge, and it sounds like Eden Hazard could be coming on for the hosts. Chelsea certainly need an injection of flair, and he could be just the man.
Can Chelsea break down the visitors? Or can Norwich take inspiration from Sunderland's win here and surprise Mourinho's side as well? We'll be back very soon with all the action from the second half.
Andre Schurrle has had the best chances of the half, hitting the post and testing Ruddy low down, but apart from that it's all been a bit lacklustre in the final third. This is another indication Mourinho needs to add more quality up front in the summer.
That's HALF TIME at Stamford Bridge and it's goalless after 45 minutes, with Chelsea seeing most of the ball but unable to do very much with it. Norwich are fairly comfortable at the moment but need to start pushing forward if they want to win this afternoon.
(45’) Chelsea keep passing it in front of the visitors, and Schurrle moves in from the left before producing a wayward pass out to Ivanovic which rolls out for a throw. Sums up the half, really.
(45’) Into the first of two added minutes and it looks like we'll be going in level at the break. Willian finds Schurrle on the left and the midfielder cuts on to his right foot before whipping a ball across the box, but Turner does well to head away.
(45’) Chelsea win a free kick on the right-hand side and Lampard whips it in from deep. Terry leaps to meet the delivery on the edge of the box, but can't generate enough power to either find the target or test Ruddy, and the goalkeeper collects easily.
(44’) Cahill advances into the Norwich half before finding Salah, who slides it into Willian. The midfielder tries to find Ivanovic out wide with a first-time pass, but it's poorly executed and rolls out for a throw.
(43’) Willian...oh dear. The Brazilian collects the ball on the left-hand corner of the box and charges along the edge of the area, before trying an effort which almost hits the corner flag. A forgettable one, to say the least.
(42’) Cahill plays it forward for Ba, who drops deep to collect before finding Salah. There's no-one running in, though, and the winger goes backwards as Norwich get time to find their shape once more.
(41’) JOHNSON!! Norwich nearly take a surprise lead as the midfielder picks the ball up 20 yards from goal, and looks to curl an effort into the corner. Terry and Cahill throw themselves at the ball and the shot deflects off the Chelsea captain before looping just wide of Schwarzer's post.
(40’) Five minutes to go until the break, and it's still very quiet inside Stamford Bridge. Schurrle has had two good chances but, for all their possession, Chelsea still haven't broken the deadlock.
(39’) Norwich aren't helping themselves, here, as another stray pass finds a blue shirt. Schurrle pushes down the right-hand side but Whittaker does well to hold the German off and win a goal kick.
(38’) Lovely stuff from Tettey, who gets out of a tight spot with some silky footwork to escape from two Chelsea players. He finds Turner, but the defender is quickly pressed and is forced to put it out of play.
(37’) Not one for the scrapbook, Ashley Cole. The full-back sees some space through the middle and charges forward before getting plenty of encouragement to shoot. He obliges, but hammers it straight into the stands from 30 yards.
(36’) Slightly comic moment as Snodgrass has to push the assistant referee out of the way to keep the ball in play. He lays back to Martin, who fires in a decent cross but Terry does well to head it out of harm's way.
(35’) SCHURRLE!! He's had Chelsea's best efforts so far, and tests Ruddy this time as he cuts in from the right and drives a low shot towards the near post, but the Norwich shot-stopper gets down well to hold on to it.
(34’) Bennett almost makes a catastrophic error as he gives it straight to Willian, who finds Ba on the left-hand edge of the box. The visitors find their shape well, though, and the striker's cross is easily cleared.
(33’) That was by far the best chance of the match, and it came as Norwich were caught in possession as they looked to break. When they get back in numbers they look very comfortable.
(32’) SCHURRLE OFF THE POST!! Chelsea so nearly in front!! Cole does brilliantly to win the ball in midfield before treading on it by accident, but Matic is there to tidy up and finds Schurrle with a lovely pass down the left. With Martin committed forward he has a chance to cut inside the box before curling a shot around Ruddy, but only on to the far post and out.
(31’) Ivanovic's cross from the right is well cleared by Turner, but Chelsea still have the ball inside the Norwich half. Salah pushes the ball into Ba and darts into the area, while the striker turns and tries to fire it across goal, but it deflects behind for a corner.
(30’) Half an hour gone, then, and it's all been pretty comfortable defensively for Norwich. Chelsea have seen so much of the ball but a lot of the play is in front of their opponents. The movement looks a little stale, to be honest.
(29’) Ivanovic sprays the ball across the pitch for Schurrle, who has drifted over to the left-hand side. Snodgrass gets back well to help Martin, and Schurrle can't find a way through the two of them as the defender hacks it clear.
(27’) Matic looks for the late run of Cole with a delicate chip over the top, but it just skips off the Stamford Bridge surface and rolls out for a goal kick. Chelsea are struggling to get in behind the visitors at the moment.
(26’) Salah and Willian move around well before the latter charges to the byeline on the left-hand edge of the box, but his cross has far too much pace in it and the visitors have a throw.
(25’) Good pressing from Norwich as Tettey closes down Matic, forcing the Serbian to put it out of play for a throw. Neil Adams will be pretty happy with the way they've held Chelsea at bay so far, and they've even had the odd moment in and around the Blues' box.
(24’) The Canaries win a throw deep inside the Chelsea half and Bennett launches it high into the box. Schwarzer can't quite get there but it rolls out of the area before Johnson shoves Willian near the corner flag.
(23’) TERRY!! Schurrle receives the ball out wide and tries to get past Whittaker, but the defender stands his ground and the German's cross deflects behind for a corner. Schurrle then swings in the set piece and Terry gets above Turner to meet it six yards out, but his header is straight at Ruddy. A very good chance goes begging.
(22’) It's fairly quiet inside Stamford Bridge at the moment, probably because there hasn't been too much to get excited about so far. Chelsea are staying patient, though, and continue to move it aroud in front of the visitors.
(21’) Willian plays a decent reverse pass to Ba just inside the box, and the striker looks to play Cole in behind, but his pass is not good enough and rolls out for a goal kick. He's been slightly disappointing with the ball at his feet so far.
(20’) Tettey spreads the ball wide to Martin before Johnson finds Olsson out wide. The midfielder carries on his run and his Swedish team-mate fires in a very dangerous cross, but it just skips through as no-one is able to make contact.
(19’) Chelsea have had 65 per cent possession so far, but haven't had a shot at goal since Schurrle's early effort. There's a distinct end-of-season feel to proceedings so far - a goal would certainly liven things up.
(18’) Salah tries to up the tempo as he moves down the left and looks to fire a ball into the box, but it's not good enough and the visitors are able to deal with it comfortably.
(17’) Most of the play is inside the Norwich half at the moment - it could be a lonely afternoon for Mark Schwarzer. Mourinho's men have struggled to break teams down in similar situations this season...
(16’) Chelsea are still moving the ball around and slowly probing - they're in no hurry this afternoon. Ba lays off for Salah but Martin does well to stay with them and win the ball before hacking it clear. The hosts are quickly back in possession, though.
(15’) Norwich move into the Chelsea half once more but Johnson's ball into the middle is poor and the hosts break. Willian runs too far but Bennett's challenge deflects off the Brazilian into Ba's path. The striker's pass into the middle, though, is very poor and Ruddy has plenty of time to gather.
(13’) Chelsea are having to take the initiative in terms of possession today, rather than last week at Liverpool when they soaked up huge amounts of pressure. Willian looks for Salah with an ambitious diagonal ball over the top, but it just evades the winger and runs out for a goal kick.
(12’) It's a lucky escape for the Blues, and they've managed to wrestle possession back once more. Willian and Cole link up well on the left before the full-back fires a dangerous low ball into the six-yard box, but Ba can't quite get there and Ruddy gratefully receives it into his chest.
(11’) Penalty? Johnson slides a wonderful pass between Cole and Terry, and Olsson is on to it like a flash. Both defenders slide in and the Norwich man goes down as Schwarzer gathers the ball off his heavy touch. The visitors want a penalty but nothing is given - would that have been given had it been a Chelsea man at the other end?
(10’) The visitors are forced all the way back to Ruddy but Johnson battles hard to win the ball off Terry's initial header. The midfielder then misjudges a pass out wide as he plays it straight out for a throw to Chelsea.
(9’) Norwich finally manage to string more than three passes together as they edge into the Chelsea half. Elmander spreads the ball wide to Martin, and this is more encouraging from the Canaries.
(8’) The hosts are dominating possession early on, here, and winning it back quickly whenever they lose the ball. Willian finds a pocket of space in the middle and looks for Ba with a ball beyond the defence, but Martin gets across well to cover and intercept.
(7’) Ba is now remonstrating with the referee, claiming foul play from the Norwich defender, but he won't get anything for it and the hosts have a corner. Lampard's delivery is easily dealt with before Ba is caught offside as he returns to the action.
(6’) Ba is down receiving treatment at the moment, and he looks pretty uncomfortable. It looks like he clashed with Turner as he charged into the box to meet Cole's attempted cross.
(5’) Whittaker tries to get forward along the left-hand side, but Ivanovic stands firm to win possession back for the Blues. It's spread to the other flank and Cole produces a lovely driving run down the wing. He holds off Johnson and Martin before forcing a corner off the defender.
(4’) Norwich can't be officially relegated this afternoon, but their goal difference is far inferior to Sunderland's so defeat would pretty much confirm it. Meanwhile, Matic slides a lovely ball beyond the defence for Ba, but the striker can't get it under control and the visitors have a goal kick.
(3’) SCHURRLE!! Martin shoves Schurrle in the back as the German goes for a header and it's another early free kick. The hosts move play to the far side and the ball is fired in towards Ba, whose touch is heavy but it rolls into the path of Schurrle, and the midfielder fires a low shot straight at Ruddy.
(2’) Neil Adams is already having to shield his eyes - the sun is beaming down on to the near side of the pitch. Cole is clipped as he moves along the left flank and the hosts have a free kick, which they take short as they keep possession early on.
(1’) Chelsea get the ball rolling for the first half, and we're underway in the Premier League once more.
The players are out, and it's a beautiful sunny afternoon in west London. We're just a few minutes away from kick-off at Stamford Bridge.
Adams' men, meanwhile, are enduring a terrible run of form away from Carrow Road, having lost eight consecutive Premier League games on the road. They've also scored just 11 away goals and conceded 44 - both records are the worst in the top flight.
The Blues have had a tough week, having crashed out of the Champions League at the hands of Atletico Madrid. The good news for Mourinho's men, though, is their record after European matches is superb - they've won 11 and drawn one of the 12 games which have come after a midweek Champions League match.
Neil Adams makes three changes from the 4-0 defeat at Manchester United - their fifth league loss in a row - as Ryan Bennett, Alexander Tettey and Johan Elmander replace Leroy Fer, Nathan Redmond and Ricky van Wolfswinkel.
Eden Hazard is on the Chelsea bench this afternoon, then, as Mohamed Salah, Willian and Andre Schurrle make up the midfield. Nemanja Matic returns after being cup-tied for their Champions League tie, while John Terry is back in defence after missing last weekend's win at Liverpool.
Norwich subs: Bunn, Bassong, Van Wolfswinkel, Fer, Hooper, E Bennett, Redmond.
Norwich (4-1-4-1): Ruddy; Martin, R Bennett, Turner, Whittaker; Tettey; Snodgrass, Johnson, Howson, Olsson; Elmander.
Chelsea subs: Hilario, Kalas, D Luiz, Van Ginkel, Hazard, Torres, Eto'o.
Chelsea (4-2-3-1): Schwarzer; Ivanovic, Cahill, Terry, Cole; Lampard, Matic; Salah, Willian, Schurrle; Ba.
The teams have been announced so let's bring you today's line-ups, starting with the hosts...
Hello and welcome to LIVE coverage of the Premier League as Chelsea host Norwich in a massive game that affects both ends of the table. Jose Mourinho's men need a win to keep their faint title hopes alive, while the Canaries have to avoid defeat or they will be effectively relegated this afternoon.

Well, what a match that was. I hope you enjoyed the action, but if you're a Liverpool fan then I would expect you didn't. Farewell.
(90’) FULL-TIME! What a match we have just witnessed at Selhurst Park and that could have absolutely massive consequences in the title race. Liverpool looked unstoppable as they marched into a three-goal lead and had one eye on Man City's goal-difference lead. Palace had other things in mind, however, and they raced back to steal a point and a 3-3 draw. Liverpool could not see the win out and although they go one point clear at the top, the title is Manchester City's to lose now. A truly disastrous night for Liverpool in London as the Premier League crown looks set to stay in Manchester for another year.
(90’) Huge chance for Liverpool!! Palace fail to clear Gerrard's corner properly and Coutinho chips it back into the danger area. Once again the hosts make a mess of getting it away and Moses has an open goal to aim at, but under pressure, he completely misses his kick.
(90’) Gayle - chasing a hat-trick - is causing Liverpool problems again. This time, however, he can only send his left-footed effort harmlessly-wide of Mignolet's left-hand post.
(90’) Five minutes of stoppage time will be played. You could see both sides scoring again before this ends!
(90’) Danger at the other end, meanwhile! Coutinho cuts inside from the left and sends a stinging drive in towards Speroni, who fails to catch the ball and has to nervously parry back into the danger area.
--- 88’ Assist G. Murray gave the assist. ---
--- 88’ Goal! GOAL!!!! PALACE DRAW LEVEL!! What a second-half performance from Palace! Murray produces an exquisite pass into the area for Gayle following a lofted pass from the back and the former Arsenal trainee pokes past Mignolet. He has been simply sensational since coming on. ---
--- 86’ Substitution V. Moses enters play, replacing D. Sturridge. ---
(86’) Palace take the corner quickly and Bolasie dazzles the Liverpool defence with his twinkle-toes, but his final ball into the area is agonisingly too far ahead of Gayle.
(86’) The free-kick drops kindly for the impressive Gayle, but his first touch is a little heavy and he ends up having to settle for a corner. This is all Palace now.
--- 85’ Substitution T. Ince enters the game and replaces K. Dikgacoi. ---
(85’) While Palace wait to take their free-kick, former Liverpool man Thomas Ince comes on for Pulis' men.
(83’) What a finish we could be in store for here! Palace are really pushing for a point now and Liverpool and clinging on. A corner goes begging for the hosts, but they now have a free-kick in an advanced position on the right.
--- 81’ Assist Y. Bolasie gave the assist. ---
--- 81’ Goal! GOAL!!! Palace get another!! What brilliant play by Bolasie as he picks the ball up on the edge of his own area, races away from his marker and then charges past Johnson. The Congolese winger eventually gets all the way into the visitors box and cuts a pass back to Gayle, who guides a lovely finish into the bottom-right corner. Game on! ---
--- 79’ Assist M. Jedinak gave the assist. ---
--- 79’ Goal! GOAL!!! Palace pull one back! Centre-back Delaney finds himself in an usual position; right outside Liverpool's area. The defender receives a pass from Jedinak and then sees his long-range effort deflected into the top corner off Johnson. ---
--- 78’ Substitution R. Sterling is replaced with Philippe Coutinho. ---
(76’) Big block by Dann! Sturridge finds himself one-on-one with a defender in the area, but instead of going for goal, he produces a stepover and tees up Sterling. Dann, however, gets in the way of the winger's eventual shot.
(75’) Liverpool nearly craft another opening as Suarez poked a pass through to Sturridge, who could see Sterling charging into the area. However, the former Man City man stumbled just when he looked set to find the pass.
(73’) Lovely footwork by Bolasie as he produces a nutmeg before jinking past Gerrard and crossing, but the delivery is a little too heavy and it sails all the way through to the left flank.
--- 71’ Substitution M. Chamakh is done for the day. G. Murray is his replacement. ---
(71’) Chamakh has run his race as Glenn Murray - Palace's top-scorer in their promotion campaign last season - replaces him with just under 20 minutes to go.
(69’) Brief moment of danger for Liverpool as Mariappa rides a challenge from Flanagan and gets into a good position to cross. His delivery is played back towards the edge of the area, but Liverpool cut it out before a Palace man can get on the end of it.
--- 67’ Yellow card S. Dann receives a yellow card. ---
(67’) Clever play by Johnson as he charges in from the right, skips past two challenges and then sees his left-footed effort palmed over by Speroni. He has scored those before!
--- 65’ Substitution J. Puncheon is done for the day. D. Gayle is his replacement. ---
(65’) Palace appear to have quietened Liverpool a little in the last few minutes, but you can bet that the visitors' urgency will be back rather sharpish if they truly are intent of getting as close as possible to City's goal-difference lead.
--- 63’ Yellow card M. Škrtel is cautioned by the referee. ---
(63’) Skrtel unfairly brings Chamakh down in a bruising clash. The Slovakian finally gets himself a yellow card, following numerous earlier offences.
(62’) Few would claim this match does not look a foregone conclusion now, but by how many goals can Liverpool win? Before the match their goal difference was nine worse than Man City's, but they still have a few more to get!
(60’) The visitors threaten again as Johnson comes inside from the right, evading challenges to good effect before sliding a clever pass into the area for Suarez. The forward manages to skip around Ward, but the defender manages to force Suarez out of play.
(58’) Liverpool are throwing everyone forward at the moment and shooting on sight as they look to cut Manchester City's goal difference lead. Suarez and Sturridge have both tried their luck again, but to no avail.
(56’) That was Suarez's 31st Premier League goal of the season, taking him level with Cristiano Ronaldo and Alan Shearer for the division's record haul. One more and it is all his.
--- 55’ Assist R. Sterling gave the assist. ---
--- 55’ Goal! Liverpool score a goal through L. Suárez! ---
(55’) GOAL!!! And there is number three for Liverpool! Suarez burst towards the penalty area, played Sterling in to his left and then received a return pass before squeezing a shot past Speroni.
--- 53’ Assist S. Gerrard gave the assist. ---
--- 53’ Goal! Goal to Liverpool, scored by D. Sturridge! ---
(53’) GOAL!!! Liverpool double their lead! Just a few moments after being agonisingly denied by the Speroni-post combination, Sturridge cuts across the edge of the penalty area and sees a left-footed effort deflected past Speroni.
(52’) What a save by Speroni! Sterling, cutting in from the left, picks out Sturridge just outside the Palace area and the former Chelsea man takes a touch, before curling a shot towards the left side of the goal, but Speroni tips it on to the post and Suarez blazes the rebound over.
--- 50’ Yellow card L. Suárez receives a yellow card. ---
(50’) Suarez is apoplectic with the decision not to give him a penalty there and Clattenburg gives him a yellow card for his incessant protesting.
(49’) More penalty claims for Liverpool. Suarez picks up possession in a deep position and charges towards the area. He lays the ball into the area for Sturridge and then looks to complete a one-two with his team-mate, but Scott Dann cynically blocks him off. Palace are lucky there.
(48’) Back down the other end, Bolasie is causing trouble again. He holds off Lucas, cuts inside Johnson and then charges into the area, but Skrtel is there to cover for his team-mates.
(47’) Good start for Liverpool as Sturridge marches down the right and gets in behind Delaney. The defender produces a good tackle to halt the forward, but Liverpool are adamant that they should have a corner.
(46’) The teams are back underway for the second half.
HALF-TIME! Clattenburg blows his whistle to end an entertaining and well-contested first half at Selhurst Park. Liverpool go into the break with a slender 1-0 lead thanks to Allen's first Premier League goal for the club and the title-hopefuls could have added a few more. However, for all their attacking potential, Liverpool have also looked troubled at the back on occasion and Palace could just have easily taken a draw into half-time. Liverpool will be pleased, but they may have to be more clinical after the break if they wish to go back to the Premier League's summit.
(45’) Two minutes of added time will be played here.
(45’) Liverpool are finishing the first half very strongly and Allen finds himself presented with another chance after a well-worked move sees Suarez cutting a pass back to the Welshman. However, the ex-Swansea City youngster skews his effort high and wide.
(43’) Good stop by Speroni! Allen plays Suarez into the left side of the area and although the pass is a little heavy, the Uruguayan gets to it in time. The former Ajax man moves back away from goal and back out to the left in order to give himself space and then tries an audacious attempt from that uninviting angle. It looks to be heading in, but Speroni does well to get down and palm it away.
(41’) Palace get themselves momentary respite as Chamakh looks to bring a lofted pass down just inside the Liverpool half, but finds himself clattered from behind by Skrtel, who claims he was looking for the ball.
(39’) Following a promising few minutes for Palace, Liverpool appear to have regained their focus and control of the ball. The visitors do look dangerous on almost every attack, but Palace have posed problems on the break.
(37’) Brilliant play by Sterling down the right as he cleverly knocks the ball inside, beating Ward and skipping into the area. The England winger cuts the ball back towards Suarez, but he sees his eventual shot go well over as he could only reach it while stretching.
(36’) Palace's corner comes to nothing as Mignolet impresses again, this time with a commanding punch clear. Liverpool race away with the ball as another counterattack beckons.
(35’) Mignolet again! Palace are growing in belief here once again and their captain is the latest to test Liverpool's keeper. Jediank is presented with significant space 25 yards from goal and unleashes a fierce drive which looks destined for the net, but Mignolet tips it over the crossbar in acrobatic fashion.
(33’) Great save by Mignolet! Palace find themselves invited forward by Liverpool and Puncheon drives a low effort towards the bottom-right corner from 20 yards, but the Belgian goalkeeper palms it away.
(31’) Wonderful effort by Suarez! The Player of the Year victor tries to curl a vicious shot into Speroni's top-left corner, but it flies just wide. Admirable effort either way.
--- 30’ Yellow card A. Mariappa receives a yellow card. ---
(30’) Mariappa is the latest player to go into the book for a cynical foul on Suarez, and the Uruguayan - who appeared to be unwell before kick-off - steps up to take the free-kick himself.
(29’) Ever since that promising opening 10 minutes or so, Palace have retreated into their shell a little. The areas in which they looked threatening - on the flanks - have since been deserted.
(27’) Liverpool's counter bodes well until they reach the Palace penalty area and Dikgacoi is there to mop up, just about. The South African almost got caught out himself, but he hurriedly booted the ball out of play.
(26’) Palace clip the free-kick to towards the back post, where it seems several of their men are waiting. However, the laboured delivery is dealt with easily by Liverpool, who attempt to spring a quick counterattack.
--- 25’ Yellow card J. Allen goes into the referee's book. ---
(25’) Goal-scorer Allen finds himself in the book now. Suarez played him into a bothersome situation with a poor pass in his own half and the Welsh midfielder stretched to steal possession back, fouling Ledley in the process.
(23’) Stoppage in play now as Skrtel and Delaney seek medical attention for an accidental clash off the ball in the middle of the pitch. Both look as though they will be fine, however.
(22’) Liverpool look to have crafted another glorious opening as Flanagan collects a long ball in the area and squares it to Suarez, but the assistant has his flag up for offside.
(20’) That was Allen's first goal for Liverpool in his 50th appearance. Prolific.
--- 18’ Assist S. Gerrard gave the assist. ---
--- 18’ Goal! GOAL!!!! Liverpool take the lead at Selhurst Park! Gerrard's corner once again travels towards the far post and the unmarked Allen shows great composure to head it back across goal and into the goal. ---
(17’) Liverpool's dominance seems to have gone up a notch in the last few minutes. Sterling does well as he comes in from the right and lashes a left-footed goal towards goal, but it is deflected just past the post. Corner.
(16’) Great chance for Liverpool! Allen produced a fine driven pass over the Palace defence and just inside Bolasie, which Johnson duly latched on to. The full-back meets it with a header, but he agonisingly puts it over the bar, with Speroni in no-man's land.
(15’) Palace steal the ball back with Liverpool trying to take control and Jedinak looks straight to the left wing with a lofted pass. That should highlight their game plan, with Bolasie very nearly getting on the end of that.
(14’) Liverpool are enjoying what is probably their first significant spell of possession, but Palace are holding firm at the moment, with everyone but Chamakh back in the defensive third.
(12’) Unsurprisingly, Liverpool are looking to dictate possession here so far, but Palace are proving to be a troublesome opponent. The home side are looking particularly dangerous down the flanks and on the break.
(10’) Mile Jedinak's corner - like Gerrard's before - sails through towards the back post and almost goes straight out of play, but Wards manages to get his head on the end of it and subsequently puts the ball into the side netting.
(9’) Not for the first time, Puncheon troubles Liverpool down the right wing. He wins a corner for the hosts, who are ensuring their visitors have a battle on their hands.
(8’) Great chance for Liverpool! Gerrard's corner is a good one and finds its way all the way towards the back post, but Sakho nods wide. He'll be kicking himself for not at least getting that on target.
(7’) Tentative Liverpool penalty claims turned down! Johnson latched on to a pass into the area and went down after Bolasie swung for the ball and missed. Referee Mark Clattenburg ignored the claims, however, and Liverpool must settle for a corner as Speroni blocks Suarez's cross.
(6’) Palace are straight back down the other end, however. Chamakh does well to hold up play and poke a pass in towards the danger area for Puncheon, but the winger's eventual right-footed effort is extremely tame as he slices wide.
(5’) Liverpool create their first opening of the match. Unsurprisingly Suarez is involved as he manages to get in down the left side of the Palace defence, but his low left-footed cross is hacked away.
(4’) Bolasie is enjoying a lively opening. On this occasion the rapid winger chips the ball past Lucas before attempting to collect it himself, but Gerrard covered well.
(3’) Threatening play again by the hosts. This time Palace get forward down the right and Puncheon crosses towards the edge of the area. Chamakh tries to cushion the ball down for a team-mate, but the touch is very heavy.
(2’) Encouraging start by the hosts as Bolasie finds space on the left before clipping an inviting cross into the centre for Chamakh, but Sakho intercepts with a crucial header.
(1’) Off we go! Liverpool get the action started at Selhurst Park.
The players are now out on the pitch as kick-off approaches. A Liverpool win guarantees them at least a second-place finish, while Palace look to give their fans something to shout about in their final home game of the season.
For Palace, though, things are a little different today. While Liverpool have title aspirations, Palace are already safe and will be celebrating their final home match of the season knowing that they will be back in the Premier League next year. How many of you predicted that when Ian Holloway was still in charge?
Of course, all eyes will be on Liverpool tonight as they look to make first place their own once again. Brendan Rodgers' men go into this fixture level on 80 points with Manchester City, who sit top due to their goal difference being nine better than the Anfield club's. Victory at Selhurst today will put the pressure back on City ahead of their home match against Aston Villa on Wednesday.

FULL-TIME: Southampton 2-0 Everton. Two own-goals could prove a fatal blow, and a self-inflicted one at that, to the Toffees' Champions League aspirations as the Saints showed the fire is still burning bright in their season, despite having little to play for. Antolin Alcaraz put through his own net with barely a minute on the board in a nightmre start and it failed to get better for Roberto Martinez and his side as Seamus Coleman unwittingly turned home past Tim Howard to give the Toffees a mountain to climb. They had a second-half penalty shout through Leon Osman turned down but the Saints were well worth their three points.
(90’) Everton also make a change as Luke Garbutt comes on for Baines but it is Southampton who almost grab a third through a sub of their own in Ward-Prowse, his powerful drive, however, is parried aside by Howard.
--- 90’ Substitution L. Garbutt enters play, replacing L. Baines. ---
--- 90’ Substitution S. Davis is replaced with Guly. ---
(90’) Substitute Harrison Reed skips past the abysmal Alcaraz and almost provides a telling cross, but the ball had already gone out of play. Pochettino takes the chance to make his side's final change by bringing on Guly Do Prado for the diligent Davis.
(88’) Southampton are content to stroke the ball around the St Mary's turf and Everton fans are beginning to filter out of the ground. They know the game is up and perhaps even their top four hopes after an insipid display.
--- 86’ Substitution A. Lallana is replaced with H. Reed. ---
(86’) Lallana goes off to a standing ovation after being at his instrumental best this afternoon and Pochettino is quick to congratulate him as he leaves the field. Another tremendous afternoon for the Saints.
(84’) Clever footwork from Lallana and intelligent movement from Lambert almost combines to fashion a shooting chance but the Everton defence do well to get rid of the loose ball.
(82’) PENALTY?! Everton want another spot-kick but this one looks slightly less clear-cut on first evidence as Lovren and McCarthy become embroiled in a tussle near the byline. Oliver is once again not impressed.
(80’) Baines is caught offside as Everton reload after the corner is cleared. The Toffees have had a lot of joy down this near side in the second half but Clyne did well to get out in time there.
(78’) Baines gets in down the left but his cross is easily cut out by Jack Cork, even though it comes at the expense of a corner from a Southampton perspective.
--- 76’ Substitution J. Ward-Prowse enters the game and replaces S. Gallagher. ---
(76’) Mauricio Pochettino makes his first substitution by bringing on Ward-Prowse for Gallagher as he looks to boost his midfield numbers and fend off Everton's increased pressure.
(74’) CLOSE! Everton almost find a route back into the game in the most bizarre of circumstances as Baines' floated cross to the far post gets caught in the wind and deceives Boruc, who can only stand and watch as the ball drops just wide.
(72’) PENALTY?! Davis threads through an intricate pass into the path of Lallana, who latches onto it and attempts to cut inside Stones, with the ball hitting the Everton defender on the arm for the third time today. Once again, however, Oliver dismisses the claims.
(70’) Lukaku hurdles a couple of feeble Southampton challenges before letting fly from long range, but the shot is deflected away and the Saints survive.
(68’) Signs that Everton are cranking the pressure up a notch on their hosts now, with Baines and McGeady combining neatly on the left regularly now.
(66’) Lambert is the latest to be mystified by the referee's actions as he decides Alcaraz's challenge on the Saints striker was a fair one, despite Lambert appearing to be blocked off as he bore down on goal.
(64’) CHANCE! What an opening for Everton, who really ought to have been back in it there. McGeady does superbly to evade Clyne's attentions on the left and his cross is even better, but the rangy frontman can only manage to direct his powerful header straight at a thankful Boruc in the Southampton goal.
--- 62’ Yellow card L. Osman is yellow-carded. ---
(62’) PENALTY?! Everton look to have been done an injustice as Osman is accused of diving by Michael Oliver despite there appearing to be a rash challenge from Lovren on the substitute in the penalty area. Osman had run off of the central defender on the left-hand side of the area but was scythed down by the Croat only to see a yellow card brandished in his direction.
(60’) POST! Lambert goes so close to a third for the Saints and that surely would have killed off an Everton fightback. The home side win a free-kick 25 yards from goal and Lambert steps up to bend an effort onto the outside of the upright. The visitors have brought on Aiden McGeady in the meantime for Deulofeu.
--- 58’ Substitution Gerard Deulofeu is replaced with A. McGeady. ---
(58’) Lallana cuts inside Coleman but can only lash a powerful strike away from goal and it veers well wide, ending up closer to the corner flag then the far corner of Howard's net.
(56’) Southampton continue to control the possession and the general flow of the game and almost engineer an opening after clever interplay from Shaw and Lambert, but Lallana cannot quite read the latter's dummy and Everton clear.
(54’) Deulofeu tests the Saints rearguard with two whipped crosses from set plays but a deflected Naismith strike aside, there was precious little to worry a well-drilled home defence. Mauricio Pochettino will be delighted with his side's performance so far.
(52’) The home side remain largely in the ascendency here and Shaw's teasing cross has to be clutched close to his chest by Howard with Lambert and Gallagher lurking.
(50’) Gallagher tries to lead the Southampton counter after Everton had built a head of steam upfield and the youngster does well to win a corner from Alcaraz's challenge but the set piece fails to test the Everton backline.
(48’) The quiet James McCarthy brings down Lallana in midfield but the free-kick is wasted as Clyne miscontrols the ball on the right wing. Moments later, Southampton benefit from a kind offside decision as Deulofeu nips in behind Shaw but is adjudged to have strayed beyond the fortunate left-back.
--- 46’ Substitution L. Osman enters play, replacing R. Barkley. ---
(46’) Southampton get the ball rolling once more and we are back underway for the second half, a huge one for Everton, who surely need at least a point here. Martinez has shuffled his pack by bringing on Osman for the peripheral Barkley.
HALF-TIME: Southampton 2-0 Everton. It has been a terrible first half for the Champions League-chasing Toffees, who have been undone by two comical own-goals at St Mary's. Barely a minute had been played when Alcaraz nodded Lambert's clipped centre into his own net before Coleman turned home Clyne's cross beyond a bewildered Tim Howard in the Everton goal. Martinez's side need a minor miracle now to keep their top four hopes alive.
--- 45’ Yellow card G. Barry is cautioned by the referee. ---
(45’) Gareth Barry receives the first booking of the contest after dwelling in possession in midfield before Saints striker Gallagher nipped in to rob him of the ball. Referee Oliver felt the challenge worthy of a yellow; Barry's 10th of the campaign.
(43’) A Coleman cross to the far post is not dealt with by Clyne and Deulofeu is able to seize on the loose ball, but his deflected cross is headed away by Shaw before Lukaku could pounce.
(41’) Lukaku drifts into an offside position and is duly flagged for his early run as the Toffees fail to build any sort of momentum to their attacks. A goal in before the interval, however, could alter this match in their favour.
(39’) CHANCE! Lukaku squanders Everton's first real opportunity of the game but it is a difficult chance as the Belgian tried to adjust his body to meet Deulofeu's stunning cross. Moments later the visitors avoid another penalty appeal as Lallana's cross hits Stones' arm but referee Oliver is not interested.
(37’) The Toffees win a corner after Coleman's ball in from a wide area is headed away by Dejan Lovren. Yet again though, the corner fails to find an Everton head and the Saints can clear upfield.
(35’) Everton trying to rally but the likes of Deulofeu, Lukaku and Barkley have not had any sort of tangible impact on the game and that will have to change if they are to get anything from a game which is slipping away from them.
(33’) Southampton fans are in good spirits and start a chorus of "Who needs Rodriguez, we've got your back four." Very apt but very damaging for Everton fans to hear after a nightmare start here.
--- 31’ Goal! GOAL! Southampton double their lead and Everton's aspirations of a top-four finish have just taken a huge dent here at St Mary's. Nathaniel Clyne gets at Baines and sends a flighted cross to the back post where Seamus Coleman is unable to get out of the way and can only divert a header past Tim Howard for Everton's second own-goal of the contest. ---
(29’) Baines whips in a devilish low free-kick into the danger area but a cluster of Southampton bodies are just about able to get the ball out of the penalty area.
(27’) Naismith is visibly struggling and Leon Osman begins a rather rigorous warm-up in the event the Scot has to be replaced.
(25’) Adam Lallana twists and turns on the edge of the area but his attempts to pick out Lambert on the far post prove futile as his dinked pass sails out of play.
(23’) Southampton continue to dominate the early stages here as we pass the midway point of the opening period. Everton are failing to offer any sort of riposte at this point, with Ross Barkley notably quiet.
(21’) CHANCE! Southampton go within inches of a second goal after some more wonderful work from Lambert on the left wing. The frontman peels wide again and brings Stones with him before slotting the ball across the area to an onrushing Steven Davis, but he swipes at his shot slightly and the ball fizzes wide of the far post.
(19’) Crisp passing from Southampton opens up some space just outside the area for Cork, who elects to shoot but can only curl the ball into the gloves of Howard before a Baines cross at the other end is caught by Boruc with Everton filling the box in search of an equaliser. It has been a breathless start here.
(17’) Naismith is pictured on the touchline writhing in agony after appearing to take a knock on his knee and will need to be attended to when the ball goes out of play.
(15’) Deulofeu skips into shooting range and plants a dipping effort on goal in the hope it might veer beyond Artur Boruc, but the Pole claims the ball easily.
(13’) Southampton are doing very well in their high-pressing game to try and unsettle an Everton side who have looked nervy and inhibited in the early stages. Can they recover to muster an equaliser?
(11’) Steven Naismith shows immaculate control to skip past Luke Shaw with his first touch but the Saints flyer is able to get back to put a block in and concede a corner. The subsequent set piece comes to nothing.
(9’) Deulofeu and Lukaku attempt to link up with a neat one-two on the near side but the latter's return pass is too heavy and rolls out of play for a goal kick to the home side.
(7’) Everton force a corner on the left flank but it comes to nothing, with the hosts able to clear with relative ease from the near-post delivery.
(5’) PENALTY?! The Saints want a spot-kick as they capitalise on early Everton nerves to steal in down the left, where Gallagher's low shot appears to strike John Stones on the arm, but referee Michael Oliver is umoved by the protests.
(3’) Everton look shellshocked by a woeful opening to the game. The goal has been timed officially at 58 seconds and all eyes will now be on the Paraguayan defender. His last start for the Toffees? A 4-0 drubbing in the Merseyside derby at Liverpool.
--- 1’ Goal! GOAL! Southampton take the lead after just a minute as Alcaraz, in for the injured Distin today, nods into his own goal. A swift Saints counter leads to Lambert pulling clear on the left and clipping a cross into the near post where, under pressure from Gallagher, the central defender nodded past the stunned Howard into the bottom corner. Awful start for Everton. ---

So that's that. FULHAM 2-2 HULL CITY.Thank you, and I hope you enjoyed joining me, Alex Stewart, for this LIVE coverage of this match. Have a great rest of the weekend. Until next time...
Hull City will be relieved that they came back so strongly. A point is not enough to guarantee them safety either, but two goals from their two strikers will leave them purring ahead of the final few Premier League games and the FA Cup Final.
Fulham will be exhausted by that encounter, mentally as well as physically. They can take heart from how well they attacked, but, as ever, their defence let them down. Shipping a two goal lead at home in a relegation battle is poor. One point doesn't do enough and it will go to the wire for the Cottagers.
There was also a decent penalty shout for Long in the first half, though he was offside, and Davies handled late on in the box but Fulham won nothing for that either.
But Fulham's relentless attacking and open formation meant that Hull could come back into it and they scored through Jelavic and Long after Steve Bruce had made his own changes to give Hull a more offensive complexion.
A superb goal from Dejagah and a lovely header from Amorebieta, who was excellent from start to finish, gave Fulham two goals in three minutes.
Caught your breath yet? It has finished 2-2. Fulham went into a 2-0 lead after bold, attacking changes from Felix Magath allowed them to attack with pace and purpose out wide.
(90’) Hull win a free kick deep into Fulham territory after that break after Fulham had thrown men forward. They don't take it though as the referee blows for full time! WHAT A MATCH THAT BECAME!
(90’) Long and Hangeland get annoyed at each other. Stockdale plays it long again with Hangeland up but Hull can break now. This is dangerous.
(90’) Heitinga sends Richardson free who tries to play in either Fulham striker, but Harper comes and claims. He sends it up and Jelavic is fouled with Long is a good position. There could have been advantage. The free kick comes to nothing.
(90’) Hull are stil going for it. Stockdale gathers a through ball and lumps it up towards Rodallega.
(89’) Fulham and Magath must be gutted. His changes forced Fulham into a lead but, paradoxically, that very attacking formation left them open to attack and with Diarra suffering, Hull capitalised.
(88’) After a drab first half this game has exploded.
--- 87’ Assist The assist came from S. Aluko. ---
--- 87’ Goal! GOAL FOR HULL! LONG! A good long cross from substitute Aluko gets over the heads of the Fulham defenders. Long is lurking and heads it down to prevent Stockdale from saving. Good, clever header to bring Hull level. What next?! ---
(87’) PENALTY SHOUT? Curtis Davies mistimes a jump and clearly handles the ball, preventing Bent from getting it in the box. Didn't seem deliberate, but these are the margins...
(85’) STOCKDALE SAVE! Boyd crosses and it comes to El Mohamady who hammers it low and hard from the right hand side. Stockdale plunges low and fast to his right and just tips it onto the post. Great keeping.
(84’) A rubbish corner from Fulham and Hull look to break, but Fulham scamper back and collect possession again. They throw themselves forward and, though Boyd intercepts and tries to break for Hull, it comes bakc to Fulham and they push forwards again. This is the pattern now.
(83’) From the corner, Fulham retain possession and ping it about. It is cleared by Hull but only for a throw-in. Bent wins another corner. This is decent from Fulham but they don't have much choice other than to attack.
--- 82’ Substitution Y. Sagbo enters the game and replaces D. Meyler. ---
(82’) Dejagah makes Davies looks a bit silly out wide then pushes the ball into the six yard box, winning a corner.
--- 81’ Substitution G. Boyd enters the game and replaces L. Rosenior. ---
(80’) Diarra sends Rodallega free with a beautiful pass. He crosses towards Dejagah but Harper sprawls and saves well. Bent fires the rebound wide. That is what Fulham need to do, but can they do it for ten plus minutes?
(79’) Hangeland tidies up after a heavy touch from Jelavic. The momentum, amazingly, has swung back towards Hull City. This I would not have forseen. Fulham really need to slow it down, but with Sidwell off and two strikers on, they are not built for that. Diarra is in trouble too and cannot come off.
(77’) ALUKO! Hits the cross-bar with a possibly deflected shot which left Stockdale stranded. It was from a fair way out too and the Fulham keeper looked leaden.
(76’) As Hull ready Sagbo and Boyd to throw more attackers on, Magath must be looking at his side and seeing that all the attacking ability he threw on to push the game is not going to close it down. Both sides will be throwing themselves foward.
(76’) This is going to be a bit bloody tense now.
--- 75’ Goal! JELAVIC! GOAL FOR HULL. Well that was messy. The ball cannons onto the bar from a Reither deflection which Stockdale saves. Jelavic is on hand to head the ball in with the Fulham keeper on his backside. ---
(73’) Beautiful touch from Bent, high and over his shoulder, to flick the ball back inside to Rodallega. That was class. It didn't come to anything though.
(72’) Bent looks a bit rusty there. There was space for him to smash it with his left but he tries to turn Davies onto his right instead and his shot is blocked. He falls over. That could have been Fulham's third and two years ago, Bent would have buried it.
(71’) Heitinga is down, clutching his right ankle. Magath must be invoking whatever god he follows that none of his players get injured as they have no subs left.
(70’) Hull win it back from Amorebieta though, but give it away almost immediately. Bent whizzes forwards into space on the left but his cross is too close to Harper.
(69’) Hull are still a bit too patient and slow. Rodallega intercepts and Dejagah and Parker combine retain possession.
--- 67’ Substitution S. Aluko comes on for A. Bruce. ---
(67’) A long throw from Amorebieta is played back to him by Bent. He bends in a cross which evades everyone with Harper clearly in two minds.
(67’) Diarra is not moving well.
(66’) Alex Bruce is replaced by midfielder Sone Aluko. He's swift and snazzy and Hull will go to four at the back too, matching Fulham's formation better and giving themselves more in attack.
--- 65’ Yellow card M. Diarra receives a yellow card. ---
(64’) Huddlestone and Diarra square up in the centre of the pitch after Huddlestone seems to mistake Diarra staying down for feigning injury. Diarra does seem to be carrying a knock, so Huddlestone is being a bit of a prat. Diarra is booked.
(63’) Hangeland heads a corner onto Bent and it loops out for a Hull goal-kick.
(63’) Diarra is struggling now. Parker is a bit on his own in midfield now, but if Dejagah and Richardson can keep the ball out wide and play directly at Hull's wing-backs, it won't matter.
(61’) Jelavic wins a throw off Amorebieta and Myler sprays it wide. Hull are being patient here. Huddlestone through to Myler results in a corner, but Fulham break at real pace.
(60’) How can Hull get back into this? They have a little possession now and Livermore and Huddlestone look to get their foot on the ball a bit.

(58’) 2-0 to Fulham and in the space of three minutes this match is on its head. Magath has obviously done a job at half time, but energising his players and making astute changes which have transformed this game in his team's favour.
(56’) All the energy and momentum is with Fulham now and the crowd are up and shouting.
--- 55’ Goal! DEJAGAH! GOAL! Thank goodness for that. Dejagah collects after Rodallega stumbles over the ball and it breaks to the Iranian. He dummies right, drags it across the two Hull defenders with his left and hammers it in. That was really very lovely. ---
(54’) Hull have still not had a meaningful attack this half.

--- 71’ Substitution T. Cleverley is done for the day. J. Hernández is his replacement. ---
(71’) Ryan Giggs makes his final change, replacing Cleverley with Hernandez, as another striker is thrown into the fray. Rooney is going to drop into central midfield, allowing for Mata to play in the hole behind the Mexico international.
--- 69’ Substitution N. Redmond is done for the day. G. Hooper is his replacement. ---
(69’) MATA! Rooney floats a clever ball deep into the penalty area, with the Spaniard able to get a toe on the ball to try and poke it beyond Ruddy. The England goalkeeper is equal to the effort however. One of Adams' last rolls of the dice, as Redmond is replaced by out-and-out striker Gary Hooper.
(68’) Norwich really haven't put in a performance which will evoke any kind of optimism from their fans, as they're essentially being beaten without so much as a whimper. Elmander has done nothing since coming on, but the visitors' lack of striking presence surely has to come from the collective not performing well.
(66’) JOHNSON! Another former Leeds man has a go from range, but drags his effort narrowly wide of the post with De Gea scrambling across. Meanwhile, Snodgrass is busy claiming that Vidic tried to headbutt him off the ball. Lee Probert isn't interested.
--- 65’ Substitution S. Kagawa is replaced with A. Young. ---
(65’) Another change for Man United, as Young replaces Kagawa, giving the hosts a more orthodox option on the wing. Howson tries his luck from 20 yards, but Vidic makes a good block to deny the former Leeds midfielder.
--- 64’ Yellow card P. Evra goes into the referee's book. ---
--- 63’ Assist The assist came from P. Jones. ---
--- 63’ Goal! GOOOOOAL! JUAN MATA SCORES WITHIN MINUTES! Ruddy initially makes a good save to palm a Rooney effort out of the top corner, but Man United keep the move alive, with Jones putting in a good cross for Mata to turn home from close range! ---
(62’) Juan Mata is wearing a black armband this afternoon, as a mark of respect towards former Barcelona coach Tito Vilanova, who tragically passed away yesterday. With half an hour to go, the Spain international will be hoping to stamp his creativity on the remaining minutes.
--- 60’ Substitution Mata enters the game and replaces D. Welbeck. ---
(60’) Ryan Giggs makes his first substitution, with Welbeck replaced by Juan Mata. This could signal a change in formation, with Rooney left on his own up front and a trio of Kagawa, Mata and Valencia in behind him. Man United might just be looking to close things up slightly in midfield, given Norwich's middle three.
(59’) SNODGRASS! Two efforts from the Scotland international in quick succession, as De Gea beats a long-range free-kick attempt away from the danger zone, before collecting a cross from the same player. The Spaniard has looked solid whenever called upon.
(57’) Howson tries to flick a near post free-kick delivery towards goal, but it's easily claimed by De Gea, who hasn't a lot to do this evening. Norwich bring on Elmander to replace Van Wolfswinkel, with the Swede able to contribute more to all-round build up play.
--- 56’ Substitution R. van Wolfswinkel is done for the day. J. Elmander is his replacement. ---
(55’) ROONEY! The goalscorer receives possession 25 yards out from goal, before setting himself to shoot immediately, aiming for the same bottom right corner. Ruddy isn't to be beaten in the same way twice, collecting the England international's effort easily.
(54’) WELBECK! Good save from Ruddy! Evra sees a shot blocked, before the rebound falls kindly to Welbeck. He tries his luck on the half volley, but Ruddy is equal to it, conceding a corner in the process. Vidic is found at the back post, but the Serbia international's bullet header shaves the crossbar.
(53’) Martin makes a rather rash challenge to try to dispossess Valencia, after the winger exchanged a smart one-two with Welbeck. He doesn't make enough contact to merit a penalty for the hosts, however. United are stepping it up a gear now, that second goal is acting as a real catalyst.
(51’) Good covering from Whittaker! Kagawa breaks down the right hand side smartly, before squaring a pass back to the penalty spot in search of Valencia. The Ecuador international takes a touch to set himself from 12 yards, but Norwich's right-back makes an important challenge.
(50’) It's now looking very likely that Norwich are resigned to their fifth defeat in a row, with Adams perhaps needing to make a change sooner rather than later. Van Wolfswinkel has been a ghost up front, with Hooper lying in wait on the bench to replace the Dutchman.
--- 48’ Assist The assist came from S. Kagawa. ---
--- 48’ Goal! GOOOOOAL! ROONEY NETS UNITED'S SECOND! The England international sets his sights from 25 yards out, before firing a low drive into the bottom left hand corner, with Ruddy unable to palm it round the post! That's the start that the hosts would have wanted! ---
(46’) We're back underway for the second half, as Ryan Giggs looks to steer Man United towards victory in his first game in charge of the club. Norwich have suffered at the hands of a Rooney penalty, but still have some options on the bench to make things interesting.
The hosts have been lacking a bit of invention in the final third, but Ryan Giggs won't mind due to his side leading. Both respective coaches have 15 minutes to instil their ideas and share their criticism, with the spoils still up for grabs due to the mere one goal advantage for United.
HALF TIME! Man United head into the dressing room with a slender 1-0 lead, courtesy of a late penalty from Wayne Rooney. Norwich haven't troubled De Gea in the hosts' net, but are by no means out of this contest yet. The home side certainly aren't in full flow.
(45’) There's one minute of added time at the end of the first half.
(44’) Good goalkeeping from De Gea, who races off his line and punches a deep cross 20 yards clear of the penalty area. He's not had a lot to do, but the sign of a good goalkeeper is to remain alert.
(42’) The only question which the home fans are left asking, if how Whittaker didn't receive a red card for his challenge. It was a slightly soft one, but Whittaker appeared to prevent the England international from firing beyond Ruddy - surely a goalscoring opportunity?
--- 41’ Goal! GOOOOOAL! ROONEY CONVERTS THE PENALTY! They've had to wait, but finally Rooney has had a big impact on this game, sending Ruddy the wrong way and burying the ball in the bottom right corner. It was a comedy of errors from the Norwich defence to give it away, but Man United won't mind. ---
(40’) PENALTY FOR MAN UNITED! Fer, Martin and Turner miss a cross, leaving Whittaker at the back post to haul down Welbeck!
(40’) Smart stop by Ruddy! The England goalkeeper gets down smartly to his right to prevent a Valencia strike from zipping beyond him and into the far corner, with Whittaker able to hoof away the loose ball!
(39’) KAGAWA! Half chance for the attacking midfield, as he manages to turn a clever effort towards the near post from an impossible angle! It's off target, but slightly promising nonetheless.
(37’) De Gea has been a mere spectator from the start, with Ruddy called into action on occasion to lump a clearance upfield. A rather uninspiring performance from both sides, given their respective reasons for wanting to win this match.
(35’) Norwich are permitted to grow back into the game, with Redmond driving at Jones down the left. Jones stands up well to the English winger, with Valencia able to pick up the loose ball and drive out of defence. That said, the hosts' counter-attacks are just that little bit too slow.
(33’) Norwich are still sat in their shape, marshalling the midfield well and forcing United to play some inaccurate searching long balls. Retaining the ball hasn't been much of a test for the hosts, but penetrating advanced areas really has been.
(31’) Less than a quarter of an hour to go and the Red Devils are still looking a little bit short on ideas. Going forward, there's not been much quality forthcoming, with no testing deliveries for Martin or Turner to contend with.
--- 29’ Yellow card J. Howson gets yellow. ---
(29’) Howson is given the first booking of the game, sliding in somewhat rashly in an area of the field which didn't merit such a challenge. Man United have the upper hand, but Rooney hasn't seen much of the ball in dangerous areas, with Ruddy still only having one save to his name.
(27’) Man United have looked fairly comfortable during the opening half an hour, holding onto the ball well and getting the ball wide quickly. That said, with Kagawa tucking in from the left, the edge of the box is a little bit congested and Norwich are able to remain hard to play through.
(25’) Good interception by Turner! Jones finds himself in space on the right, offering Valencia an outlet and receives possession. The former Blackburn defender's cross is blocked excellently by Turner, who has started the game rather solidly.
(23’) KAGAWA! The former Dortmund man is found in a pocket of space in the box, before sidestepping to get beyond Martin, but the Japanese forward's eventual strike is blocked well by the covering Turner!
(21’) Kagawa receives the ball short from a corner, with the Japan international sizing up Redmond and bypassing the winger, before being outmuscled slightly by the former Birmingham man. Norwich win a goal kick and the Red Devils' pressure subsides.
(19’) The crowd claim for handball, but the players don't appeal whatsoever! Evra drives to the edge of the penalty area, before being robbed of the ball by Martin, with the ball skipping up into the Scot's midriff. For all of the talk from their new coach, Man United haven't been too incisive going forward.
(17’) Turner makes an important interception to deny Valencia, before Norwich try to break. The likes of Snodgrass and Redmond possess pace and quality to hurt Man United on the break, but Van Wolfswinkel has been nearly anonymous yet again.
(16’) Despite Giggs' intentions, it hasn't been a particularly intense start from the home side. They're retaining the ball, but the eventual aim appears to be whipping a cross in through Valencia or Evra, with Kagawa again being deployed in a slightly alien left midfield position.
(14’) WELBECK! Good save from Ruddy! Turner's header is merely a half clearance to prevent Valencia from meeting a cross at the back post, with the rebound falling to the unmarked Welbeck. The England international fires a powerful strike at goal, but Ruddy beats it away well at the near post.
(13’) Rooney and Welbeck haven't seen too much of the ball thus far, with Norwich looking well organised and fairly tough to break down. Scoring goals has been the main issue for the away side throughout the entire season, their solidity is only called into severe question occasionally.
(11’) The first ten minutes have passed without much in the way of action, but Valencia has enjoyed some joy down the right flank for the hosts. Norwich are crowding the middle third, with Cleverley really having to drop deep to receive possession, forcing the home side down the wings regularly.
(9’) Van Wolfswinkel manages to test De Gea with a looping back post header, but the Dutchman is penalised for a shove on Phil Jones. It was a good spot by the referee and Norwich can take heart from challenging the Man United goalkeeper for a first time.
(7’) Giggs is applauded as he walks into his technical area for the first time, causing chants of 'Ryan Giggs' red and white army' once again. Man United have started this game well, possibly feeding off the positivity of the crowd.
(6’) Norwich have seen very little of possession in the opening minutes, with Snodgrass and Redmond still trying to give the away side some width. Hughton was criticised for his negative football, which isn't the case under the current caretaker but the Canaries can't afford to shirk their defensive responsibilities this evening.
(4’) Rooney has space open up ahead of him at the edge of the box, but opts to spray the ball wide to Valencia instead of taking a shot at goal. Olsson makes the block to deny the Ecuadorian's delivery, giving the hosts their first corner. The set piece comes to nothing.
(3’) All United in the early stages, with Welbeck put through on goal twice in the opening few minutes. Ruddy is able to collect both passes, however, as the service to the England international hasn't been accurate enough. Plenty of optimism in the wake of Moyes' dismissal.
(2’) Ryan Giggs has promised plenty of passion and desire from his players, as the home side appear to want to inject some positivity back into the Old Trafford crowd. The atmosphere is excellent, with chants about the new interim coach echoing around the stadium.
(1’) We are underway in the first half! As expected, Ryan Giggs got a hero's welcome after emerging from the Old Trafford tunnel, but now we need to get down to business! Given that Norwich are playing for survival, the hosts might just need to come flying out of the traps to prevent Adams' men from getting a foothold in the game.
A quarter of an hour remains before kick-off, so be sure to stick with us for all of the action, as Ryan Gigg's tries to kick-start his stewardship of Man United with a win. Norwich are in dire straits if they fail to pick up any points this evening, with all of the bottom three stick within touching distance of the Canaries. This promises to be a hard fought affair, rather than a game with that distinct end-of-season feeling.
Ricky van Wolfswinkel has managed merely one goal in 26 Premier League appearances this season, despite commanding a rather large chunk of former manager Chris Hughton's transfer budget last summer. Left on his own up front, with Adams' formation having the potential to be a 4-3-3 or a 4-5-1, it could be a quiet afternoon for the Dutchman, or the opportunity to be a lethal poacher.
Norwich substitutes: Bunn, Hooper, Gutierrez, Elmander, Bennett, Tettey, Murphy.

Nathan Redmond and Robert Snodgrass will provide the width, with the defence unchanged. The likes of Johan Elmander, Alex Tettey, Gary Hooper and Jonas Gutierrez could see some action from the bench.
