(86’) Calum Robinson has scored two goals in two games for the England U19 side. Lambert urges his young forward to instantly get involved. It is Davis who is continue to try and guide Southampton up the other end.
--- 85’ Substitution REMEMBER THE NAME. Calum Robinson makes his Aston Villa debut. The 19 year old striker would really make himself an instant Holte End favourite if he could find a goal in the closing stages at Villa Park. ---
(84’) Cork immediately brings the game to life. Southampton forage forward with intent. Aston Villa remain determined to not let their defence be breached under any circumstances though.
--- 83’ Substitution Wanyama is sacrificed in a like for like switch as Pochettino goes for broke. Both managers really trying to win this one here. ---
(82’) COUNTER OPPORTUNITY: Albrighton is appalled as he then has the chance to expose Southampton's defence in a three on two break. He is given the ball far too late and his flagged for offside.
--- 80’ Substitution Grant Holt finally comes on. Paul Lambert could really do with a saviour here. The former Norwich target man steps up. ---
(80’) HUGE ESCAPE. Aston Villa can count their blesses there. Lee Mason waves away a penalty appeal. Lallana and Wanyama push the ball side to side in the middle of the aprk.. The ball reaches Clyne who rifles the ball at Bertrand just inside the box. It looks like HANDBALL. Not given.
(78’) AGBONLAHOR was goal-side but just can't quite reach the long ball forward. He was just a yard off there and he would have certainly scored. Grant Holt patiently watches on.
(77’) It is Southampton's turn to dig deep and defend as Delph and Westwood start pumping balls to the wide men. Albrighton is a constant thorn in Southampton's side. He is constantly putting Shaw under pressure.
(76’) Aston Villa HUDDLE around Paul Lambert as they seek some fresh impetus for the final 15 minutes as there is a short break in play. Their manager looks animated as he tries to inspire his charges.
(75’) Aston Villa have had a 26 year stay in the top flight and they are playing as if survival is the aim here. Their fans are urging them on to search for a winner but Albrighton fires in a ball which is too close to Boruc. A goal now for either side would certainly settle it.
(73’) Southampton are getting OUTMUSCLED in the middle of the park by Aston Villa and the villains have used their midfield steel to remain in this encounter. The supporters still are biting their nails though.
(71’) David Moyes continues to watch on as Luke Shaw makes a great impression and hurries forward with no fear, whenever he is given the opportunity. Paul Lambert on the other hand is intense discussion with Shay Given.
(70’) Vlaar again cuts off the route to the near post as Shaw puts a searching low ball into the box. The resulting corner is collected by Guzan who is fouled as he does so.
(69’) GALLAGHER almost makes an immediate impact. Lambert drives a stunning ball low into the box at the near post and the Southampton substiute so nearly steals in.
--- 67’ Substitution The Southampton midfielder goes off to a ripple of applause. Pochettino puts on Gallagher to really try and find all that is missing from his team's commanding display. A goal. ---
--- 66’ Yellow card Luke Shaw eventually gets punished for his overzealous tussles with Marc Albrighton and takes out the Aston Villa winger. ---
(66’) Bertrand again remains a shining light for Aston Villa. He has been terrific down the left looking to bomb forward whenever he gets the opportunity. He has a cross blocked. The equally excellent Albrighton has a ball in blocked too.
(65’) Aston Villa have struggled to make an impression at the attacking end but they continue to be resilient in defence and will fancy their chances of a smash and grab. They still have only 30% possession.
(63’) FIZZLING SHOT from Albrighton. That stings Boruc's gloves. It is shoved right down his throat from 20 yards out. He catches it then has to almost drop it in the air like a hot potato taking a few steps backwards before gathering it.
--- 61’ Yellow card Lovren gives a way a free kick after blocking off his man. Lee Mason finally reaches for his pocket. He appears to be the last man at a first glance but the referee makes the right call and only awards a yellow card. ---
(60’) Aston Villa are determined to hold firm in the wave of an intense spell of pressure from Southampton. Pochettino's side simply can't find a way through. Bertrand again excellently clears.
(59’) Clyne surges down the right hand side and Southampton are trying to utilise their full backs to break down Villa's resilient defence. Davis and Wanyama give the ball to Lambert who ALMOST provides the perfect ball for Lallana. Vlaar clears. Silky football from the Saints.
(57’) Lovren has to be alert as Aston Villa continue to launch an assault of direct long balls his way. The Croatian international is more than a match for them though.
(56’) Lallana is limping around after have a strange fall after missing his last opportunity to score. The Southampton capatain is moving around gingerly, before he goes back into a gentle jog.
(54’) A big crowd at Villa park today and they were nearly stunned. LALLANA should score as Shaw slides him in along the floor. The ball again falls behind him and he fails to score. The England international will be gutted with that.
(52’) Agbonlahor TWISTS AND TURNS. He demands support from the Villa faithful and forces a corner. The resulting corner goes to Nathan Baker who can't convert the chance. Villa then fire a few more balls into the box but can't break the Southampton defence.
(50’) El Ahmadi seizes on a lapse in concentration from the Southampton defence. They hesistate on the ball. El Ahmadi gets a chance to shot and tries to place it in just outside the six yard box. It was the wrong decision and Boruc collects the ball easily.
(48’) Artur Boruc has not had a single save to make so far. This game remains a midfield battle. Both sides appear to want to find a direct through ball but can't find an effective end product.
(46’) An astonishing 71% possession for Southampton in the first half and will be looking to continue in the same vein here. Agbonlahor nudges Lovren to give Southampton a free kick. Chances have been very few and far between so far.
HALF TIME- Aston Villa 0-0 Southampton. Both sides remain firmly in contention for all three points here. Lambert and Pochettino will have seen signs of encouragement, yet it remains goalless at the break.
(45’) ANOTHER GREAT BALL from Albrighton who has really grown into the game in the last 25 minutes. El Ahmadi narrowly misses out on his cross.
(45’) BERTRAND fizzes a ball into the near post and Weimann SO NEARLY converts the ball. They get a corner as a result then quickly force a second corner.
(45’) Rickie Lambert trundles forward for Southampton. He passes to Lallana who suprisingly fluffs his lines just outside the box. There is a ping pong of the ball going between both teams.
(43’) The game opens up as half-time approaches. Nobody can capitalise on a clever early cross from Albrighton. Shaw then starts another counter attack for Southampton but they don't make the most of it.
(41’) David Moyes in deep conversation with Steve Bruce in the corporate area of Villa Park as both teams continue to cancel each other out. Steve Round and Phil Neville are both watching today's game. Luke Shaw then bodychecks Albrighton and can consider himself lucky not to find his name in the book.
(40’) Bertrand and Bacuna are providing a real outlet for Aston Villa to spring attacks from down the left hand side. Agbonlahor is played in and appears to be through one on one before being flagged up for offside.
(38’) Aston Villa have scored just 35 goals this campaign and you can see why so far. There is a clear lack of composure in their attacks,. Bertrand puts another ball into the box. He forces a corner this time.
(37’) A stalemate so far. Southampton continue to have the better of the game. Wanywama catches El Ahmadi with a flailing arm. No card from Lee Mason and Aston Villa produce a set piece chance. Bertrand puts the ball into the right area but nobody gambles and the ball trickles out for a goal-kick.
(35’) Pochettino goes about his business with minimal fuss and continues to look calm as his Southampton side have once again raised the tempo. Shaw again displays superb first touch before Bacuna manages to steal the ball away from him.
(33’) SO CLOSE! Ward Prowse hits the ball in to Lambert. It bounces off his knee and he knows very little about it. The ball immediately falls at the feet of Davis who fires the ball at Guzan and it's a MAGNIFICENT save from Guzan. Villa will be delighted with his save there.
(32’) Davis hits a delightfully chipped ball to Shaw who hits a ball in first time on the volley. It is cleared for a throw on.
(31’) Steven Davis again looking to provide a piercing ball which splits the Villa defence and Vlaar stands firm. El Ahmadi again has a tussle with Ward Prowse. The players exchange a few pushes. Referee Lee Mason has a word with both players.
(29’) Lallana BURSTS through midfield to set up an encouraging attack. Schneiderlin puts in a disappointing cross and Lambert heads it easily at Guzan and struggled to generate any pace on his attempt at goal.
(27’) Southampton continue to exchange passes between their defence in midfield with Clyne particularly lively yet can't find their way past Villa's tenacious midfield.
(26’) Aston Villa have only two games left at home including today's match with Hull the only side left to visit Villa Park and they will be hoping for three points today to allay their relegation fears. They are starting to match Southampton and with tricky away fixtures to come they will want at minimum to gain a share of the spoils today.
(24’) Luke Shaw has filled out physically significantly and he is winning his tussle with Albrighton. The ball goes to Schneiderlin and Albrighton then takes out the Southampton midfielder in frustration tracking back. He is lucky not to be booked. This is a better spell from Villa, they are pressuring the ball.
(23’) A decent spell from Villa. A lot better than the opening exchanges. Southampton still look dangerous on the counter attack. Lallana fails to find the killer pass to put through Lambert and the ball is collected by Guzan.
(21’) FOUL: Schneiderlin takes down Bacuna as he charges up the left wing. The resulting play soon leads to Southampton regaining control of the ball. Luke Shaw shows exceptional positioning and reading of the game and retrieves the ball from Albrighton.
(20’) Clyne and Jose Fonte interchange at the back before pushing a long ball forward. A few nerves appear to have set in for both sides after a close start.
(18’) Luke Shaw nearly gets caught in possession by El Ahmadi as he dithers on the ball but it richochets off his opponent and it goes out for a throw in.
(16’) Lovren was made to leave the field before coming back on. Foul by El Ahamadi as he tries to seize on a poor first touch.
(15’) Offside given against Steven Davis and Villa are slowly starting to maintain some composure. Bacuna, Westwood and Delph put together a string of passes, before Bertrand puts a teasing ball into the box. Lovren puts his body on the line to clear it. Ouch! he felt that one. He heads it out of play, but goes down injured, before getting up a few moments later.
(13’) Nathan Baker suddenly passes it to Agbonlahor and the Villa striker should do much better as he closed down with his first touch too heavy. It goes out for a corner which Albrighton takes, but it is cleared away comfortably.
(12’) The game returns to it's familiar pattern as Southampton continue to neatly pass the ball around in triangles. It is too easy for the visitors. All that is missing is the cutting edge up front and the goals.
(11’) QUICK BREAK: Aston Villa surge up the other end Andreas Weimann's cut back is just short as they can't quite make the most of a counter attack.
(9’) Shay Given sat on the Villa bench appears anxious. Aston Villa fans have not had much to cheer about recently. Only 13% possession in the first nine minutes won't help.
(8’) Clyne, Ward Prowse and Lallana interchange passes in their own half and look completely in control when in possession. Southampton continue to probe forward and dictate the tempo.
(7’) Aston Villa look visibly rattled and Mauricio Pochettino will be very happy with his side's attacking start. They are looking to equal their best ever Premier League finish.
(5’) Steven Davis with a SENSATIONAL cut back to Lambert. It is again slightly behind him. Southampton wreacking havoc down the left hand side. It could be 2-0 in five minutes.
(3’) Luke Shaw marauds forward. A GREAT CHANCE for Southampton. Rickie Lambert heads it straight at Guzan. He should do better even if it is slightly behind him.
(2’) Southampton start off with plenty of intent. Steven Davis who started his career at Aston Villa the heartbeat of the midfield. Lallana is caught by Ashley Westwood and earns a free-kick.
(1’) Southampton get the match underway with PFA player of the year nominee passing to Rickie Lambert. It is 13 years since Aston Villa lost five games in a row in the Premier League.
Aston Villa starting line-up: Guzan, Bacuna, Vlaar, Baker, Bertrand, El Ahmadi, Westwood, Delph, Agbonlahor, Weimann, Albrighton.
Southampton starting line-up: Boruc, Clyne, Fonte, Lovren, Shaw, Ward-Prowse, Schneiderlin, Davis, Wanyama, Lallana, Lambert.
TEAM NEWS: Southampton are boosted by the return of Artur Boruc in goal as he has managed to shake off a back injury. This offsets the continued absence of Kelvin Davis. Top goalscorer Jay Rodriguez will be out for the rest of the season and the World Cup. The Saints will miss Rodriguez but Rickie Lambert has scored three goals in his last three Premier League meetings with Aston Villa.
TEAM NEWS: Aston Villa still have a significant number of players stuck in the treatment room. Jores Okore, Libor Kozak and Chris Herd all remain out yet Leandro Bacuna returns. Christian Benteke remains a notable absentee and Paul Lambert will have to continue without his top goalscorer. Grant Holt will step into the breach yet has only mustered one shot on target in eight appearance for Villa so far.
I'm Grant Miles, and I will be leading you through all the action, as Aston Villa attempt to resurrect their miserable home form. They have lost 10 games at Villa Park this season, only Fulham have a worse home record. Leandro Bacuna's return will be a huge boost for Villa. However, Mauricio Pochettino will be looking for revenge after watching his team throw away a two goal lead and lose to Villa at St Mary's in December.
Hello and welcome to live Premier League coverage of Southampton's trip to Aston Villa with the visitors looking to bounce back from a shock home defeat to Cardiff last time out. Aston Villa will to be looking to prove a point and put on a united front for their manager Paul Lambert today after assistant manager Ian Culverhouse and football operations manager Gary Karsa were suspended by owner Randy Lerner, earlier this week. Villa have lost four games on the spin and a win today would provide a much needed tonic for the Villa Park faithful.

All it remains for me to say is thank you very much for joining me this afternoon and enjoy the rest of your weekend, I've been Chris Baker.
The Bluebirds live to fight another day as defeat surely would have been fatal to their survival chances but they will feel frustrated that they could channel the momentum of their equaliser into another goal. Their next game away against Sunderland has become even more significant now. Mark Hughes will probably be the most satisified man in Cardiff at the moment but he will feel that his forwards should have been more clinical in front of goal today.
Perhaps a draw was a fair result but it does little to help either side. Cardiff do go above Fulham into 18th place due to their superior goal difference but they will be praying that Liverpool can continue their outstanding recent form and beat Norwich in the early kick off tomorrow. They are two points behind the Canaries having played a game more. Stoke City sit tenth in the table on 44 points just below Newcastle United.
(90’) FULL TIME 1-1. In the end Cardiff might look at this as a point gained given how little they threatened in the last 15 minutes. Stoke will reflect on what could have been as they finished the second half strongly but couldn't find the winner.
(90’) Stoke are looking the more likely to snatch the three points as the game draws to a close. Cardiff haven't been able to get on the ball and put the away team under any sort of pressure in the final few minutes.
(90’) CHANCE! Four minutes of time have been added on and Walters almost puts Stoke into the lead as his curling effort clips the top of the crossbar with David Marshall beaten all ends up in the Cardiff goal. A whisker away from the winner from the substitute.
(89’) Whittingham's corner is palmed away by Begovic before Mutch commits a cardinal sin of taking a foul throw. Surely that's a fine? Stoke then break on Cardiff. Walters sends in a low cross which is picked up by Assaidi who brings the ball onto his left foot but with the goal at his mercy he can only shot straight at Marshall.
(87’) You sense that Cardiff are slightly beginning to run out of energy and ideas as Stoke begin to dominate. It must be said that the home fans are giving their team tremendous backing. Campbell chases down a loose ball and wins a corner for his side.
--- 86’ Substitution S. Ireland is done for the day. J. Walters is his replacement. ---
--- 85’ Yellow card P. Crouch receives a yellow card. ---
(85’) Jonathan Walters comes on in place of Stephen Ireland for the final five minutes. Walters immediately gets on the ball and holds it up nicely before bringing Odemwingie into play. The Nigerian cuts in from the right and drills a low shot in at the near post with his left foot, Marshall does well to turn the ball around the post.
--- 84’ Substitution Fábio is done for the day. D. John is his replacement. ---
(83’) Final sub for Cardiff with Fabio being replaced in a like-for-like change with Declan John. The game has got a little bit scrappy in the last ten minutes or so. The home side are looking for a grandstand finish but Stoke will also fancy their chances on the break. Crouch gets a yellow card for bumping into Cala off the ball. The Stoke striker looks less than impressed.
--- 81’ Substitution M. Dæhli is replaced with K. Jones. ---
(81’) Kenwyne Jones has entered the fray and has replaced Mats Daehli for the remaining nine minutes. The former Stoke hitman get straight into the action and makes a surging run in-field from the right hand side and looks to feed in Zaha but the flag is up for offside. Can Solskjaer's sub make the all important impact?
--- 78’ Substitution O. Assaidi enters play, replacing M. Arnautović. ---
(78’) Oussama Assaidi, on loan from Liverpool, is the man to replace Arnautovic. The Moroccan winger has been out injured and his return will please Mark Hughes no doubt. Fraizer Campbell meanwhile goes tumbling in the area but the ref is having none of it and waves away the appeals.
(76’) Zaha has been on the end of some pretty rough treatment since coming on. This time Howard Webb waves play on. Ireland's cross is easily dealt with by the Cardiff defence, the clearance drops to Whelan who is encouraged to shoot by the travelling supporters but instead pass it to Arnautovic who can only fire his effort way over the bar. It turns out to be the Austrian's last involvement in the match as he is subbed.
--- 74’ Yellow card Juan Cala gets yellow. ---
(73’) Last week's hero Juan Cala then gives away a silly free kick by fouling Odemwingie in a harmless position. Ireland flights the ball into the area looking, inevitably for the head of Crouch but Caulker heads clear. Both teams will feel they could have made more of their free kicks and corner this afternoon.
(71’) Theophile-Catherine shows excellent persistance by winning a corner for his side off of Muniesa. Whittingham curls the ball into the area but can only find the grateful gloves of Asmir Begovic. Cardiff can't afford to waste such good opportunities to put the ball into the dangerzone.
(69’) With the final twenty minutes approaching it is soon to be go for broke time for Cardiff City. A draw isn't really enough at this stage of the campaign. Will Ole Gunnar chuck on another striker to complete the turnaround?
(67’) As so many Premier League games do, this match has really opened up in the second half. Admittedly, when the home side gets a penalty so quickly after the restart it does tend to light the blue touchpaper. Stephen Ireland finds himself in a bit of space but can't keep his shot down and it flies over David Marshall's crossbar.
--- 66’ Yellow card J. Mutch goes into the referee's book. ---
(64’) This game has a real ebb and flow about it now with both sides going all out for the victory. Cardiff will feel that they should have turned their early second half dominance into a vital lead. The Potters will be relieved to have survived such an onslaught.
(61’) Stoke finally managed to release some pressure by setting Odemwingie free on the right wing, his cross is deflected out for a corner that Ireland will take. Ireland's corner is headed clear but only as far as Glenn Whelan, the Irishman looks to bend the ball at goal but his shot is just wide.
--- 60’ Substitution Bo-Kyung Kim is replaced with W. Zaha. ---
(59’) First substitution of the afternoon with Kim being replaced by Wilfried Zaha. The winger is incredibly quick and very skilful, he'll be a threat to the Stoke rearguard.
(58’) Things are beginning to calm down after a crazy start to the second period. After equalising, Cardiff put on an avalanche of pressure which it seemed that Stoke wouldn't be able to cope with but they seem to have weathered the storm, for now at least...
(55’) Goal disallowed for offside! The linesman's flag has come to the rescue for Stoke. Steven Caulker, who had stayed up following a corner, found himself in some space and drove a low shot in at goal which Begovic got down well to save. The rebound came back to Caulker who stabs it towards goal, the ball comes back of a combination of the goalkeeper and the post. It drops to Cala who turns the ball home only for his joy to be cut short.
(53’) Stoke are rattled here and the temperature has been raised within the stadium. N'Zonzi tackles Campbell from behind and is given a yellow card. Cardiff are pumping the ball into the box and causing problems. The away side will need to stand firm here.
--- 52’ Yellow card S. N'Zonzi gets yellow. ---
--- 51’ Goal! GOAL! Whittingham, the dead ball specialist, makes no mistake and levels the score at 1-1. The midfielder waited for Begovic to commit himself before guiding the penalty down the centre of the goal. Game on! ---
(49’) PENALTY TO CARDIFF! N'Zonzi is the guilty party as he dangles a lazy leg out and again the referee has no hesitation in awarding the penalty.
--- 48’ Yellow card P. Odemwingie goes into the referee's book. ---
(47’) Peter Odemwingie goes into the book after running into the back of Mutch. As the villan of the piece the home fans are very pleased to see their former striker receive a yellow card. The Cardiff fans are very much on the referee's back and will be putting Howard Webb under pressure to even things up.
(46’) Stoke get us going again for the second half. You can't help but feel that this will be a 45 minutes of monumental importance to Cardiff City. Can they get back into the match or will the visitors increase their lead?
You would imagine that Cardiff must be contemplating changes, as they simply can't afford to lose this fixture. Kenwyne Jones is an obvious substitution as Fraizer Campbell has looked a little isolated at times. Wilfried Zaha of course has the capability to make the difference.
Truth be told there wasn't a lot between the sides in the first half. Whittingham came close to giving Cardiff the lead with an exquisite free kick which was superbly saved by Begovic. Stoke grew into the game as the half wore on and have managed to grab a precious lead. I think it would be fair to say that Odemwingie 'won' the penalty but it was a clumsy and unnecessary challenge from Kim.
(45’) There's the half-time whistle which is greeted by howls of derision from the home faithful. Odemwingie seemed to go to ground very easily and theatrically. The Stoke fans don't care one bit though they are bouncing with delight!
--- 45’ +3 Goal! GOAL! 1-0 TO STOKE! Cool as you like Arnautovic steps up to calmly slot the ball past Marshall. An absolute body blow to Cardiff on the brink of the half-time interval. ---
(45’) PENALTY TO STOKE! Muniesa forced a corner with a rocket of a shot from the left back position. Ireland then delivered the ball into the area, after a bit of a scramble Odemwingie is bundled over and Howard Webb points to the spot.
(44’) Kevin Theophile-Catherine is rather unceremoniusly upended by Glenn Whelan on the touchline and requires some treatment. Meanwhile, two minutes have been ended onto the first half.
(41’) OFF THE POST! Free kick to Cardiff in a dangerous position, Whittingham curls the ball over the wall but Begovic is able to touch the ball onto the frame of the goal. Just inches away from the opening goal of the game. Fantastic save from the Stoke goalkeeper, who is probably one of the best stoppers in the division.
(38’) Nearly a moment to forget for Asmir Begovic who comes charging out of his area to deal with a long pass towards Campbell. The Bosnian goalkeeper gets their first but almost misses the ball completely - he does however get just enough on the ball to scuff it out of harms way. He was very lucky that a Cardiff player wasn't following that up otherwise Begovic could have been seriously embarrassed!
(35’) The home team may have had a decent opening ten minutes to the match but Stoke are certainly growing into it. The Potters are starting to stretch their opponents and are getting some space on the wings. Steven N'Zonzi works the ball out to Arnautovic, who looks to work the ball onto his favoured right foot but his shot is snuffed out by a combination of Caulker and Cala.
(32’) Cardiff's midfielder are just wanting a little too long on the ball and are being caught in possession far too often for their manager's liking. Arnautovic is the latest Stoke player to take advantage and whips in an excellent ball from the left that Crouch meets with his head but can only loop it up in the air which Marshall easily gathers.
--- 29’ Substitution E. Pieters is replaced with Muniesa. ---
(29’) Campbell's shot forced another corner which didn't lead to a chance for the home side. Instead Stoke sprang forward on the counter attack, Stephen Ireland carried the ball a good 40 yards before feeding the ball out wide to Odemwingie. The winger's stinging shot was well palmed away by David Marshall. Marc Muniesa has indeed come on to replace Pieters at left back for Stoke.
(27’) Erik Pieters seems to be struggling with an injury and may have to be replaced. Fraizer Campbell, who has been rather anonymous so far, picks up the ball and tries to curl the ball into the top corner but his effort is blocked well by the onrushing defenders.
(25’) A sniff of an opportunity for Mutch after neat approach work from Bo-Kyung Kim. The South Korean ducked inside from the left wing well and laid the ball square for Mutch who can only scuff his shot wide from the edge of the box. He was leaning back a bit and will be disappointed to have not done better.
(23’) Half way through the first half and their has been a distinct lack of composure from both teams in attacking areas which has meant their hasn't been a great deal of goalmouth action to tell you about so far. You can understand the nerves from Cardiff but Stoke should be able to relax a bit more and play with a little less pressure.
(20’) That's more like it from Fabio! The Brazilian left back picks the ball up in his own half and drives towards the Stoke penalty area. He takes the shot on from a fair way out but his strike is well blocked by Marc Wilson. The surge forward has certainly livened up the crowd. Cardiff fans will want to see more of that kind of endeavour.
(18’) It's no coincidence that Marko Arnautovic has started seeing a bit more of the ball and as a consequence Stoke look more threatening. After a promising start Cardiff have just gone off the boil in the last five minutes, they'll need to up the tempo and intensity of their play.
(16’) Stephen Ireland has an opportunity to throw the ball into the box with a free-kick from the right wing. His delivery isn't bad but Crouch can't make anything of it from the set piece. Stoke are just beginning to feel their way into the match and find some rhythm.
(13’) Peter Crouch is trying to get more involved in the game to give the Stoke attack a focal point but the service into the tall frontman hasn't been up to scratch so far. It will be interesting to see if Peter Odemwingie can make any sort of impact against his former club. Likewise Kenwyne Jones would love to score, if given the opportunity to come off the bench for Cardiff.
(10’) Solskjaer will be reasonably happy with the opening ten minutes of this match. His players look bright and lively going forward while Stoke haven't had anything vaguely like a serious attack on their goal. Cardiff have pressed the ball well and are hunting in packs.
(8’) Stoke are just enjoying their first period of sustained possession as they look to get a foothold in the match and quieten down the home supporters. Cardiff appear content to let the visitors pass the ball around in their own half.
(6’) CHANCE! It's all coming down the left flank for the Bluebirds. Jordon Mutch is released down the inside left channel. The midfielder looks to curl the ball into the far corner with his right foot but his effort is straight at Begovic who collects comfortably.
(4’) Peter Whittingham's corner fails to pick out a teammate and is easily cleared by Ryan Shawcross. Fabio then looks to help the ball back into the danger area but his cross is overhit and floats out for a goal kick.
(3’) Some patient and probing passing from the home side leads to the young Norwegian Mats Daehli breaking into the box, he cuts inside but his low shot is deflected out of play for the first corner of the game. Encouraging start from Cardiff.
(1’) We're underway in the bright Welsh sunshine. The home fans are in typically good voice for this potentially crucial game in their debut season in the Premier League. Howard Webb is the referee.
Cardiff haven't won two Premier League games in a row this season which is a statistic they will look to remedy over the course of the next 90 minutes. The Potters have been in good form of late and will be hoping to finish the season with a flourish. The teams are just making their way out onto the pitch...
Cardiff City will be buoyed by the news that Spurs have already seen off Fulham at White Hart Lane and with Norwich playing Liverpool tomorrow Ole Gunnar Solskjaer's team will see today's game against a Stoke City side with not a great deal left to play for as a massive opportunity.
Stoke City (4-2-3-1): Begovic; Cameron, Shawcross, Wilson, Pieters; Whelan, N'Zonzi; Odemwingie, Ireland, Arnautovic; Crouch.

Subs: Sorensen, Muniesa, Palacios, Adam, Walters, Assaidi, Wilkinson.
Cardiff City (4-5-1): Marshall; Theophile-Catherine, Caulker, Cala, Fabio; Whittingham, Medel, Daehli, Mutch, Kim; Campbell.

Subs: Lewis, Turner, Jones, Eikrem, Gunnarsson, Zaha, John.

FT: Chelsea 1-2 Sunderland. You just cannot write the script in the Premier League. Gus Poyet is jubilant on the touchline as his side have ended Jose Mourinho's 77-game unbeaten league run to boost their hopes of surviving in the top flight. What a sensational advert for English football!
FT: SUNDERLAND HAVE WON AT STAMFORD BRIDGE!

HT: Chelsea 1-1 Sunderland. Mike Dean blows his whistle to signal the end of a thrilling first-half of football. Samuel Eto'o gave Chelsea the lead when he reacted quickest to volley Willian's corner beyond Vito Mannone for his ninth league goal of the season. However, Sunderland responded brilliantly and Connor Wickham levelled the scores when he lifted the ball over Mark Schwarzer to add to his midweek double. It's been end-to-end stuff here at Stamford Bridge and there certainly seem to be more goals in this one.

The Sunderland winger has the whole goal to aim at but he decides to take an extra touch which allows Azpilicueta to get back in and win the ball. Why didn't he shoot?

--- 12’ Goal! ETO'O GIVES CHELSEA THE LEAD! The Cameroon international notches his ninth league goal of the season as he ghosts ahead of Cattermole to volley Willian's corner beyond Mannone and into the roof of the net. It's a huge mountain for Sunderland to climb now. ---

The two teams emerge from the tunnel into the Stamford Bridge sunshine and captains John Terry and John O'Shea begin the respective handshakes between the sides. Today's referee is Mike Dean.
Sunderland will be hoping to rekindle some of the spirit which helped them to knock Chelsea out of the League Cup earlier this season. The two sides also enjoyed a 4-3 thriller at the Stadium of Light and even Jozy Altidore got on the scoresheet that day. The American has only two Premier League goals in 55 appearances and his Black Cats future is very much in doubt.

SUNDERLAND TEAM NEWS: Gus Poyet unsurprisingly names an unchanged side to the team which drew 2-2 at Manchester City on Wednesday. Connor Wickham will hope that his midweek double can kick-start his Black Cats career while Vito Mannone will aim to atone for his error which allowed Samir Nasri to score a late equaliser. Phil Bardsley remains sidelined through suspension.
CHELSEA TEAM NEWS: Jose Mourinho resists the urge to rest key players for the Champions League tie against Atletico Madrid on Tuesday and makes just three changes to the side which beat Swansea 1-0. Despite scoring in his last two appearances, Demba Ba drops to the bench, with Samuel Eto'o taking the lone striking berth. Oscar replaces Andre Schurrle in the midfield while Mark Schwarzer is handed a rare start between the sticks due to Petr Cech feeling unwell. Eden Hazard once again misses out through injury.
Could there be a worse place for Sunderland to come today than Stamford Bridge? Chelsea are unbeaten in 77 home league matches under Jose Mourinho and have not conceded at home since a Javier Hernandez strike in January.
However, Sunderland manager Gus Poyet will be keen to derail his former side's title challenge as the Black Cats are six points adrift of safety, albeit with a game in hand on Norwich. With five games remaining, the pressure is really on Sunderland who have only won two of their 12 Premier League games at Stamford Bridge, conceding 38 goals - including a 7-2 defeat in January 2010.
It's title challengers vs. relegation fighters in the late Premier League kick-off today as Chelsea look to go top of the table with a win against bottom-of-the-table Sunderland. Jose Mourinho's side have a mouthwatering Champions League tie with Atletico Madrid on Tuesday but the West Londoners know that they must first focus on today's encounter against a Black Cats side who were cruelly denied all three points against Manchester City in midweek.

Well, that's all from our LIVE coverage from Carrow Road. It was a fantastic encounter, wasn't it? What a season. Thanks for joining us, and goodbye for now!
So, Liverpool go five points clear at the top of the table, and next Sunday's game at home to Chelsea could effectively seal their first Premier League title. That's 11 wins in a row, and another step closer.
All credit to Norwich, though. They looked like being blown away when Suarez made it 2-0, but they fought hard to get back in the game and will feel they deserved a point today.
FULL TIME at Carrow Road! Liverpool win 3-2! What a fantastic game, and it's a huge result for Brendan Rodgers' men, who are massive favourites to take the Premier League title now.

(18’) Snodgrass is upset after going down under Allen's challenge just outside the box, but nothing is given, before a free kick ends up going the other way.

FULL-TIME: Hull City 0-3 Arsenal. The Gunners secure the three points on Humberside in style to cap a fine week and boost their chances of a fourth-placed finish after sweeping aside the hosts in a dress rehearsal ahead of next month's FA Cup final. Hull started brightly but faded when the returning Aaron Ramsey drilled home before Lukas Podolski's strike right on the stroke of half-time killed off any Tigers hopes. Podolski added a second, and his side's third, to leave Arsenal - at least temporarily - four points clear of Everton in the race for fourth. Hull will  need to play much better than they fared at the KC to stand any chance of extending Arsenal's trophyless spell into a decade at Wembley.
(90’) Another poor finish more or less ensures Arsenal will have to settle for just the three goals this afternoon as Sagna's industry down the right presents a chance for Flamini, but the midfielder's shot is hurried and flies wide of the target.

(88’) Hull threaten a consolation as Fryatt peels away on the right wing but his low cross is well dealt with by Mertesacker, who was perfectly stationed to see off the danger in the middle.

(80’) HOWITZER! Huddlestone lets off a powerful drive towards goal which appears to take a slight nick and forces a good save in the end from Szczesny, who had to adjust his feet at the last.
(78’) PENALTY?! It looks like Arsenal may have been denied a second possible spot-kick as Oxlade-Chamberlain is swiped down by Davies after staying up initially under a Rosenior challenge. (76’) ROOF OF THE NET! Cazorla, with the Arsenal fans chanting his name behind the Hull goal, delivers a free-kick with pace from the left flank and is able to locate Mertesacker's near-post run, but the German can only flick his header onto the roof of the net, with Harper looking beaten.

(74’) Cazorla shows immaculate close control to keep Mertesacker's drilled pass close to his feet before Wenger makes his second change, with Oxlade-Chamberlain entering the fray for a tiring Giroud.
(72’) Bruce looks to avoid any further damage by introducing Stephen Quinn for the largely ineffectual Jelavic and Arsenal continue their procession towards the final whistle.

Hull, who hit the post through Livermore, have posed numerous problems to a nervy-looking backline but Wenger's side have been clinical in the final third, with Ramsey and Podolski finishing off flowing team moves with emphatic finishes to establish what could be a crucial two-goal advantage.

The Gunners have only won once on the road in their last six in the league but have beaten Hull on five consecutive occasions since a shock 2-1 defeat at home to the Humberside outfit upon their first-ever stint in the Premier League in 2008.
The strikers' absences in the final could be a huge blow to the Tigers' chances at Wembley so Bruce will be hoping to capitalise today to get the one win that is probably required to ensure safety.
Wenger can take confidence from Hull's hard-fought win over the Blades, who managed to breach their more illustrious opponents' defence on three occasions in the 5-3 thriller. Equally, though, the Frenchman will have warned his defence to be aware of the threats of Jelavic and Long, who have their own FA Cup final this afternoon.
The win over West Ham, which saw them move back above Everton, puts them firmly in the driving seat for Champions League football once more, particularly after the Toffees' shock defeat at home to Crystal Palace a day later.
In 2003, Arsenal thrashed Southampton 6-1 in the league before securing a 1-0 success when the two clubs met again at the Millenium Stadium and it is a trend Wenger will hope to repeat once more as his side looks to close in on a fourth-placed finish and a first trophy in nine years.
The Gunners, of course, won the double in 1998 - when a 2-0 win over Newcastle United in the league was enough to send the Tyneside outfit into a negative run of form, which culminated in a defeat by the same scoreline in the Wembley showpiece.
Perhaps one of the most remarkable statistics of the Premier League era is this; only once has the winner of an FA Cup dress rehearsal not gone on to lift the cup in the subsequent meeting, and that was Manchester City last year in their shock defeat to Wigan. Arsenal certainly have previous when it comes to winning in both competitions.
Arsene Wenger, meanwhile, is able to restore Mesut Ozil to the lineup after his prolonged absence with a hamstring injury, while Aaron Ramsey also starts after his cameo against the Hammers in midweek. The Gunners' third change is to bring in Nacho Monreal for Thomas Vermaelen, who has a hamstring problem of his own.
Bruce drafts in the cup-tied strike duo of Shane Long and Nikica Jelavic as he goes in search of a win which would significantly boost their hopes of remaining in the top flight. Maynor Figueroa, who flopped during the win over the Blades at Wembley, drops to the bench while Yannick Sagbo is also amongst the subs.

(73’) Danny Welbeck is given a long talking to by David Moyes as he looks set to make his way on here. Is there still time for United to rescue something from this match? Shinji Kagawa is the one to give way, and it's been long overdue as the Japanese midfielder has been very poor here today.
(71’) Everton are applying so much pressure on the ball, and United can't find a way around that! Their negative build-up is what has been plaguing them to this point, as they not only struggle to find a way through in attack, but look for a way to keep the ball in the final third.
--- 70’ Substitution L. Osman enters play, replacing R. Barkley. ---
(69’) Approaching 20 minutes left to play here at Goodison, with United still looking for a breakthrough. They started the half with so much promise, but have failed to live up to those opening few minutes as Everton have settled back in and continued their dominance in defence.
(67’) Superb run from Barkley, but it was just lacking a good finish. He uses his pace to blow by Smalling and Evans, but his final touch runs a bit far as he's forced to shoot from a poor angle, missing the net by a good distance. It would have been something of a miracle if he put that one on target, running away from goal.
(65’) McCarthy down and in some pain as he collides with Rooney trying to win a loose ball. The Irishman was caught as he kicked the ball, and may have just tweaked his ankle a bit. He's struggling to put weight on his right foot as he makes his way off the pitch.
(63’) STAT ATTACK: Manchester United have won four straight away matches in the league and are unbeaten in their last five.
--- 61’ Substitution J. Hernández enters the game and replaces J. Evans. ---
--- 61’ Substitution Nani is done for the day. A. Valencia is his replacement. ---
(61’) WHAT A BALL FROM MIRALLAS! The Belgian picks out Lukaku with an absolutely superb pass from just beyond the half-way line, but the striker gets a bit too close to goal as he can only put his shot straight at De Gea.
--- 60’ Yellow card J. McCarthy is yellow-carded. ---
(59’) McCarthy comes very hard into the back of Mata, rather overzealous there, as he earns himself a yellow card. It looked quite bad, and could have ended a lot worse for the Spaniard whose knee buckled from under him.
(57’) CLOSE TO A THIRD FOR EVERTON! From a corner kick, Mirallas delivers, and Alcaraz climbs well to meet the ball with his head, but can't get enough power behind it to beat De Gea.
(55’) United can't break out of their own half here! Great pressure by Everton on Evans and Jones, as they nearly win it back on more than one occasion. Evans has finally seen enough as he boots it up the pitch and concedes possession, much to the delight of the Everton supporters.
(53’) CHANCE HERE FOR UNITED? Baines clips Nani just outside the box and United have a free kick from close range here, with Mata and Rooney standing over it. The Spaniard is the one to take, but he smacks it off the wall and Everton clear the danger.
(51’) Horrid defending from Kagawa! The midfielder again fails to track the run of Coleman, allowing him time and space to run at Evans. He charges into the box and has a go, but mishits it as it swerves well wide at the near post. Evans livid with Kagawa who has lost Coleman time and time again in this match.
--- 50’ Yellow card C. Smalling gets yellow. ---
(49’) WHAT A START TO THE HALF FOR UNITED! Rooney's corner is cleared by Everton, but only as far as Kagawa. The Japan international unleashes an effort from long range, and strikes it well, but it's just too close to Howard who gets down to make the save.
--- 47’ Yellow card R. Barkley is yellow-carded. ---
(47’) ROONEY NEARLY GETS UNITED ON THE BOARD! Mata picks out the forward inside the box, and he twists and turns his way in close, into a clear shooting position, but Alcaraz tracks back and breaks it up at the vital moment!
--- 46’ Substitution A. Alcáraz comes on for S. Distin. ---
(46’) Everton kick-off the second half and we're underway in Merseyside! One change to note at half as Distin comes off in the centre of defence for Alcaraz. Reports are that he picked up a hamstring injury and could not continue.
STAT ATTACK: The last time Everton led Manchester United 2-0 at Goodison was back on April 28, 2007. The Red Devils would score in the 61st, 67th, 78th and 90th minutes to cap off an incredible second half comeback, winning the match 4-2.
Manchester United with 67 percent possession at the break, and nearly doubling Everton in passing, with 381 compared to their 193. The discrepancy lies in the two teams total attempts, with Manchester United managing only one through the opening 45 minutes compared to Everton's eight.
HALF-TIME: EVERTON 2-0 MANCHESTER UNITED. It's every Scouser's dream as Leighton Baines and Kevin Mirallas have the Toffees two goals up at half in David Moyes' return to Goodison. United are far from out of this game, as they haven't played poorly by any means, but they'll need to find a way to break down this Everton defence if they are to have any hope of a comeback.
(45’) Mark Clattenburg sounds his whistle and we've reached the half-way point at Goodison! Incredible scenes here, as the crowd has reached new heights with the cheers echoing throughout Merseyside!
(45’) One minute of added time indicated by the assistant referee as Manchester United win a corner. Rooney delivers it into a dangerous area, and it deflects off the back of Barry straight into the hands of Tim Howard. That's the most action he's seen all half, the American.
--- 43’ Assist S. Coleman gave the assist. ---
--- 43’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOAL! Seamus Coleman with acres of space as Everton counter. He sends in a wonderful ball to spot the run of Mirallas who slots home brilliantly past De Gea. Goodison erupts as Everton double their lead! ---
(41’) United coming closer, but not close enough. Nani crosses in for Rooney, but he can't meet the ball with his head. It rolls to Mata along the left. He sends another ball into the crowded box, but the compete level isn't there for United as Everton win the ball ball once again and clear.
(39’) STAT ATTACK: Everton’s 19 victories this season tie a club record set back in 2007-08. They can achieve a new high with a win today.
(37’) United trying for anything in attack, but nothing is working for them at the moment. Rooney picks out Nani at the far post off a corner, but the Portuguese international can't find Carrick in the centre. The visitors can't muster up anything, with Everton defending so well throughout this first half.
(35’) INCHES TOO FAR FOR LUKAKU! Everton work their way through the United defence, with Naismith sending Mirallas into space on the right. The Belgian sends a low cross in for his countryman Lukaku, but it's just too far ahead of the striker much to the relief of United.
(33’) Lovely work by Baines to chase down a ball, pressuring Smalling into conceding a corner. It's whipped in by Mirallas, but the cross is poor as United can clear with ease. They try and kick start a counter but the pass forward for Nani runs too far and eventually rolls out of play.
(31’) Manchester United dominated the possession statistics early on, but it's quite misleading, as they've done little with their 63 percent as of yet. Everton defending admirably, keeping every United move to the outside. It may require a moment of brilliance to get the Red Devils level as it stands.
(29’) Well that certainly adds to the plot doesn't it?! The man David Moyes tried so hard to poach in the summer transfer window puts Manchester United a goal down, and Goodison Park has reached deafening levels!
--- 28’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOOAAL! Leighton Baines, who has never missed a Premier League penalty, keeps that record in tact, firing straight down the middle to beat De Gea. Everton in front! ---
--- 27’ Yellow card P. Jones receives a yellow card. ---
(27’) PENALTY AWARDED TO EVERTON! Naismith and Lukaku break on a counter. The Belgian gets the ball, cuts onto his left and lets fly. Phil Jones tries to get a block in, sticks out his arm and concedes the penalty!
(25’) STAT ATTACK: The Red Devils are better on the road than at home this season, posting the league’s best away record, picking up 33 points from their 17 matches.
(23’) NAISMITH! Well that's much better from Everton! Lukaku brilliantly heads down a ball straight into the path of Naismith who hits his shot first time from the top of the box. He gets under it just a bit and it flies over the bar. With all the time and space he had, he needs to do better there.
(21’) Tough challenge in midfield as Carrick mistimes his tackle and takes the legs of Naismith out from under him. The Everton man goes down and a foul is given, but Carrick escapes without a warning and no one is the wiser.
(19’) APPEALS FOR HANDBALL NOT GIVEN! Coleman picks out Naismith with a lovely ball inside the box, and his redirect hits the arm of Evans who came sliding in. Mark Clattenburg is having none of it, and it's the right decision as the ball struck his arm from less than a couple feet away. There's nothing he could do to avoid that.
(17’) Coleman is having a blast out there! Kagawa and Buttner have given the right-back loads of space to get into attack and he's taking the utmost advantage of it. He streaks down the right and cuts into the centre, but sees his shot blocked by Evans and United break the other way.
(15’) Both teams struggling to find a way through in attack. Some sound defending from both teams has made it difficult to generate anything in terms of scoring chances through the opening 15 minutes. It's a bit of a chess match at the moment between David Moyes and his successor Roberto Martinez.
(13’) STAT ATTACK: With a victory here today, the Toffees can complete their first double over Manchester United in over 40 years. They last did so in the 1969-70 season.
(11’) Coleman just needed a better final ball! The right-back has looked so dangerous in the early going, working a little one-two with Lukaku. He charges full steam ahead into the box and tries to pick out Naismith in the centre, but his pass isn't accurate enough as United scramble clear.
(9’) FIRST CHANCE FALLS FOR EVERTON! Coleman finds plenty of space on the right and sends in a cross for Mirallas. It's cleared by Smalling but only as far as Barkley, who charges into the box but sends his volley well over the bar.
(7’) Manchester United enjoy some possession deep in Everton's end, but the Toffees are defending well, giving the visitors very little to work with. Nothing in terms of scoring chances, or even attempts on goal from either team thus far as they just get rid of these early game jitters.
(5’) Everton looked very lively in midfield in these opening moments, applying plenty of pressure on the Untied players which has led to a number of turnovers. The Toffees are eager to get forward but their passing has been less than sharp as they enter the final third.
(3’) WHAT AN ATMOSPHERE! The stadium is rocking as the players all look for a touch on the ball in the early moments. Can Everton feed off the energy of the home fans and pick up a massive victory here today?
(1’) Manchester United kick-off and we're underway at Goodison Park! The visitors, moving left to right, are sporting their red tops, with Everton in their home royal blue uniforms. Sit back, and enjoy the action. We should have quite the spirited affair on our hands today!
David Moyes finally makes his way out of the tunnel, and the boo birds rain down from the crowd! There is some clapping for the former Everton manager, but it's quite a mixed reaction, with the jeers drowning out those in applause.
David Moyes has rotated his squad quite a bit with Alex Buttner, Jonny Evans, Michael Carrick, Nani and Wayne Rooney back in the XI after missing the last league match against Newcastle. Meanwhile, Marouane Fellaini has to settle for a place on the bench as he takes on his former team.
Steven Pienaar and Phil Jagielka still aren't fit, while James McCarthy returns to the starting line-up. Steven Naismith gets the start, forcing Gerard Deulofeu to the bench.

Manchester United have been preparing 11 days for this match, having not played since the second leg of their Champions League cup tie at Bayern Munich. David Moyes will have been in the ears of his players, getting them ready for this match – and they, likewise, will know how important this is for him. There are so many factors that have contributed to this rocky season for United, but as is often the case in football, the blame has fallen on the shoulders of the manager. There is still time to salvage a spot in the Europa League for the Red Devils, and they will be given a big boost by picking up three points today in Moyes' return to Goodison.
Everton still have dreams of of a top four finish - something David Moyes only managed once in his 11 years at Goodison. Their loss to Crystal Palace midweek certainly put a dent in their plans, but their goal of playing in Europe's most prestigious competition is alive and well. Arsenal's likely victory today means Everton will need three points to keep the pressure on the Gunners in their pursuit of the fourth and final Champions League spot.
What kind of reception will David Moyes get today from his former supporters? He did a marvellous job during his 11 years in Merseyside, but considering the success the Toffees have had under Roberto Martinez, and the magnitude of this match, it is very possible he could be walking a tightrope as he makes his way out of the tunnel. What about his purchase of Marouane Fellaini and his attempt to buy Leighton Baines, to do what he said was "best for the players"? The aforementioned left-back is having his best season to date under Roberto Martinez. Will that play a large part with the fans, or will they mostly remember his nine top-10 finishes? The one thing we know for sure is you won't want to miss Manchester United taking the pitch in less than 30 minute's time here at Goodison Park!
Good afternoon to all you Premiership fans around the world, and welcome to today's match between Manchester United and Everton, as David Moyes makes his first ever return to Goodison Park with plenty at stake for both teams! I'm Alex Moretto and I'll be your in-game host, guiding you through the match LIVE as it happens!

Well, that's all from our LIVE coverage of Monday night's Premier League action. City are still in the title race, and West Brom are still in trouble. Many thanks for joining us, and goodbye for now!
Pellegrini will be happy with the result, but concerned over the fate of two of his players. Aguero looked to be struggling with a knock before he was substituted, while Silva was stretchered off with what could be a nasty injury.
West Brom, meanwhile, remain just three points clear of the relegation zone in 16th place. They still have a slightly superior goal difference, though, and will be glad City didn't try too hard to add to their tally tonight.
That moves City to within six points of Liverpool with a game in hand - they need the Reds to lose at home to Chelsea if they are to win the Premier League this season.
That's FULL TIME at the Etihad and Manchester City have registered a comfortable 3-1 win over struggling West Brom. All the action was in the first half and it was "job done" for the hosts, who saw out the remainder to pick up an important three points.
(90’) MILNER!! City nearly make it 4-1 as Fernandinho - who has been superb in midfield tonight - slides a pass through for the substitute, who fires at goal from a tight angle, but Foster saves well with his feet at the near post.
(90’) Dorrans tries to add to his tally for the night, but is nowhere near doing so as he finds some space in midfield before blasting a 30-yard effort a long way over the crossbar.
(90’) Amalfitano and Jones link up well on the right - something which hasn't happened enough for the visitors tonight - but Clichy shows good strength to win the ball back for the hosts deep inside their own half.
(90’) Clichy finds Nasri with an accurate ball forward, and the midfielder flicks a wonderful pass beyond Dawson, but Jovetic can't quite get on the end of it and it runs through to Foster, as we enter five minutes of added time.
--- 89’ Substitution A. Kolarov comes on for E. Džeko. ---
(89’) Aleksandar Kolarov is introduced for the final couple of minutes, as Dzeko is taken off by Pellegrini. Jovetic looks like he'll fulfil the lone centre forward role for the remainder.
(88’) Ridgewell is in some discomfort after going in for a 50-50 with Zabaleta by the corner flag. The defender limps off and his night's work is done. It's City, though, who look set to make a change!
(87’) Milner plays the ball into Dzeko, who says where he wants it and his team-mate obliges. The striker moves into the area from the left-hand side, and twists and turns before seeing his shot blocked by Olsson, who had followed him well.
(86’) This one's pretty much done and dusted, now, by the feel of it. City don't seem desperate to add any more and the visitors don't look like they're going to pull one back before the end.
(85’) City advance into the West Brom half again and Milner has it on the left-hand side. He looks infield and lays off to Zabaleta, who is encouraged to shoot by the home fans and does so, only to see Dorrans close him down well to block the effort.
--- 84’ Substitution Y. Mulumbu is replaced with J. Morrison. ---
(84’) DZEKO SHOULD DO BETTER!! It's a wonderful move from City, started by Nasri, who plays a neat one-two with Jovetic outside the box before sliding it into the path of Dzeko, who opens his body but curls the ball just around Foster's far post.
(83’) Fernandinho lifts the ball beautifully out wide to Zabaleta and City come forward again down the right flank. They slow things down, though, as they look to pass their way through.
(82’) Anichebe is in behind as Kompany commits to a tackle and misses, but his effort is blocked before it comes out to Dorrans, who fires the ball into the danger area and Hart firmly parries it away.
(81’) West Brom have a chance to come forward and Brunt spreads it out to Berahino, who cuts inside and plays a lovely low ball into the box. Anichebe is there beyond the defence but can't control the ball and the chance goes begging.
(80’) Dawson is penalised in midfield as he goes up for a header and shoves Dzeko down to the ground. He's on a yellow but this one doesn't warrant anything more than a peep of the whistle from the referee.
(79’) Fernandinho spreads a lovely ball out to Milner on the left-hand side as City continue to ping it around the pitch with ease. West Brom's challenge appears to have died and you expect they might just be setting up to not concede any more.
(78’) The atmosphere's gone a little bit stale inside the Etihad - you feel the fans are either just waiting for it to end, or hoping for some magic to get them going for the final 10 minutes or so. As yet, it's not been forthcoming in this half.
(77’) Good move from City as Nasri and Jovetic link up well before it's sent back to Fernandinho, who tries a speculative shot from 30 yards which flies well over the bar, much to Jovetic's anger as the striker had made a decent run beyond the defence.
--- 76’ Substitution S. Sessègnon is replaced with S. Berahino. ---
(76’) Saido Berahino is next on for West Brom, replacing Sessegnon, who was impressive in the first half but looked to be running out of steam in this second period. Can the youngster inspire an unlikely comback for Mel's side?
(75’) Foster fires a stunning ball from right to left out to Ridgewell, who controls beautifully with his chest and lays off to Brunt. It's fired in towards Anichebe but City manage to hack the ball clear for a throw on West Brom's right-hand side.
(74’) West Brom have a free kick inside the City half, but unfortunately Brunt's delivery is again poor as Hart claims comfortably. The Baggies skipper will be disappointed with his crossing tonight.
(73’) JOVETIC!! The substitute is looking lively and pounces on a loose ball in midfield, before charging past Dorrans and firing a low 25-yarder which skips just wide of Foster's post.
(72’) Good work from Anichebe, who holds off Demichelis in midfield and spreads the ball out to the left. Brunt has another chance to cross but it's a disappointing delivery which goes straight into Hart's arms.
(71’) AMALFITANO!! West Brom have really livened up since that stoppage!! Brunt fires it in from the left and Clichy does well to head it away at the far post, but Amalfitano collects it on the edge of the box before drilling a low shot across goal, which Hart does well to parry away from danger.
(70’) We're back underway and Milner is on for City as we enter the final 20 minutes. West Brom have the ball inside the City half but the hosts are pressing well. Anichebe does well to knock down Brunt's cross from the left but Amalfitano's follow-up is blocked.
--- 69’ Substitution David Silva is replaced with J. Milner. ---
(69’) Silva is being taken off to a standing ovation from the home fans. It looks like his right leg has been put in a brace. Pellegrini - and Spain coach Vicente del Bosque - will be fearing the worst.
(68’) The stretcher is on and there are some concerned looks among the City ranks. James Milner is preparing to come on, but that could be a real blow to the hosts' title charge for the remainder of the season.
(67’) Another worry for City, here. Silva is down after trying to hold off a challenge from Jones. This doesn't look good at all - could be another injury to that ankle.
(66’) Zabaleta sells Fernandinho short with a poor pass and West Brom have a rare chance to break. Sessegnon collects it in the middle and charges towards goal, but Demichelis slides in well before committing fully to win the second ball. Great defending.
(65’) Yet more City possession now, with Silva seemingly involved in every other pass. It remains measured, though, as they continue to take their time to move the ball around with West Brom sitting back.
--- 64’ Substitution S. Jovetić comes on for S. Agüero. ---
(64’) Pellegrini has decided to make a change, now, as Stefan Jovetic replaces Aguero, who trudges off slightly gingerly after that earlier knock. The rehabilitation continues, though, and the striker will be delighted to have got on the scoresheet.
(63’) Finally, West Brom get a rare spell of possession of their own, but the chance goes begging as Sessegnon knocks the ball past Zabaleta down the left, but overruns it slightly and it just goes over the line for a goal kick.
(62’) Nasri and Silva link up for the umpteenth time in midfield, and the latter looks to feed a pass through for Aguero beyond the defende, but Olsson watches it well to cut it out and prevent any danger.
(61’) Aguero sprays the ball out to the left for Clichy, who has plenty of time and chooses to use it, slowing down the attack as he squares to Fernandinho and City eventually go backwards again.
--- 60’ Substitution V. Anichebe comes on for M. Vydra. ---
(60’) Silva plays another threaded pass through, again looking for the run of Nasri, who chases it down the right but Olsson comes across well to clear the ball out for a throw to the hosts.
(59’) It looks like West Brom are preparing a change, which Victor Anichebe coming on for Vydra. This could add a bit more presence up front for the visitors, and provides a different test for Kompany and Demichelis.
(58’) NASRI SHOULD SCORE!! It's amazing how quickly the hosts can change gear, and Silva sets it going as he plays into the path of Nasri, who gives it back to Silva on the right. He flicks it on for Zabaleta, whose first-time cross is met by Nasri but the Frenchman can't divert it towards goal and it flicks off Olsson before going behind.
(57’) You could take out a third of the pitch at the moment - Joe Hart is all on his own in City's final third. The hosts are passing it around in a very controlled manner right now, and West Brom are chasing shadows.
(56’) Kompany fires a diagonal ball towards the edge of the box, but Olsson deals with it well, sending it back to Foster who hammers it into the City half. The Baggies are struggling to get any meaningful periods of possession together at the moment.
(55’) Zabaleta fires in a cross to the edge of the box and Aguero picks it up, producing a heavy touch but still managing to hold on to possession. He eventually loses out to Ridgewell and stays down for a few moments. City fans will be hoping he can run it off.
(54’) Aguero and Dzeko link up well on the left before Jones holds off the Argentina man to win it back for West Brom, who come forward along their left-hand side, but again they surrender possession easily.
(53’) Mulumbu does well to charge in and get hold of the loose ball in midfield, and he spreads it out to the left-hand side. Brunt has just one target in Vydra, and looks for him with an ambitious cross which Hart plucks out of the air with ease.
(52’) More danger for West Brom as Dzeko plays the ball into Silva with his back to goal, and the midfielder produces another silky touch to lay off for Nasri, who shifts on to his right before seeing his shot blocked by Olsson.
(51’) CHANCE!! Garcia spreads the ball wide to Nasri, whose drilled low cross is just cut out ahead of Dzeko, before Zabaleta has an effort at goal which deflects just wide of the post with Foster stranded.
(50’) It's all a bit stop-start and scrappy at the moment as the whistle goes again, this time in West Brom's favour as Dzeko is caught offside. City quickly get the ball back, though, and advance ominously into the West Brom half.
(49’) Kompany's diagonal ball forward is easily cut out by Jones, who charges down the right flank and forces a throw off Clichy inside the City half. He hasn't been able to get forward that much tonight. The visitors surrender possession again, though, as Amalfitano fouls Clichy near the corner flag.
(48’) Silva slides the ball into Aguero, but his touch is loose and Mulumbu holds the striker off to win the ball for the visitors. They move forward in numbers and Brunt looks for Dorrans down the left, but the midfielder is just offside and City get possession back once more.
(47’) Demichelis gives it away in midfield, but Amalfitano can't make the most of it as Clichy stops him in his tracks. It's a steadier start to this half than the first from City, who will want to add more goals to their tally, especially if the title race could come down to goal difference.
(46’) The hosts resume proceedings at the Etihad as the second half gets underway.
Right then, just a couple of minutes until the restart. How's this one going to finish? I don't know about you, but I'd take another goal-filled 45 minutes, whatever happens.
Is there a way back into this for Mel's men? Or are City going to run away with the game? Be sure to stick with us when we come back for the second half at the Etihad.
Silva and Fernandinho have been dominant in midfield for Pellegrini's men, although the former possibly needs to take more shots. Sessegnon has been lively for the visitors and is causing problems with his pace, but all in all it's looking reasonably comfortable for City.
That's HALF TIME at the Etihad and Man City go in 3-1 up over West Brom thanks to goals from their Argentina trio. The visitors showed promise and got back into the game through Dorrans, but Demichelis' tap-in restored the two-goal lead and looks to have set the hosts on their way to three points.
(45’) It's a poor effort from the West Brom skipper, who gets his shot over the wall, but also well over Hart's goal as it flies behind for a goal kick, and that could well be that for the half.
(45’) There's yet more dithering with the wall as the referee makes sure they're 10 yards away. Brunt is lining this one up...
(45’) Dzeko collects the ball from deep and charges down the right flank, but is easily tackled by Ridgewell before the visitors move forward and Garcia brings down Amalfitano around 30 yards from goal. We'll have two minutes of stoppage time - can the visitors pull one back here?
(44’) City clear the corner but it comes back in towards Sessegnon at the near post. Kompany is there, though, to deal with the danger and clear behind.
(43’) SO CLOSE FROM SESSEGNON!! Brunt spreads the ball wide to Dawson, who exchanges passes with Amalfitano before drilling the ball low into the area. Sessegnon finds half a yard and gets a first-time effort away, but it deflects off Kompany and loops just over the crossbar.
(42’) Silva does well to win the ball off Sessegnon in the City half and the hosts break forward as he finds Dzeko, but the striker's cross from the left doesn't find a team-mate as Olsson heads clear before Mulumbu is fouled just outside the box.
(41’) Into the final five minutes of the half, and City are stroking it around very nicely in midfield...before Zabaleta gives it straight back to the visitors with a wayward pass down the right as he ends up on a different wavelength to Aguero.
(40’) Mulumbu plays a wonderful pass out to Brunt on the left-hand side, and the West Brom skipper has plenty of time out on the flank, but wastes his chance as he produces an uncharacteristically poor cross, slicing it straight out for a goal kick.
(39’) Another lovely move from City sees Dzeko drive in from the right and play the ball into Fernandinho, who lays it off for the Bosnia striker, and he tries a speculative first-time effort from 30 yards which goes straight into Foster's arms.
(38’) The pressure relents slightly as the visitors win a corner, but Kompany wins it back in midfield before showing some fancy footwork to keep hold of the ball. Not bad for a centre-back!
(37’) Mel will be very disappointed with the marking at that corner, and there's more danger as the hosts win another, but Dorrans does well to head this one away at the near post.
--- 36’ Goal! GOOOOOALLL!! DEMICHELIS MAKES IT 3-1!! The visitors deal with the first delivery but City quickly win another, and Nasri swings in a lovely ball to the near post. Kompany flicks a header on and Demichelis is unmarked at the far post to put away a simple tap-in. ---
(34’) West Brom have a chance to go forward as Amalfitano advances down the right, but Sessegnon loses out as he falls over when going past Fernandinho. Kompany then cuts out a pass intended for Vydra before setting up a quick counter, which sees Dzeko's snap shot deflect behind for a corner.
(33’) Silva is again involved as he holds the ball off Mulumbu and moves towards the left, but Clichy is too far back and he has no option but to turn back around and go right, slowing down the move in the process.
(32’) Inside the final 15 minutes of the half, and it feels like West Brom's fightback has fizzled out. Pellegrini's men are slowly turning the screw once more and you wouldn't bet against them adding to their lead before the break.

In the reverse match at Carrow Road earlier in the season, Fulham came from behind to win. The same will be required of Norwich now if they are to avoid getting sucked into the relegation zone.
