--- 64’ Yellow card G. Dorrans goes into the referee's book. ---
(64’) SUPERB SAVE! Campbell lashes an effort from just inside the box that draws a fantastic diving save from Foster, who palms it out to Bellamy, who fails to create a chance for himself.
(62’) Zaha - who could have had a shot himself - lays it off to Bellamy, whose shot hits the legs of Ridgewell and rebounds away. The Welsh outfit are stepping it up here.
(60’) BLOCKED! Caulker throws his body in the way of a bullet of a shot from Dorrans after a good counter attack from the home side. The Bluebirds captain will be feeling that in the morning!

(56’) STAT ATTACK: Only Fulham have kept fewer clean sheets in the Premier League than West Brom's five.
(54’) Bellamy gets in round the back of the Baggies defense and twists and turns to make room for a pass to Campbell, but the striker's run is not to the former Wales International's satisfaction and he gives him a volley of verbal after being dispossessed.
(52’) GREAT SAVE! What a brilliant stop from Marshall. Vydra connects with the ball and is thwarted by the stopper and Dorrans blasts over the rebound. Pepe Mel is hopping mad on the touchline!
(50’) DEFLECTED WIDE! The hosts have come out with fire in their bellies as Cardiff fail to clear a free-kick. It falls to Mulumbu, whose low effort takes a deflection off his own players and out for a goal kick.
(48’) OVER AND OUT! The visitors are on the backfoot from the restart as Sessegnon wins a corner on the left. Dorrans delivery causes confusion in the box and the ball falls to Dawson, who blasts the ball over from close range.

(46’) The Bluebirds get us back underway, kicking from left to right. Can they get back in this match?
HALF TIME - WEST BROM 2-1 CARDIFF. A compelling contest sees the Baggies leading at the break with two early goals from Amalfitano and Dorrans putting Pepe Mel's men in cruise control before the ten minute mark. But Jordan Mutch's cross/shot has installed an air of nerves in the home side and it's all to play for after the break!
(45’) Sessegnon has had a disappointing afternoon so far on the left flank and again a short pass fails to reach Vydra, leading to groans from the home support. It's as if someone has broken into The Hawthorns with an atmosphere hoover!
(45’) There will be THREE minutes of added on time.
(44’) OVER! Vydra wins a contentious free-kick on the edge of the box for the hosts. Dorrans lines up the set piece, but his effort is tame and floats over the bar and out of danger.
(42’) WELL WIDE! Bellamy lays the ball off for Medel, who strikes from 25 yards out. But the former Sevilla man's body shape is all out and he blasts it into the crowd.
(40’) With five minutes to go, the Baggies are starting to come back into the action here. They have not created many chances since the second goal and Cardiff have begun to look more threatening. Is it possible that the winning manager will be the least happiest at half time?
(38’) EASY SAVE! The atmosphere within The Hawthorns has well and truly changed. Mulumbu works some space for himself but his low shot is saved by Marshall.
--- 36’ Substitution Fábio is replaced with W. Zaha. ---
(36’) Zaha is being prepared on the sidelines as it looks like Fabio has pulled up with a niggle. Or is it a tactical change for Solskjaer? Either way, it's one Man United loanee being replaced by another - can he make the difference?
(34’) The Bluebirds look reinvigorated by that strike and it has breathed life into this game again. Now it's Pepe Mel's turn to look pensive in the technical area.
(32’) STAT ATTACK: Before Mutch's goal, Cardiff had only scored EIGHT first half goals in the Premier League all season.
--- 30’ Assist A. Gunnarsson provided the assist. ---
--- 30’ Goal! J. Mutch hits the net for Cardiff City! ---
(30’) GOAL! Cardiff are right back in this! Mutch takes the ball down to the right of the box and loops a cross into the area, but it looks like his effort is caught by the wind and it curls into Foster's top corner. Well, well, well. I didn't see that coming!
(28’) Dorrans and Vydra are linking nicely and causing all sorts of problems in the area. This time the striker is played in by the goalscorer but Caulker is there to put the ball out into touch.
(25’) Cardiff are still showing a lack of tenacity and Mutch is cutting a frustrated figure in the middle of the park. The crowd are lifting the home side as the Baggies continue to dominate.
(23’) HALF CHANCE: Caulker meets Bellamy's corner but heads it straight up in the air and it is dealt with by Foster, who wins a free-kick following a melee in the six-yard-box.
(21’) Foster has to be quick at getting to a backpass from Reid and just manages to boot it away as Bellamy charges in. Still no signs of encouragement from the away side.
(19’) STAT ATTACK: Cardiff have lost eight of Solskjaer's 11 league games in charge (W2, D1, L8).
(17’) In comparison, this is the most explosive start the Baggies have made all season. But if they take their foot off the pedal, maybe a window of opportunity will open up for Solskjaer's men.
(15’) The visitors look so shaken right now and are struggling to build up a cohesive pattern of play. Is their afternoon - indeed season - over already?
(13’) STAT ATTACK: West Brom have lost just one of the last seven home league games, albeit against Manchester United in their last game at The Hawthorns (W1, D5, L1)
(11’) The Bluebirds just have not turned up here and Solskjaer is screaming at his charges from the dugout. Where do they go from here? Meanwhile, the home support have a minutes applause in tribute to club legend Jeff Astle. How the Bluebirds could do with a striker like him today.

(4’) The visitors are looking so nervous at the back today as Taylor struggles to clear a Ridgewell cross from the left. Marshall is then also called into action. It's all going on here.

Hello! Good afternoon and welcome to this crucial Premier League clash between West Brom and Cardiff. I am Hayden Gribble and I shall be your guide through all the ups and downs of what could prove to be a defining game for both these struggling sides. Let's get the team news...

That's all we have time for from the Emirates, as Arsenal and Man City couldn't separate themselves from one another in a hard fought 1-1 draw - leaving three teams still in the title race. I've been Simon Harrison, and I hope to see you again next time.
It's a useful point for Man City, with the Premier League title remaining firmly in Pellegrini's men's hands, while Arsenal continue their excellent home form. A late goal wasn't forthcoming for the hosts, but the Gunners can certainly take some positive from a battling performance.
FULL TIME! Arsenal grind out a 1-1 draw against Man City in the Emirates, in a game of two halves! A great visiting performance in the first half saw David Silva fortunately give the Citizens the lead, before a resurgent second half Arsenal side grabbed an equaliser through Mathieu Flamini.
(90’) NEGREDO! The former Sevilla former breaks down the left hand side with nobody in support, forcing the Spaniard to go it alone. He tries to chip Szczesny from a very tight angle, but gets it all wrong. So very wrong.
(90’) OXLADE-CHAMBERLAIN! Sanogo manages to win his aerial battle at the back post, turning a corner delivery square, but the substitute isn't able to turn the ball home with an acrobatic volley attempt! Hart is able to collect the scraps.
(90’) There are three minutes of stoppage time left for either side to grab a winner, with the home supporters urging their side on!
(90’) Cazorla has the opportunity to whip a free-kick delivery into a loaded penalty area from 30 yards out, but Hart is quick off his line to punch the cross clear of the danger area. Arsenal are pressing forward in these late stages, which would leave them susceptible to a late sky blue counter!
--- 89’ Yellow card Javi García goes into the referee's book. ---
(88’) Sanogo may not be the most prolific striker, but the young Frenchman provides Arsenal with another option for pressing Man City's central defenders. Both managers would take a point so late in the game, but the last few minutes could have a twist in the tale yet.
(86’) Giroud leaves the field without a goal against a top seven club once again, making it 22 games and merely three goals against such opposition this season. Rosicky slides in on David Silva, giving away a free-kick, with the Czech midfielder lucky to escape a second yellow card.
--- 85’ Substitution Y. Sanogo enters play, replacing O. Giroud. ---
--- 85’ Substitution Negredo enters play, replacing E. Džeko. ---
(84’) The full time whistle is edging ever closer, with Oxlade-Chamberlain finally providing some pace for the home side, to enable them to try and get in behind Clichy. Negredo comes on for the away side, replacing Dzeko, who hasn't been readily involved in the second half action at all.
(82’) Giroud looks to receive the ball into feet on the edge of the 18-yard box, but Kompany is quick to pressure the lone forward and rob him of the ball. The Belgian has had an answer for everything that Giroud has managed to come up with thus far.
--- 81’ Substitution Javi García enters the game and replaces S. Nasri. ---
(80’) Ten minutes left on the clock and the nerves in this stadium are nearly tangible! Man City opt to make a change, with Javi Garcia replacing Samir Nasri, as Pellegrini might be trying to shut up shop. Arsenal haven't lost here in the Premier League since the opening day of the season, a point would be excellent for the Citizens.
--- 79’ Substitution A. Oxlade-Chamberlain enters the game and replaces L. Podolski. ---
(78’) GIROUD! That's a poor effort! Rosicky slides a pass into his teammate, before the Frenchman sidesteps Demichelis! He decides to pull the trigger from the edge of the penalty area, with Kompany closing him down, but drags his shot awfully wide.
(77’) Plenty of nervous faces in the Emirates now, as Man City start to really look dominant. Their previous comfortable spell resulted in David Silva's opener, but Arsenal are looking much more resilient this side of half time. Oxlade-Chamberlain is warming up intensely for the home side.
(75’) YAYA TOURE! NASRI! DZEKO! Three chances in five seconds for Man City, as Toure manages to get in behind and bait Szczesny out from his goalline. The Ivorian tries to lift the ball over the Poland international from a narrow angle, but sees it blocked, before Nasri and Dzeko's later efforts on the rebound result in the same outcome!
(74’) Man City are patient, building up slowly and not rushing into making risky passes. They know that they've got the quality to hurt Arsenal, it's just a matter of retaining the ball in the right areas. The hosts are happy to sit deep.
(72’) GIROUD! A free-kick from deep is thrown into the Man City penalty area, with the Arsenal forward able to outjump Fernandinho and meet the ball! It's slightly too high for him, however, and the Frenchman can't turn his header towards goal! He curls up his hands in frustration.
(70’) Twenty minutes left on the clock and this game is still firmly in the balance! Both sides have had their chances, but neither have been able to find the back of the net in the second half, despite plenty of corners and crosses apiece.
(68’) Important header from Mertesacker! Dzeko is lurking in behind Arsenal's lines, but the German central defender manages to meet Clichy's attempted through ball. Plenty of substitutes are warming up, but both managers are keeping their cards close to their chest.
(66’) Milner and David Silva combine to release Zabaleta down the right hand side, before the Argentine swings in a delivery which is just too high for Dzeko to meet! This game is very finely balanced, with a moment of brilliance perhaps likely to settle it. Silva goes for the outrageous, but drags a 30-yard strike way wide.
--- 65’ Substitution J. Milner comes on for Jesús Navas. ---
(64’) FLAMINI! The Frenchman finds himself in the Man City penalty area yet again, but this time he can't find his goalscoring touch! From an outrageous angle, he tries to fire an effort across Joe Hart, but his shot balloons way over the bar.
(63’) FERNANDINHO! The Brazilian now goes close from range, with Szczesny pushing the former Shakhtar man's powerful effort over the crossbar for a corner! The set piece is taken short and then flung into the box, but Szczesny claims at the front post.
(62’) SILVA! Navas wins a free-kick, going down under a slight shove from Podolski, which Nasri steps up to take from the right flank. It's clipped towards David Silva at the edge of the penalty area, who strikes it on the volley, but his powerful effort strikes a sky blue shirt!
(60’) PODOLSKI! The hour mark is upon us, with Arsenal looking resurgent. Flamini's goal has given them renewed belief and they almost take the lead! The hosts get some good fortune, with the Germany international getting in behind Man City's defence courtesy of a lucky deflection, but Hart makes himself big and deflects Podolski's effort behind for a corner with a flailing leg!
(58’) The lack of pace is still startling, but Arsenal are getting some joy from moving the ball from side to side at pace. If Podolski or Sagna are given half a yard to deliver a cross, there's a good chance that Giroud can gamble and look to get on the end of said delivery.
(56’) The home fans are jubilant and Arsenal are in the ascendancy! Man City are trying to claw back some control, but Flamini's goal has blown this wide open as a contest! There's renewed belief and despite a lack of changes, the Gunners look capable of going on to win this game!
(54’) WHAT A CROSS! Sagna puts a fantastic delivery into the box, it zips across the length of the six yard box, with Demichelis choosing to let the ball go past him rather than attempt to make a risky clearance! Somehow, despite the quality of ball, it doesn't result in a goal!
--- 53’ Assist L. Podolski provided the assist. ---
--- 53’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOAL! ARSENAL ARE LEVEL AND IT'S MATHIEU FLAMINI! Podolski picks out a good cut-back, before Flamini diverts the cross into the far corner, guiding it beyond a sprawling Joe Hart from 12 yards! The Gunners are right back in this game and Man City know it! ---
(52’) Great cross from Navas! Gibbs is well beaten by the former Sevilla man, before Szczesny fails to claim the low drive! It somehow ends up zipping past the post, with Dzeko wondering how he didn't manage to turn the ball home! Arsenal break themselves, but Hart is just about equal to a long-range Cazorla strike!
(50’) The Gunners have been able to move the ball with pace in the opening minutes of the second half, but ultimately the hosts end up making their way down a cul-de-sac. Gibbs breaks down the left hand side, but Zabaleta tracks him all the way, before sliding in to dispossess the Englishman.
(48’) Arsenal manage to get Demichelis turned for the first time this evening and Giroud almost manages to slip into the penalty area! Kompany covers well to rob the ball from the toe of the former Montpellier man. The home side need more of that, Demichelis isn't the quickest.
(46’) We're back underway in the second half! Arsenal need a goal from somewhere, with Man City looking comfortable for long periods in the first half, though Olivier Giroud has only managed three goals in his 21 games against the Premier League's top seven sides.
Be sure to stick around for all of the second half action, with both sides still having a realistic chance of leaving the Emirates tonight with three points. Both managers have quality replacements on the bench at their disposal to change the game, as Arsenal look to mount a comeback to keep their slim title hopes alive, promising us a brilliant upcoming 45 minutes.
Given the nature of the lead, Man City certainly aren't home and dry yet, but have looked far more dangerous than the opposition, while being able to defend confidently. The away side have held their line well, with crosses from Arsenal's right flank being the only cause for concern.
The Gunners have moved the ball well at times, but have no pace to get in behind Man City. Kompany and Demichelis have enjoyed playing with both the ball and their man in front of them for the entire first half, with a change of tact needed for Arsenal.
HALF TIME! The Citizens head into the dressing room a goal to the good, with a David Silva goal leaving the scoreline at 1-0. Arsenal haven't played badly, but lack a cutting edge to hurt the visitors. Man City are in control, but with a couple of changes, Arsenal could well turn this game around - they're still in it!
--- 45’ +1 Yellow card David Silva is cautioned by the referee. ---
(45’) Mikel Arteta is caught late by a bad challenge from his compatriot David Silva, leaving the former Rangers midfielder on the turf in a heap - earning the ex-Valencia man a yellow card. There are two minutes of stoppage time.
(44’) A few minutes until the break and Man City remain in total control, moving the ball with purpose and direction. Meanwhile, Arsenal are able to burst upfield quickly, finding the likes of Giroud or Podolski with direct passes, but the lack of support sees the move peter out almost before it started.
--- 42’ Yellow card T. Rosický receives a yellow card. ---
(42’) David Silva is just too good, it's as though the ball is glued to his foot. He controls a Demichelis header beautifully, before pivoting sharply to escape Flamini. Rosicky then throws himself into a risky challenge with Gael Clichy, but it's only more reason for the home crowd to adore him.
(40’) Man City are winning all of the second balls, with the leading side continuing to look competitive and strong. Tomas Rosicky is leading the home charge, pressing like a maniac, earning him applause from the Gunners fans. You can't fault his commitment.
(38’) Less than ten minutes until the break, but an equaliser isn't looking too likely for Arsenal. Crosses from the advancing Sagna appear to be their best chance of threatening, but the likes of Kompany and Demichelis can certainly hold their own in aerial duels.
(36’) Man City hold their line well, as a Sagna cross is angled in the general direction of three Arsenal shirts. Fernandinho manages to beat Giroud to the delivery excellently, but it wouldn't have counted anyway, as the linesman's flag is raised for offside once again.
(35’) Good clearance from Demichelis! Podolski is released down the left hand side by an excellent crossfield ball, before the former Bayern Munich forward turns a cross in towards the near post with Giroud lurking. Demichelis hurtles back towards his own goal, before turning the ball behind for a corner.
--- 33’ Yellow card V. Kompany is yellow-carded. ---
(33’) Fantastic challenge from Kompany! Giroud drives towards the edge of the penalty area, but the Frenchman is stopped by a sliding tackle from the Belgian which was timed to perfection. The follow through catches Giroud's ankle, leaving the Arsenal forward grounded for a few moments, but he'll be okay to continue.
(32’) Man City take their turn to dominate possession, with Jesus Navas making positive runs off the ball in the hope of getting in behind Gibbs yet again. Arsenal need the likes of Navas and Silva in their side this evening, they've got no means of getting in behind the organised Man City lines.
--- 31’ Yellow card Y. Touré is yellow-carded. ---
(30’) NASRI! The former Gunner tries his luck from 25 yards, but his low drive is dealt with comfortably by Szczesny. It was well within the reach of the gangly goalkeeper, but it's another warning sign for the home side.
(28’) Man City still hold the upper hand as the half hour mark approaches, with Arsenal still not having a lethal weapon to pierce the visiting defence. Giroud has been used well as a wall, but the home side can't get in behind the Citizens. Theo Walcott would make a profound difference on this game.
(26’) Great interception from Kompany! Cazorla shows his technical ability by quickly shifting the ball between his feet, sidestepping a challenge, before trying to thread a through ball into the penalty area for Giroud to chase. The Belgium international steps out smartly to cut out the pass.
(24’) GIROUD! Great cross by Sagna, as the France international again bombs on down the right flank before whipping in a delivery for Giroud! Hart is quick off his line to rise brilliantly and claim. The ball seemed to hang in the air for an eternity!
(23’) An audacious effort from Giroud! The Frenchman clearly saw Wayne Rooney's goal against West Ham and thought he could do the same! He spirals a long-range strike towards Hart's goal, but the England international goalkeeper is confident enough to control the ball with his feet. Not quite what Giroud was looking for.
(22’) OFFSIDE! Flamini turns home inside the penalty area, but the linesman's flag is raised! Man City keep a brilliant line, so although the former Milan midfielder acrobatically looped Podolski's cross into the back of the net, it won't count! It's a good decision from the officials.
(20’) Man City aren't afraid to keep pressing, with Gibbs forced to turn a back post cross behind for a corner. Arsenal aren't looking too confident, although they've held onto the ball for reasonable spells, they don't seem to have a way of harming the away side. Szczesny is called into action to punch a Navas cross away.
--- 18’ Goal! GOOOOOOAL! DAVID SILVA GIVES MAN CITY A 1-0 LEAD! The visitors break wonderfully, with Silva sliding the ball out to left hand side, before Dzeko thumped an effort against the near post! The rebound is kind to Pellegrini's men, with the loose ball falling to David Silva deep in the penalty box, who turns the ball home! ---
(17’) Nervy moment from Szczesny! A Nasri strike is blocked by a sliding Mertesacker challenge, with the ball looping into the air and coming down to land in the Arsenal shot-stopper's grasp. With Dzeko lurking, he momentarily drops the ball, but quickly reclaims it at the second attempt.
(16’) Excellent control from Giroud! The former Montpellier man plucks the ball out of the sky despite significant pressure from Zabaleta, earning him the applause of the Emirates. Arsenal continue to stroke the ball around well, though Man City have the pace and quality to hurt the Gunners on the counter.
(15’) The opening quarter of an hour has passed without either goalkeeper being called upon to make a save, but the contest itself has been enthralling. Both sides are taking it in turns to enjoy spells of possession and there's a real ebb and flow about this one.
(13’) Rosicky and Giroud exchange possession well, before Kompany comes across definitively to take the ball from the latter. Arsenal are looking a little bit better, enjoying a spell of possession and getting plenty of the ball into Rosicky. Wenger really does like playing him in the big occasions due to his experience and intelligence on the field.
(12’) Arsenal want a penalty! Rosicky bursts into the penalty area, before sidestepping around the challenge of Zabaleta, but the experienced midfielder picks up a yellow card for his trouble. That was probably a dive, Rosicky did leave his foot trailing, expecting some contact from his Argentine adversary.
(10’) NAVAS! A dodgy effort from the Spain international, as he balloons a shot high and wide from a very tight angle. Man City's right flank has been able to provide great joy in the opening ten minutes, Gibbs looks unable to contend with the pace and trickery of Navas.
(9’) The Gunners continue to do all of the early chasing, with Man City looking like the home side. The hosts are happy to sit in their shape, but don't have an outlet to break quickly, with Giroud not blessed with much pace. Advantage to the Citizens thus far.
(7’) Sagna is forced into a rushed clearance, after a Navas cross is deflected wide of Dzeko and towards the back post. Arsenal have their backs to the wall already, the sky blue tide is relentless. Pellegrini's men are holding onto the ball well, with Gibbs being isolated easily.
(6’) Good work by Navas once again! Zabaleta and the former Sevilla winger are combining brilliantly down the right, with Gibbs already struggling to keep his man in front of him. Another cross from the Argentine full-back is dealt with firmly by the head of Mertesacker.
(5’) Man City break upfield, but Rosicky gets back well to rob Dzeko of the ball, after the Bosnia international took a heavy touch. The home fans are already uneasy and didn't take too well to Giroud losing the ball early on. The French striker needs a big performance to silence his critics this evening.
(3’) NAVAS! Two chances in the space of 30 seconds for Man City! Zabaleta is able to get to the byeline and cut a ball back in search of a sky blue shirt, but Vermaelen intercepts. Moments later, another visiting cross is half-cleared, before Navas curled a bending effort narrowly wide of the top left hand corner.
(2’) Terrible first clearance from Szczesny, as the Polish goalkeeper arrows his first touch of the ball out of play under no pressure. That won't settle the nerves! Man City look comfortable, on the other hand, moving the ball smoothly in the opening exchanges.
(1’) We're underway in the first half! This game has huge repurcussions on the rest of the league table, so don't go anywhere! Man City are favourites on paper, but Arsenal have made the Emirates a fortress this season, with a win potentially helping Gunners' supporters to forget the 6-0 thrashing at the hands of Chelsea.
With five minutes until kick-off, be sure to stick around as this game helps to define the Premier League season. With Man City looks to capitalise on Chelsea's shortcomings earlier, Pellegrini's men have to win at all costs, with their ex-Arsenal players determined to get one over on their former employers. As for Arsenal, if they don't win tonight, their unlikely challenge for the title is dead and buried.
Arsenal have won merely two of their last five games, but the Gunners have only suffered defeat once at home since last October. After conceding late against Swansea last time out, the home side will be keen to get back on track with a result against one of the favourites for the Premier League title. Man City head into this clash with three wins on the trot, as momentum certainly sides with the Citizens.

My name's Ben Cullimore and it's been an absolute pleasure describing the action to you this afternoon. Have a great rest of the weekend and make sure you tune into the live text commentary of the next Premier League clash between Liverpool and Tottenham Hotspur. Until next time, goodbye!
As for Fulham, the dark clouds of relegation are looming over Craven Cottage. They remain bottom of the table, five points from safety and with the poorest goal difference by some distance. A win away to Aston Villa next Saturday is vital.
The win moves Everton to just four points behind fourth-place Arsenal, and with a game in hand. They meet the Gunners at Goodison Park next Sunday in what is sure to be a truly exhilarating clash. Champions League football is a real possibility for the Toffees, and they certainly deserve it.
That really was a game of two halves. Everton looked like a completely different team in the second half and showed exactly why they are in contention for a Champions League spot. Naismith had a huge impact after his introduction at half-time and, despite their best efforts, Fulham weren't able to deal with the strength and skill of a very impressive Everton team.
FT: FULHAM 1-3 EVERTON
(90’) Chance for Everton! Mirallas blasts a shot from the right of the Fulham box, but it flies just past the far post and the Belgian is denied his second goal of the game.
(90’) Fulham are looking dejected as they try to string together some sort of attack in the hope of pulling off an almighty comeback. Dejagah is able to shoot on goal from the edge of the penalty area, but it's only half a chance, and one that Howard can deal with easily.
(90’) There will be four minutes of added time.
(89’) Chance for Everton! Naismith is in acres of space and darts forward into the Fulham half with the ball at his feet. He looks up and sees no white shirts around him so he decides to shoot from 25 yards out. It beats Stockdale and bounces off the post and into the feet of Baines, but the ball is coming at him too quickly and it ricochets off his shin and out for a goalkick.
--- 87’ Assist Assist by L. Baines. ---
--- 87’ Goal! GOAL! There it is; Naismith has scored and the three points will be going back to Goodison Park with Everton. Fulham's defenders, who have looked tired and nervous since the visitors scored their second goal, fail to deal with Mirallas, bringing the Belgian to the ground and allowing the ball to end up in the feet of Baines, who sets up Naismith in front of goal for a simple tap-in. 3-1! ---
(85’) Fulham's forwards are searching desperately for an equalising goal but look incredibly tired and devoid of any ideas when on the ball. Meanwhile, at the back, mistakes are being made by their defenders, and Everton look close to grabbing a third goal, which will surely seal the win.
(83’) Chance for Everton! Lukaku places a wonderful ball through the middle of the Fulham defence to set up Naismith, but the Scotsman's shot is saved well by Stockdale.
--- 81’ Substitution P. Roberts comes on for M. Dembele. ---
(81’) Hangeland is caught in possession and gives the ball away to Mirallas, who has injected a sense of urgency into his side since coming on. He darts towards goal from the right hand side of the box but the ball is cleared away for a corner, which amounts to little.
--- 79’ Assist A. McGeady provided the assist. ---
--- 79’ Goal! GOAL! A thrilling few minutes has culminated in another Everton goal. McGeady picks out fellow substitute Mirallas with a world class through-ball, and the Belgian has no trouble calmly placing the ball past Stockdale. 2-1! ---
--- 77’ Substitution L. Osman is replaced with A. McGeady. ---
(77’) Chance for Everton! Coleman bursts down the left flank and sends a deep cross towards McCarthy, who shoots towards the far post, beating Stockdale but also beating the upright.
--- 75’ Yellow card L. Baines is yellow-carded. ---
(75’) Chance after chance for Fulham! First, Holtby sends a great free kick towards Heitinga at the back post, who is completely unmarked. Howard saves his headed effort but the ball ends up with Dembele, whose half-volley is blocked and sent out to Dejagah on the right wing. The Iranian twists and turns before setting up Kasami, who fires a shot towards goal that, again, Howard saves wonderfully.
(73’) Everton look fired up. Stones sends a beautiful ball across to Baines on the left wing, and he crosses into the middle of the Fulham box. The Cottagers' defenders half deal with the danger, but the ball ends up with Distin, whose shot on goal fails to beat the plethora of white shirts in front of him and is then cleared up towards the other end of the pitch.
--- 71’ Assist The assist came from S. Sidwell. ---
--- 71’ Goal! GOAL! Fulham have equalised through a wonderful long-range goal from Dejagah! The Iranian, who has been fantastic since coming on only six minutes ago, is given far too much time and space by the Everton defenders, and he punishes them by unleashing a rocket of a shot from the edge of the penalty area that flies past Howard and into the back of the net. 1-1! ---
(71’) Lukaku is set up on the left wing and tries to push his way into Fulham's penalty area, but Hangeland out-muscles the big Belgian and stops him in his tracks.
(69’) Fulham win a corner through Dejagah down the left flank. Hangeland flies through the air and almost meets the ball with his head, but it skims just past the Norwegian's airborne figure.
--- 68’ Substitution K. Mirallas enters play, replacing Gerard Deulofeu. ---
(67’) Everton break away on another attack, with Naismith and Osman linking up well just outside Fulham's penalty area, but their former teammate Heitinga is on hand to cut out the danger before they are able to penetrate the box.
--- 65’ Substitution K. Richardson is replaced with A. Dejagah. ---
--- 65’ Substitution W. Kvist is done for the day. C. Woodrow is his replacement. ---
(65’) Chance for Everton! Fulham are too indecisive in their own box, allowing Lukaku to muscle his way onto the ball and fire a venomous shot towards Stockdale, which the goalkeeper does well to parry away with his feet.
(63’) Chance for Everton! Deulofeu weaves in and out of the Everton defence before crossing towards Lukaku, but the ball goes just over the Belgian's head. They retain possession, however, and it ends up with the young Spaniard again, who sets up Baines on the edge of the box, but the left-back's first touch lets him down and Fulham are able to clear the ball back up the pitch.
(61’) Fulham win a corner, which Holtby whips in. Sidwell meets it with his head, but it's too high and powerful and it flies out for a goal kick.
(59’) Naismith has been fantastic since coming on at half-time! This time, a wonderful pass finds Baines in front of goal, but his effort skims just wide of the far post, where Lukaku was rushing towards.
(57’) Everton look full of life and far more confident after the goal. Deulofeu remains incredibly dangerous down the right wing and is causing all sorts of problems for Riise.
(55’) Fulham break away again, this time down the opposite wing, but Kasami's cross is uncharacteristically poor and fails to clear the first line of blue shirts.
(53’) Richardson rushes down the left flank before sending a looping cross in towards Dembele, but Howard looms large over the youngster and is able to scoop the ball from in front of his head with one hand.
--- 51’ Goal! GOAL! Heartbreak for Fulham as Everton grab the first goal. The Cottagers fail to deal with a corner and it ends up with Naismith on the edge of the penalty area. He volleys the ball towards goal and it deflects off Kvist before bouncing off Stockdale's legs and into the back of the net. 1-0! ---
(50’) Richardson rushes into Everton's half and finds himself in acres of space. He decides to shoot from distance, but his effort goes nowhere near its intended target.
(48’) Great play by Everton! Naismith and Osman link up on the edge of the Fulham box and pull off a wonderful one-two, which results in the Scotsman whipping a low cross across goal, but Riise is there to blast the ball out of play for a corner.
(47’) Everton patiently push forward into Fulham's half of the pitch, but the hosts exert a great amount of pressure on them, forcing them all the way back to Howard.
--- 46’ Substitution S. Naismith enters the game and replaces R. Barkley. ---
(45’) And we're underway once again!
Everton have made once change at half-time, with Naismith coming on for Barkley, who has picked up a calf injury.
As for Everton, they have impressed at times, particularly when their attacks have been orchestrated by Deulefeu down the right flank, but they are lacking that cutting edge in the final third. Lukaku has been largely anonymous, leaving Stockdale relatively untested in the Fulham goalmouth.
Fulham will no doubt be the happier of the two sides at half-time. They have arguably carved out the greater chances and have looked more dangerous when in possession. Holtby and Richardson have been instrumental in every one of the Cottagers' attacking movements, whilst 17-year-old Dembele's impressive performance earned himself a standing ovation as he left the pitch and made his way down the tunnel. If they continue like this after the break, Felix Magath's men will surely go ahead first.
HT: FULHAM 0-0 EVERTON
(45’) Chance for Fulham! Holtby, who has played incredibly well so far, perfectly places his cross onto the head of Dembele, but his effort ends up in the arms of Howard. Anywhere else and it would have been in the back of the net.
(45’) There will be just one minute of added time.
(44’) Chance for Fulham! Hangeland thumps a terrific ball towards Richardson, who holds it up before turning and setting up Dembele on the edge of the box, but the teenager rushes his shot and it goes high and wide of the goal.
(42’) Deulofeu is having a wonderful time on the right wing. The young Spaniard sends another great ball into the heart of Fulham's penalty area, but there are no blue shirts there to tap it into the back of the net.
(40’) Temperatures are rising! Dembele is brought to the ground on the edge of the Everton penalty area, leading to cries of disgust from the Fulham faithful, and almost immediately after Richardson and Deulofeu clash on the left flank, resulting in pushing and shoving between the two players.
(38’) Chance for Fulham! Kasami wins back possession and breaks through a wall of blue shirts, but he's held off by Distin and Howard rushes out and pounces on the ball.
(36’) It's end-to-end stuff here! First, Everton carve out a chance down the right wing through Deulofeu, but his heavy cross is cut out superbly by Stockdale. The Cottagers' goalkeeper then kickstarts a great counterattack, but the visitors hold firm and break down the danger before darting back into Fulham's half once again, but Osman's long-range shot is saved with ease.
(34’) Fulham are looking the brightest of the two sides as we enter the final ten minutes of the half. Kasami half-volleys a cross towards Richardson on the edge of the penalty area, who decides to leave it for Riise, but the Norwegian's rocket of a shot flies over the crossbar.
--- 32’ Yellow card S. Coleman is yellow-carded. ---
(32’) Fulham win a free kick halfway in Everton's half of the pitch after Coleman tugs on the back of Richardson's shirt, for which he earns himself a yellow card. They play it short to Holtby who unleashes a very ambitious long-range effort, which, unsurprisingly, clears the crossbar by some distance.
(30’) Sidwell exhibits some silky smooth skills on the right wing, darting in and out of a plethora of blue shirts before sending a great ball forward, but it's slightly too long and Howard is able to cut out the danger before it can lead to a chance on goal.
(28’) Chance for Fulham! Riise sends a deep cross towards the far post and finds Holtby, whose header forces Howard into a world class one-handed save.
(27’) It's all hotting up now! After some patient and thought-out play, both sides are pushing forward and carving out some really good chances.
(25’) Osman tries to muscle his way through the Fulham defence, but he's unable to do so and the ball rolls into the hands of Stockdale. Lukaku made a wonderful run through the middle, but Osman decided to go it alone, which, in hindsight, was the wrong decision.
--- 23’ Yellow card S. Riether gets yellow. ---
(23’) Another chance for Fulham! This time it's Dembele who sets up Richardson with a selfless through-ball, but the latter's shot is saved by the feet of Howard. Almost immediately, Everton break away on a counterattack of their own and Deulofeu unleashes an almost identical shot at the other end, which Stockdale saves in similar fashion.
(21’) Chance for Fulham! Richardson dinks a lovely lofted ball over the top of the Everton defence for Dembele, but the youngster is flagged for offside, despite the replay indicating otherwise.
(18’) Good play again by Fulham and, in particular, Kasami. The Swiss midfielder picks up the ball on the right wing and sends in yet another fantastic cross, but it's slightly too long and it clears Sidwell's head by mere inches.
(16’) Everton break away down the right flank, with Baines and Lukaku utilising a wonderful one-two to penetrate the Fulham penalty area. The attack is cut out and breaks down momentarily, but Fulham quickly lose possession and the ball ends up with Deulofeu, who darts back into the box before attempting one too many step-overs and sees the ball trickle away from his feet and out for a goalkick.
(14’) Chance for Fulham! Hangeland rises high and nods on the corner towards Kasami at the back post, but the angle is too tight and his headed attempt marginally misses the upright.
(13’) Another good attacking movement by Fulham. Riise darts down the left flank before sending a dangerous ball into the box, but Barry sticks out a leg to clear the ball for a corner. (12’) Baines tries to unleash Osman down the right with a long ball, but Riether is there to shepherd the ball out for a goalkick.
(9’) Another quick break forward by Fulham. Kvist beats McCarthy before setting up Richardson on the left flank, but the Englishman's cross is poor and ends up safely in the hands of Howard.
(8’) The visitors take too much time on the ball, allowing Fulham to regain possession and push forward. Kasami picks up the ball on the right wing and sends a wonderful cross-cum-shot into the heart of the Everton box, which beats everyone, including Howard, and bounces just wide of the American's outstretched hand.
(6’) Free kick for Everton inside their own half after Kasami challenges Barry. They decide to play it back to Howard, giving them a chance to regroup.
(5’) Patient build-up play by Everton, who seem quite happy to take their time picking apart a Fulham defence that have been leaking goals this season.
(3’) Chance for Fulham! A deep cross somehow finds Holtby unmarked at the far right end of the Everton penalty area, allowing the German to fire towards goal, but his effort doesn't trouble Howard.
(2’) Early chance for Everton after Fulham lost the ball in midfield: Osman picks up possession just inside the Cottagers' half before setting up Lukaku with a deft through-ball, but Heitinga is able to throw his body in front of the Belgian to deflect his attempt wide of the target.
(2’) Heitinga launches the ball forward for Kasami on the right wing, but the Swiss midfielder is marginally offside.
(1’) And we're off! Fulham get us underway, attacking from left-to-right.
The two teams are making their way onto the pitch ahead of kick-off. Both sets of fans are in fine voice, knowing full well the importance of a victory for either side today.
A win for Fulham will move them into 18th place for the time being, and could kickstart a much-needed late push for survival. With just one win in their last 11 league games, the Cottagers need points on the board, and desperately.
As for the visitors, Roberto Martinez has opted to field the same starting 11, as well as the same substitutes' bench, that beat Newcastle United so convincingly on Tuesday evening. His side have won their last four Premier League games, their best run since March 2008, and they'll be looking to extend their run, and move to within four points of fourth-place Arsenal, with a fifth consecutive win here today.
Fulham boss Felix Magath has made three changes to the side that were thrashed 5-0 by Manchester City last Saturday. Lewis Holtby comes in for Alexander Kacaniklic, who drops to the bench, whilst Sascha Riether drops back into defence to replace the suspended Fernando Amorebieta, making way for the inclusion of Patjim Kasami in midfield. Meanwhile, the much talked about 17-year-old Frenchman Moussa Dembele has been handed his first Premier League start, replacing fellow youngster Cauley Woodrow up front.
Everton substitutes: Robles, Alcaraz, Browning, Garbutt, Naismith, Mirallas, McGeady

Good afternoon and welcome to the live text commentary of today's Premier League game between Fulham and Everton. My name is Ben Cullimore and I will be keeping you up-to-date with all of the action from Craven Cottage.

Tottenham's Champions League hopes are all but over now, with them trailing Arsenal by eight points with six matches to play, and Sherwood can have no complaints regarding today's performance. They can now just look on in envy as their hosts today continue to defy all their doubters. For now I've been Tom Maston, and thanks for joining me.
The full-time whistle blows and Liverpool climb to the top of the Premier League table. Six matches to go and the Reds can see the title on the horizon. This was yet another impressive showing from Rodgers' side, and the fans are showing their appreciation to the players.
(90’) Mignolet shows he is still aware as Eriksen cuts inside before getting away a left-footed shot that is deflected. The Liverpool goalkeeper does well to get down to his left and keep the effort out.
(90’) Tottenham will play the final few minutes with ten men as Soldado is stretchered off. There will be three minutes of stoppage time.
(89’) Into the final minute of normal time now, and Soldado again needs treatment after coming second in an aerial battle with Skrtel. The striker has been totally nullified this afternoon.
(87’) Tottenham continue their search for a consolation and they almost find the net as Eriksen swings over a corner that Dawson just heads over the top.
(85’) Skrtel has been mightily impressive, and he is alive to the danger again as Dawson heads down an Eriksen corner into Kaboul's path, but the Slovakia defender gets it clear.

(81’) Spurs haven't given this one up and Soldado suddenly finds himself with the goal at his mercy. He shapes to shoot but all of a sudden Flanagan flies across and makes a superb tackle that leaves the Spain international on the turf.
(80’) Liverpool again threaten as Henderson crosses from near the halfway line for Sturridge. Lloris is aware of the danger though and comes off limits to punch clear. He then clatters into Sturridge, but is straight back on his feet.
(78’) The Tottenham fans are still singing but in truth this match was lost inside the opening seconds when Kaboul put through his own net. That was just the confidence boost Liverpool required and they haven't looked back.
(76’) Spurs almost find a consolation as Chadli finds space in the Liverpool area, but Agger gets across to make a great block and keep the hosts' clean sheet intact.

(74’) Suarez wins a free-kick on the left and has an opportunity to add to his account...
(72’) Liverpool are denied another opportunity as Johnson is penalised for a push on Rose as he looked to latch onto a pass from Henderson. That looked soft but Tottenham breath again.

(68’) GOOD SAVE! Liverpool are almost gifted a fourth as Rose slips inside his own box, and Sturridge is able to send a backheel goalwards, only for Lloris to show good reactions and parry.
(66’) Some concern here for the hosts as Suarez pulls up after catching Lloris as he went through on goal. He is limping but wants to carry on, and why wouldn't he given his form?
(65’) The hosts have almost started winding down the clock already, with the midfield players keeping the ball with little urgency to get it forward. This has been all too comfortable for Rodgers' side.
--- 64’ Substitution J. Allen comes on for Philippe Coutinho. ---
(63’) Coutinho has had quite the week, and he receives a standing ovation as he is replaced by Allen.
(62’) There is a carnival atmosphere inside Anfield now, though the home fans will still want more goals. The title could come down to goal difference in the end, after all.
--- 60’ Substitution That was Bentaleb's last act as he is replaced by Dembele while Townsend comes on for Lennon. ---
--- 59’ Substitution A. Townsend enters the game and replaces A. Lennon. ---
(59’) Tottenham look short of all confidence, though Bentaleb is still going, and he again tries his luck with a long range effort that flies over the bar.
(57’) The home fans are in buoyant mood now, with 'We're going to win the league' ringing out around Anfield. They're certainly the team in form heading into the run-in.
--- 55’ Assist The assist came from J. Flanagan. ---
--- 55’ Goal! GOAL!!! Game, set and match, Liverpool. Coutinho is the man to find the net as the hosts break with devastating effect. (52’) Agger gets himself into all sorts of bother as a ball over the top sees him left in Soldado's wake. There is little support for the striker, however, and Agger fights hard recover and force a goal kick.
(50’) Almost an opening for the hosts as Suarez plays a delightful first time pass looking for Henderson, but the midfielder cannot quite reach it in time before Dawson gets it clear.
(48’) Liverpool again start the brighter after the restart, with Tottenham struggling to get out of their own half. The hosts will be looking to kill this match off sooner rather than later.
--- 46’ Yellow card Sigurdsson picks up a yellow card inside 30 seconds of the second period as he pulls back Coutinho as the Brazilian broke forward. ---
(46’) Liverpool kick-off and we are back underway...
The players are making their way back out onto the pitch at Anfield. Can Liverpool stretch their lead? Or will Spurs launch a fightback? We're about to find out...
Sherwood's team talk was praised as Spurs came back from 2-0 down last week, and he will have to lift his team again if they are to get back into this one. I'll be back in ten minutes to see if the visitors can claw their way back into the match.
Referee Phil Dowd blows the half-time whistle and Liverpool are well on their way to the top of the Premier League table. Kaboul's own goal and yet another strike from Suarez have given them breathing space, and in truth it could have been more.
(45’) Spurs launch one final attack as Lennon gets to the byline on the right, but Agger does well to close him down and win a goal kick for his side.
(45’) JUST WIDE! Liverpool again go close as Naughton concedes a free-kick on the edge of the area, but Suarez cannot get the necessary bend on his strike and the ball floats just wide of the upright with Lloris beaten this time.

(40’) GOOD SAVE! Tottenham are enjoying their best period of the match and after Skrtel fails to sufficiently clear Rose's cross, Soldado has time to curl an effort towards the top corner that Mignolet has to push away from the danger zone.
(38’) Mignolet is properly tested for the first time as Bentaleb hits a swerving effort from 30 yards, but the Belgian is equal to it and holds on well as the ball moves in front of him.
(36’) The Liverpool fans sing the name of Brendan Rodgers, and the Liverpool boss has certainly got his tactics right today. The pace of Sterling has added an extra dimension to the hosts' attacking play and Tottenham are struggling to cope.
(34’) With the kick favouring a left footer, Sturridge is charged with striking the set-piece.He goes for precision over power but it always too high and Lloris can just watch it over his crossbar.

(30’) Some concern here for the hosts as Johnson stays down clutching his knee after clashing with Kaboul. The England full-back is eventually back on his feet and is fit to continue.
(28’) Liverpool look rampant with every attack, and Dawson's lack of pace is already being shown up by the likes of Sterling and Suarez. This could be a long afternoon for the visiting supporters.

(21’) Opportunity for Liverpool as Sigurdsson is penalised for handball around 25 yards from the Tottenham goal. This is certainly within Suarez and Gerrard's range.
(20’) Gerrard delivers a low cross but the Liverpool attack aren't quite on the same wavelength and Spurs get the ball clear.
(19’) Coutinho comes to life in midfield and looks for Sturridge in the middle, with Tottenham forced to concede a corner on the left...
(17’) Gerrard gets his first chance to deliver a set-piece as Liverpool win a corner on the right. The captain's ball looks for Agger, but Vertonghen does well to clear.

--- 66’ Yellow card K. Nolan gets yellow. ---

The game had been decidedly average for the most part, until the 93rd minute when Cheick Tiote struck the crossbar and Cisse missed the most simple of follow-ups. Both sides look resigned to a point apiece, but Cisse had other ideas, somehow managing to steer home Hatem Ben Arfa's cross-cum-shot to seal all three points.
--- 90’ +4 Assist The assist came from H. Ben Arfa. ---
--- 90’ +4 Goal! GOAL! Newcastle have surely won it at the death thanks to Cisse's headed goal. The Senegalese striker more than made up for his error just moments earlier, stooping to head home what looked like a shot from Ben Arfa. The Frenchman picked the ball up on the right and ran at the Palace defence before hitting across the ball which flew in the direction of Cisse and we finally have an opening goal here. ---
(90’) CROSSBAR: Astonishing end to the game at St James's Park. Tiote's stunning piledriver from range comes cannoning back off the bar and falls for Ameobi. The striker passes the ball across goal but Cisse somehow fails to convert from three yards out. In defence, he was under pressure from a defender but still should have scored.
(90’) Newcastle make their final throw of the dice as Sylvain Marveaux enters the fray for Sissoko. We will have three minutes off added time to find a winner.
--- 88’ Substitution M. Sissoko is replaced with S. Marveaux. ---
(88’) Ben Arfa has added a new dimension to the Newcastle attack, but his profligacy in the final third may have cost his side here. Having weaved through challenges successfully, the Frenchman has an opening to curl home but his strike goes high and wide.
(86’) A long ball is hurled into the area towards Cisse, but the striker is unable to get sufficient pruchase on his chest down towards Sissoko and Palace hack the ball away.
--- 85’ Yellow card D. Delaney is cautioned by the referee. ---
(84’) Delaney enters the book for a rash challenge, with Palace beginning to sit deeper and deeper as a defensive unit here. Can either side find the elusive opener?
(82’) Tiote wastes another opening for Newcastle and it is all becoming rather desperate in the final third from the home side's perspective, with long shot after long shot failing to test Speroni in the Palace goal.
--- 80’ Substitution A. Guédioura enters play, replacing J. Puncheon. ---
(80’) Palace make another change as Adlene Guedioura comes on for Puncheon so perhaps Pulis may be shutting up shop after all. Can they secure a first win in five league games?
(78’) Crystal Palace are hanging on doggedly to what could prove an invaluable point in their aspirations of staying in the Premier League.
--- 76’ Substitution Y. Gouffran is done for the day. Shola Ameobi is his replacement. ---
(76’) Palace manager Pulis sends on Glenn Murray in the hope of what would be a crucial late winner, with Jerome departing. Newcastle also make a sub, with Gouffran departing and Shola Ameobi arriving.
--- 75’ Substitution G. Murray enters play, replacing C. Jerome. ---
(74’) Gouffran unleashes a speculative effort which zips well wide of the target as Newcastle's frustrations began to spill over.
(74’) Dummett delivers a corner from the left but the delivery, not for the first time, is poor and Speroni collects with the minimum of fuss. Mapou Yanga-Mbiwa then sends in a powerful volleyed cross which Cisse tries to get a flick on, but Palace again deal with the danger effectively.
(72’) Anita is denied by a desperate challenge at the far post as he looked to turn home a deep cross past Speroni.
(70’) Ben Arfa's contribution and general impact since coming on only begs the question, why did he not start? The winger has been excellent and jinks his way to the byline this time to fashion a cross which Cisse wastefully heads over.
(68’) Barry Bannan is on for the visitors, with Bolasie the man to depart. The winger has gone the closest to breaking this most stubborn of deadlocks this afternoon.
--- 67’ Substitution B. Bannan comes on for Y. Bolasie. ---
(66’) Ben Arfa sets off on a mazy run after picking the ball up just in front of the Palace defence, but his efforts to get a ball into the box ultimately result in a skewed cross which goes wide of the near post.
(64’) CHANCE: Cisse's wretched run in front of goal shows no sign of slowing, with the Senegalese striker missing a great chance to hand his side the lead. A sliderule pass from Sissoko feeds Cisse, but his finish is poor and straight at Speroni when he ought to have done better.
(62’) Sissoko reaches the byline after a barnstorming run on the left wing and cuts the ball back into a dangerous area towards Cisse and Ben Arfa. The striker misses the ball and the Frenchman is beaten to the ball by a Palace defender.
(60’) Gouffran sees his ambitious attempt from far out well blocked by the combative presence of Dikgacoi. The midfielder has been excellent alongside skipper Jedinak this afternoon.
--- 59’ Substitution L. de Jong is done for the day. H. Ben Arfa is his replacement. ---
(58’) Krul had saved brilliantly from Kagisho Dikgacoi just before that and Palace are really beginning to turn the screw here. Hatem Ben Arfa is on for the hosts, replacing De Jong, who has been poor throughout.
(56’) OFF THE BAR: So, so desperately unlucky from Bolasie, whose powerful effort bends onto the top of Krul's crossbar after dipping inside and cutting in from the left flank.
(54’) Three Palace players are caught offside as the ball is delivered into the penalty area but Bolasie misses the target anyway in a let-off for the Newcastle backline.
(52’) Krul receives treatment after a heavy fall but Newcastle do not let it affect them and Gouffran produces a cross which Delaney has to be alert to as Palace eventually clear their lines.
(50’) Another chance goes begging for Palace as their latest venture forward ends with Jerome slashing his shot wide of goal.
(48’) Crystal Palace have started the second half in inspired fashion and should be ahead more or less immediately after the restart. Another speedy break leaves Puncheon clear on the right but, having cut inside, his curling effort was just wide of the far post.
(46’) We are underway for the second half as Palace get the ball rolling once more.
HALF-TIME: Newcastle United 0-0 Crystal Palace. Not an awful lot to shout about in truth for to shot-shy sides. Newcastle are missing the dynamism up front of Loic Remy while the visitors are living up to their reputation of being the Premier League's lowest scorers. The hosts have seen presentable chances to Cisse and Gouffran fall by the wayside but it is Palace who have gone closest through Bolasie. With fellow relegation rivals winning, Pulis' side must be more clinical on the counter in the second period.
(45’) Puncheon's latest corner is superbly whipped towards the far post but is just out of the reach of a host of Palace players ganging up at Krul's far upright.
(43’) Jedinak does excellently to first shield his defence and then win a free-kick for his side after being dragged back. Puncheon and Jerome are both doing a great job up front of cutting off the supply line at the back.
(41’) Bolasie comes so close to giving his side the lead with a searing strike which flies just inches wide of the far post. He had done all the hard work, skipping inside Dummett but could not apply the finish.
(39’) Delaney is forced into a hurried clearance as Vurnon Anita, who has been on the fringes of the game, seeks to pick out the onrushing Cisse in the area.
(37’) PENALTY? Mike Williamson's downward header appears to hit Dann on the arm but despite the Newcastle players and fans' protests, Lee Probert is unmoved.
(35’) Newcastle keep the pressure on and force a corner when Cisse's cross from the left has to be flicked away from in front of de Jong by Damien Delaney.
(33’) Newcastle are slowly beginning to crank up the pressure on Palace and their increasing dominance almost told when Gouffran was spotted on the left-side of the penalty area, but the Frenchman's snapshot was straight at Speroni, who gathered easily.
(31’) CHANCE: Another slick move, this time from Newcastle, results in de Jong sliding the ball across the area to Cisse, who chooses to go with a first-time effort, which is pushed away by Speroni.
(29’) Crystal Palace are looking to get at a susceptible Newcastle defence at every given opportunity and Jerome leads the fight once more, but his pass to Puncheon sends the winger wide and he is unable to deliver a ball into the area.
(27’) Gouffran is down receiving treatment after what seemed a fairly innocuous altercation as he attempted to dribble out of his own half of the field.
(25’) CHANCE: Palace squander a brilliant opportunity on the counter attack, with Jerome selfishly electing to shoot when he had Bolasie and Puncheon either side of him in space. The striker's effort looped up into the air, courtesy of a deflection, and Newcastle were able to clear their lines.
(23’) Puncheon snuffs out Dummett's attempts to get a ball into the Palace penalty area and his cross eventually flies out for a goal kick.
(21’) Tiote bursts into space on the right flank and picks his head up for a pass, but his ball through is poor and easily dealt with by Palace.
(19’) Jerome is caught offside in his attempts to breach the Newcastle backline after a great ball forward behind Fabricio Coloccini and Paul Dummett.
(17’) Pulis will be delighted with the way his side have settled here and they have posed a threat on the counter. Adrian Mariappa gets forward on the right but Yoan Gouffran does well to shepherd the ball out.
(15’) Cisse loses out in a tussle with Jedinak before the midfielder launches it long in the direction of Bolasie. The ball is too heavy, however, and simply affords Newcastle a goal kick.
(13’) CHANCE: Newcastle work the first major opening of the game as a neat passing move results in Cisse holding the ball with his back to goal. A slick turn later and he is away from Scott Dann, but fires straight at Speroni, with de Jong nodding the rebound over the bar.
(11’) Newcastle try to release Sissoko on the right-hand side, but the ball is slightly over-hit and rolls out for a throw-in.
(9’) Cameron Jerome sees a chance come and go as Newcastle get back to deny the frontman space before the home side move forward with the ball. Palace are holding out resolutely so far.
(7’) Papiss Cisse fires an ambitious ball over the top of the Palace rearguard but Speroni is there to collect it easily.
(5’) Crystal Palace force a corner on the right flank but the delivery from Puncheon is easily punched away by the grateful Tim Krul in the Newcastle goal.
(3’) Mile Jedinak is immediately snapping at Newcastle heels, conceding an early free-kick to Moussa Sissoko before Cheick Tiote tests Julian Speroni with a long-range effort. Jedinak hauls down Tiote next, but the Newcastle midfielder's free-kick deflects off a Newcastle head and out for a goal kick.
(1’) We are underway, with Newcastle getting the ball rolling.
We are just moments away from kick off here at St James's Park.
With Remy injured, goals may be in short supply in this match - in 2014, Palace are the lowest scorers in the Premier League with seven this calendar year, while Newcastle have only managed eight.
The Magpies' run of four successive home defeats came to an end when they beat Aston Villa in their last home fixture four weeks ago, but in their last five home league matches that late winner from Loic Remy is the only one the home supporters have witnessed.
Newcastle, meanwhile, will be without manager Alan Pardew once again, as he sits out the second match of his three-game stadium ban. The man that helped the Magpies to their 3-0 win at Selhurst Park before Christmas - Yohan Cabaye - is now of PSG following his January transfer.
Palace's main worry is their lack of firepower, having scored just 19 goals in their 29 Premier League games this season but Pulis has tightened things up defensively since his arrival, with only Newcastle scoring more than two past his charges since he took the reins at Selhurst Park.
Today, of course, represents a second trip to the North East in as many games for Palace fans following the creditable point at the Stadium of Light but they still slipped to 17th as a result and, with Fulham beating today's opponents, they are now just three points above the drop zone.

FULL TIME: NORWICH 2-0 Sunderland. A huge roar greets the full time whistle as the Canaries emerge victorious. Two first half goals - one a terrific strike from Tettey - seals the points to ease pressure on Chris Hughton. The visitors were just not at the races and Alonso's second yellow for dissent in stoppage time summed up Gus Poyet's day.
--- 90’ +2 Red card! Marcos Alonso gets a second yellow card and is sent off! ---
(90’) RED CARD! Alonso walks for a second yellow card! The left-back sees red for dissent. That has all but summed up the Black Cats' day.
(90’) There will be FOUR minutes of added on time.
--- 89’ Substitution N. Redmond enters play, replacing W. Hoolahan. ---
(89’) STAT ATTACK: If the scoreline stays this way, Sunderland will be on a run of three games without a win.
(88’) Elmander enjoys a standing ovation as he makes way for Johnson. His commitment and attitude has been impecible today, even if he has struggled for chances.
--- 87’ Substitution J. Elmander is done for the day. B. Johnson is his replacement. ---
(86’) STAT ATTACK: The Canaries have conceded just 12 goals at home this season, the joint-third best tally in the Premier League. Only Arsenal (seven), Manchester City and Chelsea (both nine) have a better record.
(84’) SO CLOSE! ...and the goalscorer is just off target with a curling effort to the left of Manonne. The keeper might have had that covered but it was still a sweet strike that just failed to find the target.
(82’) Another foul against Sunderland! This time it is Hooper who is upended by Larsson. Snodgrass lines it up in a central position, roughly 25 yards from goal...
--- 81’ Yellow card P. Bardsley receives a yellow card. ---

(79’) The City fans are baying for blood as Borini slides into Ruddy in an attempt to reach the ball and there is a clash. But both players get up smiling, patting each other on the back and the game continues.
--- 77’ Yellow card Marcos Alonso receives a yellow card. ---
(76’) We have just over 15 minutes plus stoppage time to play here and it looks as though the hosts are pretty satisfied with keeping this score at 2-0. The cushion is allowing them to stay patient on the ball and they look very comfortable.
(74’) The Mackems' boss has just plumped himself back in his chair with a frustrated look on his face. Not much he can do about this, but his side have a tricky run in for the rest of the season, so they had better pick their performances up soon!
(72’) There have not been many chances in this second half for either side. Will Gus Poyet just put this performance down to a bad day at the office?
--- 71’ Substitution A. Johnson is replaced with I. Scocco. ---
--- 71’ Substitution G. Hooper comes on for R. van Wolfswinkel. ---
(70’) It looks like Van Wolfswinkel will have to wait yet another game to break his goal drought as Gary Hooper is being readied on the bench.
--- 69’ Yellow card R. Snodgrass is cautioned by the referee. ---
(68’) The intensity and atmosphere is starting to drop off at Carrow Road. Every time the Black Cats pour forward it leaves them so exposed to concede a third.
--- 66’ Yellow card L. Bridcutt gets yellow. ---
(66’) STAT ATTACK: The omens are looking good for the hosts. Norwich have won the last four games against Sunderland at Carrow Road.
(64’) Wes Brown uses all his experience to thwart Snodgrass after the goalscorer weaves his way into the box. The former Man United man dives in to block the shot and concede a corner.
(62’) Larsson hits a fantastic free-kick into a the area but the Black Cats' attack breaks down straight away. They are desperate for a window of opportunity to get back into this game.
(60’) The Carrow Road faithful have gone a little quiet. Surely they cannot be suffering from an attack of jangling nerves with half an hour to go?
(57’) The hosts are coming under increasing pressure here as Howson blasts a Bardsley cross away for a corner. The quick free-kick leads to a terrible effort from Cattermole. He hit it as if the ball had in that second turned into lead!
(55’) STAT ATTACK: Sunderland have not won at Norwich in nine attempts since the 1984-85 season, when both clubs were relegated from the top flight.

Two goals - including a belter from Alex Tettey, has put the Canaries on top here. Sunderland have been woeful and there is plenty of work to do in the second half if they to get anything out of this game.
(45’) There will be a minimum of THREE minutes of added time.
(45’) STAT ATTACK: Lee Cattermole was booked after only three minutes on the pitch.
(44’) Not long to go here before half time and Norwich are still looking quicker, brighter and sharper. What must the Black Cats do to get back into this one?
--- 43’ Yellow card L. Cattermole receives a yellow card. ---
