--- 87’ Substitution Rafael is replaced with N. Vidić. ---
(87’) SUBSTITUTION: Man Utd - Nemanja Vidic replaces Rafael in the final stages.
(85’) West Brom unable to really assert themselves in the midfield, with their disjointed passing and poor positioning, especially in the second half. man Utd preparing another substitution.
(83’) Turning into a very good day for David Moyes' men in what has been a rather routine victory to continue their good run at this stadium. Will this be a catalyst for change?
--- 82’ Assist Assist by W. Rooney. ---
--- 82’ Goal! GOAL! West Brom 0-3 Man Utd: WELBECK! Lovely move once again, and that settles it. Welbeck with a beautiful finish after Mata, Rooney and Fellaini combine in the build-up. Rooney with the decisive pass, and Welbeck just lifts it over Foster and into the net. ---
(80’) West Brom languish in 17th place in the Premier League, one point ahead of Sunderland. The Black Cats, who were in action in the Capital One Cup final last week, also are not scheduled to play this week, giving them two games in hand.
(78’) GERA! Lovely save from De Gea, his first real piece of action in this game. Great understanding from Anichebe and Gera, the latter showing good movement to give his marker the slip. Poor accuracy in the shot, and it's turned behind.
--- 76’ Substitution S. Kagawa enters the game and replaces A. Januzaj. ---
(76’) Entering the final quarter of an hour of this game. Man Utd have managed an 82% pass completion rate to West Brom's 74%. They've completed 302, about 100 more than their opponents.
(75’) SUBSTITUTION - Manchester United: Adnan Januzaj goes off, to be replaced by Shinji Kagawa.
(73’) Fantastic opening of the opposition defence by Michael Carrick, whose pass carves open a chance for Danny Welbeck, arriving inside the box on the right. The England striker loses a bit of composure, and sends the ball flying over the goal.
(71’) Sessegnon does well to hold off Rafael, and use his strength to shield the ball and carve out a chance for the hosts, but the Brazilian right-back doesn't let go too easily, and intervenes.
(70’) Stat: Wayne Rooney now has 11 goals and nine assists in the Premier League this season, contributing to just under half (44.4%) of his side's goals.
(69’) BERAHINO! Offside anyway, but what a chance that was spurned there. A cross from the wing evades the striker, but is drifted back from Gera. Towards Berahino who heads it over the bar!
(67’) SUBSTITUTION - West Brom: Third and final change for the Baggies. Saido Berahino comes on to replace the injured Chris Brunt,
--- 66’ Substitution S. Berahino enters the game and replaces C. Brunt. ---
(66’) That will put the game to bed. West Brom unlikely to recover from a two goal deficit, having failed to seriously trouble David de Gea in this game. Meanwhile, West Brom are about to throw another one on.
--- 65’ Assist Rafael gave the assist. ---
--- 65’ Goal! GOAL! West Brom 0-2 Manchester United - ROONEY! Fine goal. Lovely passing move started by Rooney in deep. Rafael with a fantastic cross from the right, towards Rooney who directs it simply into the net. Superb. ---
--- 63’ Substitution D. Welbeck enters play, replacing R. van Persie. ---
(63’) SUBSTITUTION - Man Utd: Robin van Persie departs, to be replaced by Danny Welbeck. Common sense from Moyes, with van Persie lucky to have escaped a red just moments ago.
(62’) Chris Brunt is feeling some pain, and is currently receiving treatment in the middle of the pitch. There is some action on the United bench meanwhile. A first change imminent for the visitors.
--- 61’ Substitution S. Sessègnon enters play, replacing S. Reid. ---
(60’) SUBSTITUTION - West Brom: Off goes Steven Reid, and he is replaced by Stephane Sessegnon.
(59’) Steven Reid limping for West Brom, might we see another substitution from the Baggies? Meanwhile, United have a free-kick after yet another Mulumbu foul.
(57’) And the subsequent corner comes to nothing, but Manchester United are already embarking on a counter attack here. A long ball forward from the left by Evra finds Fellaini in ACRES of space. Hits it powerfully in the absence of Liam Ridgewell, but it is blocked.
(56’) ANICHEBE! West Brom are getting closer! Mata forced to clear off the line, before Mulumbu gets on the rebound. Charged behind by the defender and out for a corner. It's got The Hawthorns in full voice!
(54’) Van Persie's lucky there. Stumbles with the ball, and launches a two-footed challenge which sends Steven Reid in the air. He is already on a yellow, and he is oh so lucky to be remaining on the pitch. Last chance.
(52’) GERA! That was a fantastic chance from the midfielder. Fine movement from West Brom, as Gera plays an intricate one-two with Anichebe, who holds off Smalling. Back to Gera, but he tumbles with the effort, with De Gea picking up the ball in a routine save.
--- 50’ Yellow card R. van Persie goes into the referee's book. ---
(50’) Pepe Mel gives an encouraging thumbs up to his side, as Anichebe produces another turn and shot, down low. His effort is rather tame however, and De Gea sees it out with ease.
(49’) Gera goes down under the challenge of Smalling, but the referee waves play on. Not much in that challenge, but West Brom are currently in a decent spell of possession.
(48’) Decent free-kick from Van Persie, hit towards the centre of the field. Headed away by Olsson, and not for the first time this afternoon, Januzaj hits a wild volley which goes absolutely nowhere.
(47’) Free-kick awarded to Manchester United. Fellaini is upended by Mulumbu on the right side of the field. The defender is furious, but United have a fantastic chance to extend their lead. 30 yards out.
(46’) Underway in the second half! Manchester United commence play, attacking from right to left. Can they hold onto, or even extend their lead?
HT: WBA 0-1 MUFC: Jones' header separates the two sides at the break, though there was controversy when Ben Foster supposedly handled outside the area. Nicely poised this at the half-time interval.
(45’) HALF-TIME: West Brom 0-1 Manchester United
(45’) West Brom providing a strong finish at the end of the first half. And they are aided with a free-kick, after Fellaini clumsily fouls Brunt on the edge of the area.
(45’) Into the first of two minutes added on at the end of the first half.
(43’) A huge call from the referee. His body is outside, but is his hand? Replays show his whole body is outside the box. No question of the handball. Moyes is seething on the touchline. A massive mistake from Foster.
(42’) CONTROVERSY! Juan Mata pings a fine ball forward for van Persie, who isn't expected to get that in time. But Foster races off his line, and connects the ball with the hand. Man Utd are furious! The referee waves play on.
(41’) ANICHEBE! Narrowly wide from the striker. Lovely turn and shot by the big striker, holding off the challenge of Phil Jones to get his shot away. Just goes wide.
--- 40’ Substitution J. Morrison comes on for C. Yacob. ---
(40’) SUBSTITUTION - West Brom: Claudio Yacob has been replaced by James Morrison.
(39’) OUCH! Claudio Yacob is on the receiving end of a heavy challenge from Marouane Fellaini. Yacob receiving a bit of treatment, and is moving gingerly.
(38’) A frustrated Pepe Mel watches on, conversing with his assistant. The last couple of mid-season managerial changes at West Brom has seen them escape relegation. Will it this time?
(36’) West Brom have conceded the first goal in their last four home games (against Everton, Chelsea, Fulham and Liverpool). Each time, they have clawed the score back to 1-1.
(35’) Phil Jones' third goal in the Premier League this season, and it just eases the pressure on Moyes and his side. Great header, with the defence a little too easily beaten.

(32’) Januzaj's deliveries causing a bit of a problem from the left. Another one deep into the danger zone, with Rafael coming on the end of that, though this time, his effort is blocked.
(31’) Chants of 'Getting Sacked in the Morning' reverberate around the stadium. Whether that's intended for Pepe Mel or David Moyes is anyone's guess.

(26’) Taken by Juan Mata, chipped in with his left. Cut out by Mulumbu, under pressure from Rooney but Evra pounces on the loose ball. He is denied by an offside call.
(25’) Van Persie wins a free-kick after a late challenge from Youssouf Mulumbu. Free-kick in a decent position, about 30 yards out. Mata, Rooney and Van Persie standing over this.
(24’) Manchester United's points total after 27 games is comfortably the worst they've endured in the Premier League era. Their total of 45 is five off the previous worst of 50 at this stage in the 1992-1993 season.
(22’) Long ball deep from Carrick towards Robin van Persie is well nullified by Reid, and West Brom are holding a very solid defensive line against the champions.
(20’) Wayne Rooney diverts his frustration towards referee Jon Moss, who awards a goal-kick instead of a corner after a challenge from Claudio Yacob. TV replays show the referee was right!
(19’) Anichebe does well to claim possession, and advances slightly on the right wing, in search of an advancing team mate. Brunt and Gera in place, but he is unable to find them
(17’) United dominating still, with West Brom unable to get the ball out of their box. Rafael advancing from the right to put pressure on the hosts, but eventually, the play fizzles out.

(15’) Poor corner, as it evades the likes of Fellaini and Patrice Evra, though it does go out via a West Brom shirt. Another corner, to be taken by Juan Mata.

(13’) YELLOW CARD - Adnan Januzaj. The young winger picks up his seventh booking of the season for handball. Bit harsh that!
(12’) Ball falls kindly for Anichebe, who races forward to get into a one on one position. Under pressure from Chris Smalling who races back in time, the England defender wins that tussle and averts danger.

The two clubs have only 11 league wins between them all season. It is sure to be full of tension and nerves for both sides, but a rare three points for either might just give them a much-needed Premier League lifeline.
Fulham have brought up the rear in the top flight since the beginning of February but know a win today would be enough to take them above their hosts. It's only Magath's third match in charge, but the team has now lost 15 of their last 20 league games.
Today represents arguably Cardiff's best chance in quite some while of boosting that number as they come up against the division's most charitable defence, which has now conceded 62 goals.
The real concern for Solskjaer is his side's goal tally of 19, which is the joint-lowest in the top flight. Worryingly, they have failed to find the back of the net in 11 of their last 16 matches. They are crying out for a natural finisher in the mould of their manager in his prime.
That's one of six defeats in his eight league games in charge so far. If there is to be a recovery, though, the Bluebirds quite simply have to address their home form, where they have won just four times all season and must navigate through games against Liverpool, Crystal Palace, Stoke and Chelsea all still to come.
For Solskjaer and Cardiff, this is a first home game since the 4-0 defeat to Hull City, which prompted him to cancel the club's warm weather training plans in the Middle East.
The match also brings together two managers who were only appointed this calendar year. For both it is an inaugural managerial spell in the Premier League and they appear in desperate need of a lift.
Some critics have already written these two - the bottom two, of course - off already, but both sides will be aware that when facing a relegation rival at this stage, a win can act as a catalyst when forming a great escape bid.
Football fans, most of them anyway, hate the phrase 'six-pointer', but there is simply no hiding it from this one, a win for either side here this afternoon will have important implications on either side's battle against the drop.
There is also a debut for the Cottagers' record signing Kostas Mitroglou, who has recovered sufficiently from injury to make his first start. Partnering the Greek striker with Woodrow is a baptism of fire for the new duo, but Magath clearly has faith in them to make the difference in this crucial encounter.
The standout team news, at least from a Fulham perspective is the inclusion of Cauley Woodrow, who is handed a first-ever Premier League start by Magath, with Solskjaer altering his team's shape from a five-man defence to a more conventional 4-2-3-1.

FULL TIME - NORWICH 1-1 STOKE. The boos ring around Carrow Road as the Canaries drop two points in a pulsating encounter. Johnson headed the home side in front but a crazy push from Bassong at the other end handed a penalty to the visitors. Walters converted the spot kick but then saw red just minutes later leading to a frantic and nerve wracking end to a great game.
(90’) WHAT A CHANCE! Johnson hits the ball into the ground and skews his effort wide of the post after the ball was squared from Elmander, who has played very well since coming on. Norwich are throwing the kitchen sink in!
(90’) Bassong is desperate to make amends for his blunder in the penalty incident and he sends a long ball into the box, but Begovic is quick off his line to collect.
(90’) There will be FIVE minutes of added on time!
(89’) Cameron manages to stop Redmond in his tracks as he blisters his way down the left-hand-side. Both sides need to keep cool heads here but it is getting desperate.
(87’) All hands to the deck for Stoke as Crouch is back in a centre-half role to clear a dangerous Redmond cross. This is becoming frantic and the nails are being bitten inside Carrow Road.
(85’) CHANCE! Crouch is back in his own half helping his side out but ends up giving the ball away to Bassong, who lays it off the Johnson, but the goalscorer loses his radar and blasts it off target.
(83’) HIGH AND WELL OVER! Hooper gets his first whiff of goal but boots his shot well into the top tier of the stand as he squanders some good build up play from the home side.
(82’) I don't know, you wait 70 minutes for a game to wake up and then it all kicks off! This should be a grandstand finish to proceedings here as the Canaries look to make their numerical advantage count.
--- 81’ Substitution G. Hooper enters the game and replaces A. Tettey. ---
--- 80’ Substitution J. Elmander enters play, replacing R. van Wolfswinkel. ---
--- 80’ Substitution J. Guidetti is replaced with S. Ireland. ---

--- 78’ Red card! J. Walters goes off after a red card! ---
(78’) Oh my word. Walters, the man who has just minutes ago levelled for the Potters, has just gone in with his studs showing on Redmond. His boot was high and referee Andre Marriner was right in front of the incident and has sent the goalscorer off. Yet another twist in this afternoon's events!
(75’) It was a moment of absolute madness from the Canaries captain and a moment which could prove pivotal for the home side's season. Chris Hughton looks frustrated in the dugout and I don't blame him.
--- 74’ Substitution M. Etherington comes on for M. Arnautović. ---
--- 73’ Goal! Penalty goal scored by J. Walters! ---
(73’) GOAL! Walters - who scored from the spot in the Potters last Premier League game against Arsenal, steps up and powers the ball side footed past Ruddy into the top corner. It might be against the run of play but they are level!
(72’) PENALTY! Bassong shoves Guidetti off the ball in the box. Madness! It's a penalty to Stoke!
(71’) Both teams are starting to give the ball away very easily and there is a growing tension spreading all over Carrow Road like a cloud of angst. Norwich really need a second goal to kill this game off as we have 20 minutes to play.
--- 69’ Yellow card G. Cameron is yellow-carded. ---
(69’) STAT ATTACK: Four of the five Premier League meetings between these two sides have ended in a 1-0 scoreline, with the other a 1-1 draw.
--- 67’ Substitution J. Howson comes on for W. Hoolahan. ---
(67’) Van Wolfsinkel continues to cut an isolated figure on the pitch. He needs support from an advanced midfielder and maybe Hughton should look at his bench where there are THREE strikers who could do some damage here.
(65’) STAT ATTACK: Norwich won 1-0 in the reverse fixture in September, and are one of only two sides to have left the Britannia Stadium with a league win this season.
--- 63’ Substitution P. Odemwingie is replaced with J. Guidetti. ---
(63’) There has been such a positive reaction from the visitors since that Johnson goal but they are finding it hard to break through the Norwich defence. Bassong and Yobo are forming a wall that the Potters just can't get past.
(61’) GREAT SAVE! Redmond has been so impressive in this game. The youngster goes for glory from 25 yards and sees his right-footed shot parried away by Begovic.
(58’) The visitors are having a real go at the Canaries here as Odemwingie is caught in an offside position, leading to ironic cheers from the home fans. Carrow Road has come to life!
--- 56’ Assist Assist by R. Snodgrass. ---

(55’) STAT ATTACK: Stoke's clean sheet against Arsenal last weekend was their first in 12 league matches.

(48’) Neither side have have made any changes during the break, but both have come out with fire in their veins!
(46’) Stoke get us back underway, kicking from right to left.

FULL-TIME: CHELSEA 4-0 TOTTENHAM. A second half masterclass from Tottenham in how not to defend has handed Chelsea an emphatic victory at Stamford Bridge. Eto'o, Hazard and Ba all benefited from a series of awful mistakes and Mourinho's men are now seven points clear at the top of the league and well and truly in the driving seat for the title.
(90’) Into the final minute of stoppage time we go then. Those last two goals have really put a shine on this result.
(90’) Tim Sherwood looks thoroughly miffed. I'm not surprised. He's just watched his side gift this game to Chelsea. Every single goal has been the result of a mistake or lapse in concentration. This kind of performance is unforgivable from a Spurs point of view.
--- 89’ Goal! GOOOAALL!!! BA AT THE DOUBLE!!! This is getting ridiculous. Tottenham assist another Chelsea goal as Walker's header back towards Lloris is picked up by Ba, who pinches the ball away from the keeper and fires into an empty net. ---
--- 88’ Goal! GOOAAAALLL!!! BA MAKES IT THREE!!! A third mistake from Tottenham and a third goal for Chelsea. Oscar puts in a cross and Sandro slips, allowing Ba to pick up the ball and slip it between the legs of Lloris. ---
--- 86’ Yellow card Azpilicueta gets yellow. ---
(86’) We're into the final five minutes then. That mad five minute spell of two goals and red card killed this game off as a competition and it's been a bit of a training exercise in keep-ball for the hosts since then.
(84’) Oscar has another chance as he gets on the end of Willian's cut back, but the midfielder fires well over the bar and into the stands. It doesn't look like that third goal is coming after all.

(80’) A nasty looking clash leaves Sandro and Ba in a heap on the floor. The Brazilian looks to have come off the worst and is clutching his knee, but both are okay to resume after a spot of treatment.
(78’) A rare chance for Tottenham as Lennon scuttles away down the right. He only has the one option in the middle though and he's not on the same wavelength as Adebayor, the striker darting to the back post as Lennon tries to cut the ball back.
--- 76’ Substitution D. Ba enters play, replacing S. Eto'o. ---
(76’) Off comes Eto'o to rapturous applause. He's single-handedly won the game for Chelsea this evening. Demba Ba comes on for the final 15 minutes.
(75’) Sandro makes another vital interception as Chelsea threaten a third. Walker makes the mistake this time and Hazard thinks he's played through Eto'o for a simple tap in before the Brazilian gets back to clear.
(74’) Ramires is clean through on the right and has all the time in the world to pick out Eto'o. The Brazilian plays the ball too close to Lloris though and the keeper snaffles the loose ball.

(68’) Eto'o is played in by Hazard but the Cameroon international has his jinking run curtailed on the edge of the area. Tottenham have gone into self preservation mode after losing a man and those two goals.

(64’) Chelsea can sense blood now as they lay siege to the Tottenham goal. They've forced a couple of corners and have the visitors penned back in their own half.
(62’) Paulinho comes on for Sigurdsson as Sherwood is forced to shuffle his pack. It looks as though Tottenham's miserable run at the Bridge is going to continue.
--- 61’ Substitution Paulinho comes on for G. Sigurðsson. ---

FULL-TIME: Arsenal 2-2 Swansea City. It is an absolute hammer blow to the Gunners' slim chances of winning the Premier League title but, perhaps more pertinently, it now leaves their top four place in danger, with Everton's 3-0 win this evening providing some competition for Champions League football next term. Arsene Wenger's side were 1-0 down after 10 minutes as Wilfried Bony steered home a Neil Taylor cross but substitute Lukas Podolski looked to have inspired his side to a win after scoring the equaliser and then teeing up Olivier Giroud for the second. But they had not read the script. Leon Britton's scooped ball into the area in penalty time wreaked havoc in the Gunners backline and it eventually ricocheted in off Mathieu Flamini. The Swans were furious with referee Lee Probert at full-time with Pablo Hernandez clean through, but Arsenal will be left equally frustrated as they toiled once more.

(79’) Nolan breaks through the Hull back line with one of West Ham's only impressive attacking movements this half, but the ball gets caught under his feet and rolls safely into his former teammate Harper's hands.
(77’) West Ham are sitting incredibly deep right now. They try and attempt to embark on a counterattack before quickly realising that every player is camped firmly in their own half, causing the movement to break down without causing Hull too many problems.
(75’) Free kick for West Ham on the halfway line. Demel lofts it into the Hull penalty area and it bounces around before ending up at the feet of Carroll on the edge of the box. He pulls the trigger with so much force that he completely misses the ball. Normally, you'd expect the West Ham fans to laugh, but their fear and nervousness is too great at the moment for them to find any missed chances funny.
(73’) Hull break away once again through Meyler and Long and win a corner. Huddlestone sends it in but fails to beat the first line of defence, and the ball is headed away from danger. The Englishman has had a wonderful game so far, but that attempt was uncharacteristically poor.
(71’) Chance for Hull! Long chests the ball down into the path of Jelavic on the edge of the West Ham penalty area. The Croatian spins around and launches a half-volley towards Adrian, forcing the Spaniard to dive dramatically to his left to save it. However, the linesman's flag had already been raised.
--- 69’ Substitution M. Diamé is done for the day. J. Cole is his replacement. ---
(68’) Hull break away and embark on a dangerous counter attack, but Meyler holds on to the ball for far too long and is dispossessed at the final moment. He should have set up Long a few paces earlier, but he decided to go it alone and pays for his indecision.
(66’) Joe Cole is warming up and looks set to enter the field of play in the coming moments. West Ham desperately need somebody with his attacking talents to help put this game to bed.
(65’) Carroll wins the ball in the middle of the pitch and darts forward, before laying the ball off to Downing on the left wing. His teammate then attempts to set him up in the centre of the penalty area with a lofted ball across goal, but the delivery is poor and it clears everyone in the box.
(63’) After a period of slight pressure in the wake of Chester's own goal, West Ham are looking increasingly frustrated when pushing forward. They need a spark, but nobody on the pitch at the moment looks like they are able to provide it.
(61’) Chance for West Ham! The Hammers patiently push forward, allowing Nolan to hold up on the ball on the edge of the penalty area before setting up Downing behind him, but the resulting shot on goal flies wide of the goal.
--- 59’ Substitution L. Rosenior enters the game and replaces M. Figueroa. ---
(59’) Figueroa wants to continue and tries to sneak his way back onto the pitch, but Steve Bruce has other ideas and sends Rosenior on in his place.
(58’) Figueroa is walking around rather gingerly and it seems as if Steve Bruce is going to be forced to bring him off. But, for now, Hull are battling on with nine men.
(56’) Further problems for Hull, as Figueroa is now down on the floor injured. It looks like the Honduran has a problem with his ankle. When it rains, it pours...
--- 54’ Goal! Goal! Out of nowhere, West Ham are back in the lead, and it's through an own goal! Diame sends in a cross that is, quite frankly, extremely poor, but the unexpected bounce takes Chester by surprise and the defender's panicked clearance bounces off his knee and into the back of his own net. Steve Bruce looks distraught. 2-1! ---
(53’) The frustration is growing around Upton Park as Jelavic almost breaks through one-on-one with Adrian, put the linesman's flag immediately goes up, much to the relief of the home fans.
(51’) The momentum is with Hull now as they push forward in the hope of going into the lead. West Ham are struggling and Carroll is looking extremely isolated up front.
--- 49’ Assist The assist came from T. Huddlestone. ---
--- 49’ Goal! Goal! Hull are back in the game! What a great start to the second half for the visitors! They win a free kick 25 yards out, which Huddlestone decides to drill towards goal. It takes a wicked deflection off Jelavic and flies past Adrian, who remains rooted to the spot and with no chance of saving it. Game on! 1-1! ---
(47’) Figueroa launches a long ball forward from a free kick near the halfway line, which causes all kinds of trouble in the West Ham penalty area. The ball ends up buried under a sea of Hammers shirts before it finally emerges again and is blasted away up the pitch, kickstarting a West Ham counterattack that eventually comes to nothing.
(45’) And we're off once again!
The players are making their way back onto the pitch ahead of the second half. It will be interesting to see if Hull can build on the momentum that they established towards the end of the first period, or if West Ham can finally make the one-man advantage count after struggling against Hull's determined ten men.
West Ham are a goal up at half time, but that hasn't stopped the home fans from booing them off the field. They have played poorly since Hull went down to 10 men, allowing the under-pressure visitors to push forward and get close to making it 1-1. It should have been West Ham in control in the final moments of the first half, but they are spending far too much time on the ball and look to be lacking ideas in the final third, which is a stark contrast to their performance in the opening moments.
HT: WEST HAM UNITED 1-0 HULL CITY
(45’) Nolan tries to meet Downing's cross with his boot but it misses the ball and strikes Figueroa on the head instead. The Honduran defender goes down injured for a moment but is quickly back to his feet, much to the relief of Steve Bruce and the Hull fans.
(45’) Chance for Hull! Figueroa finds himself in plenty of space with the ball 25 yards out, so he decides to fire a great shot towards goal that forces Adrian into a low diving save. Despite being a man down, the visitors are certainly playing the better football of the two sides at the moment.
(45’) A clumsy challenge on Jelavic by Diame gives Hull a free kick in a dangerous position on the left wing. It's delivered wonderfully again by Huddlestone and Chester meets it with his head, sending it over just over the goal. Replays show that it was deflected over by a West Ham player, but a goal kick is given.
(45’) There will be six minutes of added time.
(45’) It's been a bright end to a difficult half for Hull. After knocking the ball around in the centre of the field patiently, Elmohamady sets up Meyler down the right flank, and the Irishman knocks the ball over the head of Nolan before darting into the box, but his boot is dangerously high and West Ham win a free kick.
(43’) Chance for Carroll! Nolan sends a great cross into the Hull penalty area and Carroll once again jumps high to meet it with his head. He sends his attempt down into the ground and it bounces up and over Harper, but it also clears the crossbar and lands on the top of the goal net.
(41’) Taylor is brought down 30 yards out and Mike Dean awards a free kick to the hosts. Downing whips it in but it's headed away and towards the halfway line, where Demel gives away a free-kick himself and allows Hull time to breathe.
(39’) If Hull can hold on and go into the break just one goal down, Steve Bruce will no doubt be delighted. West Ham are trying their hardest to double their lead but, much to the frustration of the home crowd, they are failing to find a way past a resolute Hull defence.
(37’) Chance for Hull! After taking their time, they put together an impressive move that takes West Ham by surprise. The ball ends up with Elmohamady on the right wing and the Egyptian pulls it back to Huddlestone on the edge of the box, but his effort clears the crossbar.
(36’) It's all West Ham at the moment, as expected. Hull have put as many men as possible behind the ball, with only Long positioned anywhere near the halfway line. After another West Ham attack ends, the visitors try to break away themselves, but they lack any sort of options up front and are forced to pass the ball amongst themselves in the middle of the pitch.
(34’) Diame and Collins pass the ball between themselves on the left flank before the former unleashes a cross into the Hull penalty area, but it's too close to Harper and the veteran goalkeeper is easily able to claim the ball for himself, bringing an end to the latest wave of West Ham pressure.
(32’) Diame has been instrumental for the hosts since winning the penalty. Again he darts forward, but Elmohamady is there on the edge of the box to dispossess him at the last moment.
(30’) West Ham smell blood and they're looking to kill off the game as early as possible. They push forward once again and, thanks to a poor piece of defending by Figueroa, win a corner. It's whipped in and meets the head of Carroll, but his attempt clears the bar by a couple of feet.
(28’) Despite the circumstances under which the goal was scored, West Ham certainly do deserve to be ahead. They have looked the most dangerous going forward and have kept Jelavic and Long extremely quiet in the final third of their half.
--- 26’ Goal! Goal! Noble sends Harper the wrong way and calmly puts West Ham into the lead with just 25 minutes played. What a mad five minutes! 1-0! ---
--- 25’ Substitution A. Bruce is replaced with S. Harper. ---
--- 24’ Red card! A. McGregor is sent for an early shower! ---
(24’) Harper has to come on for the visitors, and Bruce is the one that makes way for the substitute goalkeeper, who immediately is required to save Noble's penalty.
(22’) Red card for McGregor! After a lengthy period of treatment for the goalkeeper, the Scotsman has been shown a straight red card for his challenge on Diame, despite the fact that the West Ham midfielder seemed to handle the ball just moments before the two collided.
(21’) Confusion at Upton Park! Noble charges through a hole in the middle of Hull defence before unleashing Diame, who clatters into McGregor in front of goal. Both are lying on the floor injured and it looks as if Mike Dean has given a penalty. The Hull players are surrounding him and protesting the possible decision, although nobody is quite sure what decision has been given...
(20’) Finally, the poor challenges have stopped (for the time being at least) and both sides have returned to playing football.
--- 18’ Yellow card J. Livermore receives a yellow card. ---
(18’) And now it's Hull's turn to be reckless. Livermore flies into Noble and receives the first yellow card of the game.
(16’) The heat is rising, and Nolan is now guilty of bringing down Huddlestone, resulting in referee Mike Dean giving the Hammers captain a talking to.
(14’) McCartney is all over the back of Jelavic and gives away a free kick 30 yards out. Huddlestone curls the resulting set-piece into the heart of the West Ham penalty area and after bobbing around off the heads of two Hull players, Adrian rises high to grab the ball and cut out the danger.
(11’) After a nervy opening 10 minutes, Hull have pushed forward and strung together a half-promising attacking movement, but the West Ham defence prove to be too much for them and the attack down the right flank breaks down without causing the hosts too much trouble.
--- 9’ Substitution R. Johnson enters the game and replaces J. Collins. ---
(9’) West Ham are forced into an early substitution after Collins goes down injured. Johnson enters the field of play to make his first appearance since mid-January.
(8’) Another chance for West Ham! Carroll jumps high again to meet a cross on the edge of the six-yard box and heads the ball towards goal. It's a tame attempt that's cleared easily but the ball falls to Taylor, who unleashes a screamer of a shot, but it's deflected just a few over the crossbar and out for another corner. The hosts are all over the visitors at the moment.
(7’) Downing darts around a static Hull defence before unleashing a low shot from the edge of the box towards McGregor, who dives low to push the ball around the post and out for a corner, which the visitors just about manage to deal with.
(5’) West Ham have picked up the pace somewhat, stringing together several good passes in the middle of the pitch and pushing forward into Hull's half of the field. A lofted ball from McCartney meets Carroll on the edge of the penalty area and the big Englishman uses his frame to win the ball, but he's unable to control it to the best of his ability and the attack eventually comes to an end.
(3’) It's been a slow start to the game so far, with a lot of long, lofted balls that have been as high as they have been unpretty.
(1’) And we're off! The hosts get us underway, attacking from right to left.
The bubbles are blowing, both sets of fans are singing at the top of their lungs, and the two teams are making their way onto the pitch. We're only a few minutes away from kick-off now.
As for West Ham, after embarking on a five-game unbeaten run - with four of those games ending in two-goal-margin victories - they have failed to pick up a single point in March, losing their last three consecutive clashes and dropping to 14th place in the table. However, victory here today will lift them up to 11th and extend the gap between themselves and the relegation zone to nine points.
Hull come into today's game in better form than their East London opponents, with Saturday's 2-0 win, their third in their last six league games, moving them above West Ham and into into 12th place in the table, seven points clear of the relegation zone.
In contrast to his managerial counterpart, Steve Bruce has made two changes to the side that beat West Bromwich Albion 2-0 on the weekend. Maynor Figueroa comes in for Liam Rosenior, whilst Alex Bruce replaces Sone Aluko.
Sam Allardyce has opted to field the same starting 11 that lost 2-0 to Manchester United on Saturday afternoon, with the only new faces on today's team sheet coming in the form of Roger Johnson, who replaces the injured Matt Jarvis, and Ricardo Vaz Te, who is involved for the first time since October of last year when he dislocated his shoulder against Swansea City.
Hull City substitutes: Harper, Rosenior, Koren, Fryatt, Sagbo, Aluko, Quinn
Hull City starting line-up: McGregor; Elmohamady, Bruce, Chester, Davies, Figueroa; Meyler, Huddlestone, Livermore; Jelavic, Long
West Ham United substitutes: Jaaskelainen, Armero, C. Cole, J. Cole, Vaz Te, Johnson, Nocerino
West Ham United starting line-up: Adrian; Demel, Collins, Tomkins, McCartney; Downing, Taylor, Noble, Diame; Nolan; Carroll

Good evening and welcome to the live text commentary of today's Premier League clash between West Ham United and Hull City. My name is Ben Cullimore and I will be keep you up-to-date with all of the action from Upton Park.

Well, that's all from our LIVE coverage of events at Anfield. It was another Premier League cracker - many thanks for joining us, and we'll see you again very soon!
Sunderland, meanwhile, remain three points from safety, and now just have one game in hand on West Brom and Crystal Palace, who lie 16th and 17th respectively. April is going to be a massive month for Poyet's side.
Rodgers' men move up to second with that win, and are now just one point behind Premier League leaders Chelsea. The title race just keeps hotting up, and Liverpool are right in the middle of it.
That is indeed it at Anfield as the whistle goes for FULL TIME! Liverpool get the win, but it was more nervous than it should have been as they dominated most of the match. It was a spirited fightback from Sunderland but the hosts held out in the end.
(90’) Just seconds away from a vital Liverpool victory. Sterling fouls Colback and Mannone hammers it forward, but Altidore loses out in the air. Surely that's it?
(90’) Yet more good hold-up play from the hosts as Johnson first draws a foul from Cattermole, then wins a throw off Colback right by the corner.
(90’) Liverpool are doing well to kill time now as they press into the Sunderland half. Coutinho has a shot blocked by O'Shea before Colback is forced to concede a throw near the corner flag.
(90’) End-to-end stuff here! Johnson is in behind to drill the ball across the area, but Allen is back to clear before Suarez picks it up inside the Sunderland half. He does really well to hold off several challenges but eventually loses out, and the visitors clear as we enter three added minutes.
(89’) O'SHEA!! What a chance!! Johnson flicks the free kick into the area and O'Shea flicks it on, but the ball flashes across the six-yard box, evading Altidore's stretch before going behind for a goal kick.
(88’) Chance here for Sunderland as Colback goes up against Johnson on the left-hand side, and knocks it past the Liverpool man before going down near the by-line. It looks soft but the visitors have a free kick.
(87’) Error by Bridcutt, who gives it straight to Sterling, and the winger spreads it out wide to Henderson. The midfielder slightly hesitates, though, and is quickly shut down by Colback and Bridcutt, who makes amends for his error by winning it back.
(86’) Suarez loses possession to Vergini, who showed good strength to muscle the striker off the ball. Cattermole wastes the opportunity, though, seeing his diagonal pass forward cut out by Flanagan.
(85’) You can feel the tension at Anfield now as the players and fans all look a bit nervous. Gerrard is called into action in his own box, clearing an Altidore cross from the right-hand side.
(84’) Real chance for Sunderland as Liverpool are caught short and Johnson spreads the ball wide for Bardsley, who charges towards the area before seeing his drilled shot deflect well out of danger.
--- 83’ Substitution J. Colback enters the game and replaces A. Dossena. ---
(83’) Jack Colback replaces Dossena, who has had a torrid time in this second half dealing with Suarez especially. Not long left at Anfield - can Sunderland get an equaliser?
(82’) Chance for Sunderland as Bardsley gets into an advanced position on the right after good work from Johnson. The defender swings in a cross looking for Altidore by the penalty spot, but the American is all over Skrtel and the whistle goes for a free kick.
(81’) SUAREZ GOES CLOSE!! It's a better effort than his set piece in the first half, as he curls a vicious shot over and around the wall, but just inches over the crossbar with Mannone scrambling desperately.
(80’) Cattermole is in trouble with the referee as the defender commits a foul 30 yards from goal. Who will take this one?
(79’) Raheem Sterling is on for Sturridge, and immediately shows lightning pace to keep the ball in play right by the corner, and Suarez shows wonderful determination and skill to both get to the ball first and then keep it away from two defenders.
(78’) SUAREZ!! The Uruguayan tries the spectacular, looking to chip Mannone from 30 yards, but the goalkeeper gets back easily to catch it from under his own crossbar. It might not be Suarez's night, after all...
--- 77’ Substitution D. Sturridge is done for the day. R. Sterling is his replacement. ---
(77’) That's made things rather interesting. Will Liverpool pay for not going further in front while they had the chance?
--- 76’ Assist A. Johnson gave the assist. ---
--- 76’ Goal! KI PULLS ONE BACK!! He's been the visitors' best player in just 15 minutes, and he's on the scoresheet as Johnson's corner evades everyone before the Korean nods into an empty net. ---
(75’) KI!! The midfielder has been superb since coming on, and chests the ball down on the edge of the area before seeing a low volley deflected behind for a corner.
(74’) Penalty? Coutinho seems to think so as he cuts inside the area before going down under a light challenge from O'Shea. The defender, and the referee, aren't impresses and play goes on.
(73’) Almost 2-1, then nearly 3-0!! It's been an incredible second half so far, but Sturridge's early goal after the break is the only action on the scoresheet in these 45.
(72’) STURRIDGE HITS THE BAR!! The woodwork at the other end is rattled straight away as Sturridge runs on to a lay-off on the edge of the box, curving a shot towards the top corner but seeing it hammer back off the frame of the goal.
(71’) CATTERMOLE SMASHES THE BAR!! What a chance for Sunderland!! The ball is lifted out to the left-hand side, and Johson volleys it back to the edge of the box for Cattermole, who rifles a first-time volley on to the crossbar with Mignolet beaten.
(70’) Cattermole tries to set a quick Sunderland attack forward, firing a diagonal ball into the path of Johnson, but he drags it and Liverpool get a throw.
(69’) Just over 20 minutes to go, and Liverpool should see the remainder of this game out now. Ki has impressed since coming on, though, but can he inspire an unlikely comeback?
(68’) Nice work, Bridcutt!! The midfielder does really well to keep an overhit ball across field in play, flicking a header up at full stretch before sliding to keep it from rolling over the line. It even prompts applause from the home fans!
(66’) Yet more danger for the visitors as Sturridge chips over the top for Suarez, who tries to return it to his strike partner, but his lofted cross is too high and Vergini heads it behind for a corner.
(65’) COUTINHO!! It's not long before the hosts get the ball back, and they're straight into the opposing half. Suarez has it outside the box and scoops a fantastic ball over the top for Coutinho, who tries to lift the ball over Mannone on the volley, but it's a simple save in the end.
(64’) Excellent work from Johnson, who almost cuts out a risky Gerrard pass before chasing down both Mignolet and Skrtel, forcing the defender to put it out for a throw.
(63’) KI!! The substitutes combine well in their first contribution, as Ki squares to Johnson before continuing his run, and the winger flicks the ball over the top of the Liverpool defence. Ki is the only one chasing but can't quite reach the ball to flick an effort at goal, and it's a goal kick.
(62’) VERGINI!! How many lives does he have?! Johnson fires in another low cross and the defender completely fluffs the clearance, slicing it behind him and just over his own crossbar.
--- 61’ Substitution A. Johnson enters the game and replaces E. Giaccherini. ---
--- 61’ Substitution Sung-Yong Ki enters play, replacing C. Wickham. ---
(61’) It's a double change for the Black Cats as Adam Johnson and Ki Sung-Yeung replace Giaccherini and the ineffectual Wickham.
(60’) Altidore goes up with Mignolet and ends up taking out the goalkeeper and Skrtel at the same time. It's a free kick to the hosts, and Poyet looks like he's preparing changes.
(59’) MANNONE SPILLS!! The Sunderland goalkeeper almost lets Liverpool in as he fumbles Johnson's cross looking for Sturridge at the near post, but he gathers it quickly before Suarez can pounce on the loose ball.
(58’) SUAREZ!! After Wickham is caught offside in the Liverpool box, the hosts quickly come forward as Suarez receives it on the left, cutting inside Vergini before flashing a shot just wide of Mannone's far post.
(56’) Excellent defending from Coutinho, who has really stepped his performance up after the break, and he halts a Sunderland attack as he tracks back to win the ball off Bardsley.
(55’) This is a very dangerous spell for the visitors now, as Agger holds off Bardsley before spreading it wide to Coutinho. It comes back to Suarez, who looks for Johnson with a diagonal ball out wide, but it skips off the Anfield surface and goes out for a goal kick.
(54’) SHOULD BE THREE!! Coutinho again gets things going with a beautiful flick to Allen, who pulls back from the by-line, and Sturridge fires first time towards the corner, only to see his effort blocked by Suarez. The Uruguayan then tries to sneak the ball in under Mannone but the Sunderland goalkeeper stands firm and turns it behind.
(53’) Liverpool look really in the mood now, especially Coutinho, who produces two lovely touches in 30 seconds, first spreading the ball out wide before later flicking it over the top of Dossena's head.
(52’) Nearly a great chance for the visitors as Giaccherini finds some space in between the lines, but Bridcutt's pass into him is too powerful and he can't bring it under control.
(51’) It's been a lonely evening for Sunderland's strikers so far, and that's shown once more as Wickham is completely isolated before losing out to Skrtel, who comfortably wins the ball and plays it to Gerrard.
(50’) A frantic couple of minutes, then! That could have killed the game off completely, although it still looks like Liverpool should see this one out comfortably now.
(49’) Penalty? Liverpool are in straight away and Suarez charges towards the area, and it looks like the striker is clipped by Cattermole just inside the box but, amazingly, nothing is given.
--- 48’ Assist The assist came from J. Henderson. ---
--- 48’ Goal! STURRIDGE MAKES IT TWO!! What a strike!! Henderson picks the ball up in midfield and squares it out to Sturridge, who cuts in from the right-hand edge of the area before bending a wonderful strike across goal and into the top corner. ---
(47’) SUAREZ!! A good chance goes begging as the familiar trio of Suarez, Henderson and Johnson link up again before the latter gets to the by-line inside the box. He's quickly closed down by O'Shea but the ball pops out and into the path of Suarez, whose left-footed effort disappointingly flies way over the bar.
(46’) Liverpool get the action back underway at Anfield as we're off for the second half.
It's almost time to resume proceedings at Anfield. It's still tight at 1-0 but the hosts have controlled the tempo of the game. Gerrard's goal was their only shot on target, and you have to worry for Sunderland if Liverpool start to find their shooting boots.
Can Poyet's men change their tactics and get back in the game? Or will it be more of the same from Liverpool? Be sure to join us when we come back for the second half.
Sunderland's deep defending looked to be working, but Vergini let them down late on in the half with a rash challenge on Suarez. It could be worse though, after that second foul which could easily have seen another booking for the defender.
That's HALF TIME at Anfield and Liverpool take a 1-0 lead into the changing room after dominating proceedings so far this evening. It took a thunderous free kick from Gerrard, but they're ahead and on course for second place.
(45’) Gerrard fires the set piece low into the six-yard box, but O'Shea heads it clear before Johnson can't make use of the second ball, giving it straight back to the visitors.
(45’) Oh, Vergini, you lucky boy. The defender has absolutely no chance of winning the ball as he slides in on Suarez on the left-hand edge of the box. The referee pities him, though, and doesn't brandish a second yellow, although it's a free kick in a dangerous position.
(44’) The first corner is easily dealt with but Sunderland scrap to win another. Unfortunately, though, it's a poor delivery from Giaccherini and Liverpool clear. Dossena is then penalised for a foul throw which, quite frankly, is embarrassing at this level.
(43’) The Sunderland pressure continues as Flanagan is forced to put it behind for a corner. Can they surprise the hosts and get a leveller?
(42’) WICKHAM!! He's been far from prolific, but the striker almost levels things as he twists and turns outside the area before firing a low shot at goal from 20 yards. It takes a deflection and looks bound for the corner before Mignolet stretches to divert it behind for a corner.
(41’) The flag goes up as Sturridge is caught offside, and Sunderland can try to push forward before the break. Anfield is much louder now; you could feel the collective sigh of relief as that free kick went in.
--- 40’ Yellow card P. Bardsley is cautioned by the referee. ---
(40’) That's the breakthrough they've been desperately hunting for, and it comes before half time, which is a real blow to the visitors, who have defended stoically until now.
--- 39’ Goal! GERRARD OPENS THE SCORING!! It's a stunning set piece from the Liverpool skipper as he steps up and bends a vicious effort towards goal. Mannone is slightly wrong-footed, still managing to get to it, but can only help it into the top corner. 1-0. ---
(38’) It's a free kick to the hosts, similar to the earlier one from Suarez, but in a more central position. Can they move in front here?
--- 37’ Yellow card S. Vergini goes into the referee's book. ---
(37’) Could this be a red card? No! Suarez is beyond Vergini and the defender takes out the striker before he gets in on goal. It looks like he's the last man but the referee only gives a yellow, suggesting Brown may possibly have got across to Suarez in time.
(36’) Wickham thinks he is through on goal as he latches on to Giaccherini's flicked ball beyond the defence, but the whistle goes as he grapples with Skrtel and the Liverpool man ends up on the floor.
(35’) SUAREZ!! Skrtel does well to snuff out a Sunderland attack and his pass forward is deflected into the path of Suarez, who races towards the Sunderland box. He is faced with three or four yellow shirts, though, and cuts on to his left before firing a 20-yard effort wide.
(34’) Johnson - and the Liverpool fans - are furious as the defender goes down under a challenge from Dossena, only to see nothing given. This is proving to be a key duel so far tonight.
(33’) Gerrard finds Suarez in a rare bit of space, and the striker tries to slot Johnson through, but his touch lets him down and he slips as two Sunderland defenders come in to steal the ball.
(32’) Henderson spreads the ball out to Johnson on the right, and the full-back tries to fire it into the box, but again the delivery is blocked by Dossena before O'Shea clears. The Sunderland defenders are working very hard tonight.
(31’) Johnson gives the ball straight to Dossena after Allen had worked hard to win it off Bardsley. It's a little tight and scrappy at times in the middle, and Bridcutt causes a stoppage as he clips Coutinho and concedes a free kick.
(30’) The atmosphere is a little more muted than usual at Anfield; you sense the tension creeping into the stands. 15 minutes to go until the break - can the hosts break the deadlock before then?
(29’) Altidore v Flanagan has been an interesting battle so far, and at the moment it's the Liverpool man on top as the striker again loses out, this time fouling his opponent on the touchline deep inside the hosts' half.
(28’) Good goalkeeping from Mannone, who is on to Coutinho's through ball like a flash, getting there at the by-line before Henderson and claiming the ball comfortably.
(27’) ALLEN!! It's the midfielder's turn to try a speculative effort, drifting towards the edge of the area before firing a 20-yard shot high and wide. Liverpool still struggling to create chances in the box.
(26’) Not the early goal fest we expected, then, but Liverpool are very much in control of this game. You suspect patience is key for them tonight, as they could end up getting very frustrated by Poyet's tactics.
(25’) Bardsley is put under all sorts of pressure from Coutinho and Allen, seeing his ball down the line deflected infield and Henderson is on to it, giving the hosts another chance to mount an attack.
(24’) Sunderland are defending very deep, and the hosts are finding it hard to get in behind at the moment. Johnson is forced to make a poor cross before Suarez is quickly closed down by three defenders. The striker wants a free kick but nothing is given and the visitors hack it forward.
(23’) Surprisingly loose touch from Suarez, who receives the ball off Coutinho before trying to cut on to his right and get a shot away, but his control lets him down and Bardsley challenges well to help Sunderland clear once more.
(22’) There's just a hint that Sunderland could grow into this game, albeit a small hint. Bardsley fires in a dangerous cross from the right but it's headed away, before Mignolet shanks a clearance out for a throw.
(21’) Excellent display of strength from Flanagan, who manages to hold off Altidore out wide and win a throw off the striker. Clearly stronger than he looks, the young full-back.
(20’) Allen is penalised for a foul on Bardsley inside the Sunderland box, giving the visitors' defence a chance for respite as Mannone will launch it forward.
(19’) Allen commits Bridcutt in midfield before playing wide to Coutinho, who charges in diagonally before sliding a pass beyond the defence for Sturridge. The striker gets to it first but is forced all the way to the by-line, and his attempted backheel is easily dealt with.
(18’) The Reds almost in as Suarez picks it up on the left, and fires in a cheeky cross with the outside of his right foot, but Sturridge has to stretch and can't get high enough to divert it towards goal.
(17’) That's poor from O'Shea, who tries to switch play out to Dossena on the left-hand side, but gets the ball all wrong and sends it straight out for a throw to Liverpool.
(16’) It's been comfortable so far for the hosts, but Sunderland have held off their usual high-tempo start and the best chances have been shots from distance. It's unlikely that will continue, though.
(15’) Good work on the right from Liverpool as Henderson and Suarez link up before the latter plays Johnson in behind Dossena, but the full-back had just strayed offside and the flag goes up.
(14’) Not one for the scrapbook for Suarez, here, as Henderson loops a header back in his direction and the striker tries a spectacular volley. Unfortunately for him, it's a complete air kick and he ends up looking rather embarrassed.
(13’) This is better from Sunderland as Cattermole spreads the ball out to Dossena, who has time to fire in a cross. It's cleared by Skrtel, but only as far as the edge of the box, and Bardsley tries a volley which is blocked before the hosts clear their lines.
(12’) Dossena looks for Wickham with an early ball in from the left, but Agger deals with it comfortably and the hosts break quickly. Suarez almost finds his strike partner with a cute ball forward, but there's too much on it and Sunderland have possession.
(10’) STURRIDGE!! If the game carries on like this the hosts will score before much longer. Coutinho has plenty of space to move into the Sunderland half before squaring to Henderson, who finds Sturridge on the right-hand corner of the box. The striker cuts inside and flashes a shot just over the crossbar from 20 yards.
(9’) The Sunderland defence has its work cut out tonight, and Sturridge shows his menace as he works into the box before producing a series of stepovers and neat touches, but his shot is blocked and then Suarez concedes a free kick on the edge of the area.
(8’) The players clearly fancy some long-range efforts tonight. Cattermole works hard to keep hold of possession before squaring to Bridcutt, who fires into the Kop from around 30 yards.
(7’) SUAREZ!! The Uruguayan steps up to take the set piece and curves it beautifully over the wall, aiming to swing his effort inside the near post, but there's too much height on it and the ball goes into the stand.
(6’) Flanagan moves into the Sunderland half and plays the ball inside to Sturridge who, with his back to goal, draws a foul from O'Shea. Here's a real chance for the hosts from a free kick 25 yards out...
(5’) Liverpool's second shot in the opening five minutes comes from Coutinho, but it's also never going to trouble Mannone as his right-footed effort from 30 yards floats high over the bar.
(4’) Good work by Dossena on the left, who nods back a high ball into the path of Giaccherini, but the midfielder can't keep control and Suarez gets hold of it. He charges down the rigth but is halted illegally by Brown and the hosts have a free kick inside their own half.
(3’) Johnson fires a wayward shot into the stands, giving the Black Cats a chance to have some of their own possession. Vergini salvages a loose ball, keeping it away from Suarez, before Dossena's long ball forward is put out for a throw by Skrtel.
(2’) Danger straight away for the visitors as Sturridge swings in a cross from the right. Allen charges into the box and can't quite reach it  before Vergini diverts it towards his own goal, but Mannone gets a good first-time clearance away.
(1’) Sunderland get the ball rolling, and we're underway on Merseyside.
The players are out of the tunnel and Anfield is as noisy as ever. We'll be treated to the customary belting out of "You'll Never Walk Alone", and then it's time to get started.
So, a win tonight will move Liverpool to within a point of leaders Chelsea. Rodgers has delivered plenty for the fans this season, but now they want more. Can they pick up their first Premier League title? Just five minutes to go until kick-off.
Liverpool, though, are having a fantastic 2014. I've already mentioned they're unbeaten this calendar year in the league, and the records look set to keep tumbling. Their tally of 82 goals is their highest ever in a 38-game season, and they've still got eight more to go.
The omens aren't good for Gus Poyet's men, it has to be said. The Black Cats have 26 Premier League goals this season, which is two fewer than Suarez has all by himself. They've also not won in their last four games and haven't scored since Fabio Borini's early goal against Manchester City in the League Cup final.
The visitors, meanwhile, ring in the changes from their defeat at Norwich, switching to five at the back as Santiago Vergini and Andrea Dossena come into defence. Lee Cattermole returns in midfield while Emanuele Giaccherini also gets the nod, and Jozy Altidore is given support up front in the form of Connor Wickham.
Brendan Rodgers goes with exactly the same XI that won 6-3 at Cardiff on Saturday as he looks for a seventh straight Premier League victory. Luis Suarez is one goal away from beating Robbie Fowler's record of most Premier League goals for Liverpool in one season, and you'd be a fool to bet against him doing that tonight.
Sunderland subs: Ki, Larsson, Johnson, Colback, Roberge, Scocco, Ustari.
Sunderland (5-3-2): Mannone; Bardsley, Brown, O'Shea, Vergini, Dossena; Cattermole, Bridcutt, Giaccherini; Altidore, Wickham.
Liverpool subs: Jones, Sterling, Aspas, Sakho, Lucas, Cissokho, Moses.
