The players are embroiled in a bit of post-match animosity, with players squaring up to one another and Torres pushing Foster. Chelsea have managed to escape their bogey ground the Hawthorns with a point, with Anichebe's glancing header handing the Baggies an important draw.
(90’) WILLIAN! Hazard drives down the left flank, before cutting the ball back into the path of Willian, arriving late on the edge of the box. The Brazilian's strike is blocked by McAuley, Foster prevents the ball from going behind, but the referee awards a corner!
(90’) BERAHINO! The youngster smashes a low drive across the penalty area, but it is just about dealt with by Luiz! West Brom remain on top, with Torres extremely isolated, and Mourinho will probably be happy with a point now!
(90’) ANICHEBE! The goalscorer races past an injured Cahill, onto a lofted through ball, but he can't find the winning goal! He is forced wide by the recovering England international, and thumps his effort into the legs of his marker. Corner for West Brom, but the first is deflected behind for another corner...
(90’) VYDRA! The former Watford striker looked to feed off the knock-down of the imposing Anichebe, but he can't keep his volley down! The Czech international hasn't found his scoring touch for the Baggies, but there's still time for him to make himself a hero.
(90’) IVANOVIC! Well, that was a terrible effort! The Serbian defender has been amongst the goals in recent weeks and tonight, and decides to try his luck from 30 yards - resulting in the most embarrassing strike of the night. As long as it's not in their half, however, Chelsea won't mind.
(90’) The home fans continue to urge their players forward, with Mourinho cutting an isolated figure in the Chelsea technical area. Their assured first half performance seems a long time ago now, and the away side have surrendered their control over this match in some style.
(90’) BRUNT! OVER! Berahino picks out his teammate on the edge of the box with a smart pass, but he can't get it out from his feet, and arrows his shot over the bar! There will be SIX minutes of added time!
--- 89’ Substitution Mohamed Salah enters the game and replaces Ramires. ---
--- 89’ Yellow card N. Matić is yellow-carded. ---
(89’) BERAHINO! The England U21 international receives possession on the edge of the area, before looking to slide in Anichebe, but the goalscorer can't quite take the ball in his stride! In the dying embers of the game, it's looking to be the Baggies who will find the next goal.
--- 88’ Yellow card V. Anichebe gets yellow. ---
(88’) Well, that goal was certainly coming, Chelsea have looked rattled since Anichebe took to the field. Salah is going to be the man coming on, rather than Lampard, as Mourinho changes his plans. A point just won't do for the visitors, especially against a side in such poor form.
--- 87’ Assist S. Berahino gave the assist. ---
--- 87’ Goal! GOOOOOOAL! WEST BROM EQUALISE THROUGH ANICHEBE! The Nigerian substitute manages to get the faintest of flicks on a great cross, allowing for the ball to bounce onto the inside of the post and trickle in! Well, the changes have worked! ---
(85’) Cahill receives some treatment on the field, before the former Bolton defender is forced to limp off the field due to his injury - but is of course taking the longest possible route to the match. Lampard is readying himself to come on, but as soon as Cahill leaves the field of play, he looks much more sprightly.
(83’) Chelsea have to weather the storm for less than ten minutes, but Mourinho's men are looking worried. They've been rattled by West Brom's switch to three strikers, and are committing foul after foul. Cahill goes down injured, and it wouldn't be surprising if the England international was simply taking the momentum out of the game.
(82’) David Luiz is all over Anichebe's shirt in the penalty area, but Anthony Taylor doesn't look interested! The Brazil international is tugging at his shirt, almost pulling it off, but Chelsea escape. Matic commits a foul, 30 yards from goal, and the league leaders are looking uncertain.
--- 81’ Yellow card David Luiz goes into the referee's book. ---
(80’) MORRISON! Great block from David Luiz! Morrison bursts into the penalty area, before looking to unleash a hammer-strike across Cech's goal, but the Brazilian defender slides in well. From the resulting corner, the delivery is excellent, but a queue of Baggies' players can't turn it home.
--- 79’ Substitution Oscar is replaced with J. Obi Mikel. ---
(79’) While Pepe Mel makes positive changes, Mourinho does the polar opposite, bringing on Mikel in place of Oscar. That is a statement of intent from Chelsea to close this game out, and it's an understandable move. The Baggies are starting to get on top, with possession sticking upfront.
--- 78’ Substitution M. Vydra enters play, replacing T. Bifouma. ---
(77’) West Brom are certainly going for the equaliser now, Pepe Mel has switched to three men up front, and it's starting to find a few chinks in Chelsea's armour. Thievy looks to have a touch of cramp, however, and may have to be replaced on his home debut,
--- 76’ Yellow card B. Ivanović gets yellow. ---
(76’) BRUNT! Another chance for West Brom, as gaps start to appear in the Chelsea defence! Brunt is found with time and space at the back post, but he chooses to strike the cross on the volley, rather than controlling it. He volleys five yards wide of the post.
(75’) THIEVY! So close for the home side! A West Brom corner is floated towards the back post, before an attempted header falls to Thievy unmarked at the back post. He thrashes it towards goal, but it takes the slightest deflection and skips narrowly wide of the far post.
(74’) The home crowd continue to urge their team forward, with the physical qualities of Berahino and Thievy continuing to shine through. As players start to tire, these two look as though they could keep playing all evening! Pressure building for the hosts.
--- 73’ Substitution M. Amalfitano is replaced with V. Anichebe. ---
(72’) MORRISON! The West Brom midfielder blazes narrowly over the crossbar from just inside the area! Thievy did excellently to beat Ivanovic and slide the ball inside to the Scotland international, but he couldn't convert the opportunity.
(70’) West Brom still have 20 minutes left to find an equaliser, but Chelsea are looking solid and disciplined, as Mourinho has set up his side excellently yet again. Hazard bursts into the area, before shaping to cross but choosing to cut back on himself. He feeds Torres the ball, but the substitute is under intense pressure and can't get a shot away.
--- 69’ Substitution Fernando Torres enters play, replacing S. Eto'o. ---
(68’) A few yellow cards have been shown in this second half, as the tempo drops and the flow of the game starts to be interrupted. Torres is warming up on the sidelines for Chelsea, just in time to see Eto'o blaze well wide. Hazard worked hard to break down the left, before releasing the former Inter striker with a clever flick, but the former Cameroon international blasts over from a tight angle.
--- 67’ Yellow card Willian goes into the referee's book. ---
(66’) Well claimed by Cech! The Chelsea goalkeeper is quick off his line to smother an intelligent flick-on by Amalfitano, as it looked to bobble through to the lurking Berahino! The young English striker throws his hands to his face in frustration.
(65’) MCAULEY! The Northern Ireland defender meets a West Brom corner, which was won by good work down the left from Berahino and Amalfitano, but can't turn it towards goal! It deflects off the side of his forehead and loops well wide.
--- 63’ Substitution Y. Mulumbu enters the game and replaces C. Yacob. ---
(63’) Pepe Mel is forced into the first change of the evening, with the injured Yacob being replaced by Mulumbu. That might be a blessing in disguise for the hosts, as the Argentine midfielder was already on a yellow card, allowing for his replacement to be a little more forceful in the tough midfield battle.
(62’) Thievy! He ducks and weaves on the edge of the penalty area, but can't bypass both Azpilicueta and Cahill, and ends up turning back into trouble. The former Espanyol man is certainly a raw talent, but he's struggling to find the final ball or great effort which would make him an instant fan favourite.
(60’) Chelsea are looking very assured, with the blend of energy from Ramires and pure strength from Matic making it very hard for the Baggies to have any extensive midfield pressure. When Oscar drops back to make a midfield three, the hosts are really struggling to find any kind of staying power in the centre of the park.
(58’) WILLIAN! Excellent strike from the Brazilian, but Foster is equal to it! It's hit with such force from 20 yards, that it looks to swerve in the air, but it in fact takes a wicked deflection! Foster re-adjusts to beat the effort away, in what turned out to be a great save.
(57’) OSCAR! He's found in plenty of space on the right flank, before skipping into the area and ballooning an effort over the back post! It's rather hard to tell whether that was a cross or a shot, but it was pretty awful either way!
(55’) One thing which West Brom fans can certainly come to expect from Pepe Mel's side is constant desire, whether it be to attack with pace or to win the ball back. At the moment, however, it's simply a case of Mourinho's side being too well-drilled and comfortable to be flustered by the Baggies' approach.
(53’) That's a late challenge on Ridgewell from Willian, but the English left-back does his opponent a huge favour, by springing straight back to his feet. It was only a clash of hips, but it did look much worse at the high speed the Premier League is played at.
(52’) Chelsea have started the game quite well in the second half, with Eto'o continuing to be an ever-present runner. West Brom aren't able to play with the same tempo as they did in the first half, and are relying more on the pace of their strikers to carry themselves upfield.
--- 50’ Yellow card C. Yacob is cautioned by the referee. ---
(50’) ETO'O! The Cameroon striker forces Foster into his first real save of the game, as he arrows a firm shot towards the front post, after being played in by a cute pass from Willian. He got behind the ball, but the tight angle made it easier for the Baggies keeper.
(48’) Good defending from David Luiz! Berahino manages to drive down the channel, before looking to cut inside the Brazilian defender, but Luiz stands tall to block his path. The West Brom forward doesn't give up, but the Chelsea man remains calm, shepherding the ball out of play.
(47’) OSCAR! The diminutive Brazilian has the first opportunity of the second half, as a half-clearance falls to the midfielder, 20 yards from goal. His first touch is a dipping half volley, but it spirals well wide of the post, with Foster looking anything but flustered.
(46’) We are back underway for the second half! Chelsea took an important lead in first half stoppage time, courtesy of Branislav Ivanovic, but Mourinho's men still have a lot of work to do to put this game to bed. West Brom's front three have been threatening on the break, so this second period of 45 minutes should be enthralling!
Chances for Eto'o, Ivanovic and Willian have been the best opportunities for the away side, who have dominated possession. West Brom haven't been scared to have a go, with Thievy and Berahino combining well at times, but Cech has been totally untroubled in the Chelsea net.
HALF TIME! Chelsea have nicked the half time advantage in stoppage time, but Mourinho's men aren't out of the woods yet. Ivanovic's goal is what the visitors deserve, but West Brom still pose a real threat on the break, forcing the away side to perhaps go looking for the second goal.
--- 45’ +3 Goal! GOOOOOAL! IVANOVIC GIVES CHELSEA THE LEAD AT THE DEATH! Good work undone for the hosts, as the Serbian right-back turns home a corner in the dying seconds, volleying home from six yards out! ---
--- 45’ +3 Assist Assist by David Luiz. ---
(45’) CAHILL! The England defender wants a penalty, as he is clambered on by Yacob, but the referee says that nothing is doing! He certainly looked to be hauled down, but no penalty for Chelsea!
(45’) Chelsea are building some pressure late in the half, firing several crosses into the box, but West Brom are weathering the storm. The duo of McAuley and Dawson are looking to be a good match for Eto'o. There are two minutes of stoppage time added on.
(44’) ETO'O! Great challenge from McAuley! Ramires is fed down the right flank by a Hazard header, and delivers a wonderful low ball towards the near post, begging for Eto'o to meet it. McAuley stretches across his man, however, and prevents Foster from making his first save of the match.
(42’) WILLIAN! Following a headed clearance by McAuley, Willian controls the ball on his chest from 25 yards out, before striking it on the volley ambitiously! It fizzes over the crossbar, but the former Anzhi winger is getting closer with each effort.
--- 41’ Yellow card M. Amalfitano gets yellow. ---
(40’) CAHILL! The former Bolton defender rises highest to meet a Chelsea corner delivery, climbing all over his marker to reach the ball! The referee would have blown for a foul, but the England international's header bounced its way into the gloves of Foster - play on.
(39’) West Brom continue to hold their shape, with Chelsea looking a little low on ideas, apart from when Hazard is on the ball. The Belgium international looks to be the game's catalyst, a chance looks like materialising whenever he receives possession.
(37’) Ramires returns to the field after a couple of minutes of physio attention, to the loud whistles of the home support. Less than ten minutes until the break, and both sets of fans remain in great voice, having seen glimpses of inspiration from both of the respective sides. This game could come completely alive with a goal.
(35’) Ramires beats Thievy with an excellent piece of skill, chopping the ball away from the attempted challenge of the West Brom forward. The Chelsea midfielder goes down clutching his leg, and will need some medical attention for what looked like an innocuous challenge. Thievy is certainly endearing himself to the home support!
(33’) RAMIRES! The Brazilian tries to cross from the left byeline, but his delivery is deflected by the leg of Reid, looping the ball towards the back post, forcing Foster to watch the effort dip wide. Moments later, Ivanovic is bearing down on the Baggies' goal yet again, but the right-back is tackled firmly, with Chelsea winning a corner.
(32’) Berahino skips around a poor challenge from Matic, before looking to pick out Thievy with an eye-of-the-needle pass into the Frenchman from the edge of the area. It's cut out by Cahill, who hoofs clear. The league leaders aren't having it all their own way at the Hawthorns.
(30’) Chelsea continue to monopolise possession, with West Brom continuing to threaten on the break. Their forward three look to get forward whenever they can, with both Berahino and Thievy able to hold up play and wait for onrushing support.
(28’) BRUNT! West Brom break down the right yet again, before a cross to the back post is nodded back square by Berahino. Thievy gets on the end of the knock-down, but his control lets him down, forcing him to pass the ball backwards to Brunt. The midfielder lets fly with his first touch, but drags his effort wide of the far post from 18 yards.
(27’) WILLIAN! The Brazilian receives possession 25 yards out from goal, before taking a quick touch out of his feet and hammering an effort towards Foster. The ball whistles narrowly over the crossbar, with the West Brom keeper having his angles covered.
(26’) HAZARD! Great ball from the young winger, he carves open some space on the right flank, before whipping a cross directly through the corridor of uncertainty, with Foster glued to his line. He's been Chelsea's most creative influence, switching wings at will, and he looks to be the player who will make the difference.
(24’) Thievy receives some instructions on the sideline for the Baggies, and the new signing might be being told to hang on the shoulder of a certain Chelsea defender. If the hosts can pick a good pass over Chelsea's defensive line, the former Espanyol man will be through on goal, with pace to burn.
(22’) ETO'O! IVANOVIC! The Cameroonian striker wriggles free of his marker, spinning off with his back to goal, and drives to the byeline. He cuts a pass back into the path of Ivanovic, who had steamed into the penalty area, but the Serbia international is denied the chance to shoot by a combination of McAuley and Foster.
(21’) Well, we're past the 20 minute mark, and neither side are yet to fashion a clear cut chance. Chelsea are in control, moving the ball smartly and sharply, but they can't seem to find an incisive pass. West Brom will be buoyed, they've held their own.
(19’) Amalfitano stabs a ball in between Azpilicueta and Luiz for Berahino to chase, but the Brazilian centre-half just about has enough of a head-start to reach the intended pass first. West Brom haven't threatened too much, but the athleticism of their forwards is causing a few issues for the away side.
(17’) The home crowd are incensed with our referee for the night, Anthony Taylor, as the match official gives two throw-ins in quick succession to Chelsea - when they believe that the decision should have awarded them to their team. Amalfitano joins the protests too, but the Frenchman needs to be careful, he's already been warned for his dissent.
(15’) THIEVY! West Brom break in numbers, with Thievy, Berahino and Amalfitano pressing upfield quickly, but the former fails to find his strike partner with a cut-back from the byeline. A couple of nice step-overs, but no final ball from the striker, who does look to have the beating of Chelsea's defence for pace.
(14’) Chelsea will be pleased with how they've started this game, dominating possession and enjoying plenty of time in the opposition half. Cech has had nothing to do apart from watch the game, so far, and Mourinho will be pleased with how his side have set up their stall.
(12’) OSCAR! McAuley hooks away the Brazilian's attempted cross! Good work from Eto'o, who holds up Dawson at the edge of the box with his back to goal, before flicking a pass backwards to the advancing Oscar. The Brazil international stabs a cross along the length of the six yard box, but only McAuley is present at the back post to ensure that nobody in black can stab it home.
(10’) The opening ten minutes have passed without either goalkeeper being tested, but both managers will be pleased with their sides' intensities. Both outfits are prepared to press and harry, with new Baggies forward Thievy in particular hassling the Chelsea backline and defensive midfielders.
(8’) Hazard cuts in from the left hand side this time, with Amalfitano unwilling to get too close to the Belgian, but his slipped ball inside rolls through to Foster. Eto'o looked to control it in the middle of the penalty area, but the pass rolled under his foot and through to the awaiting former Man United keeper.
(7’) Half chance for West Brom! The hosts break down the right once again, and this time it's David Luiz's turn to hook a powerful cross away at the near post. The final ball hasn't been forthcoming yet, but this game is certainly rather open. The hosts aren't willing to sit back, despite their recent form under new boss Pepe Mel.
(6’) Good work from Ramires! Amalfitano saves the Baggies, as the Frenchman tracks back effectively to prevent Willian from racing through on goal, following a lung-bursting run from Ramires. The Brazil international sidestepped two challenges before laying the former Anzhi man through, but Amalfitano stuck to his responsibilities well.
(5’) Smart clearance from Dawson! Chelsea's dangerman Eden Hazard cuts in from the right, before laying the ball into space for the overlapping Ivanovic. The Serbian right-back delivers early, but Dawson is on hand to scramble the ball away before it reaches the near post.
(3’) Cool head from Dawson! The former Rochdale centre-back cushions a lofted through ball back to his goalkeeper, despite being under intense pressure from the scavenging Samuel Eto'o. An even start at the Hawthorns, and the Baggies aren't looking starstruck.
(2’) Good start from West Brom! They push down the right flank, with Amalfitano and Berahino combining smartly, before the former whips in a dangerous cross. Ivanovic stoops low to head the ball away at the back post. West Brom are lining up with two forwards this evening, though Berahino looks to have some defensive responsibility on the left.
(1’) And we are underway in the first half at the Hawthorns! Snow has been falling in the stadium, but we should be fine to continue, with the playing surface looking unaffected. West Brom are in their customary blue and white shirts, while Chelsea are donning their black away strip.
Well, snow is falling at the Hawthorns, as has been the case all over England today, which will add to Chelsea's challenge here tonight. The current league leaders have struggled here in recent clashes, failing to win on this pitch in their last two outings. Title winning sides should be full of character, able to grind out important results in tough situations, so Mourinho will be looking for a favourable result despite the weather and the arena tonight.
We are 15 minutes from kick-off, so be sure to stick around for all of the action from the Hawthorns, for a game which has huge implications on the Premier League table. Chelsea need a win to keep themselves as the unequivocal frontrunner in the title race, while West Brom are looking to kick-start Pepe Mel's new era with a vital three points against challenging opposition.
The inclusion of new signing Thievy can give the home fans some hope, as the Frenchman netted a debut goal for the club last time out, with less than a minute spent on the field. West Brom have relied on sharing the goalscoring burden this season, with 16 players out of their squad contributing to the Baggies' tally, but the emergence of a dangerous, reliable frontman would be a welcome one.
With a win tonight, the Baggies could move up to 14th in the Premier League, demonstrating how close the relegation battle truly is. A few poor results, and any side can find themselves fearfully glancing over their shoulders. Chelsea, contrastingly, are looking to retain their position at the summit of the top flight pile this evening, with Mourinho's so-called transitional squad doing a good job of setting the league's pace.
Chelsea substitutes: Schwarzer, Cole, Lampard, Torres, Mikel, Schurrle, Salah.
Chelsea starting line-up: Cech; Ivanovic, Luiz, Cahill, Azpilicueta; Ramires, Matic; Willian, Oscar, Hazard, Eto'o.
West Brom substitutes: Myhill, Lugano, Anichebe, Dorrans, Vydra, Mulumbu, Gera.
West Brom starting line-up: Foster; Reid, Dawson, McAuley, Ridgewell; Amalfitano, Yacob, Morrison, Brunt; Thievy, Berahino.
TEAM NEWS: Ramires comes into the central defensive midfield pairing for Chelsea, with Nemanja Matic continuing to hold his place in Mourinho's plans. Samuel Eto'o leads the line, with the predictably chosen trio of Eden Hazard, Oscar and Willian in behind. Mohamed Salah is again included on the bench for the away side, but may look to enjoy some first-team minutes if things go to plan.
TEAM NEWS: Craig Dawson partners Gareth McAuley in the centre of the Baggies' defence, with Steven Reid slotting back in at right-back. Morgan Amalfitano is included in the starting eleven once again, with James Morrison partnering Claudio Yacob in midfield, instead of Youssouf Mulumbu. Thievy starts in attack for the hosts, after his impactful substitute's appearance last time out.
I'm Simon Harrison, and I will be leading you through all of the action, as Pepe Mel looks to improve on West Brom's meagre four Premier League wins this season. Home form becomes vital when embroiled in a relegation scrap, and thus the Baggies need to be looking for points from unrealistic sources - with tonight's visitors being the perfect example of such a foe.
Hello and welcome to tonight's latest Premier League kick-off, as Jose Mourinho's title-chasing Chelsea head to the Hawthorns to challenge struggling West Brom. Pepe Mel's side haven't been enjoying good form of late, finding themselves winless in their last five games and as a result have found themselves in the bottom three at kick-off tonight. A big game at both ends of the table.

Well, that's all from our coverage at the Emirates Stadium this evening. It wasn't a classic, but hopefully you enjoyed it! It's goodbye for now.
For David Moyes, he'll be pleased with the organisation of his defence. Vidic was imperious while De Gea produced some superb stops. But they could have won the game themselves with Van Persie missing two golden opportunities.
So, Arsenal miss the chance to go top after a cagey performance in which they lacked a real cutting edge in the final third. They were bound to have had their confidence knocked after Saturday but it was not a vintage performance tonight at all.
FULL TIME at the Emirates Stadium and it's finished goalless here after a tight, tense affair between these two. It was a game lacking in chances until the last 10 minutes when the goalkeepers came into their own.
(90’) Fantastic chance for United late on as Rooney poaches possession in midfield and the visitors have three on two in attack, but Koscielny does well to win the ball back for Arsenal.
--- 90’ +2 Yellow card A. Young receives a yellow card. ---
(90’) Sagna is taken out on the far side and the hosts have a free kick, but they're still taking their time despite there being hardly any of it left.
(90’) We're into three minutes of added time and the Gunners still have possession. Can they find a way through United and past De Gea?
(90’) DE GEA DENIES CAZORLA AGAIN!! It's a very disappointing set piece from Ozil, who smacks it straight into the wall. Arsenal keep possession, though, and it's worked back inside to Cazorla, who shifts on to his right before firing a low shot at goal which is saved by De Gea.
(89’) Here's a chance for Arsenal as Cazorla plays the ball into Giroud and looks to receive it back but is taken out by Evra. It's a free kick 20 yards out, just to the right of goal, and Ozil's lining it up...
(88’) Wilshere has the ball in midfield but comes to a complete standstill as he has no options in front of him. The home fans are very unhappy as it's pretty much summed up their night.
--- 87’ Yellow card B. Sagna is cautioned by the referee. ---
(87’) Clumsy challenge from Sagna as he deliberately clips Rooney, who had shown him a fresh pair of heels, and he goes into the book.
(86’) United have goal kick and Van Persie wins it in the air against Arteta, but there's a shove in the back from the striker and Arsenal have possession once more.
(84’) GREAT STOP DE GEA!! Giroud does really well to hold the ball up just inside the box and keep the Arsenal attack alive, and Cazorla combines with Ozil before firing a low shot at goal which De Gea saves brilliantly low to his right.
(83’) Young's first contribution is a hacked clearance into the Arsenal half, which Mertesacker heads back to Szczesny. The hosts come forward again and almost every player is inside the visiting half now.
--- 82’ Substitution A. Young comes on for A. Valencia. ---
(82’) Ashley Young is introduced for United, who might sense they can steal a victory tonight. Just eight minutes to go at the Emirates Stadium.
(80’) Van Persie has had the two best chances of the match, and he's finished neither of them. Will the visitors rue those missed opportunities?
(79’) OFF THE BAR!! FANTASTIC SAVE!! Carrick steals the ball off Wilshere in midfield and United break quickly. Van Persie squares to Rooney, who returns the ball to the striker with a delightful floated ball. Van Persie meets it with a powerful header but Szczesny produces a stunning stop to push the ball on to the bar and out.
(77’) GIROUD MUST SCORE!! This really should be 1-0 to the hosts as Sagna curls in a wonderful low cross. Giroud charges to the near post and is inches away from diverting it in. Any touch would have done but somehow he couldn't meet it.
(76’) It's just slowed down again after that slightly more frantic spell. The hosts have the ball and agaom take their time to move forward into the opposing half.
--- 75’ Substitution A. Januzaj enters play, replacing Mata. ---
(75’) The changes come, then, as Oxlade-Chamberlain and Januzaj are introduced. Can either of them inspire their side to a winning goal?
--- 74’ Substitution A. Oxlade-Chamberlain comes on for T. Rosický. ---
(74’) Over from Rosicky! Cazorla plays the ball inside to Giroud, who has his back to goal. He lets it run in front of him and Rosicky charges towards the ball before trying to bend a shot into the far corner, but it's far too high.
--- 73’ Yellow card A. Valencia is cautioned by the referee. ---
(73’) A huge cheer goes up from the home fans as Valencia is booked for a late challenge on Wilshere. Cazorla whips in the free kick but it doesn't clear the first man and United blast the ball away.
(72’) Arsenal look like they'll be making their first substitution soon, with Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain warming up, while Adnan Januzaj could be on shortly for the visitors.
(71’) It's all a bit scrappy in the middle and Rooney almost ends up lying on the ball as he goes down under a challenge, and has three Arsenal players around him. The Gunners get possession eventually but give it straight back to United.
(70’) Great defending from Vidic! Rosicky spreads the ball out wide to Sagna, who looks for Giroud with an early cross, but Vidic does superbly to get there first and head away.
(69’) The Arsenal fans aren't happy with the referee again as Rosicky challenges Evra strongly, but is deemed to have done so illegally and a free kick is given deep inside the United half.
(68’) That's rather petulant from Wilshere as he works hard to keep possession and loses out to Carrick, who plays back to Smalling. Wilshere carries on running and clatters the United defender as he plays the ball forward. He's very lucky to escape without a booking, really.
(67’) Mata gives away a free kick for a pointless handball on the far side, but Ozil doesn't punish the Spaniard's error as his inswinging ball evades everyone and goes behind for a goal kick.
(66’) MATA DRILLS WIDE!! We're finally starting to see things open up at the Emirates Stadium, and Mata will be disappointed not to do better as he drags a shot wide of the post from 25 yards.
(65’) Good goalkeeping from Szczesny as he hares off his line to head the ball away as Van Persie chases a high ball over the top of the defence. The Arsenal shot-stopper had to watch that one very closely.
(64’) Penalty shout for the hosts as Giroud goes in for a header at the near post and falls under pressure from Vidic, but nothing is given. Seconds later the striker sees another header flash across goal and well wide.
(62’) OFF THE LINE!! Finally a decent chance!! It's a lovely cross into the box and Koscielny hammers a header across goal, but Valencia is at the far post to clear it from under his own crossbar.
(61’) Mata is clipped by Arteta in midfield as the game gets very scrappy, with the referee needing his whistle fairly regularly. United can't make anything of it, though, and Arsenal force a corner at the other end...
(60’) Cazorla is furious as he's clipped out on the flank by Smalling, but the referee simply shakes his head and awards a free kick to the visitors.
(58’) Valencia flicks the ball past Gibbs and charges down the right-hand side, before firing a low cross into the area which is easily cleared by Koscielny.

(55’) Free kick for Everton now, as Lukaku misplays a pass, but recovers before it goes out of play. He's taken down near the corner flag by Delaney and wins a good chance for his team. Baines delivers, and it's met by Lukaku but headed well wide at the near post.
(53’) STAT ATTACK: Everton have won seven consecutive Premier League home matches, and have suffered just ONE defeat in their past 27 league fixtures at Goodison Park.
(51’) MCGEADY! Everton playing with a strong sense of urgency now. The Irish man cuts towards the centre of the pitch and lets fly from 25 yards out, narrowly missing at the far post. Everton desperately searching for a breakthrough.
--- 49’ Assist The assist came from Y. Bolasie. ---
--- 49’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOAAAAL! It's a massive goal for Crystal Palace who double their lead! Scott Dann, the Scouse lad who left Merseyside, is back with a goal to deliver a big blow to Everton's Champions League hopes. He gets his head to a corner and makes no mistake, bouncing it off the ground and into the roof of the net. ---
(48’) Great stuff from Cameron Jerome, who refuses to give up on an errant pass when Everton did. He gets to the ball and plays it off Coleman to win a throw near the corner flag. That determination has been the difference between the two clubs thus far.

(46’) Crystal Palace kick-off and we're underway in the second half. One substitution to report, and it is a puzzling one, as Gerard Deulofeu comes off for Steven Naismith. That should provide more of a presence inside the box, but the Spaniard looked to be one of the more creative players for Everton in the first half.
The saving grace for Everton? They've scored 73 percent of their goals this season in the second halves of their matches.
STAT ATTACK: Only Chelsea, Everton and Manchester United have conceded fewer goals away from home this season than Crystal Palace (21).
HALF-TIME: EVERTON 0-1 CRYSTAL PALACE. The visitors have looked more than up to the challenge here today. Their sheer determination to win every ball has posed quite a few problems for the Toffees, who can't seem to match that same intensity thus far. Roberto Martinez has his work cut out for him as they hope to snag a massive three points.
(45’) And that's the last of the action as Andre Marriner blows his half-time whistle with Crystal Palace leading at the break!
(45’) Great pressure from Everton as we enter added time. A free kick from Leighton Baines is just cleared, but the Toffees win it back. McGeady gets it along the left and wins a corner as his cross is cleared. Again it comes back to the Irish winger along the left, and he tries to loft one in for a second time. It's a dangerous ball that has Speroni worried, but he can relax as the ball lands on the top of his goal.
--- 44’ Yellow card D. Delaney goes into the referee's book. ---
(44’) BOLASIE! Well the Congo DR man certainly isn't afraid to have a go! He finds a little space along the left and fires from distance. It's struck with a ton of power, but just sails over the goal as a furious Tim Howard gives his teammates a earful.
(42’) Three Palace players standing over the ball, but it's Jedinak who takes. He opts to cross it in, but Distin is able to clear under little to no pressure.
(41’) Things have really opened up here as we approach half-time! Baines takes down Jerome who was making a nice run, and the Glaziers have themselves a free kick from just under 30 yards out.
(39’) WHAT A SAVE! It's a brilliant run from the young Ross Barkley who gets into the box, all the way to the touch-line before cutting it back for Lukaku. The Belgian's shot it a good one, but Speroni gets a foot on it to deny him at the near post. Much better from Everton.
(37’) Poor final ball from Deulofeu. Joe Ledley gives the ball straight away in midfield, and Everton break in numbers on the counter. Lukaku lays it off for Deulofeu who has McGeady screaming for it at the top of the box. The Spaniard instead tries to beat the defender, but can't get his cross through as Everton have to settle for another corner.
(35’) HORRIBLE MISS FROM JEROME! Out of nothing, really, Bolasie wins a long ball and has a go from long range. He has Howard beaten at the near post, but is denied by the woodwork! Jerome on the follow up has Howard down at the side of his goal, but puts the rebound wide! Really should have been a second for Palace.
(33’) MIRALLAS! Great strength shown from the Belgian who takes a wayward pass, brings it down and shields off Dann. He turns the defender well, but fires over the bar from a tight angle.
(31’) Admirable stuff from Crystal Palace in defence. Everton are starting to take the game over in midfield, but they can hardly even break into the attacking third at the moment. And when they do, they've done very little with it.
(29’) Plenty of space for Baines as Everton win the ball in midfield. The left-back streaks down the flank and spots Lukaku in space. He passes it across, but the Belgian, unaware of this, vacates the area to make a run into the box and the miscommunication allows Palace to get back in possession.
(27’) Crystal Palace have defended quite comfortably through the opening stages of this match. Everton can't find a way through at the moment, but they certainly have to! Deulofeu and Mirallas look lively in midfield, but have yet to be able to pick out a final pass. Lukaku has little space to work with inside the area, swarmed by yellow shirts every time he gets the ball.
(25’) It's a goal that Everton really couldn't afford to concede. Roberto Martinez looks on, coaching his team, knowing there's a considerable amount of work to be done if they are to turn this around!
--- 23’ Assist M. Chamakh gave the assist. ---
--- 23’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOAAAL! Crystal Palace continue to defy the odds as they open the scoring at Goodison Park! And who else but Jason Puncheon?! Bolasie makes a brilliant run down the right. His cross is punched away by Howard, but only as far as Chamakh, who lays it off for Puncheon to slot inside the far post with his left foot. ---
(22’) STAT ATTACK: Everton have won seven consecutive Premier League matches. They haven’t won eight in a row since May 1985. The last time they failed to record a victory was in a 1-0 defeat to Chelsea on February 22.
(20’) Everton have certainly enjoyed the bulk of possession early on, but they haven't managed to convert it into a good scoring chance yet, as they continue to search for their first shot on target.
(18’) GREAT DEFENDING! Deulofeu makes a nice run down the right and crosses in for Lukaku. It's touched back into the path of McGeady who has a clear shooting chance, but he can't get to the ball ahead of Mariappa who boots it out of the danger area.
(16’) Lovely movement from Palace, as Bolasie sends a clever little back heel into the path of Ward. The left-back has room to run, but sends a poor cross into the area that Puncheon can't keep from running out of play.
(14’) APPEALS FOR A PENALTY! Ross Barkley uses his quick feet to shield off a few Palace defenders before being taken down by Joe Ledley. There was an argument to be made for a foul, but it looked as though the contact occurred just outside the box.
(12’) INJURIES ALL OVER THE PLACE! Tim Howard races out of his goal to collect a ball ahead of Cameron Jerome, and Everton subsequently put the ball out of play with Jason Puncheon down injured. He's been red hot for Palace, who can not afford to have him injured.
(10’) As is to be expected from a Tony Pulis side, Palace are making Everton earn every inch of space. McGeady makes a nice run to elude two defenders, but his cross in for Lukaku is a few feet in front of the Belgian who looks to have injured himself trying to lunge for the ball. That is a worrying site for Roberto Martinez.
(8’) STAT ATTACK: Crystal Palace have won three straight matches for the first time this season, and have not conceded during that span.
(6’) Everton doing a nice job of keeping possession despite the high pressing of Crystal Palace. Mirallas is drifting to the flanks to provide the defenders with an outlet pass, and looks lively on the ball. It's important to note, nothing will come easy against a Palace team who have conceded very few goals since the arrival of Tony Pulis.
(4’) Great start from the hosts! Another corner won by the Toffees through Gerard Deulofeu and Aiden McGeeady. The cross is dealt with and Palace break on a counter. Jason Puncheon sends a nice ball through to Cameron Jerome, but the striker is called for the offside.
(2’) First chance falls to Everton who win a quick corner. Barry eludes his marker and meets the cross, but directs his header over the bar.
(1’) Back to football we go! Everton kick-off with ambitions of fourth place. The home side, moving right to left, are wearing their classic royal blue home kits, with Crystal Palace sporting all yellow.

FULL-TIME: Manchester City 2-2 Sunderland. The scoreline does not depict a particularly positive look for either side as late drama at the Etihad ensured the spoils were shared. City knew they had little margin for error in the title race and flew out of the traps, with Fernandinho scoring after just two minutes. Gus Poyet's side refused to lie down, however, and got their just rewards with Connor Wickham's well-taken double in the final 10 minutes. It looked like they were on course for a fifth win in nine over the title-chasing hosts, but Samir Nasri benefited from Vito Mannone's error to make for a tense finale. A winner did not arrive and both sides were forced to lick their wound as City fell six points off the summit with just one game in hand while Sunderland lie the same number away from exiting the drop zone on an eventful night at Eastlands.
--- 90’ +2 Yellow card P. Zabaleta gets yellow. ---
(90’) We are into four minutes of stoppage time here as Zabaleta clips Wickham near the halfway line and is promptly booked by the referee. Sunderland have a late chance to pump the ball into the area, but Mannone catches his teammate offside from the free kick.
(90’) Nasri releases Milner down the left but the England international's cross is wayward and goes straight out of play for a goal kick on the far side, when the move promised so much more.
--- 88’ Assist S. Jovetić gave the assist. ---
--- 88’ Goal! IT'S IN! CITY HAVE THEIR EQUALISER! Nasri lashes a loose ball in the box towards goal. It should be routine for Mannone, but the Italian spills the shot, and is left clawing in vain as it trickles over the line! ---
--- 87’ Substitution Fernandinho is done for the day. J. Rodwell is his replacement. ---
(87’) Fernandinho makes way for the hosts and Jack Rodwell comes on in his place. City are struggling to make inroads on the Sunderland goal, though. Can they muster an equaliser?
(85’) City rallying themselves for one final go to try and salvage a win from the depths of despair here. Surely they can't lose this, can they?
--- 83’ Assist The assist came from E. Giaccherini. ---
--- 83’ Goal! GOAL! Remarkable scenes at the Etihad as Sunderland take the lead. They have been well worth a lead in this game and they finally have it with just seven minutes remaining as Wickham grabs his second of the contest. A stunning run from Giaccherini committed the City backline and allowed him the time and space to feed Wickham, who drilled home at Hart's near post. Staggering. Could this be the end of City's title challenge? ---
(81’) WHAT A CHANCE! Kolarov dances his way through some statuesque challenges after cutting in from the left and slipped back a low ball to Dzeko, but the Bosnian snatched at the chance and screwed well wide of the near post.
(79’) Brown has been magnificent for Sunderland tonight and has looked a man on a mission after his personal disaster at the weekend. His latest action is to get in a crucial block on Jovetic as he looked to unleash a shot on goal.
(77’) Jovetic takes aim from just outside the area but sees his shot drift wide of the far post as City's frustrations grow.
(75’) City struggling to find any sort of rhythm to their play at the moment and their passing is suffering as a result. What a scoreline this would be for Sunderland who, remember, have won four of their last eight league meetings with the hosts.
--- 73’ Assist The assist came from E. Giaccherini. ---
--- 73’ Goal! GOAL! Against all the odds, Sunderland have pulled level at the Etihad through Wickham! How crucial could this goal prove at either end of the Premier League table? Substitute Giaccherini escapes his marker on the left and sends a teasing cross to the back post where Wickham was left unattended to prod home past Joe Hart. Can City rally in the final 15 minutes or will Sunderland find the winner? ---
(72’) WHAT A SAVE! Hart stands up tall to thwart Colback, who had been threaded through by Johnson's brilliant pass but chose to shoot over a cut-back, which looked the more sensible option on reflection.
(70’) Sunderland slowly cranking up the pressure here, are they about to land a fatal blow to City's title hopes?
--- 69’ Substitution I. Scocco enters the game and replaces F. Borini. ---
--- 68’ Substitution S. Larsson is done for the day. E. Giaccherini is his replacement. ---

(68’) A flurry of substitutions at the Etihad, with Poyet making two changes. The Uruguayan introduces Emanuele Giaccherini for Larsson and Ignacio Scocco also comes on for the tireless Borini. City, meanwhile, bring on Edin Dzeko for Negredo.
(66’) Jovetic attempts an acrobatic effort from Nasri's free-kick, but he miscues and the strike is not about to worry Mannone. City had won the set piece after Alonso unceremoniously hacked down Milner and earned a booking for his troubles.
--- 65’ Yellow card Marcos Alonso goes into the referee's book. ---
(64’) Liverpool midfielder Jordan Henderson is snapped in the crowd watching his former side in action against fellow title rivals but it's City who go close to scoring next as substitute Jovetic nutmegs Cattermole brlliantly but his low shot lacks the requisite power to beat Mannone.
(62’) Larsson weaves his way past a number of challenges but, after engineering some space just outside the area, he wastes the chance to send in a threatening ball and goes for a speculative chip, which sails high over Hart's crossbar.
(60’) Sunderland remain content to let City make the majority of the play before exploiting their deficiencies on the counter attack. Is it a ploy which will bring reward for the spirited visiting side?
(58’) Jovetic almost makes an instant impact on proceedings by driving at the heart of the Sunderland defence and slipping a pass out to the left, but it is too far in front of Nasri, who is forced wide and cannot deliver a telling cross.
--- 57’ Substitution S. Jovetić comes on for S. Agüero. ---
(56’) Aguero's disappointing evening comes to a close as Pellegrini introduces Stevan Jovetic to add a much-needed injection of zest to the City attack. It just didn't quite happen for Aguero this evening, but Pellegrini will undoubtedly be happy with the way his star man is slowly but surely returning to full fitness.
(54’) Sunderland survive City's first real penetrative attack of the second period as Aguero breaches the backline but Cattermole gets back well to get some form of a block in and divert the ball partially away from Nasri's reach.
(52’) City continue to keep possession neatly in and around the Sunderland penalty area but, without the craft of David Silva, there is precious little in the way of a final pass at present.
(50’) Johnson shows tremendous trickery out on the right flank to bamboozle Kolarov but his cross is cleared by the City defence, who remain comfortable despite Sunderland's increased pressure at the start of this second half.
(48’) Larsson whips a ball towards the far post but Negredo gets up above his marker to nod away from the Manchester City danger zone.
(46’) City get the ball rolling once more and we are back underway for a crucial second half for both sides here at the Etihad Stadium.
Sunderland threw away a slew of opportunities inside the opening 20 minutes or so, and have rarely caused trouble since. City still lead thanks to that early, early Fernandinho goal, but the advantage is a little too narrow for comfort. Pellegrini will want to push for the second goal in the second half.
(45’) That's it for the first half folks.
(44’) We're on the cusp of half time and it looks like just the one goal lead for title chasing City. Sunderland and Gus Poyet will be reasonably satisfied with this scoreline so far.
(42’) Not a whole lot happening out on the pitch if I'm honest. Nasri takes an uncharacteristically direct route to goal, running at a pair of defenders, but he can't keep the ball at full pace and Sunderland recover.
(40’) Aguero attempts to break through the visitors' backline by executing a one-two with Negredo, but the Spanish striker cannot put the right weight on the return pass, and the Argentine fails to bring it under his control.
(38’) Sunderland are beginning to hold some possession, keeping the hosts on the back foot. There's not enough in their approach to suggest that Joe Hart will be in trouble any time soon though.
(36’) Zabaleta trudges off the field to a warm reception from the home crowd, who have always loved his lion-hearted displays. He'll get patched up on the sidelines while we continue with the game.
(34’) Marcos Alonso ventures forward and forces Zabaleta into a brave block which leads to both players receiving treatment. Alonso is up first but Zabaleta appears on first glance to have come off far worse out of the duo.

(32’) Borini enters the book for foul-mouthing the linesman after showing diligence in his defensive work to track back and thwart Pablo Zabaleta, who had advanced down the City right flank.
(30’) Wickham v Kompany is fast becoming an intriguing battle in this encounter, but the Belgian comes out on top in the latest duel, after Vergini had looked to release the frontman on goal.
(28’) Johnson and Cattermole link up nicely but the latter fails to find a decisive return ball before Brown goes in hard on Aguero, who clutches his shins after the former Manchester United defender's challenge.
(26’) City win a corner as a riposte to Sunderland's adventurous attacking ployes but Cattermole wastes an opportunity to hit the hosts on the counter after Aguero's heavy touch. Parity, with City monopolising the ball, is restored.
(24’) Johnson looks for a path through the City defence and tries to jink his way through but discovers an uncompromising backline so instead elects to shoot, but his effort is well wide eventually.
(22’) City continue to probe in and around the Sunderland area but are unable to get anywhere despite their crisp passing moves, with Kolarov twice conceding possession far too easily.
(18’) MISS! Another chance goes begging for the visitors - how many more will they have to squander before netting the leveller? Johnson's threaded pass locates Borini's evasive run and the Italian takes aim, but his radar is slightly out and his arrowed effort veers past the post.
(16’) Another set piece wreaks havoc amongst the City rearguard as Demichelis is forced to clear Larsson's wicked centre for a corner on the far side, but Hart claims the subsequent delivery.
(14’) Fernandinho brings down Jack Colback in midfield and the constant concession of free-kicks is doing little to help City find their fluency in this opening quarter.
(12’) ANOTHER MISS! O'Shea meets Larsson's corner with a firm header but sees his effort fly harmlessly across the face of Hart's goal. Sunderland are certainly causing one or two problems here for the home side.
(10’) MISS! Samir Nasri steps onto his favoured right foot and unleashes a powerful drive towards goal which Mannone has to push up into the air where Zabaleta is able to flick back towards Fernandinho, but the goalscorer's volleyed effort flies well over the bar.

(6’) WHAT A CHANCE! Martin Demichelis scythes down Connor Wickham and presents Sunderland with a free-kick in a promising area. Johnson's delivery is expert, but somehow John O'Shea manages to nod wide. A huge let-off for the hosts, whose marking was extremely slack.
(4’) BLUNDER! Joe Hart is fortunate to get away with a lax clearance which lands straight at the feet of former City winger Adam Johnson, but his first touch is poor and he is unable to punish Hart for his gaffe. Sunderland continue to have the best of the early exchanges, with Wickham nipping away from Zabaleta before Johnson earns his side a corner after wriggling clear inside the area.

Although Liverpool may not win the Premier League this season, they could still have a major say in the destination of the title with Chelsea and Manchester City to travel to Anfield in April. Arsenal are first up and it's a must-win match for both sides.
Today's trip to Anfield marks the start of a crunch spell for the Gunners' season, with today's match followed by a four-game home run of Manchester United, Liverpool again (in the FA Cup), a mouthwatering Champions League tie with Bayern Munich and Sunderland. We should know in a fortnight's time whether their fight on multiple fronts is likely to bear fruit or not.
The squad is dovetailing nicely too - as one player drops out another comes in to replace them with a minimum of fuss. Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain's return - capped with a goalscoring brace against Crystal Palace last week - coincided with Theo Walcott's injury and is a prime example, although we still are yet to discover an answer to the oft-cried question 'what happens when Olivier Giroud gets injured?'
Arsenal haven't proven quite as potent up front, but their consistency and resilience in defence means the title challenge many continue to believe will filter away in the spring remains looking strong.
Indeed, the 2-0 defeat at the Emirates Stadium back in November was the last time the Reds failed to fire at all. In the 16 matches since, they've racked up an astonishing 45 goals - 24 of those from their lethal duo.
That includes today's opponents Arsenal - the only team to have prevented both Luis Suarez and Daniel Sturridge - or the 'SAS' from scoring in the last 12 league games they've played together.
Judging by recent results at least, the top four appears to be a realistic ambition for the Reds right now. Liverpool have beaten each of their rivals for fourth place so far, but have lost each of their encounters against the three teams above them albeit all away from home. Today provides a chance to alter that record.
With Everton and Tottenham in hot pursuit and Manchester United still in the mix it represents a difficult task for Liverpool, but one Rodgers and his charges believe they can meet.
Brendan Rodgers' ceiling of ambition has lowered somewhat in the space of a month having maintained in January that his side would "never give up the fight" for the Premier League title, with the Liverpool manager now accepting the goal this season must be to make the "big jump into the top four".
So Liverpool are unchanged for today's clash from last week's 1-1 draw at West Bromwich Albion, while Arsenal make just one change from the side that saw off Crystal Palace 2-0 last weekend as Lukas Podolski makes way for the returning Jack Wilshere.

The final whistle is blown, and Crystal Palace emerge as 3-1 victors over West Brom to send them three points clear of the Premier League relegation places! The visitors, however, drop into the bottom three courtesy of their defeat and are still winless under Pepe Mel after four matches. I've been Livio Caferoglu and it's farewell from me!
(90’) We're two minutes into the three that have been added on by the fourth official.
(90’) BERAHINOOOO!!! Lady luck just hasn't been on the side of West Brom's this afternoon. A corner is delightfully whipped into the box by Brunt, and it ricochets off the substitute and towards the wrong side of the post!
(88’) Ledley roams out towards the right and attracts a foul off Brunt. Jedinak's free kick, however, curls straight into the gloves of Foster.
(86’) Ince goes for the spectacular from a layoff on the right-hand side, but his shot is so bad that it cannons off the camera picture and into the orbit!
(84’) It's Jones turn to test Speroni with an attempt of his own after cutting inside from the right, but the Argentine is in no mood to be beaten by the right-back!
--- 83’ Substitution M. Chamakh is done for the day. J. Thomas is his replacement. ---
(82’) ANICHEBE!!!! The Nigerian does fantastically well to drop deep, turn his marker using nothing but brute force and steamroll towards goal, yet he can't find the target with his strike.
(80’) Berahino is adamant that his quick feet have done enough to win West Brom a free kick on the edge of the box, but a corner is all he can get from the referee. Brunt's delivery - for the umpteenth time - is easily cleared for a throw.
--- 79’ Yellow card C. Brunt goes into the referee's book. ---
(78’) A diagonal pass is sent towards Murray, who hangs around the shoulder of the last man in the West Brom defence, but Foster quickly darts off his line to smother the ball.
--- 76’ Substitution J. Parr comes on for Y. Bolasie. ---
(76’) Jedinak manages to ease the pressure off his team-mates by using his experience to buy a free kick from Anichebe. However, the ball returns to the Eagles box in a matter of seconds, yet Berahino is too clever for his own good as he foolishly strikes an effort from the byline. It's all too simple for Speroni at the near post!
(74’) The ball is currently being played around deep in the Palace half, after the subsequent corner from Anichebe's strike was poorly dealt with, but it's eventually cleared by Dikgacoi.
--- 72’ Substitution J. Puncheon is replaced with G. Murray. ---
--- 71’ Substitution S. Berahino enters the game and replaces C. Yacob. ---
(71’) A real heart-warming moment sees Glenn Murray - the 30-goal hero of Palace's promotion push last season - coming on for his first appearance of the season after nursing a serious knee injury. In the other corner, Saido Berahino is thrown on by Pepe Mel in a bid to further underline his wonderkid credentials.
--- 69’ Goal! Another quick-fire Palace break is on, which results in Foster hauling Chamakh to the ground. There's no question about the penalty, and the striker steps up to smash the ball into the bottom-right corner of the West Brom goal! ---
(68’) PENALTY TO PALACE!!!!!!
(67’) SPERONI AGAIN!!! Would you believe it... Mulumbu is in the box to  hammer home from close range after the corner is deflected into his path, yet the shot-stopper somehow gets both hands on the ball!
--- 65’ Yellow card C. Yacob gets yellow. ---
(65’) GREAT SAVE SPERONI!!! Morrison looks to take matters into his own hands following Yacob's booking by launching a vicious drive towards the Palace goal, but the goalkeeper is at full stretch to deny the midfielder!
(63’) Ince has been on the receiving end of two robust challenges from Dawson now, as the centre-back perfectly executes another intervention into the side of the Blackpool loanee!
(61’) Jones has been arguably the best player since the restart, and he shows that he hasn't neglected his defensive duties after clearing Delaney's header off the line!
(59’) Palace almost hit West Brom on the break from a throw deep in the visitors' half, and Bolasie dispossesses Sinclair near the corner flag fairly to earn his side the set-piece opportunity.
(57’) For all of West Brom's misgivings, Dawson has been a rock in the heart of their defence, as he does superbly well to stop Ince in his tracks with a crucial sliding tackle in the box.
(55’) Bolasie and Brunt have been engaged in a fascinating duel this afternoon, and the former has certainly come out on top. In another phase of play involving the two wide men, the Northern Ireland international was forced all the way back to his own corner flag!
(53’) The ex-Preston right-back is caught offside this time after trying to meet a Chamakh through ball. Credit to Palace for not letting their heads drop in the face of adversity!
(51’) Jones sends a low cross into the box from the right-hand side, which has proved so popular with West Brom attacks today, but it's cleared in an instant.
(49’) Baggies boss Pepe Mel spoke highly of his new striking arrival from Espanyol earlier in the week, and he's been vindicated in little less than a minute of making his debut! Elsewhere, Scott Sinclair has replaced Liam Ridgewell.
--- 46’ Substitution S. Sinclair enters play, replacing L. Ridgewell. ---
--- 46’ Assist The assist came from V. Anichebe. ---
--- 46’ Substitution Z. Gera is done for the day. T. Bifouma is his replacement. ---
--- 46’ Goal! WELL, WELL, WELL!! It's the substitute Bifouma, who plays a give-and-go with Anichebe in the box and rifles home a strike across goal. Game on!!! ---
(45’) The second half is now under way... AND IT PRODUCES A GOAL TO WEST BROM INSIDE JUST 45 SECONDS!!!!
We're back out onto the pitch for the second half, with the restart now imminent...
This is all happening while Crystal Palace continue to defy the age-old argument that new signings need time to gel together! Maybe Tottenham could take a leaf out of their book... Their cause is certainly being helped by Pulis' back-to-basics approach to football - two banks of four, accompanied by a little-and-large partnership up top. Sometimes the simplest things are most effective!
Pepe Mel will surely have learned from the experiences of Michael Laudrup that to succeed in the Premier League, you need a strong foundation first and foremost. They have shown some impressive rhythm in their passing game at times, but they are suffering from an alarming lack of pace and width in their backline. At the moment, their insistence on playing with four slow centre-backs is undoing all of their fluid football.
Bolasie looks for options to his left, but none are forthcoming and the referee blows his whistle to signal the half-time interval!
(45’) There will be two minutes of time added on.
(44’) McAuley is unmarked again in the Palace box, as he does his best to meet a diagonal free kick, but he can't keep his effort down.
(42’) The corner amounts to nothing more than a momentary phase of West Brom pressure, leaving Ward to pick up the pieces and take the throw.
(40’) Anichebe's movement catches the proverbial eye once more as Jedinak barges him off the ball on the wide right. Mulumbu's receives the rebound from the free kick and forces through a corner after Chamakh heads his volley over the bar!
--- 39’ Yellow card B. Jones is cautioned by the referee. ---
(38’) The first yellow card of the game is shown to Jones for cynically sliding into the back of Ince.
(36’) Pepe Mel looks on pensively from the touchline. His team may have seen two thirds of the ball in these opening 36 minutes, yet they have nothing to show for their efforts. It's another rude awakening for an overseas import to the trials and tribulations of Premier League football!
(34’) ... which Speroni clutches gratefully! Meanwhile, McAuley's diving header from an inswinging West Brom corner is blocked and Palace's two-goal lead is preserved.
(33’) Dikgacoi hacks down Morrison, who was in the process of setting himself up for the half-volley. Brunt lines up the free kick in a promising position...
(31’) CHAMAKH!!!! Ince lays off yet another tantalising through ball, which the onrushing Moroccan latches onto, but Foster is alert to the danger.
(29’) Mulumbu tries a speculative effort from some way out, but it's light years away from troubling Speroni. These are times of desperation for West Brom!
--- 27’ Assist T. Ince gave the assist. ---
--- 27’ Goal! It's a second debut goal for a second debutant in Joe Ledley! A corner is driven into the box, and the mid-season arrival from Celtic jumps highest to nestle the ball into the back of the net. ---
(26’) PALACE DOUBLE THEIR LEAD!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
(24’) Brunt, not for the first time, can't quite steer his dead ball onto the head of an intended target.
(22’) Pepe Mel's troops are beginning to dominate possession now. However, as we've seen so many times before, they need to match that technical ability with more of Mulumbu's brute force! Meanwhile, a corner is given...
(19’) Anichebe ventures out wide and wins West Brom a free kick on the edge of the box, which Brunt can only bend into the wall!
(17’) Mulumbu's determination can never be in question, but he needs to tone down his intensity. He wrestles another opponent to the ground and is lucky to get away with just a talking-to from the referee.
--- 15’ Assist Assist by Y. Bolasie. ---
--- 15’ Goal! GOAAAAAALLLLLLL!!!!!! Ince breaks his duck on his debut after collecting Bolasie's through ball and blasting a finish beyond Foster! Palace deservedly take the lead after just 15 minutes. ---
(14’) Puncheon stretches play down the right-hand side and crosses the ball towards the far post, but Bolasie can only aim his header at Foster.
(12’) The Congolese midfielder suddenly shoots back up onto his feet and monstrously breaks up two Palace attacks one after another! They'll need more of that commitment to the cause this afternoon.
(10’) Mulumbu is upended near the centre-circle and requires treatment. That should prove to be some welcome respite for his side.
(8’) Chamakh charges towards the byline and wins a corner off McAuley, and Dikgacoi almost nods the resulting cross in! West Brom are looking extremely sluggish in these early stages and need to pick things up urgently if they are to stay on equal terms with Palace for a little longer.
(6’) It's been an exciting start to the match by Ince, who attracts the wrath of Yacob again - this time more centrally. However, his set-piece harmlessly sails over the bar!
(4’) Gera is tripped up in advanced position by Delaney. However, the visitors fail to make anything come of their free kick.
(2’) Ince makes his first Palace foray down the right-hand side, but he is well marshalled in the end by Yacob.
(1’) We're under way in South London!
Meanwhile, Pepe Mel has yet to make a significant impact in the vein of his managerial opponent since being appointed West Brom boss last month. The 50-year-old Spaniard was unable to add beyond Thievy Bifoum to his squad.
It's a refreshed Eagles line-up named by Tony Pulis, who strengthened his ranks considerably during the January transfer window. Scott Dann, Thomas Ince and Joe Ledley - all deadline-day arrivals - slot straight into the side.
Last but not least, we have the Baggies: Foster; Jones, Dawson, McAuley, Ridgewell; Yacob, Mulumbu; Morrison, Gera, Brunt; Anichebe.
The team news is in! This is how the hosts line up: Speroni; Ward, Jedinak, Dann, Delaney; Bolasie, Dikgacoi, Ledley, Puncheon; Ince; Chamakh.
