Crystal Palace, on the other hand, remain 17th but are a point above the relegation zone - and just a point off 12th. Next up for Pulis' side is West Brom at home next Saturday. We'll have coverage of that one, as well.
The win takes the Gunners two points above Manchester City, who must now beat Chelsea tomorrow to move back into first place. All eyes on Stamford Bridge for that one! For Arsenal, meanwhile, the tough month of February has at least got off to a good start.
In the second half, however, Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain stepped up to the plate and scored two fine goals for the hosts - one with a deft volley, one with a strong drive into the box - to give Arsenal all three points.
Arsenal return to the summit of the Premier League, even if it is just for 24 hours, after a comfortable victory over Crystal Palace. Things looked doubtful at half-time, with Tony Pulis' side defending resolutely, as Julian Speroni made several good saves.
FULL-TIME: Arsenal 2-0 Crystal Palace
(90’) Arsenal now win a throw deep inside the Palace half. Monreal and Kieran Gibbs exchange passes near the corner flag and duly win themselves a corner. The final act is almost over.
(90’) Three minutes of injury time given now as Palace keep pushing forward. Their efforts seem as though they won't make a difference but you have to give credit to their work-rate. The away fans, too, are still cheering vociferously. Great spirit.
(88’) Worrying signs for Arsenal! Oxlade-Chamberlain pulls up with an injury. He's back up and running but it looks like he may have tweaked something. Wenger and co. will be hoping it's just cramp.
--- 86’ Yellow card P. Mertesacker is yellow-carded. ---
(86’) BLOCKED! The free kick hits the wall - and so too the follow-up from Bolasie. It looks like the Gunners will remain untroubled until full-time.
(85’) FOUL! Bolasie is brought down just outside the penalty area and Mertesacker receives a booking for his foul. He couldn't stay with the winger as he turned delicately. Free kick in a dangerous position for Palace now. Surely not?
--- 84’ Substitution O. Giroud is replaced with N. Bendtner. ---
--- 84’ Substitution M. Özil is done for the day. K. Gibbs is his replacement. ---
(83’) More changes as Ozil comes off for the home side and is replaced by young Serge Gnabry. Giroud also makes way, with Nicklas Bendtner on in his place. Chamakh just missed out on a reunion with another revered Arsenal striker...
--- 82’ Substitution D. Gayle enters the game and replaces M. Chamakh. ---
(82’) Dwight Gayle comes on for Marouane Chamakh, as some Arsenal fans give him a cheeky jeer when he goes off. It was all good-natured, however, though the striker would have preferred to have scored against his former club.
(80’) Sagna makes a great tackle on the right-hand side to set up another Arsenal move now. Oxlade-Chamberlain proves he is human by giving it away, though, before Ozil gets it back and hits a deflected shot at Speroni.
(79’) It has been a valiant effort from Pulis' side but they were always going to be up against it today. Particularly pleasing for Arsenal fans will be the source of their goals. Many would have questioned Wenger's decision not to sign another striker in January. At least they can look to Oxlade-Chamberlain for inspiration, though!
(77’) The Gunners now press for a third, as Arteta, Rosicky and Podolski... have fun, for want of a better phrase, in the final third. They are casually exchanging passes in front of the Palace defence, with the visitors looking keen to conserve their energy now that they are two goals down.
(75’) It looks like it's back to the top of the league for Arsenal, while Oxlade-Chamberlain is still going strong, even though he looked exhausted after just 20 minutes. It's been a classy effort from the young midfielder.
(74’) That's surely the end of Palace's staunch resistance. This was the scoreline when the sides met earlier on in the season, as well, when Wenger's men left Selhurst Park with a 2-0 win despite Arteta's red card.
--- 73’ Assist O. Giroud provided the assist. ---
--- 73’ Goal! GOAL! Oxlade-Chamberlain makes it two for Arsenal! Is that game over? Rosicky gets involved straightaway, playing the ball to the 20-year-old, who then exchanges passes with Cazorla before storming into the penalty box and dispatching a well-taken finish. That's two goals for the day - and two very good goals, at that. ---
--- 72’ Substitution L. Podolski is replaced with T. Rosický. ---
(71’) Substitution for the Gunners now, as Tomas Rosicky comes on for Lukas Podolski. How will that change things up, tactically, one wonders?
(70’) Arsenal look content with sitting back and letting Palace come at them, though, while they are taking every opportunity to get forward as well. They are definitely looking more like a counterattacking team at the minute, however.
--- 68’ Yellow card D. Delaney is cautioned by the referee. ---
(68’) SHOT! Bannan has a rare shot at goal for the visitors! It goes way over the bar, however, and Arsenal live to see another day. Can Palace possibly get back into this one? They certainly haven't given up on themselves.
(67’) Another booking now - Palace's second. It's Delaney who is yellow-carded after a clumsy challenge on Cazorla. He caught the ball with his lunge but it was a careless tackle, one that could have possibly injured the Spaniard on another day.
(65’) Cazorla and Giroud now combine up front for the Gunners, while Podolski, too, is involved in the build-up. The move ends with Oxlade-Chamberlain playing a great ball into the area - but a strong tackle from Danny Gabbidon stops Podolski in his tracks.
(63’) Less than half an hour to go at the Emirates, then, and Wenger will be a much happier man than he was at half-time. As long as his side don't concede, the Frenchman won't care if he wins by one goal or ten, especially as his side continue to press in this second half.
(62’) POOR! The corner is cleared but only as far out as the Palace midfield. The ball is then played straight back into the area but Delaney gets his header all wrong, as it sails wide. Arsenal almost gift possession straight back to Palace with some short passing from Szczesny and Monreal - but they just about survive.
(61’) Potential injury trouble here, though, as Joel Ward is down injured. Play continues without him and Bolasie, now operating on the right, surges forward and has to be stopped by Cazorla. Corner to the visitors...
(60’) POOR! Oxlade-Chamberlain gets a bit ahead of himself, however. The initial corner is cleared and, after one or two passes in midfield, the Arsenal midfielder ambitiously tries to double his tally from distance. His shot goes way over the bar, though.
(59’) CORNER! Podolski makes another effective run down the left-hand side and wins yet another corner for the Gunners. They are really putting the pressure on the visitors now.
(58’) Koscielny finds Cazorla with a good pass to the right, though the Spaniard's attempts to whip the ball into the area come to nothing, as Speroni collects with ease.
--- 57’ Substitution B. Bannan comes on for C. Jerome. ---
(56’) Bannan's first action almost plays Puncheon in with a delicate pass into the area. The Arsenal defence hold firm, though. Can they kill this game off with a second?
(55’) CHANGE! Crystal Palace are making a change now, as Cameron Jerome makes way. Unfortunately, his last action proved a wasteful one, while he hasn't had his best game in a Palace shirt overall, anyway. Barry Bannan is his replacement.
(53’) SIDE-NETTING! It's Podolski again! He is played the ball in the box and has a couple of yards of space. However, a better choice might have been - like Jerome - to pass the ball back to one of his team-mates in the box. As it happened, he blasted the ball at goal and it hit the side-netting from a tight angle.
(52’) Podolski now makes a great run into the box and wins a corner for the home side! This game has really opened up in this second half. Pulis will not want that for the visitors, though...
(50’) Jerome should probably have squared it back to Chamakh, though, and could have done better with his finish! The resulting corner comes to nothing but that's a warning for Arsenal. Oxlade-Chamberlain has put them ahead but their work is far from over here.
(49’) RESPONSE! Palace look to get straight back into this as Puncheon, who has switched wings this half, plays a great ball into the box. Chamakh is there and heads it onto Jerome, who is denied by Szczesny at the near post. What a save!
--- 47’ Goal! GOAL! Oxlade-Chamberlain puts Arsenal ahead! A move that starts on the right-hand side is perfected by Cazorla, who takes the ball into the middle and plays a lovely chipped pass into the box. There, Oxlade-Chamberlain is waiting and sends the ball home with a fantastic finish on the volley. A really delicate piece of work from the midfielder there. ---
--- 47’ Assist Assist by Cazorla. ---
(46’) The second half is underway! We've had a foul already: Arteta brings down Jerome.
So can Arsene Wenger's men break down this resilient Palace unit, or will they drop points for the second game in a row? Stay with us for the second half to find out!
As things stand, a point will take the visitors up to 15th in the Premier League, while a draw will leave Arsenal in second. If Manchester City beat Chelsea tomorrow, though, the Gunners will be three points behind Manuel Pellegrini's men.
Crystal Palace will be delighted with their first-half performance, after defending resolutely throughout, while also managing to create the odd chance. Tony Pulis has, as usual, done his homework and it will take a lot to beat his side in the second half.
So a disappointing half for the home side, who only managed to create a handful of clearcut chances, with Julian Speroni only really troubled twice. His first important save denied Nacho Monreal after he was played in by Mesut Ozil. Then, he dived to his right to stop an Ozil cross from sailing into the back of the net.
HALF-TIME: Arsenal 0-0 Crystal Palace
(45’) Two minutes of injury time have been added and it's been a frustrating half for the home side. Palace have kept them at bay and will be delighted with a point here. A draw would be of no use whatsoever to title-chasing Arsenal, though, and Wenger will likely make changes in the second half.
(43’) The visitors break down the right-hand side now but their cross into the box goes straight to Szczesny. Immediately thereafter, Podolski goes down in midfield after a rogue challenge. Wenger does not look too elated on the touchline.
--- 42’ Yellow card M. Chamakh is yellow-carded. ---
(41’) BOOKING! One foul too many from Palace, as Chamakh concedes yet another free kick. The set-piece comes to nothing for Arsenal but they now know a Palace striker is one yellow card away from being sent off...
(40’) A poor clearance almost ends up with Podolski capitalising but Arsenal continue to press. In truth, they have done far too much in the build-up to the final third and nothing at all when they get the ball forward. Looking at this first half - and their 2-2 draw with Southampton - you'd have to say it's not their best run of the season by any stretch.
(38’) It's their first corner of the game but it's cleared instantly, while Puncheon's attempts to get the ball back into the area, once again, end up with him conceding a throw. It has to be said, though, that Palace do not look scared of their opponents today.
(37’) At this rate, Hennessey will have a tough task getting into this Palace starting line-up, with Speroni in this form. Straight up the other end, though, the visitors win themselves a corner...
(36’) STOP! He's done it again! A lot of Arsenal pressure now and, this time, they advance down the right flank. The ball is played into Sagna in the box but Speroni rushes out to get to it before the full-back.
(34’) Cleared! Speroni is involved yet again, as intricate footwork from Giroud almost pays off in the box. The Argentine goalkeeper manages to get hold of a loose ball, however, and thump it out for a throw-in.
(33’) SAVE! Ozil takes the free kick and it evades everyone in the box! But Speroni lunges down to his right to save. Brilliant reflexes to deny the goal and it goes off for a corner, which is then headed away.
(32’) Jason Puncheon now has the ball down the right-hand side but wastes the chance to cross it into the area after trying to beat his man! It goes off for a throw-in and Arsenal manage to work the ball upfield and win a free kick after a foul on Giroud by Damien Delaney.
(30’) With half an hour gone, we've had just one shot on target from both sides so far today! That shot was Arsenal's, although it didn't amount to much. It's been a battle of possession in midfield during this first half.
(28’) Arsenal take the free kick quickly but use it for a slow, patient attack. That is halted by another good challenge from Bolasie, though, who has been causing plenty of problems down the left flank. His run is ended by a foul as Palace win themselves a free kick.
(27’) Giroud now goes down claiming to have been fouled, although it looked more like a slip. Moments later, Arteta is brought down by Chamakh, with a free kick this time being given.
(26’) POOR! Oxlade-Chamberlain tries to switch the play from one wing to the other but his pass is mis-hit and goes out for a goal kick. The 20-year-old looks tired already and surely won't last the 90 minutes. But his energy has been useful to the Gunners going forward.
(24’) The set-piece is cleared, though, but only as far out as Oxlade-Chamberlain. His shot is blocked for a throw-in and Arsenal continue to press down the middle. This is more like what we are used to, after that period of relative pressure from the away side.
(23’) CORNER! Lovely build-up play from Arsenal now as Cazorla, Ozil and Giroud combine in a way reminiscent of Wilshere's wonder-goal against Norwich. They win a corner for their efforts...
(22’) Yannick Bolasie now muscles his way past Sagna, although German defender Per Mertesacker is there to dispossess him with a fine tackle. What a superb buy he turned out to be by Wenger, despite his exasperating lack of pace.
(21’) Now Arsenal look to get back into their stride but Cazorla plays a loose pass on the edge of the area and it is cut out with ease by the Palace defenders. Oxlade-Chamberlain is next to give it away! Are the hosts missing the likes of Jack Wilshere, Aaron Ramsey and Mathieu Flamini?
(19’) FOUL! Another foul from Jedinak! He isn't booked as the clumsy challenge is in the middle of the pitch, away from harm. However, that's his second foul of the game - in less than 20 minutes. He needs to be careful.
(18’) Are Pulis' side starting to settle down, here? Arsenal are seeing less and less of the ball and haven't had a chance to speak of for minutes. Their supporters are sensing the shift in momentum and aren't hesitating to express their frustration.
(17’) That said, Chamakh has been a different player this season, especially under Pulis. He was fantastic against Tottenham recently, while he also achieved the significant feat of scoring at Stamford Bridge.
(16’) Interestingly, the visitors are starting to get more and more into this now - and it's Chamakh again causing the problems. This time, he advances towards the penalty area, turns Laurent Koscielny and feeds the ball through to Puncheon. The pass is poor, however, and rolls out for a goal kick.
(14’) And more great awareness from Szczesny, as the Polish goalkeeper sees the ball out for a goal kick with comfort. Some good moments from the visitors there - but nothing Arsenal couldn't handle.
(13’) Great intervention by Wojciech Szczesny! Marouane Chamakh of all people was running at goal and the Arsenal goalkeeper needed to come out early to stop him from unleashing a shot. Imagine if he scored against his former club?
(12’) A rare venture into the Arsenal half for Palace now, though, as the ball is played into Cameron Jerome in the penalty area but the striker is given offside. Jerome worked under Pulis at Stoke City and has looked a much more dangerous striker since the former Potters boss has come in at Palace.
(10’) Cazorla shoots... And that's not one for the highlight reels. Out the ball goes, yards over the bar. However, a positive statistic for home supporters: Arsenal have had no less than 74% of possession so far.
(9’) The home crowd are in good voice here and the Gunners now win a free kick in an advanced position. Santi Cazorla and Lukas Podolski stand over it. But who will take it?
(7’) The left-back, in truth, looked as though he was trying to square the ball across the box in mid-air. Speroni's intervention was needed nevertheless. Will this Arsenal dominance continue?
(6’) CHANCE! A great save from Julian Speroni! The visitors are really struggling to get hold of the ball as Arsenal push them deeper and deeper. Oxlade-Chamberlain is the architect from deep but it is Mesut Ozil who plays the ball into the box, as Nacho Monreal gets on the end of it and is stopped by Speroni.
(4’) Arsenal use the set-piece to keep attacking down the right, until Oxlade-Chamberlain spreads the ball out to his left wisely. He is looking to get as involved as he can early on, although this particular move ends as Olivier Giroud, appealing for a corner, lets the ball go out for a goal kick.
(3’) Well, we've only had three minutes and it's all Arsenal, despite a promising first bout of possession from the away side. The only problem they've had is trying to get the ball back from the hosts. Their visible frustration results in Mile Jedinak giving away an early free kick.
(2’) An even opening few exchanges from both sides, as Crystal Palace show that they are not shy to try and take Arsenal on in possession. The home side are already demonstrating their slick passing style in return, however, as Mikel Arteta and Bacary Sagna in particular exchange passes with ease.
(1’) And we're off!
Right, we're moments away from kick-off. Can Arsenal return to the top of the league? Or will Pulis' Palace side spoil the party and continue their mid-season resurgence? Stay with us to find out!
And on Palace's bench, meanwhile, we have new signing Wayne Hennessey, who has Premier League experience from his time at Wolves. The goalkeeper joined Pulis' side on deadline day but has not been thrown straight into the starting line-up. He could, however, be one to watch as the season progresses.
Back to the positive news for Gunners fans, though, and Gedion Zelalem - who only just turned 17 - has made Wenger's bench today. Could he possibly be late match-winner for the home side? His team-mates will probably hope it doesn't get to that stage...
Arsene Wenger's only January signing, of course, was designed to ease that particular problem - but Kim Kallstrom, brought in on loan from Spartak Moscow, is himself currently injured and could be out for at least a few weeks.
Those statistics might just bring an optimistic smile to an Arsenal fan's face, while the news that Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain is starting this afternoon would only increase it. The 20-year-old looks to be starting in central midfield - welcome news with the Gunners so light in the middle of the park.
But there is a lot at stake for visitors Crystal Palace, too, as a win could take them as high as 11th. Under Tony Pulis, Palace are unbeaten in their last three home games. Away from home, however, they have won just one of their last five - only scoring twice in that time.
Arsenal can return to the summit of the Premier League table with a win today, as Manchester City are yet to play this weekend and will host Chelsea on Monday night.
Palace subs: Hennessey, Mariappa, McCarthy, Gayle, Wilbraham, Guedioura, Bannan.
Crystal Palace starting line-up: Speroni; Gabbidon, Delaney, Ward, Parr; Jedinak, Dikgacoi, Puncheon, Bolasie; Chamakh, Jerome.
Arsenal subs: Fabianski, Rosicky, Bendtner, Jenkinson, Gibbs, Gnabry, Zelalem.
Let's start with today's team news. Hosts Arsenal first: Szczesny; Mertesacker, Sagna, Monreal, Koscielny; Oxlade-Chamberlain, Arteta, Cazorla, Podolski, Ozil; Giroud.
Good afternoon and welcome to live-text commentary of Arsenal against Crystal Palace! I'm your host Tim Poole and I'll be guiding you through all today's action.

Someone else City no doubt missed tonight was Fernandinho - but Manuel Pellegrini will simply have to take stock and go again when his side play Norwich City next in the Premier League. That wraps up our coverage for tonight and we hope you enjoyed what was an absolutely enthralling game. I've been Tim Poole and, until next time, take care.
Chelsea, who were simply excellent in all departments tonight, now move level on points with City, whose superior goal difference keeps them in second place. Arsenal remain two points above both - and the Premier League title race remains as captivating as it has been for many, many years.
City had their chances, though, and perhaps Sergio Aguero would have taken them had he been fit. As it was, David Silva, Yaya Toure and even substitute Stevan Jovetic couldn't beat Petr Cech - no matter how hard they tried.
Another caveat to add to Jose Mourinho's scrapbook, then, as Chelsea finally end City's reign of terror at the Etihad. Eleven wins from 11 becomes 11 from 12, as a first-half winner from Branislav Ivanovic - and a tactical masterclass from the Special One - is enough to give the Blues three vital points at the home of their great rivals.
FULL-TIME: Manchester City 0-1 Chelsea!
--- 90’ +4 Substitution D. Ba enters play, replacing E. Hazard. ---
(90’) Headed clear by substitute Ba! Then Cahill heads the ball away! No luck for City! And finally, Nastasic miskicks the final chance of the game!
(90’) SAVE!! There's still life in City yet, as Kolarov plays the ball to Jovetic, who curls a shot from outside the box and forces a great save from Cech! Hazard now comes off in another substitution designed to delay the game. One final corner...
--- 90’ +2 Substitution Willian is replaced with J. Obi Mikel. ---
--- 90’ +2 Yellow card Willian receives a yellow card. ---
(90’) Manchester City are one minute away from dropping their first Premier League points at home this season.
(90’) Navas breaks down the right and lifts a cross into the box - but Cahill is there to clear for a corner! It's Navas again who whips the set-piece into the box but Willian is then there to clear. John Obi Mikel then replaces the Brazilian, who has been impressive today.
(90’) The fourth official holds up his board and there will be THREE minutes of added time. Will there be late drama or will Chelsea go level on points with their hosts?
(89’) As much as the visitors have been impressive tonight, however, City have had their chances - and not taken them. Silva, in particular, has missed two good opportunities, as the home fans whistle in concern with a minute to go.
(88’) "Jose Mourinho!" chant the Chelsea fans. The Special One is minutes away from yet another 'special' victory. But can City get back into this one late on? Pellegrini looks rather anxious in these dying embers.
--- 87’ Yellow card M. Nastasić is cautioned by the referee. ---
(87’) On the counterattack, Chelsea had two against one, as Nastasic pulled Oscar to the ground! The incident was next to the half-way line, however, so was only worthy of a yellow card - not a sending off.
(86’) Despite attempts from Kompany, Navas and Kolarov, City can't break the Chelsea back line down. But they are getting closer, if anything. They then win another corner but it is cleared and there's a foul in the middle of the park, as Chelsea players appeal for a red card!
(85’) And now a corner to City! Kolarov brushed Willian off the ball but no foul was given, prompting Ramires to swoop in and knock the ball in behind.
(84’) Corner to Chelsea! Nastasic knocks it off and Hazard plays it short to Willian. The Blues look keen to waste as much time on the ball as they can, although the Belgian then quickly pulls the trigger and tries to slip Ramires through in the box. The pass is a little too far ahead of the Brazilian and Hart comes out to collect.
--- 83’ Substitution S. Eto'o is replaced with Oscar. ---
(82’) Now comes the change, Oscar comes on for Samuel Eto'o. The Cameroonian has had a productive game and takes his time as he walks off. Not for the first time this season, Chelsea are now operating without a recognised striker. Oscar drops slightly in behind Hazard.
(81’) City continue to push forward, although first Dzeko gives the ball away - and then Zabaleta, whose cross is simply awful as it floats off for a goal kick. Oscar waits in the technical area.
(80’) CORNER TO CITY! Toure tries to thread an intricate through ball to Silva but it is deflected off for a corner. However, from the ensuing set-piece, Navas absolutely wastes his cross, which goes straight to Cech. Oscar looks ready to come on, in the meantime...
(79’) Luiz didn't impress there, though, as he sent yet another shot way over the bar. It's a good thing he's a defender... He certainly can strike a football - but most of his shots seem to sail hopelessly wayward. Meanwhile, Willian is given offside as Chelsea almost catch City off-guard with another rapid counterattack.
(78’) Will Mourinho's side hold on? He seems to have got his tactics spot on so far this evening, with Matic and Luiz impressing in midfield and Hazard, Willian and Ramires using their pace to great effect on the counter.
(77’) CHANCE! It's John Terry of all people in the penalty area trying to get the ball past Hart! And he does so - but his shot is dealt with by Toure. This has been a truly brilliant game here at the Etihad and it isn't over just yet.
(76’) Straight up the other end we go, as Chelsea win themselves a corner. A goal at this point would be crucial...
(75’) OH, WHAT A CHANCE! The ball is worked out wide and Kolarov sends another great cross into the area - if there's one thing the full-back can do it's cross! But Spaniard Silva gets on the end of it and can only fire wide. How costly will that prove?
(74’) It comes to nothing, though, and Pellegrini looks disappointed. His side have just 15 minutes (plus injury time) to salvage something from this game now. At least if it's not their 100 per cent home record, might they manage to stay unbeaten?
(73’) SAVE! Perfect execution from Silva but Cech makes an outstanding save after the ball is curled towards the top right corner! City then press again and win themselves another corner.
(72’) FREE KICK! Jesus Navas, Silva and Toure now link up, with Willian eventually bringing Toure down! However, there doesn't look to be much in the challenge, although City won't care as they have a free kick right on the edge of the penalty area. Silva and Kolarov are standing near it.
(70’) Jovetic has the game's next shot - but it is a poor one. Under little pressure, the striker hits a low effort well wide of goal. It seemed to limp out for a goal kick.
(69’) Ramires now forces a save from Hart! This has developed into a truly sensational encounter at the Etihad. But, then again, we never doubted it, did we?
(67’) And now Cahill clears from inside the six-yard box for Chelsea! City are finally starting to threaten and we have an absolutely end-to-end game on our hands! It was a great break from the home side, with Pablo Zabaleta crossing it into the area. Jovetic got on the end of it but Cahill slid in and knocked it away.
(66’) POST!! Willian needs two attempts to take the corner and it's Cahill who gets on the end of it and heads the ball against the woodwork! From the left side of the area, he headed straight against Hart's right post and the England 'keeper was rooted to the spot. Chelsea could have been 4-0 up by now!
(65’) The home side aren't giving up here, however, as they continue to push forward and win free kicks in the Chelsea half. Their final product has really let them down today, though, something in no small part down to great defending from the Blues. Matija Nastasic does some defending of his own now, though, giving a corner away.
(63’) More trickery from Hazard unleashes Ramires again, although the Brazilian is this time offside. To reiterate, Hazard has been simply sublime tonight. He came to Stamford Bridge with a hefty transfer fee but most will argue he was worth every penny.
(62’) Great pass! Matic, another strong performer tonight, plays in Ramires with a great ball but the Brazilian can't unleash the next pass in the move. He was inches away from feeding Eto'o in but a good sliding challenge denied him.
(61’) Over! It wasn't the most spectacular free kick from Kolarov, who did get some dip on the ball - but not really enough. Cech was untroubled as the ball sailed over the bar. Half an hour remains here and Chelsea are looking good value for their lead.
(60’) Another foul now, this time from Luiz on Jovetic, whose trickery is beginning to take effect. The free kick is within shooting distance - around 25 yards from goal.
(59’) FOUL! Toure brings down Willian - and the Ivorian isn't happy with the referee for giving the free kick! Toure is visibly frustrated and he really couldn't deal with Willian's pace there. From the resulting set-piece, Chelsea play the ball back to Cech but his kick is wayward and goes off for a throw-in in the City half.
(58’) It's Alvaro Negredo who makes way for Jovetic in the end in a like-for-like swap. This hasn't been one of the Spaniard's best nights, that's for sure. But what can his replacement offer for the home side?
--- 57’ Substitution S. Jovetić comes on for Negredo. ---
(56’) FREE KICK! Chelsea now win a free kick roughly 30 yards from goal and it's Luiz to take it once again. The Brazilian does better than his first-half effort, although his shot still can't beat the wall.
(55’) Chelsea now fight for possession in midfield but Silva is able to steal the ball off them and the Etihad crowd are audibly buoyed by the Spaniard's commitment.
(53’) INCOMING! Jovetic is indeed about to come on for the home side. Can he change things? Perhaps a more important question is who will make way?
(52’) CROSSBAR! City, on the other hand, look worried every time Chelsea come forward and it's Matic who almost punishes them this time. He is played in by Willian a few yards outside the penalty area and hits a thunderous drive towards goal. He isn't far off, as he smashes the ball against the bar!
(51’) WIDE! A reasonable move from City now ends with Toure flashing a shot just wide! That's their first real chance of the half but the Ivorian had to take a rushed effort. Chelsea not too troubled by that one.
(49’) Hart collects the corner but City look very weak at the back right now. They have leaked goals at times this season but no one has been able to punish them for it, especially at the Etihad. Their phenomenal strikeforce has usually made up for any defensive discrepancies.
(48’) CHANCE! Chelsea push forward this time, though, as a cross into the box is cleared, before Luiz wins the ball back for the visitors. It was complete chaos for City in defence once again and the Blues have their second corner of the match.
(47’) Stevan Jovetic is warming up for the home side. Once again, it looks like Pellegrini's answer to not scoring will be... to throw on another striker. His side are trying to go forward early in this second half, though, as a cross is played into the danger area and Dzeko heads wide under pressure from Gary Cahill.
(46’) And we're off! Chelsea get us started and there haven't been any changes at the break.
The players are out for the second half, anyway. We're almost set to resume the action!
A lot of reaction across the world of social media has reflected on Martin Demichelis' performance in that first half. The centre-back is playing out of position but has still got plenty of criticism for his display before the break. The Argentine was out of position for Ivanovic's goal - and that wasn't the only time.
Currently, all the momentum is with the Blues. But will it continue after the break?
Ramires, Willian and Samuel Eto'o, too, have found pockets of space in key areas, with City taking more and more of a backseat as the half progressed. Manuel Pellegrini's side started well but Jose Mourinho's men sat back well, dealt with any early threats and countered their way into the lead later in the half.
So it's Chelsea who have struck first tonight, Branislav Ivanovic putting the Blues ahead with a great goal after 32 minutes. Eden Hazard was involved in the build-up - and that was hardly a one-off contribution. The Belgian has been terrific for Chelsea and the Manchester City defence have struggled to deal with him all night.
HALF-TIME: Manchester City 0-1 Chelsea. Jose Mourinho is the first to walk off at the break, quick as lightning.
(45’) Chaos in the Man City defence as Chelsea put more pressure on them! At this rate, City's 100 per cent home record this season will be over! This was always going to be the game that gave Pellegrini the most trouble. However, expect his side to come out firing after half-time - even without the talismanic Sergio Aguero.
(45’) There will be two minutes of added time as groans ring around the Etihad. Chelsea have enjoyed this half a lot more than the hosts - thanks to one man in particular: Eden Hazard.
(44’) CROSSBAR! Hazard does superbly down the left once again and crosses the ball into Eto'o, who hesitates a little before crashing the ball against the bar! Might he rue missing that? A two-goal advantage would have been extremely helpful going into the break!
--- 42’ Yellow card BOOKING! That's careless from Kolarov, who receives a booking for a poor challenge. He started promisingly but now looks more of a hindrance for his side than a help. ---
(41’) CHANCE! The corner evades its initial targets but falls to an unmarked Dzeko! The Bosnian, slightly off balance, fires a shot away at goal and it is not too far off, although it eventually goes over.
--- 40’ Yellow card Matic now enters the book after a needless foul, while City win themselves corner... ---
(39’) STAT ATTACK: The goal was Ivanovic's 15th in the Premier League and his first with his left foot.
(38’) The man of the moment, though, is Ivanovic, who took his strike like a forward when it mattered. Mourinho has tactically outwitted Pellegrini so far, although with the attacking options at his disposal, this is far from over.
--- 37’ Yellow card M. Demichelis is yellow-carded. ---
(36’) BOOKING! Demichelis is booked as he brings Hazard down. The City back line - and midfield - can't deal with the Belgian at the moment. He seems to have taken the spotlight off Toure.
(35’) CHANCE! Chelsea almost double their lead as Hazard, who has been sensational so far, works the ball to Ramires in the box again! The Brazilian clearly wasn't brought to the Etihad to sit back. He can't quite make the most of his chance once again, though, and the ball falls to Hazard, who has his shot saved by Hart.
(34’) City respond straight away - but it is hardly a vintage attack from Pellegrini's side. The ball is played from side to side and a limp shot crawls towards Cech. However, they clearly want to get back on level terms quickly...
--- 33’ Yellow card B. Ivanović gets yellow. ---
--- 32’ Goal! GOALLLL! Ivanovic gives Chelsea the lead!! How about that? Kompany is furious with his side after Hazard is allowed to cross the ball to an unmarked Ramires. The Brazilian has hit shot blocked but it only goes as far out as the Chelsea right-back, who thumps a low finish home from outside the box. What a blow for City! ---
(31’) The home side, of course, have had their own chances, with Toure in particular impressing. Negredo and Dzeko haven't offered enough in the final third quite yet, though. The possession stats still read 65-35 in Manchester City's favour.
(30’) We're half an hour into this one now and a fascinating contest is developing. You cannot, by any measure, say that Mourinho's side are here to park the bus. They are certainly here to play on the counter - but they have not been afraid to commit men forward when given the chance.
(28’) That was easily the chance of the match so far but Brazilian Ramires was unable to take advantage of his side's sheer pace (him included) on the counterattack. He only had a split second to make his decision but he could have picked a better spot for his finish.
(27’) CHANCE!! From the resulting set-piece, Cech punches the ball away and Chelsea have a counterattack that sees four blue shirts against one City defender! But Ramires hits his shot straight at Hart! Willian tries to overhead kick the rebound and it goes way over.
(26’) A fantastic tackle from Demichelis perhaps makes up for his earlier hesitance, as it almost sets up a goal! The Argentine won the ball well in midfield and City took the ball forward, with Kolarov crossing for Silva, who had his shot blocked. Corner to City now.
(24’) Hesitance from Demichelis almost puts his back four in trouble as Eto'o and co. put pressure on the City back line! The Argentine almost played his pass to a Chelsea player but Toure came in to save the day.
(23’) More trickery from Hazard on the edge of the Chelsea box but Willian, who he was playing a one-two with, is given offside. We're halfway through the first half here and there's been plenty of action. You sense the first goal will raise the dynamic even more.
(22’) Half-chance for City now, as Edin Dzeko has his first shot of note at goal. The Bosnian was standing on the edge of the box with one or two Blue shirts in front of him. As such, the best he could do was to curl a low shot just wide of the left post.
(21’) POOR! Willian and Luiz stand over the free kick... Chelsea fans won't be speaking about that one for a while. It's Luiz who steps up to the ball and lumps it way over the bar. A terrible strike.
(20’) FOUL! The visitors get themselves into a great position from that bout of possession, as Hazard is brilliant with the ball at his feet once again. The Belgian skips past at least two players before being brought down by two City defenders at once! His reward is a free kick very close to goal...
(19’) Eto'o responds for Chelsea - but it is a blunt response at best, as his limp shot finds its way straight to Hart. The City goalkeeper knocks it long but it goes straight back to the Blues.
(18’) CHANCE! Great work from Toure yet again this time sets up David Silva, who is inside the six-yard box but is only able to tap just wide. This is an encouraging time for the home crowd!
(17’) STAT ATTACK: Manchester City have had 65 per cent of possession so far. Are you surprised, or do you think that has been Mourinho's plan all along?
(16’) TOURE! The Ivorian very nearly gives his side the lead! A simple pass was played into him from the right and, a couple of yards outside the penalty area, Toure curled a wonderful shot just over the bar. What a goal that would have been.
(15’) Almost the perfect move from Chelsea as a superb Ivanovic tackle sets up a speedy counterattack (another pattern that is developing for the Blues). Several moments later, though, City are able to win the ball back in their own half. Here they come again...
(14’) OFFSIDE! Eden Hazard does brilliantly to surge deep into the City half and find Eto'o. The Cameroonian is offside, however, as he squares the ball for it to be placed into an empty net. Hart had nothing to worry about, the referee was always going to blow his whistle there.
(13’) A definite pattern is developing here, as Chelsea drop deeper and City enjoy more and more possession. Luiz shows his frustration with a clumsy foul in midfield - but the Blues are able to win the ball back just moments later...
(12’) But the corner is wasted! A looping cross is played into Negredo and the Spaniard can't get any sort of direction on his header, as it goes several yards over the bar. A busy start so far, as you would expect with two teams of this quality.
(11’) Good defending from Branislav Ivanovic next, as he heads an aerial cross out of the box, before Matic then clears again to give City a corner. The home side are enjoying a good passage of play here.
(10’) CHANCE! City attack down the left again! Their full-backs really are dangerous and Kolarov almost found Toure with a lethal ball across the box. The Ivorian slid in and was inches away from the ball. A close shave for Chelsea.
(9’) A good few moments for Chelsea, as relative new-boy (returning to Stamford Bridge after being sold by Chelsea to Benfica, of course) Matic cuts a City attack out and the Blues demonstrate their venom on the break.
(8’) COUNTERATTACK! Chelsea then hit City on the break straightaway! Willian does all the hard work and gets into the box to deliver a cross, though it is blocked well by the City defenders. It goes off for a corner, which too is cleared...
(7’) Now Yaya Toure has been brought down, as the game slows from its initially frantic pace after a couple of needless fouuls here and there. City look to keep things going through Aleksandar Kolarov, though, but Nemanja Matic cuts his cross out effectively.
(5’) FOUL! Vincent Kompany brings Eto'o down, forcing the referee to have a quick word with him. It was a rash challenge from the Belgian and Pellegrini will be looking for less of that this evening.
(3’) Alvaro Negredo fires an early warning from a tight angle! The Spaniard is played in on the left side of the penalty area and never looks like beating Cech. He has a go, nevertheless, and his shot is just wide and over.
(2’) That was almost a repeat of the blunder Joe Hart made in the reverse fixture at Stamford Bridge! Chelsea break straight up the pitch moments later, however, as Ramires and Samuel Eto'o link up well. The ball rolls out for a goal kick, eventually. Both sides feeling each other out here early on.
(1’) And we're off! The hosts get us underway. You can already see there's plenty at stake as Petr Cech is forced off his line to make a nervous clearance!
The players are on the pitch, the fans are making themselves heard and we are just moments away from kick-off!
Something's got to give, surely? Stay with us to find out exactly what, as kick-off is approximately 10 minutes away. Titles are decided by such occasions.
Mourinho, though, has promised to adopt an attacking approach. "Chelsea try to win every game," the Portuguese told reporters ahead of the clash. "We are not going to change our philosophy. We are going in a certain direction and just because we are playing a certain opponent, it doesn't mean we are going to change that."
At the Etihad this season, however, Manchester City have won 11 out of 11 in the Premier League, scoring 42 goals and conceding just eight.
But victory for Pellegrini's side would take them six points clear of Mourinho's men - and one ahead of Arsenal. Chelsea won this season's first meeting between the two sides after a fortuitous Fernando Torres winner at Stamford Bridge, now comes round two.
It's absolutely all to play for at the Etihad tonight (where hosts City have scored 72 goals in all competitions so far this season). Chelsea, in third, can move level with City with a win, closing the gap behind leaders Arsenal to just two points.
As you can also see, then, both sides have made adventurous selections on their bench. Manuel Pellegrini has once again put his faith in young starlet Marcos Lopes, while January signing Mohamed Salah could be in line for his Chelsea debut.

A comfortable debut for Mata, and a comfortable night all around for Manchester United. Ole Gunnar Solskjaer made an emotional, but ultimately fruitless return to his former stomping grounds as his side must now look elsewhere for help in their search for survival. Van Persie scored on his return from injury, and things may be finally looking up at Old Trafford.
(90’) That's it! Man Utd see it out!
(90’) Looks to be a good strike from Rooney, but it starts to bend towards the end and whizzes the wrong side of the post!
(90’) Bellamy has a good chance to play on the break for Cardiff, but hits a pass way too far ahead of Campbell, and the opening dries up in an instant.
(90’) Stoppage time upon us once again, and there will be four minutes of it.
(89’) Another Cardiff corner, which comes to nothing once again. Campbell wastes a good chance to hit a first time shot from that delivery, and instead bobbles it over the bar after some awkward control.
(87’) Rooney spots the keeper off his line, and, as he is wont to do, tries to lob him, but it falls far too close to Marshall, who catches comfortably in the end.
(86’) Cardiff have two corners back to back, but cannot get close to making any of them count.
--- 84’ Substitution Mata is replaced with A. Januzaj. ---
(84’) Final United change, as Mata's debut ends and Januzaj comes on in his stead. A solid, if unspectacular debut from the Spaniard.
(82’) United in no hurry and you can't blame them with eight minutes remaining. Moyes will be happy to see this out and pick up a vital three points.
(80’) Time starting to ebb away now, and in truth, the result has been in no doubt since Young decided to pull that goal right out of the top drawer.
--- 78’ Substitution M. Dæhli enters play, replacing C. Noone. ---
(78’) On comes Daehli for his senior debut for Cardiff. He actually played for Man Utd until 2013, and won the club's Jimmy Murphy Young Player of the Year award two years ago for his play in the youth squads. Still only 18 years old.
(76’) CRUCIAL touch from Marshall pushes a Valencia shot onto the post, after the Ecuadorian winger had shifted into space on the edge of the six yard area!
(74’) Rooney shrugs off a defender and fires away at goal. The shot, aided by a deflection off Caulker, just fizzes wide of Marshall's right hand post!
(72’) United plotting something at the edge of the area with Mata heavily involved, but Cardiff are holding their form and keeping their shape.
--- 71’ Substitution T. Cleverley enters the game and replaces R. Giggs. ---
(70’) Twenty minutes remaining, and United are sitting pretty. Keeping with the pattern this season, they've been far from their best, but two goals is just a bridge too far for Cardiff to cross one feels.
--- 69’ Substitution M. Hudson is done for the day. B. Turner is his replacement. ---
(68’) Rushed shot from Evans from all of 25 yards, which bends the wrong way and goes wide, much to the relief of Marshall!
(66’) Good play from Valencia to beat his man for pace towards the right byeline, but his cross is narrowly ahead of the lurking Rooney.
(64’) So we won't get our first glimpse at the new United big three together on the pitch, as Van Persie is replaced by Rooney.
--- 63’ Substitution R. van Persie is replaced with W. Rooney. ---
(63’) Juan Mata attemts to replicate Young's effort from moments ago, cutting onto his right peg on the left and letting fly, but this effort is straight at Marshall.
(61’) United have that oh-so-important bit of breathing space. Tough on Cardiff, who were just beginning to come alive in the game. Meanwhile, Moyes is plotting to re-introduce Rooney on the sidelines.
--- 59’ Goal! The winger produces one for the very top of his catalogue, cutting in from the left onto his right foot and arrowing a wonderful effort into the opposite corner! ---
(59’) WHAT A GOAL FROM YOUNG!
(58’) Terrific buildup play from Noone, who squeezes past his man on the byeline and nearly squares to Bellamy for the tap in! That's twice now Cardiff have beaten United to the byeline in the second half!
(56’) Cardiff have had their fair share of the ball in this second half, and are looking increasingy capable every time they attack. United still have a lot of work to do.
(54’) UNITED REALLY LET OFF THE HOOK! John sprints past Evra on the left, Evans slips, and he seems primed to square to Campbell for the finish! But his pass is just a little behind the striker at the near post!
--- 52’ Substitution J. Mutch is replaced with Bo-Kyung Kim. ---
(52’) Dangerous free kick into the area from Giggs, and it's met by Van Persie...but he heads over! Decent opening that for the home team.
(50’) Good play from United to work Valencia into a crossing position on the right, but his ping into the box is just, just ahead of Van Persie. Young cannot recover the rebound in time to punish a scrambling defence.
(48’) Cardiff have made an energetic start to the second half, and have abandoned their deeper defensive line in favour of pressing United higher up the pitch.
(46’) Here we go again!
Manchester United lead at the interval. It's not a commanding lead by any stretch, as Cardiff have rebuffed most of their other efforts to find another breakthrough. Van Persie scores on his return, and there's been cautious positivity around the play of Mata, who was involved in the opener. Cardiff are only a goal away though, and are not out of this in any way. Stay tuned for the restart in just a bit.
(45’) That's it for the half.
(45’) Into stoppage time now, of which there's only a minute.
(44’) It has to be said that the visitors have held a solid shape at the back for most of the game. Man Utd have found chances very hard to come by since the opener. One mistake can blow up in their faces.
(42’) Evans loks to switch the play out to Rafael with a searching ball, and the right back manages to keep it in, but his cross cannot beat the first man. Cardiff holding firm at the back.
(40’) Evans and De Gea confuse each other when attempting to deal with a routine cross from Cardiff. The keeper should have been all over that, if I'm honest, flattening anyone, friend or foe, that got in his way.
(38’) There's been enough in this to suggest that United won't get complacent on the back of a one goal lead. And after the season that they've had, there's no way that they should be!
(36’) Noone puts in an absolute peach of a cross into the area that narrowly evades two Cardiff bodies in the box! Best move of the match from the visitors so far.
(34’) Good move from a short corner sees Valencia pick out Van Persie at the far post, but with the angle diminishing by the second, he strikes it the wrong side of the post!
(32’) The Phil Jones Face, quite literally, comes to Man Utd's rescue, as he takes a stinging shot from Whittingham full on the nose.
(30’) Not for the first time, Campbell tries to get the better of Smalling by trying to steer a flick around the centre back, but he's not falling for it, and marshalls the play excellently.
(28’) Cardiff's turn now to hold a spell of possession, as United sit deep and soak up the pressure. Not much in the way of chances though, and this game is still very much up for grabs.
(26’) United continue to enjoy the lion's share of the ball, and are slowly chipping away at this Cardiff midfield and defence. The pressing from their frontline is admirable.
(24’) Despite all the attention for Mata's arrival, it's the return to fitness of Robin van Persie that is being sung to the heavens by the Old Trafford faithful.
(22’) Curmudgeon-in-chief Craig Bellamy puts himself under pressure for the rest of the game with a needless yellow card, kicking the ball away in protest at a free kick given against his team.
--- 21’ Yellow card C. Bellamy goes into the referee's book. ---
(20’) THERE WE GO! Mata's pinpoint ball to the far post nearly gets turned in by the sprawling Young, but he cannot make clean enough contact on the ball and a great chance goes begging!
(18’) Not much to report in terms of chances since the opening salvo, as both teams feel each other out.
(16’) Still some kinks to work out in the United front six, as Mata is dropping deeper and deeper to get the ball and get himself involved in the game. Perhaps United are overplaying it a little in the centre.
(14’) Have to say it's getting a bit unappetizing down there on the pitch. UNited have unwisely taken their foot off the gas, inviting Cardiff back into the game, but the visitors are unwilling to accept the invite, playing their own brand of cautious football.
(12’) Cardiff starting to show some signs of life in the attacking third. Campbell is run close by Smalling before eventually losing the ball near the byeline, before Mutch tries to pick out the striker again, but the pass is overhit.
(10’) United have all the time in the world to ping passes around, as Cardiff sit deep, attempting to plot their fortunes on the counter attack.
(8’) Things are suddenly looking up at Old Trafford. A dream start to the game, their main Dutchman back and firing, and Mata heavily involved already. No wonder the Stretford End is awash with noise!
--- 6’ Goal! MAN UTD STRIKE EARLY! What a scramble in the box, as Valencia's header from Young's cross hits the bar. Van Persie's follow up is saved excellently by Marshall, but he can do nothing to stop the Dutchman's second followup! 1-0! ---
(5’) Poor pass from Smalling is caught by Cardiff, but Mutch, on the flanks, cannot pick out anything other than a red shirt with the ball into the box, and the chance is gone.
(3’) Some good early pressure from United, who are keen to get Mata on the ball whenever possible. He's been spotted drifting out to the flanks regularly to pick up possession.
(1’) Here we go then!
Just five minutes to go until kick off and there will certainly be plenty of anticipation surrounding tonight's game. Can United kick start their stuttering season, or will Cardiff spoil the party and snatch a result and look to rise off the foot of the table?

(90’) Six (you read that right!) minutes of injury time will be played out.
(89’) WHAT A SAVE KRUL!!!! The visiting goalkeeper is furious with his defence for not providing enough cover as Redmond whips a ball towards the back post, and Snodgrass' diving header is parried away by the Dutchman!

(80’) RED CARD TO NEWCASTLE!!!

(60’) HE HAMMERS THE CROSSBAR!!! The attacker does a much better job than Santon at testing Ruddy from a set-piece situation after bending a curling drive onto the stanchion!

(47’) Johnson lays off Snodgrass on the right, but the former Leeds man drags his shot well wide of the target.
(45’) We're back out for the second half! It's anyone's game despite Newcastle's dominant first 45 minutes, which would have not made life any easier for Norwich's under-fire boss Chris Hughton.

(31’) Van Wolfswinkel ventures out to the right-hand side and whips up a cross for Hooper to meet, but the Tottenham youth product is nowhere near the ball, leaving Williamson to easily head away the danger.
(29’) The visitors are being afforded crossing opportunities at will here. There's been next to no closing down from Norwich's players - bar Martin's to concede a Toon corner only seconds ago.
(27’) The former Marseille ace's effort makes that 10 Newcastle attempts on target - compared to Norwich's measly haul of just the one.

Rene Meulensteen will be happy if things stay as they are, his side look fresh and good on the break, but Swansea will surely increase the pressure as they game goes on.

For Hull, this is a first opportunity to see their new club record buys line up together, with Nikica Jelavic and Shane Long - making his debut - both starting to boost the club's firepower. Bruce will hope his January acquisitions can improve the club's desperate away form, having accrued just five points on the road, a joint-Premier League low.
Pulis will be delighted with the five clean sheets his side have kept since he joined and the only slight on their form is a lack of goals; Palace are the lowest scorers in the league with just 14.
Palace's win at the KC Stadium was just their second of the campaign at the time but if they win here tonight, they will move level on points with the Tigers, testament to this recovery with Pulis at the helm.
Conversely, Palace are experiencing an upturn in fortunes under Tony Pulis' tutelage. The former Stoke manager was announced as the Eagles' new man on the day they secured all three points on Humberside and since then has secured 16 points from a possible 33. They had secured just four from their previous 11 league games.
Hull were looking relatively home and hosed after the festive break which yielded that 6-0 win over Fulham, but three straight defeats have left the Tigers looking nervously over their shoulder as they are just five points above the drop zone.
