--- 66’ Goal! ERIKSEN MAKES IT 2-0! It's a superb counter attack from Tottenham as Soldado releases Lennon down the right. The pacey winger's low cross deflects off the body of Vidic and Eriksen swoops in ahead of Valencia to nod beyond De Gea. Are all three points heading to White Hart Lane? ---
(65’) Tottenham make their first change of the game as the 19-year-old French midfielder Nabil Bentaleb comes on for Etienne Capoue. Can the youngster shine at the Theatre of Dreams?
--- 64’ Substitution N. Bentaleb enters the game and replaces E. Capoue. ---
(63’) Adnan Januzaj has failed to show his potential this evening and his tame effort is easily held by Lloris as he attempts to catch out the goalkeeper at his near post. Tim Sherwood is preparing his first substitution on the touchline.
(62’) Incidentally, Javier Hernandez is on a barren streak, having not found the net in his previous nine matches. I wonder whether he will push for a move away from Old Trafford in the newly-opened transfer window.
--- 61’ Substitution M. Carrick is done for the day. J. Hernández is his replacement. ---
--- 61’ Substitution S. Kagawa comes on for C. Smalling. ---
(61’) David Moyes decides to make a double attacking substitution as Javier Hernandez and Shinji Kagawa replace Michael Carrick and Chris Smalling. Antonio Valencia switches to right-back.
(59’) PENALTY APPEAL TURNED DOWN FOR MANCHESTER UNITED! Danny Welbeck is fortunate to escape a booking when he throws himself over Chiriches' leg after dribbling his way into the penalty area. Howard Webb waves away the appeals but decides not to brandish a card.
(58’) Chiriches has hardly put a foot wrong for Tottenham so far and he tracks Welbeck's run excellently to prevent the England striker latching onto Valencia's pass. Is this really the same defence which conceded five at Liverpool and six at Manchester City?
(56’) It's been a slow start to the second half with both sides struggling to fashion openings. David Moyes has clearly seen enough and he readies Shinji Kagawa on the touchline.
(54’) Tottenham are working so hard when they don't have the ball and they are not allowing Manchester United to settle in possession. Adebayor's work rate has been particularly impressive up front.
(52’) As things stand, Manchester United will be eleven points behind leaders Arsenal. Can they break down the resilient Tottenham backline which boasts the second-best defensive record in the Premier League?
(50’) GOOD CHANCE FOR WELBECK! Carrick opens up his former side with a cushioned lobbed pass over the Tottenham defence but Welbeck cannot generate enough power behind his volley and Lloris comfortably gathers.
(48’) Manchester United enjoy a sustained spell of pressure at the beginning of the second half without really testing the Tottenham defence. David Moyes will be praying that Robin Van Persie can recover quickly from his injury.
(46’) The two sides re-emerge from the tunnel for the second half and there have been no substitutions from either side. Can Manchester United avoid a fourth home league defeat?
MATCH FACT: Emmanuel Adebayor has now scored 25 league goals for Tottenham. That 34th-minute strike was the fourth scored with his head.
HT: Manchester United 0-1 Tottenham. Tim Sherwood's faith in Emmanuel Adebayor looks to pay dividends again as the Togo striker's header gives Spurs a slender advantage at the break. Manchester United have looked good in parts but they have struggled to get Wayne Rooney involved. Big half-time team talk ahead for David Moyes.
(45’) Chris Smalling nervously shuffles the ball behind for a corner under no pressure from a Tottenham player, much to the frustration of the home crowd. Fortunately for the right-back however, Rooney is back to head Eriksen's corner to safety.
(44’) Danny Welbeck attempts to replicate Wayne Rooney's spectacular bicycle kick against Manchester City when he meets Valencia's cross from the right. However, the in-form striker cannot divert his effort towards goal and another Manchester United attack breaks down.
(43’) Manchester United have looked dangerous down the wings but there is little penetration through the middle of the park. Surely David Moyes will be given the funds for a more incisive central midfielder in the newly-opened transfer window?
--- 41’ Yellow card Wayne Rooney picks up the first booking of the game after tussling unfairly with Dembele. The England striker is looking a little frustrated with his team's performance so far. ---
(39’) WHAT A CHANCE TO MAKE IT 2-0! Lennon has been short of fitness this season but he skips away from Evra down the right before sending a dangerous low cross towards Soldado at the back post. The Spanish striker manages to get in behind Vidic but he can only turn the ball over the bar on the slide.
(38’) Valencia has been a threat down the right for Manchester United in this first half and he fizzes a teasing cross into the box which Dawson does brilliantly to head away from the onrushing Januzaj. Can Manchester United find the equaliser?
(36’) MATCH STAT: Tottenham have not lost a league game this season where they have taken the lead.
--- 34’ Assist C. Eriksen gave the assist. ---
--- 34’ Goal! ADEBAYOR GIVES TOTTENHAM THE LEAD! Eriksen is the architect as he bursts down the right wing before standing up a cross towards the back post which Adebayor connects with, sending a brilliant header back across goal and into the bottom corner. David De Gea was motionless. That's his fourth goal of the season. ---
(32’) ADEBAYOR GOES CLOSE! The Togo striker has scored a number of fine volleys during his career and he latches onto a bouncing ball outside the box before sending a dipping half-volley narrowly wide of the top right-hand corner. If he can continue his recent goalscoring form, he could prove to be a key member of this Spurs side in the second half of the season.
(30’) Januzaj will be hoping to make an impression on his return to the side but he cannot get the better of Chiriches as the Romanian defender reads his attempted skill excellently to steal away possession. The Manchester United attack has gone a little flat in the past ten minutes or so.
(28’) Tottenham have settled into this game now after that early Manchester United pressure and Dembele takes a timeout to readjust his boots. Will we see a goal before the half-time whistle?
(26’) Valencia is proving a particular menace down the right for Manchester United and the Ecuadorian winger once again gets in behind Rose before his teasing cross is well headed clear by Dawson.
(24’) Roberto Soldado has been much-criticised in his early Tottenham career but he has looked bright so far and on this occasion, he seizes upon a loose ball on the right corner of the box before seeing his drilled effort well blocked.
(21’) VIDIC GOES CLOSE! The Serbian defender rises above Dawson to meet Januzaj's inswinging corner from the right but his header flashes narrowly past the post.
(20’) Valencia produces a brilliant piece of skill to evade Rose down the right before his low cross is hacked clear at the near post by Dawson, denying the lurking Rooney in the middle.
(18’) Antonio Valencia will be hoping for a better season in 2014 and he collects a pass on the right corner of the box before his arrowed drive is well blocked by Rose. It's been a high tempo start to the game at Old Trafford.
(16’) Tottenham are slowly growing into this game now and Capoue finds space on the edge of the box before ballooning an effort high over the crossbar.
(14’) WHAT A CHANCE FOR TOTTENHAM! The visitors create their first opening of the game as Soldado threads a wonderful ball through Evans' legs for Lennon to latch onto. The England winger is in behind Evra and clean through but can only fire straight at the legs of De Gea. He must do better there.
(12’) Tottenham are yet to fashion an attack on the Manchester United goal as the hosts dominate the early stages. However, it is important to note that only Arsenal have a better away record in the Premier League this season that their North London rivals.
(10’) Incidentally, Wayne Rooney is bidding to become only the second player, after Frank Lampard, to notch ten league goals in ten consecutive Premier League seasons.
(9’) Manchester United are pressing Tottenham high up the pitch and Evans wins a free kick on the edge of the box when he is tripped by Capoue. Rooney steps up to take it but he can only curl his effort high over the bar.
(7’) Michael Dawson receives treatment for an injury which he appeared to sustain when chasing Welbeck in that earlier Manchester United attack. With Vertonghen and Kaboul already sidelined, another defensive injury is the last thing that Sherwood needs.
(6’) SMALLING GOES CLOSE! The England defender storms forward from right-back, collecting a pass from Valencia and firing a shot towards goal at the near post. However, once again Lloris is there as he gets just enough on the ball to turn it around the post with his legs.
(5’) CHANCE FOR MANCHESTER UNITED! Danny Welbeck's pace is causing Tottenham all sorts of problems early on and he peels off of Dawson to latch onto Valencia's long ball before he is denied by the onrushing Lloris. The France No.1 has been busy in the opening exchanges.
(3’) It's Manchester United who are forcing the early pressure here and Cleverley attempts to poke a pass through for Welbeck but there is a lack of communication as the ball rolls through the legs of the England international.
(1’) Manchester United steal possession early on and Lloris needs to be alert to rush off his line and prevent Welbeck from snatching a goal after 37 seconds. Tottenham nearly suffered the same fate as they did at the Etihad there.
(1’) Howard Webb blows his whistle and Tottenham, in their traditional white jerseys, get the game underway. Can Tim Sherwood continue his unbeaten league start as manager?
The two sides emerge from the tunnel with captains Nemanja Vidic and Michael Dawson beginning the respective handshakes. Today's referee is Howard Webb.
MATCH FACT: Tottenham failed to defeat Manchester United in 26 meetings in all competitions in a frustrating run that spanned almost 14 years. However, that ended in September last year, as goals from Gareth Bale and Clint Dempsey helped them to a 3-2 success at Old Trafford - their first since 1989.
Manchester United and Tottenham are tied on 34 points, eleven points off Premier League leaders Arsenal who won 2-0 at home to Cardiff earlier. There are a valuable three points on offer today as Manchester City, Chelsea and Liverpool all secured wins. Who can keep their title hopes alive? Kick-off is under ten minutes away.
TOTTENHAM (4-4-2): Lloris; Walker, Chiriches, Dawson, Rose; Lennon, Capoue, Dembele, Eriksen; Adebayor, Soldado.
MANCHESTER UNITED (4-4-2): De Gea; Smalling, Evans, Vidic, Evra; Valencia, Carrick, Cleverley, Januzaj; Rooney, Welbeck.
TOTTENHAM TEAM NEWS: Kyle Walker and Danny Rose return to fill the respective full-back roles with Etienne Capoue starting in the centre of midfield. Emmanuel Adebayor will hope to continue his goalscoring form as he partners Roberto Soldado up front.
MANCHESTER UNITED TEAM NEWS: Wayne Rooney, Antonio Valencia, Adnan Januzaj and Danny Welbeck are all recalled to the starting eleven after the 1-0 win at Norwich.
I'm Max Bentley and I'll be leading you through the proceedings from Old Trafford. These two sides played out an entertaining 2-2 draw when they met at White Hart Lane exactly a month ago. Wayne Rooney was the hero for Manchester United that day as he dragged his side back from two goals down and the England striker has recovered from injury to start again today.
Hello and welcome to the live coverage of the standout tie of New Year's Day as Manchester United host Tottenham Hotspur, with both sides looking to get 2014 off to the perfect start. David Moyes' men have racked up four consecutive league wins to reignite their fading title challenge while Tottenham have started life under Tim Sherwood brightly with seven points from his first three league games in charge.

That wraps up our coverage of yet another Premier League thriller. Keith Downing and his West Brom side may just be satisfied with a point, although Sam Allardyce and West Ham certainly won't. Until next time, take care everyone!
Joe Cole opened the scoring for West Ham after just four minutes but West Brom hit back twice before half-time - both times through Nicolas Anelka. Modibo Maiga then scored his first Premier League goal of the season, before Kevn Nolan edged West Ham 3-2 in front. The Baggies had the last laugh, though, as Saido Berahino scored a fantastic equaliser.
What a game. What a result. Yet neither side will be delighted with the outcome...
FULL-TIME: West Ham 3-3 West Brom
(90’) Substitute Morgan Amalfitano shoots - but the ball goes straight into the stands!
(90’) Both sides are searching for a winner late on! End-to-end football once more but no real chances as of yet...
(90’) As things stand, West Brom are heading for their third consecutive draw, while West Ham will finish today bottom of the Premier League if Sunderland beat Cardiff City later.
(90’) We'll see four minutes of it!
(90’) Added time here...
(90’) Mulumbu now has a shot for the visitors but Jaaskelainen is able to save comfortably. Anxious moments now as we head into injury time.
(89’) GREAT DEFENDING! Demel sends a great cross into the area but Nolan's header is deflected wide by Gareth McAuley! Super invervention - the header was goalbound.
(87’) And Sessegnon is involved straight away, nutmegging a defender. But his touch is too heavy, with Jaaskelainen able to collect the loose ball.
(86’) Berahino now makes way for Stephane Sessegnon for West Brom.
(85’) Could this match go down as one of the clashes of the season?
(84’) Jack Collison comes on for Joe Cole for West Ham. Anyone's game with only a few minutes to go...
(83’) POST!!! Berahino takes the ensuing free kick and curls it right into the post! What an effort and the England Under-21 striker is unlucky not to score.
(82’) YELLOW CARD! Mohamed Diame is booked for a late challenge on Brunt. The West Brom man is slow to get to his feet.
(81’) West Brom seem to hold the physical advantage, with the West Ham players looking too tired to close them down effectively.
(80’) It is also hard to tell who has the upper hand at this stage. Both teams are fighting for every ball.
(79’) The feeling in the stands is hard to gage, here. They will be pleased with the heart West Ham have shown but, at the same time, they are unhappy with their side's defending.
(77’) SHOT! Brunt has a go at goal for West Brom after Demel fell asleep at the back! It fell straight to Jaasekelainen, though. Still end-to-end here. And I suppose it will be right up until full-time...
(75’) A draw will not do much for either side's ambitions this season, as their position won't change at all with a point.
(74’) West Brom attack. They lose the ball. West Ham attack. And repeat.
(72’) It's anyone's game now, with both sides' strengths and failings cancelling each other out. Will we see a winner - or possibly more than one goal - before full-time?
(70’) So off we go again...
--- 69’ Goal! S. Berahino scores for West Bromwich Albion! ---
(69’) BERAHINO!!! WHAT A GOAL!!! IT'S 3-3!!! I give up. What a game. This is the Premier League at its very best! Young Berahino receives the ball in the West Ham half and beats Demel with real ease, before curling home a superb shot to restore parity once again. Who knows what'll happen from here...
(68’) What a clash we have on our hands now...
--- 67’ Goal! Goal to West Ham United, scored by K. Nolan! ---
(67’) GOALLLL! WEST HAM TAKE THE LEAD! What a turnaround here!! Maiga does brilliantly once again to head the ball down in the box and there is Nolan, who smashes the ball into the roof of the net. There may be life in this West Ham side yet!
--- 65’ Goal! [object Object] ---
(65’) GOAL! Maiga equalises! From hero to zero, Foster tries to palm Maiga's long-range shot away but this time makes a complete mess of it. The West Ham striker's effort is from further away but it creeps through for his first Premier League goal of the season. Game on?
(64’) GREAT SAVE! The decibel levels have doubled here as Maiga has a go at goal for West Ham - but Ben Foster is there to produce a superb stop!
(63’) Frustration is evident in the stands, at the moment.
(62’) West Ham's initial resurgence this half has slowly ebbed away. Very worrying times for Allardyce.
(61’) Anelka shoots! It's blocked by McCartney but the Frenchman is in the hunt for West Brom's third here. And his own.
(59’) The calm before the storm, now. No real chances to speak of in the last few moments - which makes a change from the rest of the second half so far.
(56’) JUST WIDE! Joe Cole is the one to take the second West Ham free kick and, after some commotion about how far away the wall was, the shot flew just wide of the top corner. The Hammers are desperate to edge back into this here!
(55’) It's a good delivery but West Brom just about survive. The Hammers win yet another free kick, though! Great second half here, Allardyce has clearly motivated his side.
(54’) Free kick to West Ham now, though. Diego Lugano is the culprit.
(53’) WIDE! Berahino gets himself into a great position, switches onto his left foot and drives the ball at goal, low and hard. Jaaskelainen is at full stretch but the ball drifts narrowly wide of the post.
(51’) Great period of pressure from the hosts now...
(49’) West Ham win a free kick, which is whipped in by Jarvis, but an initial block by Olsson then ends up with the ball being knocked out for a goal kick by a Hammers player.
(47’) SAVE! Anelka almost gets himself a hat-trick! He tried to place his finish into the bottom corner but mishit his chance inside the box. Jaaskelainen gratefully collected.
(46’) We have restarted! West Ham have brought Modibo Maiga on for Carlton Cole at half-time.
All three goals were scored by former Chelsea players - for those of you who are trivia fans. Second half to come, Allardyce may be fighting for his job...
That half was a tale of two halves. Or perhaps just one half and a ten-minute salvo from the visitors. Joe Cole put West Ham in front after just four minutes but the hosts fell deeper and deeper after taking the lead. By the end of the half, Nicolas Anelka had punished them twice - with his first goals for West Brom.
The boos that rang out at the half-time whistle will be a worrying sign for Sam Allardyce...
HALF-TIME: West Ham 1-2 West Brom
--- 45’ +1 Goal! N. Anelka scores for West Bromwich Albion! ---
(45’) GOAL!!! Anelka strikes again!!! West Ham failed to capitalise on their corner moments earlier and West Brom wasted no time in winning one of their own. As the ball was played in, Anelka found himself on the ball in the box - in the perfect position - and tapped home once again. The Baggies have turned this game on its head!
(45’) They have won themselves a corner now, though, Jarvis surging down the left-hand side once again. He has been brilliant so far today.
(44’) After taking the lead, West Ham have sat back far too much and, while they have looked comfortable, they have dropped deeper and deeper.
(43’) Allardyce's half-time team talk will sound a little different now, I presume...
(41’) That's what Anelka brings to the table. The pass from Brunt was also superb!
--- 40’ Goal! N. Anelka has scored a goal for West Bromwich Albion! ---
(40’) GOALLL! Anelka scores!!! Well, it seems I spoke too soon, providing the commentator's kiss of death. Brunt was involved once again as he played the veteran striker in and Anelka went on one of his trademark runs. After entering the box, he tapped it past Jaaskelainen with the utmost ease. Suddenly, the game has turned on its head! Great goal.
(38’) Ironically, Brunt looks to find Berahino when a shot on goal could have been better! The midfielder latches onto a great through ball but chooses to cut the ball back for the striker and West Brom could have had an equaliser there!
(37’) The game has settled into a calm pace here - and that'll suit West Ham. West Brom look unable to impose themselves. Berahino needs to given better service.
(35’) WIDE! Noble has a go from the free kick, which is symbolic of the increasing confidence of this West Ham side. The shot sails a yard or so wide of goal but the intent was there and the home side can sense an opportunity to double their lead.
(34’) A foul on Kevin Nolan now. Perhaps a shooting position for the Hammers. They look comfortable at the minute - losing the ball in their own half aside.
(33’) A mix-up involving George McCartney almost results in trouble at the back! The West Ham defenders are dispossessed in their own half but get enough men back in time to clear the danger they themselves created...
(32’) Encouraging signs for the Hammers. This game might just go the way of the corresponding fixture last year.
(31’) SIDE-NETTING!! A great chance for West Ham to double their lead! Jarvis was the architect after surging into the West Brom box. He crossed it into Carlton Cole, whose header was met by no one, although Demel then latched onto the loose ball after a delay but fired into the wrong side of the net!
(30’) HE'S ALIVE! Anelka proves that he still exists, firing a shot away from 20 yards. It's blocked, though...
(28’) A win for the home side here would do wonders. Three points would move them out of the relegation zone and into 16th, level on points with their opponents today.
(27’) Jarvis now breaks but is stopped by Morrison. Mulumbu can't capitalise on having possession, though, with his pass going nowhere. Well, somewhere: off for a throw-in.
(26’) Tomkins, who came off earlier, looks to have suffered a groin injury. West Ham fans will hope he isn't out for an extended period.
(25’) OVER! Cole (Carlton) just manages to get himself on the end of the corner, though he is in a difficult position. As such, his header goes over the bar. A decent chance for the Hammers, nonetheless.
(24’) Noble himself takes the free kick and it's cleared for a corner. Another set-piece now, Jarvis to take...
(23’) West Ham clear and break up the pitch, with Mark Noble advancing and then being brought down by Mulumbu. Free kick to the hosts.
(22’) Berahino and Brunt link up well now, although Jonas Olsson ruins the move when he receives the ball and tries a 30-yard shot.
(20’) The visitors have imposed themselves well in certain areas. While West Ham perhaps look to provide the bigger goal threat (surprisingly) the Baggies do look like they can get back into this.
(18’) West Brom push forward, however... with Anelka playing Morrison through in the area. The midfielder then tries to neatly play Berahino in, though the ball floats straight to Jaaskelainen.
(16’) The hosts are becoming more and more comfortable in possession now. A game at home against fellow strugglers could be just the tonic Allardyce's side need.
(14’) Danger dealt with swiftly, however. West Ham can now look to calm play down and hold on to this 1-0 lead.
(12’) End-to-end football as West Ham break up the other end with Carlton Cole and Matthew Jarvis. The Hammers have no less than three chances on goal! They fail to capitalise and West Brom then take the ball back into the West Ham half. Saido Berahino's shot is then blocked for a corner.
(11’) The Baggies look to capitalise on the disruption in rhythm to West Ham's defence. A swift move sees a cross into the box blocked by a sliding Razvan Rat. Corner to the visitors.
(10’) Tomkins has indeed come off. Guy Demel is his replacement.
(9’) There's uncertainty as to whether he can continue...
(7’) Play has stopped here with a West Ham player down injured. There are worried faces on the bench. It's defender James Tomkins who is down.
(5’) So how can West Brom respond?

(3’) SIDE-NETTING! James Morrison gets a cross into Chris Brunt but he fires into the side-netting.
(2’) Nicolas Anelka gets a few touches for West Brom early on. He's making his return after a few weeks out. Yet to score for the Baggies is Anelka...
(1’) The West Ham faithful are in good voice, the bubbles are blowing in the air and we are off!
Baggies' caretaker boss Keith Downing will be hoping for much better today. We're just minutes away from kick-off, stay with us for all the action!

(79’) SUBSTITUTION FOR VILLA: Weimann makes way for Albrighton.
(78’) STAT ATTACK: Before today, Swansea had lost eight of their nine previous league trips to Villa Park, failing to score in all eight defeats. Their solitary win was by 2-0 on 2 January 2012.
(77’) YELLOW CARD FOR RANGEL - SWANSEA.
(76’) SAVE! Bony and Pozuelo both go for the same loose ball after some good work from Shelvey in the host's penalty area, but Guzan comes out to pluck the ball from the air.
(74’) Shelvey tries to gain control of a pass that is getting away from him but his technique is poor and rolls out of play for a throw-in, much to the ironic cheers of the Villa fans. Sums up this second half, if I'm honest.
(72’) OVER! Agbonglahor fires a wild shot over the bar. Villa fans are still looking frustrated in that Holte End.
(70’) SUBSTITUTION FOR VILLA: Bacuna comes off for El Ahmadi.
(69’) YELLOW CARD FOR BACUNA - ASTON VILLA.
(69’) These next 20 minutes may become very scrappy indeed. Villa are resorting to the long ball tactic.
(67’) SUBSTITUTION FOR SWANSEA. Pozuelo replaces goalscorer Lamah.
(65’) SHOT! The Villa Park faithful are roaring thier side forward as the hosts look to go ahead again in this match but Shelvey jangles some nerves with a deflected shot that is cleared by Baker.
(63’) There has certainly been a lack of chances in this half. Both teams surely cannot be happy with just a point?
(61’) SUBSTITUTE FOR VILLA. Kozak comes on for Tonev.
(59’) A rare counter attack from the hosts results in a very poor ball into the box from Weimann. This has not been a glittering performance again from the Midlanders.
(57’) Clarke blocks Lamah's cross and puts it out for a corner on the left-hand-side. Villa manage to get the ball away.
(55’) SUBSTITUTE FOR SWANSEA. Rangel comes on for Tiendalli.
(52’) TIPPED OVER! De Guzman lines a free-kick up from 30 yards and manages to draw a save from Guzan.
(50’) Paul Lambert is standing on the touchline with his arms crossed. There is still no real reaction from his side who need to probe the visitor's defence with more purpose.
(48’) The final ball is the only thing that has let down the Swans today as Hernandez overhits his cross to Bony and gives possession away.
(46’) Swansea get us back underway!
The teams are about to make their way back onto the pitch. Who will win this entertaining encounter?
HALFTIME - ASTON VILLA 1-1 SWANSEA. The Swans have been fantastic in this game and responded well following Agbonglahor's early strike - a goal that was totally against the run of play. A small chorus of boos emitts from the stands at the break as the Villa fans are clearly unhappy with their side's performance so far.
(45’) There will be ONE minute of added on time.
(43’) Shelvey is inches away from meeting with a fantastic Hernandez pass that would have seen him through on goal. Villa are rocking. What can Paul Lambert do at the break to inspire his side?
(41’) STAT ATTACK: Aston Villa have lost four successive league matches. They have not lost five games in a row since January 2001. (BBC Sport)
(39’) As we head towards the break all the action in the last few minutes has been in the Villa penalty area. Michael Laudrup will be pleased with how his side have not let their heads drop after that early goal - can they get another one before halftime?
(37’) SWANSEA BOOKING - LAMAH. The Belgian is booked for celebrating with the fans after that goal.
(36’) SWANSEA LEVEL IT! Lamah scores his first goal in the Premier League, meeting Hernandez' superb cross on the left and heading Swansea back into the game. To be fair, that has been coming!
(34’) CLOSE! Oh, it's inches wide from de Guzman. Baker's poor clearance falls to the Dutchman who slices it wide.
(32’) SAVE! Hernandez has switched sides and breaks into the box but he is a tad selfish and instead of squaring the ball to Bony he plants it right in the gloves of Guzan.
(30’) WIDE! Westwood nicks possession off a lazy touch from Canas and the midfielder tries to bend his shot in the top corner. Unfortunately for him, however, the ball ends up in the stands. Villa's attack is definitely waking up!
(29’) ANOTHER BLOCKED EFFORT! For this first time since the home side's goal, Weimann drives at the visitors with purpose but his long range strike hits Chico Flores and loops out for a throw-in.
(27’) BLOCKED! Lamah takes aim from 20 yards out but there are too many Villa shirts back defending their lead. The Swans continue to knock on the door!
(25’) STAT ATTACK: Swansea are enduring a four-match winless streak (D2, L2), their worst run of the season. (BBC Sport)
(22’) Swansea are really building the pressure with yet another corner. Guzan is fouled in the melee and the home defence can breathe a sigh of relief.
(20’) WHAT A CHANCE! Ben Davies has his head in his hands. A corner makes it's way to the left-back, whose free header bounces into the ground and over the bar. The Swans should be level!
(19’) Shelvey finds himself in space on the right flank and chooses to put the ball on his left foot to swing a cross in, but the youngster overhits it, much to the annoyance of teammate Bony.
(17’) CHANCE! Hernandez twists in the penalty area and manages to get a low shot away but Guzan smothers the effort.
(16’) Jonjo Shelvey makes a full-blooded challenge on Delph to put the ball out for a throw, and the midfielder almost in the stands!
(14’) Guzan has to be sharp off his line to mop up an intended through ball for de Guzman. Despite falling behind, it is the Swans who look like the better side!
(13’) STAT ATTACK: 33 - Gabriel Agbonlahor has now scored against 33 of the 34 teams he has faced in the PL, only not scoring v Crystal Palace (1 game). Angel. (OptaJoe)
(11’) The Villa faithful are right behind their team today as they applaud their first corner. It is sent in low but Weimann's flick is off target and a goal kick is awarded.
(9’) Michael Laudrup's charges come flooding forward to cancel out that early strike but Clarke and Baker stand firm against Bony, who fails to meet a de Guzman cross.
(7’) GOAL! Agbonglahor gives the home side the perfect start with a superb finish. Weimann slots the ball through to his captain who finishes low into the bottom corner from inside the area. The striker celebrates with the bench as Villa Park erupts!
(7’) It's the Swans who win the first corner of the game and a combination of Williams and Bony makes life difficult for Villa keeper Guzman, but the man between the sticks collects the loose ball.
(5’) Paul Lambert is looking slightly pensive in the dugout. How he will want to silence the boo-boys today with a win.
(3’) It is a really open start for both teams as an early delivery from Rodriguez is dealt with by the host's defence.
(1’) We are underway with Villa kicking from right to left.
The teams emerge out of the tunnel at an expectant Villa Park. Who will come out on top today?

Welcome to our coverage of this Premier League fixture between Aston Villa and Swansea. My name is Hayden Gribble and I shall take you through all of the action of today's crucial game. But first, let's get the team news...

(90’) FULL-TIME: Hull hit a stunned Fulham for six as they increase the Cottager's relegation fears while strengthening their position in mid table. All the goals came in the second period as Elmohamady, two from Koren, Boyd, Huddlestone and Fryatt secured a momentous win for Hull, while the visitors face an extremely long trip home after this humbling.
(90’) Huddlestone trots off the pitch despite Hull having no subs left and earns a standing ovation from each corner of the KC Stadium. He has been superb today.
(89’) Huddlestone sends in a corner from the left but Davies is adjudged to have fouled his marker and a free-kick is awarded to the visitors.
(86’) Huddlestone's lofted ball is exquisite and finds Boyd over the top of the abject Fulham defence but his low shot is wide of the target. Hull fans want more here.
(84’) GOAL! Hull have a sixth and it's Robert Koren who has his second after another lovely move. Rosenior is free on the right and locates Graham with a low cross. The striker's effort is parried by Stockdale quite poorly in truth and Koren is only too happy to roll the ball home into the other corner.
(81’) Fulham look content with damage limitation, stroking the ball around the back four with little harm on a rampant Hull side. The visitors cannot wait for the final whistle.
(79’) Fulham briefly rally as Rodallega tries to get off a shot but it cannons back to Zverotic, whose effort is high and wide.
(77’) Hull send on Paul McShane for the brilliant Elmohamady before Huddlestone once again elects to shoot from range at a dead ball situation and gets the ball on target from another 40-yard effort.
(75’) Hull fans jubilant, and so they ought to be with their side's efforts and are 'oohing' and 'ahhing' each pass the home side makes. Make no mistake about it, the home side have fully deserved their resounding advantage.
(73’) GOAL! Unbelievably Hull have a fifth. Huddlestone is the architect once again, this time firing in a free-kick from fully 40 yards which Stockdale can only parry straight into the path of substitute Fryatt, who is on hand to slam home the rebound.
(71’) Figueroa's cross is cut out after some lovely work down the left from the Honduran and Boyd.
(69’) Hull bring on Matty Fryatt amidst the celebrations of their fourth goal but Fulham respond when Zverotic's low strike has to be turned behind by McGregor in the Tigers stopper's first real save of the match.
(67’) GOAL! It's a fourth for Hull as Fulham allow Huddlestone - who has been outstanding today - the freedom of the edge of the area to collect, turn his marker and unleash a stinging effort low into the bottom corner past the stranded Stockdale. What a second half this has been for Hull.
(65’) Riise crosses low in from the left but substitute Bent is unable to get a telling touch ahead of Curtis Davies.
(63’) GOAL! It's a quickfire double for the hosts as Boyd makes it 3-0 to Hull! The winger collects Livermore's pass on the turn before slotting the ball unerringly into the far corner. Fulham respond by bringing on Darren Bent for Dejagah, but it's too little too late for the visitors now.
(60’) GOAL! And that should be that for Hull, who have a second through Koren. Sagbo does exceptionally once more and unselfishly sends in the perfect cross for the Slovenian to slot home into the top corner. Lovely finish to match a super cross.
(57’) Livermore escapes down the right but his cross is over-hit and sails over Koren, who had tried to make a run in towards the near post.
(55’) McGregor and Stockdale are able to claim two rather simple long balls downfield in quick succession before Rosenior fails to produce a testing enough cross for the Fulham backline.
(53’) Ruiz nods on a long goal kick from Stockdale but it goes straight through to opposite number McGregor in the Hull goal before Zverotic and Kasami fail to engineer an opportunity after working some space.
(51’) Hughes has to recover in the nick of time to deny Boyd from escaping in the left-hand side of the penalty area. Fulham completely all at sea at the back at the start of this second half.
(49’) GOAL! Elmohamady gives Hull the lead after some slack Fulham defending. Huddlestone's corner finally wreaks havoc in the away side's backline and, when the ball falls to the Egyptian, he slammed the ball into the top right-hand corner with the outside of his right foot. Game on.
(48’) Huddlestone is at the heart of things once more, freeing Sagbo, whose shot is parried by Stockdale but the keeper is up quick to block Koren's follow-up effort.
(47’) The ball falls to Huddlestone around 25 yards out and his technique is exquisite, zipping the ball towards goal but his effort flew inches wide of Stockdale's right-hand post. Close, but no cigar just yet for the birthday boy.
(46’) Both teams are out once more and Fulham get us back underway here.
HALF-TIME: We reach the interval all square at the KC Stadium, with neither side looking particularly willing to commit numbers going forwards. Hull have looked the most threatening, with Huddlestone's free-kick, which hit the post, the closest they have come while Boyd's effort had to be turned away by Stockdale - Fulham's most impressive individual.
(43’) Huddlestone lines one up from range but his shot possesses neither the power nor the accuracy to give Stockdale something to think about. The half is beginning to peter out somewhat.
(41’) Elmohamady tests his luck from out on the right with a couple of crosses but his first is easily blocked and the other is clutched by the commanding Stockdale.
(39’) It's gone a bit quiet from a Hull perspective in the last 10 minutes after the three key chances for Huddlestone, Boyd and Sagbo. Nonetheless, Steve Bruce will be happy with his side's efforts in this first half.
(37’) Both teams in need of some attacking inspiration as the two defences continue to hold firm. Rodallega and Dejagah link up nicely but the latter's speculative volley is way off target.
(35’) Replays suggest the officials were correct in not awarding a penalty as the ball hit Ruiz on the thigh. Huddlestone's latest attempt from a corner is a poor one and is flicked out of play for a goal kick.
(33’) Huddlestone's corner in prompts numerous handball shouts amongst the Hull faithful after the ball jumped up amidst a group of Fulham defenders. The visitors are dicing with death just now.
(31’) So, so close to the opener. Figueroa darts down the left and slips in the onrushing Sagbo, who claims possession and drills the ball goalwards. His shot beats Stockdale but also the post as the opener becomes more and more elusive.
(29’) Stockdale is called upon once more as he denies Elmohamady's low strike after Koren's own shot was blocked before the keeper claims a looping cross from the left courtesy of Boyd.
(27’) Fulham launch a rare counter attack but Ruiz is stopped when Boyd recovers well and tracks back to deny him after he had skipped clear of Figueroa.
(25’) A nice move involving Boyd and Livermore results in Sagbo getting away from the defence but the pass is too heavy and rolls too far in front of the lone frontman.
(23’) Hull are pegging their visitors back here and on this occasion Huddlestone's delivery is not quite up to scratch. Fulham are offering little going forward but Hull must press home their current dominance.
(21’) Fulham are struggling to get out at the moment. From the latest set piece, Huddlestone drills the ball under the wall and almost picks out Sagbo but the ball is ultimately cleared to safety. Karagounis then trips Boyd to offer the hosts another opportunity to get a good ball into the box.
(19’) Hull go close twice in quick succession as Huddlestone's free-kick crashes back off the post before Stockdale does extremely well to reach Boyd's downward effort and paw it aside.
(17’) Both sides are cancelling each other out at the moment, with plenty of long balls amounting to nothing.
(15’) Both sides are culpable of giving away possession in the early stages and dictate the play, with Robert Koren the latest guilty party after a heavy touch.
(13’) Huddlestone's devilish delivery from the left tests David Stockdale and his defence but Fulham were able to just about deal with the threat as Hull begin to find their stride in this clash.
(11’) Ashkan Dejagah is felled by Tom Huddlestone in midfield and wins a free-kick but Fulham do nothing with it. Hull seize the initiative and break upfield but Aaron Hughes does well to deal with the attentions of Boyd at the back post.
(9’) Boyd is in hard once again, this time on Elsad Zverotic, who is sent sprawling on the turf. Moments earlier Hugo Rodallega had been crowded out after being found on the edge of the area.
(7’) A lovely flowing move for the visitors produces the first meaningful chance of the contest as John Arne Riise fires in low at goal but is thwarted by a good save from Allan McGregor.
(5’) Hull have been physical in the opening exchanges, with George Boyd and Jake Livermore both going in hard. Giorgos Karagounis wins a free-kick midway inside their half for an over-zealous challenge.
(3’) Ahmed Elmohamady advances down the right and supplies a clever cross into Yannick Sagbo but the ball is just too high and the ball sails out for a throw in to Fulham on the opposite flank.
(1’) Hull kick us off and we are underway here at the KC Stadium.
The 35 league goals conceded by the Cottagers ranks as the worst in the top flight.
Despite Fulham's recent recovery, the west London outfit have actually lost eight of their last 10 league outings. Remarkably, they have performed better on the road than at home, with nine points from nine games on their travels and just seven from the same amount of home matches.
Although that did not impact on Hull's record of having one of the best home defences; the six goals in total is matched only by Arsenal, Manchester City, Liverpool and Stoke City.
A defence which had conceded just three times in the previous eight league games at the KC Stadium this season was undone, however, by Manchester United on Boxing Day, who notched three of their own in the 3-2 success.
Hull have won three of the four top-flight meetings between these two sides. The Tigers, however, have won none of their last five in the league (D3, L2).
And the Fulham line-up: Stockdale; Zverotic, Hughes, Amorebieta, Riise; Sidwell; Dejagah, Karagounis, Kasami, Ruiz; Rodallega. Substitutes: Bettinelli, Kacaniklic, Richardson, Boateng, Riether, David, Bent.
So then, the teams in full for you, starting with today's hosts Hull. McGregor; Rosenior, Davies, Chester, Figueroa; Huddlestone, Livermore; Elmohamady, Koren, Boyd; Sagbo. Substitutes: Harper, Bruce, Faye, McShane, Meyler, Fryatt, Graham.
Out go Sascha Riether, Kieran Richardson, Scott Parker, Damien Duff, Adel Taarabt and Alexander Kacaniklic and in come Elsad Zverotic, John Arne Riise, Giorgos Karagounis, Bryan Ruiz, Hugo Rodallega and Ashkan Dejagah.
Fulham manager Rene Meulensteen makes wholesale changes to his side, with over half of the side that won 2-1 at Norwich on Boxing Day dropping to the bench or the squad altogether.
The teams are in and both managers have made changes - three and six apiece to be precise - as they look to keep their squads fresh. Steve Bruce drafts in Liam Rosenior, Robert Koren and George Boyd as Alex Bruce, David Meyler and Danny Graham all make way.

FULL TIME - Man City 1-0 Crystal Palace: Maybe not the scoreline we were expecting but certainly the result that was predicted. The Citizens secure their 10th home win of the season and move back to the top of the league, though they can be displaced by Arsenal tomorrow. The Eagles were resilient and deserve credit for keeping the game so tight, but the extra quality of Pellegrini's side eventually told.
(90’) Speroni hits it long but Palace can do nothing with it as the referee blows his whistle for full time.
(90’) Nasri dances his way into the box but loses possession and in his haste to win it back he concedes a free kick.
(90’) Clichy releases Negredo down the right and as he tries to drag the ball back and move inside of Delaney he slips and handles it. Free kick to the visitors.
(90’) We are into the first of an additional three minutes.
(90’) CLOSE!! A counterattack is launched as Hart throws the ball up to Nasri. He switches the play to Navas on the right and his cross is somehow met by Dzeko from an extremely acute angle. The ball heads back towards goal but lands on the roof of the net.
(89’) Silva picks up a yellow card for a challenge on Williams. That rules him out of their visit to Swansea on New Year's Day.
(87’) Palace are putting an extra bit of effort in to close down their opponents quickly in these closing stages. Will they get another chance to try and find an equaliser?
(85’) Nasri attempts a give-and-go with Dzeko but the Bosnian's return pass is poor. A number of groans go up around the stadium, even though the striker may well be the scorer of the winning goal!
(84’) City are still playing in a very patient fashion and do not appear to be in a rush to try and add to their tally.
(81’) Palace make their final change as Gayle, the hero at Villa Park on Thursday, replaces Bannan.
(81’) Delaney catches Navas with a high boot and can have no complaints as he is shown the first yellow card of the game.
(79’) City have enjoyed 80% of possession this half. They will feel it is a huge injustice if they somehow fail to take all three points this afternoon.
(78’) Kolarov plays a one-two with Nasri and whips in a brilliant early cross for Dzeko. The Bosnian attempts to send a header past Speroni from just inside the area but the keeper holds it comfortably.
(78’) You have to give Palace their dues today, they have defended stoicly. And even though Dzeko has put that goal past them, they have remained well-drilled and disciplined. It is a credit to the impact that Tony Pulis has had since taking the helm at Selhurst Park.
(76’) Williams comes on to replace Bolasie for the hosts. The wide man has done plenty of running for the Eagles today.
(75’) Kolarov comes on for Milner and so Clichy moves over to right-back, the third different player in that position for City this afternoon.
(74’) Negredo puts in a great challenge on Jedinak but gets a flailing boot to the face for his troubles. The referee stops play but the Spaniard looks to be fine.
(72’) Parr has been tireless on that left flank but once more his delivery lets him down. This time, it goes straight into the arms of Hart who is unchallenged.
(70’) The last time Palace beat City was in the 2001-02 season and both sides were in the second tier of English football. It is going to take something very special for them to pick up three points today, though.
(68’) WARD!! What a chance! The makeshift midfielder met the resultant corner, unmarked, at the back post, but he was unable to guide his effort on target.
(67’) WHAT A SAVE!! Ward has a pop from distance and it looks to be bouncing towards the bottom corner but the keeper gets down to his left and gets a crucial hand to the ball.
(66’) GOOOOOAAAL!! DZEKO FINALLY GETS THE GOAL! Nasri's delivery only finds the head of Delaney but Navas picks up the loose ball at the back post. He looks up and spots Dzeko on the penalty spot and the striker guides a shot past Speroni and into the corner.
(64’) GOOD SAVE!! A short corner is worked to Jedinak and the Palace captain looses an effort at goal from distance. It might have taken a slight deflection but Hart has to leap up and push it over the roof of his net.
(63’) Vital clearance! Bannan's poor touch ended up falling nicely for Chamakh and the midfielder continued his run beyond the striker. A lofted pass looked to have put him through on goal but Clichy made a crucial interception.
(62’) SO CLOSE!! Puncheon provides the danger again as he is allowed to waltz towards the City goal and put the ball onto his favoured left foot. He attempts to bend his shot into the far corner and only narrowly misses out on finding it. Cracking effort.
(61’) Excellent chasing from Navas as he tracks Puncheon all the way back into his own half as the Palace man looked to initiate a counterattack.
(60’) Navas dribbles all the way over from right to left and slips a pass into Negredo. The striker is unable to get his shot away but manages to put the ball into the danger area, however, no one can tuck home from the ensuing scramble.
(58’) A Palace corner is wasted as Bolasie's delivery fails to beat the first man. The Eagles will need to make the most of those kinds of opportunities.
(57’) STAT: Negredo has scored in each of his previous nine appearances in all competitions at the Etihad Stadium. Pellegrini will want him to make that 10 this afternoon.
(55’) Attacking changes from Pellegrini as Negredo and Nasri come on for Boyata and Fernandinho. Milner or Garcia will now move into the right-back position.
(54’) Fernandinho tries to pick out Dzeko with a driven pass into the box but he is unable to do so. That may be his last action of the half.
(53’) City win another corner as Mariappa gets in the way of Milner's cross. It looks as though Pellegrini has seen enough as Negredo and Nasri will be on in a matter of moments.
(51’) CLOSE! The resultant corner is pinged in by Bannan and Chamakh manages to connect with it eight yards out from goal. He is moving away from the target and therefore fails to keep his header down and it flies over the top.
(50’) Great play from Puncheon! The winger span Clichy and then skipped past Garcia as he came in from the right. He thumped a low shot towards goal but Hart got down to it and parried the attempt aside.
(50’) Kompany brings the ball up from the back and finds himself in space to shoot inside the box. Yet once again there is no route through the swathe of Palace shirts in the area.
(49’) It is every man behind the ball for Palace now, with Chamakh dropping back into his side's own final third to try and limit the space and time offered to the hosts.
(47’) The second half begins just as the first did! Silva finding space to play a penetrating, vertical pass which Dzeko controls on the edge of the box. He slips the ball out to Milner on the right but his drilled cross is knocked behind by Gabbidon.
(46’) Man City get the ball rolling for the second half.
Welcome back! The second half will be underway shortly. Can City finally break the deadlock or will Palace be the first side to leave the Etihad with a point this season?
HALF TIME - Man City 0-0 Crystal Palace: The Citizens have been in complete control this afternoon but as of yet have been unable to find a way through Tony Pulis' resilient side. City's 100% home record could well be under threat, but they have plenty of attacking talent available on the bench. Join me for the second half in 10 minutes.
(45’) The half-time whistle goes.
(45’) Another effort from Fernandinho following a swift break from the hosts but Gabiddon gets his body in the way of it once more. Palace are proving very resolute this afternoon.
(45’) GREAT SAVE!! Milner and Navas have switched flanks here so it is the former who sends an in-swinger in from the near side. It finds the head of Fernandinho but Speroni gets a hand to his looping header to send it behind.
(45’) We are into the first of five added minutes.
(45’) That could have been a howler! Bannan's corner is not dealt with by Hart but he gets just enough on it to take it away from the incoming head of Bolasie.
(44’) SO CLOSE!! Silva attempts to find Dzeko in the box but Gabbidon gets a touch to it. The loose ball falls to Fernandinho and he lifts it over Mariappa before volleying at Speroni's goal. His technique is good but he sends his shot over the top.
(42’) Another nice move from City down the left but once more the cross into the box is cut out. Dzeko's movement has not been as bright in the latter stages of this half.
(40’) Exquisite from Silva! A brilliant pass from Boyata played the Spaniard in behind and he did excellent to keep it in play and beat Bannan. He could have squared the ball across goal but instead went for goal and blazed an effort high and wide.
(40’) Navas whips in a corner but it is headed straight back to him by the opposing defence. He drills in another low delivery and this time Bolasie deals with it.
(38’) Boyata catches Mariappa as he attempts an ambitious overhead kick inside the penalty area. Jedinak is furious with it and receives a talking to from the referee regarding that reaction.
(37’) Silva again finds space in order to pick out a tidy pass and he nearly plays Navas in by the byeline but Parr makes a crucial interception.
(35’) Chamakh finally gets himself ready and now comes on to replace Jerome.
(33’) Play resumes after that short break. Hart is left squinting on his line but will no doubt get some more treatment during the break.
(32’) That is a nasty cut which Hart has under his eye, but he was extremely brave there. Jerome had already picked up a knock this afternoon and will not be able to continue.
(31’) Both Hart and Jerome are receiving medical treatment on the pitch at the moment so we have a break in play.
(30’) OUCH! Hart comes out to collect a low cross from Parr and he beats Jerome to the ball. The Palace striker had every reason to go for it, but his foot clearly caught the keeper in the head.
(29’) Important clearance from Nastasic as he hooks away a cross into the box which Jerome was looking to get on the end of.
(28’) City break well and Silva is played in down the left. He fires a shot on goal but yet again there is a deflection which stops it from hitting the target.
(28’) Comfortable save for Hart as Bolasie's back-post volley bounces into his hand, though Jerome was chasing up to get a touch on it. Some anxious signs starting to filter down from the crowd now.
(26’) Good defending from Gabbidon. He came across to beat Dzeko to the ball and then playing it off the Bosnian striker to win his side a goal kick.
(24’) JUST WIDE!! Milner manages to dig out a shot from the far corner of the box but a slight nick off of a Palace shirt sends it behind for a corner. City have had over 70 per cent possession so far today.
(23’) That could have gone horribly wrong for Palace! Kompany's drive shot from 25 yards took a deflection on its way to goal but it did not require Speroni to adjust his position too much and he held the ball.
(22’) The Citizens are playing some great football here. Moments after Dzeko latches onto Boyata's pass but sees his shot blocked by Bannan after beating Delaney, City move the ball out to the left. Clichy sends a deep cross in for Dzeko and his header is deflected behind off of Delaney.
(21’) OVER THE TOP!! City switch the play well and Clichy cuts a pass back to Milner on the top of the box. He attempts to curl a left-footed effort into the top corner but he is unable to keep his shot down.
(20’) Slight claims for a penalty as Jedinak flattens Milner when challenging for an aerial ball. The referee sees nothing in it and awards the hosts a corner instead.
(19’) Bannan takes it short, passing out to Parr on the left. The defender takes on Navas and gets into space by the byeline to put his ball into the box, but instead he sends it straight out of play.
(18’) Bolasie breaks at pace, this time through the centre, and Nastasic brings him to ground with a clumsy challenge. What will the visitors make of this?
(17’) STAT: Tony Pulis has guided the Eagles to three wins during his first six games in charge, a run which has seen them rise out of the relegation zone. They look well-organised this afternoon, limiting City largely to shots from distance.
(15’) BOLASIE!! Wide of the target! Palace are refusing to rush when in possession but still show a willingness to get forward. After brilliant diagonal pass out to Bolasie, Parr's overlapping run enables the winger to cut inside. He fires a shot towards Hart's goal but does not manage to work the keeper.
(14’) Jerome went down after stretching to get on Jedinak's pass. Palace kick the ball out of play but the striker gets back to his feet. Maybe something for Pulis to keep his eye on from now.
(13’) It is all City at the moment. Navas comes inside to try and get in on the act too, but he runs into a Jedinak-shaped wall and is dispossessed.
(12’) Bolasie has only had a couple of chances to stretch his legs so far this afternoon but he does well there, cutting inside of Boyata and hooking a cross to the far post. He puts a bit too much on it, though, and the ball bounces out of play for a goal kick.
(11’) CLOSE!! Fernandinho runs into space along the top of the box and tees up Silva, just over 20 yards from goal. He drilled a left-footed effort towards the bottom corner but he was unable to find the target.
(10’) Palace are barely able to get the ball out of their half at the moment. They manage it temporarily but Jerome is unable to hold up the play and await support.
(8’) The corner is deflected behind and City get another chance to deliver the ball from the same side. It just won't sit down for a blue shirt inside the area, though, and Navas' effort from outside the box fails to find a route through the host of bodies still in there.

(2’) Fernandinho clips a nice ball over the top of the defence which Clichy runs onto down on the left. He attempts to hit a cutback into the centre of the box but Mariappa cuts it out and clears the danger.

The teams are out on the pitch and the second half will be underway in just a few moments.

The Citizens have won all nine of their previous home games this season, scoring 37 and conceding just six in the process. Palace, meanwhile, have only netted five times on their travels. Hello and welcome to this afternoon's LIVE commentary on the Premier League encounter between free-scoring Manchester City and the resurgent Crystal Palace. Meanwhile, a win for Manchester United moves them into a tie with Moyes' former club, Everton, who play host to Southampton on Sunday.
FULL TIME: NORWICH CITY 0-1 MANCHESTER UNITED The Red Devils win their fourth straight league game for the first time under David Moyes, and improve their unbeaten run on the road to 11 matches thanks to substitute Danny Welbeck's second half winner. It was hardly convincing from the visitors, but it's another solid road effort put in by the men in red. Norwich will rue missed opportunities in the first half, but seemed to tire as the match went on. A date with Crystal Palace awaits the Canaries on New Year's Day, as they inch ever closer to crisis mode!
(90’) PHIL DOWD BLOWS THE WHISTLE! That will do it here at Carrow Road! It wasn't pretty, but Manchester United do enough to claim all three points and keep the pressure on the top four.
(90’) The cross is dealt with quite easily, and that will surely be it now!
(90’) LAST CHANCE FOR NORWICH! Murphy and Smalling battling down the left and Murphy wins a free kick from the side of the box. Last chance here!
(90’) Norwich having no success getting the ball forward, as they turn it over yet again and United push forward again and win a corner. They'll play it short again, surely.
(90’) The Red Devils back on the ball, and Nathan Redmond concedes a free kick just outside the box for his tackle on Patrice Evra, and is shown a rather harsh yellow card by Phil Dowd, who hasn't tolerated any nonsense today.
(90’) Norwich finally win back possession deep in their own end, and they'll have four minutes of added time to salvage something from the match.
(89’) And now a corner for United. They will be in no rush to take this. Meanwhile, Johan Elmander comes on as the final substitution for Norwich in place of Wes Hoolahan.
(87’) United keeping possession down by the corner flag, and earn themselves a throw which elicits a roar from the traveling supporters.
(86’) The experienced Darren Fletcher is making his return now, as he's brought on for Javier Hernandez to try and milk the final minutes off the clock.
(84’) Now Evra is down clutching his head after a collision, perhaps wasting a bit more time for the visitors.
(83’) Finally a shot for Norwich. The ball is served up for Murphy who hits his effort with great confidence, but it flies over. It would have required something special to score from there.
(82’) You can see why the Red Devils haven't been beaten on the road in ten matches. It may not be pretty, but it doesn't have to be. They're keeping the ball and frustrating the opposition. Time is quickly dwindling down for Norwich.
(80’) Norwich pressuring the United ball carriers as much as possible. They're finding ways to win the ball back, now it's a matter of doing something with it.
(79’) Another substitution for Norwich, as the 18-year-old Josh Murphy is brought on for Robert Snodgrass. Ten minutes left for the hosts to find an equalizer.
(77’) Norwich beginning to get a bit frustrated here. They're struggling to break through this United defence, and the space they were finding down the flanks in the first half has all of a sudden disappeared.
(75’) STAT ATTACK: The Canaries have picked up just five points from a possible 15 so far in December.
(73’) APPEALS FOR A PENALTY!! Hoolahan is brought down in the box by Evra and immediately players calling for a penalty. Phil Dowd says no, however, much to the dismay of the Norwich players.
(71’) Interesting. Sounds like Hooper picked up an injury to his left hamstring. I didn't see anything, but that's the word from the Norwich sidelines.
(70’) Meanwhile, it's Kagawa who makes way for Januzaj as Moyes looks to hold onto this lead.
(69’) Wow, an interesting substitution from Norwich. It's their leading goalscorer Gary Hooper who makes way for Ricky van Wolfswinkel. With a New Year's Day fixture against Crystal Palace, perhaps Hughton wants to preserve his star striker as much as possible for what could be a six point fixture coming up.
(68’) HERNANDEZ! The ball is passed into the feet of the Mexican, who lets fire from outside the box. His shot is stopped easily by Ruddy.
(66’) Hoolahan concedes a free kick now to United, much to the dismay of the home fans. The ball is played back and United content on passing it around, forcing Norwich to come at them.
(65’) The Welbeck goal has breathed the life out of the match. Norwich are hesitant to press to early and leave themselves vulnerable at the back, while United are content with passing it around and slowing the pace of the match down to a stand still.
(63’) STAT ATTACK: The Red Devils have not lost away from home in any competition since they were beaten by Manchester City 4-1 in September - a run of ten games (six wins, four draws)
(61’) United enjoying possession now. They look a completely different team than that in the first half.
(59’) Hughton's hand might be forced now, as he will likely have to bring on a second striker with his team trailing.
(58’) Welbeck continues to create havoc moments after scoring! He bolts through the midfield and Bennett is forced to take him down, resulting in a yellow card for the defender.
(56’) GOAAAAAAAAAAL!!! WELBECK! An inspired substitution from David Moyes! He dances by two Norwich players before a heavy touch falls to Bennett, but he blasts the clearance right at Welbeck and he's able to break in, round the keeper and slot home for United. It was a fortunate bounce for Welbeck, but some suspect defending from Norwich. Ruddy absolutely livid!
(54’) After a cracking start to the second half, the teams have both settled in now and the pace has slowed a bit. Both teams still looking to press forward in numbers when in possession.
(52’) Ashley Young playing on the ball with real confidence now. He gets into space again but this time his cross is poor, resulting in a goal kick.
(50’) We're getting dearly close to an opening goal here! You can feel it coming, the crowd is absolutely buzzing! Fantastic stuff.
(49’) REDMOND NOW!! What a start to the half! This time Norwich break and Redmond is found in space inside the box. He gets a shot off that beats De Gea but sails inches wide of the far post!
(48’) YOUNG! He's looked very lively to start this second half! Here he is running at defenders and gets a shot off, but it sails just over.
(47’) Finally some life from United! Young delivers a beautiful ball in, finding Kagawa at the far post but he can't chest it down and it's blown dead for a handball. Kagawa really should have done better there.
(46’) The second half is underway! Moyes doesn't wait any longer to make a change as Danny Welbeck comes on for Ryan Giggs. Let's see if Welbeck can breathe life into the team in the second half.
Hughton on the other hand will like what he saw from his team in the first half, and has Elmander and van Wolfswinkel at his disposal if he decides to go for it. There is a strong possibility that he will not want to wait as long as possible to tamper with the team, however, and can you really blame him?
You wonder how much longer it will be until Moyes decides to make a change. Injuries have dealt United quite a blow, and perhaps an underwhelming performance was to be expected early on with all the changes to the starting XI. The Red Devils will likely regroup at the interval, but barring a drastic improvement in their performance, expect the introduction of Januzaj, Welbeck or Zaha after 10-15 minutes.
Shots in the first half were Norwich City 11, Manchester United 3. Clearly a gulf in class between the two teams after the opening 45.
HALF-TIME: NORWICH CITY 0-0 MANCHESTER UNITED A fine performance from Norwich City, who have really taken the game over. They will take pride in their performance from that first half, but will perhaps be concerned that they have nothing to show for it. Still, a very poor showing from the visitors who are desperately missing the services of Wayne Rooney and Antonio Valencia. Luckily for them, they remain tied after being outplayed for 45 minutes. Still everything to play for in the second half.
(45’) That's the last of the first half action as the whistle blows and it's a bit of relief for Manchester United who can get into the room and regroup.
(45’) United can hardly keep the ball for more than 30 seconds! Another turnover, and Martin breaks down the right, beats Evra easily, and pulls it back for Snodgrass who fires wide.
(45’) Chance for Norwich!! They pass the ball into the box nicely, but can't come up with a shot on target. Pressure stays on as they win a corner, but it's cleared yet again by United.
(45’) Ashley Young now with a shot for United. It was never going in, but still a sign of life here from the Red Devils in the closing moments of the first half.
(44’) STAT ATTACK: Manchester United have won five straight matches in all competitions, for the first time under David Moyes.
(43’) Corner for Norwich again now! They've had plenty this half, but like all the others, the header is won by United and cleared. Evans looks to have gotten the worse end of a collision there and the medical staff comes out to check on him.
(41’) Hernandez gets behind the two center backs but he's ruled offside. Silly mistake there as he just mistimes his run. Could have been easily avoided. Meanwhile, Ashley Young is hobbling and looks to have maybe picked up a knock. We'll how long he carries on.
(39’) END TO END STUFF HERE!! Hoolahan dances his way into the box and gets into a glorious area but his shot is blocked by Evans! Real scoring chance for Norwich! United break the other way and Kagawa gets the first shot on target for them, although it never really bothered Ruddy.
(37’) United finally with a bit of pressure of their own, resulting in a Giggs effort that's sent miles over the target. The visitors are still without a shot on target, as Kagawa's earlier ball was counted as a cross. They're missing Rooney desperately right now.
(36’) Redmond attacks Smalling now down the left and wins another corner for Norwich. The corner results in an attempt on goal, but it's hit straight into the waiting arms of De Gea.
(35’) Free kick is cleared easily and Young breaks out down the left. His ball for Kagawa is poor and Norwich are back in possession yet again!
(34’) Phil Dowd is trying to keep control over this game, as Hernandez is shown yellow now and Snodgrass with another opportunity to cross the ball in from a free kick.
(32’) Fer is shown yellow now for a tackle on Evra. Based on the replay it looks like there was very little contact there, if any. The Frenchman went down quite easily.
(30’) Despite a surge from Norwich, the visitors are still enjoying almost 65% possession, which is quite surprising actually. Norwich have been the better team so far you would have to say.
(29’) Hoolahan tries his luck from about 40? 50? yards out. Real hopeful from the midfielder, De Gea waits and collects.
(28’) Norwich upping the pressure! Snodgrass crosses it in three times in succession, but some good defending in the box from United prevents any real scoring chances. Still, the visitors have taken a back seat in the last 10 minutes.
(26’) Snodgrass causing all kinds of trouble here for the United defence. He tries to hurdle Giggs, but is toppled over, winning a free kick in a very dangerous area and resulting in a yellow card for the Welshman.
(24’) Norwich attacking Evra now down the right flank with plenty of success. Snodgrass has his cross turned aside and it's another corner for the hosts.
(23’) Snodgrass finds some space at the top of the box, but his left-footed effort never came close to finding the target and United finally back in possession.
(22’) HOOPER!! Again Norwich come so close to the opener!! Martin plays a low cross right to the feet of Hooper who smacks his shot straight at De Gea! United playing on the back foot here!
(21’) The Canaries playing with some confidence now enjoying some possession of their own.
(19’) Now a free kick for Nowrich from about 35 yards out. Snodgrass whips it into a dangerous area, it's cleared by Vidic right back to the feet of Snodgrass who blasts his volley well over the bar.
(18’) That was really a fine save from De Gea. It's shocking how cleanly Evra got beat by Martin. He was caught flat footed and it nearly resulted in the opening goal for Norwich.
(16’) Two corners in succession for Norwich who keep the pressure on the United back four! Nothing comes of it, however, and the visitors finally clear the danger.
(14’) NEARLY AN OPENER FOR NORWICH!! It should really be 1-0!! De Gea makes a fine save on Martin who blew by Evra, and Hoolahan can't quite get a touch on the rebound as it's turned out for a corner.
(13’) The Red Devils have enjoyed over 75% possession in the early stages, but only one real chance to show for it. Norwich are doing a good job of pressing the United midfielders and forcing plenty of negative build-up early on here.
(12’) STAT ATTACK: Only Fulham have conceded more than the 31 league goals Norwich have let in this season.
(10’) Norwich are trying to press up the pitch as much as possible, despite not having much possession early on. That should result in plenty of space for Kagawa and Hernandez who have looked sharp early on.
(7’) We have a bit of a coming together here between Vidic and Hooper! The striker rides the back of the defender, who wins a free kick right up against the by-line. (6’) FIRST CHANCE UNITED!! The ball falls nicely for Kagawa who tests Ruddy with his half-volley, but the keeper is up to the task and Norwich break the other way...
(5’) United passing the ball well early on, with players making some nice runs off the ball.
(3’) The pressure will fall on the shoulders of Shinji Kagawa today in the absence of Wayne Rooney. He scored a hat-trick against Norwich at Old Trafford in March of last season.
(2’) The Norwich fans singing loud and proud in the early stages here! It really makes for a great atmosphere.
(1’) Some fireworks less than 30 seconds in as Hernandez is bundled over by Ryan Bennett, and takes a hard fall on the gravel that lines the pitch.
(1’) And we're underway at Carrow road as Manchester United get it started, moving right to left.
The players have taken the pitch and the match is about to start!
Norwich will come into the match with some confidence having won two of three meetings against Manchester United all-time in the Premier League, however, the away team's recent form will have to be a concern for Chris Hughton.
Chris Hughton has made a few changes to his line-up as well after their midweek loss to Fulham. Russell Martin and Ryan Bennett start in place of Steven Whittaker and Michael Turner, who picked up a suspension after accumulating too many yellow cards. Johan Elmander also takes a seat on the bench with Wes Hoolahan taking his place behind Gary Hooper.

Rafael and Valencia are also out after picking up an injury and suspension respectively midweek against Hull. Vidic returns for them, with Smalling slotting over to right-back, while Michael Carrick starts for the first time since November 10th.
MANCHESTER UNITED XI (4-4-1-1): De Gea; Smalling, Evans, Vidic, Evra; Young, Cleverley, Carrick, Giggs; Kagawa; Hernandez. SUBS: Anderson, Lindegaard, Welbeck, Fabio, Fletcher, Zaha, Januzaj

After a horrid start to the season, Hughton's side managed eight points from their five league matches heading into Christmas, but a loss at home to relegation candidates Fulham has them ready to press the panic button. A result today would go a long way in boosting the team's confidence heading into the New Year.
The home side comes into this game with a very different view of the table. They sit three places out of the relegation zone, but a bad day can see them drop into the bottom three. Chris Hughton has come under a lot of pressure again after falling 2-1 to Fulham midweek. The Canaries have now lost three home matches this season, after losing just one in the second half of last season. Carrow Road will have to return to the fortress it proved to be last season if Norwich want to avoid a long and stressful 2014.
The Red Devils fell 1-0 last season at this same venue, thanks to a second half goal from Andy Pilkington, but Moyes has his men back to their old ways, winning five straight in all competitions, after failing to win any of their first three league matches in December.
David Moyes has the Red Devils back on track at the moment, and the attack is firing on all cylinders. Manchester United looked eerily similar to last year's championship team as they battled back from 2-0 down to win 3-2 at Hull City on Boxing Day as they did so many times last season. They will be desperate to pick up maximum points from today's fixture as they look to make up ground on the top four after an unconvincing start to the month.

Full-time and, somehow, it's 2-2 at the Cardiff City Stadium! Cardiff have committed the cardinal sin of not killing a game off that was theirs for the taking here. They dropped deeper and deeper during the last few minutes and paid the price after Jack Colback's late equaliser for Sunderland. A point does nothing for either side but credit to the Black Cats for a strong finish to an otherwise poor game for them. Vincent Tan left the stands as soon as he could. So did thousands of Cardiff fans.

Jordan Mutch's goal is the difference at the Cardiff City Stadium, where the home side lead Sunderland 1-0 after a thoroughly impressive half. The Black Cats are still in this, although they shouldn't be with the amount of chances Cardiff have enjoyed.

(27’) CHANCE! But Noone, Mutch and Campbell combine once again as Cardiff almost double their lead! Campbell it is who fires the header away eventually, though it is a couple of yards wide.
(26’) Sunderland almost have some joy on the counterattack once again, however.
(24’) The Cardiff fans have unveiled a banner of support for Malky Mackay! The stewards who have tried to confiscate it from them have promptly been sent for a wild goose chase. As they attempt to remove it, it is thrown from one fan to another, with the stewards eventually giving up.
(22’) CHANCE! Campbell has a shot but it is Steven Caulker who gets the final touch to it, forcing Mannone into action with a header.
(20’) Fabio Borini and Phil Bardsley combine, however, for a rare attacking move for Sunderland. It comes to nothing but it does serve as a reminder that Cardiff need more than just the one goal to seal the deal here.
--- 19’ Yellow card L. Cattermole is cautioned by the referee. ---
(19’) Classic Lee Cattermole. The Sunderland midfielder lunges in at Mutch and earns himself a yellow card with a poor challenge. How many is that in his career now?
(16’) More pressure sees Fraizer Campbell get involved in the action and things do not look good for Sunderland here.
(14’) A win could take Cardiff as high as 14th here, while a Sunderland comeback could take them out of the relegation zone. Only one of those outcomes looks likely at the moment, however...
(13’) JUST OVER! Superb play from Kim Bo-Kyung, as he forces Vito Mannone into a save with a super strike from range. Unrelenting from Cardiff here.
(11’) The Black Cats have barely had a sniff here so far. Might Gus Poyet be pondering changes already?
(9’) A superb opening from Cardiff at the moment. Mutch, Noone and Whittingham have been absolutely terrorising the Sunderland defence.
(7’) GOAL! It's there - and it's Mutch who converts his fourth goal of the season. The Cardiff man picked the ball up 25 yards from goal and surged unstoppably towards the Sunderland defence. When he unleashed his strike, it took a heavy deflection, but Bluebirds fans won't care one bit. What a start. A deserved lead for Cardiff.
--- 6’ Assist Assist by F. Campbell. ---
--- 6’ Goal! Cardiff City score a goal through J. Mutch! ---
(6’) HEADER! Peter Whittingham now comes close for the hosts, heading wide after a great run and cross from Craig Noone down the flank.
(4’) It has been a good start from Cardiff so far, with the Bluebirds making several advances into the Sunderland box already. Are they playing in honour of former manager Malky Mackay?
(3’) DIVE! Jordan Mutch's first real action of the game is to be booked for a dive. Valentin Roberge was the Sunderland defender involved, attempting a half-hearted challenge - certainly not enough to send Mutch flying to the ground like he did.
--- 2’ Yellow card J. Mutch is yellow-carded. ---
(1’) We're off at the Cardiff City Stadium!
How will managerless Cardiff get on in their first game without Malky Mackay, then? Kick-off is just a few minutes away, so we'll find out! Also keep an eye out on any "Tan Out" protests...

Good evening and welcome to live-text commentary of Cardiff against Sunderland! I'm your host Tim Poole and I'll be guiding you through the action.
