(57’) Arsenal continue to fail to penetrate the resilient Chelsea lines, as their attacks are pushed ever wider with worrying frequency. With the likes of Ozil forced out towards the touchline, the hosts don't look like doing any damage, unless a player takes a couple of defenders out of the game with a moment of inspiration.
(55’) HAZARD! Chelsea break dangerously, as Ivanovic finds Willian with an excellent transitory pass. The Brazilian bursts down the right flank under no pressure, before finding Hazard at the back post unmarked. The Belgian forces his way into the area, before being muscled off the ball by Arteta.
(53’) The tempo continues to be rather slow, with the fear of conceding appearing to outweigh any desire to find the breakthrough goal. A defeat would do much more damage to either side's title aspirations than not finding the winning goal, which is perhaps leading to this very cagey evening of football.
(51’) ROSICKY! Excellent play from the veteran midfielder! He exchanges passes brilliantly with Giroud, before bursting to the edge of the penalty area and seeing his eventual strike blocked! That's more of the creativity we want to see!
(49’) The atmosphere remains rather flat, as the rain continues to pummel down in London. Chelsea's centre-halves split, allowing for them to build from the back, and Arsenal are in absolutely no rush to close them down. It seems that both Wenger and Mourinho would take a point.
(47’) Just to remind you all of the significance of this game, Chelsea could go joint-top with a win here tonight, with Arsenal able to regain top spot with the same result. Arsene Wenger is late returning to his bench, whilst struggling to do up his zip, as always.
(46’) We're back underway in the second half, and let us hope for some goals! Chelsea have frustrated Arsenal well in the first 45 minutes, but will inevitably want to try to steal the three points which would put them right back in the title race heading into 2014. Arsenal have looked low on ideas, despite keeping the ball well in the opening stages.
Not quite the game that we expected from two teams boasting plenty of midfield and offensive quality, but there's still 45 minutes left to play. Willian has looked reasonably bright whenever he's been on the ball, with Hazard yet to really get involved. Giroud and Ozil have been too anonymous for Arsenal to have any staying power in the final third.
Vermaelen has looked a potential weak link for the home side, who settled into the game well, before petering out after the 20-minute mark. Chelsea have been well disciplined and sat smartly in their shape, committing men forward as quickly as possible once they have won possession.
Frank Lampard hitting the underside of the crossbar with a cushioned instep volley, is the closest that we've gone thus far. Szczesny has been forced into two comfortable stops to deny Torres and Willian, with Cech having very little to do in the opposite goal. The hosts appear unable to deal with the rather slick turf, misplacing plenty of passes.
HALF TIME! It ends goalless after a rather cagey first 45 minutes, where Mourinho's Chelsea have dealt with everything that Arsenal have thrown at them. Arsenal will feel aggrieved that they haven't been awarded a penalty following a trip on Walcott.
(45’) OZIL! Cahill gets in front of a firm half volley from the Germany international, as Chelsea continue to frustrate the hosts in this first half. Mourinho's side look to have the measure of their opposition.
(44’) WILLIAN! Great header from Ivanovic! Chelsea continue to weather the storm of a few Arsenal corners in quick succession, before breaking upfield with pace. The Brazilian is found in space on the left, before cutting inside and firing a comfortable strike into the waiting hands of Szczesny.
(42’) A good defensive header from Mikel prevents Mertesacker from meeting an Arsenal corner delivery, before Ozil is penalised for being offside. The former Real Madrid man looking to head the ball away from the flapping grasp of Cech, but was slightly beyond the visitors' last defender.
(40’) Five minutes until the break, and this game is in desperate need of a goal to force it into action. Arsenal continue to patiently probe, with Chelsea prepared to sit in shape and look to pick off their opponents on the counter. We're yet to see much of Hazard, however, whose involvement could prove key.
(39’) Chelsea are perhaps lucky to have eleven men still on the field, as Mikel's challenge on Arteta doesn't get any better after further viewing. Walcott could have easily picked up a penalty for the Gunners too, so it's no surprise to hear the home support chanting about the referee's decision-making.
(37’) Arteta is forced to pick himself up gingerly after being caught by a strong challenge from Mikel, after Arsenal fans claimed for a trip on Walcott by Azpilicueta inside the Chelsea penalty area. Things aren't quite going in favour of the hosts at the moment, who are second-best in this game despite seeing plenty of the ball.
(36’) Chelsea are beginning to look more confident by the minute, as Arsenal's possession continues to come to nothing. Lampard's strike has been the best chance of the game thus far, and the visitors' pressing is doing just enough to knock Wenger's men out of their stride.
(34’) TORRES! Szczesny is finally forced into a save, comfortably diving to his right to catch a strike which Torres hit on the turn. Moments later, the Spaniard is fed in behind the Arsenal defence, but an excellent sliding tackle from Mertesacker blocks his second effort.
(32’) LAMPARD! The England international cracks a brilliant effort off the underside of the bar, with Szczesny stood helpless, after a rather hopeful lofted ball towards the back post. That could be the warning shot that this game needs to kick-start it!
(31’) Just over ten minutes until half time, and this London derby is yet to burst into life. Neither goalkeeper has been tested, and the majority of long balls have been ineffectual due to their tendency to skid out of play courtesy of the recent weather.
(29’) Header away by Mertesacker! Willian does well to dance around a few Arsenal players, but is continually forced wide, until he eventually releases the ball to Azpilicueta, whose cross isn't good enough to find Torres. Chelsea are being forced to go long on occasion, given that Willian and Hazard are finding it difficult to find themselves in positions where they can either isolate their full-back or have a man to aim for in the box.
(27’) RAMIRES! The Brazilian finds himself on the edge of the 18-yard box, but can only divert a looping cross over Szczesny's crossbar! That attempt had to be absolutely perfect, given the distance from goal and the power he would have to generate, but it sadly wasn't.
(26’) Arsenal continue to see more of the ball, and are prepared to pass around patiently while they wait for a gap to appear. Chelsea continue to frustrate them, however, with only Torres staying upfront consistently. Mourinho seems to be more than aware of Wenger's key men.
(25’) Good intervention from Cahill! Sagna escapes from Mikel down Arsenal's right flank, before whipping in a dangerous cross which threatens to flash across the edge of the six-yard box. The former Bolton centre-half hooks the ball away to safety.
(24’) Ozil lofts a free-kick delivery over a two man wall of Ramires and Lampard, looking to find an unmarked Giroud at the back post. The ball bounces off the slick turf, and skids out for a goal kick before the Frenchman can stretch a foot towards it.
(22’) Eden Hazard is able to get in behind Arsenal's defence, after a strong flick-on from Torres, but the intended pass is too close to Szczesny, who races out and hoofs clear. The atmosphere is somewhat flat, as both outfits continue to cancel each other out entirely.
(20’) Twenty minutes into this top of the table clash, and both sides are continuing to play cagily, aware of the damage that the opposition are capable of doing, should they been gifted a yard too much space. Chelsea's central midfield trio are doing a good job of limiting Ozil's involvement.
(18’) We're still yet to see any shots, or anything whatsoever in terms of either Cech or Szczesny being tested. Vermaelen makes an important interception to hook away a clever Ramires pass, before Gibbs is able to nod the loose ball back to his goalkeeper. Torres complains that the Belgian dragged him to the floor in the process.
(17’) Good defensive header from Terry! The central defender heads away at the near post, after Rosicky beat his man well and swung in a pacey cross. The Czech midfielder has looked bright thus far, always using his intelligence to try and get beyond his marker and deliver.
(16’) This game certainly looks to be both sides sizing each other up, probing for any weaknesses in their personnel or system. Arsenal fire the ball up to Walcott, who controls with his back to goal at the edge of the Chelsea area, but a combination of Terry and Azpilicueta manage to scramble the ball away.
(15’) A well-organised but creatively lacking start to this game, with plenty of unforced errors being made, and neither goalkeeper being tested. The wet surface may be a contributing factor, giving passes extra zip, but we're yet to see glimpses of the offensive quality which both teams possess.
(13’) The game continues to be contested mainly in the midfield third, with Chelsea working hard to impose themselves on proceedings with some tenacity. Arsenal continue to have the better of possession, as the visitors are yet to give much of the ball to their dangerous wide men, Hazard and Willian.
(11’) Ramsey is down injured, after being tackled from behind by a stray leg from Azpilicueta. The Chelsea left-back apologises, and the Wales midfielder looks able to carry on without any lasting damage. Sagna is then dumped onto the turf by a strong challenge from Lampard.
(10’) Torres races through on goal after dragging back Mertesacker, but the Spain international is penalised for a slight tug of the shirt of the towering German defender. Mike Dean comes to Arsenal's rescue, as Torres looked certain to confront Szczesny and give the visitors an early lead.
(9’) Arsenal have had the better of the opening ten minutes, making only a few errors after misplacing passes. The midfield trio behind Giroud are free-flowing as always, with Rosicky not afraid to cut inside from his touchline and allow Gibbs space to overlap.
(7’) A cagey start to proceedings, with neither side wanting to approach this game in a gung-ho fashion and concede an early goal. Giroud has seen a few incisive balls reach his feet, but Torres is yet to have a real impact on the game, other than being dispossessed strongly by Mertesacker.
(6’) LAMPARD! The England international sees an early strike blocked, after Hazard did well to rob Ramsey and allow Azipilicueta to overlap down the left hand side. The Spaniard cut the ball back to his captain, but Lampard could only fire into a ruck of red and white shirts.
(4’) It's been a midfield battle thus far, with neither side prepared to press high and force the opposition defence into making mistakes. No chances have been carved out, with long balls finding their way through to Cech and Szczesny safely.
(2’) The hosts see plenty of the ball in the opening two minutes, with Szczesny seeing some early touches as they stroke the ball around the defensive line. Arteta and Ramsey are certainly the two midfielders tasked with marshalling the middle third, with Rosicky out on the left hand side.
(1’) We are underway at the Emirates, in a game of utmost importance at the top of the Premier League. Both teams could find themselves scrapping at the summit of the league table with three points here tonight, with Arsenal in particular needing a victory to settle themselves after three matches without a win.
The two teams are about to take to the sodden pitch, after heavy rain in London over the course of the day. There shouldn't be an issue with the playing surface, but studs are presumably a must! The wind is howling and the rain continues to hammer down, which may affect the intricacies of the game, but it's nothing that hasn't been experienced by these teams before.
Ten minutes until kick-off, and we should have an excellent game on our hands tonight. Both sides will want to give their fans something to cheer about as Christmas approaches, with top spot the target for both clubs playing on the Emirates' turf this evening. Both outfits possess exciting offensive options, Chelsea in particular, and there should be some goals in this match for the neutral to enjoy.
If Arsenal lose tonight, the Gunners could spend Christmas in fourth place, despite leading the way in the league throughout the majority of the current campaign. Should tonight's visitors pick up the three points, Mourinho will have top spot in his sights throughout the festive period. This season has been one of fine margins, and promises to boast a similarly close title race.
Plenty of pressure will be placed on Giroud to lead the line for the hosts tonight, as the Frenchman has been misfiring of late. The return of Podolski to the substitutes bench will surely force the former Montpellier man to fight for his place in the starting line-up, despite the Germany international often being deployed behind the striker. Both sides have a wealth of options on their respective benches who can have an impact on tonight's action.
Both sides have had forgettable last outings, after Chelsea crashed out of the League Cup after extra-time against Sunderland, and Arsenal suffered at the free-scoring hands of Manchester City at the Etihad. With no wins in three games in all competitions, the Gunners will be keen to get back on track and head into the New Year on top of the Premier League pile. If Chelsea are to pick upt three points, Mourinho's men will be right in the title race mix.
Wenger chooses to pick Tomas Rosicky ahead of Cazorla, with the Czech midfielder needing to put in a solid shift against the energetic Ramires. Walcott keeps his place in the side after his brace against Man City last time out. Chelsea are either deploying Ramires on the right hand side of midfield, or in a midfield trio with Lampard and Mikel.
Chelsea substitutes: Cole, David Luiz, Mata, Oscar, Schurrle, Schwarzer, Eto'o.
Chelsea starting line-up: Cech; Azpilicueta, Terry, Cahill, Ivanovic; Mikel, Lampard; Ramires, Willian, Hazard; Torres.
Arsenal substitutes: Podolski, Monreal, Cazorla, Flamini, Fabianski, Bendtner, Jenkinson.
Arsenal starting line-up: Szczesny; Gibbs, Mertesacker, Vermaelen, Sagna; Arteta, Ramsey; Rosicky, Ozil, Walcott; Giroud.
TEAM NEWS: Jack Wilshere misses out for Arsenal, following his suspension for a gesture at Manchester City's fans, with Laurent Koscielny failing to return to the first team squad after suffering a gash on his knee. Michael Essien is suspended for the visitors, who opt to play Willian as opposed to Juan Mata, despite the Spaniard enjoying successful performances against the Gunners in the past.
I'm Simon Harrison, and I will be keeping you up to date with all of tonight's action, as Arsene Wenger attempts to defeat a Jose Mourinho side for the first time. The Portuguese coach has managed five wins and four draws against his adversary, with the Frenchman still awaiting a triumph with his Arsenal side. Two points separates these two outfits in the Premier League table, so let us keep our fingers crossed for a Christmas cracker.
Hello and welcome to tonight's sole Premier League fixture, as Chelsea travel to the Emirates for what is most probably their sternest test of the season thus far. Arsene Wenger's men have been momentarily deposed from top of the pile by Liverpool, but can regain first place with a win this evening. Both sides are determined to forget their last matches, after disappointing defeats.

There was still time for Yaya Toure to add yet another from the penalty spot, as his neat finish made ie 6-3 to City. Full-time, City move to within three points of Arsenal!
Walcott struck again to pull a goal back for the visitors but David Silva quickly added a fourth for City. Fernandinho then netted his first ever goal for the home side as they went 5-2 up, before Per Mertesacker added a late consolation for Arsenal.
Words cannot really describe what on earth happened in those 90 minutes but we'll try with the following round-up... Sergio Aguero gave Manchester City the lead before Theo Walcott hit back on the half-hour mark. Alvaro Negredo put the hosts back in the lead, however, before Fernandinho made it 3-1.
FULL-TIME: Manchester City 6-3 Arsenal. Yes, that reads six three...

--- 90’ +5 Yellow card W. Szczęsny is yellow-carded. ---
(90’) PENALTY TO MANCHESTER CITY! What on earth is going on? Milner surges into the area but Szczesny brings his down. Spot-kick given.
--- 90’ +4 Assist Assist by B. Sagna. ---
--- 90’ +4 Goal! GOAL! Mertesacker does grab a consolation for Arsenal. What a strange game this is - with such poor defending. ---
(90’) Walcott tries to beat Pantilimon for his hat-trick but his free kick is easily picked up by the City goalkeeper.
(90’) This has, quite simply, been a brilliant day for the hosts.
--- 90’ Substitution Javi García enters play, replacing S. Nasri. ---
(89’) Poor Bendtner. He thinks he's given Arsenal their third as he heads home a consolation. But it is given offside...

(87’) OVER! Nasri fires the ball over the bar after a great move. The Frenchman is frustrated not to score there and looks desperate to get on the scoresheet!
(86’) Having said that, they have scored twice, which is a considerable achievement under the circumstances.
(86’) Just a few more minutes for Arsenal fans to suffer here. It has been a poor display from the Gunners.

(84’) Nasri beats two defenders but Mertesacker slides in and deals with the Frenchman well! The tackle sees the ball hit Nasri and then go off for a goal kick.
(82’) But there is no denying the angst surrounding the Emirates at the moment. They entered a key period of their season needing three big results. As it has happened, they have lost two out of two.
(81’) Where next for Arsenal after this defeat (presuming they fail to score three before full-time...)? They will still be two points clear at the top of the table (if Chelsea beat Crystal Palace today) and can strengthen their lead with a win against Chelsea next week.
--- 80’ Yellow card V. Kompany gets yellow. ---
(80’) Ten minutes remain and it's still 4-2 to Manchester City. While they can be questioned defensively - especially away from home - their sheer appetite for goals at home makes them so strong.
(78’) And Toure almost inspires another chance for the hosts, though Nasri dallies on the ball and sees it go off for a goal kick.
(77’) TOURE! The Ivorian shoots just wide. City had transitioned from one side of the pitch to the other in just a flash!
--- 76’ Substitution Nicklas Bendtner comes on for Giroud now, instead of coming on alongside him. The Frenchman has not had the best of days. ---
(75’) Both sides are relentlessly pushing forward now. Arsenal for obvious reasons. Manchester City because they have the confidence to do so.

--- 71’ Substitution Goalscorer David Silva, who has been superb today, is being replaced by James Milner. And the Spaniard is receiving a standing ovation. ---
(69’) The home side look more than satisfied to sit back and let the Gunners come at them.
(68’) Wilshere has a strike at goal but Pantilimon beats it away. Arsenal can be admired for their attacking approach but you can't help but feel that this game is beyond them now.
(67’) What a home record City possess. Eight wins out of eight (as things stand). They've had 7-0 and 6-0 wins and also beaten Manchester United 4-1 at the Etihad. This is just another feather in their cap.
--- 66’ Assist The assist came from Jesús Navas. ---
--- 66’ Goal! GOAL! Silva makes it 4-2 and that is exactly the form I was referring to. Navas was involved in the build-up but it was his fellow Spaniard who provided the finish. No matter how hard Arsenal try to get back into this one, they cannot keep up with the hosts in defence. That should be the end of the Gunners' fightback. ---
(65’) But the Gunners still need another goal, here, and that looks a tall order with City's current form.
(64’) What a wise decision it has proved by Wenger to play Walcott today.
--- 63’ Assist The assist came from A. Ramsey. ---
--- 63’ Goal! GOAL! It's Walcott again! This isn't over quite yet! A sensational effort from the Arsenal forward as he shoots from range and catches Pantilimon out. We have a grandstand finish on our hands! ---
(61’) Zabaleta now links up with substitute Jesus Navas down the right-hand side, although the move is eventually broken down by a Ramsey clearance.

(59’) Martin Atkinson does not give the spot-kick, however.
(58’) PENALTY APPEALS! Walcott's strike is blocked by Zabaleta's hand! The Arsenal players protest vigorously.
(57’) This score-line is good news for Chelsea, too, with Jose Mourinho's men able to cut the gap to just two points if they beat Crystal Palace this afternoon. Crisis, what crisis?
(56’) The hosts can afford to slip into cruise control if Arsenal don't take their chances here. As things stand, City will only be three points behind the league leaders.
(55’) GIROUD AGAIN! This time, the Frenchman is oh so close as Sagna breaks down the flank and whips a superb cross into the area. Giroud throws himself at the ball and, this time, comes extremely close. Wide it goes.

(52’) So the loss of Aguero does not hurt the hosts too much in the short term as Fernandinho gets his first ever City goal. Arsenal's respoonse is muted, as Giroud chooses to shoot instead of passing to an unmarked Ramsey. Chance wasted.
--- 50’ Goal! GOAL! Fernandinho gives City a third! Ozil, of all people, is caught out in possession after trying to feed the ball to Flamini. Brazilian Fernandinho takes full advantage, curling a fantastic shot into the back of the net from long distance. Is that game over? ---
--- 50’ Substitution Jesús Navas enters the game and replaces S. Agüero. ---
--- 49’ Yellow card David Silva is yellow-carded. ---
(49’) Aguero seems to have injured his calf, while Kompany almost deputises fantastically for him. The City captain ran the length of the pitch, evading three different challenges! But his cross went straight to Mertesacker. Great effort.
(48’) The Argentine is applauded as he walks off the field for treatment.
(47’) Bad news... Aguero is down injured for the home side.
(46’) And we're back up and running at the Etihad!

The hosts would restore their superiority eight minutes later, though, as Pablo Zabaleta played Alvaro Negredo in to fire home. Laurent Koscielny then went off injured for the visitors, meaning Arsenal have it all to do if they are to end City's 100 per cent home record for the league season.
Yet Arsenal's attacking threat meant they were always bound to trouble the City back line, although there was more than a touch of fortune involved as Theo Walcott's shot somehow found its way into the back of the net on 31 minutes.
So the hosts lead at the break - and deservedly so. It was all Manchester City from the off as Manuel Pellegrini's side came flying out of the traps. Sergio Aguero rewarded their ascendancy with a superb volley after 14 minutes.
HALF-TIME: Manchester City 2-1 Arsenal
(45’) Silva now shoots but to no avail. All City at the moment - and not for the first time this half.
(45’) SAVE! Szczesny is almost wrong-footed by a deflected shot as he claims the ball next to the post.
(45’) GOOD NEWS! The news on Koscielny's injury is that it is only a cut, meaning he might only be out for a week or two.
(45’) OVER! Samir Nasri takes a corner for the hosts now and Demichelis heads just over! The Gunners do not look at all convincing from set-pieces.
(44’) We are sure to see a few minutes of injury time. But will there be any more goals before the break?
(43’) City seem to have survived the scare of Walcott's equaliser. The Koscielny injury is also a stroke of luck for the home side. Away fans will be worried as the problem looks potentially serious.

(40’) Worrying signs for the Gunners as the strecher comes out. It looks like it's the end of Koscielny's game.
--- 39’ Assist Assist by P. Zabaleta. ---

(37’) Meanwhile, Wenger has put his coat on...
(36’) Wenger spoke before the match of the "creativity" his side have at their disposal. Wilshere definitely showed some of it there - but his target, Monreal, was in an offside position.
(35’) Do the visitors deserve to be on level terms? Probably not. But are they? They certainly are. What can City do to change that?
(33’) CHANCE!! That's where - City almost retake the lead instantly! Monreal can't track the run of Negredo and he is one on one with Wojciech Szczesny but he shoots just wide!
(32’) Where to for the hosts now?
--- 31’ Assist M. Özil provided the assist. ---

(28’) FOUL! Negredo slides in and gives away a free kick. No booking and his defensive efforts have been very noticeable so far.

(10’) CHANCE! Theo Walcott breaks forward with his first real involvement of the game and plays in Jack Wilshere. The England midfielder is in a great position but wastes the opportunity.
(9’) Negredo clears once again! Superb defending from the striker.

(3’) After their free kick, City have won - and wasted - a corner. Nevertheless, it is all coming from the hosts at the moment. They have come out of the blocks absolutely flying!
(2’) David Silva takes the resultant free kick but Bacary Sagna clears.
(2’) Aguero enjoys a chance to run at the Arsenal defence already! No surprises as Mathieu Flamini stops him in his tracks, although he gives away a foul. That could be key right there - how Flamini protects the back four.
(1’) Arsenal kick us off!
We'll no doubt be fascinated by the answer that unfolds...

(60’) Sessegnon has a go from distance but he drags his volley high and wide.

Well, that was a tense half of football devoid of much quality. Caulker had the best chance when he fired wide from a corner and Noone was lively in his first start of the season. West Brom huffed and puffed but went nowhere and manager Steve Clarke has his work cut out in the half-time break.
(45’) A scrappy first half comes to an end at the Welsh capital. Very little attacking ambition on show so far, with Cardiff enjoying more possession than the visitors.
(43’) Odemwingie produces a rare moment of quality with a peach of a cross to Campbell, which the England striker is but inches away from converting.
(41’) Cardiff have a chance to break through Campbell but Liam Ridgewell does well to track back and make the challenge. The Cardiff City Stadium is flatter than a pancake right now and I don't blame them.
(39’) McAuley concedes a needless corner on the back of a poor first touch but Cardiff cannot profit from that error. All dull and dreary so far, I'm afraid.

(33’) Cardiff have a free kick in a decent area after Gareth McAuley collides with Campbell. Whittingham's delivery is a poor one, however, as it goes straight out of touch.
(31’) West Brom cannot build any sort of attacking momentum at the moment with Sessegnon the latest to lose possession cheaply in the Cardiff half.

(21’) Craig Noone cuts back on his left foot and plays a floating cross towards Campbell but it is a touch overhit and Myhill gathers.
(19’) Turner plays a poor backpass to Marshall with Sessegnon lurking. Marshall's hasty clearance falls to Long but the Ireland striker cannot get any power behind his shot.
(17’) Both sides being wasteful in possession as a succession of passes go astray. Shane Long has an ambitious pop at goal but his effort is blocked by Caulker.

(9’) Andrew Taylor looks to slip in Odemwingie but the striker is adjudged to be in an offside position.
(7’) Cardiff goalkeeper David Marshall looks to pick out Fraizer Campbell but the ball runs out of play for a West Brom goal kick.

Thanks for joining me today, I hope you have enjoyed the action.
(90’) Chelsea are nearly there, but Mourinho won't be pleased with their display.
(90’) Luiz steps up to take the free-kick with the home fans would of expectation. However, he puts the ball straight into the wall.
(90’) The officials announce there will be four minutes of added time.
(90’) Free-kick for Chelsea on the edge of the Palace area as Jerome catches Hazard.
(90’) Delaney goes close for the fourth time as he comes to the near post and knocks a glancing header towards the top-far corner, but it goes just wide.
(89’) Integral double save by Speroni! Ramires slipped Schurrle into the area and the German hit his shot into the goalkeeper's face. Ba looks to pounce on the rebound, but Speroni saves that as well!
--- 88’ Substitution D. Gayle comes on for M. Chamakh. ---

--- 84’ Substitution D. Ba enters the game and replaces Fernando Torres. ---
(84’) And another as Demba Ba comes on for the scorer of the match's first goal; Fernando Torres.
--- 82’ Substitution Willian is done for the day. A. Schürrle is his replacement. ---
(82’) Change for Chelsea now as Schurrle replaces Willian.
(81’) Palace really look the more likely to score here at the moment. Chelsea are particularly struggling in the middle.
(78’) Delaney goes close again! He charges to meet the corner at the front post and he glances the ball into the sidenetting.

(75’) Oscar spurns an incredible chance as the ball drops to him in the area, but the Brazilian's low shot is kept out by Speroni. The officials spare his blushes by flagging Torres offside in the build-up.
(73’) Palace are giving this their all and an equaliser would not be a massive shock considering their performance thus far. Chelsea have been very lacklustre.

(45’) The corner comes to nothing as Palace defend it relatively well and get it clear.
(44’) Azpilicueta roams down the left and crosses. Torres attempts a flick, but the ball ends up with the left-back again. He crosses for a second time, but Ward knocks it behind for a corner.

(3’) Fairly encouraging start by Palace as they put Chelsea under some early pressure.
(1’) Right, Palace get the action started at Stamford Bridge.

(41’) Talk about backs to the wall, the hosts win a corner and even Dimitar Berbatov is back defending!
(39’) SHOWBOAT! Everton break away and Ross Barkley runs at the Fulham defence like a man on a mission. He produces a couple of step overs and then looks to find Lukaku in the box, but his pass is disappointing and goes out for a goal kick.
(36’) CLOSE! Finally, the Londoners get a sniff of goal. Unfortunately for them, Karagounis sends a bobbling half volley wide of Howard's goal.
(35’) DOUBLE CHANCE! The Toffees will kick themselves if they don't add to their tally. Barkley's effort is blocked and spins out to an unmarked Osman, who send a crashing volley wide of the post!
(32’) CLOSE AGAIN! Coleman's low drive from the right is palmed away by Fulham's keeper. It's a blue tide at the moment!
(30’) With half an hour gone in this game, what have we learned so far? Roberto Martinez's men are looking good so far and deserve their statement of intent on the top four places. The Cottagers on the other hand? Well, they need something soon or this will be another three points they will end up kissing goodbye.
(28’) OVER! Everton just keep 'em coming. Another chance falls to the feet of Deulofeu following good work by Barkley but the youngster fires miles over the bar.
(26’) Fulham are trying to force their way back into this game but there is little inspiration in their side at the moment. Will that change before the end of the half?
(24’) WHAT A SAVE! Everton win their fifth corner of the game. It is sent into the box by Coleman, who finds Barry, whose flick-header is deflected onto Lukaku and is turned around the post at the last second by Stekelenburg!
(21’) SHOT! After nearly twenty minutes of quiet frustration, Everton nearly double their lead! Deulofeu drives unchallenged into the box and shoots across goal when it would have been easier to square it for Lukaku.
(20’) STAT ATTACK: That is Osman's 41st Premier League goal in his 300th league appearance for the Toffees.
--- 18’ Assist S. Pienaar provided the assist. ---
--- 18’ Goal! GOAL! What a great finish from Leon Osman! Piennar finds the England International on the edge of the box and he jinks from his right foot to his left to smash the ball into the back of the net. Goodison Park erupts! ---
(17’) HALF CHANCE! A move that involves both sides giving the ball away leads to a Coleman cross on the right finding Barkley, whose looping header is carried out of play for a corner by keeper Stekelenburg.
(14’) CHANCE! A Pienaar corner swings towards the six-yard-box. It is flicked on by Jagielka towards the back post, but Osman fails to reach it and the ball goes out for a goal kick.
(12’) The Cottagers are doing very well to quell any chances being created by the Toffees and both keepers have yet to be tested. Still, early days n'all!
(10’) Kacaniklic latches onto a defence splitting pass that is just too heavy for Dejagah and the loose ball runs through to keeper Tim Howard.
(8’) STAT ATTACK: The Toffees have drawn four of their last six games, keeping four clean sheets. (BBC Sport)
(5’) The game is settling as the Cottagers are attempting to build momentum with possession in the middle of the park. Not much in the way of early chances.
(3’) It is the home side who come out of the traps early here, having already had a corner dealt with by the visitors.
(1’) We are underway with Fulham kicking from left to right!
The teams are making their way out of the tunnel...
We have TEN minutes to go before kick-off!
STAT ATTACK: ...And here it is. Fulham have never won a league game at Everton (D4, L21). Ominous record, isn't it, Fulham fans?
Meanwhile, Fulham boss Rene Meulensteen makes Scott Parker his captain for the day as Darren Bent is fit to return to the bench for the London side, who are desperate to get a result at a ground where they normally have difficulty picking up points. That's all to come in a stat attack that is just around the corner...
Toffees boss Roberto Martinez keeps golden boy Gerard Deulofeu in the side as James McCarthy is suspended. Leighton Baines is still out so Bryan Oviedo deputises yet again in defence.

Subs: Robles, Heitinga, Jelavic, Mirallas, Naismith, Stones, Alcaraz.

FULL TIME: Newcastle 1-1 Southampton - there may have been a surplus of goals today, but the action reached fever-pitch more often than not in what was a hugely open clash of top-six contenders! I'm Livio Caferoglu and it's farewell from me.
(90’) We're into an EIGHTH (you read that right) minute of injury time now, with Newcastle on the attack following the sudden breakout of tempers on the sidelines!
--- 90’ +6 Substitution J. Rodriguez is replaced with S. Gallagher. ---
(90’) Rodriguez is replaced by lanky teenage defender Gallagher as Southampton make one final foray into the Newcastle box from a throw...
(90’) Debuchy drills a cross into the box from the resulting free kick, which Davis crucially blocks!
--- 90’ +4 Yellow card M. Schneiderlin is cautioned by the referee. ---
(90’) Schneiderlin is shown the yellow card for a bad foul, and drama has erupted near the dugout! Details are imminent...
(90’) Chances being spread across either side of the pitch but the killer pass is currently lacking. Debuchy tries to play in Cisse with a through ball, but the offside flag is raised.
(90’) Six minutes of injury time will be added on.
(89’) HOW BIZARRE!! The referee Mike Jones takes a clatter after Sissoko accidentally swings his arm in the official's face while in conversation with the midfielder. Gazzaniga, on the ground, hit the Frenchman's leg in a bid to push him away.
(87’) Gazzaniga bravely jumps for the ball and collects it after Ben Arfa smashes a shot at goal which takes a heavy deflection. Sissoko showed fine footwork to cut the ball back into the box.
(85’) Chambers whips up a ball from deep, which eventually finds Lambert at the back post, but as he takes the ball down, the linesman's flag goes up.
(83’) BRILLIANT BEN ARFA!! The attacker takes on a succession of Southampton shirts in the final third before making his way into the area, but his cross is well blocked.
(81’) Tiote launches a speculative attempt which he drags just wide of the post from distance. This one could go either way!
(79’) CHEEKY!!! The full-back's fellow subsitute Ben Arfa tries to outsmart Gazzaniga with a curled free kick towards the goalkeeper's near post, but the Argentine tips away for a corner!
--- 78’ Substitution D. Santon is done for the day. M. Haïdara is his replacement. ---
(77’) Haidara is hauled on in place of Santon, and within a few seconds of his introduction he helps win his side a free kick after doubling up with Sissoko.
(75’) Shaw goes for a through ball in a bid to find Rodriguez for the winner, but once again the offside flag comes to Newcastle's rescue.
(73’) GAZZANIGA ALMOST GIFTS NEWCASTLE A SECOND GOAL!! You heard that right... an awful kick-out drops straight to Remy, who pounces on the gaffe near the edge of the box, but the striker's finish is a fraction too high!
--- 72’ Substitution Y. Gouffran is replaced with H. Ben Arfa. ---
(71’) OOOOOOOH!!!! Newcastle fail to deal with a corner and it almost comes to bite them back where it hurts the most, but Rodriguez's free header in the box - despite looping ominously - eventually lands in Krul's gloves!
(69’) ALMOST A SUDDEN REPLY! Debuchy fires a shot low and hard at Gazzaniga, who instinctively blocks the full-back's attempt.
(67’) That was a deserved equaliser from Southampton, who have looked a far more balanced outfit since the half-time introductions of Schneiderlin and Lallana. Their change in system has also allowed the Saints to bring out the best in Lambert, underlining their flexibility further.
--- 65’ Assist The assist came from S. Davis. ---
--- 65’ Goal! THAT IS A SUPERB GOAL!!!! Southampton are relentless as they counter at the speed of light once more through Rodriguez, and the striker plays a deft one-two with Davis who returns delicately through the legs of Coloccini, before he sweeps home the finish with the goal at his mercy! ---
(65’) WHAT AN EFFORT!!! Davis goes for the spectacular from some way out and sees his half-volleyed attempt creep just over the crossbar!
--- 64’ Yellow card J. Cork goes into the referee's book. ---
(63’) THE CHANCE GOES BEGGING FOR SOUTHAMPTON! Lallana breaks at the speed of light as he leaves Santon in his wake and probes into the box, but his cut-back to find a team-mate is hugely disappointing as the ball is quickly cleared!
--- 61’ Substitution P. Cissé enters play, replacing Shola Ameobi. ---
(61’) Davis is fortunate to avoid the referee's book following another deliberate trip on Tiote. Meanwhile, Ameobi's performance comes to an abrupt end. Enter the eventual star of the 2011-12 campaign - Papiss Cisse!
(59’) Ameobi's physical prowwess is causing one or two problems for Southampton, with another accurate headed attempt this time whistling just wide of Gazzaniga's goal
(57’) Not for the first time this afternoon, Rodriguez attracts the offside flag for again mistiming his run to reach Lambert's lobbed through ball.
(55’) REMY!!!! The French forward hits a snapshot on the half-volley from the edge of the box, and it is well saved by Gazzaniga.
(53’) Lambert has definitely grown into stature since Osvaldo's half-time exit. Twice has he been played in and looked to flick on lay-offs for team-mates. His ability to hold the ball up must be utilised in that manner more often if Southampton are to stage a comeback today.
(51’) Lambert scoops up a tantalising pass for Rodriguez, who successfully connects with the ball in the box, but his strike at Krul is too weak as he is slightly off-balance.
(49’) It's Southampton's turn to feel the wrath of the offside rule as Lallana times his run onto Rodriguez's through ball too early.
(47’) Newcastle already try to unlock the Saints defence within a minute of the restart, but the offside flag denies Santon from finding Sissoko.
--- 46’ Substitution A. Lallana enters the game and replaces P. Osvaldo. ---
--- 46’ Substitution M. Schneiderlin enters play, replacing J. Ward-Prowse. ---
(45’) Southampton make a bold statement of intent by bringing on talismen Morgan Schneiderlin and Adam Lallana on during the interval in place of - perhaps surprisingly - Ward-Prowse and Osvaldo. Anyway, the second half is under way!
The half-time whistle is blown, with the score reading Newcastle 1-0 Southampton!
(45’) One additional minute will be played.
(43’) Ameobi beats a shocking Southampton offside trap but his lack of composure allows Shaw to get back in time. However, Anita doubles up with the Nigerian striker and shows great feet to twist his way into the box and cut a ball back which no-one can read! Moments later, Osvaldo is flagged offside for making his run to latch onto Lambert's through pass too early.
(41’) WHAT A WASTE! Santon is caught out by an onrushing Lambert down the right wing and drills in a ball which is neither a shot at goal or an assist for Osvaldo to tuck away.
(39’) Sissoko is again found in an advanced position, which is in clear view of the Southampton goal, but *again* he is denied by a trailing leg from Hooiveld. That was a vital interception!
(37’) Lambert shows great resillience to duel with Coloccini near the corner flag and win his side a corner. There's a slight hint of handball in the box from the subsequent corner, but the referee ignores the crowd's appeals.
(35’) OOOOH! Anita is felled by Rodriguez in an inside-left position near the Saints box, and Santon smashes a piledriver at goal from around 25 yards out which swerves just over the bar!
(33’) A ball is launched into the box, which eventually reaches Ameobi, but he is well-marshalled by the Southampton defence and can only head the ball limply into the gloves of Gazzaniga.
(32’) Davis takes one for the team as he cynically scythes down Tiote, who is ready to launch an attack from his holding position in midfield. There's no booking again, however.
(30’) No idea what Hooiveld was playing at there, attempting to hack the ball away with his left foot despite being clearly off balance... Anyway it's down to Southampton now. Can they come back from the dead at St James' Park?
--- 27’ Goal! NEWCASTLE DRAW FIRST BLOOD!!! A free kick is launched into the box from the halfway line, which Williamson telepathically nods down - past a shell-shocked Lambert - into Gouffran's path, and the Frenchman shifts past Gazzaniga before tapping the ball into an empty net! ---
(27’) The gangly Argentine stopper is in on the action again, albeit in an attacking position, as his through ball to find Ameobi is ruled offside.
(25’) Coloccini lives up to his name by being in the right place at the right time to mop up another wonderful Chambers cross. Hooiveld then wastes the chance by putting the ball into the touchline after failing to find Shaw.
(23’) WHERE WAS THE QUICK-THINKING? Sissoko is caught horribly in two minds as he capitalises on a misjudgment from Shaw to set up a two-v-two situation, but he hesitates far too long and can only pass backwards, allowing the Saints to plough enough bodies back and kill off the attack.
(21’) Osvaldo is again involved, but it's another case of his colleagues not finding him on his wavelength. The striker lays off Lambert, which results in Newcastle breaking up play and retaining possession of the ball.
(19’) A delightful cross is played into the Toon box from the right-hand side by the lively Chambers, yet Osvaldo is adjudged to be in an offside position.
(17’) Shaw manages to evade the auxilary left-winger Sissoko but with the use of his hand. No yellow card is in sight, however - a decision which Alan Pardew expresses his frustration to the fourth official about.
(15’) Southampton react well to that close shave as they launch a counterattack, which Osvaldo slips into the feet of Ward-Prowse near the area, but the starlet's shot goes straight into Krul's arms.
(13’) WHAT A CHANCE!!! Pandemonium ensues in the Southampton box as Cork misreads the danger, allowing a low cross from Gouffran to be played beyond Gazzaniga and into the path of Remy, but Chambers is there to deny the French hitman on the line!
(11’) Southampton are beginning to contain Newcastle in the middle of the park, with Ward-Prowse constantly dropping into pockets of space to support the deep-lying pairing of Davis and Cork. A lobbed pass is played into the box, which the Northern Irishman flicks on for Osvaldo, but the striker cannot read his team-mate in time.
(9’) Ward-Prowse displays neat footwork near the touchline to outwit Tiote and forces Sissoko into making a clear foul.
(7’) The ball is pinged about to and fro around the centre-circle as neither team can hold onto possession at present.
(5’) Ameobi tests the credentials of Chambers on the opposing flank, but the young, replacement full-back is no fool. However, Newcastle come close from the resulting corner as Debuchy smashes a half-volley on the edge of the box just wide!
(3’) The Magpies gain another corner in quick succession, this time via Debuchy on the right, but the referee penalises Gouffran for infringement. The visitors take the free kick in their own area.
(1’) Southampton get the match kicked off, going from right to left.
The players are out on the pitch. Let battle commence!
Both sides have experienced contrasting fortunes of late - Alan Pardew's men have climbed to sixth position in the Premier League thanks to an impressive run of five wins in their last six matches. However, the South Coast outfit ended a sequence of three straight defeats last week, drawing 1-1 with Manchester City.
Newcastle's only absentee comes in the form of playmaker Yohan Cabaye who has been handed a one-match ban for accumulating five yellow cards. Southampton, meanwhile, have been dealt a blow with the news that lynchpin Morgan Schneiderlin has joined Victor Wanyama, Artur Boruc, Nathaniel Clyne, Daniel Fox and Kelvin Davis on the treatment table due to a pelvic injury.
Last but not least, we have the Saints: Gazzaniga; Chambers, Lovren, Hooiveld, Shaw; Cork, Davis, Ward-Prowse; Rodriguez, Lambert; Osvaldo.
Here's how the Magpies will look this afternoon: Krul; Debuchy, Williamson, Coloccini, Santon; Tiote, Sissoko, Anita; Gouffran, S Ameobi, Remy.

FULL-TIME: WEST HAM 0-0 SUNDERLAND Much to the dismay of the home fans, the Hammers should consider this point a gift. The Black Cats will rue their missed chances. Jaaskelainen, his crossbar and a lack of composure in front of goal proved to be too much for Sunderland to overcome, as they are forced to settle for a point. Allardyce has his work cut out for him, as they remain on the edge of the relegation zone, while Poyet continues to search for a way to get Sunderland out of the bottom.
(90’) Andre Mariner blows his full time whistle and that will do it at Upton Park.
(90’) Collins off the corner! He climbs up to get on the end of the cross but sends his effort wide. That might just do it.
(90’) McCartney! A chance out of nothing, really as his cross nearly goes in, if not for a smart tip over by Mannone.
(90’) Four minutes of added time. Fans already funneling out of Upton Park.
(89’) It's the first real chance in a while for West Ham. Maiga gets it in space and gives a good ball in for Cole, but it's sent wide for a goal kick says Mariner. Looked like it may have gone out off O'Shea for a corner.
(87’) The crowd at Upton Park gets as loud as they've been all game! It's not saying much. Giaccherini goes down easily, West Ham put the ball out in the name of fair play, and the crowd isn't afraid to voice their displeasure.
(85’) Morrison charges up the center, but lets a shot go from distance and it's well wide. This has been a very uninspiring performance from the Hammers - certainly not how Allardyce hoped to be celebrating his 100th match with the club.
(83’) This game has lost any sort of urgency. Both teams look content on playing out the draw. I can understand West Ham's willingness at this point, but Sunderland can't be content with a point after all the chances they've wasted.
--- 81’ Substitution Bardsley has picked up a knock and he'll give way to Andrea Dossena. ---
(81’) Bardsley has picked up a knock and he'll give way to Andrea Dossena.
(80’) STAT: In 41 all-time meetings between West Ham and Sunderland at Upton Park, there has never been a scoreless draw. We're less than 10 minutes from the first one here today...
(79’) Morrison this time with a great run for West Ham, but he's forced to the outside and it results in a feeble ball into the box.
(78’) KI! It's so close to an opening goal for Sunderland! The South Korea international gets off a great shot from close range, but the great reactions of Jaaskelainen keep this game scoreless.
(77’) Sunderland applying some pressure here, but West Ham are doing well to keep everything outside the box.
--- 75’ Substitution Carlton Cole on for Joe Cole. Allardyce hoping just maybe they can find a winner, although it doesn't look likely at the moment. ---
(74’) Diame is the only player for the Hammers who looks like he could have a goal in him today. Another fine run from him, but his shot is easily collected by Mannone.
--- 73’ Substitution S. Fletcher enters the game and replaces J. Altidore. ---
--- 72’ Substitution A. Johnson enters play, replacing F. Borini. ---
(72’) Sunderland aren't really going for it here. Poyet replaces Altidore and Borini for Fletcher and Johnson. You just feel like this game is there for the taking for Sunderland, but is Poyet being overly-cautious with these substitutions?
(70’) Chance for Collison, and that really sums up the afternoon for West Ham. Cole lays it off for him with too much pace, and the shot trickles helplessly wide.
(68’) A bit of life shown by Sunderland. Bardsley has space on the outside of the box, but fails to pick out Borini and West Ham break the other way.
(66’) The game has really died out here. The ball has barely left the midfield. It feels as though both teams are getting this into the final 20 minutes before they really go for it. Let's hope so, or this could be a dreary end to the match at Upton Park.
(64’) West Ham are showing no signs of snatching a goal here. You just wonder if Poyet will send on Fletcher or Johnson and try and take all three points from the Hammers.
(62’) The chances are coming, but both teams are being limited to diagonal crosses and shots from distance. A goal would really bring this game to life.
(61’) ALTIDORE THIS TIME! The American does well to turn past the tackle of Collins, and fires a strong shot back across goal. Jaaskelainen does well to get down and hold on to make the save.
(59’) More pressure from Sunderland now! Giaccherini's shot from twenty yards out is blasted high and wide, however.
--- 58’ Substitution Guy Demel is forced to sub off as he appears to have picked up a knock. Joey O'Brien will be the man to replace him. ---
(57’) Diame powers through the Sunderland defence, and gets into a dangerous area but sends his shot into the side netting.
--- 56’ Substitution Matt Jarvis gives way here for Jack Collison, as Allardyce tries to breathe some life into his squad. It's the 100th league appearance for Collison, on the same day Allardyce manages his 100th game for the Hammers. ---
(54’) Finally some life in the crowd at Upton Park
(53’) West Ham finally applying some pressure on Sunderland. A string of passes leads to a good opportunity for Ravel Morrison, but Mannone makes an easy save.
(51’) Both teams are easing their way into the second half, but surely will have to go for it as the game progresses. A draw would do Sam Allardyce no favors, while Sunderland will be hoping for more considering their performance so far.
(49’) Ki lays it off nicely for Altidore, but his thumping shot is deflected behind for a corner.
(48’) The crowd at Upton Park has been subdued this afternoon. West Ham need to find a spark or Sunderland will feel confident in their ability to take this game over.
(46’) It will be interesting to see how Allardyce approaches this second half. He knows the importance of getting three points from this fixture as they face Manchester United and Arsenal in their next two league matches.
(46’) West Ham get this second half underway...
Sam Allardyce is still waiting for someone to step up in the absence of Andy Carroll. Maiga is still looking for his first goal in his eleventh game of the season today. Ricardo Vaz Te (two goals) and Carlton Cole (one) are available as substitutes.
Sunderland are still looking for their first away win on the season, and after that first half you'd think they would fancy their chances here today.
HALF-TIME: WEST HAM 0-0 SUNDERLAND... The hosts started strong and looked like taking the game over in the early stages, but as has been the story all season, lacked quality in front of goal. Sunderland grew in confidence as the half progressed, and in all likelihood will be kicking themselves for not taking their chances. Altidore and Borini could have a goal each, while the absence of Andy Carroll continues to haunt Sam Allardyce.
(45’) CATTERMOLE! It's a remarkable effort from distance, but it's turned away nicely by the strong hands of Jaaskelainen, and with that, Andre Mariner puts an end to the first half.
(45’) One minute of added time...
(44’) Sunderland growing in confidence! A cross in is cleared, but the ball falls beautifully for Giaccherini who has his shot deflected just wide, much to the relief of Jaaskelainen.
(43’) Nice bit of skill from Ravel Morrison! He dances his way into the box, but can't find enough space to pick out a cross or a shot. Sunderland defending well there.
(40’) Cole creates a turnover in the attacking third, and had options to either side, but elects to go for goal and sends it shockingly wide.
(39’) Larsson sends a great ball in and it's cleared for yet another corner. West Ham on the back foot here!
(38’) Ki does really well down the left, he tries to skip past Joe Cole, but it's turned out of play for a corner... although it looked to be out off Ki. Tough break for Cole.
(36’) Concerted pressure here from Sunderland! Ki picks out Borini in the box, but it's a dreadful header by the Italian as he sends the ball out for a goal kick.
(34’) OFF THE BAR!! A tremendous effort by Phil Bardsley from about 25 yards out beats Jaaskelainen but not the bar! Sunderland just inches away from an opening goal!
(32’) SO CLOSE FOR SUNDERLAND! Altidore blocks the free kick of Collins and the ball breaks for Borini who has plenty of time and space, but slams his shot into the thankful arms of Jaaskelainen! The Italian really should have done better there!
(31’) Sunderland managing some pressure of their own now, and the ball goes out for another corner, but nothing comes of it.
(29’) Sunderland back the other way now, Giaccherini's ball in for Altidore is good, but he's taken down by McCartney! Mariner says no penalty, and Sunderland will have to settle for a corner.
(27’) The Hammers are having plenty of success building down the left through Diame and Jarvis. They're getting into plenty of space, but seem to be lacking the final ball.
--- 25’ Yellow card West Ham continue to apply the pressure, but Mark Noble concedes possession with a late tackle and receives the game's first yellow. ---
(23’) Celustka topples over the back of Noble right outside the area, but no foul is given! Questionable decision by Mariner, one I think he got wrong. Should have been a free kick in a dangerous area there for the Hammers.
(21’) Appeals for a penalty! Tomkins heads the corner back across the face of goal, and West Ham appeal for a handball, but referee Andre Mariner has called a foul against Guy Demel for a push. Sunderland can finally relieve some of the pressure here.
(21’) West Ham applying the pressure here! Collins' flick on is smartly cleared by Bardsley or Cole would have had a simple tap-in at the far post.
(20’) MAD SCRAMBLE! Noble takes a free kick that Collins manages to head into the danger zone, and three players had a kick at it before it's finally cleared by Sunderland!
(19’) Jarvis breaks down the left now and he nearly picks out Maiga, but Mannone manages to cover up safely!
(18’) Sunderland with a free kick from about 30 yards out. Larsson delivers, but nothing comes of it as Brown is ruled offside.
(16’) The teams are slowly starting to settle into the match now, after a very lively start.
(15’) West Ham controlling the ball well in the midfield, but seem to be forcing the ball forward, turning it over far too cheaply as a result.
(13’) Jarvis gets it on the edge of the box and his cross is turned out by Bardsley, but the assistant referee says goal kick! No corner for West Ham, much to the dismay of Jarvis.
(11’) STAT ATTACK: You have to go back to April 10, 2010 to find the last time Sunderland lost at Upton Park. The Black Cats are also unbeaten in their last four against West Ham.
(9’) Both teams with chances in the early going here, but Altidore really should have the visitors in the lead! Those are chances Sunderland can't afford to miss when you're sitting bottom of the table.
(7’) Sunderland's ensuing corner is cleared, and we have a stoppage as Collins is down after a collision with Bardsley.
(5’) ALTIDORE! The USA international is sent in alone with all the time and space in the world, but it's an inexcusable effort that's easily turned aside by Jaaskelainen.
(4’) West Ham really picking up the pace here! Diame again with a strong run and he picks out Maiga yet again, who heads it back across the face of goal and out for a goal kick. Jarvis just failed to get on the end of it.
(3’) What a great run by Diame!! The midfielder went roaring by O'Shea and Cattermole, but Maiga is unable to connect well with his final ball.
(3’) Giaccherini finds some space and lays it off for Ki but his shot rolls safely into the hands of Jaaskelainen.
(2’) The teams are content on feeling each other out early on here, with Sunderland happy to slow the tempo and keep possession.
(1’) And we're off!
Bubbles fill the air as the players take the pitch at Upton Park. Which manager will have their bubble burst today?

With Sunderland currently bottom of the table, both teams will be desperate for three points today. This should make for an entertaining match!
West Ham are struggling for goals, while Sunderland can't win away. Something has got to give today in Sam Allardyce's 100th game in charge of the Hammers!
