Hello and welcome to the live text commentary of Sunderland vs Tottenham in the Premier League. My name is Ryan Benson and I shall be describing the action for you today.

Well, that's all from our LIVE coverage of events at Craven Cottage this afternoon. Many thanks for joining us!
Villa remain 10th in the table but could drop into the bottom half depending on tomorrow night's result between Swansea and Fulham.
That win means Fulham leapfrog Crystal Palace and go into 18th place on goals scored. It's very tight at the bottom, though, as they're just two points behind 15th-placed West Brom.
Villa boss Lambert, meanwhile, will be very disappointed at a distinct lack of fight from his side. Misfiring striker Christian Benteke has now gone nine games without a goal.
It's FULL TIME at Craven Cottage and Fulham have picked up a vital win this afternoon, with a fine performance to match. The midfield was superb and Berbatov was on inspired form, and Meulensteen will be absolutely delighted.
(90’) BENTEKE TESTS STEKELENBURG!! The striker finally gets another attempt at goal as he's first to a loose ball, curling a dangerous effort which looks to be dipping just under the bar, but the Fulham shot-stopper produces a fine save to flick it over.
(90’) Substitute Marc Albrighton launches the set piece into the box and Clark gets on the end of it, but there's no pace on the header and it's an easy save for Stekelenburg.
(90’) Good defending from Baker, who does well to deal with a high ball under pressure from Berbatov and Kasami, before Villa get a free kick just inside the Fulham half.
(90’) It's a corner to Villa on the right-hand side and Westwood drills in a cross, but the whistle goes for a free kick to the hosts as the referee spots some pushing. We'll have three more minutes at Craven Cottage.
(89’) ANOTHER GOOD STRIKE FROM RIISE!! The full-back really wants a goal today, and he tests Guzan this time with a vicious strike from outside the box. The Villa goalkeeper is positioned well, though, and holds on to the ball.
(88’) GREAT CHANCE FOR KASAMI!! It's a lovely move down the right-hand side before it's pulled back to the substitute, who blazes high over the bar and almost out of the ground.
(87’) It's nearly job done for Fulham, who have the ball inside the Villa half and Baker is penalised for a push in midfield, giving the hosts a chance to run down the clock further.
(85’) Villa are still very unhappy about that penalty decision. That could have made for an uncomfortable last five minutes for the hosts.
(84’) Penalty? Great skill from Agbonlahor, who cuts inside Hughes and flicks the ball past the defender before being brought down. Nothing is given, but replays show the Villa forward might have been denied a clear spot kick there.
(83’) Dejagah nearly away!! Berbatov tries another deft flick which doesn't quite come off, but it bounces before Parker fires a half-volley over the top looking for his team-mate. Just cut out, though, and Villa have the ball.
(82’) Delph picks the ball up on the left-hand side and floats an early ball into the box looking for Benteke, but it's nowhere near accurate enough and Stekelenburg plucks it out of the air with ease.
--- 81’ Substitution M. Albrighton enters the game and replaces A. Weimann. ---
--- 81’ Substitution C. Herd is done for the day. M. Lowton is his replacement. ---
(81’) Matthew Lowton replaces Herd, who has had a tough afternoon and has apparently been struggling with an eye problem all match.
(80’) Into the final 10 minutes at Craven Cottage, and Villa look bereft of ideas at the moment. They saw plenty of possession and territory early in this half but the hosts have really asserted themselves now.
(78’) SO CLOSE FROM RIISE!! The full-back has been very impressive going forward today, and he strides towards the box once more. Amid encouragement from the crowd he belts a long-range effort which swerves just wide of Guzan's near post.
--- 77’ Substitution D. Duff enters play, replacing A. Kačaniklić. ---
(77’) Damien Duff is on for the hosts, replacing the impressive Kacaniklic. Fulham are in complete control of this game.
(76’) GREAT BLOCK!! That's superb from Herd, who shows real commitment to get in front of Riise, who was in space in the box and had fired a powerful shot at goal.
(75’) OFF THE LINE!! Kasami gets to the line and tries to pull it across the six-yard box. Baker's clearance hits Clark and looks bound for the goal before it's cleared off the line.
(74’) Westwood finds Tonev on the left, and the substitute skips past both Dejagah and Sidwell before firing an effort from 30 yards, but it hits Hughes and Fulham clear.
--- 73’ Substitution P. Kasami comes on for G. Karagounis. ---
(73’) It's Karagounis who comes off, as Pajtim Kasami replaces the veteran midfielder. A sign of intent from Meulenteen perhaps? Looks like he might want another goal.
(72’) Benteke is lucky to escape a booking, there, as he clatters Riise in the air with a late challenge. Meanwhile, it looks like the hosts are preparing a change.
(70’) CHANCES AT BOTH ENDS!! Dejagah tests Guzan with a low 20-yard effort and Berbatov nearly reaches the follow-up, before Benteke nearly gets on the end of a cross but Riise hacks it away from the floor. Both Weimann and Westwood then struggle to get it out of their feet before the former flicks a shot at goal. It hits a defender and the visitors want a penalty, but the referee isn't interested.
(69’) Fulham are really on top of this game now, and will want a third to put the result beyond doubt. Villa are still dangerous on the break.
--- 68’ Yellow card C. Herd goes into the referee's book. ---
(68’) That's rather petulant from Herd, who is challenged by Berbatov before the Villa defender takes out Karagounis with a poorly-timed tackle, earning him a yellow card.
(66’) Another chance! Riether is free on the right and drills in a low cross, which Sidwell slides in to meet but it hits a Villa defender and eventually goes back to Guzan.
(65’) OFF THE POST!! Dejagah does superbly to slide in and win the ball before getting up and playing the ball wide. It's fired into the box and Riise beats Guzan in the air, but his header loops down and flicks the upright.
(64’) Fulham have a free kick as Herd goes over the top of Berbatov in an aerial challenge. The defender has a cheeky dig at the Fulham man with his arm on the way down, but gets away with it.
(62’) Parker shoots wide!! Fulham aren't afraid to shoot, it seems, and Parker exchanges passes with Berbatov before slicing a 20-yard effort past Guzan's near post.
(61’) Oh dear. That's awful from Westwood, who gets the delivery all wrong, putting it straight into the stand behind the goal. Lambert does not look impressed.
(60’) Good work from Tonev, who flicks the ball past Parker before being clipped by the Fulham midfielder, and the visitors have a chance to fire in a dangerous ball...
(59’) DECENT HIT FROM KARAGOUNIS!! The midfielder has really solidified things for Fulham today, and he tries to help the hosts go further in front as he works the ball on to his right before unleashing an effort from 25 yards which fizzes just over the bar.
(58’) Once again we're up the other end straight away as Bacuna gets free on the right before firing in a cross looking for Benteke at the near post, but Senderos gets in front of him to head it behind for a corner.
(57’) More trouble in the Villa box as Riether's cross isn't completely dealt with and Sidwell gets to it first before trying to find Berbatov at the far post, but Baker manages to clear.
(55’) BERBATOV FIRES OVER!! It's the Bulgarian's turn to try a spectacular one as Parker floats a wonderful pass to the right-hand side of the box, and the Fulham striker meets it with a first-time volley which he blasts over the bar.
(54’) The set piece comes to nothing and goes behind off a Villa player, giving us all a chance to draw breath after that fast-paced opening to the half!
(53’) Straight up the other end!! Agbonlahor skips past Senderos with ease before floating a ball across the box. Weimann and Tonev come in late looking for it but Riise does well to get to it first and put it behind for a corner.
(52’) NEARLY FOR RIISE AND SENDEROS!! We've seen him do it for Liverpool, but the full-back doesn't quite get it right this time as he gets on the end of a diagonal ball with a first-time volley which he scuffs, but they have a corner. Senderos meets the set piece and powers a header at goal which Guzan does well to hold on to.
(51’) This is real end-to-end stuff, now. Fulham stop another Villa attack before it's spread wide to Kacaniklic, who is stopped in his tracks by Bacuna; legally this time.
(50’) Benteke should do better!! It comes out to Tonev on the right-hand side, and the substitute drills in a low corner, but Benteke's touch is too heavy and he is forced to lay back to Delph, whose shot is blocked. The hosts immediately break and Dejagah's low ball is just cut out before it reaches Sidwell at the far post.
(49’) Is that a smile from Berbatov? He's loving it out there as he produces an amazing backheel volley to find Sidwell, but sadly his flick came from an offside position.
(48’) The questions for Fulham, here, is whether they sit on their lead or press for more. At the moment they're the ones with the ball and seem to be carrying on as before.
(47’) Good start for Fulham, who are keeping the ball inside the Villa half. Dejagah receives the ball on the by-line but Clark slides in to put it behind for a corner, which evades everyone and comes to Westwood on the far side of the box.
--- 46’ Substitution K. El Ahmadi is replaced with A. Tonev. ---
(46’) The visitors get the ball rolling for the second half at Craven Cottage. Aleksandar Tonev is on for Villa as Lambert decides to change things immediately, with El Ahmadi coming off.
Not long until the restart, then. Will it be more of the same from Fulham, or can Villa assert themselves and get back into this match?
For Villa, the system change doesn't seem to have worked. They're overrun in the middle and are struggling to find a way through when they do have the ball. But for some brilliant defending by Baker and Clark, they could be even further behind.
That's the Berbatov we all enjoy watching. He showed some beautiful touches and sprayed some amazing passes around the pitch. The Fulham midfield has also been in complete control. Meulensteen will be a very happy man.
That's HALF TIME at Craven Cottage and Fulham take a 2-0 lead into the break, which you have to say is thoroughly deserved. Sidwell put the hosts in front with a dogged strike before Berbatov encapsulated his personality with a cool penalty to make it two.
(45’) There's a bit of confusion, here. Villa think they have a free kick, but the referee stops things and says he never blew for the foul. Eventually, after much chatting, a drop ball is given and Sidwell gives it back to Guzan. All a bit pointless, really.
(45’) Herd is down after going up for a header with Berbatov, but he should be OK to carry on as we enter two minutes of added time at the end of the half.
(44’) OVER FROM BACUNA!! Karagounis is penalised for a foul just outside the box and it's Bacuna who lines up the free kick, whipping it over the wall but also high and wide of Stekelenburg's goal.
(43’) That's a bit cheeky from Meulensteen, there. Dejagah thinks he's won a throw off Baker but it's given the other way. The midfielder drops the ball and the Fulham boss gives it a cheeky kick away to stop Baker taking it quickly.
(41’) Another great challenge from Baker, who slides in to stop Riether in his tracks out on the flank, before the hosts spurn the opportunity as Dejagah is caught offside.
(40’) The set piece doesn't find Weimann, who had peeled off at the far post, and Riether heads the ball away. Disappointing for the visitors, there, as that was a really good chance.
(39’) Villa win a free kick on the right-hand side of the box as Berbatov goes up to block an El Ahmadi cross. The visitors want a penalty but it's just outside the area and Westwood will fire this one in...
(37’) BERBATOV NEARLY MAKES IT THREE!! The Bulgaria striker is on fine form this afternoon, and he exchanges passes with Kacaniklic on the edge of the box before charging in and firing a shot with the outside of his right foot, which Guzan diverts behind with a good stop.
(35’) That's a waste from Dejagah. Kacaniklic strides forward before Berbatov drops deep and takes over before spreading an excellent pass wide to Dejagah, but the cross is far too hard and it goes out for a throw.
(34’) The visitors are in possession but aren't really making any progress inside the Fulham half as the Cottagers press well.
(33’) This is turning into a very good afternoon for Meulensteen and his men. Villa are usually most dangerous on the break but will now have to be the ones pressing forward.
(32’) DELPH GOES CLOSE!! What a lovely move from Villa as Delph intercepts the ball and shows some silky footwork to skip away from Sidwell and find Benteke, who flicks it on for the midfielder and Delph blasts it wide from a tight angle.
--- 30’ Goal! BERBATOV PUTS THE SPOT KICK AWAY!! Fulham are 2-0 up inside half an hour, and it's a typically nonchalant strike from the Bulgarian, as he strolls up to the ball before stroking it into the left-hand corner, sending Guzan the wrong way. ---
(29’) PENALTY TO FULHAM!! It's a brilliant break by the hosts as Berbatov sets Kacaniklic away with an absolutely stunning first-time pass. Bacuna sprints back to catch up but bundles the Fulham man over and the referee points to the spot.
(28’) Karagounis is clearly feeling much better. He tracks back well before taking out Agbonlahor with a strong shoulder. The ensuing free kick causes problems as Sidwell is forced to send a defensive header just wide of the post.
(27’) Good chance for Villa as Weimann sets Agbonlahor away down the right, and he whips in an early cross looking for Delph, but the midfielder is too late to get on the end of it and Stekelenburg claims comfortably.
(26’) Karagounis is back on after getting the OK from the physio, and we're back underway.
(25’) Ouch, that looks painful for Karagounis. Herd goes up for a header and the Fulham midfielder comes in late, ending up with a clattering of his own as the Villa defender can't stop in mid-air. The Greek comes off worse but it's Villa who have the free kick.
(23’) Close!! Berbatov drops deep to collect the ball and plays a beautiful pass around the defence looking for the run of Kacaniklic, but it just evades the wide man and Guzan rushes out to clear.
(22’) That's no more than the hosts deserve. Villa had a brief spell of pressure but the momentum has mostly been in favour of the hosts.
--- 21’ Assist A. Dejagah gave the assist. ---
--- 21’ Goal! SIDWELL PUTS THE HOSTS AHEAD!! Fulham had just stepped up a gear and their reward comes. Sidwell plays it forward and it flicks up high off a white shirt before Berbatov and Dejagah link up well. The latter flicks a ball beyond the defence and Sidwell continues his run, chasing it to the line and hooking his left foot around it to send it past Guzan and into the far corner. ---
--- 19’ Yellow card F. Delph is yellow-carded. ---
(19’) Real pressure from Fulham! Delph takes out Karagounis but play goes on and Berbatov works the ball to Kacaniklic, whose low shot is blocked but the pressure continues. Riether pops up on the left and swings in a cross which Berbatov meets but can't direct towards goal.
(18’) FULHAM SHOULD BE AHEAD!! Unbelievable drama!! The hosts have two brilliant chances in succession as Dejagah is away beyond the defence, but Clark produces a stunning last-ditch challenge to deny the Iranian, before Kacaniklic gets to the rebound but is denied on the line by Baker. Incredible!
(16’) STEKELENBURG DENIES BENTEKE!! After Senderos cuts in to stop Delph, he and Riether cause themselves their own problems, giving it away and the ball is worked inside to Benteke, who works the ball on to his right before firing a low shot at the Fulham goalkeeper from the edge of the box.
(15’) Westwood looks for Weimann on the edge of the box with a high ball, but Hughes watches it closely and heads clear. The Austrian had something of a height disadvantage, there.
(14’) Villa are just starting to grow into this game, now. The hosts' bright start has faded away, somewhat. Sidwell watches Benteke closely, though, and does well to stop the striker turning and then clear the ball forward.
(12’) WIDE FROM BENTEKE!! It's a massive let-off for Riether, who flails at a high ball over the top, completely missing it and letting Agbonlahor go free down the left-hand side of the box. The Villa man crosses for Benteke, who meets it with a late run and powers a low header wide of the far post.
(11’) The hosts are focussing most of their attacks down that left-hand side, and again Riise gets forward, this time turning Herd inside and out but overhitting his touch past the defender and the ball goes out for a goal kick.
(10’) Villa win a free kick just inside the Fulham have and Westwood drills a flat ball into the area. Baker manages to get on to it, but gets more on it that he needs to and the ball flies way over the bar.
(9’) FANTASTIC SAVE!! After Berbatov just misses out on meeting a Kacaniklic cross from the left, the striker rises to connect with a corner from the other side, guiding a header towards the top corner and drawing a superb one-handed stop from Guzan.
(7’) Agbonlahor is penalised for a foul on Parker deep inside the Fulham half and the hosts have it back. The visitors haven't got going yet.
(6’) The visitors try to set their first counter away as Benteke links up with Agbonlahor, but the latter's flick doesn't quite work out for the Belgian and Fulham clear.
(5’) Delph tries to bring the ball away for Villa but Karagounis slides in superbly to steal the ball back. The hosts are looking determined in these opening stages.
(4’) Riise fires in a long throw but it's headed away. Parker brings the ball down and looks for Riether but El Ahmadi cuts it out before he's fouled by the Fulham midfielder.
(3’) Villa already look happy to sit back and allow the hosts to keep possession. Good work from Herd on the flank, though, as he wins a throw off Kacaniklic deep inside his own half.
(2’) Good positive start from Fulham, who break down the right through Berbatov, but Delph is there to win the ball. Riether wins it back, though, and sends a pass through for Parker, but Delph does brilliantly to slide in and take the ball away.

(45’) Martin Olsson clears downfield and Wes Hoolahan is on hand to tee up Johan Elmander, who has been anonymous so far, but the Swede's effort sums up his first-half offerings - woeful, as the ball flies way off target.
(45’) Raheem Sterling wins a corner off Martin Olsson down the right flank but Sebastien Bassong is equal to the delivery from the corner and clears.
--- 43’ Yellow card S. Gerrard is cautioned by the referee. ---
(43’) Steven Gerrard is into the book as he scythes down Nathan Redmond and from Norwich's subsequent attack, Daniel Agger does well to stand up Jonny Howson, who had strode forward well towards the area.
(41’) Nathan Redmond has been a rare bright spark for the Canaries this afternoon and he supplies the goods from out wide again but this time Simon Mignolet can gather rather easily.
(39’) Raheem Sterling sets off down the left before whipping in a ball towards Luis Suarez but Ryan Bennett averts the danger but it is only brief respite as Steven Gerrard tests John Ruddy from 20 yards out.
(37’) Norwich briefly threaten as Nathan Redmond floats a ball into the area but John Flanagan can clear with ease. Liverpool are romping to victory here.
--- 35’ Assist The assist came from R. Sterling. ---
--- 35’ Goal! GOAL! Remarkable, absolutely remarkable. Luis Suarez completes his hat-trick with a goal of the highest order and creates Liverpool history in the making. After flicking the ball over a bewildered Leroy Fer, Suarez advances into the area and drills past Ruddy to become the first-ever Liverpool player to score a hat-trick three times against the same opposition. Wow. ---
--- 34’ Yellow card J. Allen gets yellow. ---
(34’) Joe Allen is cautioned for hauling back Bradley Johnson but Nathan Redmond's free kick is straight at a grateful Simon Mignolet.
(33’) Luis Suarez is at the heart of everything and almost sets up two presentable chances for his side first with a cross to Raheem Sterling, who is flagged offside, before finding Steven Gerrard in the box only for Leroy Fer to recover and clear.
(31’) Bradley Johnson goes for goal from just outside the area but it flashes wide of Simon Mignolet's left post. The Canaries continue to threaten here.
--- 29’ Assist The assist came from Philippe Coutinho. ---
--- 29’ Goal! GOAL! Luis Suarez is at the double and while this is far less glamorous than his first, it is still vitally important in building on his side's lead as he turns Philippe Coutinho's corner home from close range. The Brazilian's delivery is excellent but Suarez does brilliantly to flick into the back of the net with the ball bouncing. What a player. ---
(27’) Norwich City are tracking back to good effect however, and both Russell Martin and Wes Hoolahan have to be on red alert to deal with John Flanagan and Philippe Coutinho's forward surges into the box.
(25’) Norwich go so close to a leveller and it's Wes Hoolahan for a fourth time now who has the chance but this time, he really should have put his side ahead. Bradley Johnson's centre is deliciously placed but Hoolahan goes for goal with his left foot when his right would have been better suited and volleys harmlessly over the bar. A huge let off for Liverpool.
(23’) Philippe Coutinho goes close to finding a route to a second Liverpool goal on two occasions in the space of a few minutes. First, the diminutive playmaker whips a cross across the face of goal but no-one is there from a Liverpool perspective before playing a one-two with Raheem Sterling before unleashing an effort from range but Russell Martin was on hand to mop up for Norwich.
--- 20’ Yellow card B. Johnson gets yellow. ---
(20’) Bradley Johnson cynically hauls down Luis Suarez to gift Liverpool a free kick around 35 yards out. Suarez declines the opportunity to shoot on this occasion but the Reds try to pass the ball through to him, only for John Ruddy to collect.
(19’) Norwich's riposte is to march to the other end and find another avenue towards goal but Wes Hoolahan is frustrated by those in front of him yet again as Steven Gerrard is on hand to get a block in.
(17’) John Flanagan makes inroads up the left hand side of the pitch but Norwich eventually clear as Liverpool look to press home their advantage, handed to them by a Luis Suarez masterclass.
--- 15’ Goal! GOAL! Oh my word, this man is capable of just about anything. Proof is in the pudding with this goal as Luis Suarez scores one of the goals of the season so far. John Ruddy's clearance isn't particularly great and when Martin Skrtel nods the ball back into the Norwich half, Suarez picks the ball up 25 yards out and volleys into the top corner past a stunned Ruddy. Breathtaking. ---
(14’) Luis Suarez is denied by some brilliant defending from Russell Martin as he looked to bend the ball towards goal before Glen Johnson finds Jordan Henderson, whose hooked effort across goal is poor and lacking in conviction.
(12’) Liverpool are slowly beginning to build some momentum here and come close again as Glen Johnson and Jordan Henderson both go close in quick succession. Johnson has an effort blocked before Henderson fires high and wide when well placed.
(11’) Steven Gerrard is the latest to get a shot off on goal but finds Jonny Howson in between him and goal after Philippe Coutinho and Glen Johnson had combined to tee up the skipper.
(9’) It's poor play from Liverpool again but Norwich fail to benefit. Joe Allen is sloppy in possession and the ball breaks for Wes Hoolahan once again, who charges forward with intent.The Irishman gets a shot off on goal but Simon Mignolet is equal to it, getting down well to his left to hold onto the ball.
(7’) Now Norwich are almost in again in a yo-yo like start to the match. Nathan Redmond, again, is the instigator with a determined run down the left before crossing for Wes Hoolahan. 

Unfortunately the Irishman could not adjust in time and scuffed his effort with Raheem Sterling in attendance to help clear the ball upfield.
(6’) Philippe Coutinho goes on an incredible mazy run, committing three challenges and shapes to shoot but Sebastien Bassong makes a terrific block to thwart the Brazilian.
(4’) All that after Nathan Redmond had launched a cross into the area which Martin Skrtel did well to clear under pressure. Luis Suarez then tries to release the ball down the left wing to Philippe Coutinho but Russell Martin shepherds the ball out.
(2’) Bright start from Norwich City, who engineer the first shooting chance of the evening as Johnny Howson takes aim from range but his right-footed effort ultimately sails over the bar.
(1’) And we're underway here at Anfield as Liverpool kick us off after the teams swap ends.
Luis Suarez, though, has scored seven in his last three matches against this opposition, netting two hat-tricks in the process and, as a collective, Liverpool plundered five goals past Norwich in both of last season's meetings.
The Reds badly struggled in Daniel Sturridge's absence at Hull and looked bereft of ideas up front, with even Luis Suarez struggling to exert his matchwinning influence but Liverpool's home form - defeat to Southampton aside - cannot be faulted, with five wins out of six at Anfield.
Liverpool's surprise 3-1 loss at Hull was the second time in successive matches that Liverpool have conceded three goals and, having registered three clean sheets from their first trio of fixtures, Brendan Rodgers' side have kept just one in their last 10.
It may come as something of a surprise to Norwich City fans and the Liverpool faithful alike that Gary Hooper is dropped instead of Johan Elmander after the former's matchwinning contribution against Crystal Palace at the weekend, which sealed a second win in three league games.
And here's the Norwich City starting XI. Ruddy; Martin, R Bennett, Bassong, Olsson; Redmond, Howson, Fer, Johnson, Hoolahan; Elmander.Substitutes: Nash, Whittaker, Turner, Hooper, Garrido, Becchio, Murphy.

Chris Hughton, meanwhile, makes just the solitary change as Bradley Johnson comes in for Gary Hooper meaning a slight reshuffle for his Norwich City charges.

Hooper's relegation to the bench should mean the Canaries will line up in a 4-5-1 formation as Hughton tries to thwart the Liverpool midfield with added numbers.
The team news is in and Liverpool manager Brendan Rodgers makes three changes to the side that lost 3-1 to Hull City on Sunday, with Daniel Agger, Joe Allen and Philippe Coutinho stepping in for Kolo Toure, Lucas Leiva and Victor Moses, who all disappointed in defeat to the Tigers.
Good evening and welcome to this LIVE commentary of Liverpool v Norwich at Anfield.

With Wayne Rooney now suspended for Saturday's encounter with Newcastle, David Moyes will be praying that Robin Van Persie can recover from his groin injury as Manchester United go in search of their first league win in four games. As for Everton, they face a tricky trip to leaders Arsenal but if they can produce a similar performance to what they showed tonight, they could halt the Gunners' title charge. That's it from me, Max Bentley, on this live commentary, thanks for tuning in. Until next time, goodbye.
As for Everton, they stay in fifth place but extend their lead over Manchester United to five points. Having already beaten Chelsea this season, Roberto Martinez's side are certainly showing that they are capable of beating anyone on their day and some might say they should be considered as top four contenders.
That result means that Manchester United's 12-game unbeaten run in all competitions is brought to an abrupt halt and David Moyes' side now trail Premier League leaders Arsenal by 12 points. With Manchester City, Chelsea and Liverpool all set for three points, it has not been a good day for the Red Devils.
FT: Manchester United 0-1 Everton. Bryan Oviedo's late strike ensures it is not a happy reunion for David Moyes against his former club. His goal marks a first Everton win at Old Trafford for 21 years as the Roberto Martinez revolution continues.
(90’) There does not appear to be any sign of a Manchester United fightback here and Lukaku almost doubles Everton's lead when he collects Osman's pass outside the box before firing a left-footed effort narrowly wide. With Arsenal closing in on three points over Hull, Manchester United look set to be twelve points off the Premier League leaders.
--- 90’ +3 Yellow card R. Giggs gets yellow. ---
--- 90’ +2 Substitution The Everton fans are now shouting 'You're getting sacked in the morning' as their side close in on a historic victory against David Moyes' Manchester United. Roberto Martinez makes a final change for the Toffees as Kevin Mirallas is replaced Steven Naismith. ---
(90’) Gerard Deulofeu's pace is causing this tiring Manchester United defence problems and he gets in behind Evra again but cannot beat De Gea with his cheeky chip. The Everton fans tant their former boss with chants of 'Are you watching David Moyes?'
(88’) Incidentally, just to rub salt into the wounds, Lukaku's cross was deflected into Oviedo's path via the legs of Fellaini. That's the Costa Rican's second goal in as many games, since replacing Baines in the Everton line-up.
--- 86’ Assist R. Lukaku provided the assist. ---
--- 86’ Goal! EVERTON TAKE THE LEAD! Moments after Mirallas' free kick crashes against the post, Bryan Oviedo wheels away to celebrate in front of the travelling fans as he drills a shot into the far corner after connecting with Lukaku's low deflected cross. Everton are set for their first win at Old Trafford in 21 years, sensational! ---
(84’) Everton win a free kick in a fantastic position just outside the box when Valencia clumsily trips Coleman. Leighton Baines watches on from the stands as Mirallas lines up the strike.
(82’) Marouane Fellaini is fortunate to escape a yellow card after a late, mistimed challenge on McCarthy. The Belgium midfielder is still settling into life at Old Trafford and awaiting his first goal for the club.
--- 81’ Substitution J. Hernández comes on for D. Welbeck. ---
(81’) It's the final straw for David Moyes as he makes his last substitution, introducing Javier Hernandez in place of Danny Welbeck. Roberto Martinez responds with a change of his own, with Leon Osman replacing Steven Pienaar.
--- 80’ Substitution L. Osman enters the game and replaces S. Pienaar. ---
(79’) The Everton chances are starting to dry up now and Lukaku has received little service in the last twenty minutes or so. Oviedo produces a burst forward from the left-back but his cross cannot pick out a blue shirt in the box.
(77’) It's all Manchester United here and they continue to pour forward. Januzaj has certainly made an impression since coming on but neither he nor any of his teammates can penetrate this resilient Everton defence. Are David Moyes' side set for a third consecutive league draw? There are thirteen minutes remaining at Old Trafford.
(75’) Tim Howard, with his impressive beard, is producing an equally impressive performance here to keep his former side at bay. Ryan Giggs swings a teasing cross into the box but the American goalkeeper comes through a crowd of players to punch the ball clear.
(73’) HOW HAVE MANCHESTER UNITED NOT SCORED? Rooney whips a superb corner into the penalty box and Evra meets it, forcing Howard into a brilliant reflex save. Welbeck then pounces onto the rebound but can only see his header come back off the crossbar. The ball is then tossed into the box from the right but Rooney wildly blazes a volley into row z. Everton's goal certainly lived a charmed life there.
(70’) JANUZAJ GOES CLOSE! That Deulofeu miss almost proves so costly for Everton as Howard is forced into action to tip Januzaj's swerving effort over the bar. That has livened the Old Trafford crowd up.
--- 69’ Substitution Gerard Deulofeu enters play, replacing R. Barkley. ---
(69’) WHAT A CHANCE FOR EVERTON! Deulofeu almost makes an instant impact when he finds space behind Evra down the right wing but he can only fire straight at the legs of De Gea with the goal gaping. A let-off for the hosts.
(68’) Roberto Martinez opts to make his first substitution of the game and Ross Barkley, who has once again been impressive, is replaced by the weekend hero Gerard Deulofeu. Can the Barcelona youngster make the difference?
(66’) The Manchester United fans scream for a penalty after Pienaar appears to clumsily nudge Januzaj to the floor inside the box. However, Martin Adkinson is not interested in the appeals and waves play on.
(64’) It's no surprise that this Everton defence has kept the joint-highest number of clean sheets (seven) in the league this season. They are so organised at the back and are dealing with everything that Manchester United are throwing into the box. It seems that United may be missing a certain Robin Van Persie this evening.
(62’) You can sense the confidence running through this Everton side and moments after Oviedo fires a shot narrowly wide, Barkley sees his effort well blocked by Fellaini.
--- 61’ Yellow card Wayne Rooney picks up the first booking of the match after a nasty challenge on Jagielka after the Everton defender had played the ball. That means he will be suspended for the home weekend encounter with Newcastle. ---
(59’) Nani has struggled to show his form from two seasons ago and he instantly frustrates the Old Trafford faithful by firing wildly over the bar from Welbeck's lay-off. Will it prove to be an inspired substitution from David Moyes?
--- 58’ Substitution Rafael is replaced with A. Januzaj. ---
--- 58’ Substitution Nani enters play, replacing S. Kagawa. ---
(57’) There's going to be a double change for Manchester United as David Moyes attempts to shake things up. Shinji Kagawa and Rafael are the players to make way, with Nani and Adnan Januzaj, who mysteriously found himself on the Young Sports Personality of the Year shortlist, coming on.
(55’) The home fans are growing restless themselves however and Mirallas produces a brilliant feint to jink past Evra before slicing a shot well wide of the top right-hand corner. That opening goal somehow continues to elude us. Can Everton end their 21-year Old Trafford hoodoo?
(53’) Roberto Martinez is looking a little agitated on the touchline as his side continue to come under pressure. Rooney attempts to bulldoze his way into the box but a combination of McCarthy and Distin manage to smuggle the ball to safety.
(51’) Manchester United have made a brilliant start to the second half and Valencia surges past Oviedo down the right wing but struggles to pick out Welbeck with his cross into the box. I wonder whether we will see Hernandez introduced soon.
(49’) JAGIELKA TO THE RESCUE! McCarthy finds himself dispossessed excellently by Fellaini and the Belgian feeds Rooney who slips a ball beyond the Everton defence for Welbeck to chase. It's a straight race between Jagielka and Welbeck and the Everton defender produces a superb sliding challenge to deny his international teammate a route to goal. Fantastic defending, he had to get that right.
(47’) GOOD SHOT FROM EVRA! The French left-back comes close to opening the scoring within 90 seconds of the restart when he latches onto a loose ball outside the box, but his fizzing strike towards goal is well palmed over by Howard.
(46’) Pienaar and Barkley get the second half underway for Everton after a brief delay for Lukaku who was having trouble getting his gloves on. There have been no substitutions at the break.
With Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool and Manchester City all winning, the pressure is really on David Moyes to get three points out of this game. As things stand, Manchester United are eleven points adrift of pacesetters Arsenal.
Premier League half-time scores: Arsenal 1-0 Hull, Liverpool 3-0 Norwich, Southampton 0-1 Aston Villa, Stoke 0-0 Cardiff, Sunderland 1-2 Chelsea, Swansea 1-0 Newcastle. In the later kick-offs, Manchester City lead West Brom 2-0 whilst Fulham v Tottenham is goalless.
HT: Manchester United 0-0 Everton. It's all square at the midway point after a fantastic end-to-end half of football. Wayne Rooney went the closest to opening the scoring when he struck the post but Romelu Lukaku has looked equally dangerous, forcing David De Gea into several smart saves. Expect some goals in the second half.
(45’) Manchester United look to snatch the lead just before the break but Jagielka produces a brilliant header to prevent Fellaini from nodding in Rooney's flick-on. I can't quite believe this game is still 0-0.
(43’) Moments after Barkley spurns a glorious three-on-two counter attack opportunity for Everton, Manchester United go close to opening the scoring themselves. Kagawa feeds a brilliant low cross into the box from the left but it somehows evades the outstretched boot of Welbeck before going through Rooney's legs. As the ball comes back into the box from the right, Howard shows his reflexes to deny Rooney's hooked effort.
(41’) GOOD SAVE FROM DE GEA! Lukaku is certainly getting the better of Vidic in the first half here and he muscles his way into the box once again before his drilled right-footed effort is saved by the legs of the Spanish goalkeeper. It's rather frightening that Lukaku is still only 20.
(40’) Everton are defending brilliantly here and every time Manchester United attack, there a crowd of blue shirts blocking their way in the box. Rafael tries to pick out Kagawa in the box but Oviedo makes a crucial interception. The Costa Rican has impressed in Baines' absence.
(38’) BARKLEY GOES CLOSE! The Everton youngster has only started one of the last four games but he shows his potential by holding off the challenge of Fellaini before firing a left-footed shot over the bar from just outside the box. He will certainly be hoping to achieve a spot in Roy Hodgson's 23-man World Cup squad.
(36’) Elsewhere in the Premier League, Luis Suarez has notched a 35-minute hat trick as Liverpool lead Norwich 3-0. Arsenal and Chelsea also lead in their respective matches against Hull and Sunderland.
(34’) Everton are looking lively whenever they attack however and Mirallas wiggles his way past three red shirts but Lukaku's lay-off is just behind Barkley. Will we see a goal before half time?
(31’) Manchester United are in the ascendency here and Valencia's cross causes panic inside the Everton penalty box but Jagielka just about manages to hack the ball clear. The atmosphere has mellowed a little here at Old Trafford.
(29’) ROONEY HITS THE POST! It's end-to-end stuff at Old Trafford and Wayne Rooney goes within inches of opening the scoring when his shot from outside the box takes a deflection before striking the inside of the post. Howard reacts quickly to deny Kagawa from converting the rebound.
(26’) Lukaku's strength is causing the Manchester United defence all sorts of problems and he bulldozes his way down the right wing but fails to pick out a blue shirt with his low cross. I'd be surprised if this one stayed 0-0.
(24’) SO CLOSE FROM GIGGS! Rooney plays a neat pass out wide to Rafael on the overlap and the Brazilian whips a splendid cross into the middle. Giggs surges into the box late to meet the ball with a glancing header but it flashes inches past the far post with Howard stranded. That would have been a brilliant goal.
(22’) Kagawa is getting himself into some dangerous areas for Manchester United and he capitalises upon an error at the back by Jagielka but cannot quite lift the ball over the advancing Howard and the American goalkeeper makes a vital stop.
(20’) GOOD DEFENDING FROM MANCHESTER UNITED! Romelu Lukaku shows his strength to muscle international compatriot Fellaini off the ball and then surges past Smalling and towards goal. However, just as he looks set to pull the trigger, Fellaini tracks back to nip the ball away.
(19’) The home fans are screaming for a free kick on the edge of the box as they believe Howard has carried the ball outside of his area. However, it seems that the goalkeeper with the evergrowing beard did drop the ball just before he left his area. Good call from the referee.
(18’) Coleman is getting into some brilliant advanced positions down the right but the Irish full-back is prevented from getting his cross into the box after a brilliant challenge from Evra. There were plenty of blue shirts waiting for the cross there.
(17’) GOOD SAVE FROM HOWARD! Manchester United are starting to grow into this game and Evra does brilliantly this time to pick out Rooney inside the box but the striker's low strike is well blocked by the legs of the former Manchester United goalkeeper. Incidentally, Rooney is looking for his 150th Premier League goal for Manchester United this evening.
(15’) Ryan Giggs actually made his Manchester United debut against Everton back in 1992. What a servant he has been to his club and the Premier League!
(14’) Manchester United threaten for the first time in the match when Kagawa feeds the ball out wide to Evra. However, the French left-back seems to get stuck in two minds and fizzes the ball out of play wastefully.
(13’) Everton have a decent record against United in recent years, having won two of the last seven meetings and drawing another two. The Red Devils have not lost at home to the Toffees in their last 20 top-flight meetings, though, and won the corresponding fixture 2-0 last season thanks to goals from Ryan Giggs and Robin Van Persie.
(11’) A few jeers ring out from the travelling support as Fellaini gets hold of the ball in the middle of the park. Manchester United look to enjoy a sustained spell of possession to stem the early Everton pressure.
(9’) GOOD SAVE FROM DE GEA! Moments after Mirallas' flicked header from Pienaar's corner flashes just past the far post, the Belgian attacker cuts inside Rafael before fizzing a shot at goal which De Gea does well to tip over. It's all Everton in the opening nine minutes.
(7’) Everton have started brilliantly here and Barkley bursts forward from midfield before finding Lukaku on the left side of the box. The powerful striker attempts to get his shot away but Vidic produces a good block to deflect the ball behind for the game's first corner.
(4’) Everton are clearly not here to sit back and Lukaku goes close when he fires wide from the edge of the box. Remember that the Belgian striker scored a hat trick against Manchester United for West Brom on the last day of last season.
(2’) It's a slow start at Old Trafford with both sides feeling their way into the contest. Seamus Coleman attempts to find Lukaku with his cross from the right but Smalling produces a good header to get the ball clear.
The players emerge from the tunnel to a brilliant reception from both sets of fans and it is good to see the travelling supporters applaud David Moyes as he walks towards the dugout. Can he mastermind a victory over his former employers? Kickoff is minutes away...
Both teams have strikers who are in fantastic goalscoring form. Wayne Rooney has scored ten goals in 16 appearances for Manchester United this season whilst Romelu Lukaku has notched eight goals in ten games for Everton since moving on loan from Chelsea.
As for Everton, Roberto Martinez makes two changes to the team which defeated Stoke 4-0 on Saturday. Despite his man-of-the-match performance, on-loan Barcelona youngster Gerard Deulofeu is replaced by Kevin Mirallas in the starting XI whilst Ross Barkley comes in for Leon Osman. Romelu Lukaku, who was named as the runner-up in Tuttosport's Golden Boy award earlier today, starts as the lone striker.
David Moyes makes three changes to the side which drew 2-2 with Tottenham on Sunday. Rafael returns from injury to start at right-back, with Chris Smalling being moved infield to replace Jonny Evans. Former Everton star Marouane Fellaini starts alongside Ryan Giggs in the centre of midfield with Phil Jones suspended and Tom Cleverley dropping to the bench. Robin Van Persie remains sidelined with a groin injury so in-form Wayne Rooney leads the line once again.
EVERTON (4-2-3-1): Howard; Coleman, Distin, Jagielka, Oviedo; McCarthy, Barry; Pienaar, Barkley, Mirallas; Lukaku.
MANCHESTER UNITED (4-2-3-1): De Gea; Rafael, Smalling, Vidic, Evra; Fellaini, Giggs; Valencia, Kagawa, Welbeck; Rooney.
Without further ado, here are the line-up's, starting with a Robin Van Persie-less Manchester United.
Manchester United are unbeaten in their last 12 games in all competitions whilst Everton have lost only one game (a 3-1 away defeat to Manchester City) in the league this season, the lowest in the Premier League. Who can secure the valuable three points tonight? Bringing you all the action from Old Trafford, my name is Max Bentley.
As for Everton, they occupy a respectable fifth place in the table and new boss Roberto Martinez has certainly managed to follow in Moyes' footsteps and bring more entertaining football and good results to Goodison Park. Having shared the spoils in a fascinating 3-3 draw in the Merseyside Derby with Liverpool eleven days ago, Everton returned to winning ways at the weekend by thumping Stoke 4-0 at home.
Manchester United have stumbled to consecutive 2-2 draws to Cardiff and Tottenham in their previous two league matches, albeit with a record 5-0 UEFA Champions League away victory to Bayern Leverkusen sandwiched in between. Moyes' men sit in a disappointing eighth position in the table and with Arsenal showing no sign of relent at the summit, the Red Devils can ill-afford to drop any more points.
Having enjoyed eleven years and 516 matches as Everton manager, David Moyes sits in the opposing dugout this evening as his Manchester United side go in search of a much-needed three points. The fair-haired Scotsman left an everlasting legacy at the Goodison Park outfit when leaving to replace Sir Alex Ferguson in the summer but he will harbour no sentimental thoughts today as he hopes to get the Premier League Champions back to winning ways.

That's it, 0-0. This result won't suit either side but Malky Mackay will be the happier of the two managers. His side have recovered from losing to Arsenal and have a point on the road. (49’) The corner is taken by Whittingham again but Campbell mistimes his jump and the ball runs out for a throw in to Stoke.

Statistically very even half. Both sides managed seven shots , where Stoke had two on target compared to Cardiff's one. The Potters have have had more possession, 56 to 44 per cent.

(37’) The Bluebirds really are that tonight, Wearing their blue away strip. Could be worse, they could be about to be re-named Cardiff Tigers.
(35’) It's too near Begovic who launches the ball down field for the counter. It falls nicely to Arnautovic but Caulker nicks it off him and plays it wide.

So, let's see who they've selected for tonight's encounter, we'll start with the home side.
For Malky Mackay and Cardiff, two home games against Manchester United and Arsenal yielded just one point, but more concerning is there overall form. Just one win in seven matches. Both managers know how important it is to beat the teams around you, especially with the Christmas season about to begin, they'll want as many points on the board before the new year as possible.
Worryingly for the Potters they have won just once in the Premier League since August, something Hughes will be desperate to change tonight. Former boss Tony Pulis has already managed one win with Crystal Palace and he's only been there two games. I wonder if Stoke fans would rather be happy with mid table safety in the Premiership or their new passing style in the Championship? We'll find out in May.
Mark Hughes will be looking for a response from his players tonight after they were hammered 4-0 at the weekend away to Everton. Martinez's side were brilliant, but the manner of the defeat will be worrying for Hughes too – only three times in their six Premier League seasons have Stoke been beaten more heavily (5-0 at both Bolton and Manchester United and 7-0 at Chelsea).

What a game, a seven-goal thriller at the Stadium of Light. Eden Hazard was the star of the show, he gave Bardsley a torrid night and was involved in everything good about the Blues. Bardsley summed up a manic finish when he followed an own-goal up with an actual goal late on. Chelsea were worth the victory but Sunderland can take plenty of heart from the fight they put up.
