(81’) None of Clark's substitutes have had any real effect on this game, with Anichebe being as consistently absent as Long was in the first half. Gera has offered nothing on the right hand side, and again City's second-choice left-back of Kolarov, that is somewhat worrying.
(79’) MILNER! The substitute fires a well-struck effort straight at Myhill, who claims with ease. City are happy to sit back in their shape and break at their leisure, and the away fans are now enjoying their comfortable away visit to the Midlands.
(78’) The last ten minutes of the game are rapidly approaching, and there's no foreseeable way for the hosts to get back into this game. Any pressure has been rather fleeting and inpenetrative, with Berahino providing the only optimism that the Baggies can improve offensively in the future.
--- 77’ Substitution Javi García enters the game and replaces S. Nasri. ---
--- 76’ Substitution M. Vydra enters play, replacing M. Amalfitano. ---
(76’) OFFSIDE! Dzeko looks to race in behind a very high Baggies' defensive line, but the linesman raises his flag immediately. The Bosnian will presumably want to turn this game into a rout, and get himself on the scoresheet, to prove that he merits a starting place ahead of Negredo.
--- 74’ Goal! GOOOOOAL! YAYA TOURE CONVERTS THE PENALTY! The Ivorian smashes the ball rather centrally, but it's too powerful for Myhill to deal with! West Brom have improved in the second half, and that goal is a definite sucker punch! City lead 3-0! ---
(73’) PENALTY! Kolarov is brought down by Yacob, and the referee makes no mistake, pointing to the stop immediately! The Serbian danced around the outstretched foot of Yacob, and was caught by the midfielder!
(71’) West Brom are slowly starting to press more players forward with every attack and set piece, leaving themselves very open to the counter attack. Given the amount of time left and the result, Clark is clearly beginning to try his luck at getting back into the game as a contest before it's too late. One goal now could make all the difference.
--- 69’ Substitution J. Milner enters the game and replaces S. Agüero. ---
(69’) Slightly more than 20 minutes left on the clock, and Pantilimon is yet to be troubled in this game. Aside from watching several skidding shots fizz wide of the target, the Romanian has had very little to do, and looks well on his way to an easy clean sheet.
(67’) City have gone quiet in terms of creating chances, but remain very comfortable. With Fernandinho and Toure screening the defence, and West Brom not managing to break at pace, Pellegrini's gameplan is continuing to work well. All that needs to be done is the continual injection of fresh legs.
--- 65’ Substitution V. Anichebe comes on for S. Long. ---
(65’) Gera receives a very warm reception on his return from injury, and rightly so given his contribution to West Brom as both a top flight and second-tier football club. He'll need to produce something special to drag the Baggies back into this game, however.
--- 64’ Substitution Z. Gera enters the game and replaces J. Morrison. ---
(64’) Brilliant tracking back from Fernandinho yet again. The Brazilian has been everything this evening, picking up the pieces and slowing the Baggies' breaks whenever they look to hit City on the counter. Certainly an unsung hero in a very talented squad.
(62’) Clark looks to change the game with a double substitution, throwing on Anichebe and Gera. The Nigerian striker is capable of acting as an attacking catalyst, as his physical ability should keep him ever-presently in the game, battling with the likes of Kompany and Demichelis. Something extra for Kompany and Co. to worry about.
(60’) Half an hour left on the clock, and this game still looks a bit beyond West Brom. The home side have given a better account of themselves in the second half, but it's a little bit too late, given City's sizeable goal cushion. Long continues to be anonymous, it would be unsurprising to see Sessegnon or Anichebe introduced soon.
(58’) Fernandinho tracks back excellently to deny Amalfitano! The Frenchman is picked out behind City's defensive line, but the Brazilian does well to pick up the pieces from Kompany's block to clear the danger! Berahino then fires harmlessly wide from range.
(57’) Good defending from McAuley! A clever piece of skill from Navas creates a bit of space for Zabaleta to deliver a back post cross, but McAuley is there once again as an aerial presence.
(55’) AGUERO! Absolutely delightful skill and control from the former Atletico striker, as he dances around two West Brom defenders with consummate ease. Rolling the ball past the first, before weaves his way past the second. Beautiful footwork.
(53’) Steve Clark won't be too disappointed with how his side have started the second half, but there's certainly a sense that City are allowing West Brom greater space and freedom, to invite them forward. Such an action would draw the home team out, making them susceptible to City's pacey breaks.
(51’) Great through ball from Brunt! The Northern Ireland international slots his pass inbetween Demichelis and Kolarov, allowing for Long to chase, but his teammate is outsmarted by the former Bayern Munich centre-half. Another brief opening for the hosts.
(50’) LONG! The lone West Brom striker goes down in the penalty area, after squeezing between two visiting defenders! The referee didn't look interested whatsoever, but the crowd are incensed! I think that official was right, Long did look to dive there!
(49’) AGUERO! Myhill does well to pluck the Argentine's cross from the air, as Dzeko shaped to attack it at the back post yet again. The Baggies' goalkeeper has done well to disrupt the harmony between the City striking partnership when he can.
(47’) Audacious from Nasri! The Frenchman weaves past Reid and Morrison, before shimmying back inside the Republic of Ireland right-back and nutmegging the Scot once again! The former Arsenal man is full of confidence here tonight.
(46’) We are back underway for the second half! City dominated the opening 45 minutes, grabbing two well-deserved goals for their efforts, but the Baggies showed in the final ten minutes that they can threaten Pantilimon's goal. Long has been quiet, but Clark has options on the bench.
Pellegrini will certainly be buoyed by what he has seen in the opening 45 minutes, as the combination of Dzeko and Aguero upfront has worked excellently. Chances have flowed for the away side, and the Chilean coach will definitely be hoping that a lack of killer instinct won't come back to haunt his team in the second half.
HALF TIME! An imperious display from City in the first half, with West Brom only being allowed into the game in the final ten minutes of the half. The visitors lead 2-0, courtesy of good finishes from Sergio Aguero and Yaya Toure.
(45’) OFFSIDE! Amalfitano wriggles through the dense City defensive line, but the linesman's flag is raised, and rightly so! Three blue and white striped shirts were in offside positions, but the Frenchman still has to complain a little.
(44’) West Brom have started to contest the game in the last five minutes or so, but they're sorely lacking an offensive presence in and around the box. Long is being physically dominated and has touched the ball extremely rarely. Perhaps the more durable Anichebe would be an interesting alternative for the second half?
(42’) LONG! The Republic of Ireland international gets the ball caught under his feet and the chance escapes him! Great work from Brunt to wriggle free of Zabaleta's attentions on the left flank, before a delicate cut-back to his teammate, but Long is wasteful.
(41’) Five minutes until the break, and West Brom need a goal if they are to claw themselves back into this game. A couple of corners and chances in quick succession for the likes of Brunt and Berahino are lifting the home crowd's spirits somewhat.
(39’) Excellent defending from Kompany! Berahino opens the ball up onto his left foot on the edge of the 18-yard-box, but as the young forward pulls the trigger, a sizeable Belgian centre-half throws himself into the block, and it cannons away from danger. He's been sidelined, but you can never lose your defensive instinct!
(38’) BRUNT! A very, very ambitious effort from the West Brom midfielder, who arrows a long-range strike into the City fans behind Pantilimon's goal. He's probably still full of confidence from his goal against Newcastle at the weekend, but to try his luck from there was rather wasteful.
(36’) FERNANDINHO! The Brazilian wastes yet another opportunity for City! Aguero releases Navas on the right flank, before the Spain international cuts a chipped ball back to the former Shakhtar man, who was arriving on the edge of the box. He tries to strike a volley towards Myhill's goal, but instead fizzes the ball over the crossbar.
(35’) DZEKO! Non-existent marking from the home side allows for Dzeko to rise unchallenged and nod a header over the bar from eight yards out! The City striker should really be doing better than that, he had a run at the delivery, and still couldn't get over it.
(34’) AGUERO! The Argentine manages to get away from Olsson with ease, before trying to finish across Myhill from a very tight angle! The Welsh goalkeeper gets a slight touch to give away a corner, but Dzeko wanted the ball delivered to the back post!
(33’) BERAHINO! The youngster looks to turn on the edge of the 18-yard-box, but a crafty nudge from Fernandinho puts the Baggies' forward off-balance, causing him to fire wide of the target.
(32’) BRUNT! The Northern Ireland midfielder strikes from the edge of the box, but Demichelis makes the block! The rebound falls to Amalfitano, who loops a cross into the penalty box, but Long can't get on the end of it! A few niggling fouls are creeping into this game too.
(30’) DZEKO! The Bosnian is inches away from making it three for City! A great cross to the back post from Kolarov looks to find his teammate sliding in to finish off the move, but the delivery narrowly escapes its intended target! City are in overdrive here!
(29’) Well beaten away by Pantilimon! A sliced clearance by Fernandinho loops the ball high into the air, causing his goalkeepers all kinds of problems! The Romanian punches clear under plenty of pressure from Long.
(28’) City look majestically comfortable, with their full-backs having free reign and Yaya Toure and Fernandinho seeming to have endless amounts of time on the ball in the centre of the field. The visitors appear to be able to break forward and craft themselves a chance whenever they wish.
(26’) AGUERO! The Argentine blasts the ball well off target yet again, but there's certainly a possibility that the former Atletico man will get on the scoresheet again tonight. He's popping up in worrying areas constantly as City push forward relentlessly.
(25’) DZEKO! McAuley does well to rise above his marker and head the ball from danger! Moments earlier, Amalfitano goes down in the penalty area, looking for a spot-kick, but the referee waves away his claims. It did look to be a hopeful dive from the loanee.
--- 24’ Assist A. Kolarov provided the assist. ---
--- 24’ Goal! GOOOOAL! YAYA TOURE CONVERTS TO MAKE IT 2-0! The away side carve West Brom apart yet again, with Yaya Toure slotting home Kolarov's cut-back absolutely beautifully! Excellent, excellent finish from the Ivory Coast international! ---
(22’) Excellent defensive contribution from Dzeko! The striker makes his way back to his own penalty area, to nod away a Brunt free-kick delivery, following Kolarov being penalised for a rather naughty and cynical foul on Amalfitano. City aren't allowing the Frenchman nor Long a moment on the ball.
(21’) AGUERO! It's wide again from the Argentine, but Dzeko's lay-off is again encouraging for City. Their two strikers are combining well, and Aguero looks likely to grab the second goal of the evening. The home fans are perhaps getting a little restless, their side look like the away side.
(19’) Poor delivery from Navas! The Spaniard's cross is turned away easily by Olsson, after the former Sevilla man was played into plenty of space on the right flank by Nasri. One-way traffic at the Hawthorns, with the subdued home atmosphere mirroring the performance of their side.
(18’) Still no real signs of a West Brom resurgence, as City continue to monopolise the ball effectively. Dzeko turns on the edge of the penalty box, but Olsson steps in efficiently to block the Bosnian's strike. Even then, the rebound falls to a City player. Everything is going brilliantly for the visitors.
(17’) Good defending from McAuley! Kolarov is allowed to overlap on the left, before Reid doesn't get close enough to prevent the cross. Aguero and Dzeko are lurking in the penalty area, but a good sliding interception from the former Ipswich central defender turns the delivery away from danger.
(16’) BERAHINO! His shot is always going wide, skidding off the turf and thudding into the advertising boards behind Pantilimon's goal. The Romanian goalkeeper is forced to cover his post, but I suspect that the City man is simply keen to not make any mistakes to gift Hart a way back into the starting line-up.
(15’) The first quarter of an hour has been packed full of action, with City certainly having the better of the opening exchanges. Dzeko and Aguero are too much for the Baggies to handle, with Amalfitano and Berahino the only likely catalysts for the hosts. Long has been anonymous.
(13’) AMALFITANO! Awful effort from the loanee! A pocket of space opens up on the edge of the penalty area, with both Kompany and Demichelis reluctant to close down the opposition midfielder, but the Frenchman drags his eventual shot well wide of the target.
(12’) DZEKO! Myhill does well to claim the Bosnia international's header, after a good cross into the target man by Aguero. The Argentine was initally picked out by a lovely diagonal ball from the returning Kompany, showing that City are prepared to attack directly if allowed.
(10’) The dream away start for the away side, as dominance has been rewarded with the breakthrough goal. West Brom look unable to repel the visitors when they're in possession, with the likes of Dzeko and Aguero working extremely well together to find gaps in the Baggies' defence.
--- 9’ Assist P. Zabaleta gave the assist. ---
--- 9’ Goal! GOOOOOOAL! WHAT A GREAT TEAM GOAL! City take the lead, with Aguero smashing beyond the helpless Myhill, following a delightful range of passing. Dzeko slides Zabaleta in behind Ridgewell, before the Argentine squares for his compatriot! City lead 1-0! ---
(8’) NASRI! The Frenchman pops up in the centre of the penalty area and is picked out by Aguero, but his touch lets him down, allowing for McAuley to clear. Pellegrini's will be satisfied from what he's seen thus far, the fluid front four he has deployed are working well.
(7’) An all-action start of the Hawthorns, and despite the absence of plenty of supporters who are presumably stuck in the traffic outside the stadium, the game has sprung into life early on. End-to-end stuff from two sides with interesting attacking options.
(6’) AGUERO! Wonderful interplay from City, as Dzeko feeds Aguero following some excellent control from the Bosnian. His strike-partner races through of goal, but can only drag his shot wide of Myhill's right hand post.
(5’) Great play from Berahino! The youngster causes plenty of problems for Fernandinho, beating the Brazilian with ease, before the Englishman's cross can only find the gloves of the tall Pantilimon. So excellent until the end product!
(4’) Good defending from McAuley! The West Brom man gets a flick onto a Navas cross, turning it away from the awaiting head of Aguero. That was so nearly an opening goal for the away side.
(3’) OFFSIDE! The linesman has his flag raised to deny the central defensive duo of McAuley and Olsson from having a run at a good free-kick delivery from Brunt. The two defenders rose well, but the official was very quick to give the offside decision, and right too.
(2’) NASRI! The Frenchman is rather unbalanced as he strikes the first effort of the game towards goal, but the ball balloons off target. City have seen all of the ball thus far, and Clark's men will presumably want to disrupt the visitors before they get into any sort of rhythm.
(1’) We are finally underway in the first half of tonight's game! Man City welcome some much-missed and interesting faces into their starting line-up, while Berahino will be keen to prove that his contract renewal was worth West Brom's hard-earned money. Hard to call which way this game will go, with Man City having already been defeated four times on the road this season!
We've been delayed here tonight, with kick-off now being pushed back by fifteen minutes due to traffic problems. Not to worry, as we'll be continuing as planned, but unfortunately we won't be getting underway for a little while longer!
Under ten minutes to go until kick-off, and Pellegrini will hope that a win here tonight will allow Man City to keep pace with the early front runners of the Premier League, Arsenal. The Gunners are steaming through the season quite frighteningly, and City need to keep their winning run going to hang onto their coattails. The Baggies need a win to elevate themselves from the potential relegation mire.
Edin Dzeko interestingly gets a start ahead of Negredo for the away side, with Kolarov given an opportunity at left-back ahead of Clichy. Berahino celebrates signing a new long-term deal at the Hawthorns with another Premier League start, with Reid replacing Jones at right full-back too. With both Vydra and Sessegnon starting on the bench tonight for Clark's side, the Scot certainly has the ability to change the game.
Man City substitutes: Hart, Richards, Lescott, Milner, Negredo, Javi Garcia, Rodwell.
Man City starting line-up: Pantilimon; Zabaleta, Kompany, Demichelis, Kolarov; Fernandinho, Toure; Navas, Aguero, Nasri; Dzeko.
West Brom substitutes: Popov, Lugano, Anichebe, Daniels, Vydra, Gera, Sessegnon.
West Brom starting line-up: Myhill; Reid, McAuley, Olsson, Ridgewell; Morrison, Brunt, Yacob, Amalfitano; Long, Berahino.
TEAM NEWS: Vincent Kompany returns at the heart of City's defence, with Pantilimon continuing in between the sticks for the visitors. Silva, Nastasic and Jovetic remain absent through injury. The Baggies are missing two key players of their own, with Ben Foster still in the physio room, and Mulumbu sidelined through suspension.
I'm Simon Harrison, and I will be keeping you up to date with all of the action this evening, as City look to continue their recent momentum. Four wins from their last five games have positioned Pelligrini's outfit only two points off second-placed Liverpool. West Brom, on the other hand, ended a three game unbeaten run with a defeat to Newcastle last weekend, a blow that the home side would like to recover from as quickly as possible.
Hello and welcome to live coverage of Manchester City's visit to the Hawthorns, as the Premier League's third-placed side search for three points against Steve Clarke's stuttering West Bromwich Albion. The hosts have had patchy form of late, while City arrive in rather potent goalscoring form. Whether Manuel Pellegrini's side can recreate their high-scoring home exploits tonight, remains to be seen.

FULL-TIME Aston Villa 0-0 Sunderland - And that's the final whistle here on what has been an afternoon largely to forget at Villa Park.Sunderland boss Gus Poyet will be delighted to have arrested the slide of five consecutive away defeats but for Villa and Paul Lambert, the most worrying statistic in all of this will be Christian Benteke's continued goal drought. The Belgian has failed to score in his last seven Premier League outings now.
--- 90’ +4 Yellow card P. Bardsley is yellow-carded. ---
--- 90’ +3 Yellow card G. Agbonlahor receives a yellow card. ---
(90’) Sunderland look in a hurry to get rid of the ball each time they get it and Vito Mannone punts straight downfield to opposite number Brad Guzan.The game threatens to get a little bit nasty late on, with Gabriel Agbonlahor picking up a yellow card for a trip on Phil Bardsley while the latter then crashed into Ciaran Clark.
(90’) Sebastian Larsson commits a foul on the half-way line but Aston Villa have looked so bereft of attacking ideas all afternoon that this latest free-kick also comes to nothing.
(88’) John O'Shea goes down with what looks to be like a groin injury. It looks bad at first, but the Sunderland captain will continue here.
--- 86’ Substitution C. Benteke is replaced with L. Kozák. ---
(86’) Christian Benteke has embodied Aston Villa's frustration today and he is hauled off for Libor Kozak as Villa go in hunt of a winner.The frustrations continue on the pitch as Fabian Delph's long-range effort flies over Vito Mannone's crossbar.
--- 84’ Substitution O. Celustka enters play, replacing A. Dossena. ---
(84’) Ondrej Celustka comes on for Andrea Dossena for Sunderland.Meanwhile, Aleksandar Tonev's strike from range is easily collected by Vito Mannone. Audible groans around the ground at present.
(82’) Marc Albrighton has proved an inspired substitution by Paul Lambert here, sending in another brilliant cross but Christian Benteke, who has been poor, is unable to make the run towards the near post.
(80’) Sunderland getting nervier at the back now and Aston Villa are getting into good attacking areas.Aleksandar Tonev embarks on a weaving run towards the area but Jack Colback does brilliantly to regain possession.
(78’) Marc Albrighton delivers two excellent crosses in succession and, from the latter, Christian Benteke believes he is impeded by Phil Bardsley's challenge.Nothing doing this time either for Neil Swarbrick.
--- 76’ Substitution J. Colback enters the game and replaces C. Gardner. ---
--- 76’ Substitution F. Borini is done for the day. A. Johnson is his replacement. ---
(76’) Sunderland make a double change of their own, as Jack Colback and Adam Johnson come on to replace Craig Gardner and Fabio Borini. Two like for like changes but it appears Gus Poyet has matched his counterpart Paul Lambert's idea of tightening up in the midfield and wide areas.
(74’) Both defences look to be tiring but the final ball is still sorely lacking. Can either side rally themselves to find a much-needed winner here?
(72’) More good work from Emanuele Giaccherini almost results in an opening. His ball is forced through a gap in the Aston Villa defence but Steven Fletcher is not quite alert enough to deal with the oncoming pass and Brad Guzan easily collects.
--- 71’ Substitution K. El Ahmadi is done for the day. A. Tonev is his replacement. ---
--- 71’ Substitution A. Weimann is replaced with M. Albrighton. ---
(70’) Marc Albrighton and Aleksandar Tonev come on for Andreas Weimann and Karim El Ahmadi respectively. It looks like Paul Lambert is shoring up the midfield but can these substitutes have the same sort of impact as on Monday night?
(68’) Sunderland win a corner and when Ki Sung-Yueng mops up the pieces in midfield, the South Korean feeds Emanuele Giaccherini who takes a tumble in the area. Neil Swarbrick rightly waves away the protests.
(66’) CROSSBAR! It's becoming the Emanuele Giaccherini show here for Sunderland. Superb work from the Italian again, who this time produces the goods from out wide and scoops a ball into Fabio Borini.The fellow Italian is desperately unlucky to see his header come cannoning back off the crossbar. Sunderland slowly getting on top again.
(64’) Emanuele Giaccherini skips past Leandro Bacuna and the challenge on the Italian is desperate, but his cross is a disappointing one and ends up in the gloves of Brad Guzan.
(62’) Gabriel Agbonlahor does superbly for Aston Villa down the left, committing men and riding challenges before forcing a corner but, again, Wes Brown is there to clear up from the subsequent set piece and Sunderland can rebuild.
(60’) It's far more of an even contest now, with Aston Villa looking to hassle and harry their opponents in possession but Sunderland still look a threat on the counter.
(58’) Sunderland win a free-kick around 30 yards out but they cannot make the most of it as Craig Gardner wastefully fires over with Sebastian Larsson also well poised over the ball.
(56’) Ki Sung-Yueng thinks he is set to put Sunderland on the front foot by robbing Andreas Weimann but the Black Cats are then pegged back themselves and Villa break.Again, Gabriel Agbonlahor is the instigator but he cannot force his way through when he reaches the box.
(54’) Emanuele Giaccherini turns onto his favoured right side but is fouled and the Black Cats earn a free kick in an attacking position.
(52’) Aston Villa certainly on top now and Gabriel Agbonlahor's pace, in particular, is helping to stretch this game.The winger darts down the left but is confronted with traffic when he reaches the penalty area.
(50’) That's better from Aston Villa, as Gabriel Agbonlahor engineers a shooting chance and tests Vito Mannone with a stinging near-post effort, which the Italian has to turn aside for a corner.
(48’) Sunderland start the second half as they ended the first, on top.First, Andrea Dossena goes marauding down the left and sends in an inviting centre which Steven Fletcher cannot quite keep up with before Ki Sung-Yueng feeds Phil Bardsley on the other wing, but that also comes to nothing.
(46’) We are back underway here at Villa Park, as Sunderland get the ball rolling again for the start of the second half.
Sunderland can feel slightly aggrieved not to be in front here, having created many of the first half's most promising moments in the attacking third with Aston Villa unable to get going so far.Emanuele Giaccherini's shocking miss has been the main talking point, but Sebastian Larsson's narrow miss from a free-kick and a cross-cum-shot that evaded everyone illustrating the Black Cats' attacking endeavour.
(45’) There goes the whistle to signal the end of the opening period. HALF-TIME: Aston Villa 0-0 Sunderland
(45’) WHAT A MISS! Somehow Emanuele Giaccherini, the player who has looked the biggest threat for Sunderland so far, scoops the ball over the bar from a matter of inches out, and with the goal gaping, after a tremendous knockdown from Phil Bardsley.Remarkably, the score remains 0-0 here at Villa Park.
(43’) Now it's Sunderland's cries for a handball as John O'Shea nods down towards Ciaran Clark but the ball is adjudged to have hit the Republic of Ireland international's chest and not arm.
(41’) Sunderland fail to deal with a Gabriel Agbonlahor flick and Wes Brown has to concede a corner under pressure but moments later, the visitors think they have the lead.Craig Gardner is threaded through by a lovely Fabio Borini pass and tucks past Brad Guzan but the linesman's flag is up and the goal is ruled out.
(39’) Huge appeals for a penalty as Ashley Westwood's driven shot from just outside the area appears to strike Phil Bardsley on the arm. Neil Swarbrick is unmoved, however, and waves play on.Sunderland nearly capitalise, as Emanuele Giaccherini's devilish cross into the front post area is hacked clear by Ciaran Clark with the visitors unable to get a decisive touch in time.
(37’) Aston Villa's riposte is Fabian Delph's vicious 25-yard strike, which ultimately flies harmlessly wide. Despite that, Sunderland goalkeeper Vito Mannone is furious at his defenders for allowing the shot to be engineered in the first place.
(35’) Signs that Sunderland are just beginning to dominate the midfield battle and, though there is a lack of quality in the final third from both sides, the visitors are beginning to look the most threatening.
(33’) Gabriel Agbonlahor, yet again, chases down a lost cause but it is to no effect as Christian Benteke is flagged offside.
--- 32’ Yellow card R. Vlaar receives a yellow card. ---
(31’) Emanuele Giaccherini goes down on the edge of the area after a foul from Ron Vlaar, which the Dutchman picks up a booking for.The free-kick is whipped towards the back post by Sebastian Larsson and, evading everyone, is only inches wide.
(29’) Aston Villa waste their best chance as Christian Benteke's goal drought continues.A storming run down the right from Karim El Ahmadi results in Ashley Westwood teeing up Benteke, but the Belgian can only curl over the bar from the left-hand side of the 18-yard box.
(27’) Gabriel Agbonlahor escapes down the left and squares up to Phil Bardsley but credit to the Sunderland defender who recovers to concede a corner.
(25’) It's absolute chaos in the Aston Villa area as Phil Bardsley's quick corner leaves the home side's defence at sixes and sevens. Ki Sung-Yueng's low ball into the area on the follow up cannot be turned home though, despite five Black Cats bodies going for it.
(23’) Sunderland just beginning to establish a foothold in the match and they work a corner down the left after a tricky run from Emanuele Giaccherini.
(21’) John O'Shea almost leaves his side in an almighty mess as he breaks from the back but, when Villa attack in numbers, Wes Brown shows wonderful discipline to come across and cover for his fellow central defender.
(19’) It has been the epitome of an end-to-end contest so far, with both sides looking to counter one another but so far, nothing to report in terms of clear goalscoring chances.
(17’) The Aston Villa defence fall asleep as former Villan Craig Gardner almost cashes in on the lapse in concentration.Andrea Dossena's long ball is not dealt with and Gardner steals ahead of Ron Vlaar before poking goalwards but Brad Guzan's presence puts off the Sunderland man, who could only steer wide.
(15’) Antonio Luna is being given the freedom of the left wing at times and after his first cross is easily caught by Vito Mannone, the Spaniard delays the second time around and earns a corner for his side.
(13’) Ron Vlaar has to be alert to deal with Emanuele Giaccherini's teasing cross into the area after good work from the Italian and Phil Bardsley down the right flank.
(11’) Aston Villa force a corner as Karim El Ahmadi latches on to Andreas Weimann's clever pass but it ultimately comes to nothing as Sunderland break downfield with the ball.
(9’) Aston Villa have probably started the brighter of the two sides and both full-backs Leandro Bacuna and Antonio Luna have looked to get forward at every opportunity. The former almost gets a shot away but swipes at thin air after a neat switch of play from Christian Benteke.
(7’) Andrea Dossena wastes Sunderland's first presentable opportunity, as he lashes wide following some neat link up play.Steven Fletcher retains possession well in front of the Aston Villa defence and feeds the onrushing Italian full-back but his shot is into the side netting when his teammates were well placed in the centre.
(5’) Andreas Weimann drives at the heart of the Sunderland defence and releases the lively Gabriel Agbonlahor on the left.Agbonlahor cut inside and unleashed a curling effort towards the far post but Vito Mannone had everything behind it and held on well.
(3’) Aston Villa create the first opening of the afternoon as Gabriel Agbonlahor heads Fabian Delph's right-wing cross just wide after a short spell of pressure following a throw from Leandro Bacuna.
(1’) And we're off, with Aston Villa getting us underway here at Villa Park.
Villa, meanwhile, have only lost two of their last eight games (W3, D3, L2) and are now the side to have gained most points from losing positions (seven) in the top flight after the 2-2 draw at West Brom on Monday.

Arsenal dominated, and pull out a comprehensive and convincing victory in Wales. It was hardly an easy match in the capital, but the Gunners dug their heels in and scrapped Cardiff all the way. Ramsey led the way with a double, and Flamini added another off the bench, but the victory was built on a superb defensive display from Koscielny, Mertesacker and Co. Provisional seven point lead at the top for Arsenal now.
(90’) Turner, probably Cardiff's best player on the night, makes a VITAL interception on Walcott, who was primed to shoot from point blank range! And Lee Mason has seen enough!
(90’) This has been a gritty performance from the Gunners, sprinkled with quality at the right moments. Their defence and midfield have been superb, and the attack has come through when required.
--- 90’ +3 Assist The assist came from T. Walcott. ---
--- 90’ +3 Goal! Immediately we see the benefit of Walcott in the Arsenal side. Odemwingie fails with a penalty appeal, and Ramsey is off storming down the middle. Ahead of him streaks Walcott, who is played in by the Welshman, and unselfishly returns the ball for Ramsey to smash into the same corner as Flamini minutes ago! Scintillating counter! ---
(90’) RAMSEY ADDS ANOTHER!
--- 90’ +1 Substitution M. Özil is done for the day. T. Walcott is his replacement. ---
(90’) We've got five minutes of added time to round this one off, but it's dead rubber as far as the result is concerned.
(90’) Off goes Ozil, decisive as ever, and on comes the speedy Englishman. The German is taking his sweet time to make his way to the sidelines!
--- 89’ Yellow card A. Ramsey goes into the referee's book. ---
(89’) It's all Arsenal now as Cardiff have the wind knocked out of them. Walcott is finally looking like he's ready to come on.
--- 88’ Substitution A. Cornelius comes on for A. Taylor. ---
(88’) Two assists for Ozil today, who has not been at his effervescent best, but has popped up with the killer contributions at the key moments. Still a match winner.
--- 86’ Assist M. Özil gave the assist. ---
--- 86’ Goal! What a goal from the Frenchman, who came on to protect the back four but comes up with a stunner to ice the game! Ozil plays a perfectly, repeat PERFECTLY weighted pass right onto the penalty spot. Flamini timed his run superbly and smashes an emphatic finish into the top corner! ---
(86’) FLAMINI SEALS IT!
(84’) Whittingham's free kick is thrown into the mixer, but GIroud heads clear. It doesn't go as far as he would like though, and Cowie collects and lets one fly from 20 yards. It's not too far from Szczesny though, who gets down and holds onto the ball. Cardiff have shot a lot from long range, but have never really troubled Szczesny from there, which is a testament to the Gunners back four for taking away the clear cut chances.
(82’) The game winding down now as the pace slows, which will suit Arsenal just fine. They've got less then 10 minutes plus added time to see the points through.
--- 81’ Substitution Nacho Monreal comes on for J. Wilshere. ---
(80’) Arteta gets his name in the book for clipping the legs of Cowie. A deserved booking, but a slight blot on the copybook of the Spaniard, who has been assured today.
--- 79’ Yellow card Arteta is cautioned by the referee. ---
(78’) Whittingham thumps a half volley from the top of the box, but it's right at Szczesny, who does not have to move to make the save. Good goalkeeping.
--- 77’ Substitution M. Flamini enters play, replacing Cazorla. ---
(76’) Noone nearly makes an instant impact with a lovely, incisive pass down the centre for Mutch to chase, but Szczesny is out in time excellently to smother the ball right on the edge of his area.
--- 75’ Substitution Bo-Kyung Kim is done for the day. C. Noone is his replacement. ---
(74’) More subs coming up for both sides, as Kims' race seems to be done, with Noone set to come on. Meanwhile, Cazorla appears to be on his way off for Flamini in a clear defensive swap from Wenger.
(72’) Great touch from the Arsenal fans, who are singing the praises of former long-serving assistant manager Pat Rice, who was admitted to hospital with cancer earlier this week.
(70’) We may yet be seeing Walcott, as the forward continues his warmup on the sidelines. My guess would be Ozil to depart, as the German has, surprise surprise, faded from proceedings shortly after the restart. Something the playmaker still has to work on.
(68’) Wilshere picks the ball up and drives forward excellently on the counter. He continues his good work with a deft pass to Cazorla, who digs out a shot from 15 yards that's somewhat disappointingly right at Marshall.
(66’) The Gunners boss has options though; Walcott, Gnabry and Rosicky to speed things up in attack, or Vermaelen, Flamini and Monreal to steady the ship at the back. Choices in reserve he's often lacked at times this season due to injury.
(65’) The expected Cardiff change does happen, but no signs yet of a response in kind from Arsene Wenger.
--- 64’ Substitution P. Odemwingie comes on for F. Campbell. ---
(64’) Poor decision from Lee Mason, who awards a goalkick on a GIroud effort near the byeline, despite the ball clearly pinging off Caulker on its way out. Hardly the best decision for Giroud to shoot from there either, mind.
(63’) First change of the match about to happen, as Peter Odemwingie is set to come on, and the word is that Frazier Campbell is the man to be sacrificed.
(61’) Finally we have a chance to breathe. The game has settled into familiar patterns, as Arsenal and Cardiff trade relatively harmless bouts of possession. Nothing's shooting down the momentum of this home crowd though, who are making a magnificent racket in the stands.
(59’) Not a bad attempt from Giroud, who tries to curl the ball into the top shelf from outside the area, but it's spotted all the way by Marshall, who positions himself well to make the save.
(58’) Arsenal take the sting out of Cardiff's tail with a spell of possession deep in the opposition half. The Gunners are not really looking for the killer ball, rather, they aim to keep the ball as long as possible to strangle the momentum and get the home crowd to settle down.
(56’) Catherine lines up an attempt from all of 30 yards, and hits the target, but it's never going to trouble Szczesny, who smothers it well in the face of pressure from Campbell, who was angling to lap up any spills.
(54’) Terrific response from the some side after they were put under Arsenal's thumb to start the half. Whittingham sees a good shooting opportunity blocked with desperation by a sliding Arteta at the tip of the D.
(53’) Cardiff have their tails up, no question about that. They're flowing forward in attack now, finding spaces and channels that were not there previously. Arsenal's turn to weather the storm.
(52’) What a MAGNIFICENT save from Szczesny! Taylor whips one in from the left, Kim helps it onto the far post, where Campbell towers over the sheepish Gibbs to power a header to the opposite side, but the Polish stopper stretches to his right to push the ball away incredibly!
(50’) Complete dominance from Arsenal to start the second half, which will be worrying for Mackay. Ramsey comes within inches of weaving his way through again!
(48’) GIROUD! How are Arsenal not two up! Ramsey does supremely well to wriggle down the byeline, and he cuts the ball back to the Frenchman about eight yards out. But Turner is Johnny on the spot, making a crucial clearance off the line!
(46’) Here we go again!
The story of the show so far has been who the headline writers have been penning all week - Aaron Ramsey. The midfielder continued his insane goalscoring form with a superb header against his former club - which prompted a standing O from the entire stadium. It's given Arsenal the lad, and they're 45 minutes and change away from assuming a seven point lead at the top of the table. Stay tuned for the restart in just a bit.
(45’) That's the end of an absorbing first half.
(45’) The Gunners passing the ball around patiently, Cardiff sitting deep to nullify their threat. Both teams seem to have their minds set on the break.
(45’) Into the first of four added minutes.
(44’) Ramsey turns on a dime and frees himself for a shot in the box, but he can't find his range! A good opening!
(42’) Giroud shows some insane strength to hold off his man and kill a Gibbs cross on is chest. He turns towards goal to shoot, but the angle, and space, just runs out on him, and the defence can block his shot at the near post.
(41’) Cazorla loses out to Kim after failing to connect with a loose pass from Sagna, but Wilshere saves the Gunners' bacon with a splendid tackle to stop the counter attack in its tracks.
(40’) Ozil and Cazorla are weaving in and out of pockets of space, but Cardiff are doing a tremendous job of keeping their wizardry confined to the area near the left corner of the field. Giroud looks a bit swarmed by red shirts at the back.
(38’) Catherine overruns a ball badly out on the right flank. He had Gibbs backpedaling, but his dreadful first touch allows the Arsenal left back to get rid without too much trouble.
(36’) Good spell this from Cardiff as Cowie just overplays a pass into the box which Koscielny gets rid of. We've got a real game on our hands.
(34’) The free kick is not defended well by Arsenal, and Whittingham's delivery is nearly turned in by Kim! The Gunners defence get away with it as the ball snakes past the post!
--- 33’ Yellow card K. Gibbs is cautioned by the referee. ---
(33’) Gibbs picks up the first caution of the day with a rash challenge on Catherine, a deserved caution as it was late, but without hate.
(31’) Now we will see what Cardiff are made of. They came back against Manchester United, twice, and they'll need to do it at least once today now.
--- 29’ Goal! Who else but the Arsenal Welshman! Ozil provides a ball into the box, but Ramsey still has some work to do. And he takes care of business, angling a superb header high into the goal. He pointedly refuses to celebrate against his former club, and there's a standing ovation for his goal - and not just from the Arsenal fans. ---
--- 29’ Assist The assist came from M. Özil. ---
(29’) RAMSEY SCORES! ARSENAL LEAD!
(28’) Excellent from Mertesacker, to get a gangly toe in on Campbell, who was sprinting a mile a minute towards goal. Koscielny hacks away the loose ball, but a warning sign there as that chance was created by a sloppy Arteta pass.
(26’) Kim is ready to come back onto the pitch, but he'll have to wait for this free kick to commence...which it does, but comes to nothing.
(25’) Kim is in need of some assistance, coming off worse in a challenge with Sagna. To add insult to injury, he's pulled up for a free kick, and Arsenal have a decent shout to get the ball into the box.
(23’) Ozil does well to shimmy his way into a pocket of space at the top of the 18, and lays one off to Cazorla, who attacks the ball square. The Spaniard shoots on sight, but it's blocked with distinction by Medel.
(21’) The Gunners are trying a bit too hard to make something happen in the attacking third, and are losing the ball with their cutthroat tempo around the box. Cardiff are closing the gaps as soon as they appear.
(19’) Szczesny, normally one of the best in the league at taking command of the ball in the air, is put in a sticky situation by Whittingham's deep cross, as Turner charges in to challenge the Pole. He's beaten to the ball, but bailed out by the referee's whistle.
(17’) Wenger is losing his mind on the touchline at Giroud's decision, which he has every right to. The Frenchman really should have done better there, there was no signs that the officials were angling to call an offside. Cardiff with two let-offs, can they make Arsenal pay?
(16’) What an EXTRAORDINARY incident! Ozil flicked delicately into the path of Giroud, but he and the rest of the back four stop in anticipation of the offside flag...which does not appear! The Frenchman was onside, and clean through as well! Isn't the first rule in football to play to the whistle?
(14’) Cardiff are fighting Arsenal for every ball, and thus far, are winning most of those 50-50's. It's keenly contested out there, but signs that the Gunners midfield might be able to break through.
(12’) Campbell takes full advantage of Arsenal's temporary numerical advantage to streak down the right, and ping a cross onto the head of Mutch, who glances just wide of the far post! Mertesacker is right back on the pitch after that near miss.
(10’) Thomas Vermaelen is stripped and running, but Mertesacker is back on his feet. However, the physios have told Vermaelen to continue his warmup, as the jury's still out on Mertesacker's condition. We've seen a lot of focus on concussions thanks to the Hugo Lloris incident. Arsenal underwent a similar scenario when Flamini went down in a Premier League game, was patched up, and then soon departed with a concussion after failing to recover.
(9’) Trouble here for Mertesacker, who has taken a meaty whack to the chops after a mid-air collision with Bacary Sagna. He's down on the deck, and is immediately swarmed by the physios as the game is halted.
(7’) The match just beginning to settle into its foundations as Cardiff sit deep in their own half and look to soak up the opposition pressure.
(5’) A lovely, open start to this game. Cardiff are clearly angling to get Fraizer Campbell to use his pace behind Laurent Koscielny and Per Mertesacker, but so far, their intentions have been read every step of the way by the Gunners pair.
(3’) Wilshere scored in the opening seconds against Marseille midweek on his way to a double, and it's clear that he's brimming with confidence, coming within inches, inches to doing the same here in Wales. Arsenal fire a ferocious warning shot!
(2’) JACK WILSHERE! SO UNLUCKY! One touch takes him past Kim at the top of the 18 yard area, and with another touch, he unleashes a hellacious piledriver that cracks the frame of the goal!
(1’) Here we go! Cardiff get the ball rolling.
We're just about ready to go here, as the players are in place...
By stepping out onto the Cardiff City Stadium pitch today, Aaron Ramsey has pretty much come full circle as a footballer. He returns to his old stomping grounds, where he appeared first as a schoolboy, and then during a brief loan spell in 2011 in his road to recovery from the Ryan Shawcross incident. He's a different man today though, having banished the physical and mental demons from that injury to become - on form - one of the finest midfielders in the world.
Malky Mackay has a fully fit squad at his disposal to take on the league leaders, but he's another manager with little to tinker after an enterprising display in their last league outing, a 2-2 draw against Manchester United. Kim Bo-Kyung usurps Peter Odemwingie in the starting lineup, while Gary Medel is available to patrol the centre of the park after escaping retribution for slapping Marouane Fellaini.
Mesut Ozil's rather meek form in the last few weeks has become the new hot topic, but it should soon be getting better for the German international. Theo Walcott continues his race to 100 per cent fitness with a berth on the bench, while Lukas Podolski is closer and closer to doing the same after returning to training from his hamstring woes. Finally some runners to lap up all those delicious through balls.
If it ain't broke, don't fix it. And if it ain't sick, start it. Arsene Wenger sticks with the same merry band of brothers that took care of Southampton last weekend, with Kieran Gibbs returning to the XI after missing the midweek jaunt against Marseille due to illness.

CARDIFF (4-3-3): Marshall; Taylor, Caulker, Turner, Theophile-Catherine; Medel, Kim, Mutch; Cowie, Whittingham, Campbell.
ARSENAL SUBS: Fabianski, Vermaelen, Monreal, Rosicky, Flamini, Walcott, Gnabry.
ARSENAL (4-2-3-1): Szczesny; Sagna, Mertesacker, Koscielny, Gibbs; Arteta, Ramsey; Wilshere, Ozil, Cazorla; Giroud.

Greetings one and all, and I'm glad to welcome you to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Cardiff City and Arsenal in the Welsh capital. I'm Keeghann Sinanan, your designated scribe for all the action.

As for Stoke, they will have to regroup after being chased out of town by a side who are unbeaten in the league at home this calendar year. They go down to 16th in the league tonight whilst the Toffees rise up three places into fourth. I hope you have enjoyed out coverage and feasted on this goal glut...have a fantastic weekend, folks. This is Hayden Gribble, signing off.
FULL TIME: EVERTON 4-0 STOKE. The Goodison Park faithful applaud their team off the pitch after a clinical and highly impressive display against an overwhelmed Stoke side. Goals from Coleman, Oviedo and Lukaku added to a first half strike from the impressive 19-year-old Deulofeu to take the Toffees into the top four, Is it too early to talk about the blue half of Merseyside as contenders for the Champions League places?
(90’) SAVE! There is just no stopping this attacking onslaught from the home side. This time Mirallas curls a shot from the edge of the box but Begovic is equal to it.
(90’) There will be a minimum of FOUR minutes of added time.
(89’) CHANCE! Mirallas puts Jelavic clean through but the Croatian shoots straight at Begovic when it was easier to score!
(88’) CHANCE! Crouch gets on the ball, he looks up at the target, he shoots!...but the former England man's effort isweak and it bobbles into the hands of Howard. I'd be surprised if there was any mud on his gloves, that's how little the American has had to do today!
(86’) SAVE! Jelavic draws a fine save from Begovic, who gets down low to stop the Croatian's right footed effort.
(85’) With five minutes to go Stoke are enjoying a spell on the ball. But they have been dominated by their opponents today and Tim Howard may never have a quieter afternoon in goal for the Toffees.
--- 83’ Substitution K. Mirallas comes on for S. Pienaar. ---
(83’) Jelavic is a man who has really run out of luck in front of goal this season, but he looks sharp here and draws a block out of Shawcross to halt his advances. Everton are still attacking and the fans are loving it!
(81’) We are into the final ten minutes here at Goodison Park and man-of-the-match contender Deulofeu is at it again. He jinks his way past two defenders - dare I say, Messi style? - but is brought down by Shawcross roughly 12 yards out. The Everton faithful cry penalty but the referee waves play on.
--- 79’ Substitution N. Jelavić enters play, replacing R. Lukaku. ---
--- 79’ Assist The assist came from B. Oviedo. ---
--- 79’ Goal! GOAL! The big man from Belgium finally gets his name on the scoresheet. Lukaku, who was about to be taken off in place of Jelavic, latches onto a square ball in the six-yard-box to tap in his eighth goal of the season. Game over! ---
(77’) STAT ATTACK: The Potters have won two of 10 Premier League games against the Toffees. (BBC Sport)
(75’) HANDBALL? Oviedo runs at Cameron and attempts to put the ball in the area but it appears to hit the arm of the Stoke right-back and behind for a corner. I've seen them given...
--- 74’ Substitution J. McCarthy is done for the day. J. Stones is his replacement. ---
(72’) OUCH! Lukaku lines up a free-kick roughly 25 yards from goal. The Belgian smashes it straight into the wall and the chance to add a fourth goes begging.
(69’) BLOCK! Lukaku manages to pick out Pienaar in the box but the South African International has to take a touch before shooting and his effort is blocked by Shawcross, who threw himself in the line of fire.
(68’) CHANCE! Peters drives the ball across the six-yard-box and Shea is unable to get a touch on the ball. The Potters might have just sent a reminder to the Toffees back four there!
(67’) There is a clash in mid air as Jagielka mis-judges the flight of the ball and crashed into N'Zonzi. The Stoke man is showing his pain but is okay to continue as we near the 70 minute mark with Everton fully in the driving seat.
(65’) The visitors are finally enjoying an extended spell of possession but the Toffees defence is resiliant. Roberto Martinez must be overjoyed by his clincal side today.
--- 64’ Yellow card E. Pieters goes into the referee's book. ---
(63’) CHANCE! Finally Peter Crouch gets a chance to pull one back for the Potters but his first sight on goal of the game is stopped by a smart save from Howard. He managed to get his left arm down to the shot and its a corner.
(60’) Those substitutions have come about 15 minutes too late. The Potters win their second corner of the game but a foul in the box leads to audible groans from the away end.
--- 59’ Substitution C. Adam is done for the day. K. Jones is his replacement. ---
--- 59’ Substitution J. Walters is replaced with B. Shea. ---
--- 58’ Assist The assist came from Gerard Deulofeu. ---
--- 58’ Goal! GOAL! Bryan Oviedo, in for the injured Baines, gets himself on the scoresheet with a rocket of a hit from outside the area. The left-back looks shocked as he wheels away after comnig inside onto his right foot and rifles it past Begovic. Wallop! ---
(57’) Ironic cries of delight ring around Goodison as Walters miscontrols and puts the ball out of play. Stoke really are struggling.
(54’) DOUBLE SAVE! Deulofeu runs clear in the box with only the keeper to beat, but Begovic comes out to block the youngster's shot and then saves the follow-up from Lukaku. It's just a question of how many for the Toffees!
(53’) Adam knocks a free-kick into the Everton box and Stoek win their first corner of the game. Predicatably, it leads to nothing.
(51’) STAT ATTACK: After that Coleman strike, 13 of the 16 Premier League goals that Stoke have conceded this season have come in away matches.
--- 49’ Assist G. Barry gave the assist. ---
--- 49’ Goal! GOAL! Everton double their lead through Seamus Coleman. Deulofeu put the ball into the box and Barry misses it but the Irish right-back arrives late and scuffs the ball into the back of the net! ---
(48’) STAT ATTACK: The Toffees are unbeaten in the league at Goodison Park in 2013 (W10, D5). (BBC Sport)
--- 46’ Yellow card G. Whelan gets yellow. ---
(46’) The floodlights flicker into life and Stoke get us back underway!
Both teams are heading back out onto the pitch. What kind of response will Stoke make in this second half? One things for sure, they need to create more chances or they can forget about nicking even a point from Goodison Park today!
What can Mark Hughes do to reignite his charges for the second half? The Potters have been very quiet in the opening 45 minutes and they have given very little for their travelling fans to sing about.
HALFTIME: EVERTON 1-0 STOKE. The Toffees go in at the break a goal to the good thanks to a lovely strike from Barcelona loanee Deulofeu. He tip-toed into the box and exchanged a couple of passes with Pienaar and Barry that looked fresh from the training ground to put the home side into as deserved lead at the interval.
--- 45’ Assist G. Barry provided the assist. ---
--- 45’ Goal! GOAL! Who'd have guessed it? Deulofeu - the brightest spark in the Everton team today, starts and ends the move down the left this time, playing a one-two with Pienaar. The ball then falls to Barry who cushions it to the 19-year-old who slots home from eight yards. ---
(45’) There will be ONE minute of added on time.
(43’) SHOT! Finally, the Potters register a shot on target and it is Walters who tests the palms of Howard, who saves with ease. A wake-up call, perhaps?
--- 42’ Yellow card G. Cameron is yellow-carded. ---
(41’) Howard decides that enough is enough and races out of his box a full 30 yards to clear before Walters has a chance to threaten the American.
(39’) HALF-CHANCE! Lukaku climbs up in the air and headers just wide of the post. The Belgian struggled to meet the ball with any real power, there.
(38’) Every Everton attack is being fashioned through Deulofeu on the right. He is released down the flank and flies at the Potters' defence but his final ball is poor and it flies out of play.
(35’) Howard is awoken from his slumber to take a goal kick after Assaidi runs the ball out of play. Stoke need to find a plan B...
(33’) Stoke are enjoying a spell of possession but it still has not brought any chances for the visitors. Charlie Adam tries to orchestrate something for Crouch up front but Distin is sticking to his man like glue.
(30’) With half an hour gone it is all Everton. As Pink Floyd once sang, they are coming through in waves (sorry!) and Mark Hughes is cutting a frustrated figure on the touchline as his side have yet to challenge Tim Howard in the Toffees goal.
(28’) ONE TRICK PONY? For the second time in the game Deulofeu tries to bamboozle the Potters defence with a few step overs but to no avail.
(26’) WHAT A SAVE! Begovic is certainly earning his money this afternoon. The keeper is wrongfooted by a shot from Osman that is deflected but somehow manages to claw it away from goal. Lukaku follows up and he finds the Bosnian's palms again...and the offside flag up.
(25’) STAT ATTACK: The Potters have scored eight times in their last four league games, having netted just four times in their opening eight matches. (BBC Sport)
(22’) What brilliant defending from Peters. The Stoke man beats Jagielka to a cross from Deulofeu on the right and manages to put the ball out for a corner before the Toffees captain could reach it.
(20’) Despite testing the home side's reserve a couple of times so far in this half, Stoke have failed to test Tim Howard between the sticks. It's all Everton at the moment, who have not been weakened by the absence of Baines. They miss his dead-ball expertise, though.
(17’) CLOSE! Some lovely movement from the Toffees leads to a one-two between Lukaku and McCarthy and the former Wigan man sidefoots the ball wide.
(17’) STAT ATTACK: The last seven meetings between these two sides have produced just nine goals.
(15’) CHANCE! As soon as Distin got his tackle in his side are up the other end creating another chance. Deulofeu performs a couple of step overs before shooting straight at Begovic from a tight angle. End to end stuff!
(14’) Stoke are beginning to come in to this game a little more now as N'Zonzi plays the ball to the feet of Crouch, but a superb tackle from Distin frustrates the visitors.
(12’) The Potters find their first attack end in disappointment as Adam surges forward and swings a superb cross into the box for Crouch, but the ball flies over the head of the Stoke targetman and beyond him.
(10’) Everton fans get off their seats in anticipation as Pienaar slots Osman through. Begovic is quick to get off his line and stop the midfielder in his tracks and knock the ball away from danger.
(9’) CHANCE! Bryan Oviedo, debutising for Leighton Baines today, takes the ball down on the edge of the area but swipes his shot into the stand behind Begovic's goal. Everton are playing some lovely stuff, here!
(7’) For the Potters, the lone frontman - Crouch - has not seen anything of the ball so far. Mark Hughes will want as much of the play towards the former England International today and to make the Toffees defence as uncomfortable as possible.
(5’) The game has failed to find it's groove yet as the Toffees play a patient passing game.
(3’) SAVE! Pienaar is brought down early on and wins Everton the first set piece of the game. Oviedo lays it off to Pienaar, who is fouled again and wins yet another free-kick in a more central position. Deulofeu steps up...and Begovic gets down low to turn the ball around the post for a corner.
(1’) We are underway with Everton kicking from right to left!
The players are making their way out of the tunnel as Z-Cars timeless theme blares out of the speakers. Can the Toffees maintain their unbeaten home run this calendar year? Or will Stoke spoil the day for Martinez's men?
Not long until kick-off here at Goodison Park...looks like I picked the wrong time to remind myself that Baines, Barkley and Wilson are all in my fantasy league team and are all either injured or benched. Damn...

(22’) Much better from Newcastle here, who are attacking engagingly through the centre of midfield. WBA struggling to keep up at the moment.
(20’) REMY! The Frenchman nearly strikes the hosts into the lead, as Sissoko muscles himself into room on the left, and he crosses for Remy at the near post, but Jones makes a crucial intervention to deflect it around the post!
(18’) Suddenly Newcastle break! Cabaye slips in Remy down the left, but the striker squares up for too long against his man, and loses the ball.
(16’) Hard to see where a breakthrough will come at this point. It's been very cagey and unambitious from both outfits.
(14’) Remy drives through the centre, eating up the miles afforded by the WBA midfield. He lets fly from 25 yards, but ultimately drags the effort wide.
(12’) A minute's standing ovation in the memory of Gary Speed is faithfully observed by all in attendance. The former Wales manager was a loyal servant of the Magpies for many a year.
(11’) West Brom are looking the more promising side in attack, with Debuchy's left flank in particular looking ripe for exploitation. Long has gotten through more than once.
(9’) Diego Lugano is spotted going through his paces on the sidelines, as McAuley is looking a little woozy from a heavy collision moments ago.
(7’) Apart from that Brunt attempt, it's been a real ho hum start to the game. Both sides are clearly still feeling each other out here.
(4’) Then Krul makes a hash of the resulting corner, as Sessegnon attacks from the keeper's spill, but Sissoko is on the line to prod clear.
(3’) A WICKED free kick from Brunt is struck with an insane, horseshoe like bend, but Krul is at full stretch to tip it wide!

Newcastle have won three on the trot, with huge victories against Spurs and Chelsea among their scalps during the run. After a troubling start to the season, the Magpies can provisionally move into fifth place with a win today.

Hello, and welcome to Newcastle's EPL matchup against West Brom at St James's Park. My name is Keeghann Sinanan, and I'll be your guide for all the action.
