Good afternoon and welcome to out live text commentary of this Premier League match between Aston Villa and Everton. My name is Hayden Gribble and I shall be your guide through all the action as it happens. Who's up for some team news?

Well, that is it from me, Tom Webber, for this afternoon. Thanks a lot for joining me and I hope you enjoyed that game as much as I did. Have a great evening!
FULL TIME - Liverpool 4-1 West Brom: The Reds keep pace with Arsenal, largely thanks to a brilliant hat-trick from Suarez. Things got shaky later in the second half as Morrison pulled one back from the spot, but Sturridge secured the three points with a truly wonderous chip in the closing stages. On the whole, a deserved three points for the hosts.
(90’) The final whistle goes!
(90’) Anichebe shows great strength to hold off Skrtel, though he could be accused of backing into him. He spins the centre-back and shoots for... well, I would usually say goal, but he must have been aiming for the corner flag as it rolls out for a throw in!
(90’) Three minutes of additional time are set to be played.
--- 89’ Substitution Luis Alberto enters the game and replaces L. Suárez. ---
(88’) BRILLIANT STOP! Myhill gets down to his left to stop Suarez from netting his fourth with an effort from the top of the box after he had jinked away from Olsson. It is his last act of the game as he is withdrawn moments later. Still, a fantastic performance for the Uruguayan.
(87’) The game remains very open in the closing stages and both sides have had a chance to score even more goals. This has been a thoroughly entertaining game.
--- 86’ Substitution J. Allen enters the game and replaces S. Gerrard. ---
(85’) TOP SAVE!! Sessegnon cuts the ball back to the penalty spot and Morrison gets on the end of it. His shot takes a slight deflection but Mignolet adjusts and manages to divert the attempt behind for a corner.
(84’) Liverpool came in for some real pressure in the second half but that Sturrdige goal has breathed new life into them. They are breaking at pace when they win the ball and have every chance of adding to their tally in the closing stages.
(82’) OFF THE BAR!! Brilliant, acrobatic improvisation from Suarez as he smashes an overhead kick at goal after Olsson's clearance looped up into the area inside the area. It cannons back off the frame of the goal and Sturridge holds onto his 'best goal of the afternoon' award.
(81’) That is another excellent run from the right-back, Jones, as he dribbles all the way across the pitch before sending an effort towards goal. Unfortunately for him, Anichebe gets in the way of it!
(79’) STAT: That goal means Sturridge has only failed to score in one of his nine Premier League appearances so far this term! That suggest some clinical finishing.
--- 77’ Goal! GOOOOAAAL!! WHAT A STRIKE!! Sturridge continues his great start to the season, chipping a sublime effort across goal that looped over Myhill before nestling in the far corner. That rivals Suarez's opener for best goal of the afternoon! ---
(75’) West Brom are really stepping up the pressure now! Having converted that penalty, the Baggies clearly feel they have a chance of a miracle comeback.
(74’) HE HAS TO DO BETTER!! Anichebe does excellently to control the ball inside the area and then have the vision to spot Brunt on the far side of the box. The Northern Ireland international attempts to arrow the ball back across goal and into the bottom corner but he fires well wide.
(73’) Not close enough! The striker tries to bend the free kick around the wall and back inside the post but it lacks the curl to find the back of the net. Not his greatest effort today.
--- 72’ Yellow card J. Olsson is cautioned by the referee. ---
(72’) Sturridge is again allowed to drop deep and find the ball and as he bares down on goal Olsson scythes him to ground. Suarez is placing this one, does he fancy a fourth?
(70’) GREAT SAVE!! Sturridge picks the ball up on the half-way line and wriggles away from his marker. He sprints into the area but slips as he tries to glide past Olsson. His touch falls to Gerrard just outside him fires a shot at goal from an acute angle, but Myhill has it covered and deflects it behind for a corner.
--- 69’ Substitution S. Long comes on for N. Anelka. ---
--- 69’ Substitution C. Brunt enters play, replacing C. Yacob. ---
(68’) WHAT A CHANCE! Sessegnon spots the overlap of Ridgewell on the left and supplies his team-mate with the ball. He whips in a fantastic cross, right between the goalkeeper and his defenders, but Anichebe makes his run a little too late and fails to connect.
(67’) The referee's assistant was close to the penalty incident there and it appears it was his decision to award the spot-kick. It was perhaps a tad harsh as contact was minimal, but if anyone did clip Jones it looked to have been Cissokho.
--- 66’ Goal! GOOOOAALL! Morrison pulls one back for the visitors, hammering the spot-kick down the middle as Mignolet dives to his left. Game on at Anfield! ---
(65’) PENALTY TO WEST BROM!! Jones races into the area and goes down under pressure from Lucas and Cissokho.
(64’) SO CLOSE!! The Baggies whip the ball into the box from a free kick which Sakho conceded, and Olsson nods it back into the danger area from the back post. No one can bring it under control but it eventually bounces for McAuley, but the centre-back blazes his attempt over the roof of the goal.
--- 62’ Substitution G. Johnson is replaced with M. Kelly. ---
(62’) Johnson did well to continue to after picking up that knock in the first half and is maybe being brought off as a precaution by Rodgers. In his place comes a man who looks like he should be a regular on Hollyoaks rather than the Liverpool side, Martin Kelly.
(61’) West Brom's two holding midfielders, Mulumbu and Yacob, have done a terrible drop of restricting the space between the lines for Suarez and Sturridge. They are failling to pick the forwards up and this is enabling the to run at the defenders, which is precisely when they are at their most-dangerous.
(59’) OFF THE BAR!! What a strike from Sturridge, again picking the ball up deep and turning to run at the West Brom defence. Olsson continually backs off and when he reaches the top of the box Sturridge thunders an effort on goal that comes crashing back off the underside of the bar. Myhill had no chance.
(58’) HE SHOULD SCORE!! Johnson races in behind the defence and he puts the ball across the face of goal, where Sturridge meets it at the back post. He falls as he connects with it, though, and sends his effort well over the top.
(57’) A half-chance for West Brom as a scramble inside the box ends with Morrison trying to head the ball into the net with Mignolet elsewhere. He fails to generate enough power on the effort to guide it past the group of red shirts back to cover, though.
(56’) That is Suarez's fourth hat-trick for Liverpool, but his first in front of the Anfield faithful. I'm sure it is one they will remember for some time.
--- 55’ Assist S. Gerrard gave the assist. ---
--- 55’ Goal! GOOOOOAAAL!! Suarez gets his hat-trick! A cheap free kick is given away out on the left and Gerrard curls it into the box brilliantly. The Uruguayan rises at the near post, completely unmarked, and glances the ball into the far corner with his head. Awful defending. ---
--- 54’ Yellow card C. Yacob goes into the referee's book. ---
(53’) Cissokho falls to the ground in absolute agony as he takes a ball to the face but play continues. He writhes around on the floor and, oh my, his shirt is all red. Wait, it was like that before wasn't it. Phew, he's OK! No need for all that acting.
(52’) Henderson should do better there! He did the part, winning the ball on the edge of the box, but he flicked the ball into the area before volleying at goal. He should have just shot first time and instead sliced his attempt wide.
(51’) Not for the first time Mignolet comes off of his line to try and gather a ball into the box but he again misses it. Possession is worked to Yacob at the top of the area but his effort sails wide of the target.
(49’) Suarez does superbly to move inside from the byeline before laying the ball back to Cissokho on the corner of the box. He sets himself with his first touch and his shot is deflected behind for a corner. That kind of disguised how poor the wing-back's effort actually was!
(48’) What a waste! West Brom win a corner but Morrison sends it in far too deep, evading all of his team-mates inside the box. They could do with changing things up soon.
(47’) ... JUST WIDE!! Unbelievable whip on that effort from Sturridge, but not enough to guide it back inside the far post.
(46’) West Brom up to their old tricks, giving away free kicks just outside the area. Yacob brings down Sturridge 20 yards from goal and he looks like he fancies this one...
(46’) Liverpool kick the second half off!
Welcome back! The teams will be back on the pitch shortly so that we can begin the second half. Hopefully we will have an equally entertaining 45 minutes!
HALF TIME - Liverpool 2-0 West Brom: The Reds have been in complete control so far this afternoon, showing energetic movement and high-quality passing throughout. A pair of sublime goals from Suarez give them the lead at the break, and the Baggies desperately need to step it up after the break if they are to take anything from this game. Join me in 15 minutes for the second half to see if they can.
(45’) The half-time whistle goes!
(45’) SO CLOSE!! West Brom immediately counter and Mulumbu fires a long diagonal ball over the top of the Liverpool defence. Anichebe latches onto it and pokes a shot past Mignolet, but Skrtel gets back to cover and clear it away before it rolls into the back of the net.
(45’) What a challenge! That was like Bobby Moore in his prime! Olsson stands Suarez up before going to ground and taking the ball of the attacker's toes with a stunning tackle on the edge of the box.
(45’) We are into the first of an additional three minutes.
--- 45’ Substitution M. Amalfitano is replaced with J. Morrison. ---
(45’) Gerrard flights the ball in and Skrtel meets it at the back post, however a few ricochets make it difficult for him to direct it on target and a goal kick is awarded.
(44’) The latest to concede a free kick in a dangerous area for the hosts is Amalfitano as he jumps through the back of Cissokho in his attempts to win a header. It proves to be the Frenchman's last action in the game as he is replaced by Brunt.
(42’) The Baggies seem content to try and get to half time with the score as it is. A third goal before the break would be disastrous, and all but end their hopes of returning to the Midlands with something to show for their work.
(40’) OVER THE TOP!! Suarez and Cissokho combine well down the left but the eventual cross runs back out of the area. It is worked to Henderson at the top of the box, left of centre, and he attempts to curl an effort into the top corner on the opposite side. His technique is brilliant, but he fails to keep it down and the ball whistles narrowly over.
(38’) West Brom are conceding far too many free kicks outside their box this afternoon, but fortunately for them Liverpool fail to make anything of their most recent one. They need to stay tighter to the red shirts and not allow them the opportunity to bring the ball under control so close to goal.
(36’) Liverpool have possession on the half-way line and West Brom have all 11 players back behind the ball. The hosts are still managing to find space as they pass it around quickly with great movement. Rodgers will be delighted with the performance of his side so far.
(34’) JUST WIDE!! Half the ground think Suarez has curled a free kick into the top corner for his hat-trick, but the ball actually hit the post behind the net and rolled across the back. Great technique from the Uruguayan, but not close enough.
(33’) The Reds are in complete control here, knocking the ball about brilliantly and West Brom appear to just be chasing the about the whole time. Yacob fails to stay tight enough to Sturridge and thus pulls on his shirt. The referee awards a free kick 25 yards from goal.
(31’) Amalfitano whips in a good delivery and Olsson gets his head to it, but the assistant referee has his flag raised for offside. It looked to be the correct decision.
(30’) Johnson is back on his feet but he does not appear to be moving completely freely. He looks to be trying to shake it off, but in the meantime West Brom can put their free kick into the box...
(28’) Johnson is down after a collision with Anichibe and he is holding his knee. It doesn't look good, but it is actually a free kick to West Brom as the former Everton striker was brought to ground by Toure moments later.
(27’) WHAT A CHANCE!! Suarez slips a short pass from the free kick to Gerrard down to the byeline. The midfielder cuts it back but unfortunately Skrtel is the man who receives it and his attempted shot actually ends up going behind him. Oh to have had Sturrdige on the spot there!
(26’) Mulumbu holds onto the ball for far too long and is caught in his own half by Henderson. The referee sees no foul and Gerrard picks up possession before being flattened by Yacob. That, the official cannot ignore and he awards the hosts a free kick in a dangerous area.
(24’) Suarez plays a great pass down the challenge for Cissokho and Olsson steps across to get in the way of it. Under pressure from the left-back, though, the Swede can only put it out for a throw in level with his own area.
(23’) Great covering from Lucas! West Brom break and Anelka switches the play from left to right to find Jones. Cissokho gets beaten by him far too easily, but fortunately for him his Brazilian team-mate chases across to put in a well-timed challenge inside the area.
(21’) Confidence really looks high for the Reds this afternoon. It is perhaps not surprising, given that they have only lost once in their last 16 league outings! Their passing is quick, crisp and incisive today and West Brom are going to step it up if they are to contain them.
(19’) STAT: A total of 13 of Liverpool's 15 Premier League goals so far this season have now come in the first half. And there is still plenty of time for them to add to that tally!
--- 17’ Assist A. Cissokho gave the assist. ---
--- 17’ Goal! GOOOOOAAAL!! SUAREZ HAS TWO! More excellent football from Liverpool as Sturridge passes to Suarez, who then plays a reverse pass out wide for Cissokho. The Frenchman's first time cross is then met by the striker who doesn't break his stride and powers a header into the top corner from the edge of the box. Outstanding. ---
(16’) West Brom respond well and begin to hold onto the ball inside the opposing half but they cannot find a way through the hosts, who are doing a good job of restricting the space in which they can play. After coming up against a dead end the ball is played back and Mulumbu sends it hopelessly long.
(14’) STAT: That was Suarez's fourth goal in as many Premier League appearances this season. Love him or hate him, you cannot help but appreciate that.
--- 12’ Goal! GOOOAAALL! Stunning from Suarez! He drops off the play and instantly looks to run at goal, accelerating past Yacob before passing the ball through Olsson's legs at the top of the box. The Uruguayan then picks it up on the other side and places his finish into the bottom corner. Great goal. ---
(10’) PENALTY CLAIM! Sturridge drops off of Olsson and turns to face goal from 20 yards out. He spots Suarez's run into the area and slides in a great pass but the Uruguayan goes down under pressure from McAuley. The referee is unmoved by the striker's claims of a shirt pull, and waves for play to continue.
(9’) UNLUCKY! Deep defending from Liverpool as Anichebe gets the ball played into feet on the penalty spot and he controls it well. However, he loses his footing and Skrtel takes the chance to stab it out of the box.
(8’) Exquisite from Suarez! He kills a high ball inside the area and brings it under his control with an impeccable touch, even with Jones breathing down his neck. He holds off the defender and tees up Gerrard for a shot, but the captain's effort fails to worry Myhill.
(7’) Sturridge and Suarez combine for the first time this afternoon, with the Uruguayan being found in space to get a shot away from distance. He snatches at it somehwat, dragging his effort wide of the far post. Plenty of bright movement from the forward already today.
(5’) Cissokho pushes forward for the first time this afternoon and he drills a great cross across the six-yard box. It takes a nick off of Jones, but no one gambles to try and get on the end of it and Myhill is able to gather it under minimal pressure.

As the half progressed, however, Chelsea grew back into the ascendancy - and Fernando Torres stole the show. The Spaniard could have netted a double himself, though his most notable contribution was teeing up Andre Schurrle, whose goal separates the two sides at half-time. It's a well deserved lead for the hosts at Stamford Bridge.
Indeed, an impressive back line has been a prominent feature for the Blues so far today. Jose Mourinho's side faced early pressure from Manchester City as David Silva, Yaya Toure and Sergio Aguero threatened to take control of the encounter.
STAT ATTACK: Chelsea have not conceded more than one second-half goal so far this season. City need to think this one through...
HALF-TIME! Chelsea go into the break with the lead.
(45’) Toure again! The Ivorian sends a right-footed strike in from the edge of the area but it skims the crossbar.
(45’) HEADER! Toure gets on the end of the resultant cross but it is off target. Some food for thought for Pellegrini at the break - his side just can't force a breakthrough.
(44’) Could there be one last chance for the visitors? Nasri sees off some Chelsea pressure and wins himself a corner, though he may have preferred a free kick.
(43’) OVER! Lampard whips the ensuing set-piece onto the head of John Terry - a famous old combination - but the skipper's header sails over the bar. Incessant pressure from the Blues.
(42’) TAKE A BOW, FERNANDO! Torres is at it again, beating two players and then winning a corner for the home side.
(41’) SAVE! The visitors make their presence known, however, as Aguero tests Cech before Lampard hurriedly clears the danger. Fernandinho attempts to follow that up - but his long-distance strike is desperately wayward.
(40’) Ramires now plays Schurrle in on the edge of the area, though the move eventually breaks down after some overly fancy play from playmaker Oscar.
(38’) Can the away side get back into this one before the break? Or will Mourinho's side double their lead?
(37’) The visitors now look shellshocked as Toure and Nasri try to spark things up in midfield. All of their strong early link-up play has somewhat been undone by a period of unstoppable brilliance from Torres.
(36’) CROSSBAR! Torres once again!! This really is the Torres of old as he hits a sweet strike that crashes against the bar. The hosts really could be 3-0 up by now. But will they rue these missed chances?
(34’) CHANCE! Torres and Schurrle combine yet again and Chelsea almost lead 2-0! Mourinho really is getting the best out of the Spanaird, isn't he? Could this be another way to one-up Rafa Benitez?
--- 33’ Assist Fernando Torres gave the assist. ---
--- 33’ Goal! GOAL! Schurrle puts the Blues ahead! Superb work from man of the moment Torres once again but it is the German who finishes off after being teed up. Suddenly, the hosts look the stronger - and their resilience is rewarded with the lead! ---
--- 31’ Yellow card M. Nastasić is yellow-carded. ---
(31’) The momentum has well and truly swung in Chelsea's favour here.
(29’) Threatening signs from Torres, who now tumbles to the ground without being awarded a free kick. He should have converted that earlier chance, though...
(28’) WHAT A MISS! Torres is in once again but fluffs his lines! The Spaniard is completely unmarked yet seems to hesitate that he's offside. He can't miss - but does, probably due to his unawareness that he was completely onside and free of any opposition defenders.
--- 27’ Yellow card P. Zabaleta is cautioned by the referee. ---
(27’) Chelsea win a free kick in a reasonably dangerous position now, with Lampard driving it forward and Torres flicking it on. The visitors make a clearance but it falls back to the Spaniard, though he cannot make the most of the chance.
(25’) Schurrle and Ivanovic now combine, until Fernandinho slides in unconventionally and breaks the Chelsea move down.
(24’) Boos from the home crowd as Zabaleta rashly challenges Hazard but no free kick is given.
(23’) Poor play from Torres now as the home side look to get back into their rhythm. The Spaniard receives the ball and tries to play one of his team-mates in but overhits his pass. A good idea - but badly executed.
--- 22’ Yellow card FOUL! Lampard dives in from behind for the second time today, giving away a free kick in the Chelsea half. ---
(21’) The visitors undeniably have the upper hand here, though...
(20’) More superb movement from Aguero forces another corner for the away side. It escapes the attentions of everyone initially, though City regain possession and try to play Aguero in. The pass is underwhelming, however, and rolls off for a goal kick.
(19’) Can City make their early energy count? Silva, Nasri, Toure and Aguero have been finding space in between the lines at a rate that will no doubt alarm Mourinho and his back line.
(18’) We're almost 20 minutes in at Stamford Bridge and it's still goalless - but the tactical battles on show are nothing short of fascinating.
(16’) Yet another corner is whipped in but Hazard clears. However, Gael Clichy pushes forward on the rebound, though he is dispossessed and Chelsea finally regain the ball in their own half.
(15’) Andre Schurrle clears but Mourinho is clearly perturbed as he enters the technical area to bark some instructions to his side.
(14’) The hosts are now struggling to get possession as the away side press and press. After initially winning a corner (but failing to capitalise) pressure from Silva, Nasri and Sergio Aguero has won them another set-piece.
(12’) OFFSIDE! Nasri is played in and unleashes a shot at goal. The effort is wide, though, and the offside flag is raised anyway.
(11’) Chelsea's early progress should not be discounted, however - they started the brighter of the two.
(10’) Silva, in particular, looks as though he could provide the difference between the two sides here. His link-up play has been nothing short of magnificent so far - and that's just ten minutes in.
(9’) Samir Nasri and Toure now combine as City start to settle into the game. Their five-man midfield looks to be giving them an extra edge in the middle of the park, something they were desperately missing in the away defeats to Cardiff City and Aston Villa.
(8’) Cue Chelsea losing possession and Yaya Toure capitalising. The Ivorian looks to latch onto the loose ball and forces a foul out of Frank Lampard.
(7’) City hit straight back through a long run from David Silva, with the Spaniard eventually spraying the ball out to Fernandinho. The Brazilian cannot return the favour, however, and out the ball goes once again. Put a foot wrong and it will be costly here.
(6’) Ramires and Hazard now exchange passes in the centre of the pitch and the Brazilian is able to find Torres in the area. The Spaniard leaps and gets his head to the ball, though his header is straight at Joe Hart.
(5’) It's been an end-to-end start already, something that will no doubt please both managers. Chelsea are now caught unaware by a quick free kick and Zabaleta is once again the target. But this time, Ashley Cole is there to shepherd the ball out of play.
(4’) City bring themselves into the action now, however, as Pablo Zabaleta advances forward and sends a searching cross into the area. Petr Cech is on hand to collect, though.
(2’) Chelsea have already enjoyed half-chances through the brilliant movement of Eden Hazard. Will the Belgian shine today?
(1’) We're off! And it's been a bright start from the hosts already.
Despite it being just eight games into the season, the magnitude of this one needs no emphasis as Jose Mourinho's Blues fight it out with Manuel Pellegrini's charges for a vital three points. Before the start of the season, many had tipped these two sides as their favourites for the title. Several weeks later, little has changed.
And the visitors will look like this: Hart; Zabaleta, Clichy, Demichelis, Nastasic; Fernandinho, Nasri, Javi Garca, Yaya Toure, Silva; Aguero. Subs: Pantilimon, Richards, Milner, Negredo, Dzeko, Kolarov, Navas.

Good afternoon and welcome to live-text commentary of Chelsea against Manchester City - arguably the biggest Premier League clash of the season so far! I'm your host Tim Poole and I'll be guiding you through the action. We'll no doubt be in for a treat...

It ends all square at the Liberty Stadium between Swansea City and West Ham United. Sam Allardyce has masterminded another clean sheet on the road for the Londoners. Swansea huffed and puffed but couldn't blow down the visitor's defensive wall. Jussi Jaaskelainen, Winston Reid and James Tomkins will get a pat on the back for their displays. Laudrup will have some stern words reserved for the Welsh side. Despite some heavy rotation, they were well off the pace after their Europa League excursions.
FULL-TIME: Swansea City 0-0 West Ham United
(90’) PENALTY SHOUT! Dyer slams the ball at Cole inside the box and pleads with referee Phil Dowd for a spot kick. The man in charge is having none of it though.
(90’) West Ham are in no rush to get on with a set-piece. They won't give this away now. This has been a disciplined, organised and effective display from the visitors. Sam Allardyce deserves great credit. With a potent forward, they might have even won this.
(90’) A loud cheer of encouragement rings around the Liberty Stadium as the board signals four minutes of additional time.
(89’) Stewart Downing is casual on the right wing as he thinks he is settling for a throw in. He looks gobsmacked when the linesman flags for a Swansea throw! West Ham survive the danger, much to Downing's relief.
--- 87’ Yellow card J. Cole is cautioned by the referee. ---
(87’) Noble carries the ball forward with a surging run from midfield, he crosses into the box but Joe Cole's swinging shot is well blocked by Angel Rangel. West Ham could snatch this on the break and complete a flawless away performance.
(85’) Michu is fed through on goal by Leon Britton but the flag goes up for offside. It was a really tight decision, but Jaaskelainen made another great save regardless. The veteran goalkeeper and his two centre-backs have been immense.
(83’) Great defending from Tomkins again to nip in ahead of Bony as he tried to combine with Michu in the final third. Carlton Cole and Chico are embroiled in an off-the-ball incident. Allardyce looks amused.
(81’) Chico forrays on to the right wing and somehow wins his side a corner with a deflected shot. Swansea are throwing the kitchen sink at their opponents but the corner is wastefully overhit.
(80’) West Ham are camped right back in their own half. They are inviting pressure from the hosts. They look confident in their ability to shut the Swans out.
--- 78’ Substitution J. Cole enters the game and replaces R. Morrison. ---

(76’) Great defending from Tomkins. De Guzman's free kick crossed into the box looked like it was about to drop on Bony's head but the West Ham defender did really well to intervene and save his team. Defending like that is as good as a goal.
(74’) West Ham are trying to play some keep ball now to take the impetus out of Swansea's attack. Bony goes in hard and late on Jaaskelainen as the Hammers almost gave it away under pressure.
(72’) GREAT SAVE! A Swansea corner falls kindly for Wilfried Bony in the box, the substitute fires a shot at goal from close range but Jaaskelainen does brilliantly to react and push the ball away from danger. Still got it, the Finnish stopper.
(70’) More confusion with Vorm and his defenders. There is a lack of communication it seems as Williams and the Dutchman almost take each other out going for the same ball.
(68’) The corner is easily defended by the hosts though. Looks like Allardyce is going in for the kill with the introduction of Carlton Cole.
(67’) Rat launches a long throw into the box and Carlton Cole is there to flick it on with his first touch of the match. Chico slices the ball out for a corner...
--- 66’ Substitution W. Bony comes on for Álvaro. ---
--- 65’ Yellow card Àngel Rangel goes into the referee's book. ---
(65’) Carlton Cole comes on for West Ham, his first appearance since re-signing for the club earlier this month. A goal from him would complete a great narrative...
--- 64’ Substitution C. Cole enters play, replacing M. Diamé. ---
(64’) Morrison searches for an opening in the box but Chico defends well, as he has all afternoon. Vasquez has a long-range shot moments later, but it's high, wide and not at all handsome.
(62’) CLOSE! Reid makes Vorm's life difficult from a corner by standing right in front of him, allowing Noble to have a strike at goal from the cross but the midfielder can't find a gap in the wall of bodies in front of him.
--- 61’ Substitution Pablo Hernández comes on for W. Routledge. ---
(60’) Rangel casually nods the ball back to Vorm and the goalkeeper has to scramble to the byline to prevent a needless corner.
(58’) West Ham squeezing Swansea back to the halfway line. The home side are going to have to be patient if they are to score this afternoon. At the moment they are finding it incredibly difficult to manufacture chances.
(55’) CHANCE! Nathan Dyer does brilliantly to lose his man and create space for a cross. He delivers one low and hard for Vasquez but it has too much on it and despite the striker's best efforts, it flies away for a throw.

(49’) Almost a chance for Swansea early in this second period but Vasquez fails to control the ball when he is fed through and it comes to nothing. Early signs of improvement though.
(46’) West Ham take the kick-off and we are underway in the second half. Let's hope for some goals!
The teams are slowly making their way out for the second period. Let's see if Swansea can find some penetration, otherwise West Ham could be on their way to successive away wins in the Premier League for the first time since December 2007.
Surprising statistic which sums up the story of the first half. West Ham managed 11 shots in that 45 minutes, compared to the home team's total of two (via Opta).
Sam Allardyce will definitely be the happier of the two managers at half-time. His strikerless West Ham side have dealt with the limited threat Swansea have posed well and have had the better of the chances. Downing and Nolan have come closest without success. Michael Laudrup needs to inspire his team to improve in the second period. They have not been their usual selves.
HALF-TIME: Swansea City 0-0 West Ham United
(45’) CHANCE! Ravel Morrison does brilliantly to get to the byline and cross into the box but Kevin Nolan can't quite connect cleanly with his header and it goes flying over the bar!
(45’) Two minutes will be added on at the end of the half.
(44’) Routledge gets back to help out Taylor. Despite his best intentions all he's done is make matters worse as he concedes a free kick near the corner flag. Swansea are not at the races, the referee's whistle couldn't come sooner.

(38’) Diame breaks down the right and he makes his way into the box. Swansea hammer clear for a throw though. West Ham are coming on strong late in this half. This hasn't been the flowing stuff we usually associate with Swansea.

(24’) CLOSE! Rangel clears off the line after Vorm makes a complete mess of a routine ball into the box. Almost a catastrophe for the Dutchman in goal for Swansea.

(20’) It's safe to say this match is being played among a torrential downpour. It should benefit Swansea's slick passing style, if anything.

Both teams are emerging from the tunnel, kick-off at the Liberty Stadium is moments away...

So looks like we may be in for a draw if those last two tidbits are anything to go by. However, it should be a goalfest - there have been more goals scored at the Liberty Stadium this season (16) than at any other Premier League ground.

A valiant effort from the Tigers, but they fall victim to a controversial penalty decision, that saw Soldado strike the only goal of the game from the spot with 10 minutes remaining. Not a vintage Spurs display by any means, but three points is all that matters, and they've snared just that to move within three of league leaders Arsenal. Hull remain in 10th place.
(90’) No time for any more action, Tottenham seal the points.
(90’) Huddlestone goes for the headlines against his former club with a stinging drive...that sails a yard or so above Lloris' post! And that may be that.
(90’) Free kick right on the edge of the area, after a foul by Dawson! Last chance for the visitors, and a good one...
(90’) Spurs slowing the tempo of the game down nicely, keeping the ball calmly and making Hull chase the ball. The visiting fans sing: "One nil to the referee," still clearly bitter about the penalty decision that led to Soldado's opener.
(90’) Five minutes of added time to go.
--- 90’ Yellow card C. Eriksen is cautioned by the referee. ---
(90’) Brady takes charge of a dangerous free kick just over 20 yards out, but though powerful, his effort is too central, and Lloris catches with not too much trouble.
(89’) Townsend is finally up, and though a bit dazed, he can still make his own way to the Tottenham dugout - though judging from his body language, he wants to get back on the pitch! His hand has been bandaged up quite heavily, but he looks to be ok otherwise. Good signs.
(88’) The game has had the stuffing rather knocked out of it since the collision, which will suit Spurs just fine, as they look to close out a tough three points.

(87’) An absolute throng of staff is attending to Townsend, effectively blocking the cameras from getting a view of the player. Still, this incident is reminiscent of Robin van Persie's similar misfortune at Loftus Road last season.
(85’) Still not clear what the final verdict of damage is on Townsend, but one of the photographers has clearly come off worse for wear, strapped up with a massive bandage to cover a gash.

--- 84’ Substitution G. Boyd is replaced with R. Brady. ---
(84’) Nasty tumble from Townsend, who goes barrelling over the advertising hoardings into a pit of photographers. Not a nice collision to witness at all, and a stretcher has been called to the scene as the game moves on.
(82’) Steve Bruce will be fuming at that decision, but his side better watch out, as they fail to make a corner count, and Townsend scampers with the loose ball down the right. (79’) Elmohamady is unfortunate to get whistled for a handball, as Vertonghen's cross deflects off his leg and onto his hand. Not intentional in the slightest, but Soldado has a chance to give Spurs the lead...
(79’) SPURS HAVE A PENALTY!

(73’) Boyd booked for upending Lennon, as Spurs have a free kick. However, Hull manager to clear the delivery.

(71’) Spurs cranking up the pressure. The addition of Eriksen has added an extra dimension in the attacking third. There's still a lack of killer instinct up front though, as Soldado looks off the pace.

(63’) Eriksen with a corner, and Harper comes off his line to get to the ball just ahead of Dawson, who was lurking for a header on the post.

(57’) The defender is able to get to his feet, as Hull defend against some more Spurs pressure.
(57’) Davies has stayed down and requires some treatment from the physios, after he looked to have tweaked something during that last sequence.

(40’) Rosenior, by the way, was booked for fouling Chiriches on that play.

Hello and welcome to this afternoon's LIVE commentary on the Premier League meeting between Tottenham Hotspur and Hull City.

Phew! What a game. Only just catching my breath! So, on a day of personal history for Steven Gerrard, the England skipper leads his side back to the top of the Premier League - for the time being at least. As for Newcastle, Alan Pardew will be encouraged by his side's efforts - especially after they went down to ten-men. Thank you for joining me for this thriller. I have been Hayden Gribble, and you stay classy football fans!
FULLTIME: NEWCASTLE 2-2 LIVERPOOL. Steven Gerrard netted his 100th Premier League goal in a thrilling encounter at St James Park. Yohan Cabaye put the Magpies in front in the first half with a long range effort but Newcastle's joy was short lived as Yanga-Mbiwa pulle Suarez down in the box and saw red, leaving the England captain to slot home the equaliser. A full-blooded seconf half saw substitiute Dummett sneak in at the back post to put the home side in front again but the SAS combined again as Daniel Sturridge snatched all three points away from Alan Pardew's men after finishing from close range after a cut back from Suarez.
(90’) FULLTIME! ...But Krul is equal to his effort and the fulltime whistle blows! It is all over at St James Park.
(90’) What a chance for a Liverpool winner. The Newcastle fans are disbelieving as Suarez is pulled down on the edge of the box. Free-kick to the visitors - but the final whistle should have blown, surely? Suarez steps up...
(90’) CHANCE! Luis Alberto - a late substitute for Liverpool - has the chance to settle the game, but he smashes the ball over from 15-yards. It was easier to score!
(90’) The Newcastle faithful are willing their team forward but the players are playing for time and are content to keep possession. Not long to go, now...
(90’) We are into the last minute (plus four minutes of stoppage time) as Sturridge wins a corner for Liverpool. Gerrard steps up to take it...but it is cleared and leads to a break on for the home side.
(89’) A few ironic cheers implode from the home fans as Moses overhits a pass and sees it trickle out of play. Sounds to me like they are happy to settle for a point!
--- 86’ Yellow card M. Debuchy receives a yellow card. ---
(86’) CHANCE! Sturridge - who was booked a couple of minutes ago for a clumsy challenge on Gouffran - miskicks in the box after good work from Gerrard and the ball goes harmlessly out of play. Any connection from the England man there would have poked Liverpool in front!
(85’) How many classics have we had between these two sides over the years? This one may not be as memorable as the 4-3's of old but at 2-2 it is perfectly poised for a frantic finish.
--- 84’ Yellow card D. Sturridge goes into the referee's book. ---
--- 83’ Substitution G. Johnson is replaced with R. Sterling. ---
(82’) CHANCE! Henderson finds himself in asimilar position to his earlier shot and again he dips it high and wide from the edge of the area after latching onto a weak clearance from as Liverpool corner. Newcastle are hanging on a bit in these last few minutes.
(80’) We have ten minutes to go...and plenty of time for more goals as this game has well and truly come to life in this half. Who will emerge victorious?
--- 78’ Substitution Y. Cabaye is replaced with V. Anita. ---
--- 78’ Substitution Sammy Ameobi enters play, replacing H. Ben Arfa. ---
(77’) STAT ATTACK: There have now been 126 goals in #BPL matches between Newcastle and Liverpool - more than any other fixture. (OptaJoe)
(75’) OFF THE POST! Oh, what a chance for Liverpool - and Suarez in particular. The Reds find joy down the right flank again and the ball is cut back to the Uraguayan, who pings his half-volley onto the crossbar from 12-yards. 15 minutes to go and it's a red tide at the moment!
--- 72’ Assist Assist by L. Suárez. ---
--- 72’ Goal! GOAL! Liverpool are back on level terms! And would you know it - it's the SAS who attack! Suarez gets free of his marker in the box and cuts the ball across goal to an on-rushing Daniel Sturridge, who meets the cross with his head before Debuchy has a chance to clear. We are in for a special final chapter in this incredible game! ---
--- 71’ Yellow card K. Touré is yellow-carded. ---
(71’) CHANCE! Suarez sparks into life and snaps a shot across Krul's goal-line - but the dutchman is equal to it ad Debuchy mops up the loose ball. Just under twenty minutes to go!
(69’) CHANCE! How many time have Newcaslte been trroubled by a set-piece in this game? This time it is Moses who is left with a free header from a corner but he smashes it over. On another day, the Reds would have put a couple of these corners away. Is it not to be  for them today?
--- 68’ Yellow card Y. Gouffran is cautioned by the referee. ---
(65’) One of the main problems that Liverpool have had today is the level of impact their deadly SAS strike has had on the Newcastle defence. Both Suarez and Sturridge look tired after their appearances for their countries in midweek and their ineffectiveness is stiffling Liverpool's attacking ideas.
--- 63’ Substitution M. Sakho is done for the day. Luis Alberto is his replacement. ---
(63’) CHANCE! Henderson looks very disappointed with himself for not hitting the target. The midfield man finds himself on the edge of the 'd' but skews his shot so high it would be a conversion if he were playing rugby. But he isn't so it's a goal kick to the home side.
(61’) STAT ATTACK: 1 - Liverpool have scored just one second half goal in their previous seven PL matches this season. Splutter. (OptaJoe)
(60’) What a game this has been! Full of talking points, memorable strikes, controversy and a personal milestone for Steven Gerrard. We have half an hour to go but it isn't over yet! Not by a long chalk..
--- 57’ Goal! GOAL! Ten-man Newcastle are back in front! Cabaye floats a free-kick from the left into the box and the Liverpool defence are guilty of ball watching as the substitute Dummett sneaks in at the back post to steer the ball past Mignolet. A shot in the arm for the Magpies! ---
(55’) CHANCE! Liverpool are knocking on the black and white door as a nice passage of play leads to Moses punting the ball high over Krul's goal. Should have kept it down, there.
(50’) PENALTY APPEAL! The Newcaslte faithful are raging! They believe that they should have a penalty as Skrtel makes a critical interception to stop Remy from pulling the trigger from close range. (48’) CHANCE! Henderson hits a diagonal ball to Johnson, who cut in on his left foot just outside the box and sends a stinging low shot towards goal, but Krul is equal to it and pushes it out for a corner. Great save from the Dutch keeper!

STAT ATTACK: 118 - Liverpool have been awarded more penalties than any other team in PL history (Arsenal 115, Man Utd 110). Award. (OptaJoe)
So, which way has the pendulum swung now? Newcastle do look the fresher of the two sides as there appears to be a few jet-lagged faces in the Liverpool line-up. But will the one-man advantage benefit the Reds? We are about to find out as the second half is coming right up...
STAT ATTACK: 9 - All nine of Newcastle's first half shots vs Liverpool came from outside the penalty area. Distanced. (OptaJoe)

(43’) STAT ATTACK: 24 - Steven Gerrard becomes the 24th player to score 100  Premier League goals. Landmark. (OptaJoe)
--- 42’ Goal! GOAL! Krul goes the right way but Gerrard smashes the ball low to his right. That's a century of league goals for the Kop legend and relief for the travelling fans as it has been a laboured Liverpool performance so far! ---
--- 40’ Red card! The referee sends off M. Yanga-Mbiwa! ---
(40’) PENALTY AND RED CARD! Suarez hits Liverpool on the break but is pulle down in the box by Yanga-Mbiwa - it's a clear penalty! Newcastle plead the defenders innocence but referee Andre Marriner produces the red card. He's off!..and it's a chance for Steven Gerrard to grab his 100th Premier League goal from the spot...
(40’) STAT ATTACK - Ten of the Reds' 11 league goals this season have been scored in the first half. Their only second-half strike was in the 3-1 win at Sunderland last month, netted by Luis Suarez. (BBCSport)
(36’) CHANCE! It is nearly deja-vu as Cabaye gets into a similar position to his goal - but instead of powering his shot he goes for a dipper instead - but Mignolet is happy to see it drop a foot away form his net. The St James Park faithful took in a collective gasp as the French artist continues to wield his talents. So close to doubling the Magpies' lead!
(33’) CHANCE! Alan Pardew will be tearing his hair out as another free header is gifted to Toure in the Newcastle box. Luckily for his side, though, the defender headers it over. The home side need to get tighter on set-pieces or Liverpool will make them pay eventually...
(31’) The SAS have failed to get involved much in this game as Daniel Sturridge has come off the field...to change his boots! Remarkable, shouldn't he be sorting his footwear out BEFORE the match?
(28’) Newcastle's fans have sparked back into life but Liverpool need to find their voice as it looks like an International Break hangover for Brendan Rodger's men so far this half.
(25’) STAT ATTACK - 13 of Newcastle's last Premier League goals have been scored by Frenchmen.
(24’) CHANCE! Oh, Cissokho, that was your chance to be an instant hero for your new side. The debutant headers over from six-yards. He was unmarked too. Liverpool need to wake up to get back into this game.

--- 23’ Goal! GOAL! What a strike from Cabaye! The French playmaker brings the ball forward from the centre circle and lashes the ball into the bottom corner from 30-yards. Mignolet saw it late but let's not take that away from Cabaye. First blood, Newcastle! ---

(11’) CHANCE! Moses goes on a good run and cuts the ball back to Sturridge, but the England International hits a poor shot straight at keeper Tim Krul.

Meanwhile Alan Pardew has approached the technical area with a notepad and pen in his hand. Either he is making early notes or he is about to give the Liverpool number 7 a parking ticket!
(9’) The home side are playing some nice passes across the Liverpool defence but there is little penertration into the box at the moment. A timid start to proceedings.

Good afternoon and welcome to the live text commentary of Newcastle versus Liverpool. My name is Hayden Gribble and I will be taking you through all the goals and action of a game with a history of classic Premier League encounters. But before we go any further, let's have a look at the team news...

FULL-TIME and Chelsea have come from behind to secure an ultimately rather easy win against Cardiff, who took the lead through Jordon Mutch early on. But Eden Hazard struck before half-time to level matters and Samuel Eto'o and Oscar put Jose Mourinho's side firmly in control at the start of the second period.Eden Hazard put the gloss on the win with a late effort to cap a terrific individual display from the Belgian.
(90’) John Terry defends well with Fraizer Campbell threatening a late consolation and earns himself a free-kick as the hosts close in on an comfortable victory.
(90’) David Luiz breaks out of defence, looking doubly determined to get in on the act after his first-half gaffe but his shot is wild as he approaches the Cardiff penalty area.
(88’) The game is beginning to filter out somewhat, with Chelsea content with their three-goal advantage in the final exchanges.That said, they have to be on their guard to prevent Cardiff scoring again after Peter Whittingham's devilish delivery.
(85’) Chelsea almost hit Cardiff on the break once more as Eden Hazard, Oscar and Ramires pour forward but the final ball is lacking this time. The visitors have reached the stage in this contest where they are content to take a breather after the barrage they have been subjected to in this second period.
--- 82’ Goal! GOAL! The goals really are flowing now at Stamford Bridge as Eden Hazard makes it four but, once again, David Marshall will not be best pleased watching that one back.
Frank Lampard releases Hazard down the left and the Belgian does superbly to check back inside Steven Caulker and fire in low at goal, but Marshall really should have dealt with it. ---
--- 81’ Substitution R. Gestede enters the game and replaces A. Gunnarsson. ---
(79’) Chelsea almost snatch a fourth after countering on their wounded opponents devastatingly. Eden Hazard feeds in Willian with several options to choose from but the Brazilian's low effort is saved well by David Marshall.
--- 78’ Assist Ramires provided the assist. ---
--- 78’ Goal! GOAL! And that should be that for Chelsea, as substitute Oscar makes it 3-1 to the home side. Ramires battles well in midfield and dispossesses Aron Gunnarsson to feed the Brazilian, who advances and sends a dipping effort over the outstretched reach of David Marshall, who may feel he could have done slightly better with that. ---
(75’) So close to an equaliser for Cardiff, as Petr Cech denies Kim Bo-Kyung with a sprawling stop.
Andrew Taylor's clever pass into the left-hand channel finds Kim, who unleashes a ferocious strike towards the far post but the Chelsea stalwart does superbly to reach out a hand and tip the ball away for a corner.
(73’) Jose Mourinho is asked to move to the seats just behind the Chelsea dugout after remonstrating with the officials a bit too actively.The Blues then counter at rapid speed, scything through the heart of the opposition. The ball ends up with Fernando Torres on the edge of the box but after moving it onto his left foot, Steven Caulker gets in the way of his thumping shot.
(70’) It proves to be the Cameroonian's last contribution as he is replaced by Cesar Azpilicueta. Mourinho returning to a back four following the introduction of Fernando Torres moments ago.
--- 69’ Substitution Azpilicueta comes on for S. Eto'o. ---
--- 67’ Substitution F. Campbell enters play, replacing P. Odemwingie. ---
--- 66’ Assist E. Hazard provided the assist. ---
--- 66’ Goal! GOAL! Samuel Eto'o scores his first goal for Chelsea! A great spell of pressure from the hosts leads to them taking the lead. Eden Hazard picks up the ball outside the area and feeds a brilliant pass into Eto'o. The former Barcelona striker shuffles it past Steven Caulker before rifling an effort past the keeper and into the bottom corner. ---
(65’) WHAT A CHANCE! Peter Whittingham whips a great cross in from the left and it is knocked down for Aron Gunnarsson on the edge of the box. His effort is appalling though, as he fails to shoot or cross the ball, and Chelsea clear the danger away.
--- 64’ Substitution R. Bertrand is done for the day. Fernando Torres is his replacement. ---
(64’) Peter Odemwingie feeds Don Cowie out on the right but with the Nigerian dropping deep there is no one to aim for in the area. The Cardiff man's cross is therefore headed away comfortably by Branislav Ivanovic.Cardiff then get some room just outside the area and Jordon Mutch goes for goal from about 20 yards. It proves to be a waste, as he fires well over the top of the bar.
(61’) Chelsea make their first change as Juan Mata departs and Oscar steps up from the bench to help offer his side some fresh attacking invention.
--- 58’ Substitution Oscar enters play, replacing Mata. ---
(58’) Willian again causes havoc thanks to some impressive link-up play with Ramires but the Brazilian's cross is well intercepted by Ben Turner before Samuel Eto'o's cross is deflected away from Eden Hazard.
--- 56’ Substitution Bo-Kyung Kim enters play, replacing G. Medel. ---
(55’) Eden Hazard, Willian and Ryan Bertrand link up to devastating effect as Juan Mata manages to send an acrobatic volley just wide before David Marshall is booked for timewasting.
--- 54’ Yellow card D. Marshall is yellow-carded. ---
(52’) A string of corners from the right test Petr Cech and he has to be particularly alert to deal with Peter Whittingham's inswinger as Ben Turner's goes close to heading home before Gary Medel fires over.
(49’) Samuel Eto'o is picked out by Willian 25 yards from goal but his curling strike from just outside the area is claimed rather easily in the end by David Marshall. Chelsea starting this half how they ended the first, largely on top.
(46’) Chelsea get us back underway for the second half.
HALF-TIME and it's Chelsea 1-1 Cardiff thanks to two freak goals. Jordon Mutch capitalised on David Luiz's lax defending to dink past Petr Cech before David Marshall's clanger allowed Samuel Eto'o to nip in and eventually tee up Eden Hazard to level matters at the break.
(45’) Juan Mata is felled by Don Cowie on the left wing but Frank Lampard wastes the subsequent free-kick as he curls it wide of the far post above everybody.
--- 45’ Yellow card D. Cowie is cautioned by the referee. ---
(45’) Ryan Bertrand has to be composed in defence as Cardiff press the hosts high up the pitch when they try to play out from the back.Moments later, Eden Hazard looks to add a second as he steps inside from the left and unleashes a low effort that David Marshall comfortably fields.
(42’) Chelsea have struggled when Cardiff launch high balls into their area. Peter Whittingham almost steals in after more hesitancy from the hosts at the back but John Terry is across to block.
--- 41’ Yellow card David Luiz goes into the referee's book. ---
(39’) David Luiz thrashes the ball over the bar after advancing into a promising position but Cardiff seem to be retreating into their shell at the moment, as the hosts look to push home their increasing domincance on this game.
(36’) The goal looks to have spurred Chelsea on as they are starting to get more and more bodies in attacking areas. Willian slips through Samuel Eto'o but the striker's low cross is intercepted and lashed away for a corner.
--- 33’ Assist Assist by S. Eto'o. ---
--- 33’ Goal! GOAL! In bizarre circumstances, Chelsea are level. David Marshall, moments after getting away with handling outside the area, bounces the ball from his hands and Samuel Eto'o nips in to play in Eden Hazard. (31’) Eden Hazard drives at the defence and tries to slip in the overlapping Ryan Bertrand but cannot quite keep his footing as Fernando Torres already begins his warm-up down on the touchline.David Marshall is lucky, meanwhile, as he looks to have handled outside the area when collecting a long ball.
(28’) Fans around Stamford Bridge are beginning to get frustrated with their side's sloppy start.The hosts have largely controlled possession but are not getting in behind the Bluebirds' defence enough for Jose Mourinho's liking and he won't be happy with his side's defending as Aron Gunnarsson is afforded too much room, but the Icelandic international can only head over.
(25’) Branislav Ivanovic fizzes in a stinging cross which David Marshall has to deal well with to prevent it from flying into the far corner of his goal.Signs in the last few minutes that Chelsea are beginning to crank things up a notch to find an equaliser.
(22’) Peter Whittingham's free-kick from deep is headed towards the far top corner until Petr Cech produces a stunning stop, tipping the ball away for a corner before claiming the ball from thr resultant set piece.The Blues swiftly head downfield and earn a corner of their own, which John Terry again meets but cannot direct an effort on target.
(19’) Juan Mata's delivery from the corner flag is much better this time around, as he picks out John Terry's near-post run and the skipper's header is firm but veers just beyond the upright with Gary Medel covering on the far post.
(16’) Chelsea earn a corner after more good forward play from Samuel Eto'o but Juan Mata's delivery is disappointing and the set play ultimately comes to nothing. Cardiff are content to sit and protect the precious advantage they have established.
(13’) The goal has stunned Chelsea, who cannot get any sort of rhythm going in their play. Cardiff boss Malky Mackay will be delighted with the start his side have made here.
--- 10’ Goal! GOAL! Cardiff stun Stamford Bridge as they take the lead with their first attempt on goal but they owe a great deal of gratitude to David Luiz here as Jordon Mutch opens the scoring.From a routine clearance from goalkeeper David Marshall the ball is played back to the Brazilian, who inexplicably leaves the ball for Petr Cech to collect but Jordon Mutch nips in to dink the ball over the Blues stopper to send the travelling faithful into raptures. ---
(9’) Samuel Eto'o pulls wide into the left-hand channel and finds Juan Mata with a clever cut-back, but the Spaniard kicks at thin air and Branislav Ivanovic wastes the rebound.
(7’) A good strong challenge on Eden Hazard by Peter Odemwingie leaves the Belgian bemused as to why he hasn't been awarded a free-kick and leads to a Cardiff breakaway, but the Nigerian dwells on the ball as Chelsea get back to deal with the danger.Then, after Samuel Eto'o is felled, Frank Lampard fires a free-kick straight into the wall and Cardiff clear.
(4’) Chelsea have started the game brightly, knocking the ball around with ease but Gary Medel and Aron Gunnarsson are doing a good job of getting in the faces of Juan Mata and Eden Hazard early on.
(1’) And we're underway as Cardiff, kicking from right to left in this first half, get the ball rolling.
The Bluebirds can take comfort, however, in the fact they won the last time these two faced off in the top flight. Cardiff were 3-2 winners way back in September 1961.
The stats do not read well for Cardiff fans either. The last time the two sides met was in an FA Cup fifth-round clash in February 2010 as today's hosts ran out comfortable 4-1 winners.Chelsea's current unbeaten streak in the league here stands at 11 games, with 10 victories and just the one draw while the Blues have scored at least two goals in their last eight league games here too.
But today's opposition will not be about to hand out any favours as Jose Mourinho look to maintain their 100% league record at Stamford Bridge so far this campaign, off the back of a four-game unbeaten run on the road prior to the international hiatus.
It has been a turbulent week at the Cardiff City Stadium, to say the least, after head of recruitment Iain Moody was relieved of his duties but Bluebirds fans will have breathed a huge sigh of relief that Malky Mackay remains in charge.
So Willian and Eden Hazard, after their goalscoring cameos in Chelsea's late win at Carrow Road, are drafted in as Oscar drops to the bench and Andre Schurrle sits out after sustaining an injury with Germany despite his hat-trick heroics. (65’) GREAT CHANCE! It's Stoke's best moment of the match. Stephen Ireland is the guilty party. The ball is cut back for him inside the box and he really should have put the home side a goal up. Instead, he blasted his effort wastefully over. He knows it.

(62’) Those changes have disrupted the rhythm of the game, what little rhythm it had. Lets hope the added firepower from both sides mean more goalmouth action!
(59’) In an answer to Stoke's substitution, West Brom are readying Nicolas Anelka to join the action.

(58’) Kenwyne Jones has come on for Jon Walters in the meantime, lets see if that can help Mark Hughes' side gain some impetus in proceedings. Very flat from them on the whole thus far.
(56’) PENALTY SHOUT! Berahino goes down in the box after Charlie Adam treads on his heel! It looked a clear penalty from angle, the referee is having none of it though! Stoke get away with one!
(53’) Mulumbu and Yacob combine to great effect to escape the pressing game of Stoke, giving Sessegnon the space to pick out Ridgewell, who's cross is easily caught. West Brom now showing signs of their form early in the first half.
(50’) Almost a chance as Ireland plucks the ball excellently from the sky and sends a through ball in for Walters, but it's a touch too long. Agonising for Stoke.

(45’) Stoke have a chance in the one additional minute at the end of the half from a free kick out on the right. Arnautovic's delivery is easily cleared before N'Zonzi shoots from the edge of the area, but his shot is tamely dragged wide.

(42’) Two of Stoke's best chances have come in the final few minutes of the half. West Brom need to be wary not to concede just before half-time. Looks like Hughes' men sense a chance though.
(40’) CHANCE! Close for the home side. A very clever freekick from the training ground tricks the Baggies back-line but Ireland's low effort is well-saved. Easily the best chance for Stoke so far.

(33’) No real action in the last few minutes. Stoke are failing to find any penetration in the final third. All of the chances have come, and gone, for West Brom.
(30’) Great composure and skill from Pieters to bamboozle Anichebe and lose his man, playing Stoke out of a potential spot of bother. Stoke have taken some of West Brom's early momentum now.
(27’) Referee Howard Webb is having a stern word with Nzonzi, who is close to getting a booking after a couple of late challenges. He's trying his best to disrupt the visitor's flow.
(24’) GREAT SAVE AGAIN! It's fine passing and interchange from the Baggies before the ball eventually comes to Amalfitano, but before he can set himself for the shot, Begovic is off his line in a flash to smother the shot.
(21’) Stoke have found their feet on the ball again but on reflection, West Brom should be ahead with their early chances. The Potters have weathered the storm and are growing into the game.
(18’) GREAT SAVE! Begovic denies Sessegnon with a super save using his feet from point-blank range. Anichebe fed Sessegnon who jinked his way inside the box but just when you thought he would side foot it into the back of the net, Begovic reacted to make a fine stop.
(15’) Shaky moment at the back for Begovic with Berahino closing down, but he does well to get it clear. Almost a blunder from the normally reliable shotstopper.
(12’) Anichebe and Berahino are combining well up top for West Brom. The Baggies are beginning to pile some pressure on Stoke but as of yet the Potters' defence is holding strong. The hosts' look most threatening on the break, strangely enough.
(9’) CHANCE! That aformentioned corner comes to nothing. Moments later though, Sessegnon smashes a volley at goal from Berahino's cross from deep on the left flank. He strikes it sweetly but it sails over the bar.
(7’) Sessegnon shows great pace on the right to burst past two Stoke defenders into the box but the summer signing couldn't find a cross once he got to the byline. WEst Brom corner...

(3’) First chance falls to the hosts. Wilkinson's cross is cleared for a corner by Mulumbu after some neat work on the right-hand side by Arnautovic. The set-peice comes to nothing though. Stoke have started on top.

The teams are emerging from the tunnel into a super atmosphere at the Britannia Stadium. Kick-off is only moments away...

Anyway, that'll be all from me, Sam Wells, today. I hope you enjoyed the game as much as I did and, until next time, farewell!
Pellegrini, meanwhile, will be pleased with his side's performance. They survived the Hammer's strong spell after Aguero's second goal and, although he would've no doubt preferred a win at a canter, this victory not only illustrates the Citizen's class, but also their resolve and spirit. As he's no doubt already become accustomed to, Aguero put in another fantastic performance, capped by two goals and an assist which, coupled with Silva and Negredo's similarly sterling performances, provides City with confidence as they head into a potentially tricky week.
Sam Allardyce won't, you imagine, be too disillusioned by that defeat; they can't really have expected to claim any points here, in spite of their scalp at Spurs a couple of weekends ago. They can, meanwhile, draw positives from the fact that they made City work for their win, something that looked unlikely after the Citizen's opening goal. It'll be interesting to see whether Big Sam persists with the striker-less formation as they face weaker teams - he certainly has a lot to think about after this game.
(90’) And the referee's whistle brings an end to proceedings here at Upton Park! West Ham fought valiantly but the Citizens proved too strong for them as goals from the outstanding Sergio Aguero and David Silva consign the home side to defeat.
(90’) The Hammers continue to try to make something work in these late stages but, as Tomkins tries, and fails, to meet another delivery, it appears as though this game is done and dusted.
(90’) West Ham work a nice move in the City area, eventually resulting in a shooting opportunity for Morrison on the edge of the area. He attempts to curl into the far corner but his effort flies well over the bar.
(90’) As four minutes of injury time are called, Milner fouls Petric, affording the Hammers an opportunity to launch a ball into the box. Rat does just that and Tomkins wins the delivery but can only head into Hart's grateful arms.
(89’) It simply appears a case of running down the clock now as City casually retain possession with West Ham clearly feeling the effects of a game that involved a significant amount of harrying.
(87’) Toure, seemingly under a significant amount of duress from Reid, lopes into the box before going down under said pressure. That looked a decent shout at first but, on second inspection, it appears as though the shirt-pulling was actually from the Ivorian, rather than the New Zealander.
(86’) Petric, just on for Nolan, attempts to get involved in the action but he can't quite retrieve Rat's pass and City have possession once more.
(85’) The Hammers launch a counter through Jarvis but the substitute finds himself surrounded by City players within seconds of getting the ball. The away side have not just shown their class today, they've shown some fight too.
--- 83’ Substitution M. Petrić enters the game and replaces K. Nolan. ---
(83’) West Ham earn a free kick in a dangerous position; they work it short and Downing delivers but it eventually comes to nothing. (81’) Aguero is replaced by Jovetic, greeted by a suitably emphatic reception from the away support. He's been excellent today, playing a major part in all of the three goals and proving a constant thorn in the West Ham defence's proverbial side.
--- 80’ Assist The assist came from S. Agüero. ---
--- 80’ Goal! GOAL! It's David Silva and surely that is that! Another beautifully worked move ends in the Spaniard curling a ball into the far corner, after more sterling work from Aguero provided him with the ball on the edge of the area. The Argentine backheeled into his teammate's path, allowing Silva to do the rest and put Manchester City 3-1 up! ---
(77’) The Hammers continue to push for that elusive equaliser as we approach the final ten minutes of this contest. They are peppering crosses into the City area but the Citizens are coping adeptly with anything West Ham can throw at them.
(76’) Jarvis gets forward well down the left, exposing Garcia's lack of pace before cutting back inside and attempting to square to the oncoming Nolan. They aren't quite on the same wavelength, however, and Fernandinho duly steps in to avert any potential danger.
(75’) Downing, impressive in this second half, whips in another cross from the right wing but, alas, he gets too much on it and the delivery runs out for a goal kick.

At the moment, and despite what this commentator said just minutes earlier, this could go either way!

Though the Hammers have posed little actual threat, Pellegrini will want his side to dominate and he'll be keen to ensure that they don't become complacent going into the second period.
Sam Allardyce will be feeling mixed emotions as he conducts the half-time team talk in the dressing room; though they endured spells of City domination where the dual threat of Negredo and Aguero appeared simply too potent to deal with, they also enjoyed a decent amount of possession as the half wore on.
