(85’) Joe Cole is primed to come on for the Hammers now. Incidentally, he was supposed to come on just before West Ham opened the scoring but, clearly, Allardyce opted to shut up shop after the first goal and, somewhat inadvertently one must presume, managed to conjure up two more goals!
(84’) Soldado almost gives Spurs a glimmer of hope after taking down a long ball majestically with his first touch, before firing an effort goalwards. The strike gets a deflection, however, and it's behind for a corner.
(83’) Walker, playing practically as a right winger now, attempts to find a man in the box but the Hammers simply have too many in there. Diame, one of eight West Ham players in the box, intervenes and hoofs clear.
(82’) Spurs look resigned to their fate here; they attempt to get something going down the left but Lamela can only find the head of Winston Reid who, in turn, finds the gloves of Jussi Jaaskelainen.
(81’) Holtby replaces Naughton after that goal as Tottenham, somewhat nominally, one must think, throw caution to the wind as they find themselves three goals adrift with eight minutes remaining.
--- 80’ Substitution M. Diamé is done for the day. J. Collins is his replacement. ---
--- 80’ Substitution K. Naughton is done for the day. L. Holtby is his replacement. ---
(80’) Tottenham had thrown men forward in search of a goal to initiate a fightback and they paid the price. To be fair, they wouldn't have anticipated any West Ham player taking advantage, especially not in such style!
--- 79’ Goal! Goal to West Ham United, scored by R. Morrison! ---
(78’) GOAL! And it's fantastic from Ravel Morrison! The youngster finally delivers on his promise and in some style, running half the length of the pitch, beating Dawson and outmuscling Vertonghen before dinking the ball over the onrushing Lloris. An excellent run and a fine finish - West Ham are 3-0 up!
(77’) Townsend provides another opportunity after some sterling work down the right, getting beyond Rat before cutting back on his left and whipping a dangerous ball in. Paulinho meets it but his header can only find the grateful arms of Jaaskelainen.
(75’) West Ham have a free kick in a dangerous area as they go in search of a third (who would've though I'd be saying that at the half-time break?!) but Downing's effort floats harmlessly over the bar.
(74’) West Ham continue to cause Spurs problems as Diame's cross is cleared behind by Dawson. Vilas-Boas will be wondering how his team found themselves in this position; they've played some nice football but have lacked the penetrative touch to break down the Hammers and, ultimately, it looks as though they've paid the price.
--- 73’ Substitution Soldado enters the game and replaces C. Eriksen. ---
--- 72’ Goal! GOAL! And, against all odds, it's a West Ham second! As with before, it's a decidedly scrappy goal, involving another fortuitious rebound. After being threaded through nicely by Noble, Vaz Te struck goalwards, only to find his shot saved by Lloris. The save rebounds into the legs of the falling Vaz Te, however, and the strike (if you can call it that) finds it way into the net! 2-0 at White Hart Lane! ---
(70’) Townsend causes Rat some problems down the right but Vaz Te, anticipating the issues the English winger can cause, doubles up on him and wins the ball, putting it out for a throw. Good defensive work from the Hammers winger there.
(69’) West Ham are now, as one might expect, operating even more defensively. One also senses that Spurs are facing a thankless task in trying to break down this well-drilled Hammers outfit as we approach the final twenty minutes of this contest.
(67’) It'll be interesting to see how Spurs respond to going behind - they've played some nice football thus far but have lacked any real urgency, that goal could be the catalyst that they needed to go and win this game. Or, perhaps not. It'll also be interesting to see whether Allardyce decides to introduce Cole, as planned prior to the opening goal.
--- 66’ Assist K. Nolan gave the assist. ---
--- 66’ Goal! GOAL! And it's Winston Reid! In a manner entirely befitting of a fairly scrappy game, the Hammers centre back has opened the scoring from a set piece. He headed Downing's cross goalwards, only to find himself denied by Nolan. The ball, quite fortuitiously, fell back to the New Zealander's feet, however, and he duly struck into an empty net. Scrappy but the Hammers won't mind - it's 1-0! ---
(64’) Joe Cole gets ready to make his return from injury as he limbers up on the touchline, Sam Allardyce clearly deeming it an apropos time to introduce the creative midfielder.
--- 63’ Substitution G. Sigurdsson is replaced with E. Lamela. ---
(63’) There is a brief interval in play as Rat goes down following a collision with Townsend. It is, in fact, very brief as the left back is up and fine within no time. He's dealt better with the threat of Townsend since that opening 45 minutes; the England international has been quiet in this second period.
(62’) Lamela does indeed come on and it's, perhaps unsurprisingly, Sigurdsson who makes way. The Icelandic midfielder has been on form recently but nothing has really gone his way today.
(61’) Lamela appears primed to come on for Spurs as Vilas-Boas appears intent on injecting his side with some much-needed creativity.
(60’) Spurs engage in some neat interplay in the middle of the park but there are simply too many numbers up against them. Diame eventually dispossesses Eriksen as Tottenham continue to struggle to break their opposition down.
(59’) Sigurdsson gets forward down the left as Spurs appear to have resumed their strangehold on the game. His cross is cleared by the hitherto impressive Tomkins, however, and Tottenham have to build from the back once again.
(58’) Spurs, after enduring some rare West Ham pressure, launch an attack of their own but Townsend puts a halt to any potential danger with a misplaced pass.
(56’) Diame goes down under the challenge of Diame in the Spurs area but the referee deems it unworthy of a penalty. To be fair, the Tottenham midfielder appeared to get the ball as the Hammers midfielder went down very easily.
(54’) After the ensuing corner comes to nothing, Walker, quite bewilderingly, decides to give them another one, despite Downing's cross clearly being goal kick bound. From that corner, Tomkins goes incredibly close! He headed Downing's delivery into the ground and almost managed to beat Lloris, though the Frenchman did just about succeed in palming the ball away, albeit with some difficulty. A good chance that!
(53’) In response to Tottenham's increasing pressure, West Ham attempt to launch a counter as Morrison threats Vaz Te through down the left. The winger, in turn, feeds the rapidly advancing Nolan, who plays off Dawson for a corner.
(52’) Spurs go close and, once again, its Jermain Defoe! He forces Jaaskelainen into another save, this time from the edge of the area after some lovely interplay between Eriksen, Sigurdsson and Paulinho. The goalkeeper tips over adeptly and Tottenham have yet another corner.
(51’) Spurs earn a corner and, after Eriksen and Defoe work it short, the former attempts to whip in a cross. Tomkins deflects it behind, however, meaning the Dane is tasked with putting in another delivery, his third in as many minutes.
(50’) It's a fantastic delivery from the Dane, causing the West Ham defence all kinds of problems as they all leave it for fear of diverting into their own net. Unfortunately for Spurs, their players can't quite make any meaningful contact either, Vertonghen just about reaching it at the far post but proving unable to do anything with it. That really was a great ball in.
(49’) Spurs continue with their strong start to the half as Paulinho is fouled by Reid about 35 yards from goal, giving Spurs a decent opportunity to whip a cross into the box. Eriksen looks as though he's primed to do just that.
(48’) Diame, still operating further forward than usual, puts a cross into the area but it's dealt with adeptly by Vertonghen, the Belgian centre back duly heading clear.
(47’) Tottenham almost get off to a cracking start to the half as Defoe almost finds the net within the opening 30 seconds! The England international, after being threaded through nicely by Paulinho, is denied by Jaaskelainen, however, as he spurns the best chance of the game thus far.
(46’) Spurs get us underway in this second period as, with their close rivals Arsenal currently losing against West Brom, they look for a win that may just take them top of the league.
The teams are just coming back onto the pitch now as we await the beginning of the second half at White Hart Lane - let's hope for a more entertaining spectacle than the first!
Sam Allardyce, meanwhile, will probably be quite pleased with that half. They had the best chance of the half through Noble's ingenuity and Nolan's acrobatics as a set piece came closest to breaking the deadlock towards the end of a chance bereft of any gilt-edged opportunities. They have looked, Rat's Townsend-induced frailities aside, fairly confident defensively, though they must be aware that the worst is yet to come from a Spurs side rife with attacking potential. The Hammers will be hoping for more of the same in the second period as they look to stay stoic at the back and capitalise on any set-piece opportunities that come their way.
Vilas-Boas will, despite West Ham barely threatening their back four, be disappointed by that first half; they have found themselves unable to break through the densely packed Hammers ranks as chances have been few and far between in this opening period. Still, there is cause for optimism in the form of Townsend's performance down the right wing - he has looked more than capable of making something happen as Rat has struggled to contain the England international. Nonetheless, the Spurs boss will be looking for more invention from a side that has struggled to get going in the opening 45 minutes.
(45’) The referee's whistle brings an end to a first half that, frankly, will not live long in the memory! It's 0-0 at the interval here at White Hart Lane.
(45’) Townsend, as has been the story of this first half, causes West Ham problems down the right side, this time cutting inside before feeding the advancing Walker down the right. The England international's cross is deflected behind by Reid as Spurs have a corner with a minute remaining in the half.
(45’) Three minutes of injury time are called, just as the half appears to be getting going. Let's see if either team can get what would undoubtedly be a vital goal just before the half-time interval.
(45’) Defoe almost works a shooting opportunity in the Hammers' box but finds himself crowded out. Dembele finds himself subject to the same fate thirty seconds later after Demel got back well to halt a typically marauding run.
(43’) Instead of shooting, as perhaps everyone expected, Noble dinked the ball over the wall, finding Kevin Nolan, who had peeled off the wall. The midfielder attempted a volley on the turn and almost pulled it off! He gets, if anything, too much on it, however, and the effort flies wide of the far post. Probably the best opportunity of the half!
(42’) Sigurdsson brings Morrison down quite cynically on the edge of the Spurs area, giving West Ham a free kick in a dangerous position.
(41’) Reid does well to dispossess the ever-bright Christian Eriksen as the latter looks for the pass that will unlock the Hammers defence. West Ham work the ball down the other end and, after Morrison forces a mistake from Dawson, the former Manchester United man attempts to cut back to the edge of the area but his pass is deflected behind for a corner by the same man he just robbed of the ball.
(40’) Townsend continues to cause Rat problems down that right flank as the Romanian left back is pulled up for getting too tight to the Spurs winger. It'll be interesting to see whether Spurs can reap the rewards from that battle - it appears as though the England international has the beating of his opponent all day long.
(39’) West Ham attempt to get in behind Spurs but, as with Morrison minutes before, Downing is caught offside. That was much more clear-cut, the former Liverpool winger's run was never going to come to anything there.
(38’) Eriksen jinks in his inimitable style on the edge of the area, before feeding Paulinho with a smart pass. The Brazilian takes a pop from the edge of the area but doesn't get his left foot around it, skewing his effort well wide of the goal.
(37’) Ravel Morrison, hitherto quiet in this first period, almost breaks through the Spurs defence but is caught offside. He went marginally too early as, but for the linesman's flag, he would've been through on goal from Diame's pass.
(36’) West Ham, as has oft been the case in this first half, hoof a long ball towards no-one in particular, affording Spurs possession before getting men behind the ball.
(35’) Townsend, who continues to look dangerous, outpaces Rat down the right wing before putting in a dangerous delivery. Defoe attempts to meet it but can't quite make contact and the opportunity goes begging.
(34’) A lovely turn from Eriksen completely bamboozles Nolan as he brings the Dane down quite cynically. That was lovely skill from the Spurs summer signing.
(33’) West Ham have a corner which, given their first-half showing thus far, could be their best chance to score. Reid gets his head on the delivery but can't get quite enough on it, flicking the ball well wide of the post.
(31’) Paulinho spurns probably the best chance of the half! Townsend, who's looked the most dangerous of the Spurs attacking quartet thus far, gets forward down the right before cutting back to the Brazilian. The midfielder attempts to volley goalwards from just inside the area but his effort fails to find the target.
(30’) The Hammers attempt to work something offensively through Diame and Nolan but, in all honesty, they look fairly impotent in attack without the threat of an orthodox striker.
(29’) Paulinho threads Defoe through on goal but the offside flag thwarts the England international and rightly so, he made his run way too early there.
(28’) Stewart Downing whips in a dangerous cross from the right flank and Diame meets it, only to get too much on his header as his effort flies well over the bar.
(26’) Tottenham have threatened in fits and starts but, having just passed the halfway mark in this first period, Vilas-Boas will have wanted more from his team. Though, to be fair, the Hammers have been resolute defensively, despite not posing any real problems going forward (as one might expect, given their goalscoring record this season).
(25’) Tottenham are close to forging their first real opportunity but, again, Tomkins is there to step in and clear the danger. Once again, it was Sigurdsson who caused the problems after he attempted to put Defoe through on goal, only to find his pass intercepted by the Hammers centre back.
(24’) Townsend goes close from distance! After receiving the ball from Dembele on the right, he cuts inside and absolutely leathers a ball from distance. The strike swerves this way and that but ends up whistling a few inches over the bar.
(23’) Spurs do almost manage to do just that through a nifty chipped ball in from the right foot of Eriksen. Paulinho can't quite make contact, however, and Tomkins is there to avert any potential danger.
(22’) Tottenham are enjoying the better of the possession since that brief stoppage, they're stroking the ball around nicely but can't get work a way through the densely-packed West Ham ranks.
(21’) Jaaskelainen, whose every touch is now greeted with a chorus of boo's from the home support after that boot incident, hoofs the ball clear as West Ham attempt to gather some momentum.
(20’) Jaaskelainen has a new boot (he only changed one, oddly) and the game can now resume. Exhilarating stuff here at White Hart Lane.
(19’) It soon becomes evident, however, that Jaaskelainen is, in fact, swapping his boots as his current choice of footwear appear to be causing him some problems. It says a lot about this game thus far that this is probably the most noteworthy incident of the first 20 minutes.
(18’) There's a stoppage in play as Jaaskelainan appears to be having some sort of problems, though it's not clear what exactly is wrong with the Hammers goalkeeper.
(17’) Dembele sidesteps Nolan with some style in West Ham's half but his pass goes astray, finding the feet of Diame. The ball rebounds off of the Hammers player into the stride of Paulinho, who takes a hopeful pop from distance. His effort flies well over the bar, however, and it's a West Ham goal kick.
(16’) The slow tempo start persists in this encounter as West Ham retain possession in their own half before pumping a hopeful long ball forward, aimed in the general direction of Diame. Dawson is there, however, and it's Spurs' turn to indulge in a spot of aimless possession.
(15’) West Ham attempt to go to long to Diame, who appears to be playing the nominal role of lone striker today. The stand-in forward attempts to make something of it but can't quite make contact with the ball, allowing it to run through to Lloris in the Spurs goal.
(14’) Townsend does well to beat a couple of men before allowing Sigurdsson to take over on the edge of the area. In characteristically opportunistic fashion, the Icelandic midfielder takes a touch before striking it goalwards. Nothing doing though as Jaaskelainan proves more than equal to it, claiming it with a fair amount of ease.
(12’) Spurs then have their first half-chance of the game, coming courtesy of a smart Sigurdsson through ball. The midfielder finds Paulinho breaking through the Hammers ranks but Reid is there, the centre back doing enough to put the Brazilian off as he strikes off-target.
(11’) The first half-chance of the game as Downing crosses a ball in from the right, finding Nolan in the area. The ever-dangerous midfielder attempts to head goalwards but gets it slightly wrong, instead heading harmlessly wide of the far post.
(10’) Townsend attempts to get in behind the West Ham defence but Rat intervenes, tackling adeptly and getting the ball clear as we await the first real opportunity here at White Hart Lane.
(9’) West Ham attempt to probe down Spurs' left but come up against a white wall. Diame therefore passes the ball all the way back to his own defenders.
(8’) West Ham are actually in the ascendancy here; while Spurs struggle to find a foothold in this contest, the Hammers are pushing forward, though they are yet to forge a real opportunity.
(6’) From the ensuing throw-in, Rat tries to launch one into the box but it only succeeds in finding a Spurs defender. It's headed out to the edge of the area and Noble attempts to dink one towards the far post. He sees his effort fly harmlessly wide but the Hammers have made a decent start here.
(5’) It's Dawson's turn to intervene after Rat does well, getting forward down the left. The Romanian drives in a dangerous cross but the Spurs captain is there to divert the ball away, clearing for a throw.
(4’) It looks like Spurs are going to have to be patient today; West Ham are certainly getting numbers behind the ball. That notion is illustrated by Reid adeptly stepping in to prevent a Sigurdsson through ball from finding Defoe.
(3’) It's got off to a slow start as White Hart Lane as West Ham are packing the midfield and constantly rotating their frontman, in the absence of an Andy Carroll-like figure.
(2’) Hugo Lloris gets Spurs off to an unconvincing start as an early clearance ricochets against the rapidly advancing Ricardo Vaz Te. Nothing comes off it though, much to the relief of the French goalkeeper.
(1’) And we're underway! West Ham kick off proceedings as they look for a win that would take them out of the relegation zone.
Both teams are coming out on the pitch now as we're minutes away from kick off at White Hart Lane!
West Ham, meanwhile, make three changes from the side that fell to a disappointing 1-0 defeat against Hull last weekend, with Guy Demel, Stuart Downing and Ricardo Vaz Te all starting at the expense of Joey O'Brien, Matt Jarvis and Modibo Maiga.
Andre Vilas-Boas makes just one change from the side that drew 1-1 against Chelsea last Saturday, with Roberto Soldado dropped as Jermain Defoe comes in upfront after scoring in their 2-0 win against Anzhi in midweek.
West Ham: Jaaskelainen, Demel, Tomkins, Reid, Rat, Noble, Morrison, Nolan, Downing, Diame, Vaz Te. Subs: Adrian, O'Brien, Collins, Cole, Jarvis, Petric, Maiga.
Tottenham: Lloris; Walker, Dawson, Vertonghen, Naughton; Dembele, Paulinho; Townsend, Eriksen, Sigurdsson; Defoe. Subs: Friedel, Chiriches, Sandro, Holtby, Chadli, Lamela, Soldado.
And here come the team line-ups:
Their lack of a goal threat in the continued absence of Andy Carroll is perhaps the main concern, as they have managed a paltry return of four goals in six games; a record that goes some way to explaining their poor position in the league. As the cliche goes, however, anything can happen in the Premier League and, though a trip to White Hart Lane won't fill Hammers fans with optimism, Allardyce will fancy his chances of causing an upset. This could be a cracker!
Sam Allardyce and his men, however, might have something to say about that. Although, given their recent form, it is likely that words are as far as it'll go; the Hammers currently sit 18th in the table, having fallen into the relegation zone following Fulham's fairly fortuitious 1-0 win against Stoke yesterday.
So everything appears to be rosy for Spurs and, with eminently winnable league fixtures against Aston Villa and Hull completing their fixture list for October, they could be a force to be reckoned with come the end of the month. However, first thing's first – Vilas-Boas will be expecting to take a fairly comfortable win into the international break as they come up against struggling opposition today.
Tottenham come into this game appearing in fine fettle, Andre Vilas-Boas' men haven't lost a game since the 1st of September and have only dropped points against Arsenal and Chelsea thus far this season. Their new signings appear to be gelling with each and every game and their form means that they could feasibly go top of the league today, should other results go their way.

An excellent, hard fought contest that sees both teams deservedly split the points. Arsenal's away win streak ends, but the draw is still enough to see them go back to the top of the table, level on points and goal difference with Liverpool, but ahead on goals scored. West Brom meanwhile show that their victory over Manchester United was no fluke, giving the Gunners a run for their money all the way to the final whistle.
(90’) Rosicky goes streaming forward on one last Arsenal attack, but Bendtner loses the ball, and Lee Mason immediately blows the final whistle!
(90’) Koscielny a tad lucky there perhaps, barging into the back of Long under the pretense of challenging for a high ball, which got nowhere near the pair. Appeals for a penalty, but again, no dice.
(90’) Ozil loses the ball under pressure from Jones. Haven't seen much of the German international today, a statement that rings true for most of Arsenal's attacking players.
(90’) Into the first of FOUR added minutes.
(90’) A left back for a winger, a clear signal of intent from Clarke, despite Amalfitano's niggle. West Brom happy with the point it seems, and a hard earned one it will be, IF they hold on!
--- 89’ Substitution C. Brunt enters the game and replaces M. Amalfitano. ---
(88’) Amalfitano clearly struggling, clutching his glute and grimacing in some pain. Clarke reacts quickly by introducing veteran Baggie Brunt in his stead.
(87’) The match just slowing down a tad in the last few minutes, but Flamini does have a decent shooting opportunity from 18 yards, in the end, seeing it deflected harmlessly into the path of Myhill.
--- 85’ Substitution N. Bendtner enters play, replacing O. Giroud. ---
(85’) Off goes Giroud, relatively ineffective today, and on comes the great Dane, looking noticeably slimmer since his tubby visage at the start of the season!
(83’) Cometh the hour, cometh the man...Nicklas Bendtner the golden samurai is stripping down on the sidelines...
(82’) Arsenal continue to probe. Wilshere's cross to Giroud is headed away, Arteta resets and plays into Giroud again, who is brought down, legally, by Mulumbu on the edge of the box!
(81’) Jenkinson for Arsenal, with a good purposeful run down the right, but his cross is met by the planted Olsson on the near post.
(80’) Good news for you Gunners fans though, Tottenham have just gone 3-0 down to West Ham at White Hart Lane!
--- 79’ Substitution J. Morrison enters play, replacing S. Sessègnon. ---
(79’) What a great finish to this game, both sides going for broke. You'll not find me calling a winner at this tenuous stage!
(78’) Hang on, that was a RISKY challenge from Mulumbu, going in from behind on Wilshere, who was primed to shoot from just inside the box! His gamble paid off though, as he just got to the ball first, and it's deemed legal by Lee Mason!
(77’) EXCELLENT goalkeeping from Myhill! Wilshere has put Giroud through, and the French striker tries to round the Baggies keeper, but he is having none of it, and pushes the ball away at the last!
(76’) Credit to West Brom for still pushing forward, and not letting their heads drop after conceding. The hosts still look capable of another.
(74’) Long with an incisive ball to pick out Amalfitano, who has a gap to aim at on the near post, but Koscielny just does enough to harry him off his shot!
(73’) JONES! A rasping drive from the right back, who pushed forward well, but Szczesny is on it, and pushes wide smartly!
(72’) More pressure from Arsenal, this time coming down the left hand side. Gibbs' cross narrowly misses Giroud and West Brom breathe again!
(70’) Jenkinson left worse for wear after a towering Yacob challenge. A bit of treatment required for the right back.
--- 69’ Substitution S. Long enters play, replacing N. Anelka. ---
(69’) Anelka is replaced by Long. A terrible game from the forward, if I'm honest, anonymous for the most part but still found time to miss a golden chance.
(69’) All of a sudden, the Arsenal pressure breaks down, and Sessegnon is released through the middle! Anelka is in acres of space on the left, and Sessegnon tries to slip him in, but the heel of Koscielny intercepts that dangerous pass!
(67’) Arsenal coming on strong again, and West Brom are forced into an increasingly tenuous defensive stance at the back!
(65’) Game well and truly on folks! That deflection upon reflection played a significant part in Wilshere's strike beating Myhill, but those are the breaks of the game, and maybe just the stroke of luck Wenger and his side needed.
--- 63’ Assist T. Rosický gave the assist. ---
--- 63’ Goal! Out of nowhere, a seemingly stagnated Arsenal attack is converted into a goal! Giroud was challenged on the edge of the area, and Rosicky bobbles the ball up to Wilshere, who catches it clean on the volley, hammering it into the bottom corner! Hint of a deflection, but try to get anyone in an Arsenal shirt to care. ---
(63’) TOO LATE! WILSHERE DRAWS ARSENAL LEVEL!
(63’) You get the feeling that this game is on the verge of another breakthrough. Arsenal are getting the ball into some good positions, and West Brom may just want that second goal to cushion their lead.
(61’) Rosicky gets his first touch after a strong Arsenal spell in the West Brom penalty area, but hacks his volley horribly into orbit. Earlier, a Gibbs cross was taken inadvertently on the elbow by Jones, a hard call for the referee to make, and one that he avoids by waving play on.
--- 59’ Substitution A. Ramsey is replaced with T. Rosický. ---
(59’) Rosicky on, Ramsey off. Not a good game from the Welshman who looked to be struggling with a knee problem. Wenger opts for the safe option in Rosicky, over gambling on Gnabry or Miyaichi.
(57’) Rosicky getting stripped and ready as Flamini sees a good shot blocked by Amalfitano.
(56’) Dangerous free kick for West Brom after Gibbs fouled Sessegnon. Amalfitano whips it into the mixer, but Mertesacker gets his head to it first. The Gunners try to counter through Giroud, but Myhill is on it.
--- 54’ Yellow card J. Olsson is cautioned by the referee. ---
(54’) Olsson clambers all over Giroud to win a header, and ends up fouling the striker quite dangerously. Yellow card for the defender.
(53’) NEARLY A SECOND for West Brom, as Amalfitano gets in down the left, and tries to beat Szczesny with a curler towards the far bottom corner, but just misses! Close shave, but Jenkinson is getting grilled here.
(51’) Sessegnon has picked up where he left off, troubling Jenkinson again, and winning a corner off the right back. The ball comes in from Amalfitano, but Szczesny wins the challenge against Olsson and pushes clear.
(50’) Ramsey drills a threatening cross in that is just ahead of a wall of yellow shirts. An entertaining start to the half!
(48’) TWO CHANCES BACK TO BACK! Sessegnon gets past Jenkinson on the flank, and squares the ball to Anelka, right on the six yard line, but the striker fluffs his lines horribly! Arsenal go back up the pitch, Giroud holds up well and slips in Wilshere, who is barged off his shot by Olsson! Some arguments for a penalty there.
(47’) There is a complete lack of penetration from this Arsenal side out wide and it's no surprise why. Ramsey and Wilshere are not wingers. A look to the bench may hold the answer though. Rosicky, as tidy as he was against Napoli, may be more of the same, but wild card wingers Gnabry and Miyaichi, can the youngsters change the tide?
(46’) Here we go again!
We've got a game folks! Arsenal huffed and puffed, but in the end failed to spark into life. West Brom made the most of a strong ending to the half, as Yacob headed in the opener from Amalfitano's perfect cross. The Gunners have it all to do in the second half, but this Arsenal team have shown increasing resilience of late and are not to be taken lightly. For Clarke and West Brom, a perfect end to the half. Will they keep up the pressure after the break or will they set up shop? Join me for the restart in a bit.
(45’) And that's it for the half!
(45’) Olsson shanks a clearance badly, and Ramsey is nearly on it in a flash to poke home! But the defender recovers just enough to marshal the Welshman away from goal.
--- 45’ +2 Yellow card J. Wilshere receives a yellow card. ---
(45’) Smiles all around at the Hawthorns, but nothing of the sort on the Arsenal bench.
(45’) Frustration getting the better of Wilshere, who loses the ball on the edge of the area and goes into Yacob from behind. Arsenal's second yellow of the day.
(45’) Three added minutes to go, three minutes for Arsenal to survive. Who would have thought it?
(44’) West Brom are piling on the pressure! All of a sudden Arsenal's left flank looks ripe for the taking as Jones hurtles forward, with only a last ditch Wilshere tackle getting the ball out of harm's way!
--- 42’ Assist Assist by M. Amalfitano. ---
--- 42’ Goal! Arsenal's soft centre makes an appearance! It was a simple goal in the end from the hosts, Amalfitano's cross coming in to the near post, where Yacob leaves Jenkinson and Arteta for dead to bounce a header in off the ground! ---
(42’) YACOB BREAKS THE DEADLOCK!
(41’) Sessegnon leaves Gibbs for dead and has time to pick out a cross that Koscielny just manages to hack away!
(41’) West Brom free kick, Amalfitano whips it in, and Szczesny gets to the ball, but not entirely convincingly, and palms it clear. He swore a foul, the Polish keeper.
(40’) Gibbs preventing from getting a cross in on the overlap from a heroic challenge by Jones. Ozil's resulting corner is cleared to the edge of the box, where Ramsey strikes, but Myhill is spared the save by a inadvertent block from Giroud!
(38’) This is more like it from the Baggies! The direct running of Sessegnon, as ever, causes a few problems for that Arsenal left side, and GIbbs narrowly manages to clear for a corner. From the delivery, Mertesacker gets a strong head onto the ball.
(38’) With Giroud and Olsson tussling for the ball, Wilshere spots an opportunity and runs in to nick the ball, but is instead clattered by the defender. No foul, and another moment of discomfort for the midfielder.
(36’) Sessegnon loses out to a firm Flamini tackle right on the top of the D. Arsenal break again, Ramsey spreads wide to Giroud, who shifts onto his left foot, but cannot come up with a powerful enough shot to trouble Myhill.
(34’) PENALTY!? Sessegnon goes hurtling past Gibbs and immediately tumbles down inside the box. Lee Mason had an excellent view of that though, and waves play on, to the fury of the home fans.
(34’) Wilshere back on, still rubbing his eye in some discomfort.
(33’) Again Arsenal probe, but after some fanciful footwork from Ozil and some neat touches from Ramsey and Gibbs, the West Brom backline win the ball.
(31’) Wilshere has stayed down, in fact, and has gestured to the bench for some treatment. Nothing muscular folks, it looks like he just got a solid but unintentional poke in the eye from Yacob. Painful one for sure!
(30’) Wilshere runs right into Sessegnon on the edge of the box and goes down in a heap. West Brom go forward, and Wilshere is getting up very gingerly.
(28’) Not quite a false alarm maybe? Rosicky is spotted warming up on the touchline, signalling a potential early departure for Ramsey. You can't really blame Wenger for wanting to play him every game, but perhaps a little more caution with his midfield star may be needed.
(26’) Another slick Arsenal move at the top of the box sees Wilshere take aim, and skids it just wide of Myhill's right hand side!
(25’) False alarm it seems, as the Welshman is back in action. But lest we forget, he needed a spell of treatment midweek against Napoli as well. Ramsey has played almost every minute for Arsenal this season, so are these early signs of burnout?
(23’) Surprise, surprise, Flamini has been booked for taking down Anelka in the middle. Less surprising and more worrying for Wenger is the sight of Ramsey down on the deck clutching his knee...
(23’) Giroud's openings are slowly and slowly getting more obvious. Another through ball, another run, but McAuley just gets his boot in.
--- 22’ Yellow card M. Flamini is yellow-carded. ---
(22’) The game starting to pick up pace now as both sides go back and fourth. West Brom see a good cross blocked, and Arsenal break, but Ozil's in swinging cross just fails to be met with enough conviction by Giroud.
(20’) Arsenal on a stunning run of form away from home, winning a dozen straight games outside the Emirates. The last time they notched up such a streak, they channeled it into a Premier League title. Eat your heart out Gunners.
(18’) A stunning pass from Ozil goes diagonally across the top of the box and picks the overlapping Gibbs out perfectly, but the left back wastes that glorious set up with a wild shot into orbit.
(17’) Another probing period for Arsenal nearly bears fruit when Ozil and Ramsey combine, but the Welshman's slipped ball is just behind the streaking Flamini, and Olsson intercepts.
(15’) West Brom finally sustain possession for longer than five seconds in the Arsenal half, and make some good of it! Berahino gets the step on Jenkinson, and blasts an effort in on goal that nicks wickedly off Flamini, forcing Szczesny to change direction well to make the save!
(13’) It's Ramsey, brimming with confidence, who takes the set piece, but its a terrible hit, miles over the top.
(12’) Most definitely Arsenal have been the quicker side to settle into their rhythm. Giroud, after a smart turn, is brought down by Yacob, a decent 25 yards from goal. Freekick to come.
(10’) Mulumbu clatters Wilshere in the centre circle. Just a warning from Lee Mason at this early stage for the Congolese, who has racked up three cautions already this season. Occupational hazard.
(9’) Arsenal probe and pick at West Brom, but the Baggies are standing firm, with all 11 men well behind the halfway line. The move breaks down when an ambitious Giroud backheel fools his teammates and his own self.
(7’) Nearly a route through the centre for Jones, who goes all the way from right back to the edge of the penalty area, and is half a yard from intercepting Szczesny's clearance!
(6’) Straight from a failed West Brom corner, Arsenal break! Ozil effortlessly slips in Giroud, marginally onside, but the Frenchman, with only Wilshere to pick out in the box, ends up skying it.
(5’) Mulumbu not having the best of times to start here, he and Olsson get in each others way, almost allowing Ozil to break through in the confusion!
(3’) Arsenal have held the ball since Mulumbu's early fail, but have not made any advances into the opposition half. A nice atmosphere ringing around The Hawthorns as well.
(1’) West Brom kick us off and immediately waste the ball with a hopeful hack by Mulumbu to catch Szczesny off his line. No dice.
Arsene Wenger and Steve Clarke shake hands, the teams are in place, and our referee Lee Mason is ready to get us started!
West Brom meanwhile have finally found a decent vein of form, with two league wins in their last two games. One of those games, a 3-0 topping of Sunderland was the final nail in Paolo Di Canio's coffin, and the other, a 2-1 switch at Old Trafford, may possibly, potentially, maybe, end up being the first nail in David Moyes'. The Baggies are buzzing, no doubt!
Arsenal of course have been the most in form team in the country, winning ten games on the trot in all competitions, and shhhh...looking like they have a legit title challenge in store! One of those wins came against the Baggies last month in the Capital One Cup, a marathon 4-3 penalty shootout triumph after a trudging 1-1 draw during normal time.
Arsene Wenger also makes two changes to his side that handily defeated Napoli midweek, with Jenkinson and Wilshere replacing Sagna and Rosicky. Wilshere will play in his newfound home out wide, of course, and it looks like duties on the opposite flank will be split between Ozil and Ramsey, two of Arsenal's stars of the season.
Anichebe and Sinclair out, Berahino and Anelka in - the two changes for the hosts. The veteran French striker lines up against the club where he made his name, but only time will tell if Anichebe's abscence will be felt. Hardly the most technical player, but the ex-Everton man has been key at times for the Baggies this season with his brand of physicality and tenacity. A battering ram, if you will. Anelka is a different player at this stage of his career, rather dropping deep than running in behind.
ARSENAL: Szczesny; Jenkinson, Koscielny, Mertesacker, Gibbs; Arteta, Flamini, Ramsey, Wilshere, Ozil; Giroud. SUBS: Fabianski, Monreal, Vermaelen, Rosicky, Gnabry, Miyaichi, Bendtner.
WEST BROM: Myhill; Jones, McAuley, Olsson, Ridgewell; Yacob, Mulumbu, Amalfitano, Sessegnon; Berahino, Anelka. SUBS: Daniels, Popov, Morrison, Brunt, Lugano, Long, Rosenberg.

The Hawthorns is the venue, West Bromwich Albion vs Arsenal is the show. Greetings from me, Keeghann Sinanan, your designated scribe for another round of EPL action!

Thanks for joining me this afternoon. Until next time, goodbye!
A second half header from John Terry was enough to cancel out Gylfi Sigurdsson's first half header as both sides share the spoils at White Hart Lane. Jose Mourinho and Andre Villas-Boas share an embrace at the final whistle but I'd bet they won't see eye-to-eye on the Torres sending off.
FULL-TIME: Tottenham 1-1 Chelsea
(90’) The promise of a good chance is wasted by Chadli. He recieves the ball in midfield and goes for an ambitious shot from a long way out. He leans back and sends the ball into row Z. Perhaps the last chance for Tottenham.
(90’) There will be four minutes added on at the end of the match.
(90’) Defoe and Holtby exchange passes on the edge of the box before the Englishman's shot from outside the box is deflected for a corner. Petr Cech makes a commanding catch from the resulting set-piece.
(88’) CLOSE! Sigurdsson is a yard away from a spectacular second goal. After minutes of patient build-up the Icelandic midfielder elects to shoot on the half-volley just outside the box but he clips his effort just wide of of the post, with Cech rooted to the spot.
(86’) CHANCE! It's a great chance for Defoe to give Spurs a late lead. The substitute receives the ball inside the box and manages to turn but his shot is snatched at and well read by Cech. He knows he should have scored.
(85’) Chelsea have parks the proverbial bus in front of goal. It's all mans to deck as they look to see this out with ten men.
(83’) As a result of Torres' dismissal, Oscar has been sacrificed for the introduction of Azpilicueta. Tottenham have less than 10 minutes to win this against the 10 men of Chelsea.
--- 82’ Substitution Oscar is replaced with Azpilicueta. ---
--- 81’ Red card! Fernando Torres gets a second yellow card and is sent off! ---
(80’) RED CARD! Torres and Vertonghen both go in for a header with full commitment and after a slight delay Mike Dean sends off the Chelsea striker! The Spaniard slowly walks off the pitch and recieves a whisper in the ear from Mourinho.
--- 78’ Yellow card M. Dembélé receives a yellow card. ---
--- 77’ Substitution J. Defoe enters play, replacing Soldado. ---
(77’) GREAT SAVE! Torres sends Schurrle away with a fine through ball but the German is denied a Chelsea goal by a superb save from Lloris. The Frenchman dashed off his line to make himself big and make the stop. Good stuff from Torres too.
--- 75’ Yellow card M. Dawson goes into the referee's book. ---
(75’) Tottenham have stopped the Chelsea tide in the last couple of minutes and are trying to maintain possession. But Soldado and Sigurdsson, who were lively in the first period, are very quiet in this half so far.
(72’) Ramires sends Schurrle galloping into space on the left flank but the German is ajudged to be offside when the pass was made. Almost a great chance for the Blues.
--- 70’ Substitution C. Eriksen is replaced with L. Holtby. ---
(70’) This game has opened right up. Both sides have chances within seconds of each other. Tottenham's broke down because of a poor ball from Dembele and Oscar's weak cross allowed Vertonghen to snuff out Chelsea's counterattack.
--- 69’ Substitution E. Hazard is replaced with A. Schürrle. ---
(68’) CHANCE! Torres is found with a bit of space on the right-hand flank and he looks for Mata in the box but Dawson makes the intervention at the front post. Mata's cross from the resulting corner is poor. Chelsea are on top.
--- 65’ Assist Mata gave the assist. ---
--- 65’ Goal! GOAL! John Terry equalises for Chelsea with his first of the season! Juan Mata delivers a cross in from the deep free kick and finds the defender at the back post. Terry heads in low into the bottom corner leaving Lloris without a hope. ---
(65’) CONTROVERSY! Ramires is about to burst through on goal before Vertonghen clips him down. The Spurs defender is booked but he might have seen red had he recieved a yellow in the two earlier spats with Torres.
--- 64’ Yellow card J. Vertonghen is yellow-carded. ---
(63’) Chelsea twice look for Oscar with two diagonal balls from deep but they fail to execute either properly. Fustrated looks from David Luiz and then Jose Mourinho on the bench.
--- 62’ Substitution A. Townsend is replaced with N. Chadli. ---
(61’) There's a little bit of spice creeping into the derby game as Torres and Vertonghen again clash. The game is delayed as Mike Dean attempts to restore a bit of order.
(59’) Now Chelsea are looking alive in attack. Oscar squirms through Spurs' defence on the left before crossing for Torres. The reaches Mata via a deflection but he fluffs his shot on goal. Hazard then as a go himself which Lloris easily saves.
--- 58’ Yellow card B. Ivanović is yellow-carded. ---
(57’) CHELSEA GOAL DISALLOWED! Mata has the ball in the back of the net but it won't count. The Spaniard was in an offside position as he recieved the ball from Torres' flick on and slotted it in the back of the net.
(55’) Tottenham have a corner on the right which Eriksen hits too deep. Dembele picks up the pieces and then does well to hit the byline, outmuscling Ivanovic on his way, before crossing. Chelsea manage to clear.
(53’) CHANCE! Great stuff from Torres to swerve past two challenges inside the box. To his credit, Lloris does well to rush out and make the one-on-one finish hard for the Spaniard. Great keeping. Torres does look lively.
(52’) A bit of handbags between Torres and Vertonghen as the Spurs defender tumbles down following a slight nick on the heels. Torres gets booked much to his annoyance.
--- 51’ Yellow card Fernando Torres is yellow-carded. ---
(50’) Chelsea win a free kick in a deep position on the left. Mata delivers into the box but Dawson wins the header and Lloris is able to gather.
(49’) CHANCE! Terrific play from Fernando Torres on the right to get past Naughton at Vertonghen but his low cross is perhaps hit too firmly. Oscar can only send it wide with his outstrectched leg. Chelsea's best moment of the game.
(48’) By the looks it, Eden Hazard has gone into the role behind Fernando Torres with Oscar on the left and Mata on the right. I imagine they'll be interchanging as we go on. Tentative start to the second half from both sides.
--- 46’ Substitution Mata enters the game and replaces J. Obi Mikel. ---
(46’) Tottenham take the kick-off and we are underway for the second half!
Juan Mata replaces John Obi Mikel at half-time.
Jose Mourinho does have the likes of Andre Schurrle, Samuel Eto'o and, heaven forbid, Juan Mata on the bench to call on in the second half. I don't think Spurs are going to settle on the a 1-0 lead though, so the Portuguese will be wary. Tottenham go top of the league if they hold on for the three points.
What a first half for Andre Villas-Boas and his Tottenham side. They've blown away Chelsea in this first half and are more than value for their one-goal lead. Gylfi Sigurdsson's third goal in three games is the difference at the break. Jose Mourinho has plenty to do before the second half begins...
HALF-TIME: Tottenham 1-0 Chelsea
--- 45’ +2 Yellow card C. Eriksen receives a yellow card. ---
(45’) Ramires delivers a deep cross from deep, after Chelsea's intial free kick is dealt with, but John Terry can't direct his header on goal after getting up well to meet it.
(45’) There will be two minuted added on at the end of the first half.
(45’) OFF THE POST! Spurs should have doubled their lead! Townsend scares the Chelsea defenders into backing right back into their box. He advances forward before sliding a smart pass into the path of the oncoming Paulinho. The Brazilian attempts a near-post finish but only succeeds in hitting the frame of the goal!
--- 43’ Yellow card A. Townsend is yellow-carded. ---
(43’) CHANCE! Chelsea win a free kick as Townsend is punished for a dive. They send a diagonal into the box, Torres competes for the header with Vertonghen and manages to direct it to Oscar. The midfielder can only shoot directly at Lloris.
(42’) Townsend comes flying in from the right flank and nudges the ball to Paulinho. The Brazilian dinks a ball through to Soldado but the Spanish hit man is a yard offside.
(40’) CLOSE! Chelsea swing a corner in from the left via Frank Lampard and Hugo Lloris comes flying out of his goal to make a punch at the edge of his box. Moments later Hazard fires a shot in from the edge of the box which deflects wide for a corner.
(37’) Great stuff from Spurs on the counterattack. Once again Eriksen dazzles White Hart Lane with his footwork, Sigurdsson cutely steals the ball of his foot and takes it into the opposite direction before Paulinho centres a cross for Soldado. Chelsea get the ball clear but they know Spurs are carving them up at will.
(34’) Finally Chelsea get a hold of the ball in the Spurs half with some possession. Frank Lampard tries to thread a pass into Hazard in the box but Kyle Walker does brilliantly to anticipate and intercept.
(32’) Ivanovic gets forward from right back and tries to cross from the byline but Vertonghen does well to get ahead of Torres and make a clearing header. Solado tries to hold the ball up for Spurs and wins a free kick from a clumsy challenge from David Luiz.
(30’) Kyle Naughton eventually has a right-footed shot from range at the end of that Spurs attack but it's hit rather tamely and Cech easily gathers.
(29’) Demebele appears to be moving freely enough now as Spurs knock the ball about under little pressure from Chelsea. Walker tries to cross from the right but Cole does well to close him down. Spurs look dangerous.
(27’) That opener was Gylfi Sigurdsson's third goal in three Premier League appearances. The Icelandic midfielder is in top form and looks to have forged a good understanding with Eriksen.
(25’) Eden Hazard goes in hard, but fair, on Moussa Dembele. Chelsea continue on the attack but Spurs knock the ball out when they lose their forward momentum. Time for a breather after a couple of breathless minutes.
(23’) CHANCE! Spurs nearly double their lead through Paulinho. Roberto Soldado flashes a low ball across the box that looks certain to reach Paulinho in the box but Ivanovic comes in to make a vital intervention.
(21’) Let me remind you that Tottenham have only conceded one goal in their last nine competitive fixtures. Could this be another defeat for Mourinho's men?
--- 19’ Assist Assist by Soldado. ---
--- 19’ Goal! Goal to Tottenham Hotspur, scored by G. Sigurdsson! ---
(19’) GOAL! Gylfi Sigurdsson gives Spurs the lead. It's a well worked goal from the hosts, Eriksen beats a couple of players on the left before finding Soldado in the box. The Spanish striker sees Sigurdsson's run and cleverly lays the ball into his path with a first time touch. A fine finish too!
(18’) Torres feels hard done by as he goes down on the edge of the box but nothing is given. Chelsea haven't really got going yet.
(15’) Luiz does well to read the danger as Soldado wins the ball on the right and finds Eriksen. Tottenham are definitely the team on the ascendancy.
(12’) Eriksen is seeing plenty of the ball in these early stages, he finds Sigurdsson, who is then brought down. The Dane takes the set-piece but his ball into the box is headed harmlessly wide by Vertonghen.
(9’) Eden Hazard goes stays down following a challenge with Kyle Walker. The Belgian reveals a hole in his sock as he protests with the referee but he looks fine to continue.
(7’) Lampard again looks for a long ball for one of his midfield runners. This time Eden Hazard beats the offside trap but the ball just runs a little long for him and he is unable to bring it under his spell.
(5’) Eriksen tries to feed Soldado with a clever ball through the middle of the Chelsea defence but Terry is alert to the danger and does well to snuff out the chance. Real signs of intent from Eriksen and Spurs early on.
(3’) Now Tottenham make a forray into the final third for the first time. Christian Eriksen has a chance to deliver from a corner but the Dane's cross is easily claimed by a confident Cech.
(2’) Chelsea launch the first attack of the game as Frank Lampard looks for Ramires' forward run with a lofted pass. The Brazilian is a little too eager and strays offside with his movement.
(1’) Chelsea take the kick-off and we are underway at  White Hart Lane!
Chelsea: Cech; Ivanovic, D Luiz, Terry, Cole; Mikel, Lampard; Ramires, Oscar, Hazard; Torres. Subs: Schwarzer, Azpilicueta, Cahill, Essien, Mata, Schurrle, Eto'o.
Tottenham: Lloris; Walker, Dawson, Vertonghen, Naughton; Paulinho, Dembele; Townsend, Eriksen, Sigurdsson; Soldado. Subs: Friedel, Chirches, Lamela, Holtby, Chadli, Sandro, Defoe.

A fantastic result for Aston Villa - and a horrible one for City, who are yet to win an away match. Phew, what a game! This is why we love football and this is why we love the Premier League.
City dominated, took the lead twice and hardly allowed their opponents any room to breathe. Yet, somehow, Villa scored three brilliant counterattacking goals - and the rest was history.
Words can barely describe what has just happened at Villa Park as the home side steal three valuable points against supposed title contenders Manchester City.
THEY THINK IT'S ALL OVER AND IT IS! Amazing win for Aston Villa!
(90’) Kolarov heads wide at the near post!! Is that as close as City can get?
(90’) Ninety seconds remain!
(90’) Luna sends a low cross into the area and Nastasic is forced to clear! The home side are really stepping into their own here.
(90’) Libor Kozak's first telling contribution of the day is to win a free kick against Toure to use up even more time!
(90’) There will be FIVE minutes of added time!
(90’) Into injury time we go...
(89’) It is desperate, heroic defending and, now, Villa have a free kick in their own half that will no doubt allow them to slow things down and use up some valuable time.
(88’) City push forward but the advances of Toure, Kolarov and Jovetic are to no avail as the home defence smash anything in their path clear of danger.
(87’) The visitors look no closer to drawing level as Fernandinho concedes a free kick in the middle of the park.
(86’) Funny old game... City have absolutely dominated this afternoon's game. Yet they have fallen victim to three classic counterattacking goals. Is time running out for them here?
(85’) It is the away side's turn to look disconsolate. Their body language is indicative of a beaten team.
(84’) Kolarov attempts to bypass Bacuna on the left-hand side but ends up running the ball out for a goal kick.
(83’) Seven minutes left and the clock is ticking here. Suddenly, the prospect of ending today at the top of the table looks impossible for the visitors. What is it with Pellegrini and away games?
(81’) Their first real late push sees them win a throw-in, from which Toure sets up Stevan Jovetic - but the ex-Fiorentina man's shot is blocked by Villa hero Vlaar. An unconvincing finish but a brave challenge.
(80’) Just 10 minutes left here but, in truth, City look shellshocked. Even if they grab an equaliser, it will hardly compensate for letting in three poor goals. Realistically, the visitors need two here. But is there enough time? And do they have enough firepower?
--- 79’ Substitution A. Weimann is done for the day. J. Bowery is his replacement. ---
(78’) The fact that Guzan got an assist for that Weimann goal tells you everything you need to know about Villa and their lightning quick approach. What a day for the Midlands: West Brom lead Manchester United and Villa lead here. Can they hold out until full-time?
(77’) Not for the first time this season, Pellegrini's side have been found wanting away from home. And not for the first time, they are 3-2 down away from home.
--- 75’ Assist B. Guzan gave the assist. ---
--- 75’ Goal! GOAL!! Weimann!! Unbelievable scenes as Villa complete a stunning turnaround. It is, somehow, 3-2 to the home side but you have to wonder how! What a quick move as Weimann catches Matija Nastasic out and pokes home to give the hosts the lead. They have hardly been competitive all game and yet they lead. Football, eh? ---
--- 74’ Substitution E. Džeko is done for the day. S. Jovetić is his replacement. ---
--- 73’ Goal! GOALLLL!!! Bacuna! Talk about making the most of what they have had: Leandro Bacuna, with a free kick from outside the area, has been more accurate with one chance than City have with more than ten! What a strike, what a goal. Villa, amazingly, back on level terms! ---
(71’) The set-piece is dealt with, though, and Villa are able to break, winning a free kick nine yards outside the City penalty area. They have not had many opportunities but they have made the most of the few they have had...
(70’) The visitors are really pushing for a third here as Kolarov advances into the area and forces a corner.
(69’) Offside! Villa can pause for breath as a City attack is halted abruptly by the linesman's flag.
(68’) The introduction of Jesus Navas makes an instant impact as the Spaniard sends a sublime through ball to Negredo, although the striker is unable to convert.
(67’) Rare chance for Villa! It comes from a set-piece as a reasonably threatening delivery is sent into the box and Vlaar is able to connect with it on the volley. However, the end result is a tame effort that Hart is perfectly able to deal with.
--- 66’ Substitution S. Nasri is replaced with Jesús Navas. ---
(66’) Toure has been outstanding once again for the away side this afternoon. City really did complete one of the Premier League's best ever signings when they recruited the Ivorian from Barcelona.
(65’) Dzeko! Defended well! The Bosnian was seconds away from pulling the trigger for what surely would have been 3-1 but Bacuna came from nowhere to heroically keep his side in the contest. A third is looking likely, though..
(64’) Encouraging energy from Weimann and Delph comes to nothing as Vincent Kompany effortlessly deals with the danger.
(63’) No - not for now, at least, as the City defence clear calmly.
(62’) A rare venture forward from Villa now. Can the home side grab another unexpected equaliser?
(61’) Despite Pellegrini's summer spending, it is currently City's old guard that are flying the flag for their side. The likes of Dzeko, Nasri, Toure, Zabaleta, Milner and Kolarov have been heavily influential today. Fernandinho and Negredo have failed to make a similar impact, however.
--- 60’ Yellow card Believe it or not, this might be City's first away win of the season. They now have a free kick on the edge of the area after a clumsy challenge from Sylla. ---
(60’) Nasri whips the ball in at pace but an unmarked Dzeko cannot convert his second of the game as his header goes out for a goal kick.
(57’) SAVE! Guzan saves from Negredo as the away side look to close the game out!
--- 56’ Assist The assist came from S. Nasri. ---
--- 56’ Goal! GOAL! Dzeko! City's lead is restored - and perhaps this is the true indication of how Pellegrini's men will react. How unlucky for the hosts, who only just began to really believe in themselves. After typically fluent build-up play, it was an easy finish for Dzeko. 2-1. ---
(55’) Joe Hart, who has not had much to do today, collects the ball with relief as Clark fails to keep control of the ball due to the pace at which it came into his possession.
--- 54’ Yellow card If you were wondering how the visitors would react, Nasri has provided a hint: petulantly. The Frenchman is booked for kicking out at Bacuna and, now, Villa have a corner.. ---
(52’) City have cause to feel aggrieved, however, as replays suggest that El Ahmadi may have been offside when he received the ball from a cross into the area. Intriguing.
--- 51’ Assist Assist by L. Bacuna. ---
--- 51’ Goal! GOAL! El Ahmadi! Where on earth did that come from!? As City's possession figures almost went beyond the 70 per cent mark, Villa launched a rare move into the away penalty area and, suddenly, El Ahmadi found himself with the ball in the box and thumped a low finish into the back of the net! Game on? ---
(50’) More danger signs for the hosts now as a clever through ball almost releases three different players for City! The pass is overhit, though, and slips into Villa's grasp.
(49’) There is big incentive for a City win this afternoon, with three points meaning Pellegrini's side will leapfrog Tottenham on goal difference and move to the top of the Premier League.
(48’) This has been a terrible restart from the home side. Toure's strike on the stroke of half-time remains the difference between the two teams but if Villa carry on in similar fashion, that gap looks set to widen.
(47’) CHANCE! Sylla plays a shocking backpass to Guzan, almost gifting the ball to Negredo with the goal at his mercy! Luckily for the hosts, the American is able to clear - but only just.
(46’) Manchester City kick us off for the second half! There have been no changes for either side at the break.
The second half will be upon us shortly.
Is there any way back for Villa? Or has Toure simply opened the floodgates for the visitors? Stay with us to find out!
The visitors may have been worried by the profligacy of their forwards but, now that they have the lead, their only concern will be killing the game off. Villa have almost been non-existent from an attacking perspective but one can sympathise with Lambert and the injury crisis he is currently having to cope with.
Manchester City had been piling the pressure on Aston Villa all half but Paul Lambert's men had defended admirably for 44 minutes or so. But in stepped Yaya Toure and their defence was no more.
HALF-TIME! And that's that! Pellegrini's side just about achieve what they had been pursuing all half and go into the break a goal to the good.
--- 45’ Goal! GOAL! Toure! A simple finish from the Ivorian - but he will not care. Initially, the powerful midfielder surged forward and unleashed a strike from distance that was deflected for a corner. From that resultant set-piece, Toure tapped home from seven yards. Villa's resistance is broken. ---
(42’) Yet still no goals for either side, which will suit Lambert a lot more than it will his opposite number.
(41’) But Pellegrini's men get the ball back and pile forward once again, with Nathan Baker being forced to clear for yet another corner - and then once again. That is an astonishing seven corner kicks for Manchester City now.
(40’) Nasri's ball is cleared by Luna, however, before Andi Weimann attempts to break for the home side.
(39’) Free kick to City in a dangerous position now, with several blue shirts forward.
(38’) Ron Vlaar exemplifies the Villa solidity with a superb block against Milner's pass, before Ciaran Clark clears a great Kolarov ball over the bar for a corner. Pressure rising once again from the visitors, although the hosts look more than equal to it.
(36’) The City pressure has died down now as the home defence looks more certain and authoritative in the face of attacking trickery from the likes of Toure, Nasri and Zabaleta.
(34’) EMBARRASSING! Fernandinho tries to thread a pass through to Milner but it rolls off for a goal kick. Hardy Samba Soccer from the Brazilian.
(33’) Lambert moves to the edge of his technical area to bark some orders to his players. At 0-0, it is so far, so good for the home side. But a goal could change things dramatically.
(31’) Bacuna weathers the storm! The Dutch winger is able to advance forward and have a shot at goal. It is not a good strike - but Villa will be pleased to force a pause for breath for their defenders nonetheless.
(29’) Are Pellegrini's men going to open their account any time soon?
(28’) CHANCE! Once again, the visitors knock on the door as Milner and Toure combine to feed Zabaleta in the area, before the Argentina plays a sumptuous ball into Negredo. The Villa defence are just able to intercept, however, and clear the danger.
(27’) Either way, it is all City at the minute...
(26’) DENIED! Pablo Zabaleta surges into the Villa penalty area and is brought down by Luna! But the referee waves away City's penalty appeals.
(24’) POOR EFFORT! A promising attack for the visitors ends with Dzeko skying a hopeless shot several rows into the stands. Anti-climactic.
(23’) The visitors bring every one of their players back to defend this one - but they are not needed as Karim El Ahmadi's 30-yard free kick sails over the bar.
(22’) Villa now have a free kick in a dangerous position!
(21’) Kolarov is on hand to surge down the left-hand side for the away team once more and Bacuna has no option but to clear for City's third corner of the day. (20’) Possession alone does not win football matches but, if it did, the visitors would have this one in the bag already. Nevertheless, the figures will suit Villa's style, as well. 0-0 20 minutes in here.
(18’) Milner unleashes a shot from distance from the ensuing corner but it is blocked and City have to backtrack somewhat. Until, that is, a strike from Dzeko that just skims the crossbar.
(17’) City when yet another corner after intricate work from Fernandinho and Dzeko, although the set-piece itself could have quite easily been avoided.
(16’) Villa's counterattacking nature helps ensure a speedy pace to the game as well, however, despite the absence of star striker Christian Benteke, who is out injured for a month.
(15’) The away side are doing very well to put the hosts under pressure here, with every loose ball and mishit pass being pounced on with the utmost speed.
(14’) From the resultant set-piece, Negredo heads just over!
(13’) Kolarov and Milner now combine to win City a corner, as a sense of foreboding sweeps across Villa Park. Can the visitors break the deadlock?
(11’) End-to-end football here as the hosts almost counterattack from the corner that was initiated from a City counterattack...
(10’) JUST WIDE! But not for Villa. What a counterattack from the visitors, who broke with Toure and Nasri once again and it was the Frenchman who ended up taking a shot at goal, only for a deflection to take it out for a corner.
(9’) First corner of the game! It is won by the home side - and Luna specifically, who has recovered from his earlier injury worry.
(7’) Edin Dzeko comes close to troubling Villa stopper Brad Guzan as his short-range finish prompts a save from the American. The home fans are in good voice at the moment, however, although City have gradually taken control of possession.
(5’) Samir Nasri and Yaya Toure now exchange short passes, before Kolarov once again gets involved. However, Nasri is then played through but the Frenchman is given offside.
(4’) Luna now finds himself down injured, although it is unclear how bad the problem is. An even start so far.
(3’) Villa attack down the left after contributions from Antonio Luna and Yacouba Sylla but City defend the danger well and counter with a move of their own down the left-hand side, with Aleksander Kolarov breaking and whipping a cross into the box. (2’) After a few opening exchanges, it is the home side who are retaining the majority of possession - though there has not been anything of note quite yet.
(1’) We're off at Villa Park!

FT: Fulham 1-2 Cardiff. Jordan Mutch's superb stoppage-time strike gives Malky Mackay's side a first win on the road this season. The Bluebirds were good value for the victory and opened the scoring in the first half courtesy of Steven Caulker's header. Fulham were simply second-best although Bryan Ruiz produced a moment of genius to level the scores on the stroke of half-time. Martin Jol's side miserable home form continues as they remain in the relegation zone.
Boos ring out around Craven Cottage as the referee blows the final whistle! Cardiff have their first ever Premier League away win.
--- 90’ +2 Goal! CARDIFF TAKE THE LEAD AND WHAT A GOAL IT IS! Richardson fails to deal with Marshall's long ball and Mutch seizes onto the ball and sends a superb swerving left-footed shot into the top left-hand corner from the right corner of the box. The three points look to be heading back to Wales! ---
(90’) WHAT A CHANCE FOR FULHAM! Karagounis produces a brilliant pass to send Richardson clear down the left and this time the left-back produces a fantastic low cross which skids across the face of goal, but there is no white shirt to meet it. All it needed was a touch.
(88’) Cardiff win a free kick around 35 yards out and Bellamy opts to go for goal, blazing the ball high over the crossbar. The way Whittingham has been playing, I'm surprised he didn't cross that into the box.
--- 86’ Substitution Martin Jol makes a final roll of the dice as he throws on Adel Taarabt for Darren Bent. Will it prove to be another inspired substitution? ---
(85’) Cardiff attack down the other end but Whittingham cannot quite divert Bellamy's reverse pass the right side of the post. Will we see a late winner?
(84’) WHAT A CHANCE FOR FULHAM! Kasami embarks on a bamboozling run and he takes on several defenders before his shot is blocked bravely by Caulker. The rebound falls kindly for the Macedonian but his shot lacks conviction and is saved by Marshall.
(83’) Fulham work the ball out to the left smartly but once again Richardson overhits his cross. The London side have really lacked creativity in wide areas today.
--- 81’ Substitution Peter Odemwingie cannot add to his goal in midweek as he is hauled off for Craig Bellamy. The Welshman has not scored a league goal in this calendar year. It wouldn't be a bad time to end that run. ---
(80’) Kieran Richardson has been really poor for Fulham today and his cross from the left sums up his performance as it flies straight out of play. Craig Bellamy readies himself on the touchline.
(79’) Andrew Taylor produces a strong run from left-back but his cross is just behind Mutch who volleys the ball over the crossbar. Cardiff are not giving up hope of a first Premier League away win just yet.
(77’) Fulham have Cardiff pegged back into their own half here but it is really sloppy passing from the Cottagers. Darren Bent has hardly had a sniff of Marshall's goal.
(75’) The Fulham crowd are starting to get behind their side as they sense the chance of what has to be called an undeserved winner. Can they find a late goal to lift them out of the relegation zone?
--- 72’ Substitution Malky Mackay opts to make his second change as Nicky Maynard replaces Fraizer Campbell. Can he give the Bluebirds an extra attacking dimension up front? ---
(72’) Fulham launch a counter attack but Bent plays a pass just behind Ruiz and the move breaks down.
(71’) Peter Whittingham has been superb for Cardiff today but he can only strike his free kick straight into the wall before Gunnarsson's shot is well blocked.
(69’) However, Fulham have certainly improved in this second half and Ruiz tees the ball up for Kasami on the edge of the box, only to watch the Macedonian's weak effort comfortably saved by Marshall.
(67’) Hangeland has looked constantly shaky on his 200th Premier League appearance and he nearly gets robbed of possession by Campbell in a dangerous area. Cardiff are certainly going to get more chances in this one.
--- 65’ Yellow card Dimitar Berbatov is the first Fulham player to be booked after a mistimed challenge on Theophile-Catherine. It's been a rather frustrating afternoon for the Bulgarian so far. ---
(62’) FULHAM GO CLOSE! Riether produces a rare burst to get forward from right-back and his cross finds Berbatov who heads against the outside of the post from a narrow angle.
(61’) Make that 16. Whittingham receives the ball on the edge of the box but he cannot replicate Ruiz's effort as he curls a shot over the bar.
(60’) Fulham have hardly tested Marshall in the Cardiff goal and Kasami's shot from distance flashes narrowly wide. The statistics show that Cardiff have had 15 shots on goal in comparison to Fulham's four.
(58’) WHAT A CHANCE FOR CARDIFF! Mutch makes an instant impact when his teasing low cross finds Campbell in the box, but the striker can only poke the ball over the top from close range. Will Mackay's team live to rue all these missed opportunites?
--- 56’ Substitution Cardiff make their first change of the game and it is a surprising one as Kim is replaced by Jordan Mutch. ---
(54’) Cardiff win a free kick in a promising area but this time Whittingham's delivery is too close to Stockdale and the Fulham goalkeeper comfortably claims.
(52’) Theophile-Catherine has produced some good quality play down the right and his fizzed cross is met on the volley by Whittingham but bobbles towards the corner flag.
(50’) Cardiff have started the second half well and Stockdale needs to be alert to prevent Campbell from heading in Turner's flick-on. The Bluebirds centre-back has been immense in the air today.
(48’) Cardiff continue to look a threat from set-pieces and Medel shovels a shot over the bar after Fulham failed to clear their lines from a corner.
(46’) The referee blows his whistle and Cardiff get the second half underway. I'm sure Martin Jol has had some stern words with his players at the break whilst Malky Mackay will be asking his team for more of the same.

HT: Fulham 1-1 Cardiff. Bryan Ruiz's fantastic strike on the stroke of half-time ensures the two low-lying sides are level at the break. In truth, it has been all Cardiff and they took the lead through Steven Caulker's first goal for the club. The Welsh side have dominated the midfield battle and Malky Mackay must be wondering how his side are not in front.
(45’) Cardiff look to respond immediately with Odemwingie, who wriggles into the box before his shot is well blocked.
--- 45’ Assist The assist came from S. Riether. ---
--- 45’ Goal! WHAT A STRIKE FROM BRYAN RUIZ! It's an inspired substitution from Martin Jol as the Costa Rican receives the ball on the edge of the box before bending a wonderful shot into the top corner, with Marshall stranded. Fulham do not deserve to be level, but that is a goal of the highest quality. ---
(44’) It really has been all Cardiff this half but it seems they will only have one goal to show for their efforts at the break as Campbell heads Theophile-Catherine's cross over the bar.
(43’) This time the corner is headed out to the edge of the box but Medel can only slice his shot well high and wide of the target.
(42’) Fulham continue to look shaky at the back and Cardiff win another corner when Riether nervously clears the ball behind.
--- 41’ Substitution Second substitution for Fulham as Bryan Ruiz replaces Alexander Kacaniklic. The Costa Rican marches onto the field, dishing out instructions to a number of teammates. ---
(40’) Kim has looked lively in this first half but he cannot deceive Stockdale with his cheeky chip as it goes narrowly over the crossbar.
(39’) It seems that Martin Jol will not even wait until half-time to make the changes. Bryan Ruiz is stripped and ready to go on the touchline. Fulham have been woeful in this first half.
(37’) Cardiff threaten again when Theophile-Catherine stretches his legs down the right and his cross is glanced wide of the target by the head of Gunnarsson.
(36’) FULHAM FINALLY DEFEND WELL FROM A CORNER! Whittingham whips the ball into the box and Stockdale is given good protection from his back four to pluck the ball out of the air.
(36’) Cardiff appeal for a handball when Taylor is convinced that his cross hits the hand of Riether. The referee is not interested however and points for a corner.
(35’) Cardiff are well on top here and they are dominating the midfield battle. Bent and Berbatov have been mere spectators up front for Fulham.
(34’) Fulham just cannot cope with Whittingham's corners! This time, Caulker knocks the ball down for Campbell who acrobatically strikes the ball over the top. Martin Jol does not look a happy man.
--- 32’ Yellow card Theopile-Catherine is the first player to be booked as he cynically brings down Kasami to prevent a Fulham counter attack. ---
(31’) Moments after Caulker has a goal ruled out for a foul from a corner, Fulham go close as Karagounis' fizzing shot is well pushed around the post by Marshall.
(29’) Brede Hangeland is certainly not playing well on his 200th Premier League appearance and he allows Campbell to nip in behind him but his blushes are spared by Stockdale.

(26’) Kim has produced some neat touches for Cardiff and he is fouled by Kasami. The Fulham players are looking a little frustrated here.
(24’) Fulham just do not look comfortable at the back and Turner flicks a header from Whittingham's cross narrowly wide.

(21’) BETTER FROM FULHAM! Kacaniklic's run causes problems down the left but his cross is just too high for Berbatov. The ball falls to Richardson on the edge of the box but he slices over the bar.

(16’) OFF THE LINE! Whittingham's crosses are causing all sorts of problems and Hangeland produces a brilliant header to deny Cardiff a second goal before Kasami clears Turner's effort off the line! Fulham are at sixes and sevens at the back.
(14’) Cardiff have suddenly sprung into life and Whittingham's dangerous cross to the back post is hooked behind by Richardson for another corner. Can Fulham defend this one better?
--- 12’ Assist P. Whittingham gave the assist. ---

(11’) Odemwingie embarks on a mazy dribble before slipping the ball through for Kim. However, he cannot shift the ball out from his feet and Fulham survive.

(3’) Speaking of the tall Norwegian, he plays a long ball into the right channel for Bent to chase but there is nobody in the middle to meet his low cross.
(2’) Incidentally, Brede Hangeland is making his 200th Premier League appearance for Fulham today. What a servant he has been in the heart of the Cottagers' defence.

Cardiff will be boosted by the fact that Fulham have only managed to take one point from their last six home Premier League matches and only one side (Stoke City) have failed to score in the last 17 at Craven Cottage.
As for Cardiff, they have coped reasonably well on their long-awaited return to the top flight and Malky Mackay's side pulled off one of the upsets of the season when they defeated Manchester City 3-2. However, that has proved to be their only league victory so far, and they lie just above the relegation zone on five points.
Things have not gone quite as planned so far this season for Martin Jol. Fulham have only picked up four points from their opening five games with their solitary win coming against bottom side Sunderland. They have only managed to score three league goals in that time but their 2-1 Capital One Cup victory over Everton in midweek, with Dimitar Berbatov and Darren Bent both on the scoresheet, suggests that their season may be about to turn.
A big game towards the bottom of the Premier League today as 18th place Fulham host 16th place Cardiff City at Craven Cottage. It really is a tale of two sides who have come so far over the past two decades and the fact that the last meeting between them came in the fourth tier during the 1996-97 season is testament to their success.

For a game with so many chances we have been slightly short changed with only one goal. I have been Hayden Gribble and you have yourselves a great weekend!
Sam Allardyce throws his gum to the floor as he shakes hands with a victorious Steve Bruce. (90’) There will be FOUR minutes of added time.

(88’) A collective sigh of relief surrounds the KC stadium as the Tigers win a goal kick. They are nearly there...

(84’) CHANCE! Vaz Te sees his free-kick from 20-yards fly close to Jaaskelainen's goal but it goes over. It's all West Ham at the moment.
