(37’) A sensational strike from Rangel! The ball falls to the right back on the edge of the area from a corner and the Spaniard strikes goalwards on the volley. Speroni dives well to his right, tipping behind for a corner - that would have been some goal!
(36’) Guedioura is the man who has a strike from the free kick but there's nothing doing as the midfielder, prone to strikes from distance, fails to really catch the effort right.
(35’) Chico gives away another free kick in a dangerous position, this time fouling Jerome. Jedinak looks primed to take control of this free kick.
(34’) Swansea's stranglehold over the game resumes as they retain possession with consummate ease in their own half. They'll be keen to turn their dominance into a greater deficit, however - anything can happen at 1-0.
(32’) Palace finally have an opportunity to pack the Swansea box as more good work from Puncheon earns the home side a corner. The same man looks to whip it in but Michu heads clear.
(31’) Davies whips the ensuing corner in and it's Michu, once again, who is causing the problems in the Palace area as his header flies over the crossbar.
(30’) Michu strikes just over! Routledge does excellently again, this time down the left, before feeding the Spaniard on the edge of the area. The striker's effort is deflected by Gabbidon, whistling just over the bar.
(29’) Palace continue to struggle as the Swans are, in typical fashion, asserting themselves on the game impressively here. They're controlling possession and Palace are barely getting a look-in.
--- 28’ Yellow card D. Moxey is cautioned by the referee. ---
(27’) That's a strong challenge from Moxey on Routledge and, perhaps correctly, he is booked. That was late and rash - the left back hasn't enjoyed the first half thus far, he's struggled to cope with Swansea's threat down the right.
(25’) Swansea attack again, putting together a nice move down the right wing. It ends up with Rangel but the right back can't find a man in the middle, overcooking the cross a touch, allowing Palace to come forward with the ball.
(24’) Michu has another opportunity but, surprisingly, the goalscorer elects not to shoot! Routledge does well down the right and finds the Spaniard in the box but, instead of striking at goal, Michu flicks the ball on, attempting to find Vazquez but failing - an odd choice there.
(23’) Swansea were lucky there! Bannan clips a free kick into the box from deep and Vorm comes and flaps at it. The goalkeeper was completely unconvincing there - he'll be grateful it fell to a Swansea defender.
(22’) Vazquez, quiet thus far, is called offside as the Swansea debutant attempts to steal in behind the Palace defence. He's worked hard but he's had little to show for his efforts, despite the away side's strong start.
(21’) Puncheon is definitely the focal point of Palace's attacks at the moment; the former Southampton man is at the centre of the action again as he feeds Bannan. As with a few minutes earlier, the midfielder can't find a man as his attempted through ball is cut out by Rangel.
(20’) And it is Puncheon who strikes at goal from the free kick! The wall does it job though as Davies blocks the effort.
(19’) Palace have a free kick in a dangerous area here after Chamakh is fouled on the edge of the box by Chico. Excellent play from Puncheon, once again, to feed the frontman there.
(18’) Puncheon does really well the middle to turn away from Cana before feeding it to Bannan. The debutant is dispossessed though and the chance comes to nothing.
(17’) Holloway is, apparently, calling for a change in formation as he looks to switch from their original 4-4-2/4-3-3 to a 4-2-3-1 as they appear intent on matching Swansea's formation; whatever the tactical intricacies, it's clear to see that the Palace manager is unhappy with the opening 17 minutes here at Selhurst Park.
(15’) The game's definitely calmed down a tad since that ferociously-paced opening; both sides appear content on sitting back a bit now, perhaps understandable given both Swansea's dominance and Crystal Palace's susceptibility at the back.
(14’) The home side finally put together a nice move as a string of passes almost results in an opportunity; Jerome fed in Mariappa down the right wing but his cross finds no-one and it's a Swansea goal kick.
(13’) Palace almost have a chance to capitalise on some poor defending by Williams but Chamakh misplaces his pass as, once again, the move breaks down.
(12’) Crystal Palace attempt to gather some momentum with some passing in Swansea's half but they can't quite get it right and moves continue to break down.
(10’) Answer to that question: no. Shelvey makes a complete and utter hash of the free kick - the former Liverpool man drives the ball in to the box, albeit at about 15 feet too high for anyone to make any contact. A truly curious effort at a delivery from a man that's had a mixed week.
(9’) The referee gives a controversial free kick against Palace centre-back Delaney on the right wing. He went in strongly on Dyer but there was nothing wrong with that - the Swans have a free kick in a dangerous position now, can they make it two?
(8’) Angel Rangel is clearly feeling some sympathy for the home side as he plays an incredibly lax pass out of play down the right wing. That was fairly horrific, more in keeping with Palace's start than Swansea's.
(7’) Crystal Palace, I think it's fair to say, have started abysmally here; Swansea have managed an early goal, could have had another and are in complete control of the game as it stands. A nightmare start for Holloway's men.
(6’) Almost another goal! Shelvey whips in the corner and Chico strikes goalwards. The centre back can only strike against the post, however, and the ball is deflected behind for another corner. Can Palace survive this early pressure?
(5’) A truly torrid start for Crystal Palace continues as Gabbidon gives away a corner through a poor piece of miscontrol.
--- 2’ Assist W. Routledge gave the assist. ---
--- 2’ Goal! GOAL! Just 80 seconds gone and Michu has opened the scoring! It was a nice move from the away side as the goalscorer started the move, linking well with Shelvey and Routledge in the final third. The former provided the ball through to Michu and he duly complied, striking in off the bar and Swansea are already 1-0 up! ---
(2’) Swansea appeal, albeit fairly half-heartedly, for a penalty after Dyer's cross is blocked by Jedinak. Nothing in that really but a promising start for the Swans.
(1’) And we're underway! Crystal Palace kick off proceedings at Selhurst Park as they go in search of a win that would take them out of the relegation zone.
A minute's applause is taking place before kick-off for Peter Morley, Crystal Palace's former club president, who sadly passed away this week.
Both teams are in the tunnel now as we eagerly await the kick-off at Selhurst Park.
Swansea, meanwhile, and perhaps as expected, make a variety of changes from their heroic 3-0 win against Valencia as Jordi Amat, Dwight Tiendalli, Jonathan de Guzman, Alejandro Pozuelo and Wilfried Bony all make way, as Ashley Williams, Ben Davies, Jonjo Shelvey, Wayne Routledge and debutant Alvara Vazquez all come in to the starting eleven.
Crystal Palace make two changes from the side that lost 2-0 to Manchester United last Saturday as Adlene Guedioura comes in for the suspended Kagisho Dikgacoi, while Barry Bannan and Cameron Jerome also displace Loris Campana and Dwight Gayle from the starting eleven.
Swansea: Vorm; Rangel, Chico, Williams, Davies; Canas, Shelvey, Dyer, Routledge, Michu, Vazquez. Subs: Tremmel, Amat, Britton, De Guzman, Pozuelo, Tiendelli, Bony.
Crystal Palace: Speroni; Mariappa, Gabbidon, Delaney, Moxey; Jedinak, Guedioura, Bannan; Puncheon, Jerome, Chamakh. Subs: Alexander, O'Keefe, Campana, Kebe, Thomas, Gayle, Phillips.
And here come the team line-ups...
The two sides facing one another today come into this game off the back of considerably different weeks; the away side enjoyed arguably their greatest ever night in Europe as they romped to a 3-0 win away to Valencia, while Crystal Palace sit just two points off the bottom of the table after their 2-0 defeat at home to Manchester United last Saturday. Gary Holloway and his men will be hoping that Swansea's hectic schedule will play to their favour as three points could see them move into 12th in the table – a win that would suddenly change the complexion of their start to the season. Michael Laudrup, meanwhile, will be looking to prove that the Swans can compete on both a European and domestic basis today – a loss today would surely invoke some worry amongst the fans with regards to the depth of their squad. With so much to play for, this game could be a cracker!

FULL TIME - Cardiff 0-1 Spurs: Paulinho's brilliant late winner ends the Bluebirds' unbeaten home record this season and gives Andre Villas-Boas' men all three points. Their fourth win from five games sees them join arch-rivals Arsenal at the top of the league.
(90’) The final whistle goes! Spurs have won it in dramatic fashion!
(90’) Spurs manage to counter and win a corner. Surely they will keep it down there until the final whistle.
--- 90’ +4 Yellow card Soldado goes into the referee's book. ---
--- 90’ +3 Assist E. Lamela provided the assist. ---
--- 90’ +3 Goal! GOOOOAAAL!! EXQUISITE FINISH!! Lamela pulls of his marker and runs to the byeline before squaring the ball into the six-yard box. Paulinho is in there and he finds the back of the net by flicking the ball behind Theophile with his trailing leg. Top-drawer finish. ---
(90’) Naughton almost finds the far corner with what was most certainly a cross from the left. No one got a touch on it and Marshall scrambled to his right to make sure it did not sneak in.
(90’) WHAT A SAVE!! Paulinho drifts into acres of space inside the box and Holtby picks him out with a lovely pass. Marshall races off his line to close the Brazilian and he is quick enough to get a block on his shot and parry it aside.
(90’) Walker goes for goal from distance but he slices his effort wide of the goal. We are going to have four minutes added on here! Can one of these teams find a winner?
--- 89’ Substitution C. Eriksen is replaced with L. Holtby. ---
(89’) Vital clearance from Kim! The midfielder gets back and manages to head Lamela's cross out of the six yard box. Kane was lurking at the back post and that could well have been the winner.
(88’) SO CLOSE!! Kane pulls out to the left and receives the ball on the corner of the box. He moves inside of Theophile but his attempt to guide a shot into the far corner sails wide of the post.
(87’) ...He fails to beat the first man and Cardiff can get the ball away. Only a few moments left now, and I cannot foresee too much time being added on.
(86’) Handball from Taylor gives Tottenham a free kick out on the right in the Cardiff half. Eriksen is going to pump this into the box...
(83’) Tottenham have enjoyed 62 per cent possession so far today but as things stand it is Cardiff who are looking the more likely to steal a late goal. Are we set for a dramatic finish?
--- 82’ Substitution A. Townsend is replaced with H. Kane. ---
(81’) WHAT A CHANCE!! Odemwingie beats Vertonghen inside the area and then pulls the ball back to Gunnarsson on the penalty spot. Again he takes it first time and yet again he sends his effort over the top! That was a chance to grab the winner.
(79’) Caulker gets on the ball at the back and charges up field. He lofts a ball over the top in the hopes that Cowie will run onto it, but he puts far too much power on it.
--- 77’ Substitution C. Bellamy is done for the day. D. Cowie is his replacement. ---
(76’) That is a brilliant interception by Gunnarsson! The Icelandic midfielder gets a foot in as Townsed races into the area following some lovely link-up play from the visitors.
(75’) Odemwingie is caught offside yet again. He really needs to show a little bit more patience with his movement as he is wasting some good opportunities for the hosts.
(73’) That is two poor passes from Lamela! He has time and space on the left side of the area but he rolls his first one into a red shirt, before sending his second to no one!
(72’) Spurs have kept a clean sheet in their last three matches against Cardiff in all competitions. Could another one be on the cards this afternoon? The Bluebirds have certainly upped the pressure again.
--- 71’ Substitution E. Lamela enters the game and replaces G. Sigurdsson. ---
--- 70’ Yellow card M. Dawson is yellow-carded. ---
(70’) Dawson picks up a booking after he clatters into Kim on the half way line. The midfielder had stolen the ball away from Paulinho and his quick feet drew the foul. He has been very impressive this afternoon.
(69’) Odemiwingie's introduction seems to have galvanised the hosts, but he is unable to add a finish after beating Vertonghen in the box. His attempt to bend the ball inside the far stick ends up going wide.
(68’) Good play from the Bluebirds as they work a shooting opportunity despite a host of Spurs bodies in the box. Odemwingie clips the ball to Gunnarsson who volleys first time but misses the target.
(66’) WELL OVER!! Eriksen bides his time before setting up Naughton to shoot at goal. The left-back tries to bend a shot in the far corner but he completely misses the target.
--- 65’ Substitution P. Odemwingie enters play, replacing F. Campbell. ---
(65’) Not overly adventurous from Mackay as he replaces Campbell with the Nigerian striker. Perhaps he hopes some fresh legs can cause the Spurs defence some trouble.
(64’) The answer is no! The ball is fired straight into the wall and the secondary attempt is no better. It looks as though Odemwingie is going to come on for the hosts here.
--- 63’ Yellow card B. Turner receives a yellow card. ---
(63’) Poor challenge from Turner! Townsend runs down the right at full speed and the centre-back puts in a late tackle which brings the winger to ground. Can Spurs make somthing of this?
(62’) Theophile is really struggling up against Sigurdsson now. Once more he is beaten towards the byeline but the Iceland international puts in a cross that is far too deep.
(60’) Across the face of goal! The short free kick is almost wasted by Gunnarsson manages to bulldoze a pass out to Whittingham. He has acres of space on the far side of the area and he plays the ball across the face of goal. However, none of his team-mates gamble to get on the end of it and it rolls out on the far side.
(59’) Campbell is becoming increasingly isolated in attack for the Bluebirds this half. He does well there, though, holding up the play before knocking it past Naughton and drawing a foul.
(57’) That would have been special! Spurs again work the ball across the pitch and Sigurdsson ends up beating Theophile to the byeline. He cuts it back to Paulinho at the near post and the Brazilian flicks the ball with the outside of his foot, but Marshall has his angles covered and keeps it out.
(55’) Great save from Marshall! The keeper does brilliantly to keep out Soldado's volley at the back post, but it would not have counted anyway as the flag was raised for offside.
(54’) Walker waltzes into the area from the right and throws a couple of stepovers at Taylor. He left-back is not fooled to his counterpart attempts to lay possession off to a team-mate, however his pass is far too short and the attack breaks down.
(53’) Gunnarsson pops up wide on the right and he receives the ball from Campbell in space. He gets his head up but Walker quickly closes him down and manages to steal the ball away.
(51’) OFF THE BAR!! Townsend runs across the top of the box before laying the ball off to Sigurdsson. He curls an effort towards the far corner that leaves Marshall rooted to the spot. Fortunately for him it comes back off his bar and the keeper does well to keep out Soldado's follow-up.
(50’) Soldado's movement inside the box has been impressive all afternoon and he gets away from Caulker to pick up the ball in space. He fires the ball across the face of goal and no one gets on the end of it. Was that a cross or a shot? I'm not sure even he knows.
(49’) In the Manchester derby, City now lead United by 4-0. How about they share some of the goals with this game for us!
(48’) Cardiff have already put a few crosses into the area this half but as of yet they have been unable to worry Lloris. The Frenchman comes off the line to claim their latest on without a challenge.
--- 47’ Yellow card A. Townsend is cautioned by the referee. ---
(46’) Instantly the Bluebirds get in behind the visitors with Kim's exquisite flick over the top of the defence being latched onto by Bellamy. He races into the area and tries to square for Whittingham, but Lloris manages to intercept the cross.
(46’) We are back under way at the Cardiff City Stadium.
Welcome back! The two teams are making their way out onto the pitch now so the second half will begin imminently.
HALF TIME - Cardiff 0-0 Spurs: The Bluebirds again fail to score in the first half, while despite peppering Marshall's goal with shots, the visitors have yet to beat him.  It is all to play for in the second half so be sure to join me for it in 15 minutes!
(45’) You are never scoring that, Turner! Whittingham's free kick is headed away by Dawson, but only as far as Turner who goes for an ambitious overhead kick. His technique is poor and he puts it well wide of the target.
(45’) The tempo of the game has really died down now, but Kim wins a free kick for Cardiff in a dangerous area as he turns Dawson and is pulled back by the defender.
(45’) We are in the first of three added minutes.
(44’) GOOOOAAL... not allowed! The resultant corner is sent to the back post and it flies over the top of Lloris. Turner nods it in but he is adjudged to have fouled Dawson as he climbed to head the ball. His hands where in the defender's back.
(43’) Awful control from Lloris! The keeper tries to stop the ball from going out of play but he knees, and then thighs, it out for a corner.
(41’) Cardiff are pressing a lot higher and a lot quicker in the closing stages of this half. Tottenham are finding it more difficult to get Eriksen on the ball, and he has been dictating things for much of the game so far. Positive signs for the Bluebirds.
(39’) That is great vision from Kim as he sprays a pass from the right touch line, all the way over to Taylor on the far side. It is bending away from the full-back the whole time though and he is unable to stop it from going out for a throw in. Could have been beautiful that!
(37’) That is poor from Dembele! He picks up the ball after it is cleared away from a corner and looks to force his way to the byeline. He is hassled all the way, though, and ends up running it off the field.
(36’) That is a good challenge from Whittingham as he tracks the run of Townsend inside from the right and times his slide tackle perfectly to take the ball. Cardiff starting to cope with Spurs' play a bit better now.
(34’) Good effort! Spurs work the ball from left to right and eventually Townsend finds space to have a go at goal from the corner of the box. He strikes it well enough but he aims it straight at Marshall, who holds onto it.
(31’) Bellamy clips a lovely ball over the top for Kim but Dawson gets across to make a crucial interception, though his foot was quite high. The Korean is still down at the other end so the Cardiff players force Spurs to kick it out of play.
(30’) That is where Medel is more useful, hounding Paulinho in midfield and forcing him back into his own half. The Chilean then puts in a great tackle and wins possession in the opposing half for his team. Campbell is unable to create anything with it from the left, though.
(27’) Well over the bar! Medel picks up a loose ball in the centre circle and bares down on goal. He smashes it towards the target but is unable to keep it down.
(26’) Cardiff look reluctant to shoot here! Some great interplay between Gunnarsson and Kim gives the latter the opportunity to go for goal, but instead he lays it off to Bellamy. Spurs manage to get bodies back and the momentum of the attack fizzles out.
(25’) For those of you that have not seen it, you have to find a picture of Cardiff City owner Vincent Tan's matchday attire. He has taken to wearing the club's shirt, but could not possibly wear it without his shirt and tie on underneath. So many layers can look untidy, but Mr. Tan sorts that by tucking it all into his trousers!
(23’) ANOTHER SAVE FROM MARSHALL! Spurs do brilliantly to hold onto possession and push Cardiff deeper and deeper. Sigurdsson unleashes their 10th attempt of the game and it is a powerful one, but the keeper gets his body in the way.
(22’) Cardiff cannot keep hold of the ball here. Villas-Boas men are absolutely dominating possession and are putting Marshall through his paces. Still, they have yet to find the back of the net.
(20’) ERIKSEN! Just wide! The Dane has had a cracking start to this game and he pulls another save from Marshall as he follows up from Soldado's strike, which was blocked by former Spurs man Caulker. The keeper got just enough on that to send it outside the frame of his goal, but he could not hold onto it.
(19’) That was an opportunity for Cardiff! Campbell gets on the ball inside the area and lays it off to Bellamy. The pass makes it difficult for the Welshman to pull the trigger so he then rolls it to Kim. Also unable to shoot, the midfielder feeds Theophile on the right but his cross is awful.
(17’) A great run from Sigurdsson as he darts in and out down the left but loses momentum and sends his cross into the first red shirt in the area. Spurs are looking dangerous here.
(16’) In the Premier League game running simultaneously to this one, Sergio Aguero has just put Manchester City 1-0 up against Manchester United.
(15’) GREAT EFFORT! Eriksen is not closed down within shooting distance of goal, and he takes the opportunity to do just that. He looses an effort which skids towards the bottom corner, but Marshall manages to get a hand to it.

(12’) Such pace! Walker steams through the heart of the defence at high speed but Turner manages to get across and make a crucial interception inside the area. It was crucial that he timed that tackle right.
(11’) Another cross into the box causes problems for the hosts. This time it is Naughton who delivers the ball from the left and Sigurdsson is in there to get his head on it. He is falling backwards as he connects with it so is unable to generate enough power to guide it past Marshall.
(10’) GREAT SAVE!! Again Spurs probe down their right and Townsend and Walker combine to get the ball into the middle for Soldado. The Spaniard peeled off his marker and shot first time at Marshall's near post, but the keeper gets down and somehow turns the shot behind.
(8’) That is good play from Spurs' midfield duo. Dembele hunts down Campbell and dispossesses the striker before Paulinho dribbles past a couple of red shirts in the centre of the park. Eventually the Brazilian is brought down and he wins a free kick for his side.

(6’) GREAT STOP FROM LLORIS!! An awful pass back from Naughton sells the keeper short and Campbell races onto the end of it. He feigns to shoot an attempts to round Lloris, but the keeper manages to get a hand to the ball right on the edge of his area to kill the attack.
(4’) Walker and Townsend combing well on the right to hold onto the ball and the latter whips a cross into the area. Sigurdsson looks to get onto the end of it at the back post but he can only knock it backwards. Naughton picks up the loose ball and plumps for goal, but he fires well over the top.
(2’) Cardiff pushing down their right during the early stages. Campbell latches onto a long throw and takes the ball into the corner. He hits the ball out of play, seemingly off of Naughton, but the referee's assistant points for a goal kick.

Hello and welcome to this afternoon's LIVE commentary on the Premier League clash between Cardiff City and Tottenham Hotspur. The Welsh outfit are undefeated on their own turf so far this campaign, so Andre Villas-Boas' side could be in for a tough afternoon. My name is Tom Webber and I will be watching this one alongside you.

Right, that's it from me - I've been Tom J Doyle, and thanks for joining in the debate on Twitter (@TomJDoyle). What a day, and what a Manchester derby - bye for now.
Wayne Rooney struck late on to become the all-time top scorer in Manchester derbies, but City fans won't care one jot as they have emphatically beaten United today. It was a demolition to be honest, and while the visitors improved in the final 30 minutes, it could well have been worse than the famous 6-1 defeat at Old Trafford.
That's it - what a day for Manchester City! They've beaten Premier League champions and city rivals Manchester United 4-1, and looked so, so dominant. Yaya Toure and Vincent Kompany starred, while Sergio Aguero netted twice to stun David Moyes' men - where do the Red Devils go from here?
(90’) So close for Dzeko! The big striker almost makes it five as he unleashes a low drive from 20 yards, but the ball swerves a yard wide of De Gea's post with the keeper static/not bothered.
(90’) Blue Moon is ringing out around the ground - it's been a near-perfect day for City fans...
(90’) Three minutes of injury time left - it's been a chastening start for Moyes. Surely he will look to the likes of Kagawa, Wilfried Zaha and even Adnan Januzaj in the wake of performances from the likes of Young and Valencia. There's even Jesse Lingard, who scored four on his Birmingham debut on a one-month loan deal.
(89’) United have been better in the last half hour, but that's an easy thing to achieve when you've let in four in the first 50 minutes.

(82’) Cleverley is down and clutching his face as Ferdandinho catches him in the eye with his fingers - that looked painful.

(71’) Negredo wants five as he bears down on goal, but wastefully slices a shot wide fom 25 yards with team mates better placed.

(31’) Amalfitano almosts get in down the right wing but Richardson recovers well, muscling the new West Brom loanee to the ground in a manner that the referee deemed fair.
(30’) West Brom persist in their attempts to hit Fulham back with a goal but they're not looking as though they're about to break through the home side's defence anytime soon.

Even though it remains early in the season, the two sides today find themselves in need of three points, having both endured a tough start to the season. Their problems were exacerbated in the transfer window as they failed to bring Romelu Lukaku back in on loan, though they did manage to secure the signatures of Stephane Sessegnon and Victor Anichebe from Sunderland and Everton respectively. Well in the end both sides have to settle for a point on a frustrating afternoon for City, who just failed to show any spark in the final third. Stoke had chances to break the deadlock but Walters and Jones were unable to make them count. Hughes is now four matches unbeaten in all competitions.

Both sides have just lacked that killer instinct in the final third. Stoke boss Hughes will probably be the happier of the two managers at the interval, with his side creating the best chances so far. Jon Walters should have converted Adam's centre in the fifteenth minute but somehow headed wide.

(45’) Just one minute of additional time at the Britannia Stadium as Hart collects the loose ball from Adam's in-swinging delivery.

A Giroud goal, and two quality second half strikes from the increasingly irreplaceable Ramsay has seen the Gunners past Sunderland, who have a Graig Gardner penalty as slim consolation. The visitors were pushed to their limits in the second period by the spirited Black Cats, who have a bone to pick with the officials after a controversial disallowed goal from Altidore. They've now only taken one point from their opening four games, while Arsenal have now won three on the trot after losing their season opener.

(36’) Arsenal just taking the foot off the gas as the first half enters its final lap. Sunderland don't seem in any hurry to press them off the ball, and the Gunners are quite happy to take advantage of that and keep hold of the ball in safe areas.
(34’) The influence of Ozil has been palpable, with his vision and geometric passing opening up avenues all over for Arsenal. An accomplished debut so far, reminiscent of the creativity shown by Santi Cazorla during his bow 11 months ago, which incidentally was also against Sunderland in a 0-0 draw. Better fortunes this time around for the Gunners though.
(32’) Ozil with another lovely pass forward to Wilshere, giving the England man a good run on goal, but he's barged off the ball by Roberge, legally mind you.
(31’) Good ball into the box from Mavrias, which Altidore curiously opts against attacking, giving Szczesny a catch that was more comfortable than it should have been.
(29’) Wilshere deftly releases Ozil, who sprints through the centre and puts Walcott through again. A bit of a tighter angle this time but same result - Westwood ashes off his line expertly to make another fine save.
(27’) A potentially dangerous free-kick just outside the box is taken by Ozil, who gets it over the wall, but cannot generate near enough power or unpredictability to beat Westwood. The keeper saw that all the way.
(26’) Arsenal completely comfortable at the Stadium of Light. The natives are getting a bit testy as the visitors continue to dominate the ball. Still only a goal in it though.
(24’) Steven Fletcher is down after a tussle with Sagna. He looks okay though, back on his feet relatively quickly .
(22’) Again on that left hand side Arsenal attack, this time Ozil and Wilshere linking well, but the latter's pass is just over-hit towards Gibbs on the overlap. Goalkick.
(20’) Excellent little triangle between Wilshere, Gibbs and Ramsey, as the fullback picks out his Welsh teammate inside the area, but he's caught between a shot and a cutback, and ends up slamming it right into Roberge.
(18’) Altidore does well to turn and squeeze a shot in from distance, and the movement on the ball confuses Szczesny for a second, but the Pole just about manages to parry! Hint of a deflection on that shot, but a needed positive sign for Sunderland.
(16’) That really should have been 2-0, Walcott having all the time in the world to line that one up. Huge credit must go to Ozil for that pass though, and also to Westwood, who pulled off a very vital save.
(15’) WESTWOOD MAKES THE SAVE! Ozil is already stamping his influence all over this Arsenal side, with a delightful early ball for Walcott, who is completely in the clear, but cannot pick his spot and the keeper blocks!
(13’) So very close for Sunderland! Again they cause problems in the air, as Diakite beats Giroud to a corner, planting a header onto the crossbar with Szczesny beaten!
--- 11’ Assist M. Özil gave the assist. ---
--- 11’ Goal! It's in from Giroud! A classic counter attack from Arsenal, a long ball over the top picking out that man Ozil perfectly on the left flank, who swiftly arrows in a peach of a low cross that is stabbed home confidently by the French striker! ---
(11’) GOOOOOOOOOOOALLLLL!
(10’) Not much of note in an attacking sense from Sunderland, as the Gunners have had most of the ball so far. But they do look dangerous on the break, as evidenced by their lone chance, so don't count them out for one second.
(8’) With the abscence of Cazorla, who can play through the middle or on the left, it will be really interesting to see how Ozil lines up in the Arsenal XI. Ostensibly he has began on the left flank, but has already been spotted drifting onto the opposite side, with Wilshere looking to fill the resulting gaps.
(6’) First real glimpse of Ozil as he prepares to take an Arsenal corner, but his delivery cannot make it past the head of Diakite. Good defending.
(4’) Uncertainty in the Arsenal ranks! The ball comes in, and looks to be routine stuff for Jenkinson to deal with. But he hashes the clearance, heading it straight into the air, and Altidore nearly pounces to tee up a chance for Steven Fletcher on a plate.
(2’) Wilshere advancing menacingly through the middle. Sunderland's players are very reluctant to make a challenge, but the Arsenal man overruns it and ends up losing the ball just inside the area.
(1’) Bang.
Sunderland, with ony one point for their opening three games, are not exactly flying high, and last beat Arsenal in 2009 thanks to a Darren Bent goal. Arsenal have seemingly shaken off that opening day collapse against Aston Villa, winning their last four games in all compeitions.
Meanwhile, for the home side, Paolo Di Canio has handed a place in the XI to midfield signing Ki Sung-Yueng, who was swiped from Swansea in a loan deal on the last day of August. Steven Fletcher, with his goalscoring exploits against Crystal Palace still fresh in the memory, is also granted a start, his first in six months. He will do the heavy lifting up front with Jozy Altidore.
Ozil starts for Arsenal. That much has dominated the pre-match news. Gunners fans will get a chance to see their record signing right away. Interestingly, with Santi Cazorla missing the trip to Wearside, it looks like the German will line up on the left flank, with Flamini, Ramsey and Wilshere filling out the midfield three. Per Mertesacker is also absent, so Bacary Sagna is drafted in at centre-back, with Carl Jenkinson starting on the right side of the defence.
Sunderland: Westwood; Celustka, Colback, Roberge, Diakite; Vaughan, Mavrias, Ki, Johnson; Fletcher, Altidore. SUBS: Mannone, Brown, Cuellar, Larsson, Gardner, Wickham, Borini.
Arsenal: Szczesny; Jenkinson, Sagna, Koscielny, Gibbs; Flamini, Ramsey, Wilshere; Ozil, Walcott, Giroud. SUBS: Fabianski, Vermaelen, Monreal, Frimpong, Ryo, Gnabry, Akpom.

Those three points see Spurs up to second in the Premier League table just  behind Arsenal, but above Liverpool on goal difference. It looks like Norwich will slip to 13th after the loss, depending on other results.
FULL-TIME: Tottenham 2-0 Norwich
(90’) This one is all over now despite Norwich's late push here. The Canaries are doing their best to give the travelling support something to go home happy about.
(90’) Erik Lamela is properly involved for the first time and his cross almost gives Soldado a chance, but it's kicked out. Snodgrass then fouls the Argentine in the corner.
(89’) Sebastian Bassong is called into action again. This time he clears Walker's right-wing cross as Tottenham look for a third goal. There will be four minutes of time added on.
(86’) Norwich win a free kick right on the edge of the area, slightly to the right. Robert Snodgrass goes for goal but his left-footed strike slams straight into the wall, which looked suspiciously close to the ball...
--- 85’ Yellow card H. Lloris is cautioned by the referee. ---
(84’) More danger for the hosts to deal with as Norwich win their first corner of the afternoon after Spurs struggle to clear a deep ball into the area. It's headed away by Paulinho quite easily though.
--- 83’ Substitution E. Lamela enters the game and replaces M. Dembélé. ---
(82’) Snodgrass intercepts a Dembele pass, and Norwich have the ball in Spurs half. But another chance to threaten is wasted and Spurs win the ball from a loose pass and break.
(80’) Gylfi Sigurdsson looks a bit miffed as he is replaced by Sandro with a few minutes to play. The Icelandic midfielder looked like he might have bagge an unlikely hat-trick. Sandro comes on in a change which should sure up the points.
--- 79’ Substitution G. Sigurdsson is replaced with Sandro. ---
(77’) Norwich  manage their best period of possession since the first half and it gives substitute Pilkington the chance to break down the left, but he's flagged offside. Just not happening for the Canaries.
--- 75’ Substitution A. Tettey enters the game and replaces J. Elmander. ---
--- 74’ Substitution A. Pilkington enters play, replacing N. Redmond. ---
(74’) Another Andros Townsend cross is out for a throw. The youngster has been heavily involved in the action this afternoonn but he has lacked final product.
(72’) Christian Eriksen walks off to a standing ovation from the White Hart Lane crowd. Lewis Holtby comes on in his place.
--- 71’ Substitution L. Holtby comes on for C. Eriksen. ---
--- 71’ Yellow card J. Elmander gets yellow. ---
(71’) CHANCE! An excellent opportunity for Norwich as Redmond's deflected strike after a Lloris punch falls to van Wolfswinkel in the box. But he takes too many touches, allowing Rose to make a block tackle.
(68’) CLOSE! Sebastian Bassong's sloppiness at the back allows Tottenham to drive forward once again, and after Soldado miscontrols Paulinho's pass, Townsend gets in a shot that Ruddy saves with his foot.
(66’) Snodgrass and Van Wolfswinkel combine down the right flank before Snodgrass is upended by the physical, but fair, Danny Rose. Norwich have had their moments but Tottenham don't look too concerned when they do forray forward.
--- 64’ Substitution B. Johnson is replaced with J. Howson. ---
(64’) Erik Lamela has been told to warm up by Andre Villas-Boas. His introduction into the game looks imminent.
(62’) CLOSE! Gylfi Sigurdsson is on the hunt for his hat-trick and nearly gets with a right-footed piledriver from range. John Ruddy does well to get a strong hand on it to parry it away.
(61’) Sebastian Bassong has to get across quickly to reach the ball ahead of Soldado, who was played into space down the right flank. The Frenchman does well to clear the danger.
--- 60’ Yellow card Javier Garrido is cautioned by the referee. ---
(59’) Norwich look like they might get a glimmer of a chance on the break but Johan Elmander is flagged offside as they look to make in-roads on the Tottenham goal.
(56’) It's all Spurs . A neat interchange between Paulinho, Rose and Sigurdsson almost provides another opening for the hosts but they're continuing to put pressure on this Norwich rearguard.
(54’) Is there any way back for Chris Hughton's men? They still have Gary Hooper on the bench if they want to increase their goal threat. Looking like a tall order though...
(52’) A rare attack for Norwich ends with Nathan Redmond mistake. The so far impressive youngster overhits a simple enough pass for Snodgrass on the wing. Tottenham look very comfortable now.
--- 49’ Assist Paulinho provided the assist. ---
--- 49’ Goal! G. Sigurdsson has found the target for Tottenham Hotspur! ---
(49’) GOAL! Tottenham double their lead through Sigurdsson! Spurs worked a fine move to get Paulinho away down the right flank unmarked, he fires a low cross along the six-yard box for the Iceland international to tap in at the back post!
(47’) First effort of the second half comes from the right boot of Christian Eriksen but it's an audacious effort from range which sails both high and wide.
(46’) Norwich take the kick-off and we are underway for the second half!
Any thoughts or questions to you at half-time, send them into me via @HushKerai. How do Norwich get back in to this? Should Andre Villas-Boas introduce Erik Lamela after the break?
Looking at a replay of Tottenham's goal. I didn't give near enough credit to Christian Eriksen for his final ball. A deft, perfectly-weighted pass, which sliced the Canaries backline open. Fine debut for the Dane.
For all those chances Spurs had, if Ricky van Wolfswinkel had been able to steer his effort, following Redmond's cross, a yard to the right, then the Canaries would be trodding in at the break level.
Tottenham have enjoyed 73% possession in this first half and have had 13 shots on goal. Just a sign of their domination, but they only have a single goal to show for it.
HALF-TIME: Tottenham 1-0 Sunderland
(45’) Only one minute of time will be added on at the end of the half.
(45’) Nice passing and interchange between Christian Eriksen and Mousa Dembele. Those two look have forged a fine understanding very quickly. Great news for the home side's fans.
(43’) CHANCE! Fine Tottenham move as Walker crosses from the right, and Soldado tries to connect but Bassong puts just enough pressure on the Spaniard. The ball comes across to Rose, who fires over from a tight angle.
(40’) Despite that scare from Van Wolfswinkel, Tottenham look comfortable with their one-goal lead and looks to cruising into half-time with a lead...
(38’) Tottenham intercept an overhit Johnson pass allowing Eriksen to break forward. He gives the ball to Dembele, who almost releases Sigurdssson on the edge of the box but Norwich manage to snuff out the danger.
(36’) CLOSE! Ricky van Wolfswinkel nearly equalises! The Dutchman gets on the end of a low cross from Redmond but his side footed finish is put wide from close range under pressure from Rose.
(35’) Vertonghen is takes one in the face from Elamander. He's fine though, and there's no booking. Walker is again dispossessed as the hosts build an attack but Spurs are swiftly back to win the ball.
(32’) Soldado tries to get onto Rose's lofted pass, but Ruddy is out smartly to deny him the opportunity. It's still all Spurs here, they look more likely to add a second, Norwich aren't really threatening.
(29’) STAT: That's Tottenham's first goal from open play in the Premier League this season.
--- 28’ Assist Assist by C. Eriksen. ---
--- 28’ Goal! Goal to Tottenham Hotspur, scored by G. Sigurdsson! ---
(28’) GOAL! Gylfi Sigurdsson puts Tottenham into the lead with a fine finish at the end of a flowing move. Soldado chested the ball down to Eriksen on the edge of the area. The Dane played a sweet short pass into the area for Sigurdsson to run onto and he finished across Ruddy into the corner from 10 yards.
(26’) Christian Eriksen has a chance to deliver in a succession of corners but Norwich defend them all with relative ease and keep Spurs at bay. Getting slightly frustrating for the home fans now.
(24’) Chris Hughton's men have come back into this fixture now with soe more possession it's still the hosts who look the most dangerous in the final third.
(23’) Paulinho does brilliantly on the right to keep a Tottenham attack moving. Townsend gets away with a poor touch, and then Walker fails to retain possession. Spurs then press Norwich all the way back to their goal but manage a rare break forward until Van Wolfswinkel is dispossessed.
--- 20’ Yellow card B. Johnson gets yellow. ---
(20’) The first booking of the game goes to Bradley Johnson after he takes a couple of chunks out of the wincing Roberto Soldado. The former Valencia man has troubled the Canaries with his movement early on.
(17’) Paulinho has a go from about 25 yards out but his shot hits Turner and goes behind for a corner. Eriksen's set piece which follows is easily cleared by Norwich.
(15’) Christian Eriksen is muscled off the ball by Bassong after a header down by Soldado. Spurs are happy to mix up their style as they look to find a way past the deep Norwich defense. Andros Townsend's second strike from distance also goes over.
(12’) OFF THE POST! A superb effort from Soldado after some fine skill from Eriksen - but no goal for Tottenham! The Dane nutmegged Turner, Ruddy couldn't hold the ball and Soldado improvised - only to see his backheel hit the post.
(10’) Danny Rose looks like a threat down the left-flank but Steven Whittaker looks well up for the challenge of going up against him.
(8’) Christian Eriksen aims to flick a little cross into the path of Roberto Soldado but Sebastian Bassong is wise to the danger and does well to intervene. Spurs still probing deep in the Norwich half.
(6’) Norwich quickly break and Elmander runs into the area, but Vertonghen slides in and manages to put him off.
(6’) Andrre Villas-Boas' men are enjoying all the possession in the early stages. Norwich are sitting deep in the own half and are struggling to make any movement up the pitch.
(4’) Another shot from long range misses the target for the hosts. This time Andro Townsend jinks one way then the other before firing a low left-footed effort just wide of John Ruddy's left-hand post.
(3’) Michael Turner heads away Andros Townsend's clipped cross from the right flank, then Paulinho sees his delivery from a similiar area blocked.
(2’) Gylfi Sigurdsson has the first effort of the game. His right-footed shot after cutting in from the left flank is hit over the bar as the Spurs fans chant: "We'll sing what we want".
(1’) Tottenham take the kick-off and we are underway at the Lane!
Pre-match huddles have been taken care of. It's a grey, cold afternoon at White Hart Lane. Perfect for a hearty game of Premier League football.
Meanwhile, Roberto Soldado has been assigned a mascot who is nearly as tall as him. Moments away from the action now...
Looking at some of Norwich's stats; the Canaries have only one one of their last 11 league away games. They'll be hoping to curb that trend this afternoon.
Here's a stat for you while we wait for the action to get underway. Spurs have fired more shots off target than any other team so far this season (27). Andre Villas-Boas' men are also yet to score from open play.
Meanwhile Norwich are unchanged after beating Southampton 1-0 last time out.
Christian Eriksen makes his debut, while Gylfi Sigurdsson also starts as Andre Villas-Boas makes two changes to the team that lost 1-0 at Arsenal. Nacer Chadli and the injured Capoue make way.
Norwich (4-4-1-1): Ruddy; Whittaker, Bassong, Turner, Garrido; Snodgrass, Fer, Johnson, Redmond; Elmander; van Wolfswinkel. Subs: Bunn, Martin, Howson, Hooper, Pilkington, Olsson, Tettey.
Tottenham (4-2-3-1) : Lloris; Walker, Dawson, Vertonghen, Rose; Dembele, Paulinho; Townsend, Eriksen, Sigurdsson; Soldado. Subs: Friedel, Kaboul, Naughton, Holtby, Lamela, Sandro, Defoe.

Jose Mourinho's side were out fought and out thought this evening. Samuel Eto'o's debut didn't go as swimmingly as expected. There are quite a few selection issues for the Portuguese to sort through. Does he know his best team?
What a game. Roberto Martinez has properly arrived at Goodison Park. There were moans and groans at times when the Toffees persisted with their manager's preferred passing build-up, but in the end it paid dividends.
FULL-TIME: Everton 1-0 Chelsea
(90’) The Goodison crowd are all whistling, only seconds left now....
(90’) CHANCE! It opens for Leon Osman to have a strike from the edge of the area but the Everton midfielder has a rush of blood to the head and blasts into the stands!
--- 90’ +2 Substitution Gerard Deulofeu comes on for K. Mirallas. ---
(90’) There will be a minimum of three added minutes. Torres misses his kick inside the box with his weaker left foot at Chelsea look for one final chance. Everton feel like they'll hang on...
--- 89’ Substitution J. Stones comes on for S. Naismith. ---
(89’) OFF THE BAR! Leighton Baines clips the top of the bar with the set-piece with Petr Cech rooted to the spot.
(88’) CHANCE! Everton are playing the situation superbly. Mirallas is holding on to the ball well and allowing his team-mates to give him support up the pitch. Barkley has run at the visitor's all evening and he wins a free kick right on the edge of the area with the clock running down...
--- 87’ Yellow card J. Obi Mikel goes into the referee's book. ---
(85’) Petr Cech and David Luiz have a mix up in communication and allow Mirallas to gather a long clearance from the back. Unfortunately for the Toffees the Belgian doesn't spot Barkely's marauding run up the field and Everton surrender possession.
(83’) CONTROVERSY! Ross Barkley plays a simply superb ball into Mirallas who beats David Luiz, the last man for Chelsea in defence. The Brazilian hauls him down but escapes with just a booking because of how far up the pitch the challenge took place.
--- 82’ Yellow card David Luiz is cautioned by the referee. ---
(81’) PENALTY SHOUT! Coleman flies away down the right flank and is brought down by the backtracking Hazard. Howard Webb judges the foul to have taken place outside the box. Sigh of relief from the Chelsea bench.
(80’) CHANCE! Ross Barkley does brilliantly in two stages. First breaking into the Chelsea half and then winning the ball back. Mirallas eventually cuts in from the left and shoots powerfully with his right. Petr Cech makes a fine block!
(80’) SAVE! Tim Howard does just enough at the near post to deny Samuel Eto'o who looked to have turned in Ramires' cross.
--- 79’ Yellow card E. Hazard is yellow-carded. ---
(77’) Barry wipes out Ramires off the ball in one of the more comedic fouls you'll see this season. Meanwhile, Everton are working their blue and white socks off, pressing and harrying the Chelsea players in possession. Frantic finish to this match.
(74’) Corner after corner after corner! Chelsea are hanging on here as the Toffees throw hammer and tong at them from these set-pieces in search of that elusive second.
(72’) CHANCE! It's brilliant from Everton, it really is. They pull Chelsea's backline here and there with some fine passing and interchange but Coleman's cross is blocked by Luiz. Goodison Park is electric!
(70’) Fernando Torres joins the action to a chorus of boos because of his history at Liverpool. Mind you, he gets booed there too!
--- 69’ Substitution A. Cole is done for the day. Fernando Torres is his replacement. ---
(69’) CLOSE! It's another one into the side netting! This time Ramires, on the full stretch, misses the target after meeting Ivanovic's cross.
--- 66’ Substitution J. McCarthy enters play, replacing N. Jelavić. ---
(66’) James McCarthy comes on to make his Everton debut. He will be requried to be defensively solid rather than offensively expansive in these final 25 minutes as Everton aim to hang on for three points.
--- 65’ Yellow card B. Ivanović is cautioned by the referee. ---
(63’) Lampard breaks into the box and collects a threaded pass following a dummy from Ashley Cole, but the club's record goalscorer cannot bring it under his spell and Howard is able to gather.
(61’) It's all one way traffic following the introductions of Lampard and Oscar. Everton can't make the ball stick to Jelavic when they have it. The Toffees are badly in need of some respite here...
(58’) PENALTY SHOUT! Oscar goes down inside the box under a challenge from Sylvain Distin but Howard Webb is having none of it. From first impressions, it looked like the Chelsea man got his toe to the ball first.
--- 57’ Substitution F. Lampard comes on for A. Schürrle. ---
--- 57’ Substitution Mata is done for the day. Oscar is his replacement. ---
(57’) Hazard tries to get the ball through the smallest of gaps inside the box to find Juan Mata but that's not the way Chelsea are going to penetrate this deep lying Toffess defence.
(55’) Good cover from Osman as he stands up Eto'o outside the box and prevents a cross. The Cameroonian looks off the pace slightly but I wouldn't write him off from making an impact just yet.
(52’) Chelsea are certainly putting the pressure on the Toffees now. Mikel works his way into the box, but the ball gets stuck under his feet and Everton clear. Yet to score for Chelsea, Mikel.
(50’) CHANCE! Eden Hazard slams a shot from range right down Tim Howard's throat and the Everton goalkeeper can only block. Thankfull for him, Eto'o can't quite connect properly with the rebound which trickles harmlessly wide.
(47’) CLOSE! Andre Schurlle almost gets Chelsea right back in it. The German makes a good run across the Everton defence and is threaded through on goal but his delicate finish from a tightish angle only hits the side netting!
(46’) Everton take the kick-off and we are underway in the second half!
A brilliant 45 minutes of action at Goodison Park. Chelsea did all the huffing and puffing and squandered a long list of glorious chances. Everton, though, have had plenty of impressive in the first half. None more so than the goalscorer, Steven Naismith, on his 26th birthday no less.
HALF-TIME: Everton 1-0 Chelsea
--- 45’ +1 Assist Assist by N. Jelavić. ---
--- 45’ +1 Goal! Everton score a goal through S. Naismith! ---
(45’) GOAL! Birthday boy Steven Naismith gives Everton the lead after some fine build-up from the Toffees. Leon Osman stands a ball up at the back post, where Jelavic arrives to knock the back into the middle for the Scot to head over the line!
(44’) Eden Hazard skips past a couple challenges as in runs along the width of the box before laying the ball of to Juan Mata. The Spaniard attempts to dink the ball into the back post but doesn't quite manage to get over the ball.
(43’) Branislav Ivanovic clatters into Jelavic as the pair renew their Serbia - Croatia rivalry from midweek.
(41’) Hazard turns Barry right on the edge of the area and wins a free kick off the midfielder. Mata swings the cross in using his right boot but Ivanovic can't direct his header on target from inside the box.
(38’) WHAT A MISS! Andre Schurrle has the chance to put Chelsea ahead but miscues his shot spectacularly. Ramires springed the offside trap to run clear through on goal before nudging the ball wide to the German under pressure but the visitors let another chance go begging.
(35’) GREAT SAVE! Howard makes up for his earlier error with a superb stop! Eto'o squares a ball to Ramires in the box who fires a right-footed shot in towards the top corner. Thankfull for the hosts, the American shot-stopper manages to get a hand to it.
(33’) Everton go back on the attack and Mirallas causes problems for Chelsea before crossing for Naismith who can only stab wide at the near post. The Scot has had an impressive first half.
(30’) MASSIVE CHANCE! Howard has moment of madness and passes the ball straight to Hazard from the back. The Belgian squares for Eto'o but Barry rushes across to make the most miraculous of challenges. Barry is making himself an instant hero with the fans.
(28’) David Luiz charges out of the back and bypasses his and Everton's midfield in one swoop before attempting an ambitious through ball for Eto'o, which doesn't come off. Good enterprise from the Brazilian, bad execution.
(25’) Everton earn themselves another corner and Naismith's cross is met by both Distin and Luiz at the back post, but Chelsea are given the goal kick much to the Toffees defender's annoyance.
(22’) Gareth Barry trips over David Luiz as the Brazilian looks to break into the Everton third. Moments later the Chelsea defender does the same to Kevin Mirallas as the Belgian threatens to start an Everton break.
(20’) Brilliant stuff from Gareth Barry has he snaps on the heels of the Chelsea midfield to win the ball back twice in quick succession. The former Manchester City man has settled right into life at Goodison Park.
(17’) Kevin Mirallas almost squirms through on goal down the left but Ivanovic uses all his strength to wrestle the ball back off the Belgian. Everton are looking lively in attack after what was a electric start from the visitors.
(15’) Everton earn a corner after a fine attack with Jelavic and Naismith combining with a series of lobbed passes. The corner is overhit though, and Chelsea survive the danger and are able to push back out.
(12’) Superb stuff from Ross Barkely. The youngster charges out of defence and skips past Mikel with a lovely piece of dribbling but his attempt at a very difficult through pass for Mirallas is cut out by Ivanovic.
(9’) CHANCE! Everton have a opportunity to break and they do just that with Naismith tearing forward down the right flank. His cross floats over David Luiz and into Nikica Jelavic, but the Croatian can't get any purchase on his header which bounces into Cech's grateful arms.
(7’) Mata finds Eto'o inside the box with a cute little pass but Leighton Baines sees the danger and shoulder charges the Chelsea striker off the ball to deny him the chance to shoot.
(5’) CLOSE! It's those two again! Ramires this time delivers a fantastic ball into the far post from the right flank. Eto'o rushes in at the back post but his header flies over the bar.
(4’) CHANCE! Early chance for the Chelsea as Samuel Eto'o gets involved. Ramires looks for the Cameroon international with a cutback inside the box but Phil Jagielka is there to make the interception.
(2’) A fine start from the Toffees. Ross Barkely tries to skip past a few challenges on the right flank while Gareth Barry gets his Everton career off to a solid start with a couple of neat passes.
(1’) Everton take the kick-off and we are underway!
The teams are emerging from the tunnel to a raucous atmosphere inside Goodison Park. Kick-off is moments away...
While Jose Mourinho said this on Mata: "He is a player I like very much, that's why he's here. He is a player I trust a lot and will fight for position like everybody else. Sometimes he will start, sometimes on the bench and sometimes he may not be selected because the squad is so competitive. With a match every three days, I will make 'strange' decisions to your eyes but because I think further than the next match and I want to have him at his maximum level."
Roberto Martinez on Barry in his pre-match interview: "I see him getting back in the England team because there are not many like him. Normally in England you get the box-to-box midfielder, but Gareth brings a more continental approach."
Gareth Barry starts for Everton after making his deadline day move to Goodison Park. James McCarthy will have to wait for his chance to play under Roberto Martinez again.
Chelsea fans finally get the chance to see Samuel Eto'o get his first-ever taste of Premier League action this afternoon. He replaces Fernando Torres who drops down to a very strong looking Chelsea bench.
Chelsea (4-2-3-1): Cech; Ivanovic, Luiz, Terry, Cole; Ramires, Mikel; Schurrle, Hazard, Mata; Eto'o. Subs: Schwarzer, Essien, Lampard, Torres, Oscar, De Bruyne, Cahill.
Everton (4-5-1): Howard, Coleman, Jagielka, Distin, Baines, Naismith, Mirallas, Barry, Barkley, Osman, Jelavic. Subs: Robles, Heitinga, Oviedo, Deulofeu, McCarthy, Gueye, Stones.

(75’) 15 minutes to go and Everton continue to press, but Coleman is put under pressure from a crowd of red shirts and his cross hits the side netting. Is there some form of rain dance you can do to make it rain goals?
(73’) Ultimately, that corner was a waste and the Toffees come back into the game. Is there a late winner here?
(70’) We have twenty minutes to go and Cardiff have a corner on the right-hand side. Can they score from here?
--- 68’ Substitution N. Jelavić is replaced with A. Koné. ---
(67’) Instead, Pienaat steps up and tries to play Jelavic in, but the tide of red shirts break apart the attack. The confidence-stricken Croatian International prepares to depart the field of play after another disappointing afternoon in front of goal.
(67’) Another free-kick is given to the Toffees in a similar position to the last one. Will Barkley improve his radar with this one?
(65’) ...Actually, it's Barkley who steps up and tnrashes the ball into the Cardiff wall.
(64’) Wittingham tickles Barkley's heels and a free-kick of awarded to the visitors about 25-yards-out centre to the goal. Will this be a Baines special?...
(62’) CHANCE! The Bluebirds support roars their team forward and Craig Bellamy is onside and threw on goal! But the Welshman's touch is too heavy and he has to scramble the ball back to Gunnarsson before Coleman gets it clear. If only the Cardiff captain's touch had been better, we would have had our first goal of the afternoon.
(61’) The Toffees are currently boasting a poccession percentage of 66% but that final ball is still missing. Martinez looks to his bench. Is the time approaching to throw Wigan old-boy Kone into the mix?
(58’) Nearing the hour mark at the Cardiff City Stadium and it is still 0-0. Would it be too much to ask for a goal?
(55’) There's a bit of argy-bargy as Fellaini brings Campbell down inside the Everton half. The Bluebirds striker gets into a needless but short scuffle with the Belgian and both players are spoken to by the referee.
(54’) STAT ATTACK: Only once under David Moyes (in 2010-11) did Everton fail to win any of their opening three games in a Premier League season (D1 L2). (BBCSport)
(52’) CHANCE! Oh, Jelavic. Good work from Barkley as he puts the striker through on goal but the out-of-form hitman scuffs his shot high over the bar when it looked easier to score.
--- 49’ Yellow card M. Connolly is yellow-carded. ---
(49’) ...which finds Jelavic in an offside position.
(49’) Connolly is booked for impeding on Baines. Free-kick to the Toffees...
(47’) CHANCE! Connolly slices the balls wide after a corner from the right-hand side is cleared to his feet at the edge of the area.
(45’) The two teams are back out on the pitch and the second half begins. Can the Bluebirds claim another major scalp or will the Toffees win their first game of the season?
It's goaless at the break, yet my spidey-sense is tingling and telling me that goals will flow in the second half. How many? Well, you'll have to stick around to find out...
STAT ATTACK:  Including eight games as Wigan manager, Roberto Martinez has won just one of his last 10 Premier League matches (W1 D5 L4). (BBCSport)
Both teams leave the field with Everton on top in this game. The Bluebirds only clear cut effort came with Wittingham's corner which was scrambled away by Howard in the six-yard box. But that fingertip save in the final minute from Howard's opposite number, Marshall, was majestic. More to come in 15 minutes!
(45’) CHANCE! What a save! Coleman puts a cross in from the right and Jelavic gets his head to it. It takes a deflection and looks to be sailing into the back of the head before Marshall, who was wrong footed in the deflection, manages to scramble low to his left and turn the ball away. That is an early contender for save of the season, surely! What a moment for the keeper.
(45’) There will be two minutes of stoppage time...
(44’) We are one minute plus stoppages away from the break and both sides are yet to break the deadlock. Roberto Martinez will be happier with his side's performance but maybe thinking how they have been denied a penalty in this first-half.
(41’) PENALTY SHOUT! Ooh, is that a penalty for the Toffees? Leighton Baines plays a fantastic one-two with Pienaar and goes down under a challenge from Taylor in the box. The left-back does not complain as the visitors appeal, but that could easily have been given.
--- 38’ Yellow card R. Barkley goes into the referee's book. ---
(38’) It is fair to say that the referee is having a bit of mare so far today. Barkley goes in on Kim and the official waves play on but the flag is waving from his linesman, over ruling the man in charge. The teenager is subsiquently booked for a foul that would bot have been given if the ref had not taken the advice of his fellow officiator.
(36’) Everton catch the home side on the break and Fellaini, being booed the whole time by the Cardiff support, is tackled by Caulker who puts the ball into safety. The Toffees definitely have the edge in this game.
(34’) CHANCE! Another free-kick, floated in from the left from Baines, is met by a leaping Jagielka, whose looping header is comfortably smothered by Marshall.
(32’) CHANCE! I wonder if Tim Howard likes butter? Why, I hear you ask? Because his gloves are the colour of buttercups. A through ball from Gunnarsson away after it had been intercepted by Campbell...despite the Iceman's intentions to find Wittingham instead, who had made a great run into the box.
(30’) CHANCE! Jelavic cuts the ball back on the left-hand-side of the City box and puts a lovely cross onto the head of Mirallas, who once again fluffs his lines and sees his free header skim wide.
(28’) Baines is being given license to roam down the left flank but he is crowded out by the Bluebirds defence before he can find a killer pass. Like I said earlier, we are one cracking final ball away from an opener here.
(25’) CHANCE! Baines swings in a free-kick from the left flank and Mirallas is left unmarked but skies his header into the stand.
(23’) CHANCE! Fraizer Campbell, who is making his 150th career appearance today, latches onto a bouncer in the box but sees his effort skew high over the crossbar. The lineman's flag is up anyway, so it would not have counted, but the Bluebird striker was almost in the right place to strike, there.
(21’) Seamus Coleman is spoken to by the referee after leaving his leg in and bringing Kim down near the halfway line. The intensity of the crowd bays for a yellow but it's just a ticking off for the Everton youngster.
(18’) The visitors are enjoying a spell on the ball and Mirallas sees one ball into the area headed away by Caulker and then his next two attempts for a cross are also thwarted. The final ball is all thats lacking for the men in blue right now.
(16’) CHANCE! Bellamy swings a corner in from the left and Caulker gets up to meet it, but the ball brushes the head of an Everton player for another corner on the opposite side. Taken by Peter Wittingham, Tim Howard makes a bit of a hash of it and punches the ball away from just under his own bar. The American needs to dry his gloves and find his composure after that one!
(13’) Barkley's movement is superb as the 19-year-old shows just why he has been picked by Roy Hodgson for England's double header next week. The youngster jinks past two Cardiff defenders but his through-ball is too heavy for Jelavic. The intensity of this game is slowly beginning to rise.
(10’) CHANCE! The Toffees are knocking again as Pienaar slots the ball through to England hopeful Ross Barkley, whose shot from the edge of the box is blocked by Steven Caulker and trickes wide for a corner, which ultimately leads to nowt. Great play from Roberto Martinez's men.
(9’) OUCH! It looks like Craig Bellamy's personal vendetta today is to get in Baines' face...literally. The Bluebirds captain punts an elbow into the England International's face in what looked like a deliberate attempt to unsettle the defender. Well, i'd be!
(7’) STAT ATTACK: Malky Mackay's team beat Manchester City in their last match despite having only 30% of the possession, as calcuated by Opta. (BBCSport)
(4’) CLOSE! The Toffees knock on the door, first and Mirallas is beaten to a loose ball at the back post by Taylor, who clears it behind. The away support are incensed when a goal kick is given. That looked like the Bluebirds ball, to me.
(3’) It's Cardiff who are getting stuck in first as Leon Osman is bundled over by Gunnarsson in the centre circle. Plenty of time for this game to settle.
(1’) Everton get the game underway, kicking from right to left.
Both sides are lining up, about to be welcomed by beautiful sunshine and screaming fans. They emerge, kick-off is not far away now.
We are only ten minutes away from kick-off but the atmosphere is building inside the Cardiff City Stadium. If the home fans can roar their charges forward like they did against City last week, the Evertonians may be in need of ear plugs!
STAT ATTACK: Craig Bellamy could become the first player to score for seven different clubs in the Premier League. He has previously scored for Coventry, Liverpool, Manchester City, Newcastle, Blackburn and West Ham. (BBCSport)
STAT ATTACK: Nikica Jelavic has only scored one goal in 21 hours and 47 minutes of Premier League football. (BBCSport)
So, Cardiff boss Malky Mackay keeps the faith with the team that put Man City to the sword last weekend, whilst Roberto Martinez also names an unchanged line-up, with Man Utd targets Leighton Baines and Marouane Fellaini both taking their places on the team sheet. Can the home support create more epic atmosphere this afternoon here in Wales like last time out?
