(75’) Gouffran has looked lively since entering the game and it is his cross from the left that almost finds Ameobi in the box. The striker, though, is adjudged to have committed a doul as he looked to challenge for the ball.
(73’) Ben Arfa has vanished this half. The Frenchman has not been anywhere near as threatening or creative as he was in the first half. He tries to start something for his team here but Collins does well to stop Sissoko from advancning into the area after receiving his pass.
--- 72’ Substitution Y. Gouffran enters the game and replaces P. Cissé. ---
(71’) Newcastle are starting to pile on the pressure now and West Ham are coming under attack after every time they clear it. It is going to be a tight end to this game.
(69’) The game has descended into a bit of a scrappy affair now. Both teams are eager to push the ball forward but in doing so are conceding possession quickly. A little more patience to work an opening is required here.
(67’) The Magpies have lost their previous three home Premier League games.West Ham, meanwhile, have failed to win in 13 of their last 14 away matches in the league. Read into that what you will, but both sides could certainly nick this one.
--- 66’ Substitution Sammy Ameobi enters play, replacing S. Marveaux. ---
(65’) Pardew counters with a change of his own, replacing Marveaux with Sammy Ameobi. The Frenchman has put in a good shift today.
--- 64’ Substitution J. Cole enters play, replacing S. Downing. ---
(63’) Downing is the man to make way and he is visibly disappointed. He has created more than Jarvis so is right to feel a bit aggrieved at the decision.
(62’) Joe Cole is stripped and ready to come on for the visitors. Allardyce signalling his intent to try and get all three points here. Unless he takes of Maiga of course!
(61’) We have a slight break in play here as a collision between Reid and Cisse leaves both players needing treatment.
(60’) HOW HAS HE MISSED! Nolan finds space between Coloccini and Yanga-Mbiwa but cannot find the target with a free header from eight yards out. You would really expect him to score from there.
(59’) Newcastle have failed to score in five of their last seven matches in the Premier League. Their finishing today suggests this could be their sixth!
(57’) That is lucky for Krul! The keeper comes to claim Downings cross but is unable to hold it under challenge from Maiga. Fortunately for him, there are now claret shirts waiting in the box for a simple finish and he can gather at the second attempt.
(55’) The tempo to the game is starting to rise and now the hosts are looking dangerous. Santo picks up the ball on the left and drives forward. He ducks inside and attempts to curl a shot into the far corner but fails to hit the target.
(53’) Almost! Ben Arfa does well to switch the play from right to left, finding Marveaux on the far side. The midfielder looks to play a one-two with Ameobi but he slips as he goes for the return pass in the area. That could have been a very pretty goal.
(51’) A defensive mix up between Collins and Jaaskelainen almost gifts Cisse with an opportunity to break the deadlock. Fortunately for the visitors, though, the keeper manages to swipe his leg at the ball and clear it into touch.
(50’) The Hammers are now trying to slow down the play a bit and keep hold of the ball in the Newcastle half. They are showing good patience but movement seems to be rather restricted and so Noble ends up sending a pass straight out of play.
(48’) GOOD STOP! Downing manages to find some space in the channel and has the pace to outrun Coloccini and enter the area. He shoots at goal but only looks for the near post, which Krul has covered and gets both hands to the ball.
(47’) Good play early on from Newcastle as Ameobi wins a corner out on the left. The ball is swung in and Coloccini beats Collins to it at the back post, but fails to direct his header on target.
(46’) Here we go, the second half is under way!
Welcome back! The players are back out on the pitch and the second half will commence shortly.
HALF TIME - Newcastle 0-0 West Ham: The visitors have had the better opportunities to break the deadlock but unfortunately for them the best ones fell to centre-back Reid. Pardew's men have still posed a threat, mainly through Sissoko and Ben Arfa, but the game remains goalless. Join me in 15 minutes for the second half.
(45’) The half-time whistle goes!
(45’) We are into the first and only minute of additional time. Newcastle have another opportunity from a set play but Ameobi heads wide from Marveaux's cross.
(45’) A nice delivery from Marveaux finds Coloccini in space at the back post. The Argentine sends the ball back into the danger area with a header but the referee, Phil Dowd, halts play for a foul inside the area from a Newcastle player.
--- 44’ Yellow card J. O'Brien is yellow-carded. ---
(43’) Good play from Ben Arfa again, this time skipping past Nolan 30 yards from goal and sending a left-footed effort towards goal. Once more, though, his aim lets him down and Jaaskelainen watches the ball sail over.
(40’) Newcastle manage to win the ball from another corner, which Ben Arfa won after a brilliant run, but yet again they do not hit the target. It is Sissoko who gets his head to it this time but his hopeful effort goes well wide.
(38’) GREAT CHANCE! Jarvis beats Debuchy for pace down the left and hangs a cross up at the back post. Downing is the man to meet it but there is no conviction in his header, which he puts straight back across goal and out for a goal kick.
(38’) Good defending from Reid! The centre-back does well to stop Ameobi from turning and shooting 20 yards from goal with a quality challenge on the edge of the box.
(36’) Good break from the Magpies as the try to catch West Ham out by attacking straight after their free kick. Cisse does well to bring the ball in from the left and find Anita, but Sissoko's effort from the midfielder's lay of was never going to worry Jaaskelainen.
(34’) GOOD HEADER!! Yanga-Mbiwa gets away from Reid at the near post to get his head to Marveaux's corner, but from such an acute angle it always going to be difficult to find the target, and the defender has no success.
(33’) WHAT A CHANCE!! Unfortunately for the Hammers it again falls to Reid, and he is unable to connect with Collins' long ball forward from a free kick in his own half. Krul can breathe a sigh of relief after that.
(32’) Newcastle have enjoyed no less than 59 per cent possession so far this afternoon. Despite that dominance of the ball, though, they are yet to really test Jaaskelainen and in fact West Ham have actually looked more threatening in the final third.
(30’) Poor delivery from Noble! The midfielder takes a free kick from wide on the left but he fails to beat the first man, Debuchy, who kicks the ball out for a throw.
(28’) Sissoko has been the driving force in Newcastle's midfield and he pushes them forward once more here. Ben Arfa drifts inside to try and get involved in the game but as he is closed down by three West Ham players he opts to shoot. He does not catch the ball well and his attempt rolls wide of the target.
(27’) Jaaskelainen's long ball from deep is flicked on at the edge of the box and Reid manages to find space between Yanga-Mbiwa and Coloccini just outside the six-yard box. He beats Krul to the ball but loops his effort well over the top. Had a more capable finisher been there it could have been a different story.
(25’) A good break from Newcastle sees Marveaux come inside and play the ball out to Ben Arfa, who has acres of space on the left. He takes a few touches to close in on goal before unleashing a rocket of a shot. However, he fails to keep it down and it completely misses the target.
(23’) Demel continues to push forward down the right and once more his delivery is a source of danger to the Newcastle defence. He picks out Jarvis at the back post, who in turn tries to cushion a header down to Nolan. The former Magpies player's touch lets him down, though, and in his haste to win the ball back he concedes a free kick.
(22’) The Hammers are well organised when without the ball this afternoon. Newcastle are finding it difficult to play through the middle and instead opt for a long ball from deep by Anita. He puts too much weight on the pass and West Ham are awarded a goal kick.
(20’) Downing gets onto a loose ball in his own half and looks to dribble at the Newcastle defence. Coloccini backs off but Sissoko tracks him all the way and puts in a strong challenge to dispossess him.
(18’) WIDE OF THE TARGET! Demel does well to push forward down the left and hold off the challenge of Marveaux. He then manages to dig out a cross for Maiga, who rises high in the area but is unable to divert his header on target. That was a great chance for the striker.
(16’) Noble manages to get on the ball for the first time this afternoon but his attempts to find Jarvis on the left ar scuppered as Debuchy reads the pass and intercepts. Little in the way of creativity in the final third from either side so far.
(14’) The resultant corner is headed clear but only as far as Sissoko. The midfielder swings a leg at the ball in an attempt at an ambitious volley. He does not pull it off and sends an awful effort high into the stands.
(13’) CLOSE TO AN OWN GOAL!! Anita wins the ball 35 yards from goal and looks to thread a pass up to Cisse. His aim is slightly off but in his attempts to play it back to his own keeper, Reid almost diverts the ball into the far bottom corner. That would have been seriously embarrassing!
(10’) That is poor from Diame! Sissoko sends a sloppy back pass into his own half and the West Ham midfielder latches onto it. He does not seem to have any ideas on how to beat Yanga-Mbiwa and is tackle easily by the centre-back.
(9’) Jarvis picks up a long ball in behind Debuchy and looks to cut inside of the France international. He manages to knock the ball past him but the referee's assistant has his flag raised for an offside decision.
(7’) WHAT A WASTE!! Ben Arfa is the man to take it and his effort is appalling, flying high over the bar with little chance of ever testing Jaaskelainen.
(6’) Powerful running from Sissoko as he tears through the West Ham midfield, bearing down on goal. Collins comes out to challenge him but he shifts the ball to the right and is brought down by the centre-back's clumsy challenge. A chance to shoot for goal frmo this free kick.
(5’) Not sure how he has managed to win that one! Demel flings a wild leg towards the ball but Cisse manages to get in the way. Rather than see it as a kick, the referee awards the defender a free kick...for some reason.
(3’) GOOD BLOCK!! The resultant corner rolls all the way through to Reid at the back post and the centre-back digs a shot out from under his feet. He tried to bend it inside the goalkeeper's near post but Anita gets a foot in the way and clears the danger.
(2’) Great work from Diame to win the ball in his own half and stride away from his opponent. He carries the ball forward before rolling it out to his left for Jarvis. The wide man races to the byeline but sees his cross deflected behind for a corner.
(1’) We are under way in Newcastle!
The Magpies will be hopeful of an improved result in front of their home fans today after suggering a 4-0 defeat to Manchester City last Monday. West Ham, meanwhile, will be keen to build on their victory over Cardiff. The players are making their way out onto the pitch so we are just a few moments away from kick off.
Sam Allardyce is unable to share his return to face Newcastle with Andy Carroll as the striker is still struggling with an ankle injury. Joe Cole begins on the bench this afternoon despite scoring in the win over Cardiff last weekend.
As you can see there is once more no Yohan Cabaye for Newcastle this afternoon. The Frenchman has been the subject of much speculation regarding his future in the north east and misses out again today. Davide Santon returns, though, and so Mapou Yanga-Mbiwa moves back to his more favoured centre-back position.

West Ham: Jaaskelainen; Demel, Collins, Reid, O’Brien; Noble, Diame; Jarvis, Nolan, Downing; Maiga.

(90’) FULL-TIME! Southampton and Sunderland share the spoils as they draw 1-1 at St. Mary's. The home side dominated the match and generally played well, but their visitors defended excellently and will be pleased with a point, even if they were within grasping distance of the win.
(90’) Southampton desperately pressing for a late winner now. They've less than two minutes to get it!
(90’) Four minutes of stoppage time added.
--- 88’ Assist Assist by J. Ward-Prowse. ---
--- 88’ Goal! GOAL!!! Southampton equalise!! Saints win a free kick just inside their opponents' half and it is fired into the box by Ward-Prowse and Jose Fonte to guides it past Westwood with a glancing header. ---
(88’) There were big expectations as Larsson stepped up to take that, but the Swede could only hit his effort into the wall.
(87’) Excellent play by Johnson as he skips past Chambers and then draws a foul from Ramirez. Sunderland now have a free kick just outside the Saints area.
(85’) Osvaldo is walking a fine line now. The forward fouls Johnson this time and the referee has another word with him.
--- 83’ Yellow card P. Osvaldo receives a yellow card. ---
(83’) Yellow card for debutant Osvaldo as he inexplicably kicks and trips Diakite on the edge of the Sunderland area.
--- 82’ Substitution E. Giaccherini is done for the day. C. Wickham is his replacement. ---
(81’) Well-worked move by Southampton. Ramirez plays a diagonal ball high into the far side of the area. Lambert heads it back across the box for Osvaldo, but he can only head wide via a big bounce off the floor. Osvaldo was not pleased about O'Shea's attentions.
(79’) All-out attack from Saints now. The final 10 minutes approach and they still seek an equaliser. Sunderland have everyone apart from Altidore in defence at the moment.
(78’) Southampton fans enraged as Ramirez skips past Gardner and his knocked over, the referee fails to give the free kick. Bizarre decision.
(76’) Sunderland are afforded a few moments of possession but they completely waste it and invite pressure on to themselves again as Larsson hammers a long diagonal ball out of play.
(74’) The referee seemed to take a long time before allowing that free kick to be played, but eventually Lambert runs up to the ball and smacks it over the wall... And well over the goal too.
(72’) Free kick in an excellent position for the hosts as Ramirez drifts across the Sunderland defence and on to his left foot before getting pushed over by O'Shea.
(70’) We have a pause in play now as Altidore seeks medical attention after banging his head during that corner.
--- 69’ Substitution A. Lallana is done for the day. G. Ramírez is his replacement. ---
(69’) Ramirez is now on for Saints as Lallana comes off. That is a bizarre change in all honesty. Lallana had looked the most likely player to create something.
(68’) THe corner is delivered into the area, but Westwood finds himself with the ball again as Lambert gets another header on goal.
(67’) Clyne has done far more attacking than defending since he came on and he is at it again. He produces a stepover and beats Celustka, runs along the byline before seeing his delivery put behind for a corner.
(65’) Sunderland can hardly get out of their own penalty area at the moment. Southampton's pressure is intense and determined, but they still cannot get that elusive goal.
(63’) This is all Southampton now. Chambers gets forward down the right and produces an excellent curling cross, but Lambert heads at Westwood again.
--- 61’ Yellow card S. Larsson is yellow-carded. ---
(61’) The corner is played into the area and a melee ensues as no one can get the ball under control and Sunderland manage to get it away in scrappy fashion.
(60’) This time it's Lambert who tests Westwood. The forward fell back into the midfield and fired a powerful shot at goal from 20 yards, but the goalkeeper palmed it around the post.
(59’) Sunderland go straight down the other end of the pitch and almost get a second goal. Gardner feeds Altidore into the box and he gets a left-footed shot away, but Boruc came out and met the effort well.
(58’) What a chance for Saints! The elegant Osvaldo comes in from the left-hand side and crosses brilliantly for Rodriguez, but the English forward heads straight at Westwood from five yards out.
(56’) Osvaldo comes deep again and tries to pick out Lambert with a lofted pass with the outside of his foot, but Diakite intercepts.
(55’) Altidore is the latest to try his luck from range, but again the ball soars into the crowd.
--- 53’ Substitution J. Colback is replaced with D. Vaughan. ---
(53’) Saints substitution now as Vaughan comes on for Colback.
(53’) Lallana impresses again as he comes in from the left, skips past one challenge and then holds off O'Shea before laying the ball off for Ward-Prowse. The youngster shoots over with a first-time shot.
(52’) Throw-in for Saints in the final third. Clyne finds Osvaldo who heads towards the area for Lallana to volley at goal, but his effort goes wide of the far post.
(50’) Lallana drifts over to the right and combines well with Chambers before getting trapped in the corner. He tries to trick his way out of the situation and wins a corner.
(49’) First involvement for Osvaldo as he comes deep to collect the ball before chipping a pass out wide for Chambers, but he puts the ball straight out of play.
(47’) Three changes have been made as Clyne and Osvaldo replace Shaw and Schneiderlin for Saints, while Ji replaces Sessegnon for the visitors.
--- 46’ Substitution L. Shaw is replaced with N. Clyne. ---
--- 46’ Substitution S. Sessègnon is replaced with Dong-Won Ji. ---
--- 46’ Substitution P. Osvaldo enters play, replacing M. Schneiderlin. ---
(46’) Here we go. Can Southampton rescue a result from this?
The players are back out for the second half.
(45’) HALF-TIME! The referee blows his whistle for half-time and Sunderland take a well-earned lead into the break. Saints produced plenty of attacks but they did not test Westwood enough in the Sunderland goal.
(45’) Penalty shout again for Saints! This time Lallana holds the ball up in the area and tries to partially turn O'Shea only to be brought down by the Irishman. The referee refuses to give the penalty, however.
(43’) Southampton doing plenty of attacking as they look to equalise before the break, but their play has been far too narrow for the most part. They are offering very little down the flanks.
(40’) Wanyama has looked excellent on the ball at times in this, but a lot of his passing has been off target.
(39’) Ward-Prowse causes havoc again. This time he crosses from the right with his left foot, but Lambert can only head it over at the back post.
(38’) In that passage of play Southampton should probably have been given a penalty. O'Shea held on to Fonte and brought him down in the area, stopping him from connecting with Ward-Prowse's free kick, but the referee failed to spot the foul.
(37’) Ward-Prowse curls in a brilliant delivery and it appears to be heading straight in at the far post. Luckily for Sunderland it evades everyone and Rodriguez's header at the far post is too late as he is already off the pitch.
(36’) However, the hosts now have a free kick on the left as Rodriguez is brought down. Ward-Prowse stands over it.
(35’) Sunderland will be very happy at the moment. Defensively they have been fantastic and very solid until now.
--- 33’ Yellow card C. Gardner receives a yellow card. ---
(33’) Gardner now finds himself in the referee's little black book as he clatters into Shaw. It was not particularly dangerous as he did not go to ground, but the 18-year-old certainly felt that.
(30’) Sunderland are unable to create anything from the resulting free kick and Saints are back in possession.
(29’) Sunderland win themselves a free kick just inside the Southampton half as Lambert is adjudged to have fouled Diakite.
(28’) Eye-catching play at the back by Southampton as they play their way out of a stick situation. Altidore took up possession in the area and tried to lift the ball over defenders for Sessegnon, but Lovren is there to clear up.
--- 27’ Yellow card J. Ward-Prowse is cautioned by the referee. ---
(27’) And there is the first yellow card of the afternoon. Colback bursts in front of Ward-Prowse who trips the Sunderland man and gets booked.
(25’) Southampton are generally controlling this but they are struggling to create clear-cut chances, while their visitors look solid at the back and dangerous on the rare occasions that they get forward.
(23’) Unfortunately for Saints the following corner comes to little and Sunderland hack it away.
(22’) Southampton's pressure continues. Ward-Prowse manages to get through several challenges in the right side of the area thanks to ricochets. Eventually the ball drops to Rodriguez, but O'Shea deflects it just wide of the goal.
(21’) Westwood makes a good save as he gets down to his right and palms Lambert's header around the post.
(20’) Fierce delivery from Larsson again as he gets devastating whip on the ball and Boruc has to dive across his goal and punch it away just before it can get inside the post.
(19’) Encouraging play from Sunderland as they advance down the left. Colback plays Altidore down the line before receiving the ball back again and winning a corner.
(17’) Saints get themselves a free kick 30 yards from goal but it is wasted as Lambert hammers it into the wall and then Wanyama is forced to pass all the way back to Boruc.
(16’) Southampton can't quite get their moves and passes to connect at the moment. Lambert brings the ball down well inside Sunderland's area, but Celustka is there to put his foot in again.
(15’) Lambert searches for Lallana on the left flank. He outmuscles Celustka and then turns the full-back, but he gets back and produces a very important tackle before taking the ball away.
(14’) Wanyama's pass inside from the right is a little slack and Giaccherini manages to catch Schneiderlin in possession straight after receiving the ball, but the covering Fonte is able to bail his teammate out.
(12’) Chambers is involved again, but this time his clearance is blocked by Giaccherini and it almost drops to Altidore in the area, but luckily for the young Saints man Boruc is quick off his line.
(11’) Chambers gives away a free kick for an unfair tackle on Colback, but the hosts' intensity has been very good until now.
(9’) The hosts are really pressing for an equaliser now. Schneiderlin almost gets a cross in from the right, but Sunderland defending well so far.
(7’) Replays show the offside decision again and it was incredibly close, but the officials appear to have made the correct call. Excellent start to proceedings here.
(6’) Southampton thought they had pulled level, but their celebrations are painfully cut short. Lambert played a through-ball behind the visitors' defence for Rodriguez to stroke home, but the young English forward was slightly offside.
(5’) Sunderland's impressive start continues as Colback attacks down the left, but Fonte is alert to the danger and he allows the ball to run out of play for a goal kick.
--- 3’ Assist S. Larsson provided the assist. ---
--- 3’ Goal! GOAL!!! Sunderland take the lead at St. Mary's! After a brilliant free kick delivery, Larsson betters himself with an exquisite corner and Emanuele Giaccherini heads it past Boruc! ---
(3’) Positive start for the visitors. They win a free kick on the left and Seb Larsson delivers excellently, but Southampton put it behind for a corner.
(1’) Off we go! Southampton get the match started.
The teams are out and almost ready to go.
And the Sunderland team is: Westwood; Celustka, O’Shea, Diakite, Colback; Johnson, Larsson, Gardner, Giaccherini; Sessegnon, Altidore. Subs: Mannone, Cabral, Wickham, Vaughan, Ji, Moberg Karlsson, Roberge.

Stoke have their first win of the season after coming from a goal down to beat Premier League new-boys Crystal Palace 2-1. Chamakh put the visitors ahead with a neat goal but the forward won't be receiving much praise from his manager after a poor clearance and less-than-half-hearted tackle that lead to the Potters winner. Adam firstly but the hosts level, pouncing on the loose ball to finish well, before Shawcross got the better of the former Arsenal man to net the winner. On balance Hughes' men probably deserved their win, though the Londoners did look good in patches.
(90’) The referee blows the full-time whistle!
(90’) Stoke try and keep it in the corner but Palace win it back via a throw in. However they give the ball away and almost allow Pennant in.
(90’) The Potters come forward with Cameron Jerome but Williams gets back and forces it out for a corner.
(90’) Four minutes added on in Stoke.
(90’) A flowing Palace move ends with Begovic once more claiming the ball high after Moxey's cross from the left.

(77’) Kevin Phillips gets his first sight of goal but drags the shot wide of the post.

Palace lead 1-0 at the Britannia as we head into the half-time break. Holloway's men might have had a penalty when Etherington shoved Ward to the floor inside the Stoke 18-yard box, however they were eventually rewarded for some neat football just after the hour-hour mark when Chamakh capitalised on some woeful Potters defending. There was nothing woeful about the Moroccan's finish, though, the forward beating Begovic with a cool shot into the corner. Speroni acrobatically kept Crouch out seconds later, tipping his header onto the bar, but it's been the visitors who have had the better of the play since the goal.

A quick match fact for you before kick-off, which is moments away: Stoke beat Palace 4-1 in an FA Cup third-round replay last season. Let's see if they can reproduce that form this afternoon.
Potters keeper Asmir Begovic impressed during that match at Anfield, keeping the score at 1-0 with numerous fantastic saves. Will he be kept busy by the visiting attackers this afternoon? Holloway will be hoping on-loan winger Puncheon and summer signing from Arsenal Chamakh can threaten, handing both starts.
Now, penalties played a big part in both teams' last fixtures - Stoke's Jonathan Walters missing a late one against Liverpool, while Spurs' only goal in their win over the Eagles came from the spot. Will we see any more this afternoon?

Liverpool are nine games unbeaten in the league, but Lambert's side are keen to show their impressive attacking style that saw them beat Arsenal, and push Chelsea all the way on Wednesday.
And Liverpool boss Brendan Rodgers is wary of the threats the hosts pose: "They are very much a counterattacking team that set up to defend half a pitch and then break out with the pace of Benteke, [Gabriel] Agbonlahor in particular and young Andreas Weimann on the side but our focus is really on our own game."
The Villans will be hoping for a first win at home against Liverpool since the final day of the 2011 season, with Liverpool prevailing 3-1 and 2-1 in both of their last visits to Villa Park. Christian Benteke scored three times against the Reds last year, however.
But nevertheless, Lambert, with top scorer Benteke line-up against a Liverpool side who started their season with a narrow 1-0 win over Stoke City. The Rodgers revolution continues at Anfield, where their new signings, particularly Iago Aspas and Simon Mignolet have looked rather sharp against the Potters last weekend.
Aston Villa, it's safe to say, have been the most talked about side in the league since the big kick-off last weekend. (27’) Fantastic play from Connolly as he swings an early cross in for Campbell, but the flag goes up. Replays show the striker may have been level, so the visitors get lucky with that one.
(26’) Toure looks OK to continue and play gets going once more as Campbell knocks the drop-ball through to Hart.
(25’) Dzeko isn't happy after an old-fashioned shoulder charge from Gunnarsson dispossesses him. Meanwhile, Toure is down receiving treatment, giving the Cardiff players a chance to take a drink.
(23’) Cardiff's early energy has petered out somewhat. The visitors are playing a very high line, passing it across the back with the defence camped in the Cardiff half.
(21’) Lovely stuff from Aguero and Silva sees the latter dart into the box and drill a low ball across goal, but Taylor reads it well and clears from in front of Marshall.
(20’) Bellamy is upended in midfield and the hosts have a chance to keep some possession. The Wales man has been running for everything so far today.
(18’) Man City are doing a good job of stifling the hosts, now, just keeping the ball and moving it around patiently. David Silva makes a run around the back and wins a corner for the visitors, which the hosts clear before it's fired back in towards Dzeko, who heads well wide of the target.
(16’) Whittingham fires a low shot from distance straight at Hart, while Gary Medel and Gunnarsson both feel the force of tackles in midfield, but both look happy to continue.
(14’) Pellegrini's men are just starting to take control of things here. Navas thinks about a shot from distance but checks and spreads the play wide, before it comes back in towards Yaya Toure who wastes all that good possession and puts it out of play for a goal kick.
(13’) Jesus Navas has had a couple of forays down the right-hand side already today, and the winger forces a corner for the visitors, which Caulker does well to head clear.
(11’) Chance! Aron Gunnarsson picks the ball up in the Man City half, and promptly ends up on the floor after a challenge from Yaya Toure. Whittingham's free kick causes some real trouble as Steven Caulker diverts the ball towards goal, forcing a superb low save from Hart before the flag goes up for offside in the aftermath.
(10’) It's an absolutely pulsating atmosphere inside the stadium, but on the pitch things have just slowed down a touch after that frenetic start. David Marshall has to rush out to clear a short backpass with Aguero bearing down on him.
(8’) Matthew Connolly gives it straight to Sergio Aguero, but immediately there are four red shirts around the striker and Cardiff win the ball back.
(6’) So close! Peter Whittingham swings a beautiful curling free kick around the wall and it whistles past Joe Hart's near post. A narrow escape for the visitors, there.
(5’) Joleon Lescott gives it away and Cardiff push forward through Bellamy. Bo-Kyung Kim holds off the defender with a good show of strength, winning the hosts a free kick for his troubles.
(3’) Campbell - who's looking very lively today - tries to break through the middle, but Javi Garcia stops the striker in his tracks.
(2’) Real early drama as Craig Bellamy bursts down the right flank and hammers a dangerous cross in. The ball comes towards Fraizer Campbell who appeals for a penalty after a clumsy challenge by Fernandinho, but the referee isn't interested. A breathless start.
(1’) We're underway in Wales as Cardiff get the game going.
The Bluebirds - in red - get together for a huddle. We're moments away from kick-off in Cardiff.
The players march out of the tunnel to be confronted by an absolute wall of noise. The crowd are really up for this one. Could the hosts spring a surprise this afternoon?
An obligatory hat-tip for Yaya Toure, who is captaining Man City today on his 100th Premier League start for the club.
Edin Dzeko has been speaking to Sky Sports ahead of the match, hinting that he's happy with the start he and City have made to the season: "I have a lot of confidence especially with the new manager and the way the team is playing this year. We showed in the first game against Newcastle how we want to play this season, we just have to keep going. He [boss Manuel Pellegrini] called me before pre-season and told me he counts on me and wants me to stay here and he wants me to do my best. I'm trying to do my best on the pitch."
So, no Vincent Kompany for the visitors, as Manuel Pellegrini drafts Javi Garcia into the City defence after the Belgium defender picked up an injury in Monday's win over Newcastle. Meanwhile, Andrew Taylor comes back into the Cardiff back line at the expense of Declan John, and new signing Andreas Cornelius could make his Bluebirds debut from the bench.
MAN CITY: Hart; Zabaleta, Garcia, Lescott, Clichy; Navas, Fernandinho, Toure, Silva; Dzeko, Aguero. // Subs: Pantilimon, Nastasic, Kolarov, Rodwell, Milner, Nasri, Negredo
CARDIFF: Marshall; Connolly, Caulker, Turner, Taylor; Medel, Kim, Gunnarsson; Whittingham, Campbell, Bellamy. // Subs: Lewis, Hudson, Cornelius, Noone, Mutch, Cowie, Maynard.
The teams are in, so let's take a look, starting with the hosts...

So Tottenham join Chelsea and Liverpool on six points at the top of the table after two weeks of the Premier League season. Swansea still without a point. I've been Tom Maston, and thanks for joining me.
The penalty incident will be looked at again and again, though with the spot kick that wasn't given in the first half it was no more than Andre Villas Boas' men deserved. For Swansea, it's two defeats from two admittedly difficult opening fixtures.
And there it is. Neil Swarbrick blows the final whistle and Spurs hold out for their second 1-0 win in as many weeks. It was again a Roberto Soldado penalty that sealed the points for the North London outfit.
(90’) Spurs now have everyone in their own half defending this narrow lead. Rangel absolutley livid with the referee as a free-kick is given to the hosts. One minute to go.
(90’) Spurs almost wrap it up as Paulinho breaks through but can't chip Vorm before flashing the rebound over. Swansea throwing everyone forward in search of an equaliser.
(90’) Tottenham in possession and keeping the ball in the corner. For a side as good as their's that's a bit defensive but three points are three points at the end of the day. Four minutes added time to come.
--- 88’ Substitution Townsend, whose fall in the box will dominate the headlines, is the man withdrawn for Sandro. Two minutes left of normal time. ---
(87’) Sandro being readied to help the Spurs defensive effort as Swansea keep pushing but with no end product. Time running out for Laudrup's men.
(85’) Swansea still looking for that killer ball over the top but with Shelvey now off the field they are struggling to find it. Need to try get Hernandez on the ball as much as possible as he has been their brightest spark in the second half.
(83’) Swansea looking the more likely in the last ten minutes, but can't quite find that clear sight of goal. Spurs looking to hit on the counter now.
(81’) de Guzman looks for Bony at the back post but the striker can't control his header and the ball trickles out for a goal kick.
--- 80’ Substitution Before that is taken, though, there is a standing ovation for goalscorer Soldado as he is replaced by Defoe. ---
(80’) Free-kick to Swansea on the left as Walker brings down Hernandez. Chance for Swansea to throw some men forward.
(78’) Townsend and Walker again combine down the right and it's only a good tackle from Hernandez that denies the right-back a chance of getting in another cross. The English pair have been excellent this afternoon.
--- 76’ Yellow card First Spurs booking as Soldado brings down Pozuelo after some lovely trickery in midfield. Free-kick comes to nothing despite Bony's presence. ---
(75’) Brilliance from Hernandez gets him past Walker, and the Spaniard gets a sight of goal as he continues his run. His shot is blocked, but ricochets back off him and almost over Lloris' head. Goalkeeper does well to catch.
--- 73’ Yellow card Some great hold-up play by Soldado eventually draws a foul from Williams, with the defender picking up Swansea's fourth booking of the afternoon. ---
(72’) That man Bony wins a free-kick, and after it is taken short, Hernandez swings over a cross to Chico at the back post. The defender unleashes a ferocious volley that Lloris does well to tip over the bar.
(71’) Swansea have certainly been much better since the goal, and the introduction of Bony should give them some more bite up front.
--- 69’ Substitution Better from Swansea as Shelvey and Hernandez combine before the latter tries to bend one around Lloris but sees his effort go just wide. That was Shelvey's last action as record signing Bony replaces the midfielder. ---
(68’) Townsend's original free-kick is blocked by the wall, and in trying to redeem himself he slices a shot high and wide of Vorm's goal. Into the final quarter in North London.
(67’) Williams penalised as Vertonghen somehow ends up on the right wing and is brought down by the Swansea skipper. Chance for Spurs to get bodies into the box.
--- 65’ Substitution Superb break from Townsend, who has been a real threat for Spurs this afternoon. Good challenge from Chico stops him in his path. Sigurdsson now on in place of Dembele. ---
(62’) You can't say Spurs haven't deserved that goal, but the decision to award the penalty was a poor one from referee Swarbrick. Former Swansea man Sigurdsson being readied on the Spurs bench.
--- 59’ Substitution Change for Swansea on the back of conceding that goal as Pozuelo replaces Routledge. Bony still waits on the bench. ---
--- 58’ Goal! GOAL!!! For the second week running, Soldado has made no mistake from 12 yards. Placing the ball to Vorm's left, the goalkeeper went the wrong way. Spurs should have had a penalty in the first half, but probably shouldn't have had one in the second. Nevertheless, Spurs 1-0 up. ---
(57’) PENALTY! Shelvey on Townsend again, and this time Swarbrick points to the spot. Great break from the winger but it looks like the contact was minimal. Soldado to step up...
(57’) Swansea playing some nice stuff as de Guzman looks for Hernandez breaking through. Vertonghen gets back though and clears the danger.
(55’) Swansea bring it forward through Hernandez before finding Michu advancing on goal. The striker looks set to fire in on goal when Dawson comes across and makes an excellent tackle. Opportunity missed for Laudrup's side.
(54’) SO CLOSE! He scored a superb goal in Europe on Thursday, and Townsend almost had another one there as he cut onto his left foot and let fly from distance. Vorm was struggling and the ball flew just over the top, thankfully for the Dutch goalkeeper.
(52’) Quieter opening to the second half compared to the pace of the opening 45 minutes. Rose tries to get Soldado in over the top but the ball skips away from him and into Vorm's waiting arms. Swansea holding firm.
(50’) Vertonghen gets into a bit of a mess at the heart of Tottenham's defence, but Swansea can't find the killer pass to make him pay. Let off for the big Belgian.
(48’) Walker is again giving Davies a torrid time as he gets in behind the left-back yet again. Williams is there though to clear his low cross.
(46’) Swansea get us back underway here with the game remaining goalless.
Players making their way back out onto the pitch in North London. All eyes on referee Neil Swarbrick after his poor decision just before the break.
Not long now until we are back underway at White Hart Lane. The deadlock is yet to be broken but Tottenham couldn't have done much more to take the lead. Lloris has made a couple of good saves at the other end, but Spurs will be happy with the way they went about their business in the first period.
So, after that first half, you would be a brave man to bet against Tottenham eventually finding the back of the net. Michel Vorm has been inspired in the Swansea goal and will need to keep up his great form if Swansea are to come away with anything. I'll be back for the second half in ten minutes time.
(45’) Walker's low free-kick is easily cleared and Swansea see out the sole minute of stoppage time with relative ease. Spurs well on top and should have had a penalty. Swansea look dangerous but have been second-best for much of the opening 45 minutes.
(44’) Appeals for a penalty as Townsend is brought down by Shelvey. The foul is clearly inside the box but the referee only awards a free-kick on the edge of the are. Contentious one.
(43’) Townsend cuts inside from the right and has options in the area. He only has eyes for goal, though, and fires a weak effort straight at Vorm.
(42’) Villas-Boas' side still on top though Swansea holding firm in the middle of the park. Can they find the breakthrough before half-time?
--- 40’ Yellow card Michu gives away a free-kick halfway into the Swansea half and is booked for his troubles. Big striker looking very frustrated so far this afternoon. ---
(38’) At the other end de Guzman breaks from midfield and shoots from around 25 yards. A slight deflection takes it wide, though the referee signals for a goal kick, much to Swansea's frustration.
(37’) Walker is proving a real threat down the right as yet another cross is palmed away by Vorm. The ball eventually falls for Chadli on the left, and his centre is volleyed into the ground by Paulinho and just over the bar. Spurs doing everything but score.
(35’) GREAT SAVE! Vorm again to the rescue as Walker again gets to the byline before finding Dembele at the back post. The midfielder aims for the top corner but the goalkeeper tips his curling effort over the bar. Dawson heads over from the resulting corner.
(34’) Finally a minute to breath as Spurs play the ball around in midfield. Been a frantic first-half.
(32’) Great skill by Paulinho gets him past Shelvey before he fires in another shot from distance which rolls harmlessly wide. Brazilian midfielder showing great promise.
--- 31’ Yellow card A pass sells Shelvey short and the midfielder trips Soldado, though he may have got some of the ball. Vorm booked for dissent towards the referee as Spurs get another chance to create something. ---
(31’) Townsend whips in the free-kick and Capoue beats Davies in the air. His header is only a flick-on though and it bounces wide of Vorm's right-hand post.
(28’) Routledge is freed down the right but he loses his footing and Spurs can clear his weak cross looking for Michu. Big Spaniard not really been involved as yet.
(26’) Spurs switch off from a throw-in and Shelvey can cut in from the left. His low effort is deflected and Lloris tips it behind. The resulting corner is cleared but Tottenham have to be careful despite their dominance.
(25’) Walker just fails to lay in Townsend down the right. Closer viewing of that Paulinho effort shows Williams blocked the effort on the line before Vorm grasped at the ball.
(23’) All Tottenham as Rose gets in down the left-hand side and fires in a low cross. A deflection sends into the waiting arms of Vorm though and the danger is gone, for now.
(21’) OFF THE POST! Ashley Williams gets away with one as he heads Walker's driven cross against his own goal frame. The ball then falls for Paulinho, but Vorm somehow hangs onto his rasping drive. Spurs the better side here.
(19’) Shelvey looking to play diagonal balls at every opportunity for Laudrup's side, and he pings another delightful pass towards Routledge on the left. The former Spurs man is, alas, offside. Still goalless.
--- 17’ Yellow card Sloppy defending from Rangel gives it away to Townsend on the edge of the area. He is then brought down by Davies, who is booked, and Spurs have a chance from a dead ball. ---
(17’) Three Tottenham men standing over it, but it's Chadli who strikes it. Not a bad effort from the Belgium international but he can't get enough dip and Vorm is untroubled.
(15’) Paulinho and Capoue already forming a dynamic partnership in midfield. The former this time is at the centre of things as he wins a free-kick inside the centre circle.
(13’) Swansea aren't here just to defend. Rangel tries to get in behind after ball over the top but Lloris is out quickly to collect the ball.
(11’) Shots starting to rain in now Capoue again wins the ball in midfield before marauding forward and shooting from fully 40 yards. Vorm right behind the low effort.
(9’) GREAT SAVE! Some neat interplay from Swansea gets in Michu in behind, and though Walker gets back, Hernandez forces Lloris into a good parried stop from just outside the area.
(8’) Paulinho looking bright in the opening stages, and after Capoue wins the ball in midfield, the Brazilian gets in a low shot which doesn't have enough power to really trouble Vorm in the Swansea goal.
(6’) Our first sighting of Paulinho sees him winning the ball and driving forward. Swansea get back in numbers though and extinguish the danger.
(4’) As is Swansea's way , they are looking to keep the ball in the middle of the pitch. Plenty of pressing from Tottenham early on as they look to disrupt their visitors.
(2’) A pair of early corners for Tottenham who look to gain some initiative from the off. Easily cleared by the Welsh outfit though.
(1’) After a slight delay waiting for the referee, we are underway.
We are all set here for kick-off. Tottenham will be kicking-off in their traditional white shirts and dark shorts. Swansea in blue and yellow.
Great reception for the two sides as they enter the arena at White Hart Lane. The obligatory handshakes pass by without incident, and we are just moments from getting underway.
The teams are in the tunnel in London as Tottenham look to make it two wins on the bounce to start the campaign. Swansea on the other hand aiming to pick up their first points of the new season.
Of course there is no Gareth Bale for the hosts today as his protracted move to Real Madrid moves ever closer. Spurs were efficent if not at their best against Crystal Palace last week, and how they perform today could be an indication as to how they will cope without the Welsh wizard. Just under ten minutes till kick-off now.
Both these sides are returning to domestic matters after European exploits in midweek, and after both found the net no less than five times, both attacks are certainly on form. Defenders will certainly have to be on their toes from minute one at White Hart Lane.
After their 4-1 defeat to Manchester United, Michael Laudrup recalls Jonathan de Guzman and Pablo Hernandez in place of Leon Britton and Nathan Dyer. Wilfried Bony must again sit on the bench despite his strike last week.
Andre Villas-Boas hands a first Premier League start to Etienne Capoue while Andros Townsend comes in on the right wing. Gylfi Sigurdsson and Aaron Lennon are those replaced.
Swansea: Vorm, Rangel, Chico, Williams, Davies, Routledge, Shelvey, de Guzman, Hernandez, Michu, Canas.Subs: Tremmel, Amat, Britton, Pozuelo, Richards, Bony, Lamah.
Tottenham: Lloris, Walker, Dawson, Vertonghen, Rose, Capoue, Paulinho, Dembele, Townsend, Chadli, Soldado.Subs: Friedel, Kaboul, Naughton, Sigurdsson, Carroll, Sandro, Defoe.

Next up for Manchester United is a mouthwatering game against Liverpool at Anfield in the Premier League. While Jose Mourinho's men gear up to face Pep Guardiola's Bayern Munich in the European Super Cup.
No real hint as to where the Premier League title is heading after tonight's stalemate. David Moyes' was bold in picking Wayne Rooney but that's where the brave decisions ended for both sides. Neither manager was prepared to risk a draw in order to go for the win, as both adopted cautious approaches.
Liverpool and Tottenham are the only two teams with a hundred per cent records but it's Chelsea who sit on top of the Premier League, having played a game more than their rivals.
FULL-TIME: Manchester United 0-0 Chelsea
(90’) The corner is swung into the box but Chelsea manage to get the ball out of the danger zone at the second time of asking.
--- 90’ +3 Substitution Azpilicueta comes on for E. Hazard. ---
(90’) CHANCE! Manchester have one last surge forward as Wayne Rooney comes away with the ball in midfield. He turns one way than the other before laying the ball out to Ashley Young on the right flank. The winger's cross is cut out at the front post. Corner to United...
(90’) If things stay as they are it's Chelsea who will move to the top of the table having played a game more than everyone else, apart from Aston Villa.
(89’) Chelsea look happy with a point as they casually knock the ball about in deep areas. There will be three minutes of added time.
--- 87’ Substitution A. Schürrle is done for the day. J. Obi Mikel is his replacement. ---
(87’) SCRAMBLE! Phil Jones crosses into the box, Cahill gets his head to hit but it only falls as far as Van Persie. His volley hits Mikel's arm at point-blank range before Patrice Evra flings his volley well wide of the far post. Heart in mouths on the Blues bench.
(85’) Fernando Torres and Oscar try to combine in attack for the Blues but the pair are heavily outnumbered by Manchester United defenders. The tempo has seeped out of this affair following Evra's injury.
(83’) There will be a lengthy delay in the proceeding as Patrice Evra lays on the deck and recieves treatement from the United doctor. A chance for the players to catch their breath and prepare for a push in the final ten minutes. Plenty of time should be added on.
--- 80’ Yellow card Fernando Torres is yellow-carded. ---
(80’) STAT ATTACK: Juan Mata has scored in each of the last three Premier League games between Chelsea and Manchester United. He remains on the bench tonight though.
--- 78’ Substitution D. Welbeck is done for the day. R. Giggs is his replacement. ---
(78’) STAT ATTACK: Ryan Giggs comes on for his 50th Manchester United appearance against Chelsea alone.
(77’) SAVE! Wayne Rooney fires a trademark right-footed cannonball from 35 yards out at Petr Cech but the Chelsea goalkeeper gets across well to palm it away for a corner, which results in nothing.
(75’) Wayne Rooney tracks back right the way into his own half and makes a superb sliding challenge on Ramires before finding Van Persie with a long ball which gets United on the attack. Ashley Young strays offside when he recieves the ball a moment later to end the momentum.
(73’) SAVE! Ashley Young delivers two dangerous crosses into the box, the second of which causes Petr Cech to come out and parry away the ball. Manchester United look a better attacking proposition following the introduction of the England winger.
(72’) PENALTY SHOUT! Ashley Cole nutmegs Phil Jones right on the edge of the area and then goes down as he flys past him and into the box. Jones' hand did come out in Cole's direction but the referee again waves away the protests.
(70’) The passing in the final third from both sides is horrendously below their usual standards. Both sides are struggling to fine any sort of rhythm.
(68’) Antonio Valencia saw plenty of the ball in this game but was beginning to draw some moans and groans from the home crowd. David Moyes does what he is paid to do and hauls him off for Ashley Young.
--- 66’ Substitution A. Valencia is replaced with A. Young. ---
(66’) Manchester United are pressing and probing in the final third but as of yet are finding it very difficult to carve this resolute Chelsea defence open. Replays suggest the earlier penalty shout would have been harsh.
(64’) First Fernando Torres bursts into the Manchester United half before tamely surrendering he ball to Rio Ferdinand. He then launches Manchester United on to the attack via Valencia. Significant increase in noise and tempo inside Old Trafford now.
(62’) CONTROVERSY! Tom Cleverly hits a half-volley from the edge of the area and it appears to strike the arm of John Terry who charges down the shot. Referee Mike Atkinson is having none of it.
(61’) I have to say more of you asked for the introduction of Fernando Torres ahead of Romelu Lukaku over on Twitter. Your wish is Mourinho's command as the Spaniard replaces De Bruyne.
--- 60’ Substitution K. De Bruyne is replaced with Fernando Torres. ---
(60’) OFFSIDE CALL! Andre Schurrle is fed through on goal and rattles the crossbar with a shot but is flagged offside. A very, very narrow call it was, though.
(59’) SHOT! Gary Cahill strikes a vicious effort from about 35 yards with the outside of his boot but David de Gea watches it all the way and makes a fine save.
(58’) Antonio Valencia zooms past Ashley Cole but then casually prods the ball into the path of Phil Jones, who with his back turned, allows Gary Cahill to come and steal the ball away. Big chance for the visitors, that.
(56’) CHANCE! Welbeck again! Rooney feeds Welbeck inside the box and the striker has time to turn and settle himself as John Terry slips. Unfortunately he rushes his effort and and digs a shot over the bar.
(54’) SHOT! Michael Carrick sprays a ball out to Danny Welbeck on the left flank and the England striker is invited to cut inside by Robin van Persie's crossover run. Welbeck obliges but then only curls his shot, aimed for the top corner, high into the stands.
(52’) Eden Hazard crashes in a shot from distance that David de Gea saves comfortably. Good handling from the Spaniard. Chelsea beginning to edge back in terms of possession percentage.
(50’) Chelsea are being pegged back in their own half. Patrice Evra breaks through central mdifield and Chelsea back-off allowing him space to shoot. Instead, the left-back looks for Danny Welbeck and finds him, but the striker attempts to flick the ball back to his team-mate allowing Cahill to intervene.
(48’) CHANCE! Patrice Evra's cross into the box sails all the way to Antonio Valencia at the back post but the winger takes an age to decide what to do, in which time Chelsea get back in numbers and the chance dissipates.
(46’) Manchester United get us underway in the second half!
The teams are out of the tunnel for the second half and we are moments away from the beginning of the second half.
STAT ATTACK: Manchester Utd have lost five of the last nine Premier League games where they've gone in 0-0 at half-time (via OptaJoe).
Quick straw pall, if you were going to replace Andre Schurrle in attack for the second period, who do you go for - Romelu Lukaku or Fernando Torres? Send in your thoughts to @HushKerai.
@gonwudiwe: "Why are Chelsea playing without a natural striker? Are they trying to reinvent Jose Mourinho's negative football style?" This is a popular view amongst many Chelsea supporters.
@katangatimothy: "caution by both teams with the two defensive midfielders." - That could be one of the reasons behind that toothless first 45 minutes.
Not a lot in the form of goalscoring chances in the first half at Old Trafford. It's all been a bit tentative and cautious from David Moyes' and Jose Mourinho's respective sides. Chelsea need a striker and perhaps the introduction of Mata to shake things up. But that might just open things up for the hosts...
HALF-TIME: Manchester United 0-0 Chelsea
(45’) Chelsea have a throw-in deep inside the Manchester United half but they unadventurously play the backk all the way back to their defence. Ramires eventually goes forward with it but his cross into the area was a waste of time considering no team-mate had made an effort to get in the box.
(43’) SHOT! Oscar has another go at goal this time following a nice series of short passes from the visitors. Hazard's lay-off was met by the Brazilian at the edge of the area but the shot had no power or direction and David de Gea gathered easily.
(40’) Kevin De Bruyne looks to pick out Hazard on the right but plays the ball straight out of play. It's been that type of half for the Blues. Wayne Rooney then looks for Robin van Persie over the top but, he too, overhits his pass.
(38’) HALF CHANCE! Tom Cleverely eventually fires the ball over the crossbar from range after series of Manchester United crosses had Chelsea defending nervously for a bit. Terry and Cahill have been immense for the visitors so far.
(36’) This is a game which will delight those who you who are more inclined to appreciate team shape and tacitical defending. Not much in terms of excitement in terms of attacking action, yet.
(34’) STAT ATTACK: Jose Mourinho has lost just two of his seven competitive games as a manager at Old Trafford. That's including his time at Porto, Inter and Real Madrid, as well as his first stint with the Blues.
--- 32’ Yellow card K. De Bruyne receives a yellow card. ---
(32’) Kevin De Bruyne has blood flowing from his mouth following an altercation with Phil Jones but the Manchester United man gets the free kick. The match is beginning to open up.
(30’) CHANCE! Eden Hazard flies forward down the right-hand side before flashing a ball across the pitch. Kevin de Bruyne and Andre Schurrle both miss the ball as it whizzes past behind their runs.
(28’) SHOT! Wayne Rooney has his first effort of the game. It's a tame one from the edge of the area as he tried to guide the ball through the narrowest of holes. No question about the striker's commitment, though.
(26’) First ramblings of 'Jose Mourinho' eminate from the Chelsea supporters high up in the away end at Old Trafford.
(25’) Now Manchester United are piling on some pressure with Patrice Evra doing well to surge up the left flank. After some assured build-up the defender crosses into the box, looking for Van Persie, but his ball has just a bit too much pace on it. United on the up!
(23’) Half a chance as Robin van Persie does well to get a shot at goal under close attention from Ivanovic. The Dutchman worked an effort from a tight angle but could only send his strike into the side netting.
(22’) Finally, a flowing move from the Chelsea midfield. It all starts with some fine running by Andre Schurrle to salvage a lost caust ends with De Bruyne's first-time lay-off for Oscar. The Brazilian goes for  first-time effort himself but slices the shot wide.
(20’) No sign of the passing and interchange which was on show in Chelsea's opening game of the season. It's not very neat or tidy from either side at the moment, unfortunately.
(18’) Branislav Ivanovic gets forward from right-back and goes for a ambitous strike from range but only succeeds in earning a big ironic cheer from the home crowd.
(17’) That last move has finally injected some life into the Old Trafford crowd. Meanwhile, Jose Mourinho can't find his pen on the touchline.
(16’) CHANCE! Robin van Persie finds Wayne Rooney on the right flank in acres of space before making a break to get into the area. The England striker whips a right-footed cross into the area but John Terry does just enough to prevent the Dutchman from getting on the end of it.
(14’) It looked promising for Chelsea as De Bruyne found Hazard in space on the left but the Blues midfielder hesitated for too long on the ball before sailing a cross high over his team-mates head. Should have done better from that.
(13’) Robin van Persie swings one into the box from the corner but John Terry gets up high, unchallenged, and heads the ball clear.

Things started brightly for the Gunners with Olivier Giroud's early opener, but Wojciech Szczesny gave away a penalty which Christian Benteke converted on the rebound after the Poland shot-stopper saved the spot-kick. Laurent Koscielny then gave away another (harsh) spot-kick in the second half and saw red minutes later after Benteke made no mistake from the spot this time round, while Antonio Luna capped a dream debut with a nonchalant finish late on.
And that's it! Aston Villa shock Arsenal by taking a 3-1 victory at the Emirates, and the home crowd are not happy at all. Arsene Wenger may contest the key decisions, but since the first penalty conceded the Gunners began to unravel badly, in terms of both tactics and discipline.

(41’) Rosicky feeds Walcott down the right and the forward pulls it back at the byline for Giroud, but the striker can't find the room to finish. The half started well for the Gunners, but it's beginning to unwravel a little now.
(39’) Ooh, Agbonlahor is hopping up and down here as he is wide open on the right, but Delph fails to find him with a simple through-ball. Arsenal's defence is a little porous at the moment.
(37’) What is Szczesny doing?! The Arsenal 'keeper sprints way, way out but doesn't deal with a long ball, and Benteke tries to round him from 40 yards. He loses out but Ashley Westwood thinks he's Eric Cantona goes for a 40-yards chip, which the shot-stopper has to scramble back to acrobatically tip wide. My, my...
(36’) Oxlade-Chamberlain gallops forward towardas the Villa goal but his pass is behind Jenkinson, who can't find a team-mate with a low pass from the right.
(34’) Close for Walcott! There's a mix-up between Luna and Guzan here with neither willing to claim the ball, and Walcott pinches the ball from the clutches of a prone Guzan - but he can't find Giroud properly to tap into an empty net. A waste there.
(33’) The Arsenal crowd sarcastically applaud getting a free-kick here - they feel hard done by, but they haven't got a case over the penalty.
(31’) Guzan flies out to punch the free-kick away - and Villa are almost through here! Delph wastes the ball with Weimann clear through - it was a great block by captain Per Mertesacker in truth.
--- 30’ Yellow card R. Vlaar goes into the referee's book. ---
--- 30’ Yellow card J. Wilshere is cautioned by the referee. ---
(30’) Everybody's getting tetchy now as Ron Vlaar flies into a block tackle with Wilshere to cause a mass scuffle, and the defender gets a yellow card for his troubles. Taylor will have to calm things down a little here beforew somebody gets sent off.
--- 28’ Substitution C. Jenkinson enters the game and replaces K. Gibbs. ---
(28’) Carl Jenkinson is on for Gibbs, as the injury is too close to his eye to continue.
(27’) The break in play for Gibbs gives us a moment to go back to the penalty - referee Taylor played the advantage, but with Arsenal players scrambling back to block Weimann's follow-up, the official had no choice but to point to the spot. Wenger didn't look pleased, but that's football.
(25’) Kieran Gibbs is a bloody mess here as Weimann catches him with his head in an aerial collision. Blood is streaming down his face and the left-back looks in some discomfort.
(24’) Giroud is furious at giving away a free-kick in the Villa box here and it's all threatening to boil over. What a start!
(22’) Penalty saved by W. Szczęsny!
--- 22’ Goal! BENTEKE SCORES! Szczesny saves the penalty well but the ball spins up into the air, and the Belgium striker makes no mistake by planting a header past the unlucky 'keeper. Game on! ---
--- 22’ Missed penalty ---
(22’) Controversy here as Agbonlahor races through the entire Arsenal team and Szczesny brings him down. The ball falls to Weimann who misses, but Taylor points to the spot. Arsenal are apoplectic, but it's the right decision. The 'keeper escapes with a yellow card...
--- 21’ Yellow card W. Szczęsny is cautioned by the referee. ---
(21’) PENALTY TO VILLA!
(20’) Chance for Giroud now, but he can't get enough on the header and can only steer it wide of Guzan's left-hand post. The striker is hungry for more goals today.
(18’) Arsenal have committed six fouls to Villa's two so far - Wenger's side are taking it to Lambert's and not letting them breathe.
--- 17’ Substitution N. Baker is replaced with C. Clark. ---
(17’) Baker hasn't been able to shake off that early injury and has been replaced by Ciaran Clark. He'll be desperately disappointed to be subbed so early.
(16’) A sign in the stands reads "You Can't Buy Class" - but can Arsene Wenger buy anybody? It doesn't look like he needs Luis Suarez at the moment, but it's a long, long season...
(15’) Benteke tries to take on Bacary Sagna on the left wing but the French full-back does well to see the ball back to Wojciech Szczesny. Top stuff from a player thought likely to leave the Emirates this summer.
(13’) Wilshere looks for a curved pass over the top to Walcott but the ball is blocked out. Great idea, and there'll be plenty of passes like that this season.
(11’) Villa are always going to be a threat on the counter today and Agbonlahor is showing plenty of pace down the left wing. He cant fashion a chance for anybody with his low cross, but Benteke is sniffing around for chances in the centre.
(10’) Well, what a start for Giroud. Much has been made of Wenger's pursuit of first Gonzalo Higuain and then Luis Suarez, but if the Frenchman keeps netting like that, the Gunners boss may not need a new finisher.
(8’) Both teams are down to 10 men - but it's due to injury as Walcott and Nathan Baker are hurt. Both have carried on though.
--- 6’ Assist A. Oxlade-Chamberlain gave the assist. ---
--- 6’ Goal! GIROUD SCORES! It's all so easy for Arsenal as Wilshere twists away from danger at left-back and Vlaar commits himself to a challenge on the halfway line, letting in Oxlade-Chamberlain. The England midfield races down the line into the box and cuts the ball across for Giroud to finish low past Brad Guzan from six yards. A top start for the Gunners. ---
(5’) Aaron Ramsey hooks a wasteful ball across midfield and Laurent Koscielny fouls Benteke in the middle of the park. The Welshman will have to be better in possession than that.
(4’) Tomas Rosicky tries a cute through-ball for Giroud here but the Villa defence does just enough to block out the France striker. A confident start from Wenger's men.
(3’) Two corners in quick succession here and there are ealy shouts for a penalty for Arsenal, but nothing doing from referee Anthony Taylor.
(2’) Arsenal win a corner here as they come flying out of the traps. Can they sneak an early lead?
(1’) We're underway! With more goals at the Emirates last season than anywhere else in the top flight, let's hope for a few today.
The teams are coming out of the tunnel and the home crowd expects - but can the Gunners deliver without a major signing? Villa had a desperate season last year, but they certainly won't be pushovers today.
